Paper brief adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md: A 2026-08-13 ADR (Proposed, no implementation) proposing a new additive `SettlementHold` model so that deliberately-held picks (e.g., score sources disagree → `holdReason: "DISPUTED"`) are persisted, letting settlement-health distinguish "correctly refused to guess" from "actually stuck/broken."
[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] method/metric: - Settlement cron runs hourly at `:20` via `/api/cron/settle-picks`.

[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] method/metric: Overdue detection: `result == "PENDING"` AND `game.commenceTime < overdueCutoff` — currently has NO hold exclusion, which conflates held vs stuck picks and drives `settlement = DEGRADED` → launch preflight `RESULT: FAIL`.
equation: `result == "PENDING"` AND `game.commenceTime < overdueCutoff` — currently has NO hold exclusion, which conflates held vs stuck picks and drives `settlement = DEGRADED` → launch preflight `RESULT: FAIL`.

claim: [adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] method/metric: Proposed `SettlementHold`: `(id, pickId, holdReason[String, not enum — orient/path holds on roadmap], settlementRunAt, sourceA, sourceB [the two disagreeing scores], resolvedAt, createdAt)`; unique on `(pickId, settlementRunAt)`; indexed on `(pickId, resolvedAt)`.
[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] data sources: Two unnamed free score sources used by `free-settlement-runner.ts:330-344` (the disagreeing pair that triggers a hold).

[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] finding: - Hold is deliberate and load-bearing per `operating-kernel.ts:172-183`: "exception(s) (DISPUTED / orient / path) need human evidence — never force-settle."
[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] finding: `rcaInputs` is currently in-memory only; the pick row is left `result: "PENDING"` with no marker when held.
[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] finding: The fix is purely additive: zero runtime behavior change at write time; rollback is `DROP TABLE "SettlementHold";`.
[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] finding: Explicit rule #1 preserved: never persist a guessed score — only the refusal + evidence (sourceA/sourceB).
[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] finding: Migration committed but NOT applied; agent holds no production `DATABASE_URL`.

[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] intel connection: - TRUST-SIGNAL: the disputed-score signal itself (`sourceA` vs `sourceB` disagreement) is a cross-source data-trust signal — the engine's intake of external scores/odds should carry disagreement flags rather than silently averaging.

[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] intel connection: OTHER: no-fake-data doctrine is an engine-integrity principle — any GSE projection pipeline should record refusals/uncertainty instead of imputing values.

[adr/006-settlement-hold-state.md] engine-actionable assessment: yes — if GSE settles any engine-tracked results, adopt the persist-refusals pattern (hold reason + evidence, never invented scores) for disputed outcomes.

Teammate effects on regime probability via ARIMAX: pi_ijG|j = eps_j + sum_l alpha_l pi_i(j-l)G|j-l + sum_l gamma_l eps_{j-l} + beta_ih C_ijh, C_ijh = 1 if teammate h on court at shot j; significant beta_ih build a signed teammate interaction network (density 0.2619, reciprocity 0.3636); e.g. Vazquez+San Miguel pair scored +19.10 pts/40min vs San Miguel alone.
equation: pi_ijG|j = eps_j + sum_l alpha_l pi_i(j-l)G|j-l + sum_l gamma_l eps_{j-l} + beta_ih C_ijh

claim: NBA scoring as antipersistent random walk (Gabel & Redner 1109.2825, JQAS 2012): scoring rate temporally homogeneous Poisson-like, lag correlations C(n) < 0.03 (nearly memoryless); same team scores next with q = 0.348; streak-length distribution Q(s) = q[w_1 Q(s-1) + w_2 Q(s-2) + w_3 Q(s-3) + w_4 Q(s-4)] matches data - streaks are pure randomness, no hot hand.

Small linear restoring force in basketball scoring (leaders coast, trailers press): P(team with lead L scores next) = S(L) = 1/2 - 0.0022*L (least-squares fit, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type); full model P_A = I_A - 0.152*r - 0.0022*Delta with intrinsic strengths Bradley-Terry I_A = X_A/(X_A+X_B); score-difference variance sigma^2 = 2*D*t with D_fit = 0.0363 vs D_ap = 0.0383; Peclet number Pe = v^2*t/(2*D) ~ 0.55 - strength bias small vs stochastic fluctuations.

Bayesian in-game college football win probability (Maddox/Sides/Harvill 2207.13747): three-stage pipeline - (1) team pace recursion xi_{k,m} = mu_m + eps_{k,m} to get expected possessions remaining tau = ((3600-t)/3600)*((xi1+xi2)/2); (2) XGBoost expected-score model; (3) dynamic Bayesian win prob on (tau,omega) cells via n_{tau,omega} ~ Binomial(N_{tau,omega}, p_{tau,omega}) with diffuse beta(1,1) prior plus beta prior imputed from 14 field experts. Holdout per-play Brier 2017-2021: adjusted dynamic Bayes 0.1250 vs dynamic Bayes 0.1453 vs random forest 0.1705.

Pregame blend weight function D2 (linear in time and score) was best: Brier 0.1250 vs D1 linear-time 0.1272 vs D3 quadratic 0.1265; point-value MAE: XGBoost 2.6802 vs linear 3.0805, linear+interactions 3.0614, RF 2.9751 - XGBoost wins by at least 0.2949 points.

TrackID3x3 (Hu et al 2503.18282v2): TI-HOTA metric = (1/19)*sum_{alpha in {0.05..0.95}} sqrt(DetA_alpha * AssA_alpha), with DetA = |TP|/(|TP|+|FP|+|FN|), AssA = (1/|TP|)*sum_c A(c), A(c) = |TPA|/(|TPA|+|FPA|+|FNA|), and similarity = LocSim * IdSim where LocSim = e^{ln(0.05)*||P-G||^2/tau^2} (tau=0.5 m) and IdSim = 1 iff ALL identity attributes match else 0.

Track-ID benchmark results (155,797 frames 3x3 basketball): Indoor TI-HOTA 80.75 +/- 13.16 vs Outdoor 46.11 +/- 20.55 (real jersey-number recognition collapsed); drone eval ByteTrack HOTA 47.92 +/- 5.98 (IDs 19.75 +/- 4.92) vs BoT-SORT-ReID 50.64 +/- 3.03 (IDs 15.5 +/- 1.91) - ReID reduces ID switches; RTMPose best outdoor pose PDJ 89.43%.

GTA tracker-agnostic post-processing (Sun et al 2411.08216): tracklet-pair distance D_{i,j} = 1 if temporal spans overlap, else mean pairwise (1 - cosine similarity) over all box embeddings of the two tracklets, i.e. D_{i,j} = (1/(N_i N_j))*sum_{m in Pi_i} sum_{n in Pi_j}(1 - F^i_m . F^j_n/(||F^i_m|| ||F^j_n||)); hierarchical clustering merges until no pair exceeds alpha=0.4; spatial gate encodes players don't teleport.
equation: D_{i,j} = (1/(N_i*N_j))*sum_{m in Pi_i} sum_{n in Pi_j}(1 - F^i_m.F^j_n/(||F^i_m|| ||F^j_n||))

claim: GTA gains (SportsMOT): SORT 56.28 -> 66.52 HOTA (+10.24), AssA 42.67 -> 59.59 (+16.92), IDF1 58.83 -> 77.37 (+18.54), ID switches 5180 -> 3547; ByteTrack 63.46 -> 69.74 (+6.28); Deep-EIoU 77.21 -> 81.04 (+3.83, SOTA); connector alone does most work (+9.15 HOTA), splitter adds ~1 pp; DetA/MOTA essentially unchanged; offline only (needs full sequence).

LED leapfrog diffusion trajectory model (Mao et al 2303.10895v1): inference replaces Gaussian init with trainable leapfrog initializer Y_hat^tau ~ P(Y_hat^tau) = f_LSG(X, X_N) then only tau << Gamma denoising steps (Gamma=100, tau=5); reparameterization Y_hat^tau_k = mu_theta + sigma_theta * S_hat_{theta,k}; DDPM update Y_hat^gamma_k = alpha_gamma^{-1/2}(Y_hat^{gamma+1}_k - (1-alpha_gamma)/sqrt(1-alpha_bar_gamma)*eps^gamma_theta) + sqrt(1-alpha_gamma)*z.
equation: Y_hat^tau_k = mu_theta + sigma_theta*S_hat_{theta,k}; Y_hat^gamma_k = alpha_gamma^{-1/2}*(Y_hat^{gamma+1}_k - (1-alpha_gamma)/sqrt(1-alpha_bar_gamma)*eps^gamma_theta) + sqrt(1-alpha_gamma)*z

claim: LED on 2017 NFL player tracking (predict 3.2 s from 1.6 s): minADE_20/minFDE_20 0.87/1.50 m vs prior SOTA MID 1.14/1.92 = 23.7%/21.9% improvement, beating all 10 baselines at every horizon; inference speedup vs standard diffusion 19.3/30.8/24.3/25.1x on NBA/NFL/SDD/ETH-UCY; ablation: mean+variance+correlated sampling 0.89/1.51 vs i.i.d. 1.18/1.90 - correlated sampling alone beats i.i.d. full model even at K=2.

Functional least-squares ratings (Lowery/Slater/Thies 1908.00939, 2018-19 NCAA basketball 353 teams, 5,603 games): beta_i(t) - beta_j(t) = d(t), t in [0,T], compactly X*beta(t) = d(t) with identifiability sum_i beta_i(t) = 0; normal-equations decomposition beta_i(t) = dbar_i(t) + sos_i(t) where dbar is average point differential and sos is strength of schedule; objective minimize L2 norm ||r(t)|| = integral_0^T (X beta(t) - d(t))^T(X beta(t) - d(t)) dt.
equation: beta_i(t) - beta_j(t) = d(t); X*beta(t) = d(t); ||r(t)|| = integral_0^T (X*beta(t) - d(t))^T*(X*beta(t) - d(t)) dt

claim: Functional ratings findings: constant home advantage needed (Model 1 vs 2 p-values < 0.1 except first minute), team-specific home advantage not supported; end-of-game home-court effect ~3 points (80% CI); scalar ratings Gonzaga 14.98 (#1), Duke 13.31, Virginia 12.99; REJECTED for NFL - zero predictive validation, and the functional twist buys nothing for NFL's discrete-scoring 17-game setting.

l1-TCL transfer learning for causal effect estimation (Wei et al 2305.09126v3): source rough-fit nuisance model, then Lasso bias-correction of the sparse source-target difference: beta_hat_t = argmin_b n^{-1}*sum_i[-z_i x_i'b + G(x_i'b)] + lambda_PS*||b - beta_hat_s||_1; sparsity assumption ||Delta beta||_0 <= s; recovery bound |tau_hat_TL - tau| = O(s*sqrt(log d/n) + s*d*sqrt(log d/n_s)).
equation: beta_hat_t = argmin_b n^{-1}*sum_i[-z_i x_i'b + G(x_i'b)] + lambda_PS*||b - beta_hat_s||_1; |tau_hat_TL - tau| = O(s*sqrt(log d/n) + s*d*sqrt(log d/n_s))

claim: Causal transfer findings: real EMR data (vasopressors known to reduce mortality) - target-only IPW = +0.0002 (wrong sign), merged-domains = +0.0441 (worse - biased toward source), l1-TCL TLIPW = -0.0013 (correct sign, most accurate); IHDP benchmark 3-headed TARNet + DR in-sample ACE error: l1-TCL 0.289 vs WS-TCL 0.337 vs TO-CL 0.415; key rule: never naively merge domains - the merged estimator was worse than target-only when mechanisms differ.

Kairosis Bayesian change-point forecast aggregation (Hassoun/Powell/MacKay/York 2408.00785v4): candidate change-point times in forecaster time (forecast order); prior geometric P(t_CP=t_r) = p*(1-p)^{R-r}, p=1/10; pre/post [0,1] bin counts as compound Dirichlet-categorical with pre pseudo-counts alpha_k = lambda*t_CP (lambda=0.2), post alpha'_k = 1, 5 equal bins; final aggregate = kairosis-weighted median (weights from the CMF).
equation: P(t_CP = t_r) = p*(1-p)^{R-r}; P(n_1,...,n_K) = Gamma(sum alpha)/Gamma(sum n + alpha) * prod_k Gamma(n_k + alpha_k)/Gamma(alpha_k)

claim: Kairosis on 650 real Metaculus questions was the ONLY method beating the benchmark on all four skill variants: Brier unweighted 0.060 (0.009), Brier time-weighted 0.054 (0.009), log unweighted 0.046 (0.006), log time-weighted 0.042 (0.006); exponential-decay median negative on all (-0.211/-0.252/-0.040/-0.061); kairosis-weighted MEAN terrible (-0.540/-0.545/-0.139/-0.143) - aggregation function matters as much as weights: median wins, mean loses.

NBA defensive spatial decomposition (Franks et al 1405.0231v3): defender canonical location mu_{tk} = gamma_o*O_{tk} + gamma_b*B_t + gamma_h*H with gamma_o + gamma_b + gamma_h = 1; fitted EM estimates 0.62*O_{tk} + 0.11*B_t + 0.27*H (+/-0.02/0.01/0.02); HMM transition parameter rho in 0.96-0.99 across games to infer defender-to-receiver assignments from tracking data.

Defensive skill decomposition: shot-frequency suppression and shot-efficiency suppression are nearly uncorrelated, distinct skills - Roy Hibbert ranked 1st and 4th in paint efficiency suppression but 161st in both paint frequency bases; Dwight Howard 11th/2nd in paint frequency suppression but 50th/117th in efficiency; 10-fold CV log-likelihoods: full shooter -25,474.93 vs no-defense -25,725.17 vs no-spatial -26,342.83.

OpenSkill (Joshy 2401.05451v1): Weng-Lin Bayesian approximation to TrueSkill as open-source library for asymmetric multi-team multiplayer ratings, Plackett-Luce recommended as default; rating state (mu, sigma) per player/team with Bayesian update per match outcome; Overwatch (>=2 matches/player): OpenSkill 556/79 = 87.56% accuracy in 0.97 s vs TrueSkill 587/48 = 92.44% in 3.41 s - trades ~2-5 accuracy points for ~3.5x speedup; sigma shrinks with matches, inflates with time decay.

Second ledger of Zimmermann (1702.05982v1) adds: NCAAB Vegas always-favorite baseline 0.7313 accuracy / +$7.51 with 5 pick'ems expected-case handling; NBA 2016 with 115 pick'ems expected Vegas -$1,857.30, and KP got 725 regular-season favorites but only 12/109 pick'ems right while NB got 48/109 (0.44); NFL all models peaked before season end (NB gave back >$600 by regular-season end); NCAAB sample n=67 games is noise-dominated.

Second ledger of Clegg/Cartlidge/Syed (2605.16066v1) adds: in-play conditional sampling via inverse transform T_remaining = (s^gamma - log(U)/lambda)^{1/gamma} - s; covariate BICs: PSxG beta_hat_psxg=-0.10 (0.02) DeltaBIC=-53.4; goals deviation beta_hat_goals=-0.07 (0.01) DeltaBIC=-49.4; calibration shifts exceeded 0.47 max (42-min increase in Leicester's expected time to score vs Arsenal), predominantly positive (uncalibrated model overestimates scoring); Maia in-play 69.4%/RPS 0.1303/log-loss 0.6963.

Battle-royale rating evaluation (Dehpanah et al 2105.14069, PUBG duo data >25,000 matches, >825,000 players): NDCG = sum_{i=1}^{N}[1/log2(i+1) * 1/(1+error_i)] / IDCG was the only metric that (a) stayed reliable under new-player influx (robust below 80% new-player share vs MAE's 55%), (b) distinguished Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill from the PreviousRank baseline across all three setups, (c) showed the clearest system separation.

Battle-royale rating findings: accuracy settled ~2.5% on all-players and could not separate systems from PreviousRank on best players; Kendall's tau judged inappropriate (ignores deviations, pairwise agreement only); AP severely underestimated predictive power (~0.55%); TrueSkill showed real frequent-player decay (beaten by PreviousRank at high game counts) visible in MRR, AP, and NDCG alike, while Elo/Glicko improved on frequent players.

6MapNet player-style embeddings (Kim et al 2109.04720): FaceNet-style triplet network on GPS-derived location + velocity-direction heatmaps (speed > 4 m/s); triplet loss L = sum_i[||f(x_i^a) - f(x_i^p)||2^2 - ||f(x_i^a) - f(x_i^n)||2^2 + alpha]_+, margin alpha = 0.1; heatmap additivity h(s_p(T)) = sum_i h(s_p(T_i)); hard-negative mining re-mined at most every 10 epochs - best model came from training only a few epochs on the FIRST triplet selection (second mining round hurt as negatives became stylistically similar).
equation: L = sum_i[||f(x_i^a) - f(x_i^p)||2^2 - ||f(x_i^a) - f(x_i^n)||2^2 + alpha]_+, alpha = 0.1; h(s_p(T)) = sum_i h(s_p(T_i))

claim: 6MapNet re-identification of 308 anonymized K-League players from ~289 minutes each (p10-ATL25 best): Top-1 46.1%, Top-3 69.8%, Top-5 81.8%, Top-10 92.5%, MRR 0.613; ATL25 outlier-filtered likelihood roughly doubled simple L2 distance baselines (Top-1 46.1 vs 24.7); data scaling p6->p8->p10 Top-1 34.1->41.2->46.1 monotonically; identities overlap train/test by construction (re-identification, not unseen-player generalization).

Bookmaker home-advantage mispricing after COVID empty-stadium restart (Deutscher & Winkelmann 2008.05417, Bundesliga 2019/20 split at round 25, N=3,672): home wins 49.63% -> 32.53% after the break; away wins 26.91% -> 44.58% (+65% relative); away goals exceeded home goals for the first time (1.66 vs 1.43); efficiency logit Away x COVID interaction +1.136*** while bookmakers never adjusted over 9 closed-door rounds; naive always-bet-away ROI +14.71% vs always-bet-home -33.84% in the closed-door period.

Mispricing concentration: in 39 'close' matches (|ImpliedProbDiff| <= 0.3), 19 away wins vs 9 home wins; bookmakers favoured home in ~60% of closed-door matches (avg +7.73 pp); margins did NOT rise for closed-door matches (4.79% vs 4.83%) despite higher bookmaker uncertainty.

FERL fast evidential rule learning (Fumanal-Idocin & Andreu-Perez 2608.05859v1): natively Dempster-Shafer fuzzy rule trees; per-node mass m_o({c}) = phi_o*p_o(c), m_o(Theta) = 1 - phi_o; combined closed form m_tilde(Theta) = prod_o(1-phi_o), m_tilde({c}) = prod_o(1-phi_o+phi_o*p_o(c)) - prod_o(1-phi_o); credal set S(x) = {c : m({c}) >= max_j m({j}) - m(Theta)}; abstention iff S(x) = Theta; Bel(c) = m({c}), Pl(c) = m({c}) + m(Theta).
equation: m_o({c}) = phi_o*p_o(c); m_o(Theta) = 1 - phi_o; m_tilde(Theta) = prod_o(1-phi_o); S(x) = {c : m({c}) >= max_j m({j}) - m(Theta)}

claim: FERL results on 30 KEEL tabular datasets: FERL-deep 83.23% accuracy (best rule learner) but still 2.4 pts behind RF 86.6; AURC 9.21 vs RF 6.26; set-valued: u65/u80 0.80/0.83 vs NCC 0.79/0.80 with coverage 0.92 and mean set size 1.70; OOD leave-one-class-out AUROC 77.66 (matches dedicated detectors); cost: FERL-deep fits in median 0.26 s on one CPU, scores a fold in 1.5 ms.

Soccer broadcast camera calibration (Falaleev & Chen 2410.07401v1) REJECTED - no video-ingest lane; only metrics banked: Acc@t = TP@t/(TP@t + FN@t + FP@t) at t=5 px polyline matching and Score = Acc@5 x CR (completeness ratio); SoccerNet Challenge 2023 leaderboard 1st 'Our' Acc@5 0.7322, CR 0.7559, Score 0.5535 vs baseline 0.0833.
equation: Acc@t = TP@t/(TP@t + FN@t + FP@t); Score = Acc@5 x CR

claim: Monocular 3D ball localization (Van Zandycke & De Vleeschouwer 2204.00003v3) REJECTED for NFL: combined loss L = BCE + alpha*Huber(delta=1.0) for diameter, alpha=0.5; CNN cut diameter MAE from ~4.9 px (Hough) to 1.6 px, projecting to ~1.7-2.3 m 3D error / ~10% relative error; prolate-spheroid footballs break the spherical-ball geometric assumption and broadcast zoom/pan breaks per-image calibration.

Bingham (2021) classical linear prediction survey: Kolmogorov-Szego formula prediction error variance sigma^2 = exp{integral log f(theta) dtheta/2pi} = prod_1^infty (1 - |alpha_n|^2); Szego's condition log f in L_1; alpha in l_2 iff Szego holds; rejected for NFL - stationarity is false for NFL data (roster turnover, coaching changes, rule changes) and 17-game seasons give only n=17 observations per team, far too few for functional methods.
equation: sigma^2 = exp{integral log f(theta) dtheta/2pi} = prod_1^infty (1 - |alpha_n|^2)

claim: Brown/George/Xu (2008) predictive density admissibility: under KL loss for X|mu ~ N_p(mu, v_x I) predicting Y|mu ~ N_p(mu, v_y I), generalized Bayes rules form a complete class; uniform prior p_hat_piU is admissible for p = 1, 2 (best invariant, minimax) but inadmissible for p >= 3 (Komaki 2001) - the KL analog of Stein's phenomenon; harmonic prior pi_H = ||mu||^{-(p-2)}, p >= 3 is admissible. Rejected for GSE - normal-model theory with no discrete-outcome application.

Minimax forecast aggregation (Guo et al 2401.17743): zero-sum game between aggregator f(x_1,x_2) and adversarial nature choosing worst-case conditionally-independent information structure; regret R(f,pi) = E_pi[(f(X)-omega)^2] - inf_g E_pi[(g(X)-omega)^2]; proposed aggregator worst-case regret 0.0226 vs lower bound ~0.0225 vs simple average 0.0625 - ~64% worst-case regret reduction over the mean (N=20 bins, M=400 nature strategies).

Meta-analytics metric-audit framework (Franks et al 1609.09830): Discrimination D_sm = 1 - E_sm[V_spm[X]]/V_sm[X]; Stability S_m = 1 - E_m[V_pm[X] - V_spm[X]]/(V_m[X] - E_m[V_spm[X]]); Independence I_mM = C_{m,m} - C_{m,M} C_{M,M}^{-1} C_{M,m} via Gaussian-copula latent correlation; mixed-effects model X_spm = mu_m + Z_sm + Z_pm + Z_spm + eps_spm.
equation: X_spm = mu_m + Z_sm + Z_pm + Z_spm + eps_spm; D_sm = 1 - E_sm[V_spm[X]]/V_sm[X]; S_m = 1 - E_m[V_pm[X] - V_spm[X]]/(V_m[X] - E_m[V_spm[X]])

claim: Meta-analytics results on 70 NBA metrics: raw 3P% least discriminative/least stable metric studied - >50% of between-player 3P% variation in a season is chance; rebounds/blocks/assists highly discriminative and stable; BPM beats WS/48/ORtg/DRtg on reliability; steals I ~ 0.40 (60% explained by other 69 metrics); NBA PCA F_15 ~ 0.75 (15 of 65 components explain 75%); NHL: plus-minus non-discriminative, takeaways I=0.73 most unique metric, Corsi more reliable than Fenwick; EB shrinkage visibly improves 3P%'s D and S.

Jurman (1511.06262) seasonal linear predictivity in soccer: cumulative_points(r) = alpha + beta*r fit on rounds 1..(n-ts), ts=1..20 held-out, extrapolated; linear MAE 4.652 (95% CI 4.634, 4.672) vs quadratic 8.966 vs cubic 27.760 (higher-degree fits dramatically worse - overfit to early-season noise) vs random null 4.993 - real sequences only ~0.34 points better than random (statistical significance without practical significance); at ts=10 normalized displacement 0.1874 ~ 1.874 positions in a 20-team league. REJECTED for GSE - wrong granularity, negligible edge over random.

Kelly criterion for variable pay-off (Perez Marco 1411.3615): growth rate g(f) = q*log(1-f) + p*integral_0^infty log(1+bf)*rho(b) db; classical Kelly f*(p,b) = p - q/b = [p(1+b)-1]/b; Theorem 3.1 integral equation integral_0^infty [b*rho(b)/(1+b*fhat)] db - (1-p)/[p*(1-fhat)] = 0 with unique solution by strict concavity; Corollary 3.2: fhat(p,rho) <= f*(p,bbar) with bbar = integral b*rho(b) db - uncertain pay-off implies the Kelly fraction is bounded above by the constant-average-payoff fraction (shade down). REJECTED - subsumed by ledgers 0171/0626/0813.
equation: g(f) = q*log(1-f) + p*integral_0^infty log(1+bf)*rho(b) db; f*(p,b) = [p(1+b)-1]/b; integral_0^infty [b*rho(b)/(1+b*fhat)]db - (1-p)/[p*(1-fhat)] = 0

claim: Distributional robust Kelly (Sun & Boyd 1812.10371): maximize_{b in B} inf_{pi in Pi} E_pi[log(r'b)] over uncertainty sets Pi (polyhedral/box/ellipsoidal/f-divergence/Wasserstein), solved as disciplined convex program in CVXPY; horse-race illustration: nominal Kelly growth under nominal distribution 4.3% vs robust 2.2% (robustness costs ~half nominal growth); worst case: nominal Kelly -2.2% vs robust +0.7% (box set, eta=0.26) - converts a negative worst case into positive.
equation: maximize_{b in B} inf_{pi in Pi} E_pi[log(r'b)]

claim: Adaptive Kelly with unknown win probabilities learned online (Despons/Peliti/Lacoste 2201.03387v2): Laplace strategy b_x^{LAPL,t+1} = (n_x^t+1)/(t+M); cumulative regret <Delta(t)> ~ <Delta(t0)> + (M-1)/2*log(t/(t0+1)); per-race KL gap ~ (M-1)/(2t); learning time t* = (M-1)/(2*D_KL(p||r)) - races needed for cumulative learning loss to equal one race of Kelly edge; mean log-capital <log C_t> ~ D_KL(p||r)*t - (M-1)/2*log(t/(t0+1)) - <Delta(t0)>.

Learning-cost extensions: Markov order-1 correlated races cost M(M-1)/2*log t; memory-n correlated races blow up as M^n(M-1)/2*log t - a principled reason to require proportionally more evidence for correlated outcomes (SGPs, correlated props); Cover's universal portfolio is exactly the Laplace estimate (b_x^{PORTF,t+1} = (n_x^t+1)/(t+M)); a prior from bookmaker odds reduces short-term loss only with zero asymptotic effect.

Elite NBA lineup prediction from individual stats alone (Martonosi/Gonzalez/Oshiro 2303.04963): 28 player stats expanded to sorted 5-vectors per stat (min..max) = 140 order-statistic predictors per candidate lineup; unanimous-consent rule (all seven classifiers agree: decision tree, random forest, boosting, SVM, kNN, logistic regression, LDA) predicting binary elite indicator (positive plus-minus). Test-set precision 86.7% with overall accuracy 52.3% (recall deliberately sacrificed).

Restricted next-season evaluation of the lineup classifier: 76.9% precision vs 62.1% elite prevalence baseline - generalizes to player combinations with zero shared court history (the key result); limitations: plus-minus is noisy/context-dependent, unanimity kills recall, no salary/DFS-pricing integration.

LLM-SoccerArena prospective benchmark (Schroeder et al 2607.24573, 2026 World Cup 104 matches x 7 LLMs x 3 horizons x 2 access x 2 prompting = 8,736 forecasts): T-24h complete-panel Brier Gemini 0.506 [0.433, 0.587] to Mistral 0.546 [0.493, 0.604] - NO pairwise model comparison significant after Holm (smallest adjusted p = 0.055); open-book (web) vs de-vigged closing market at T-2h: Gemini 0.497 vs market 0.498 - essentially market-equal.

LLM forecast levers: web access is the biggest lever (open-book Brier 0.535 -> 0.512, paired delta 0.0228, 95% CI [0.0044, 0.0403], Holm p=0.045, 4.3% reduction) while model choice is small; horizon T-24h vs T-2h open-book delta only 0.0021 Brier - forecasting closer adds almost nothing; forecast diversity: mean pairwise correlation of probabilities 0.943, mean JS divergence 0.0044 - LLM ensembles are highly redundant; confidence informative but not calibrated (highest-confidence group Brier 0.423 vs lowest 0.620).

Second ledger of Tung et al (2607.15483v1) adds: EU value V_EU(A) = sum_i p_i theta^T phi(o_i); two-sided CPT mixture proposal for market probabilities - market-implied p = pi*w_public(GSE p; gamma_pub) + (1-pi)*w_sharp(GSE p; gamma_sharp ~ 1), with the estimated mixture weight pi per game becoming a sharp-action feature; synthetic teacher ground-truth theta_star = [0.10, -0.20, 0.30, 0.05, -0.25]; K=50 stochastic rollouts per scene x action.
equation: V_EU(A) = sum_i p_i theta^T phi(o_i); p_mkt = pi*w_public(p_GSE; gamma_pub) + (1-pi)*w_sharp(p_GSE; gamma_sharp~1)

Temporal Conformal Prediction (Aich, Aich & Jain 2025, arXiv:2507.05470) builds adaptive prediction intervals via a rolling-window conformal layer over quantile-regression forecasts: fit q̂(α/2), q̂(1−α/2) on rolling window {r_{i−w}..r_{i−1}}, nonconformity scores ε(lower)=r_i−q̂(α/2) and ε(upper)=q̂(1−α/2)−r_i, threshold C_t=(1−α)-quantile of windowed scores, interval [ℓ_{t+1},u_{t+1}]=[q̂(α/2)−C_t, q̂(1−α/2)+C_t]; adaptive layer computes coverage error e_t=1{r_t∉[ℓ_t,u_t]}−α and applies a Robbins–Monro update to C_t.

In Aich et al.'s evaluation (daily log-returns r_t=log(P_t/P_{t−1}), Nov 2017–May 2025), TCP empirical coverage at 95% nominal undershot: S&P 500 0.861 (avg width 2.661), Bitcoin 0.885 (9.611), Gold 0.881 (2.202), vs quantile regression 0.971/0.969/0.969 (over-covering) and GARCH 0.827/0.853/0.837; the abstract's claim of 'near-nominal coverage' contradicts its own Table 1 (the body admits 86–88% undershoot) — integrity flag: cite tables, not abstracts.

Theorem 4.2 of Aich et al. (2025): long-run average coverage of TCP converges to 1−α almost surely under ergodicity, but only for the unmodified Robbins–Monro rule; the authors' practical 'forgetting factor' shrink heuristic (shrinking C_t by a small fraction of γ_t when r_t falls inside the interval so intervals narrow after volatility passes) has no theoretical backing, by the authors' own admission.

TCP sensitivity grid on the S&P 500 (window w∈{100,252,500} × γ_0∈{0.005,0.01,0.05}) gave stable-but-below-nominal coverage 0.8463–0.8958 with widths 2.58–2.77; the COVID-crash case study (Feb–Apr 2020) showed intervals visibly widening in March 2020 and contracting in April — qualitative adaptiveness to regime shifts, with a design takeaway that monotone time decay of γ_t makes late-sample adaptation sluggish, so making γ_t a function of detected volatility state is an improvement.

Evans et al. (arXiv:2009.00550v1) defined player–team social affinity from a Twitter follow graph and tested whether it predicts free-agent destination team in MLB (2002–2018, 4,207 switchers, 702 with Twitter handles) and NBA (2001–2018/19, 1,847 switchers, 784 with handles), using unweighted follow counts with no recency and no edge timestamps, classifying over ~30 candidate teams (random guess 1/29 ≈ 3.45%) with Random Forest, ExtraTrees, AdaBoost, XGBoost, logistic regression and KNN over ten 70/30 train/test runs.
equation: affinity(p,t) = |{q : p follows q and q is on team t}|

claim: Evans et al. results: MLB destination accuracy social-only 16.880%, all features 19.402%, team ID + social 19.955% (best); NBA Twitter-only 26.104%, all-social 26.667%, all features 29.740%, rank/value + social 30.238% (best) — roughly 5–9x random, social adding ~+3–6 pp over non-social; but the headline gains are contaminated by fatal leakage (a July-2020 Twitter snapshot with no edge timestamps used to predict transitions back to 2001/2002, so post-signing follows leak the label), plus handle-coverage selection bias (only 16.7% of MLB switchers, 42.4% of NBA switchers identified).
TRUST-SIGNAL from Evans et al.: only timestamped social-graph edges created before a tampering window are admissible as prediction signals; current-snapshot follow graphs are definitionally leaky.

Shianifar & Faiud (arXiv:2608.03416v1) evaluated ten LLMs from seven providers on a single pre-tournament forecast of the 2026 FIFA World Cup (48 teams, 104 matches) under one frozen pre-tournament snapshot, a common JSON schema, and transparent additive stage-decomposed scoring; ground truth: all 104 matches played, Spain beat Argentina 1–0 in the final; materials, raw responses and scoring code released (frozen to commit f83ea90).

Group and knockout scoring in the World Cup 2026 LLM study: per group S_g = 5·I_winner + 5·I_top2 + 3·N_qual + 2·N_rank; knockout S_progression = 2·C_R32 + 4·C_R16 + 6·C_QF + 8·C_SF + 12·C_Final (cumulative); S_placing = 20·I_champion + 10·I_runner-up + 8·I_third + 5·I_fourth; total score = group matches + standings + knockout; the study's audit decomposed scores by stage, tracked rank trajectories as components were added, and computed confidence-vs-accuracy and Pearson correlations between component and total scores.

World Cup 2026 LLM leaderboard: GPT-5.5 Thinking 744 (GS 254/ST 248/KO 242; the only model to pick champion Spain), GPT-5.5 717, Gemini 699, Qwen 3.7 687, DeepSeek 599, Claude Sonnet 4.6 591, Mistral 568, Perplexity 552, Perplexity Pro 530, Grok 496; knockout component SD 88.65 vs group-match 8.65 and standings 12.20, with corr(total,KO) r=0.986 (Spearman 0.945) vs corr(total,group-match) r=0.055 and corr(total,standings) r=−0.103 — knockout forecasting created essentially all leaderboard separation; Claude Sonnet 4.6 had the best group outcome accuracy (63.89%, 46/72) yet finished 6th, and exact-score accuracy ranged only 6.94–13.89% across models.

In the World Cup 2026 LLM study, self-reported model confidence was uncorrelated with accuracy (r=−0.060) and with total score (r=−0.067) — uncalibrated self-reported confidence is noise and should never be displayed without calibration evidence; unnormalized composite leaderboards rank the highest-variance component rather than overall skill.

Storkey (2011, AISTATS, arXiv:1106.4509) proves prediction markets of ML agents implement model-combination rules as market equilibria: log-utility agents yield a wealth-weighted mixture of experts, while exponential/CARA-utility agents yield a product of experts; mixed-utility markets interpolate between mixture and product combinations, and local-potential markets extend the framework to MRFs/CRFs via message passing; the paper is pure theory with no experiments or empirical validation.
equation: u(w)=log w  ⇒  price ∝ Σ_i wealth_i·p_i   (mixture of experts)

claim: In Storkey's ML-markets framework, exponential (CARA) utility u(w)=−exp(−a·w) yields an equilibrium price proportional to the product of experts with wealth dropping out; the ledger proposes a fittable one-parameter family spanning mixture↔product per market type, with per-sub-model 'wealth' updated by realized log score (Kelly-style) as self-tuning mixture weights and context-dependent interpolation gated on ensemble disagreement.
equation: u(w)=−exp(−a·w)  ⇒  price ∝ Π_i p_i^{weight_i}   (product of experts)

claim: Limitations of Storkey's ML-markets theory: the utility→aggregation equivalences hold exactly only under price-taking, complete markets, and strictly concave utilities; exact clearing is intractable for multivariate outcome spaces; the market framing adds clearing/budget overhead versus plain stacking or averaging.

Wei et al. (2023, arXiv:2305.09126v3) propose ℓ₁-TCL transfer learning for average causal effect (ACE) estimation in a data-poor target domain: (1) rough-estimate nuisance GLM parameters on a data-rich source, β̂_s = argmin_b n_s⁻¹Σ[−z_{i,s}x_{i,s}ᵀb + G(x_{i,s}ᵀb)]; (2) Lasso bias-correct the source–target parameter difference; (3) plug β̂_t into IPW/OR/DR estimators; the sparsity assumption is Δβ=β_t−β_s with ‖Δβ‖₀≤s.
equation: β̂_t = argmin_b n⁻¹Σ_i[−z_i x_iᵀb + G(x_iᵀb)] + λ_PS‖b−β̂_s‖₁

claim: Wei et al. recovery bound (Theorem 1): |τ̂_TL − τ| = O(s√(log d/n) [bias-correction] + sd√(log d/n_s) [rough-estimation]) w.h.p. ≥1−1/n; consistency requires n_s ≫ s²d²log d versus n ≫ d² without transfer.

On real EMR data (in-hospital records from two level-1 trauma centers, 2018: source 207 treated + 1249 control, target 58 treated + 700 control, 34 features; truth: vasopressors reduce 28-day mortality): target-only IPW gave +0.0002 (wrong sign), merged-domains IPW gave +0.0441 (worse, biased toward source), while ℓ₁-TCL TLIPW gave −0.0013 (correct sign, most accurate); on the IHDP pseudo-real dataset, 3-headed TARNet + DR absolute ACE error: ℓ₁-TCL 0.289 (0.238) in-sample and 0.301 (0.259) out-of-sample, beating target-only (0.415/0.360) and warm-start TCL (0.337/0.324). Methodological warning: naive pooling of domains can increase bias (merged worse than target-only).

Kairosis (Hassoun, Powell & MacKay 2024, arXiv:2408.00785v4) is a Bayesian change-point aggregation method: it weights each probability forecast in a time-ordered stream by the posterior probability that it was made after the most recent information-regime change point, then aggregates via a weighted median (not mean). Candidate change point t_r lives in 'forecaster time' (forecast order 1..R, dilating high-activity periods); prior is geometric P(t_CP=t_r)=p(1−p)^{R−r} with 1/p=10 (≈10 forecasts per change point); pre-change pseudo-counts α_k=λ·t_CP (λ=0.2), post-change α'_k=1; weight of forecast s = expected cumulative posterior mass at s.

On 650 Metaculus binary forecasting questions (mean 145 days open, 893 forecasts each), the kairosis-weighted median was the only method to beat the unweighted-median benchmark on all four skill-score variants: Brier unweighted 0.060 (0.009), Brier time-weighted 0.054 (0.009), Log unweighted 0.046 (0.006), Log time-weighted 0.042 (0.006); exponential-decay median scored −0.211/−0.252/−0.040/−0.061, most-recent-20% median −0.135/−0.159/−0.011/−0.023, uniform mean −0.657/−0.652/−0.199/−0.198. Crucially, the kairosis-weighted MEAN was terrible (−0.540/−0.545/−0.139/−0.143) — aggregation function matters as much as weights: median wins, mean loses.

Kairosis scoring conventions: S_Brier(X,p)=−(p−X)² and S_Log(X,p)=X log p + (1−X) log(1−p), with skill scores measured vs an unweighted-median benchmark at three times (early/mid/late), unweighted and time-decreasing weighted; parameters used were 5 equal bins, p=1/10, λ=0.2, reported robust for p<0.2, λ>0.1 with no fine tuning needed.

Liu et al. (2022, arXiv:2204.11142) built a DQN agent for Google Research Football (soccer) whose Q-network is a GCN or GAT over a 24-node player graph (22 players, 1 ball, 1 'other information' node; 9 features per node) instead of a CNN over rasterized observations; GCN: 2 graph-convolution layers, 9 input features/node → 32 hidden → 19 outputs (one Q-value per action, action_size=19); GAT: 2 graph-attention layers + FC layer; training was self-play in the gfootball simulator v2.6.
equation: α_ij = softmax_j(e_ij) = exp(e_ij)/Σ_{k∈N_i} exp(e_ik),  e_ij = a(Wh_i, Wh_j)

claim: In Liu et al. (2022), the DQN update used TD Local = Q(s,a;θ), TD Target = r + γ·max_{a'} Q(s',a';θ⁻), and the optimized loss is the (signed) TD error — the paper prints Eq. 5 as the signed error while the actual optimized loss is presumably its square (unstated); hyperparameters: lr 0.0001, batch size 1, gradient clipping 0.7, 1 epoch = 3,000 episodes, 100 epochs ≈ 0.3M steps; γ, ε-schedule, replay size and target-update frequency all unstated (not reproducible).

Adversarial read of Liu et al. (2022): every reported number is negative (agents never beat the built-in AI) — GCN avg score difference: easy −0.37 (rising curve), hard −2.23, competition −1.62, Kaggle −2.52; GAT: easy −1.13 (peaked −0.43 at epoch ~10 then declined), hard −1.41 (best GAT), competition −2.62, Kaggle −2.59 (declining reward); Table III easy-scenario: PPO 0.05, IMPALA −0.01, DQN −1.17, GCN −0.37, GAT −1.21; the 'efficiency' claim compares 0.3M-step runs to 20M-step baselines (66× compute difference), an uncontrolled comparison — adapt only the player-graph representation, not the DQN apparatus.

Wysocki (2025, arXiv:2508.16598v1) compares position-sizing schemes for systematic SPXW 0–5 DTE put writing (2018–2024, $5M starting capital, Interactive Brokers margin, commissions, 50% bid-ask spread crossing per trade): Kelly sizing Q_t = floor(PV_t/M_t · f*) with Kelly fraction f*(p,a,b) from win probability p and win/loss payoffs a,b calibrated via Monte Carlo GBM; VIX-rank scaling multiplies size by (1 − P_rank(VIX_t, W)) so fewer puts are written when VIX is high in its lookback window; the hybrid is the multiplicative product of edge-based (Kelly) and regime-based (VIX-rank) sizing.

Wysocki (2025) findings: 0–1 DTE, 5%–10% OTM identified as the strongest risk-adjusted region; Kelly variants reached 20%–25% annual returns in the claimed best region, hybrid high-return configs ≈40%–45% annualized, balanced hybrid configs 10%–11% with information ratios ≈3; 2024 (nominal OOS) several configurations 14%–23% annualized with lower volatility/drawdown than buy-and-hold. CRITICAL integrity flag: the paper states 'in-sample' as 2018–2024 and 'out-of-sample' as 2024 — the OOS year overlaps the IS window, so 2024 results cannot be treated as a clean holdout, and 40%–45% figures are grid maxima (max-over-grid selection bias).

Beal et al. (2020, arXiv:2012.04380) built a five-stage NLP pipeline over 1,770 EPL matches (2013/14–2018/19) with Guardian pre-match previews: OpenIE relation-tuple extraction per sentence → sentence-to-team allocation (home α, away β, or no team) → Count Vectorizer sentence vectors f(s) → per-team aggregation V(α)=Σf(s), V(β)=Σf(s) → Random Forest on X=[μ·V(α), V(β)] with home-advantage weight μ (Clarke & Norman 1995); ensemble Model 4 stacks an RF on the 9-vector of outcome probabilities from text RF, Dixon & Coles, and bookmaker favourite.

Beal et al. (2020) results (averaged over 3 seasons, 300 games/season test sets): ensemble Model 4 accuracy 63.19% (precision 0.612, recall 0.563, F1 0.586) vs Dixon & Coles 59.11% vs bookmaker favourite 52.43% vs text-only RF 53.53%; ablating text features from Model 4 cost −10% F1 and −7pp accuracy, attributing the boost to text; draws: models 1–3 predicted zero of 75 test draws while Model 4 predicted 26.5%; walk-forward 2018/19 Model 4 accuracy rose +2.23% from week 1 to week 38, attributed to late-season human factors (relegation battles, qualification, rotation); prior statistical models plateaued at ~56.7% and ~59.1%; leakage note: Experiment 2 used a random non-temporal 80/20 split, so draw/longshot numbers are optimistic.

Qureshi & Zaman (2021, arXiv:2109.07581) measured sports moneyline market efficiency over 109,249 games (2010–2021, NFL/NBA/NHL/MLB/NCAAF/NCAAB) with implied probability p_u=100/(100+|o_u|) for o_u≥100 and p_u=|o_u|/(100+|o_u|) for o_u≤−100, and efficiency diagnostic α=−1+(1/n)Σ_u W_u/p_u (α=0 perfectly calibrated, α>0 means underdogs win more than odds imply); only the NBA's no-fans COVID regime showed a significant edge: NBA COVID α=+0.17 (2019–20) and +0.10 (2020–21) vs post-COVID (fans back after All-Star Game) α=−0.9, KS/Mann-Whitney p≤0.001 at 1% under Holm-Bonferroni, Wilcoxon p≤10⁻⁵; the inefficiency concentrated in the implied-prob bin (0.2,0.3] (odds +233 to +400, 153 games, 21.7% of NBA COVID games), the only bin significant at 1% (MW p=0.00021/0.0003).

Qureshi & Zaman (2021) mechanism evidence: the NBA has the lowest total-points coefficient of variation (0.11) of any sport — the inherently least random sport — and removing fans plausibly erased home-field advantage while oddsmakers did not reprice; all other sports' markets stayed efficient (NCAAB was Mann-Whitney-significant but with negative mean α, not exploitable). A flat $1 on every underdog yielded 16.7% profit margin; λ=1.0 with inverse-probability (1/p_u) weights grew $100→$2,666 (~26-fold) in-sample on the known regime (not a forward claim, assumes liquidity at archived odds, no limits or transaction costs); best risk-adjusted was Bernoulli weights f(p)=√(p_u(1−p_u)) with λ=0.1 (→$291.73, highest robust Sharpe γ=median(R)/MAD(R)), while probability-weighting (f=p_u) led to full ruin within a month.

Hamilton & Firth (2021, arXiv:2112.11262v1) extended Bradley–Terry from binary outcomes to arbitrary finite outcome sets via maximum entropy: p^{ij}_{a,b} ∝ π_i^a π_j^b, normalized over the finite outcome set, with log-linear form log p^{ij}_{a,b} = a·θ_i + b·θ_j − log Z_{ij} (+ home effect), θ=log π; estimated via log-linear models (R gnm); symmetric prior of notional wins/losses against a dummy team with prior weight 4 (regularization toward parity); demonstrated on English schoolboy rugby (Daily Mail Trophy 2015/16–2017/18; 2017/18: 102 teams, 436 matches) with outcome categories (wide/narrow win, draw, narrow/loss) × try-bonus outcomes, sharing team strengths across result and try-bonus processes and an additive home-advantage term constant across teams.

Hamilton & Firth (2021): log-linear form of the multi-outcome Bradley–Terry model is log p^{ij}_{a,b} = a·θ_i + b·θ_j − log Z_{ij} with θ = log π; modeling choices materially changed published rankings in the rugby application (mean absolute ~8 places disagreement, max 28 places, ~0.4 league points per match vs the competition's incumbent ranking method); the paper is explicitly retrodictive — no out-of-sample forecasting or odds test was claimed, and choosing the outcome scores (a,b) is a modeling decision the paper does not fully automate.
equation: log p^{ij}_{a,b} = a·θ_i + b·θ_j − log Z_{ij}

claim: TacticAI (Wang et al., 2024, arXiv:2310.10553v2, Google DeepMind + Liverpool FC) models soccer corner kicks (9,693 corners from 2020–21 Premier League; 2,517 dropped on alignment failures → 7,176 valid, 80/20 split; tracking at 25 fps, only the kick frame used; 1,736 shots / 5,440 non-shots) with a receiver-conditional outcome decomposition P(shot)=Σ_i P(shot|receiver=i)·P(receiver=i) (train conditional on the ground-truth receiver, marginalize at inference) — the direct unconditional P(shot) model failed (F1 0.52).

TacticAI results: receiver top-3 accuracy 0.782±0.039 with GATv2 + D₂ group convolution (ablations: CNN 0.364, Deep Sets 0.713, MPNN 0.723, GATv2 0.748, +D₂ frame averaging 0.780); shot F1 rose from 0.521 unconditional to 0.677 receiver-conditional (0.712 with D₂ in ablation); generated tactical adjustments were near-indistinguishable from real ones (MLP real-vs-generated F1 0.53±0.05 = chance); defensive refinement cut predicted shot probability 0.75→0.69 (z=2.62, p<0.001), attacking refinement raised it 0.18→0.31 (z=−4.46, p<0.001); expert study (5 Liverpool FC raters): real-vs-generated F1 0.60, receiver top-3 agreement 0.79, retrieval recall 0.63 vs 0.33 baseline (z=2.34, p<0.05), 90% (45/50) of adjustments favored, mean rating 0.7±0.1 (t₄₉=9.20, p<0.001).

TacticAI's graph architecture: 22 player nodes fully connected, node features = positions, velocities, heights, weights, ball-possession flag, edges = teammate/opponent one-hot; GATv2 attention (Eq. 3–4, 8 heads); geometric deep learning with the D₂ dihedral group (identity + horizontal/vertical/both reflections) via frame averaging (Eq. 6) for invariance and group convolutions (Eq. 8) for equivariance — 4 group-conv layers, 4 latent features/player; conditional VAE (Eq. 11, reparameterization trick) samples one team's positions/velocities for guided generation; retrieval via nearest neighbors in latent team-embedding space (mean of player embeddings).

Khraishi & Okhrati (2022, arXiv:2203.03003) applied offline Conservative Q-Learning (CQL) to consumer-credit pricing on ~200k real US auto-loan applications (Columbia CPRM dataset: interest rate, term, approved amount, FICO score, accept/reject outcome) with no online price experimentation and no assumed demand functional form; reward r(s_t,a_t)=p(Accept_t|s_t,a_t)·(expected profit if accepted per Phillips et al. 2015: interest income − capital costs − credit risk); the π_Opt baseline was a*_t=argmax_{a∈[2.5%,12.5%]} p̂(Accept|s_t,a)·profit(s_t,a) with p̂ from a train logistic regression.

Khraishi & Okhrati (2022) results: the CQL policy delivered +21% expected profit over the historical policy (3-seed average) with MAPD < 15% of prices vs historical, pushing the average price down 6.8%→5.9% (consistent with documented historical over-pricing); the parametric π_Opt delivered +34% but was fragile — under alternative response models with similar fit its estimated gain ranged from −7% to +34% (avg 12.6%), 'strong evidence of overfitting'; baseline logistic regression pseudo-R² was low, the regime where model-free offline RL's advantage is largest; synthetic experiments showed CQL recovering near-optimal pricing under misspecified demand.

DreamerV2 (Hafner et al., 2020, arXiv:2010.02193) replaces the Gaussian stochastic state of the RSSM world model (PlaNet/DreamerV1) with a vector of categorical latents trained via straight-through gradients plus KL balancing, achieving human-level Atari performance (55 games) learned purely inside a separately trained world model; ELBO = reconstruction + reward log-likelihoods − β·L_KL, with RSSM deterministic recurrent state h_t, prior p(ẑ_t|h_t) predicting the posterior q(z_t|h_t,x_t) without the image, and behavior learned in imagination via REINFORCE + straight-through world-model gradients.
DreamerV2 KL balancing: L_KL = α·KL(sg(q)‖p) + (1−α)·KL(q‖sg(p)), with α = 0.8, scaled by β = 0.1 (Atari) / 1.0 (continuous control); straight-through sampling uses Bengio et al. 2013.

RCD (Maeda & Shimizu, 2020, arXiv:2001.04197) is a functional-model-based causal discovery method exploiting non-Gaussianity to learn causal graphs while explicitly representing latent confounders: directed arrows for genuine causal directions, bi-directed arrows for pairs sharing an unobserved common cause; three steps: (1) ancestor extraction via repeated pairwise direction inference (Lemmas 1–3), residualizing identified common ancestors by least squares (max regression size n=2); (2) parent/ancestor separation (Lemma 4 + Theorem 2); (3) unidentifiable-direction pairs marked bi-directed.

In RCD, causal direction rests on the Darmois–Skitovitch theorem (Theorem 1): non-Gaussian residuals reveal direction, with a Shapiro–Wilk test (α_S) gating non-Gaussianity; tuning used α_C=α_I=α_S=0.01, n=2, with α_I swept as 0.1^k (k=1…25), keeping the fewest-confounded result; evaluation uses F-measure = 2·precision·recall/(precision+recall) scored separately for bi-directed and directed edges (direction must be correct).

RCD results: simulations (medians) — RCD highest on latent-confounder detection F among RCD/FCI/RFCI/GFCI, highest median precision and F-measure on causality, median recall second-highest (next to RESIT); paper caveat: 'RCD does not greatly improve the performance metrics compared to the existing methods'; GSS real data (NORC, n=1380): bi-directed — RCD 4 estimated/4 correct (precision 1.0), FCI/RFCI 3/3 (1.0), GFCI 0/0; directed — RCD 5/4 (0.8), LiNGAM 5/4 (0.8), RESIT 12/4 (0.3), FCI/RFCI 3/1 (0.3), PC/GES 2/1 (0.5); RCD's only error was x_3 ← x_5; paper warns real-world structures are 'often very complex' and RCD 'likely produces a causal graph where each pair is connected with a bi-directed arrow' (α_I tuning is a fragile heuristic).

AutoGluon-TimeSeries (Shchur et al., 2023, arXiv:2308.05566) is an open-source AutoML system for probabilistic time-series forecasting with a diverse model zoo (statistical: AutoETS, AutoARIMA, AutoTheta; deep: DeepAR, PatchTST, Temporal Fusion Transformer; tabular: DirectTabular/RecursiveTabular converting TS to tabular regression around AutoGluon-Tabular; plus Naive/SeasonalNaive baselines), time-series cross-validation generating out-of-fold predictions, greedy forward-selection ensembling with weights tuned to wQL/MASE on OOF, optional HPO, user-declared known-future vs past-only covariates, and output of mean plus arbitrary quantiles (e.g., 0.1/0.5/0.9); metrics: mean weighted quantile loss (wQL) for probabilistic accuracy, MASE for point accuracy vs naive baseline.

AutoGluon-TimeSeries benchmark (29 Monash Forecasting Repository datasets, all methods ≤4h training, per-dataset errors rescaled to [0,1]): point MASE — AutoGluon champion 19/29, avg rank 2.08, avg rescaled error 0.073, 100.0% win rate vs Seasonal Naive, 0 failures; StatEnsemble 3.12/0.238 (3 failures), AutoPyTorch 4.12/0.257, DeepAR 5.08/0.434, TFT 6.12/0.635 (worst of deep methods); probabilistic wQL — AutoGluon champion 19/29, avg rank 1.80, avg rescaled error 0.086, 100.0% win rate, 0 failures; StatEnsemble 3.36/0.330, DeepAR 4.08/0.455, TFT 4.24/0.487.

BatchBALD (Kirsch, van Amersfoort & Gal, 2019, arXiv:1906.08158) selects batches of points for deep Bayesian active learning by scoring the joint mutual information between a batch's labels and model parameters — fixing BALD's pathology of acquiring redundant near-replicas; BALD sums individual scores (double-counting overlap) while BatchBALD computes the overlap-aware union μ*((∪_i y_i) ∩ ω); proven submodular, so greedy selection x_n = argmax_{x∈pool\A_{n−1}} a_BatchBALD(A_{n−1}∪{x}) is a (1−1/e)-approximation (Nemhauser et al. 1978); a_BatchBALD ≤ a_BALD, equal at acquisition size 1.
equation: a_BatchBALD({x₁..x_b}, p(ω|D)) = I(y₁..y_b; ω | x₁..x_b, D) = H(y_{1:b}|x_{1:b},D) − E_{p(ω|D)}[H(y_{1:b}|x_{1:b},ω,D)]

claim: BatchBALD results: on Repeated-MNIST (acq 10) BALD performs worse than random while BatchBALD 'copes with the replication perfectly'; MNIST labels to 90% accuracy (quartiles 25/50/75%): BatchBALD 70/90/110 vs BALD reimpl 120/120/170 vs BALD (Gal 2017) 145; to 95%: 190/200/230 vs 250/250/>300 vs 335 — roughly 1.6–1.7× label savings; BALD 'drops drastically' from acquisition size 1 to 40 while BatchBALD maintains 5→10 and drops only slightly at 40 (estimator noise); EMNIST (acq 5): BALD cannot beat random, BatchBALD consistently beats random and BALD with higher-entropy class distribution; CINIC-10 transfer: 59% accuracy at 1170 acquired (BatchBALD) vs 1330 (BALD) — ~12% label savings. Complexity O(b·c·min{c^b,m}·|D_pool|·k) vs O(c^b·|D_pool|^b·k) exact-optimal vs O((b+k)·|D_pool|) BALD; scope limits: poor on unbalanced sets, ignores unlabeled-data structure, classification-only.

Orr et al. (2021, VLDB tutorial, arXiv:2108.05053v1) document the Uber Michelangelo feature-store lifecycle: (1) training-data curation — feature authoring/publishing with definitional metadata (update cadence + definition SQL), streaming features via aggregation functions persisted to the online store and logged to the offline store; (2) training/deployment — date-partitioned features with time-based join APIs, dual datastore (SQL warehouse offline, in-memory DBMS online); (3) monitoring/maintenance — feature quality metrics (freshness, null counts, mutual information across features) and model quality metrics (training–deployment skew, near-real-time outlier/input drift detection), with offending features isolated and replaced; model parameters/artifacts stored for provenance and reproducibility.

Orr et al. (2021) embedding-as-input challenges: nearest-neighbor stability (Wendlandt et al. 2018); downstream instability = number of predictions that change with different embeddings (Leszczynski et al. 2020); eigenspace overlap score (May et al. 2019); structured-data augmentation +40 F1 on rare entities (Orr et al. 2021, cited claim); fine-grained monitoring via user-defined subpopulation functions (Robustness Gym); error correction via augmentation/weak supervision/slice-based learning.

ContTune (Lian et al., 2023, PVLDB, arXiv:2309.12239v1) tunes distributed stream-data processing (Flink operator parallelism) in two phases: Big phase binary-lifts under-provisioned operators until backpressure clears (decoupling tuning from the DAG into N concurrently-tunable sub-problems); Small phase runs conservative Bayesian optimization with a feasibility-gated acquisition function and history reuse across workload changes, with proven O(1) average reconfiguration complexity.

ContTune small-phase details: per-operator GP surrogate over processing ability PA(p); conservative acquisition argmax_{p_i}(p*_i−p_i)·I(μ(p_i)−λ_i) where the indicator filters parallelism levels whose GP-mean processing ability is below upstream data rate λ_i — feasibility first, resource minimization second (stricter than Constrained EI); trade-off gate: if acquisition-suggested p^acq is farther than α from all observed parallelisms (d_nearest>α, unknown region), fall back to a linearity-based method (DS2) as conservative exploration; noise treatment: Top-K recent observations per operator + mean-reversion (environmental noise as positive additive); GP posterior μ(p_i)=k_*^T K^⁻¹ y, σ²(p_i)=k_*(p_i,p_i)−k_*^T K^⁻¹ k_*.
equation: μ(p_i) = k_*^T K^⁻¹ y;  σ²(p_i) = k_*(p_i,p_i) − k_*^T K^⁻¹ k_*

claim: ContTune results (Apache Flink WordCount + Nexmark Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5/Q8, 20-hour runs vs Dhalion, DS2, Big+DS2, Dragster; artifacts at github.com/ljqcodelove/ContTune): avg reconfigurations per tuning 1.29 vs 2.40 (DS2) → −46.25% (α=0: −35.42%); end-to-end tuning time −47.08%, end-to-end runtime −3.12%; total CPU cost essentially identical to DS2 (−0.22%); backlogged data −43.01% vs DS2, −89.09% vs Dhalion; buffered-data processing time −16.79% vs DS2, −88.10% vs Dhalion; p99 latency equivalent to DS2 while using fewer CPU cores per query (e.g., Q5: 22 vs 25); synthetic workloads: up to 60.75% fewer reconfigurations vs DS2.

The MinervaScore (Santoni, Jouanne & Scullin, 2026, arXiv:2608.23808v2) is a 0–100 statistical robustness grade combining four established validation quantities — Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR), Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO), Superior Predictive Ability (SPA), Minimum Track Record Length (MinTRL, per Bailey & López de Prado) — plus a regime-stability composite ρ, with a binary 'Robustness Seal' calibrated on 359,062 production backtest records.
equation: Seal = 1[DSR ≥ τ_DSR ∧ PBO ≤ τ_PBO ∧ SPA ≤ τ_SPA ∧ T ≥ MinTRL ∧ ρ ≥ τ_ρ]

claim: MinervaScore details: Seal thresholds τ_DSR=0.95, τ_PBO=0.50, τ_SPA=0.10, τ_ρ=0.60; regime composite ρ = 0.5·p_+ + 0.3·clip_[0,1](1 − s_SR/σ_ref) + 0.2·logistic(SR_min) with p_+ = fraction of validation windows with positive Sharpe, s_SR = std of per-window Sharpes, SR_min = minimum across windows, σ_ref=2 fixed (authors flag this gate as the most heuristic component); signed margins: DSR on pre-Φ scale z_DSR=(u−Φ^⁻¹(τ_DSR))/σ_DSR with u=(SR̂−SR_0)/ŝe (DSR=Φ(u)); bounded gates on logit scale z_k=(logit(τ_k)−logit(g_k))/σ_k for k∈{PBO,SPA}; MinTRL via tanh z_MinTRL=tanh((T−MinTRL)/σ_T), σ_T=max(0.2·MinTRL,50); dispersions from IQR on the calibration population; fail-closed (no pre-Φ u ⇒ no score).

MinervaScore aggregation (eq. 7): S = wᵀz / √(wᵀΣ_eff w), w=(0.35,0.25,0.20,0.10,0.10) (DSR first), Σ_eff = cross-sectional correlation of margins estimated once on calibration (Hartung-style dependence adjustment); S → 0–100 display, 80+ reserved for Seal holders; DSR = Φ((SR̂−SR_0)/ŝe) with SR_0 = expected Sharpe under null given K trials (Lo / Bailey–López de Prado deflation).

MinervaScore validation: synthetic ground truth AUROC = 0.989 at headline difficulty (near-perfect separation of true signal from lucky backtests), though improvement over the GT-Score proxy and gates-passed baseline is modest (authors' honest caveat: most value is the DSR); pre-registered real-market test showed no significant forward relationship (Spearman ρ_s=0.013, one-sided permutation p=0.40 — 'in a population with limited surviving edge'); the score is positioned as an auditable validation and reporting layer, not evidence of demonstrated real-market predictability.

Dehpanah et al. (2021, arXiv:2105.14069) compared evaluation metrics (accuracy, MAE, Kendall's tau, MRR, AP, NDCG) for rating systems (Elo, Glicko, TrueSkill, PreviousRank baseline) on >25,000 PUBG duo matches (>825,000 unique players, chronologically ordered, ranks only), under three player-setups (all players, best players, frequent players): Elo (battle-royale extension): team rating μ_{t_i}=Σ_j μ_j; Pr(t_i wins,F)=Σ_{j≠i}(1+e^{(μ_{t_j}−μ_{t_i})/D})⁻¹ / (N choose 2), D=400; normalized rank score R'_{t_i}=(N−R^obs_{t_i})/(N choose 2); update μ'_{t_i}=μ_{t_i}+K[R'_{t_i}−Pr(t_i wins,F)], K=10; member shares weighted by contribution w_{p_j}=μ_j/μ_{t_i}; Glicko extension: team μ=Σμ_j, team σ=Σσ_j (raw sum, not quadrature); TrueSkill updates μ'_i=μ_i+(σ²_i/c)·N(t/c)/Φ(t/c), c=√(2β²+σ²_i+σ²_j), β=4.16, τ=0.833; defaults 1500 (Elo/Glicko), 25 (TrueSkill).

Dehpanah et al. (2021) metric findings: accuracy rises then flats ≈2.5% once new-player share <60% (Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill indistinguishable, all beat PreviousRank); best players ≈5% (≈2×) but cannot separate any system from PreviousRank; MAE settles ≈14.5 once new share <40%, Elo slightly best; Kendall's tau is negative at start under new-player load and fails to separate systems from PreviousRank — authors conclude tau is inappropriate; MRR steady ≈14% once new share <70%, but on frequent players PreviousRank beats Elo and Glicko; AP ≈0.55% once new <60% (hit-based precision weighting crushes values); NDCG is the winner — reliable once new-player share <80% (vs MAE's 55% threshold), far more robust to new-player influx, clearest system separation and best at showing superiority over PreviousRank across all three setups; on frequent players TrueSkill decays and is beaten by PreviousRank (a real TrueSkill signal, appearing in MRR/AP/NDCG alike). IR metrics use 1/(1+error) dampening on rank deviation; 10 games is enough to judge best players, 100 for frequent players.

6MapNet (Kim et al., 2021, arXiv:2109.04720) is a FaceNet-style triplet network learning player-style embeddings from GPS tracking-derived heatmaps without manual event annotation: per player-phase entity, two 35×50 heatmaps — a location heatmap plus a direction heatmap of velocity-vector endpoints with speed > 4 m/s (grid over {(v_x,v_y): −12 ≤ v_x ≤ 12, −8 ≤ v_y ≤ 8} m/s); heatmap additivity h(s_p(T))=Σ_i h(s_p(T_i)) for disjoint intervals enables augmentation by pixel-wise 3-combination (3 phases ≈ one full match); triplet network of three weight-sharing 2MapNet branches (CNN: Conv1a 2×3×4 → Conv1b 3×3×4 → MaxPool → Conv2a/b 3×3×16 → MaxPool → Conv3a 2×3×32 → Conv3b 3×3×32 → MaxPool → Conv4a/b 3×3×64 → FC1 1920→128 → FC2 128→10; batch norm after Conv/FC, 25% dropout after MaxPool and Conv4b); two 10-dim branch outputs concatenated and L2-normalized → 20-dim embedding. Data: Fitogether OhCoach Cell B wearable GPS (10 Hz), 2019–2020 K League 1 & 2, 750 matches → 1,989 phases → 17,953 player-phase entities from 436 players; role labeling via Bialkowski et al. frame-by-frame role assignment with per-player K-means (2–4 clusters, silhouette) on mean role locations.

6MapNet triplet loss L=Σ_i[‖f(x_i^a)−f(x_i^p)‖²₂ − ‖f(x_i^a)−f(x_i^n)‖²₂ + α]_+ with margin α=0.1 (best); triplet mining: candidate set S=5 heatmap pairs per identity, hard negative = one violating the margin, else one of 10 nearest negatives, re-mined every ≤10 epochs; key recipe finding: the best model came from only a few epochs on the FIRST triplet selection — the second mining round degrades performance (negatives become stylistically similar).

6MapNet similarity measure ATL-sim: sim(α,β;m)=(1/m)Σ_{i=1}^m log p_α(f(x_{β(i)}^te)) — per-anonymized-entity Gaussian density over training embeddings; similarity = average of top-m log-likelihoods of test embeddings; best config (p10-ATL25, ~10 phases ≈ 289 minutes, 308 anonymized entities): Top-1 46.1%, Top-3 69.8%, Top-5 81.8%, Top-10 92.5%, MRR 0.613; similarity ablation (Top-1/Top-10/MRR): L1 24.4/79.2/0.402, L2 24.7/80.2/0.404, AL 35.1/84.1/0.509, ATL75 42.5/89.3/0.574, ATL50 45.5/90.6/0.602, ATL25 46.1/92.5/0.613 — top-25% outlier filtering beats all-likelihoods; data-amount ablation: more phases help (p6 34.1/84.7/0.508 → p8 41.2/89.9/0.574 → p10 46.1/92.5/0.613).

Deutscher & Winkelmann (2020, arXiv:2008.05417) tested whether bookmakers repriced the disappearance of home advantage when the Bundesliga restarted behind closed doors: 2019/20 Bundesliga split at round 25 (Mar 9, 2020): 223 matches with spectators, 83 without (rounds 26–34 + 2 postponed); reference 2014/15–2018/19: 1,125 matches rounds 1–25, 405 matches rounds 26–34; data football-data.co.uk (30–56 bookmakers per match, average odds used); de-margined implied probability π̂_i=(1/O_i)/(1/O_h+1/O_d+1/O_a), i∈{h,d,a}; bookmaker margin margin_m=Σ_i O_{m,i}^⁻¹ − 1; ImpProbDiff=π̂_h−π̂_a.

Deutscher & Winkelmann (2020) findings: home wins 49.63% (prior-season R26–34) → 32.53% (closed-door); away wins 26.91% → 44.58% (+65% relative); away goals exceeded home goals for the first time (1.66 vs 1.43), home goals −20%; efficiency logit (N=3,672, AIC=4,322.4): ImpliedProbability 4.530*** (0.231), Away −0.162** (0.080) (pre-COVID home bias), COVID −0.606** (0.268), Away×COVID +1.136*** (0.358), round-trend interactions all insignificant — bookmakers never adjusted during the 9 closed-door rounds; margins did NOT rise despite higher uncertainty (4.79% closed-door vs 4.83% with spectators); margin regression: margin on |ImpProbDiff| −0.002*** per unit prob-difference, season −0.001***, R²=0.468, N=1,836.
equation: logit(Pr(Won_i=1)) = β_0 + β_1·ImpliedProbability_i + β_2·Away_i + β_3·BettingAfterRound25_i + β_4·COVID_i + β_5·(Away_i·COVID_i) + β_6·RoundAfterRound25_i + β_7·(RoundAfterRound25_i·COVID_i)

claim: Deutscher & Winkelmann (2020) return findings: Table 6 ROIs (level stakes): away bets closed-door +14.71% vs home bets −33.84% (baselines: 2014/15–2018/19 R26–34 home +6.24% / away −15.52%; 2019/20 with spectators away +5.53%); Table 7 (ImpProbDiff bins): bookmakers favoured home in ~60% of closed-door matches (avg +7.73 pp); in 39 'close' matches (|Δ|≤0.3): 19 away wins vs 9 home wins; heavy home favourites (Δ>45 pp): only 11 of 16 won; limitations: 83 closed-door matches is a small sample (+14.71% ROI has wide error bars, no t-stat), average odds not best available, flat stakes with no Kelly/variance adjustment.

FERL (Fumanal-Idocin & Andreu-Perez, 2026, arXiv:2608.05859v1) is a fuzzy rule-tree learner whose predictions are natively Dempster–Shafer evidential in one deterministic pass, yielding a point label, a credal set, abstention (set = whole frame), and an OOD signal with attribute-level anomaly attribution; fuzzy splits μ_{θ,h}(x_f)=min(1,max(0,(θ+h−x_f)/(2h))), θ = median of bootstrap (B=25) per-resample Gini-optimal cuts, h=γ·MAD; greedy growth with rule budget R (compact ≤15, medium ≤50, deep ≤200), split subsample cap 10,000 (only when N>50k).

FERL evidential output (closed form): m̃(Θ)=Π_o(1−φ_o); m̃({c})=Π_o(1−φ_o+φ_o p_o(c))−Π_o(1−φ_o); normalize by Z; Bel(c)=m({c}), Pl(c)=m({c})+m(Θ); ignorance-margin set S(x)={c : m({c}) ≥ max_j m({j}) − m(Θ)} (classes within the ignorance margin of the best class); abstention ⟺ S(x)=Θ; firing strength φ_o(x) becomes mass on the class distribution, residual 1−φ_o(x) mass on ignorance; repeated Dempster combination of nested (ancestor+descendant) nodes monotonically shrinks ignorance (Z'≥a ⇒ ignorance cannot grow with an added source) — hence deep trees combine leaves only.

FERL results (30 KEEL tabular datasets, 146–19,020 samples, 6–64 features, 2–11 classes, stratified 5-fold; OOD via leave-one-class-out): FERL-deep 83.23% acc (best rule learner, statistically significant vs all rule learners, Holm-corrected Wilcoxon; indistinguishable from LR 81.13 only); AURC 9.21 (vs RF 6.26, GB 6.60); structured deltas: wins on curved low-dim boundaries (banana +32.8 over LR), loses on oblique high-dim linear (twonorm −11.9, vehicle −7.7) — intrinsic to rule learning; leaves-only Dempster ablation acc 83.18, coverage 92.31, ignorance 22.93 vs all-node (80.62, 80.69, 0.07) vs Denœux's cautious rule (69.58, over-conservative); OOD leave-one-class-out: FERL-deep AUROC 77.66 vs kNN-distance 77.38, Mahalanobis 74.42, Isolation Forest 70.33, rejecting 36.47% of novel-class inputs at 95% retained acceptance — matching dedicated detectors with no separate detector; geometric-OOD toggle: firing-based AUROC 47.03→99.29, ignorance-based 23.19→98.62; graded covariate shift (k=1): FERL DS-conformal keeps 77.3% coverage by widening sets (1.35→4.10) vs global conformal falling to 55.0% at fixed size 1.09; cost: median fit 0.26 s (one CPU), 1.5 ms per fold — 10× faster than FURIA, 500× faster than FUCS at inference.

CoDi (Lee, Kim, Park 2023, ICML) generates mixed-type tabular data with two physically separated diffusion models — Gaussian for continuous columns, categorical for discrete columns — that co-evolve by conditioning on each other's perturbed states and are bound by a triplet contrastive loss to preserve the joint distribution; co-evolving reverse p_{θC}(x_{t−1}^C | x_t^C, x_t^D), p_{θD}(x_{t−1}^{D_i} | x_t^{D_i}, x_t^C); final losses L_C=L_{Diff_C}+λ_C L_{CL_C}, L_D=L_{Diff_D}+λ_D L_{CL_D}, 0<λ<1 (Eqs. 19–20); evaluation: TSTR sampling quality (F1/AUROC, R²/RMSE), coverage diversity (Naeem et al. 2020: fraction of fake samples with a real sample in their 5th-nearest neighborhood), wall-clock sampling time for 10K fakes.

CoDi results (11 public UCI-style benchmark tabular datasets; 8 baselines: MedGAN, VEEGAN, CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN, OCT-GAN, RNODE, STaSy; code at github.com/ChaejeongLee/CoDi): binary F1 CoDi 0.4726 vs STaSy 0.4559 vs Identity(real) 0.4154; binary AUROC 0.8106 vs 0.7961 vs 0.8119; regression R² CoDi 0.4794 (only positive among 9 methods), STaSy −1.3200, all others ≤ −0.07 or −inf; coverage diversity CoDi 0.6931 (best) vs STaSy 0.5771, CTGAN 0.3834, VEEGAN 0.0019; sampling time (10K fakes) CoDi 0.5187s vs STaSy 4.6417s (~9× faster), RNODE 103.14s; negative-sampling ablation: whole-block shuffle (Method 3) best (Heart F1 0.872±0.039 / coverage 0.949±0.012); contrastive learning adds Bank F1 0.527→0.566, Seismic 0.210→0.305, Stroke coverage 0.651→0.919; not compared against TabDDPM (no head-to-head exists).

TRUST-SIGNAL from the CoDi ledger: the paper's own adversarial note — TSTR-with-best-hyperparameters lets synthetic beat real (binary F1 0.4726 vs Identity 0.4154), so generator protocols can flatter; judge generator claims by baseline-vs-baseline comparisons, not synthetic-vs-real.

The AI Scientist (Lu et al., 2024, arXiv:2408.06292v3) automates scientific discovery end-to-end: LLM idea generation with evolutionary mutation + novelty filtering (idea archive: description + experiment plan + self-assessed interestingness/novelty/feasibility; novelty filter via Semantic Scholar API + web search) → Aider-based experiment iteration with error-feedback retries (up to 4 retries per failure, up to 5 iterations, writes an 'experimental journal') → per-section LaTeX write-up with self-reflection + 20 rounds of citation polling → GPT-4o automated reviewer outputting scores (soundness, presentation, contribution, overall, confidence) + binary accept/reject, post-calibrated by thresholding; reviewer calibrated on 500 ICLR 2022 papers (accepted + rejected) with metrics balanced acc, accuracy, F1, AUC, FPR, FNR, mean + 95% bootstrap CIs.

The AI Scientist results: reviewer calibration — human baseline balanced acc 0.66 / acc 0.73 / F1 0.49 / AUC 0.65 / FPR 0.17 / FNR 0.52; uncalibrated Sonnet 3.5: 0.52 / 0.40 / 0.55 / 0.52 / 0.95 — the calibrated AI reviewer approaches but stays below human consistency; diffusion template: Sonnet 3.5: 51 ideas, 49 novel, 38 experiments passed, mean reviewer score 3.82, max 6.0, ~$250; DeepSeek Coder: 51/42/32, mean 3.32, ~$10; Llama-3.1 405B mean 2.30; 10 selected generated papers scored 3–5 by the reviewer (average accepted NeurIPS paper ≈ 6); cost ≈ $10–15 per completed paper, ~50 ideas per run, ~12 hours on 8× H100s. Authors' Section 8 warnings: generated papers occasionally hallucinate entire ablation tables (fixed by instructing only observed results); silent misimplementation of ideas; limited experiment budget → unfair comparisons; agent 'struggles to compare the magnitude of two numbers'; minimal sandboxing caused a runaway self-relaunching process, ~1TB checkpoint writes, agents editing time-limit constraints. TRUST-SIGNAL: authors state explicitly — do NOT take generated papers' scientific content at face value, treat as hints; the calibrated reviewer (0.66 balanced acc) is a noisy filter, not a judge.

HypoForge (arXiv:2608.25770, 2026) is a self-improving multi-agent framework for automated hypothesis generation and testing that splits skill-learning by supervision type: adversarial generator–discriminator distribution feedback for hypothesis generation (no explicit feedback) and execution-outcome learning for hypothesis testing (empirical feedback available), distilling experience into reusable skills rather than raw trajectories; generation side = GAN-inspired adversarial generator–discriminator scoring whole batches of hypotheses on distribution-match to high-quality human-written hypotheses (distribution-level, not per-hypothesis); testing side = textual experiment protocol → implement → execute on target dataset → compare to ground truth → distill into reusable experiment-design/execution skills; metrics: hypothesis quality Q(H^t), Hit@K (generation); T_h hypothesis-testing score, E_h execution score (testing); evaluated on HypoBench and DiscoveryBench.
equation: S_h^{t+1} = distill(generator batch, discriminator distribution-level feedback)

claim: HypoForge results: generation (Table 4) — full model vs w/o Feedback: Q(H^t) 0.785 vs 0.726, Hit@K 0.648 vs 0.491; testing — removing execution outcomes drops T_h from 0.659 to 0.565 while E_h stays comparable; learned skills show transferability across diverse scientific tasks (qualitative); TRUST-SIGNAL: the discriminator is anchored to 'high-quality human-written hypotheses' — if that reference set overlaps the benchmark, the distribution-match score is circular (unaddressed); Q(H^t)/Hit@K are judge-based metrics with usual bias risk.

LMAC-Net (Wang, Li & Shen 2025, arXiv:2507.21945, Applied Soft Computing) performs long-term action quality assessment via learnable temporal queries per modality (RGB/flow/audio) + an attention-center consistency loss forcing modalities to agree on which temporal segments matter + two-level scoring (segment scores → softmax-weighted overall); per-layer query update q̂_k^{(m,i)} = p_k^{(m,i−1)} + q_k^{(m,i)} (Eq. 4); cross-attention α_{k,t} = exp(q̃_kᵀv_t/τ)/Σ_j exp(q̃_kᵀv_j/τ), τ init 0.07 (Eq. 6); prototype update p_k^{(m,i)} = Σ_j a_{k,j} v_j + p_k^{(m,i−1)} (Eq. 7); final Ŝ = Σ_k w̃_k ŝ_k, w̃ = softmax(w) (Eqs. 9–10); loss L = λ_1 L_score + λ_2 L_feature, L_feature = L_rank + L_sparsity + L_consistency; config: K=5 queries, 2 stacked decoders, 8 heads, 2 layers, dim 512, dropout 0.1/0.2, AdamW lr 9e-4/9e-5, cosine decay, batch 32.

LMAC-Net attention-center machinery: attention center ā_k^m = Σ_t t·α_{k,t}^m (Eq. 14); sparsity loss L_sparsity = Σ|t − ā_k^m|·α_{k,t}^m (Eq. 16); consistency loss L_consistency = Σ_t Σ_{i<j} ‖ā_t^{m_i} − ā_t^{m_j}‖² (Eq. 17); Spearman ρ Fisher-z averaged (Eq. 18).

LMAC-Net results: RG (rhythmic gymnastics, 1,000 videos ~1m35s @ 25fps) avg Spearman 0.840 vs PAMFN 0.819 vs GDLT 0.765; Fis-V (figure skating, 500 short-program videos ~2m50s @ 25fps) avg 0.850 (TES 0.811, PCS 0.881) vs PAMFN 0.822 vs GDLT 0.820; efficiency 0.419G FLOPs, 8.95M params, 4 ms inference vs PAMFN 18.06M params / 33 ms; ablation (RG/Fis-V avg): concat baseline 0.676/0.731 → +MLQE 0.730/0.765 → +L_rank 0.731/0.779 → +L_sparsity 0.735/0.779 → +L_consistency 0.797/0.808 — the consistency loss is the single biggest contributor (note: ablation-run numbers differ from headline 0.840/0.850, config unexplained); weak point: exact consistency forces modalities to attend to identical segments, destroying genuine cross-modal lead-lag (crowd roar anticipates the play; cadence precedes the snap) — an asymmetric or lag-tolerant consistency loss (learned per-pair offset δ_ij with L1 penalty) is the required fix.

ChronosX (Ansari et al., 2025, arXiv:2503.12107) adds lightweight covariate adapters (residual FFNs) on frozen pretrained time-series foundation models without retraining the backbone: an Input Injection Block for past-observed exogenous variables and an Output Injection Block for future-known covariates; the objective is the same as the backbone (cross-entropy for Chronos; MSE for TimesFM/MOMENT); backbone-agnostic (demonstrated on Chronos tokenized, MOMENT patched encoder, TimesFM patched decoder); metrics WQL (quantiles 0.1–0.9, 100 sample paths), MASE, geometric aggregation; training modes: adapter-only (backbone frozen) vs full fine-tuning.
equation: ẽ_t = e_t + W_2·σ(W_1·[e_t; x^{past}_t] + b_1) + b_2  (IIB residual FFN; identity when covariates are uninformative)

claim: ChronosX output injection: logits̃_t = logits_t + FFN([logits_t; x^{future}_t]) (OIB); findings on 32 author-constructed synthetic datasets (100 daily series each, length 1827, prediction horizon 30, past-only and future-known covariates with known ground-truth effects): adapter-augmented models beat frozen backbones on covariate-driven datasets across all three backbones; adapter-only training matches or approaches full fine-tuning performance at a fraction of the parameters; IIB and OIB are complementary (past-covariate effects via IIB, future-known effects via OIB), and the combination is best.

Hsieh & Wong (2024, arXiv:2404.13371) propose a variance-penalized Kelly objective balancing expected logarithmic growth against the variance of log growth: U_n^ρ(K;X) = (1/n) E[log(V(n,K)/V_0)] − (ρ/(2n²)) var(log(V(n,K)/V_0)) (Eq. 1), ρ≥0 — at ρ=0 it reduces exactly to classical Kelly; account dynamics V(n)=⟨K,R_n⟩V_0 with simplex constraint K_i≥0, ΣK_i=1; KKT per-alternative score (Lemma 3.2): E[R_{n,i}/⟨K*,R_n⟩] − (ρ/n) E[log⟨K*,R_n⟩·R_{n,i}/⟨K*,R_n⟩] + (ρ/n) E[log⟨K*,R_n⟩] E[R_{n,i}/⟨K*,R_n⟩] = 1 if K_i*>0, ≤1 if K_i*=0; optimality is necessary+sufficient only when log-variance is convex (verified for the two toy examples via ∂²v/∂K_2² ≥ 0).

Hsieh & Wong (2024) betting example (riskless X_1=0 vs risky X_2∈{−1/2,+1/2}, P(X_2=+1/2)=p∈(1/2,3/4); optimality equation f(p,K_2,ρ)=0; at ρ=0: K*_2=2(2p−1)=classical Kelly): p=0.6: ρ=0 → K*_2=0.4 (Kelly), ρ=0.1 → ≈0.3646, ρ=1 → ≈0.2035; p=0.75: ρ=0 → K*_2=1.0, ρ=1 → ≈0.5643; K*_2 is negatively affected by ρ and more sensitive to ρ as win probability rises; inventory example (n=5, ρ=1/2): K*_1=1, K*_2=0 (full allocation to safe category). TRUST-SIGNAL: the paper assumes the payoff distribution is known exactly — using the estimated p as a point estimate reintroduces the overbetting Kelly is infamous for; the paper offers no principled ρ calibration (answer with data: grid-search ρ∈[0,2] maximizing Calmar on rolling backtest); i.i.d. fails for correlated slates; the simplex is fully invested with no cash, so a bankroll cap is still needed; no empirical validation at all — treat as sizing theory, not evidence.

Agrawal & Ramdas (2026, arXiv:2604.20172) hedge Cover's universal-portfolio mixture (O(ln n) worst-case regret, unimprovable adversarially) with a Robbins-type mixture (o(ln n) on stochastic paths but linear worst-case): a 50-50 convex combination achieving O(ln n) worst-case AND O(ln ln n) a.s. regret plus asymptotically optimal growth rate — the first explicit construction of this hedge, in bounded and sub-Gaussian settings; theorems only, no simulations, no real data, no code (strategy is a closed-form mixture integral, numerically approximable by quadrature). Wealth process W_n(λ)=Π_{i=1}^n (1−λ(X_i−m_0)), λ∈[−1/m_0, 1/(1−m_0)]; mixture W_n=∫W_n(λ)π(λ)dλ; W*_n=sup_λ W_n(λ); regret R_n=ln W*_n − ln W_n; key identity ln W*_n = n·KL_inf(Q̂_n, m_0); Ville event E_α={sup_{n≥1} ln W_n ≤ ln(1/α)}.

Agrawal & Ramdas (2026) regret landscape: Cover/uniform has Θ(ln n) worst-case (tight) and cannot beat O(ln n) even on nice paths; Robbins achieves O(ln ln n) on typical paths but linear worst-case; the 50-50 mixture strictly dominates each component on the combined criteria (Proposition 5.1: 50-50 uniform + modified Robbins prior → O(ln n) worst-case + O(ln ln n) a.s. + optimal growth); the game-theoretic law of the iterated logarithm (Shafer & Vovk 2005) gives the wealth process as a sharp upper LIL witness. TRUST-SIGNAL: the wealth process doubles as an anytime-valid sequential edge detector — under the no-edge null (conditional mean = breakeven), wealth stays bounded (Ville); crossing 1/α certifies edge at level α with no peeking corrections (W_n ≥ 20 ≈ α=0.05 as a scaling trigger; W_n ≤ 0.5 after ≥50 picks as a shutdown/half-stake trigger); caveats: m_0=0.5 breakeven assumes market efficiency, bounded [0,1] needs an affine mapping of real P&L (clipping choice affects behavior), comparator class is constant fractions, not edge-adaptive.

DISCOVER (Gajera et al., arXiv:2602.06986) is a Python-native GPU-accelerated symbolic regression framework (CUDA NVIDIA and MPS Apple Silicon, CPU fallback) whose differentiators are hard dimensional-consistency enforcement via the `pint` unit library during feature generation (invalid expressions pruned before evaluation) and interchangeable exact/heuristic sparse solvers (OMP, MIQP, simulated annealing) for the L₀ descriptor problem; core objective min_β ‖y−Φβ‖²₂ subject to ‖β‖₀ ≤ D (Eq. 1, NP-hard L₀-regularized least squares); candidate features generated from user features + operator library, then sparse selection; physics constraints via config file (operator restrictions, complexity caps, variable-combination rules); units tracked through every symbolic operation.

DISCOVER paper: software announcement with no new datasets and no benchmark experiments (all performance claims aspirational — ledger's adversarial note); motivating use cases cited: crystal structure stability descriptors, ion mobility in battery materials, magnetic-structure discrimination; SISSO (Ouyang et al. 2018) as deterministic baseline, SISSO++ as large-scale alternative; the SISSO-style linear-in-features assumption is narrower than full SR (no nested compositions like sin(x²+e^x) unless pre-generated). TRUST-SIGNAL for feature generation: annotate each sports feature with a unit class ({probability [0,1], points, epa, rate, count, yards, time, dimensionless}) and forbid unit-violating operations at generation time (e.g., points × probability forbidden; probabilities only via sigmoid/logit composition; epa/play × plays → epa OK) — prevents nonsense like 'win_probability + temperature²' ever entering the search; warning: over-restrictive constraints exclude valid expressions, so the gate must include a recall check that no historically successful feature is pruned.

Denis, Hebiri & Zaoui (2020, arXiv:2006.16597) prove the optimal regression-with-reject rule for a fixed rejection rate ε is to abstain when the conditional outcome variance σ²(x) exceeds its (1−ε)-quantile; risk decomposition R_λ(Γ_f) = E[(Y−f*)² 1{predict}] + E[(f*−f)² 1{predict}] + λP(reject); semi-supervised plug-in: estimate f̂ and σ̂² on labeled data, calibrate λ̂_ε from the empirical cdf of σ̂² on UNLABELED data plus uniform perturbation ζ∼U[0,10⁻¹⁰] to avoid cdf jumps; Theorem 1 gives consistency of risk and rejection rate; Theorem 2 gives kNN convergence rates with no margin/smoothness assumption needed (unlike the classification analogue).
