claim: Horseshoe posterior mean is competitive in sparse-signal regimes but its risk explodes in dense-signal regimes: for k = p the risk rises to approximately 7.5 for p = 5, 66 for p = 50, and 130 for p = 100 versus minimax benchmarks of 5, 50, 100 -- shrinkage-method selection must depend on signal density (horseshoe-class wins sparse, collapses dense); the hyperprior Bayes predictive density under KL loss is likewise minimax and admissible (Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2).

A quantitative-finance framework (Ben Alaya, Kebaier & Sarr 2024) converts diffusion models from the risk-neutral measure Q to the real-world measure P via Girsanov's theorem: from RN SDE dY_t = b(Y_t)dt + sigma(Y_t)dW_t the Lamperti transform phi(y) = integral dy/sigma(y) gives dX_t = L(X_t)dt + zeta dW_t, and Theorem 2.1 gives RW drift = -vartheta[(X*_t - X_t) - alpha_t] (mean-reversion toward the RN path shifted by a calibration function alpha), with Corollary 2.1.1 Y*_t = phi^-1(phi(Y_t) + vartheta*integral_s^t alpha_u e^{-vartheta(t-u)} du) -- demonstrated on a CIR++ credit-spread model for Credit Agricole (simulated 5Y spread expectations matched targets 113/109/107/105/103 bp 'almost exactly' in a 20,000-draw Monte Carlo), but the corpus verdict is REJECT with no sports transfer: the RN/RW distinction has no GSE analogue since GSE models real-world outcome probabilities directly.
equation: RW drift = -vartheta[(X*_t - X_t) - alpha_t]; Y*_t = phi^-1(phi(Y_t) + vartheta*integral_s^t alpha_u e^{-vartheta(t-u)} du)

claim: Bingham (2021) gives shortened proofs of the classical Wiener (whole-past) and Krein (finite-section) prediction theorems for stationary continuous-time stochastic processes: whole-past predictor E-hat[X(t) | {X(u): u <= t-tau}] = integral_{-inf}^{t-tau} c*(u-t) d xi(u) with prediction error variance sigma^2(tau) = integral_{-tau}^{0} |c*(s)|^2 ds (error grows with lag tau) under the Szego non-determinism condition integral log G'(mu)/(1+mu^2) dmu > -infinity -- the corpus verdict is REJECT: pure restatement of the theoretical substrate beneath the Kalman/AR state-space tools already implemented, with no data, no estimation component, and MA kernels assumed known.

Calibration surfaces for continuously-updated forecasts use adaptive rank-based bins (M=10, bin reference p-tilde_j(t) = median forecast in bin because in-play forecasts cluster near 0/1 late) with Wilson intervals plus Bonferroni correction over M bins; a forecaster is calibrated iff the reference plane f(t,p) = p lies between the upper and lower surfaces U_{1-alpha}(t,p), L_{1-alpha}(t,p), summarized by U^min_{1-alpha}(t) = min_j[U(t,p-tilde_j) - p-tilde_j] >= 0 and L^max_{1-alpha}(t) = max_j[L(t,p-tilde_j) - p-tilde_j] <= 0, smoothed with a 5%-of-game moving average -- validated on ESPN's real-time NBA home-win forecasts (1,137 games train 2017-18, 1,213 games test 2018-19) and adopted as GSE's live win-probability calibration protocol.
equation: U^min_{1-alpha}(t) = min_j[U(t,p-tilde_j) - p-tilde_j] >= 0; L^max_{1-alpha}(t) = max_j[L(t,p-tilde_j) - p-tilde_j] <= 0

claim: Pointwise Brier skill confidence intervals: Delta-hat_N(t) = N^-1 sum_i [L(Y_i, p-hat_i^A(t)) - L(Y_i, p-hat_i^B(t))] with asymptotic normality (Delta-hat_N - Delta_N)/s_N -> N(0,1) where s_N^2(t) = N^-1 sum_i delta_i^2(t) p_i(t)(1-p_i(t)), using the conservative CI Delta-hat_N(t) +/- z_{1-alpha/2} s_N(t)/sqrt(N) with the p(1-p) <= 1/4 bound; the functional skill test H_0: ||Delta_N||^2 = 0 has ||Z_N||^2 = N||Delta-hat_N||^2 ->^D sum_{i>=1} lambda_i chi^2_i(1) with lambda_i conservatively estimated by eigenvalues of C-hat_cons(t,s) = N^-1 sum_i [p-hat_i^A(t) - p-hat_i^B(t)][p-hat_i^A(s) - p-hat_i^B(s)] and p-values via Q_D = sum_{i=1}^{D} lambda-hat_i chi^2_i(1), D = 10 -- invalid for nested models (degenerate kernel), which matters for GSE engine version A/B testing.
equation: (Delta-hat_N - Delta_N)/s_N -> N(0,1); ||Z_N||^2 = N||Delta-hat_N||^2 ->^D sum_{i>=1} lambda_i chi^2_i(1)

claim: ESPN's NBA forecasts were well-calibrated at all game fractions t: of 555 games with p-hat > 0.995 at some t, home won 553 (0.9964); of 343 games with p-hat < 0.005, home won 1 (0.0029); ESPN significantly beat the PgRS, ScD, LS, PgRSLS pointwise GLMs in aggregate, but against a simple logit on pregame probability plus live score difference (PgRSScD) the Brier-skill point estimates slightly favored the simple model except in the final moments and were not significant at 5% at any t nor in aggregate -- a proprietary in-play model's extra information adds no demonstrable skill, so a 2-covariate logit is the permanent simple baseline GSE's live model must demonstrably beat; the power analysis shows N >= 500 is needed to separate competitive models.

Frank & Klotz (2001) generalize Nakazi (1984) to the multivariate case, relating approximation in L^2(W) to approximation in L^2(W^-1) for q-variate weakly stationary sequences: the duality correspondence P_S I = I - (I - I-tilde_S, I)_tilde^-1 (I - I-tilde_S) W^-1 with Delta_S = (I - I-tilde_S, I)_tilde^-1, and the Szego infimum analog P_S I = I - (integral W^-1 d lambda)^-1 W^-1, Delta_S = (integral W^-1 d lambda)^-1, delta_S = [det(integral W^-1 d lambda)]^{-1/q} -- the corpus verdict is REJECT: closed-form formulas with no estimation component cannot be operationalized for NFL data (infinite past, known spectral weight W assumed), and NFL outcomes are not stationary linear sequences.
equation: P_S I = I - (I - I-tilde_S, I)_tilde^-1 (I - I-tilde_S) W^-1; Delta_S = (integral W^-1 d lambda)^-1

claim: Four-stage tennis momentum framework (2023 Wimbledon men's singles, 31 matches, 7,284 point observations): (1) existence via a 2x7 contingency table (streak length W_1..W_7+ x extension/termination) with Pearson chi^2 = sum sum (n_ij - n-hat_ij)^2/n-hat_ij on k-1 df -- chi^2 = 111.497, df = 6, p = 9.51e-18 on n = 3,595 winning streaks rejects independence; conditional P(W_next|W_k) = 0.5503, 0.5801, 0.5741, 0.4597, 0.3929, 0.4000, 0.5435 for k = 1..7+, nonlinear and threshold-like at k = 4 (though the p-value reflects n = 3,595 more than a large effect -- conditional probs move only +-0.05-0.10 around 0.5).

(2) Momentum quantified by an entropy-weight composite index: standardize features, p_it = z_it/sum z_it, e_i = -(1/ln T) sum p_it ln(p_it + eps), w_i = (1-e_i)/sum(1-e_i), M_t = sum w_i z_it (the final-match weights were dominated by a first-serve indicator at 0.3959, a tautology caution -- supervised weighting on next-drive EPA is proposed instead for NFL); (3) CUSUM change-point detection C_t = M_t - mu + C_{t-1} - d with a change point when |C_t| > h and shift intensity V_{t_i} = CP_{t_i}*(D_max/D_i); (4) BP neural net + PSO (v_i(k+1) = omega v_i(k) + c_1 r_1(p_best - p_i) + c_2 r_2(g_best - p_i)) improved point-outcome AUC only from 0.7125 to 0.7443 vs logistic regression at 0.7310 -- a marginal +1.3pp that is not worth porting.
equation: M_t = sum w_i z_it; C_t = M_t - mu + C_{t-1} - d; V_{t_i} = CP_{t_i}*(D_max/D_i)

claim: Hybrid NBA season simulator (Erazo 2023, 10 NBA seasons 2011-12 to 2021-22): win percentage with prior p-hat_1^i = (pi + sum_{k=1}^{i} x_1^k)/(1+i) with x_1^k in {0,1} and pi in (0,1); net rating = (points scored - points conceded over games 1..i)/(total possessions); Bernoulli Race game probability P(team 1 wins) = p_1(1-p_2)/[p_1(1-p_2) + (1-p_1)p_2] (vs an average team with p_2 = 0.5 the win prob is exactly p_1); incentive rules for eliminated teams owning their pick and locked playoff teams with <= 3 games remaining (win pct halved or net rating -5) improved every method with gains concentrated in the second half.

Per-method optimal historical lookback windows on a sweep of last-N-games: method (ii) home-adjusted Bernoulli Race peaks at last 8-15 games while method (vi) home-adjusted largest-value on net rating peaks at 18-25 games -- more data is not always better (accuracy rises, plateaus, then slowly declines), contradicting one-size-fits-all trailing windows; basic model second-half accuracy: Bernoulli Race on win pct 57.3-58.6% vs largest value on win pct 66.0%, but largest-value methods are strongly biased (systematically over-credit good teams' win totals) while Bernoulli Race gives more balanced simulated standings at lower accuracy -- a calibration-vs-accuracy tradeoff warning for any engine reporting accuracy without calibration.

Nonparametric maximum likelihood (Kiefer-Wolfowitz) for multivariate mixture models made practical by finite-grid convex approximation: G-hat = argmin_{G in G_T} l(G) with l(G) = -(1/p) sum_j log{integral_T f_0(X_j|theta) dG(theta)} approximated as G-hat_Lambda = argmin_{G in G_Lambda} l(G), equivalent to the convex simplex problem min_{w in Delta^{q-1}} -(1/p) sum_{j=1}^{p} log{sum_{k=1}^{q} f_0(X_j|t_k) w_k}; Proposition 1 shows that under an elliptical unimodal likelihood the NPMLE support lies inside the convex hull of the per-unit MLEs, so a regular grid inside that hull suffices; posterior mean pi-hat_j = integral pi_j f_0(A_j,H_j|lambda_j,pi_j) d G-hat_Lambda / integral f_0(A_j,H_j|lambda_j,pi_j) d G-hat_Lambda.
equation: min_{w in Delta^{q-1}} -(1/p) sum_{j=1}^{p} log{sum_{k=1}^{q} f_0(X_j|t_k) w_k}; pi-hat_j = integral pi_j f_0(A_j,H_j|lambda_j,pi_j) d G-hat_Lambda / integral f_0(A_j,H_j|lambda_j,pi_j) d G-hat_Lambda

claim: On 2005 MLB data (567 train, 499 test) bivariate NPMLE total squared error relative to fixed-MLE = 1.0 was 0.29 (all) / 0.26 (pitchers) / 0.14 (non-pitchers) -- best or tied-best on all splits, vs James-Stein 0.54/0.35/0.17 and grand mean 0.85/0.38/0.13 -- and the estimated population mixture discovered the pitcher/non-pitcher bimodality without being told, a trust-worthy archetype-discovery property; multivariate EB shrinkage beats univariate exactly when mean and noise are correlated (the sports case, where high-usage players have noisier per-game estimates); implementation guidance: EM is the simplicity/performance choice, grid 30^d is sufficient (insensitive to density), but cost explodes beyond d = 3.

Bayesian dynamic Bradley-Terry state-space rating on 197,926 men's pro tennis matches (1968-2025): dynamics theta_{i,t} = theta_{i,t-1} + w_{i,t} with w_{i,t} ~ N_S(0, tau^2 R(rho)) independently across players, exchangeable correlation R(rho) with off-diagonal rho; match probability P(i defeats j | theta_{i,t}, theta_{j,t}) = [1 + exp{-a_f (theta^{(s)}_{i,t} - theta^{(s)}_{j,t})}]^-1 with a_3 = 1 normalization; posterior p(Theta | y, psi) proportional to the product of initial conditions, random-walk transitions, and match likelihoods; filtering by mean-field across players plus iterated Laplace Gaussian approximations (Glickman 1999) to convergence with Carter-Kohn trajectory sampling (300 posterior samples).
equation: P(i defeats j | theta_{i,t}, theta_{j,t}) = [1 + exp{-a_f (theta^{(s)}_{i,t} - theta^{(s)}_{j,t})}]^-1

claim: Model fit: predictive accuracy 0.675, Brier 0.207 on 188,771 matches; Platt recalibration on the logit scale (intercept 0, slope 0.851, fit on odd years / evaluated on even years) removed systematic overconfidence (predicted 0.934 -> observed 0.910 in the highest band; reliability flat to 0.006 post-calibration) -- any dynamic rating module needs this odd/even Platt protocol built in; cross-surface model estimated rho-hat = 0.90 with +1,365 prequential log-likelihood units over independent components.

Summary-function robustness on 25 simulated records: longest-run estimate/true ratio mean 1.75 (Elo) / 1.32 (posterior median) with sd 0.87/0.60 -- non-robust -- vs fixed-window lag persistence pi_1 ratio mean 1.12/1.08 with sd 0.07/0.06 -- robust; fixed-window summaries win and run-based statistics are unreliable under estimation error (a methodological rule for any 'best team of the decade' content); rate-calibrated exceedance thresholds (mean N-bar = 1 and 2 players/period) solve cross-era comparison by comparing gaps not levels; at the strict threshold only 2002-2013 had periods where three-way dominance was more probable than not (57 such periods vs none in any other block).

RENEW (offline model-based RL, 2026) learns/repairs world-model transition dynamics from binary human preferences over imagined trajectory rollouts instead of a reward model: DLHF preference P(sigma^0 > sigma^1) = logistic(l_theta(sigma^0) - l_theta(sigma^1)) with trajectory log-likelihood l_theta(sigma) = sum_{t=0}^{H-1} log T-hat_theta(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) and DLHF loss L_DLHF(theta) = -sum_{(sigma^0,sigma^1,y) in D_>} [(1-y) log P(sigma^0 > sigma^1) + y log P(sigma^1 > sigma^0)], plus an epistemic-uncertainty-directed active querying loop (sample segment pairs proportional to u(sigma) = sum_t u(s_t, a_t)) -- filed as reference only (GSE has no world model or simulator), so the corpus verdict is REJECT; key numbers: naive DLHF with 1M preference labels roughly equals supervised learning on 1K transitions (e.g., Maze 10x10 DLHF l_1 0.0001 vs supervised 0.0003; Sliding 5x5 0.0105 vs 0.6622), RENEW roughly halves final l_1 error on Sliding Tile 3x3 (0.2070 vs naive 0.4190, where naive DLHF degraded the pretrained model via catastrophic forgetting), and RENEW wins transition-accuracy repair at every maze size with tighter CIs.
equation: P(sigma^0 > sigma^1) = logistic(l_theta(sigma^0) - l_theta(sigma^1)); L_DLHF(theta) = -sum_{(sigma^0,sigma^1,y) in D_>} [(1-y) log P(sigma^0 > sigma^1) + y log P(sigma^1 > sigma^0)]

claim: Matrix Chernoff-type concentration for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains under Ollivier-Ricci positive curvature, applied analytically to Elo tracking under a dynamic Bradley-Terry model with evolving skills: Elo curvature kappa = (1/8)*eta*e^{-4M}*lambda where lambda is the matchup-Laplacian spectral gap (how fast result information propagates through the matchup graph); expected tracking error E||X^t - rho^t||^2_2 <= (1-kappa)^{t-1}||X^0 - rho^1||^2_2 + Delta/kappa + 2 eta^2/kappa where drift Delta bounds E[||rho^{t+1} - rho^t||^2_2 + 4M||rho^{t+1} - rho^t||_1 | F_t] <= Delta; Elo update X-hat^t_I <- X^{t-1}_I + eta sigma(X^{t-1}_J - X^{t-1}_I) (loser mirrored), then orthogonal projection onto [-M,M]^n intersected with {x perp 1}.
equation: E||X^t - rho^t||^2_2 <= (1-kappa)^{t-1}||X^0 - rho^1||^2_2 + Delta/kappa + 2 eta^2/kappa; kappa = (1/8)*eta*e^{-4M}*lambda

claim: Since kappa is proportional to eta, the tracking bound is minimized at step size eta = Theta(sqrt(Delta)) -- a concrete K-factor scaling law for online ratings under drifting skills (small enough to minimize bias, large enough to track drift); NFL's sparse 17-game schedules give a small matchup-connectivity lambda (slow tracking), prescribing raising eta in sparse-schedule regimes; NFL schedules are fixed in advance so the worst-case min-connectivity lambda can be replaced by the actual season's schedule-Laplacian spectral gap lambda_sched computed exactly; curvature decays exponentially in the rating bound M (kappa proportional to e^{-4M}) so rates, not constants, are the usable guidance.

Latent MMHC hybrid structure learner for mixed-type variables (ordinal questionnaire scores, categorical demographics, continuous indicators): map mixed variables to a latent Gaussian copula space, then constraint-based skeleton via Max-Min Parents-and-Children (MMPC) with conditional-independence tests at threshold alpha in {0.01, 0.05}, then constrained score-based hill-climbing restricted to the skeleton with SEM/BIC-style score, returning a single DAG factorized as P(X) = product_i P(X_i | Pa(X_i)); on synthetic DAGs latent MMHC (SEM, alpha = 0.01) achieved the lowest median structural Hamming distance in 7 of 8 settings for p = 30 graphs -- but the corpus verdict is REJECT because GSE has no ordinal psychometric or mixed-type questionnaire data, and the volleyball application (164 amateur players) is severely underpowered with scenario analyses that are purely associational, not causal interventions.

Continuous-time Bayesian hierarchical model separating between-season career trajectory from within-season peaking cycle, applied to elite swimming: observation model y_{i,j,k} = g(t_{i,j,k}) + f_{i,j}(t_{i,j,k}-a_i-j+1) + x_{i,j,k} zeta + epsilon_{i,j,k}; population ageing function g(t) = sum_l delta_l B((t-d_l)/theta), cubic B-splines, L = 31 knots, theta ~ Exp(1); within-season component constrained restricted Bernstein polynomial h*_{i,j}(z) = sum_{k=2}^{K} sum_{v=1}^{k-1} beta^{(i,j)}_{k,v} b_{k,v}(z) with b_{k,v}(z) = C(k,nu) z^nu (1-z)^{k-nu}, K = 6, h*_{i,j}(0) = h*_{i,j}(1) = 0 for identifiability; between-season season starts follow a random walk with t-distributed increments (heavy tails allow abrupt career changes); global-local shrinkage via standardized Lomax(1/2) priors p(x) = alpha^{-1}(1+x)^{-(1+alpha)} chosen because the horseshoe's half-Cauchy caused MCMC instability -- a load-bearing prior-choice lesson for sparse-observation shrinkage.
equation: y_{i,j,k} = g(t_{i,j,k}) + f_{i,j}(t_{i,j,k}-a_i-j+1) + x_{i,j,k} zeta + epsilon_{i,j,k}; g(t) = sum_l delta_l B((t-d_l)/theta); b_{k,v}(z) = C(k,nu) z^nu (1-z)^{k-nu}

claim: Errors are positively skewed with the right tail (worse-than-expected) much heavier than the left tail (left tail close to normal) -- elites rarely massively overperform their optimum but can underperform via illness/injury/execution, mapping to NFL injuries and motivating skew-t errors for form predictions; the population age curve is reverse-J (rapid improvement 15-20, peak around 24, slow decline; age of peak typically 23-28), and athletes replicate their seasonal peaking patterns through training (Gamma_i shifted left of Delta_i); caveat: no out-of-sample forecasting was demonstrated -- all findings are in-sample posterior descriptions.

Bivariate Poisson conditionals (BPC) distribution where both conditionals are Poisson: joint pmf P(X=x,Y=y) = K(lambda1,lambda2,lambda3) * lambda1^x lambda2^y lambda3^{xy}/(x! y!) with X|Y=y ~ Poisson(lambda1 lambda3^y), Y|X=x ~ Poisson(lambda2 lambda3^x), (lambda1,lambda2) > 0, 0 < lambda3 <= 1 -- the model admits only negative correlation (lambda3 = 1 is independence), so the corpus verdict is REJECT because the negative-only dependence matches no NFL paired-count quantity (home/away points are near-independent to weakly positive); methodological warnings: 4.75%-17% of simulation runs produced negative variance estimates from the observed Fisher information (fragile asymptotics -- do not trust observed-FIM CIs for count-model parameters without bootstrap validation), and no out-of-sample predictive evaluation exists anywhere in the paper.
equation: P(X=x,Y=y) = K(lambda1,lambda2,lambda3) * lambda1^x lambda2^y lambda3^{xy}/(x! y!)

claim: GNNRank unsupervised framework for global rankings from pairwise comparisons: a directed GNN (DIMPA or Inception Block) embeds the directed comparison graph, embeddings are converted to a learned similarity S_ij = exp(-||z_j - z_i||^2_2/(sigma^2 d)) and Laplacian L = D - S, and a Fiedler-style ranking is computed as min_r r^T L r subject to ||r||^2_2 = 1 and r^T 1 = 0, orthogonal-Q rotated to a sphere constraint and unfolded into differentiable projected/proximal-gradient steps (default Gamma = 5 steps; convergence theorem: if the Fiedler vector is a strict local minimizer and 0 < alpha < 1/(4(n-1)), Algorithm 1 converges locally uniformly); trained end-to-end on differentiable upset losses L_upset,ratio = ||T-tilde - M||^2_F/t(M) and L_upset,margin = sum_ij (M_ij + |M_ij|) ReLU(r_j - r_i + epsilon)/t(M) with default margin epsilon = 0.01.
equation: S_ij = exp(-||z_j - z_i||^2_2/(sigma^2 d)); L = D - S; min_r r^T L r s.t. ||r||^2_2 = 1, r^T 1 = 0; L_upset,ratio = ||T-tilde - M||^2_F/t(M); L_upset,margin = sum_ij (M_ij + |M_ij|) ReLU(r_j - r_i + epsilon)/t(M)

claim: On 78 real-world digraphs (NCAA basketball 1985-2014, EPL 2009-2014, tennis, finance), GNNRank-P averaged upset losses (in-sample -- the paper's decisive caveat is that every real-data edge is used for unsupervised fitting AND in-sample evaluation, so numbers are ranking reconstruction, not forward prediction): Basketball 0.73 vs SpringRank 0.78 vs BTL 0.91; Football 0.78 vs SpringRank 0.91; a 1985-trained proximal model applied inductively to other seasons achieved L_upset,simple = 0.75 +- 0.02 vs season-specific retraining 0.74 +- 0.00 (near-parity transfer); on ERO synthetic graphs Kendall tau degrades smoothly with noise (sparse, uniform, eta = 0.1: 0.79; eta = 0.3: 0.70) and dense graphs recover truth much better than sparse ones; directed GNNs beat a two-layer MLP by ~2%.

Any GNNRank port must use strict time-forward walk-forward training (never in-sample upset fitting) and be judged only on held-out future-game log-loss/Brier/ATS with a Platt-style calibration layer mapping score gaps to win probabilities (acceptance gate: log-loss beats best baseline by >= 0.005 nats/game, Brier >= 0.002 better, ATS >= 52.4% over n >= 500 picks, ECE within 0.01 of baseline); the proximal refinement component ('proximal baseline') refines any arbitrary baseline ranking vector r' (e.g., dynamic Elo), with the largest gains observed when refining SyncRank-style initializations (improvement 1.02 on avg L_upset,simple).

Item Response Theory diagnoses classifier benchmarks: 3PL IRT P(U_ij=1|theta_j) = c_i + (1-c_i)/(1 + e^{-a_i(theta_j-b_i)}) with theta_j classifier ability, b_i item difficulty, a_i discrimination, c_i guessing; True-Score = sum_i P(correct) per classifier per dataset; Glicko-2 round-robin tournaments summarize pairwise True-Score comparisons into a global rating R with deviation RD and volatility sigma (rating interval [R-2RD, R+2RD] ~ 95% CI; defaults R = 1500, RD = 350, sigma = 0.06); standard cutoffs: difficult if b_i > 1, highly discriminating if a_i > 0.75, high guessing if c_i > 0.2 -- the corpus ADAPT transfer is treating historical game-weeks as items and engine model versions as respondents, ranking versions by difficulty-adjusted ability instead of raw accuracy.

On OpenML-CC18 (60 evaluated datasets): 49 of 60 (81.67%) have < 27% difficult instances and only ~7 have > 50% difficult, while 31/60 have >= 80% very-discriminating instances -- difficulty and discrimination are inversely related (hardest datasets least discriminating; most discriminating easiest), so a single benchmark cannot simultaneously stress models and rank them; Glicko-2 final ratings were optimal 1732.56, MLP 1718.65, RF 1626.60, RF(5) 1606.69 -- but MLP sits within RD range of 3rd/4th place and the top-3 do not statistically differ (Nemenyi heatmap; Friedman p ~= 9.36e-80), so the 'MLP wins' headline overstates separability; negative-discrimination instances (weak classifiers score higher) corrupt True-Scores and must be quarantined or removed (adoption gate: reject the IRT layer if > 10% of games show negative discrimination).

Continuous-time Gaussian-process skill model (KDD '19) generalizing Elo/TrueSkill (recovered as a Wiener-kernel special case): score process s_m(t) ~ GP[0, k_m(t,t')] (eq. 1) with composable kernels -- constant (offset), piecewise-constant (discontinuities across seasons), Wiener (Brownian), Matern(nu) (nu = 1/2 is mean-reverting Brownian), linear (trends) -- and likelihoods ordinal probit/logit (win/loss/tie), Gaussian on point difference, Poisson-exp on points scored (Maher 1982); variational inference with mean-field factorization converges in < 100 linear-time iterations, embarrassingly parallel (7M chess observations at ~5 s/iteration on 16 threads).

Prequential log-loss / accuracy (Table 3) on ATP tennis 0.552/0.714 (Affine+Wiener) vs Elo 0.563/0.705, TrueSkill 0.563/0.705; NBA 0.630/0.645 (Constant+Matern 1/2) vs Elo 0.634/0.644; world football 0.926/0.558 vs Elo 0.950/0.551, TrueSkill 0.937/0.554; chess 1.026/0.474 vs Elo 1.035/0.447 -- GP wins or ties everywhere but gains over Elo are modest (0.004-0.024 log-loss); learned dynamic timescales are 1.75 years for basketball (volatile) vs 7.47 years for tennis (stable); likelihood ablation: Gaussian on point differential best for NBA (0.627 vs 0.630), Poisson-exp best for football (0.922 vs 0.926) -- using the score beats using only the outcome; learned home advantage cuts football log-loss 0.926 -> 0.900 and accuracy 0.558 -> 0.579.

Uncertainty-aware target sampling for noisy labels: train on standardized labels mu_i = (r_i - 1516)/543 with y_i ~ N(mu_i, phi_i^2) clipped to [mu_i - 3 phi_i, mu_i + 3 phi_i] where phi_i = RD_i/543 encodes per-sample label reliability (most chess-puzzle RDs in [80, 90], infrequently-solved puzzles RD > 200) -- this sampling-based target augmentation served as sufficient regularization with no dropout or weight decay needed; evaluation uses MAZ = (1/N) sum |r_i - r-hat_i|/RD_i (error normalized by per-sample label uncertainty) alongside MAE and Accuracy-within-kRD = (1/N) sum 1(|r_i - r-hat_i| <= k*RD_i) for k = 1,2,3.
equation: y_i ~ N(mu_i, phi_i^2) clipped to [mu_i - 3 phi_i, mu_i + 3 phi_i]; MAZ = (1/N) sum |r_i - r-hat_i|/RD_i

claim: On 4.2M Lichess puzzles, Factorized Encoder GlickFormer achieved test MAE 217.71 vs ChessFormer baseline 227.00 (-9.29 rating points, ~4.1% relative), Factorized Self-Attention 221.80; accuracy within 1RD/2RD/3RD was 27.00%/50.45%/67.66% vs baseline 25.42%/48.21%/65.29% -- meaning 73% of best-model predictions miss the label's own 1-sigma band (MAE 217.71 vs label std 543); competition placement 11th in IEEE BigData 2024 Cup with an unexplained >2x gap between preliminary and final test MSE (75,995 vs 158,292); the spatio-temporal transformer architecture is domain-locked to chess boards (rejected for porting), only the uncertainty machinery transfers.

Smolgen learnable per-square attention bias in the ChessFormer spatial backbone: A^(j) = Q^(j)(K^(j))^T/sqrt(d_k) + B^(j) where B^(j) in R^{64x64} is derived from chess-movement topology rather than Euclidean distance; training used Mish activation f(x) = x*tanh(ln(1+e^x)), d = 256, h = 16 heads, 28,000 steps, RMSprop, lr 1e-6, batch 4096 -- Adam or higher learning rates collapsed to predicting the dataset mean with zero variance.

Pre-game Twitter supporter sentiment in the 6 hours before kickoff predicts soccer upsets: potential-upset score PU(g) = (O^g_max - 1)/(O^g_min - 1) (games with PU(g) > theta = 5 are 'potential upsets'); marginal profit P = (r - b)/b (paper equation 3, r = total payoff, b = total staked); a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier on per-team mood features over 56 potential-upset games (25 World Cup + 31 live-monitoring, 2014) reported World Cup accuracy 0.7898 / AUROC 0.7286 and live accuracy 0.8363 / AUROC 0.7887, with a 100-round betting simulation ($1 per test game) averaging 8.57% marginal profit vs 8.43% for the odds-reshuffled control while all four fixed strategies lost money.

Everything in the Twitter-upset paper rests on n = 56 potential upsets with stratified 3-fold cross-validation inside the same 56-game pool (optimism inherited); bookmaker margins and stake limits were ignored; the control profit of 8.43% vs reported 8.57% shows the headline is fragile; the NFL has no draws so the paper's $0.50 underdog + $0.50 draw stake split needs redesigning; the corpus ADOPT bar is a strict out-of-sample pilot: X/Reddit NFL team-community sentiment in the 6 hours before kickoff (2022-2023 train, locked 2024 test), mood-divergence classifier vs upset, adopted only if locked-test AUROC >= 0.60 with positive flat-stake profit.

Two-stage NFL pass-completion framework on Next Gen Stats tracking data (Big Data Bowl 2021, 2018 season): Stage 1 identifies the pass target frame-by-frame via inverse-distance weighting P_k(T=i|j) = 1/[d^(k)_ij * sum_i (d^(k)_ij)^-1] (Eq. 7) combined via frame weight f(W) = W*P_1 + (1-W)*P_2 (Eq. 8), with four adaptive weights W^(1..4) from order statistics of the closest player's distance metrics and a logistic blend W^(2,3)_t = 1/(1 + e^{(13.34183-t)/2.57}) (Eq. 13) with inflection at mean 13.34 frames and scale 2.57 via grid search (W^(2) early -> W^(3) late); Stage 2 estimates conditional completion probability with a random forest (mtry = 15) on 32 features (13 play data, 3 player data, 16 frame data); marginal completion probability P(C) = sum_i P(C|T=i)*P(T=i) (Eq. 15).

Stage-2 model AUC (10-fold leave-group-out CV, plays as groups): random forest 0.8829 vs binomial logit 0.7874, probit 0.7861, LDA 0.7840, cloglog 0.7814, QDA 0.7487 (RF took 3.88h vs 2 min for logit); target-ID accuracy final 86.92% (vs equal-weight 82.67%); calibration of P(C|T=i) per frame vs completion percent: Pearson 0.998, Lin's concordance 0.998 (per-play averages strictly worse -- frame-by-frame beats play-level aggregation); case studies include a Rodgers-to-Allison 39-yard TD at 62.4% at the catch frame (model higher than NGS's 'most improbable' label on a completed pass) and Brady-to-Gronkowski TD at 28.8% final.

The completion model is real-time computable using only current and past frames (frames filtered to between pass-release and outcome events, x/y only, no ball height, interceptions treated as incompletions, no player-skill priors); authors' own missing-input flags: no ball z-coordinate is the main missing input, no player-skill features (elite and replacement-level receivers get identical geometry), and target-ID errors propagate into P(C); ball-height estimation via a projectile model (release point, catch point, airtime -> launch angle/height) is the stated contested-catch improvement path.

Time-variant Bradley-Terry models on pre-game information for 1,826 AFL games (2015-2023): outcome encoding Y_ijr = 1 if team i beats team j at round r; BT win probability P(Y_ijr = 1) = pi_ir/(pi_ir + pi_jr) with pi_ir = exp(lambda_ir); standard BT logit(P(Y_ijr = 1)) = lambda_i - lambda_j; contest-specific adds home effect logit(P(Y_ijr = 1)) = lambda_i - lambda_j + delta Z (Z = +1/-1 home/away indicator); team-specific time-variant model lambda_ir = sum_{k=1..p} beta_k X_ik + epsilon_i with epsilon_i ~ N(0, sigma^2) iid Gaussian team errors, fit with per-feature 5% significance screening then backward elimination to p < 0.05.
equation: logit(P(Y_ijr = 1)) = lambda_i - lambda_j + delta Z; lambda_ir = sum_{k=1..p} beta_k X_ik + epsilon_i, epsilon_i ~ N(0, sigma^2)

claim: Forward-walk results (train season t, predict t+1): standard BT test accuracy ~60% (single-season windows 57.46%-63.83%; accuracy degrades as training windows lengthen); AT_HOME significant and positive on all data (coefficient 0.29; single seasons 0.08-0.63) with contest-specific BT max test accuracy 67.37% (2022 -> 2023); team-specific time-variant max 69.38% (season-cumulative, train 2019 -> test 2020); round-by-round Incremental strategy best single-season 71.5% (train 2015 -> test 2016); majority voting stable 60%+, up to 67.96%; finals-series prediction weak (3-7 of 9 games); the paper's 'up to 71.5%' headline is a single best-season result with a typical range of ~60-66%, a ~3-8pp lift over plain BT; instability flags: cumulative-wins differential flips sign in some models, and accuracy-only evaluation with a 0.5 threshold provides no log-loss, Brier, or calibration assessment -- the paper's gains justify nothing until a Brier/log-loss gate against Elo and the closing spread is cleared.

Kelly-Index difficulty classification for soccer match prediction (1,140 EPL matches 2019-2021, six European bookmakers): per-outcome per-bookmaker Kelly Index K_H = (O_H/avgO_H)*F_99 (F_99 = payout rate; O_H = bookmaker odds, avgO_H = mean odds across books) with K_D, K_A defined analogously; Type rule: count bookmakers with any K > 1 -- Type 1 (>= 2, easiest), Type 2 (exactly one), Type 3 (none, hardest); per-class classifiers (CatBoost, XGBoost, RF, GB, LR, KNN, DT, stacking, voting) tuned via RandomizedSearchCV with SHAP explainability and expanding-window forecasting validation.

Accuracy by type: Type 1 CatBoost 70.0% (precision 66.6, F1 63.6) vs Type 2 RF 52.7% vs Type 3 RF 41.1% vs all-matches RF 52.0%; SHAP shows Type 1 driven by home historical stats while Type 2/3 driven by bookmaker odds features; naive $1-flat-stake ROI was mostly negative (Type 1: Bet365 -1.1%, Pinnacle +1.4%; Type 2/3: all -3.3% to -6.3%); the only profitable configuration was Type 1 matches with model confidence >= 70% on Pinnacle odds -> final ROI +17% -- but even 'easy' matches rarely exceed 60% model confidence (Type 1 2020 had 0% of matches above 0.7 confidence), so the +17% ROI rests on a small slice; stacking/voting unexpectedly underperformed the single best models; odds features leak market information into 'model' predictions; the corpus ADAPT transfer is a Kelly-style difficulty index across US books per NFL game gating pick publication (easy + engine confidence >= 70% -> full unit, medium -> half unit or pass, hard -> pass).

Selective ensembles (Black, Leino & Fredrikson 2021): with mode predictor g_{P,S}(x) = argmax_y E_{S~S}[1[P(S;x)=y]] (Eq. 1), predict the majority vote only if a two-sided binomial test on the top-2 vote counts rejects a toss-up at level alpha -- if binom_p_value(n_A, n_A+n_B, 0.5) <= alpha return argmax(Y) else ABSTAIN (n_A, n_B = top-2 vote counts) -- with Theorem 4.1: for all x, Pr_{S~S^n}[g-hat_n(P,S;alpha,x) !=_ABS g_{P,S}(x)] <= alpha, plus Corollary 4.2 E_x[V(x)] <= alpha + beta (expected loss-variance bounded by alpha + abstention bound beta) and Corollary 4.3 E_x[Pr[two ensembles disagree]] <= 2(alpha + beta).
equation: if binom_p_value(n_A, n_A+n_B, 0.5) <= alpha return argmax(Y) else ABSTAIN; Pr_{S~S^n}[g-hat_n(P,S;alpha,x) !=_ABS g_{P,S}(x)] <= alpha

claim: Singleton retrained models disagree on up to 57% of test points (German Credit) and typically 5-10% elsewhere, while selective ensembles of n = 10 had zero points with p_flip > 0 across all seven benchmark datasets; abstention at n = 20, alpha = 0.05 was 1.4-3.6% (Adult 2.4%, Seizure 1.4%, Warfarin 3.1%, Taiwanese Credit 2.3%, FMNIST 3.6%, Colon 1.9%) except German Credit 16.5% (tiny dataset, 57% baseline disagreement); n = 5 -> 100% abstention (alpha must be raised for tiny ensembles); selective-ensemble accuracy (abstain as error) stayed within a few points of non-selective ensembles (Adult .830 vs .842); cost is 10-20x training per publish cycle; GSE's season-level samples resemble German Credit (n = 800) more than Adult, so expect higher abstention than the headline 1.5-5% in production.

Metalearning metamodel that predicts BEFORE the forecast is issued whether a global deep forecaster will incur a large error at a given origin, using only structural features of the recent lag window: target u_{i,t} = #{j in T_i: j != t, e_{i,j} < e_{i,t}}/(|T_i|+1) is the per-series empirical percentile rank of error in (0,1) (scale-invariant so the rejection mechanism transfers across domains); errors computed with sMAPE; predictors m_{i,t} = g(X_t^i) are TSFEL statistical/temporal/spectral features of the lag window (trend, seasonality, lumpiness, complexity); metamodel is CatBoostRegressor (30 random-search configs, grouped CV by series); rejection rule u-hat_{i,t} >= q -> abstain at coverage ~= q with q in {0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40}; selective predictor (f,s)(x) = f(x) if s(x) = 1 else bottom, coverage phi(s) = P(s(X) = 1), risk R(f,s) = E[l(f(X),Y) | s(X) = 1).
equation: u_{i,t} = #{j in T_i: j != t, e_{i,j} < e_{i,t}}/(|T_i|+1); (f,s)(x) = f(x) if s(x) = 1 else bottom

claim: Meta-level: in-domain Spearman rho between predicted and realized error percentile 0.71-0.90 with the smallest AUCO (closest to the oracle curve); zero-shot transfer drops (e.g., M3-M -> M1-M KAN 0.628, NHITS 0.571) but domain adaptation (fine-tune on 30% of target origins) recovers (0.820/0.812); base-level (sMAPE kept, domain-adapted): T-M KAN keep-all 0.288 -> 0.215 at q = 0.40 (avg oracle gap 0.033, lowest of all methods; PI-width avg gap 0.089, residual-var 0.093; PI width worse than random near coverage 0.5); the load-bearing lesson is 'uncertainty is not equivalent to forecasting risk: wide intervals do not necessarily imply large errors' -- interval width is a bad proxy for forecast risk; grouped CV by series is load-bearing for the rho numbers (leakage across origins within a series would inflate them); targets are relative risk, not calibrated probabilities.

Inductive (split) conformal prediction: split data 75/25 into proper training and calibration; nonconformity = absolute residual |y_i - y-hat_i|; interval [y-hat(x) - q-hat, y-hat(x) + q-hat] with q-hat the (1-alpha)-quantile of calibration residuals; normalized conformal prediction (NCP): nonconformity = |y_i - y-hat_i|/sigma-hat_i with a dispersion estimate sigma-hat_i, giving interval [mu-hat(x) - sigma-hat(x)*q-hat, mu-hat(x) + sigma-hat(x)*q-hat] whose width adapts per observation; benchmarked against quantile regression averaging (QRA), naive, and empirical-error intervals across a full 144-path factorial (markets x model types x point-predictor choices) on German day-ahead and intraday electricity prices (noisy, heavy-tailed, heteroscedastic), evaluated by empirical coverage (PICP), average width, Winkler score, pinball loss, and Christoffersen conditional-coverage tests.
equation: interval [y-hat(x) - q-hat, y-hat(x) + q-hat]; NCP: [mu-hat(x) - sigma-hat(x)*q-hat, mu-hat(x) + sigma-hat(x)*q-hat], nonconformity |y_i - y-hat_i|/sigma-hat_i

claim: NCP is equal or better than QRA, naive, and empirical-error intervals depending on market regime but no single configuration dominates -- the optimal point predictor, normalization, and split are market-dependent; coverage targets are met (PICP ~= nominal) while Winkler and pinball scores favor NCP in the heteroscedastic intraday regime where normalization matters most; stated limitations: a random 75/25 split on time series risks leakage (ordered data needs a rolling/expanding window); exchangeability is false under structural breaks (market rule changes in power; injuries/coaching changes in NFL) -- the paper's own #1 failure mode; calibration eats 25-50% of data (expensive at ~272 games/season); intervals are symmetric only (blowout vs defensive-slugfest tails differ); the corpus ADAPT is a normalized-nonconformity option in the interval layer (sigma-hat = per-game dispersion like recent total-volatility) with rolling-window calibration run per market.

On 292M trades across ~327K binary contracts on Kalshi + Polymarket (note: the abstract claims '353 million trades across 429,000 binary contracts' but the paper body reports 292M/327K -- the abstract appears to describe an earlier sample), prediction-market calibration is a structured function of domain x time-to-resolution x trade size, not domain-agnostic: cell-level logistic recalibration logit(P(y_i=1)) = a + b*logit(p_i) with logit(x) = log{x/(1-x)}, fit by MLE (L2 C = 10), where slope b is the calibration measure (b = 1 calibrated; b > 1 underconfident, compressed toward 50%, favourite-longshot bias; b < 1 overconfident, too extreme); additive decomposition theta(d,tau,s) = mu(tau) + alpha_d + beta_d(tau) + gamma_d(s) + eps with sum-to-zero constraints; variance decomposition: universal horizon mu 30.2%, domain intercept alpha 14.6%, domain x horizon beta 26.0%, domain x size gamma 16.5% (total R^2 = 0.873, adjusted 0.810); 216 cells = 6 domains x 9 horizon bins x 4 size bins.
equation: logit(P(y_i=1)) = a + b*logit(p_i); p* = sigma(theta-hat*logit(p)) = p^theta-hat/(p^theta-hat+(1-p)^theta-hat)

claim: The recalibration transform p* = sigma(theta-hat*logit(p)) = p^theta-hat/(p^theta-hat+(1-p)^theta-hat) extremises when theta-hat > 1 and moderates when theta-hat < 1 (example: p = 0.70, theta-hat ~= 1.83 for politics 1 week out -> p* ~= 0.83); the universal horizon effect has cell-mean mu(tau) rising from 0.99 (0-1h) to 1.32 (1mo+) -- prices are roughly calibrated close to the event but drift underconfident (favourite-longshot bias) far out -- and Kalshi Sports slopes by horizon are 1.10/0.96/0.90/1.01/1.05/1.08/1.04/1.24/1.74; Bayesian domain intercepts: Politics +0.151, Sports +0.010, Weather -0.086, Entertainment -0.085; the politics trade-size effect (Large 1.74 vs Single 1.19, Delta = +0.53, 95% bootstrap CI [0.29, 0.75]) is platform-specific to Kalshi -- Sports Delta = +0.07 (null) and Polymarket politics Delta = +0.11 (not significant) -- so it does not replicate cross-platform; temporal stability of the decomposition is untested ('an open question').

The PART (Predictive Athlete Readiness for Tennis) framework fuses wearable physiology, self-report questionnaires, workload, vertical-jump assessments, and match-video motion analysis into an Athlete Readiness Score: ARS_initial = w1*Wellness + w2*(1-InjuryRisk) + w3*PhysicalCapability with weights learned by multiple linear regression against expert-consensus ARS labels (0-100), then a playing-style aggressiveness penalty: w_style in {1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6} by ASP quartile (ASP <= 5 -> 1.0; 5 < ASP <= 8 -> 1.2; 8 < ASP <= 12 -> 1.4; ASP > 12 -> 1.6) and ARS_final = ARS_initial/w_style -- defensive grinders get readiness discounted for higher cumulative load exposure; four sub-models: XGBoost classifier (injury probability, upper/lower body variants), XGBoost regressor (Recovery Score %), MLP and LSTM on temporal physiological sequences (physical capability), computer-vision motion analysis on match video (playing-style aggressiveness).
equation: ARS_initial = w1*Wellness + w2*(1-InjuryRisk) + w3*PhysicalCapability; ARS_final = ARS_initial/w_style

claim: PART results on 9 collegiate tennis players (Monmouth University, WHOOP wearables): XGBoost wellness regressor best -- MAE 3.82, R^2 0.838 vs linear-regression baseline MAE 14.05, R^2 0.009; injury risk XGBoost best -- AUC-ROC 0.695, accuracy 0.852, F1 0.100 (logistic regression F1 0.000) -- the file holds this up as honest reporting of weak rare-event classification setting the bar for credible injury-model evaluation; LSTM beats MLP on physical capability (validation loss 0.6059 vs 0.6391); limitations: n = 9 athletes, no player-wise holdout reported (temporal leakage possible), ARS labels are subjective expert consensus; the w_style exposure penalty ports to NFL as a cumulative-hit-exposure discount for dual-threat/rushing QBs and bellcow RBs.

Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging (iQRA) turns a sorted point-forecast ensemble into predictive quantiles by imposing nonnegativity on the quantile-regression slope coefficients (stochastic-order regularization): Q-hat(tau) = beta_0 + beta^T p-hat, beta fitted by pinball-loss linear programming with all slope coefficients constrained >= 0 (beta_i = beta_i^+ - beta_i^-; drop all beta_i^- from the LP), cutting LP complexity from O-tilde(2MT + T^2.5) to O-tilde(MT + T^2.5) -- a hyperparameter-free alternative to Lasso-QRA with statistically indistinguishable accuracy at 30x the speed; pinball loss (1[P < P-hat^tau] - tau)(P-hat^tau - P); PIPS(alpha) = 1/2 PS(alpha/2) + 1/2 PS(1-alpha/2); CRPS ~= average pinball over 99 percentiles; reliability by ACE(alpha) = empirical coverage - nominal coverage and TB = right-tail miss rate - left-tail miss rate.
equation: Q-hat(tau) = beta_0 + beta^T p-hat, beta_i >= 0; pinball (1[P < P-hat^tau] - tau)(P-hat^tau - P)

claim: On German day-ahead electricity prices (8 Jan 2015 - 31 Dec 2024; 25 NARX neural networks as the point ensemble; 1,833-day out-of-sample test from 1 Jan 2020 covering COVID and the Ukraine invasion): PIPS at 98% -- iQRA 0.781 vs LQRA 0.788 (best at 98%), LQRA slightly better at 96/90/80% -- with iQRA-LQRA differences insignificant per the Giacomini-White CPA test while iQRA significantly beats QRA, QRM, CP, HS, and IDR at all levels; compute per forecast day: iQRA 20 s vs LQRA 600 s (30x faster), CP/HS 1 ms, QRM 10 s; CRPS 2024 iQRA 7.482 vs LQRA 7.492 (iQRA significantly better); iQRA selects 14.2% of regressors vs 12.3% for LQRA, and ensemble extremes (min for low quantiles, max for high quantiles) are selected far more often than middle members -- tail quantiles are driven by extreme ensemble members, which matters since tail quantiles drive bet-sizing decisions.

Game-theoretic 'Skeptic' framework that systematically exploits a miscalibrated probability forecaster: capital K_n = product_{i=1}^{n} (1 + nu_i(x_i - p_i)) (Eq. 1); Kelly-optimal stake fraction nu_n = (p-hat_n - p_n)/(p_n(1-p_n)) = p-hat_n/p_n - (1-p-hat_n)/(1-p_n) (Eq. 2), maximizing E_{p-hat_n}[log(1+nu(x_n-p_n))]; capital as likelihood ratio (Eq. 3) K_n = product p-hat_i^{x_i}(1-p-hat_i)^{1-x_i} / product p_i^{x_i}(1-p_i)^{1-x_i}; logistic correction log(p-hat_n/(1-p-hat_n)) = log(p_n/(1-p_n)) + theta' c_n (Eq. 5) with p-hat_n = p_n e^{theta' c_n}/[1 + p_n(e^{theta' c_n}-1)] (Eq. 6) and K_n^theta = e^{theta' sum c_i x_i}/product(1 + p_i(e^{theta' c_i}-1)) (Eq. 7); Bayesian strategy with prior pi(theta) positive near origin -> K_n^pi = integral K_n^theta pi(theta) d theta (universal-portfolio-style mixture); auxiliary S_n = sum c_i(x_i-p_i), V_n = sum c_i c_i' p_i(1-p_i).
equation: K_n = product_{i=1}^{n} (1 + nu_i(x_i - p_i)); nu_n = (p-hat_n - p_n)/(p_n(1-p_n)); log(p-hat_n/(1-p-hat_n)) = log(p_n/(1-p_n)) + theta' c_n; p-hat_n = p_n e^{theta' c_n}/[1 + p_n(e^{theta' c_n}-1)]

claim: Against the Japan Meteorological Agency's Tokyo precipitation forecasts (2009-2011, ~1,096 days): JMA 'tends to be closer to 50% than the actual ratio' -- announces 20% when the actual rain rate is 11.1% and 80% when actual is 90.0% (avoids clear-cut forecasts), with hindsight beta ~= 1.5 on announced log-odds; the capital process 'works very well against JMA' (figure-only, no exact final capital or drawdown numbers) but shows seasonal fluctuation and performs poorly in the June-July rainy season -- regime-dependence of the correctable bias; caveats: beta prior tuned with hindsight (Uniform[0,2] chosen because hindsight beta ~= 1.5 -- data snooping on the hyperparameter), Kelly fractions explode near p_n -> 0/1 with no stake cap, and bookmakers adapt while JMA does not.

Kelly betting as Bayesian model evaluation: each candidate forecast model is a Kelly bettor wagering its bankroll on its own time-updating probabilities against market-implied probabilities, using terminal bankroll share to discriminate correct from misspecified models -- separating models far earlier than log loss or Brier; bankroll update w_i' = (p_i/m_i) * sum_i m_i w_i (wealth compounds by the likelihood ratio of model vs market); market probability = eigenvector of the outer product p*w^T, model credibility = eigenvector of w^T*p (mutual-consistency fixed point between market prices and model wealths); Kelly-optimal growth equals Bayesian evidence accumulation (log bankroll = cumulative log-likelihood ratio); assumes models bet fractionally at market prices with no limits or costs and a coherent market probability observable and bettable at every update (false in thin live markets).

Correct-model identification rates (simulation of a volleyball-like first-to-100 contest): correct 0.50 vs incorrect 0.53 -- Kelly 55.1% vs log loss 49.9% vs Brier 49.9%; correct 0.53 vs incorrect 0.50 -- Kelly 76.3% vs log loss 80.5% vs Brier 80.5%; faulty recency model -- Kelly 96.0% vs log loss 73.1% vs Brier 80.2%; noise-variable model -- Kelly 74.4% vs log loss 57.6% vs Brier 58.3%; across 110 probability-pair scenarios after 5 games Kelly wins 98 (89%), ties 1, loses 11, and after 50 games wins 61, ties 47, loses 2 -- Kelly dominates early and stays competitive late, with the largest edge against structurally misspecified models (recency, noise); near-indistinguishable models (55.1% barely above chance) show the method separates the structurally wrong, not the slightly-worse-calibrated; the corpus ADAPT is a Kelly-tournament evaluator with notional bankrolls per candidate live win-probability model, auto-promoting dominating challengers over rolling windows.

Multi-modal Attention Network (MMAN) for 5-day stock movements fuses social-media text with numeric price history: text via Deep Averaging Network with flatten into C^s in R^{n x d}, social-impact features via Linear into A^e in R^{n x d}, price history via 3D-CNNpred into H in R^{n x d}; Transformer encoder with time-based positional encoding using relative post-time dispersion PE(t,2i) = sin(t/c^{2i/d}), PE(t,2i+1) = cos(t/c^{2i/d}), c = 10000; credibility fusion C = TransDecoder(A^e_q, A^e_k, C^e_v) with social-impact features as queries/keys and encoded text as values; inter-attention H^{itv} = softmax(H_q C_k^T/sqrt(d)) C_v (eq. 14) with channel gates G_H = sigma(Linear(Avg_Pool(C^{itd}))) and H-hat^{itd}_q = (1+G_H) dot H^{itd}_q; margin loss Loss_k = Y_k max(0, m^+ - ||Y-hat_k||)^2 + lambda(1-Y_k) max(0, ||Y-hat_k|| - m^-)^2 with lambda = 0.5, m^+ = 0.9, m^- = 0.1, total = sum Loss_k + 0.0005(FM - Re(Y-hat))^2.
equation: PE(t,2i) = sin(t/c^{2i/d}), PE(t,2i+1) = cos(t/c^{2i/d}); Loss_k = Y_k max(0, m^+ - ||Y-hat_k||)^2 + lambda(1-Y_k) max(0, ||Y-hat_k|| - m^-)^2

claim: MMAN full accuracy 61.20%/MCC 0.1193 beat best baseline CapTE 59.87%/0.0976 (+1.33pp accuracy); ablations: social-impact credibility features add +1.14pp (60.06% -> 61.20%), history adds +0.74pp (60.46% -> 61.20%), text+history fusion beats either alone; but the paper describes no explicit chronological train/test split (temporal leakage risk -- treat 61.20% as optimistic), the corpus is Chinese-language (Xueqiu), dropping samples with |movement| < 0.75% flatters accuracy, the trading window is 3 months, and the abstract's claimed 9.13% trading profits are not reconcilable with Table 3's dollar figures -- so the corpus ADAPT is only for two transferable ideas (credibility-weighted social-text attention; time-dispersion positional encoding), not the stock pipeline wholesale.

On 2,770 traders on the Almanis prediction-market platform (Dec 2015 - May 2017), information enters prices through the amplified flow of a few price-sensitive ('informed') traders ('wisdom IN the crowd'), not through crowd averaging: per-trader price-sensitivity regression Delta p_i(t_i+1) = alpha_i + beta_i(p_0(t_i+1) - p_{m,i}(t_i)) + eps(t_i) (eq. 2), where traders with t-stat < -1.65 on beta_i are labeled price-sensitive/informed -- Kyle (1985) predicts informed traders show negative (reverting) price sensitivity, while positive sensitivity is momentum, not informedness; LMSR market maker p_i(q) = e^{q_i/B}/sum_j e^{q_j/B} with B = 150.
equation: Delta p_i(t_i+1) = alpha_i + beta_i(p_0(t_i+1) - p_{m,i}(t_i)) + eps(t_i); p_i(q) = e^{q_i/B}/sum_j e^{q_j/B}

claim: Price-sensitive traders' trades add information while others' trades destroy it: Delta AUC (offer price p_0 vs final marginal price p_m vs settlement) was PS +0.0394 [+0.0196,+0.0592] vs non-PS -0.0026 for days-to-EOS [0,5), and PS +0.0376 [+0.0244,+0.0508] vs non-PS -0.0119 [-0.0208,-0.0030] for [30,infinity) -- larger minimum price impact gives larger PS gains and larger non-PS losses, reproduced on all four external replication datasets; markets with 2-3 or 4+ price-sensitive traders converge significantly faster and better than 0/1-PS markets (p < 0.001 at every horizon 14 -> 1 days before settlement); mean 3.06 price-sensitive traders per market (7.3% of traders); informedness is NOT a persistent trait -- 75% of traders are price-sensitive in fewer markets than the mean, and the most PS trader was PS in 64 markets but non-PS in 42 (expertise is topic-specific, so do not assume NFL-sharp flow is NBA-sharp); detection blind spot: when prices are already good, informed traders have no incentive to trade, so 'no PS traders' can mean 'no informed' OR 'too many informed'.

Bayesian generalization of Bradley-Terry separating two failure modes of standard BT -- an irreducible upset floor alpha and a competition-depth parameter beta: f_{alpha beta}(s) = alpha/2 + (1-alpha)/(1+exp(-beta s)) where s is the score difference, alpha in [0,1] the irreducible upset/luck probability ('coin-flip floor'), beta > 0 the depth of competition (steepness of the skill curve, interpretable as the number of ~73%-win skill levels spanning a typical pair); priors s_i ~ N(0, 1/2), alpha ~ Uniform(0,1), beta ~ HalfCauchy^+(0, 4); posterior sampling via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo in Stan; model comparison by 20%-holdout cross-validation, >= 50 repetitions per model per dataset.

The full luck+depth model was best or tied-best by held-out log-likelihood on EVERY one of 15 sport/game/social-hierarchy datasets (within reported uncertainty), beating BT MLE, logistic-prior BT, depth-only, luck-only, and SpringRank; posterior-mean depth ordering: Scrabble beta = 0.68 < NBA 1.01 < chess 1.17 < tennis 1.44 < soccer 1.73 < video games 1.77 -- a quantitative ordering of competition depth; authors' own identifiability warning: alpha and beta are confounded in shallow competitions, hardest to separate exactly where most informative; caveats: random (non-chronological) holdouts measure interpolation not forecasting, and no sportsbook odds, calibration, CLV, or betting-return test appears anywhere.

Descriptive + null-model study of 4,418 men's ODI cricket matches (1971-March 2024, 2,863 players, howstat.com): era normalization nf = <Team runs>_all/<Team runs>_year multiplies runs scored/conceded (borrowed from citation normalization); fractional contribution fc = 1/2*(runs scored/total team runs + wickets taken/total team wickets) in [0,1] (specialists capped at 0.5); effective team size S_eff = 2^H with H = -sum_c fc log_2 fc (entropy of the contribution distribution); null models shuffle performance timestamps 100x per player for hot streaks and match-result timestamps 10^4x holding win count for team streaks.
equation: nf = <Team runs>_all/<Team runs>_year; fc = 1/2*(runs scored/total team runs + wickets taken/total team wickets); S_eff = 2^H, H = -sum_c fc log_2 fc

claim: Hot streaks: Delta N/N in [0, 0.2) ratio > 1 (Wilcoxon p < 0.001) -- best performances genuinely cluster in time vs the shuffled null; drop/re-entry: ~19% decline over the 5 matches pre-drop, then post-return +36% (batsmen) / +30% (bowlers) vs the final pre-drop match, and the gains persist; captaincy: 172 captains -- captain-batsmen avg 31 vs 26 runs (+16%), captain-bowlers 0.96 vs 1.13 wickets (-18%), MWU p < 0.001 (batsmen rise during captaincy, bowlers fall, both decline post-captaincy); team streaks: P(7+ straight wins) = 9x chance, P(7+ straight losses) = 3x chance vs 10^4 shuffled nulls; winning teams' median S_eff ~= 6.9 vs 6.6 for losers (+4%, p < 0.001, r = 0.56) -- balanced contributions win; early-to-full-career R^2 = 0.45 (batsmen), 0.66 (bowlers), and the random-impact rule (peak can occur anywhere in a career) held, K-S vs null p > 0.05.

Nine simple behavioral features (strategy, goals, expertise -- not outcomes) predict battle-royale ranks better than Elo, Glicko, and TrueSkill using a trivially simple single-feature sort predictor Phi = arg sort_{i in {1..n}}((F,p_i)|beta) -- sort players by one feature (descending; ascending for rank ratio), ties random, no learning at all: beta1 games played (experience), beta2 kill/death ratio, beta3 firing accuracy = sum kills/sum damage, beta4 survive ratio = sum time_survived/#games, beta5/6 walking/riding ratio = sum distance/#games, beta7/8 walking/riding velocity = sum distance/sum time_survived, beta9 rank ratio = sum rank_percentile/#games -- on >75,000 PUBG solo matches (1.7M unique players), features computed from pre-match history only (chronological online prediction).

Average %NDCG (Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill vs Phi): All Players 56.8/56.2/57.4 with rank ratio beta9 = 61.3 best overall and K/D (60.1), survive ratio (59.7), walking (58.6), riding (58.5) all beating the best system; Top-tier 73.7/62.4/79.1 with rank ratio 85.1 best and survive ratio 79.4 edging TrueSkill's 79.1; Frequent 59.3/63.8/57.9 with games played beta1 = 86.4% -- highest of any model in any setup, beating the best system (Glicko 63.8) by 22.6 points; the transferable lesson is that input-side engineering (what you feed the model) matters more than the rating algorithm; limitations: PUBG solo only, single-feature models, no significance tests, ties broken randomly with unquantified noise.

Every NFL tackle gets a value -- Prevented Expected Points (PEP) -- by computing the counterfactual end-of-play yard-line density with the tackler removed from the tracking frame: PEP = E[g(Y)|x_removed] - g(y_0) (eq. 3, used for player evaluation) where y_0 is the observed end-of-play yard line, with the alternative PEP_alt = E[g(Y)|x_removed] - E[g(Y)|x_0] (eq. 4, conditional treatment effect); the conditional density of EOPY is a random forest regression (N = 1000 trees, R ranger defaults, untuned) with tree predictions treated as samples from the conditional density (non-parametric, captures multi-modality and heteroscedasticity), trained on 8 weeks / held out 1 week across nine folds; EP model EP = E[Y|X] = sum_y y*P(Y=y|X) with y in {-7, -3, -2, 0, 2, 3, 7} via XGBoost multi-class trained on 2011-2021 play-by-play (evaluated 2022) achieving MAE 3.6391 vs Carl & Baldwin's 3.6395 (on par); player strength via GAMLSS mixed-effects PEP_i ~ SST(mu_i, sigma, nu, tau) (4-param skew-t selected by wormplots) with mu_i = x_i beta + T_it + B_ib + O_io (random intercepts for tackler, ball carrier, offensive team) and uncertainty via 1,000 bootstrap samples resampling full drives.
equation: PEP = E[g(Y)|x_removed] - g(y_0); PEP_alt = E[g(Y)|x_removed] - E[g(Y)|x_0); EP = E[Y|X] = sum_y y*P(Y=y|X)

claim: RF out-of-sample EOPY RMSE 5.74, MAE 3.13 ('similar to existing approaches'); example play: true EOPY = 12-yard line -> EP 5.41, hypothetical (tackler removed) density mass in end zone -> mean EP 6.2, PEP = 0.79; cumulative PEP top 20 dominated by ILB/LB and safeties (a CB at 21.685 on 28 tackles, Bobby Okereke ILB 20.369 on 63, Ryan Neal SS 20.300 on 25, Adrian Amos FS 20.179 on 31, Tremaine Edmunds ILB 19.035 on 47, Derwin James FS 18.625 on 55); position finding: ILB/SS highest cumulative PEP (tackle most), DE/NT/DT low cumulative PEP (misses remediated by others), but on AVERAGE PEP defensive backs (CB/SS/FS) overtake ILBs -- with the authors' explicit caveat that CBs can generate PEP by allowing a catch then tackling (rewards last line of defense, not coverage quality); mixed-model top-10 ILB (bootstrap medians) includes the top-3 2022 tackles leaders Nick Bolton, Foyesade Oluokun, Jordyn Brooks; authors' own gaps: missed tackles are NOT punished (only real tackles scored), run/pass conflated in the main model, counterfactual validity caveat (removing the tackler != a real missed tackle -- other defenders' reactions change), no comparison to existing tackling metrics (no demonstrated incremental value over stops or PFF grades).

NBA season win percentage as a systematic predictor of point-spread cover rate (1990-91 to 2015-16, 24-season train + 2-season test), testing whether extreme win-% teams escape the house edge: running average cover-side H-bar_Cpct = (1/T_Hw) sum_{i=0}^{T_Hw-1} t_c(t_Hw - i) where t_c = team cover %, starting at the highest-win% team (mirror formula for the no-cover side from the lowest-win% team); note the paper defines house edge as 2.54% around 50% (i.e., -110 odds) and reports 'profit' as deviation from 50%, NOT actual bankroll ROI -- true -110 breakeven is 52.38%, so reported profits are overstated ~2.4pp in absolute terms, a calibration-honesty flag; reported 'correlation' W/L<->C/N ~= 0.2 is computed nonstandardly as 'proportion of extreme outliers', not Pearson.

Training cumulative deviation sums: no-cover side (12 worst teams) sum = 15.92% (best cell: most-losing team 44.68% cover -> 2.92% deviation); cover side (12 best teams) sum = 13.35% (best cell: most-winning team 55.48% -> 3.08%); test set 2014-15/2015-16 (ex-ante rule, 3 worst / 2 best): worst teams no-cover 44.44% (3.16%), 43.64% (3.96%), 45.25% (2.35%) -> sum = 9.47%, best teams cover 57.14% (4.74%), 57.61% (5.21%) -> sum = 9.95%; over/under shows no systematic edge (high-win% teams go under ~= 1.3% more, low-win% teams over ~= 1.2% more, both inside the house-edge band); zero significance tests, no confidence intervals, tiny test sample, extreme cutoffs selected retrospectively on training data (circular, partially mitigated by the 2-season holdout); the file's bottom line is that lines are shaded toward elite/popular teams, so extreme bad teams carry contrarian ATS value -- worth testing on NFL/CFB with proper binomial CIs per implied-win% decile.

Abstention based solely on epistemic uncertainty (uncertainty from limited data) minimizing expected regret vs the Bayes-optimal predictor: Theorem 1 -- the minimizer of Bayesian expected regret-based reject loss R_B^delta(Q) is Q_E(x,D) = H_B(x,D) if E(x,D) <= delta, else reject, where conditional regret E(x,D) = E_{(theta,y)~p(theta,y|x,D)}[l(y,H_B(x,D)) - l(y,h(x,theta))]; uncertainty decomposition T(x,D) = A(x,D) + E(x,D) (total = aleatoric + epistemic) with A(x,D) = E[l(y,h(x,theta))] the expected conditional risk under the posterior; closed forms: squared loss -- E = Var_{theta~p(theta|D)}[E_{y~p(y|x,theta)}[y]], T = Var_{y~p(y|x,D)}[y]; 0/1 loss -- E = E_theta[max_y p(y|x,theta)] - max_y p(y|x,D), T = 1 - max_y p(y|x,D); cross-entropy -- E = E_theta[D_KL(p(y|x,theta) || p(y|x,D))] (the Depeweg et al. 2018 mutual-information measure, here derived as optimal rather than postulated).
equation: Q_E(x,D) = H_B(x,D) if E(x,D) <= delta, else reject; T(x,D) = A(x,D) + E(x,D); 0/1: E = E_theta[max_y p(y|x,theta)] - max_y p(y|x,D)

claim: Behavioral distinction: the epistemic predictor ACCEPTS high-aleatoric inputs (noisy but well-modeled) and rejects inputs not reliably supported by training data; in synthetic experiments (1-D cubic regression, heteroscedastic noise, 3000 trials) the epistemic predictor achieved the lowest Area-under-Regret-Coverage (AuReC) at every dataset size -- at small m the Bayesian total-uncertainty predictor ~= epistemic (epistemic dominates), at large m the Bayesian converges to the aleatoric-only predictor as epistemic uncertainty vanishes, and the plug-in ML rejector (theta-hat) is consistently worst; limitations: entirely synthetic (no real-world, sports, or classification data), deep-network deployment needs approximations (MC dropout, deep ensembles), and no distribution-free guarantee (model-dependent posterior quantity) -- most valuable exactly where posteriors are hardest to trust (small m).

For OOD setups where test = mixture of ID and OOD (p(x,y-bar) = p_O(x)*pi for y-bar = empty (OOD), p_I(x,y-bar)*(1-pi) for y-bar in Y (Eq. 1)), the cost-based, bounded TPR-FPR, and bounded precision-recall reject models all share the same optimal strategy class: a Bayes ID classifier plus a selective function that is a LINEAR combination of the conditional risk r(x) and the likelihood ratio p_O(x)/p_I(x) of OOD vs ID; the practical double-score method combines one score good at OOD/ID discrimination with one good at misclassification detection (tested: KNN+MSP and VIM+MSP, where MSP is asymptotically the best misclassification detector and KNN/VIM the best OOD discriminators by AUROC).
equation: p(x,y-bar) = p_O(x)*pi for y-bar = empty; optimal selective = linear combination of conditional risk r(x) and likelihood ratio p_O(x)/p_I(x)

claim: On the OpenOOD benchmark (CIFAR-10 as ID, three OOD datasets; selective risk / AUROC / OSCR): MSP 0.00984/0.861/0.973, KNN 0.00665/0.896/0.974, VIM 0.01232/0.872/0.972, KNN+MSP 0.00652/0.896/0.977, VIM+MSP 0.00676/0.879/0.977 -- the double-score combination is consistently best in ALL metrics, and single-score leaders differ by metric (AUROC vs OSCR rankings are reversed, a metric-discipline warning for any no-bet layer); gains are consistent but small in absolute terms (selective risk 0.00665 -> 0.00652); limitations: theory assumes known p_I, p_O (learning the selective function is out of scope) and benchmark OOD fractions (pi > 0.5) are unrealistic; GSE's concrete OOD games named: rookie-QB first starts, extreme weather games, international/travel games, mid-week coaching changes, games with anomalous line movement.

Partial sports-field registration recovers kinematically valid 3D running kinematics from close-up broadcast footage: detect visible lane lines (OpenCV Hough), compute one vanishing point, construct a dense family of candidate camera calibrations consistent with it (1-degree azimuth increments; elevation/roll/FoV solved to match; translation fitted to lane positions; residual 1-DoF per frame resolved via the static-camera constraint across the sequence), then ray-cast lifting -- from ground-contact frames, ray-cast the foot pixel to the ground plane, interpolate ground projection between contacts to define the sagittal plane, cast the pelvis ray onto that plane, then walk the skeleton outward (torso -> limbs), intersecting each joint's camera ray with a sphere of radius = limb length, pruning 2^3 configurations per segment via range-of-motion + frame-to-frame consistency; geometric relations: projection matrix P^C = K^C * (R^C | t^C), joint = ray intersect sphere(limb_len) around the parent joint.
equation: P^C = K^C * (R^C | t^C); joint = ray intersect sphere(limb_len)

claim: On synthetic data (10,571 frames, 31 sequences, Unreal Engine 5 + Mixamo MoCap + MetaHumans), mean reprojection/3D/knee-angle errors: MeTRAbs 6.36 px / 10.33 cm / 20.31 deg, MeTRAbs+rotation 5.01 / 7.92 / 12.41, their method 2.76 / 6.41 / 9.91, their method +context (GT 2D joints + cyclical step-frequency, idealized) 3D 2.44 cm / knee 2.87 deg -- but running literature reports meaningful knee-angle differences of 3-4 deg between conditions, so MeTRAbs' 20.31 deg is two orders of magnitude too coarse for real kinematic analysis and even the base 9.91 deg only approaches usefulness with the idealized +context (2.87 deg); the fundamental ambiguity result (Figure 2) proves identical image pixels can come from 3D skeletons whose right-leg angle differs by 7.8 deg -- provably unrecoverable without scene geometry; football fields (yard lines every 5, hash marks, numbers, sidelines) are even richer in marking geometry than a 400m track, and Next Gen Stats player (x,y) positions can anchor the ray-cast lifting as hard positional constraints -- GSE-exclusive data the paper never had.

In a four-team double round-robin, fixture order changes how many late group games are stakeless dead rubbers: five Poisson goal-model variants fit to 1,632 UEFA Champions League matches, 12 distinct schedules enumerated for 4 teams x 6 matchdays, one million Monte Carlo tournaments simulated per schedule (ex-ante, pre-tournament strengths only -- no result leakage); operative definitions: weakly stakeless -- at least one team's final rank cannot change regardless of result; strongly stakeless -- neither team's rank can change; the best vs worst schedule reduces weakly-stakeless probability by 35% on Matchday 5 and 28% on Matchday 6, and strongly-stakeless probability by 32% -- a citable schedule-design number; sanity check: stakeless probabilities must be exactly 0 before Matchday 4.

Limitations: four-team double round-robin only (larger groups and the new Swiss-style UCL format need re-derivation), Poisson goal models are simple with no team-specific motivation parameters, stakeless is binary (ignores partial incentives like seeding within qualification); the corpus ADOPT is ex-ante stakeless probability as a model feature (p_stakeless_weak, p_stakeless_strong) interacted with team-news/rotation signals, plus effort-discounted outcome models conditional on stakeless status and a test of whether closing lines already price stakelessness -- the adoption gate requires weakly/strongly stakeless games to show a statistically significant shift in goal/point distributions or favorite cover rates vs matched non-stakeless games in GSE's historical group-stage data.

Vector quantile regression under misspecification (Carlier, Chernozhukov, Galichon 2016): VQR primal (3.1) max{E(V*Y) : Law(V) = mu, E(X|V) = E(X)} -- correlation maximization with a mean-independence constraint, mu = uniform([0,1]^d), solved by the Brenier map Y = grad phi(U); dual (3.2) inf_{(psi,phi,b)} E(psi(X,Y) + phi(U)) s.t. psi(x,y) + phi(t) + b(t)*x >= t*y pointwise; Theorem 3.3: under misspecification Y in partial Phi_X^{**}(U) a.s. (the solution lives on the contact set of Phi_x with its convex envelope); univariate Theorem 4.9: mean-independence correlation maximization equals the Koenker-Bassett check-function program with an added global constraint t -> U_t nonincreasing (t-grid monotonicity); Lemma 4.10: sup_{v in C} integral_0^1 v(t) q(t) dt = max_t Q(t), Q(t) = integral_0^t q(s) ds -- the corpus verdict is REJECT (zero numbers, zero experiments, zero datasets): the one operationally adjacent observation (t-grid monotonicity avoids quantile crossing) is well-known folklore with cheaper remedies (post-hoc quantile sorting; Chernozhukov-Fernandez-Val-Galichon 2009/2010 rearrangement), and the mean-independence constraint is strictly weaker than full independence so the estimated 'quantiles' need not be conditional quantiles at all.
equation: VQR primal: max{E(V*Y) : Law(V) = mu, E(X|V) = E(X)}

claim: Multivariate scoring rules for joint forecasts: energy score ES_beta(F_X, y) = E||X-y||_2^beta - 1/2 E||X-X-tilde||_2^beta (2), beta in (0,2), strictly proper; marginal-copula score MCS = MS*CS (5), strictly proper when components are (Theorem 1); copula energy score CES (6) with lower bound lb_CES = 1/4 - 1/(2 sqrt(6)); CVS (7)-(10); CDSS (11)-(12) is unbounded ('useless for applications'); estimation via K-band energy estimators (14)-(16) and copula observations via mid-point ecdf with rank adjustment u* = (2R-1)/(2N) (22); evaluation by sample mean score (25) plus relative change (26) -- explicitly misleading, never report it -- and the Diebold-Mariano test (27) under weak stationarity.
equation: ES_beta(F_X, y) = E||X-y||_2^beta - 1/2 E||X-X-tilde||_2^beta; MCS = MS*CS; u* = (2R-1)/(2N)

claim: The energy score separates the true model from all alternatives in every simulation including correlation-only misspecifications -- almost as powerful as the Gaussian-only DSS, beating the variogram; the earlier 'energy score is insensitive' claim was an artifact of using relative change instead of the DM test; copula energy score (CES) was the single most sensitive detector of mis-predicted dependencies (airline study DM statistics 28-158 with only N = 19 windows); DM statistics only stabilize at ~= M = 1,024 ensemble paths for simple settings, and even M = 16,384 may be insufficient for tricky 9-dimensional cases -- literature's M = 8/19/51 is far too small, so the hard engineering gate is to audit ensemble sizes against M >= 1,024 (below that the energy-score comparison is not trustworthy); rank-adjusted copula observations fix misspecified-marginal leakage into the copula score, so CES comparisons are only valid across variants with the same marginals or after rank adjustment.

Exigent 4d-VAR proposal for worst-case tornado forecasting (Hoffman, Henderson, Nehrkorn 2011): standard 4d-VAR J = J_b + J_o (background + observation terms), exigent variant J = J_b + J_o + w_d*J_d where J_d rewards severe-weather proxies, with tornado damage proxy J_d = -(1/Delta t)(1/A) integral integral STP dx dt where STP = Significant Tornado Parameter (MLCAPE, 0-6 km shear, 0-1 km SRH, MLLCL, MLCIN); proposed setup: WRF model with NARR initial/boundary conditions (32 km, 8x daily); validation proposed-only as subjective map-vs-tornado-report comparison -- corpus verdict REJECT: no experiment was actually run, the single cited number is negative (in the Andrew MM5 experiment damaging land winds were eliminated at the 6-hour forecast but regenerated afterward), and 4d-VAR requires a full NWP model plus its adjoint -- computationally enormous and operationally inaccessible, with no connection to game-level forecast calibration.
equation: J = J_b + J_o + w_d*J_d; J_d = -(1/Delta t)(1/A) integral integral STP dx dt

claim: SportSense: real-time detection of NFL game events from Twitter -- two-stage matched-filter recipe: Stage 1 keyword-based tweet retrieval (claimed 60% recall, <5% irrelevant-tweet false-positive rate); Stage 2 matched-filter event detector on per-second tweet-rate time series, plus a combined detector fusing multiple signal components (exact equation-level template not stated in the paper); historical search variant: window = 30, threshold = 8; manual timing of touchdowns as ground-truth labels; validation by leave-one-out cross-validation over 18 games / 100 touchdowns, time-ordered by construction (streaming simulation) -- the corpus ADAPT is the recipe ported to live injury/news detection on X: filtered stream on NFL keywords + beat-writer lists, per-game rolling median/MAD baseline over the last 15 min, matched filter over z-scored rate with a template learned from 2024 games, alert into the event bus with a latency SLO.

LOOCV: combined detector 98% true-positive / 9% false-positive; single matched filter 96% TP / 13% FP; keyword retrieval 60% recall, <5% FP rate; historical search (window 30, threshold 8): 97% TP, <4% FP; latency: average detection delay ~45 seconds, 60% of events within 40 seconds, all events detected within 90 seconds; limitations: small event set (100 touchdowns, 18 games); 2011-2012 Twitter API and tweet volumes (today's X API is paid, rate-limited, and tweet distribution has shifted -- bots, engagement farming); manual timing may bias latency favorably; 60% keyword recall means 40% of signal is discarded upstream; events tested were easy-mode (touchdowns) -- injuries, controversial calls, and news were not tested; acceptance gate: >= 90% of 2025-season injury-designation news detected, median latency < 3 min, FP < 15%.

X-VARS: explainability in football refereeing with multi-modal LLMs (Held et al. 2024) -- fine-tuned CLIP ViT-L/14 (temporal + spatial pooling of frame features, linear projection into Vicuna/Video-ChatGPT token embedding space) with the key trick of injecting the foul/severity classifier's predictions as text into the LLM prompt so explanations are conditioned on (grounded in) the model's own decision; two-stage training: Stage 1 CLIP fine-tune 14 epochs, LR 5e-6, batch 64, 16 frames at 224p (~9h on a V100); Stage 2 QLoRA fine-tune of the LLM (1% of layers), 3 epochs, LR 2e-4, batch 32 (~2h on two A100 40GB); dataset SoccerNet-XFoul: 10,000 clips, 22,000+ QA triplets annotated by 70+ experienced referees (~1.5 answers per question/action, 540,000+ words, mean ~25 words/answer).

Human study (20 referees x 20 clips): human-written explanations mean 4.0 vs X-VARS 3.8, with X-VARS rated higher than the human in 46% of comparisons; severity/foul classification accuracy: CLIP-only 0.52 -> X-VARS 0.62 (paper claims 19% above prior SOTA); the faithfulness gap: X-VARS agreed with the injected CLIP predictions in only 76% of cases -- the LLM overrides its own classifier's input nearly 1 in 4 times, with hallucination explicitly acknowledged as a limitation -- so the text is not a reliable readout of the decision; the corpus ADAPT transfers the 'inject structured engine outputs as text into a fine-tuned LLM' pattern to GSE's show-your-work pick narratives with a structured consistency loss (penalize the model when generated text contradicts injected numbers, extracted via regex/NER) and an acceptance gate requiring prediction-text agreement > 90% (vs the paper's 76%), blind mean rating >= human mean - 0.3, and human review before posting.

Assumption-lean quantile regression: a model-free conditional-association estimand Psi_tau = E[(A-A*){Q_tau(Y|A,L) - Q_tau(Y|A*,L)}]/E[(A-A*)^2], equivalently residualized via A - E(A|L) -- a weighted average of conditional quantile contrasts, identified without a parametric quantile model; its efficient influence function involves the conditional quantile, the exposure regression, the conditional expectation of the quantile, and the density at the quantile; estimators are cross-fitted DML and TMLE (the TMLE fluctuation step targets the EIF), with nuisance models needing faster-than-n^{-1/4} rates or product-rate conditions; the GSE spec is Python (DoubleML-style cross-fitting + TMLE fluctuation), gradient boosting for E(A|L), quantile forests for Q_tau, kernel density for f(Y|.) at the quantile, starting at tau in {.25, .5, .75} before extremes.

Simulation experiment 1 setting 1 (n = 500, tau = .5): plug-in bias -70e-2 with 0.1% coverage of 95% intervals -> cross-fitted TMLE bias 1.2e-2 with 97.2% coverage -- the honest-CI methodology; Belgian application (3,925 participants, excess weight exposure -> health-care costs): TMLE estimated cost differences of EUR 205.09 at the median vs EUR 1,142.42 at the 90th percentile -- the tail effect is 5.6x the median (the distributional point); caveats: extreme-quantile performance degrades, near-zero density estimates destabilize the estimator, and no code was released; adoption gate: ADOPT if TMLE-CF achieves 90-98% coverage with |bias| <= 25% of plug-in bias at tau = .5/.75 on a semi-synthetic test, REJECT (restrict to central quantiles) if coverage collapses at tau = .9.

Large-scale diverse combinatorial optimization for ESPN fantasy football trade packages (Baughman et al., IBM/Disney/ESPN; 4,733 exemplars from ESPN-rated trades, 146 predictors per trade, 24 experts, train 3,786 / test 946; deployment 2020: 2M trade proposals, 240M insights, 55M interactions; 2021: 2.5M trades/day, 525->600 K8s pods on OpenShift): boom ratio = fraction of games with scoring above the 85th percentile of the position (Eq. 2), bust ratio = fraction below the 15th percentile (Eq. 3); season-long projection valuation PV = CDF_normal(ESPN per-position mean mu, SD sigma; player projection x) (Eq. 4); SME decay v = alpha1*tier1 + alpha2*tier2 + alpha3*tier3 + e^{-weeks/D}*tier4 (Eq. 5); tradability cost pre_pc = mean(position importance, projection ratio at position, projection ratio overall, positional rank) (Eq. 17), normalized to [0,1]; team dissimilarity theta = cos^{-1}(t1*t2 / ||t1|| ||t2||) (Eq. 18); knapsack maximize sum norm_pval*x, x in {0,1}, s.t. sum norm_pcost*x <= alpha*C_opp^max (Eqs. 19-22) with alpha = user risk parameter.
equation: PV = CDF_normal(ESPN per-position mean mu, SD sigma; player projection x); maximize sum norm_pval*x, x in {0,1}, s.t. sum norm_pcost*x <= alpha*C_opp^max; theta = cos^{-1}(t1*t2 / ||t1|| ||t2||)

claim: Strip the quantum theater: classical XGBoost 95.70% beat every quantum model (Hybrid QNN CNN-PI 94.30%, QSVM-PI 85.50%, QSVM-ALE 85.50%, VQC-PI 57.3%) and the quantum simulators ran on classical hardware with 14-feature tiers (21 features took 22 hrs/tier) -- no quantum advantage demonstrated; trade quality 2020 deployment 76.9% high-quality, 2021 (three paradigms + filters) 97.3% -- but quality is expert ratings, not league outcomes (kappa 70% inter-rater agreement, blinded compute type A/B/C); scale: 239M proposals/55M interactions (2020), 200 req/s at <1s latency; limitations: 95.7% XGB accuracy on 4,733 exemplars smells of overfitting to rater idiosyncrasies, no out-of-time validation, personalization weights w1-w4 not reported; the corpus ADAPT keeps boom/bust ratios as standard player descriptors and reformulates the DK optimizer as a 0-1 knapsack with bust-risk constraint sum(bust_ratio*x) <= tau and contest-adaptive risk alpha, gated on bust-constrained lineups matching current-optimizer mean within 2% AND improving top-1% tail hit rate by >= 15% relative on a 6-week holdout (2025 DK main slates).
