Key honesty notes: TFT/DeepAR perform badly due to failures on many series with mean MASE dominated by explosive failures (DeepAR std 51.51), so headline AutoML rankings are mean-failure dominated and median-based claims are more honest; AutoGluon-TS scores poorly (6.00 MASE) under the 5-min budget because its ensemble needs ~4h — AutoML comparisons are budget-sensitive and the 'beats AutoGluon' headline is budget-conditional. Limitations: no probabilistic/quantile output (point forecasts only); no sports data; short-series behavior (17-game NFL seasons) untested; warm-start transferability asserted more than ablated.

ACS-FW (Pinsler et al. 2019, arXiv:1908.02144) is a Bayesian batch active learning method that re-casts batch construction as sparse subset approximation of the complete-data log posterior, solved with Frank-Wolfe to avoid correlated top-b duplicates of naive greedy acquisition: the objective chooses batch D′ so log p(θ|D_0∪D′) approximates E_{Y_p}[log p(θ|D_0∪(X_p,Y_p))]; decomposition E[log posterior] = log p(θ|D_0) + Σ_m ℒ_m(θ) with ℒ_m(θ) = E_{y_m}[log p(y_m|x_m,θ)] + H[y_m|x_m,D_0] (Eq. 4); sparse approximation w* = argmin_w ‖ℒ − ℒ(w)‖² s.t. w_m ∈ {0,1}, Σ⑪_m ≤ b (Eq. 5), relaxed to polytope Σ_m w_mσ_m = σ minimizing (1−w)ᵀK(1−w), K_mn = ⟨ℒ_m,ℒ_n⟩ (Eq. 6); Frank-Wolfe selects the vector most aligned with residual ℒ−ℒ(w) each iteration (Eq. 7) with closed-form line search and ≤ b nonzeros after b iterations; the final heuristic binarizes weights (admitted by the paper to increase approximation error). Inner products: weighted Fisher ⟨ℒ_n,ℒ_m⟩_{π̂,F} = E_{π̂}[∇ℒ_nᵀ∇ℒ_m] (Eq. 8); weighted Euclidean ⟨ℒ_n,ℒ_m⟩_{π̂,2} = E_{π̂}[ℒ_n(θ)ℒ_m(θ)] (Eq. 9); random projections for arbitrary models: ℒ̂_n = (1/√J)[ℒ_n(θ_1),…,ℒ_n(θ_J)]ᵀ, θ_j∼π̂ (Eq. 16), ⟨ℒ_n,ℒ_m⟩ ≈ ℒ̂_nᵀℒ̂_m (Eq. 17), giving batch construction O(|P|J) instead of O(|P|²). Linear-regression closed form: ⟨ℒ_n,ℒ_m⟩_{π̂,F} = (x_nᵀx_m/σ_0⁴)(x_nᵀΣ_θx_m); single-point acquisition α_ACS(x_n;D_0) = (x_nᵀx_n/σ_0⁴)(x_nᵀΣ_θx_n) (Eq. 12), equivalent to BALD under greedy maximization, with x_nᵀΣ_θx_n ≈ leverage score x_nᵀ(XᵀX)⁻¹x_n. UCI regression results (final RMSE, mean ± 2 SE): yacht Random 1.272±0.0593 vs ACS-FW 1.031±0.0438; boston Random 4.068±0.0852 vs ACS-FW 3.799±0.0858; energy Random 0.959±0.0337 vs ACS-FW 0.855±0.0259 (note: naive MaxEnt top-b is WORSE than random on energy, 1.443 vs 0.959); year Random 13.165±0.0307 vs ACS-FW 12.194±0.0596. Classification: ACS-FW ≥ Random, MaxEnt, BALD, K-Medoids, K-Center on CIFAR-10, SVHN, Fashion-MNIST. Runtime: MaxEnt-I vs ACS-FW 1057.4s vs 101.7s on yacht (10×); total cumulative runtimes on par with MaxEnt. Trust warning: the final binarization of FW weights is unprincipled and increases approximation error (paper's admission); no cost-awareness; i.i.d. benchmarks only.

Abolfadl (2026, arXiv:2608.22389v1) treats point-in-time feature correctness as a machine-falsifiable invariant: f(e, E) = f(e, {e′ ∈ E : e′.ts < t}) — the computed value must be invariant to every event at/after t — with window semantics t − W ≤ h.acceptance_ts < t (left-closed, right-open on event time; strictly prior to the scored event). Two Hypothesis test families enforce it: (1) batch-vs-online elementwise equality; (2) perturb-the-future: replace all events at/after t and assert nothing computed before t changes. These property tests found three point-in-time defects that survived code review: LEFT JOIN + COUNT(*) fabricating history=1 for first events; debtor/creditor entity-key collision in the online executor; an accumulator admitting same-millisecond events into strictly-prior windows — all would have inflated performance. An ONNX export of the GBM had mean |score| diff 7.4×10⁻⁸ and max 1.7×10⁻⁴, yet 774 decisions changed (0.26%) and alert volume inflated +12.0% (6,458 → 7,232) because 32-bit accumulation moved scores across the cost-optimal threshold 3.98×10⁻⁴ — serving-format conversion is a model change until measured in decisions at the deployed threshold, not mean score error. On an agent-based simulation of a German retail payment ecosystem (1,562,860 payments, 6,576 accounts, 270 days, 0.19% criminal rate), PR-AUC under 0.19% positives: constant 0.0001, LightGBM 0.0053, +static graph 0.0144, +TGN no memory 0.0734, +memory 0.1717 (per-node memory more than doubled PR-AUC); paired day-blocked bootstrap difference (memory TGN vs LightGBM) +0.166, 95% CI [0.105, 0.241]. Ranking metric vs deployed-threshold cost diverge: rung 2 cost EUR 53,529 vs rung 1 EUR 20,459 (2.6×) despite rung 2's 3× better PR-AUC; recall at capacity rung 2 0.795 vs rung 1 0.909. Latency p50/p99 ms: feature fetch 1.84/4.67, inference 0.42/1.78, total 2.71/7.97 (200 ms budget met; measured on the GBM path only — the graph model is not deployed). Chronological splits use purge (1-day band; a 30-day band removed 79% of usable data and was rejected by a guard on bands exceeding 25% of a fold) + embargo.
equation: f(e, E) = f(e, {e′ ∈ E : e′.ts < t})

claim: Karimov et al. (2018/2019, arXiv:1802.08496v2) introduce a stream-processing benchmark methodology with three pillars: sustainable throughput = maximum ingestion rate sustained without large latency fluctuations (measured by controlling the driver's ingestion rate, not by max-rate ingestion which just measures backpressure collapse); event-time latency for stateful operators = source production timestamp → sink result emission, measured externally in the driver (prior work measured inside the SUT, hiding backpressure); driver/SUT separation with a scalable on-the-fly generator. On 2/4/8-node clusters: windowed aggregation avg latency (seconds) — 2-node: Storm 1.4, Spark 3.6, Flink 0.5; 8-node: Storm 2.2, Spark 3.1, Flink 0.2; lowering load 10% below max collapses latency fluctuation; Storm outperformed Spark by ~8% in sustainable aggregation throughput; Flink bounded by network bandwidth at 4+ nodes (saturation ~1.2M events/s); windowed join sustainable throughput (M events/s) — 2-node: Spark 0.36, Flink 0.85; 8-node: Spark 0.94, Flink 1.19; join avg latency 2-node Spark 7.7s vs Flink 4.3s, 8-node 6.2s vs 3.2s. Large windows (60s): Spark throughput halved, avg latency 10× — fixed with inverse reduce functions (incremental eviction instead of recomputing; recomputing full windows is the failure mode). Under extreme single-key skew, Flink/Storm throughput bounded by one machine slot (Flink 0.48 M/s, Storm 0.2 M/s, no scaling), Spark handled it via tree aggregation (0.53 M/s on 4-node) — but for joins under skew Flink went unresponsive and Spark showed extreme latencies. Storm most susceptible to fluctuating workloads; Flink handled join spikes best. The file explicitly rejects the absolute 2018 numbers as decision inputs — methodology only.

AlphaEval (Berkin Chen et al. 2025, arXiv:2508.13174) is a backtest-free, parallelizable 5-dimension evaluation framework for formula alpha mining: Predictive Power Score PPS = β·IC + (1−β)·RankIC, β=0.5, IC = (1/T)Σ_t IC_t (Pearson), RankIC = average Spearman (eqs. 5–10); Temporal Stability via Relative Rank Entropy RRE = 1/(T−1)·Σ_{t=2..T} 1/(1+KL(S_t‖S_{t−1})), rank vectors converted to discrete distributions p(S_{t,i}) = R[S_{t,i}]/Σ_j R[S_{t,j}] (eqs. 11–13); Robustness via Perturbation Fidelity Score PFS_D = Corr(S, S′) (Spearman between original and perturbed rankings) with PFS = min{PFS_N(0,σ²), PFS_t(ν)} over Gaussian and heavy-tailed t(df=3) noise (eqs. 14–15), noise σ = average daily volatility of the market index; Financial Logic Score (LLM rates symbolic expression/description for logical coherence, averaged); Diversity via Diversity Entropy: flatten m signals over (t,n), covariance C ∈ R^{m×m}, eigenvalues λ_i → p_i = λ_i/Σλ_j; DH = (−Σ p_i log p_i)/log m (eqs. 16–17); an integrated weighted score ranks/selects alphas. On Qlib A-share/U.S. data (miners GP, AutoAlpha, AlphaEvolve, AlphaGen, AlphaQCM, AlphaForge, FAMA, AlphaAgent + random): A-share table (Predictive/Stability/Robustness/Diversity/Logic) — GP 0.017/0.724/0.983/0.693/63.5; AutoAlpha 0.027/0.774/0.971/0.946/64.0; AlphaEvolve 0.028/0.975/0.688/0.897/63.0; AlphaGen 0.034/0.978/0.997/0.650/59.0; AlphaQCM 0.029/0.975/0.996/0.477/62.0; AlphaForge 0.040/0.977/0.677/0.743/62.5; FAMA 0.031/0.868/0.992/0.831/69.0; AlphaAgent 0.041/0.779/0.415/0.812/70.0; Random 0.009/0.844/0.846/0.981/60.0. GA-based miners are most robust/stable; RL-based stable + robust but low logic; LLM-based best predictive + logic, weaker robustness; integrated-AlphaEval selection beats any single-dimension selection on cumulative returns (Fig. 2). Honesty caveats: LLM Logic Score is subjective with no inter-rater reliability; PFS perturbations are synthetic input noise that may not reflect regime breaks; DH can be maximized by mutually anti-correlated junk signals (diversity ≠ quality); no multiple-testing correction anywhere; backtest consistency asserted without a reported rank-correlation number.
equation: PPS = β·IC + (1−β)·RankIC ; RRE = 1/(T−1)·Σ_{t=2..T} 1/(1+KL(S_t‖S_{t−1})) ; DH = (−Σ p_i log p_i)/log m

claim: FinDiff (Sattarov, Schreyer, Borth 2023, arXiv:2309.01472) is a diffusion model for synthetic financial tabular data that encodes categoricals through learned embeddings (E ∈ R^{D×C}, D=2) inside a single Gaussian diffusion process, avoiding the one-hot dimensionality explosion that breaks baselines: forward q(x_t|x_{t−1}) = N(x_t; √(1−β_t)x_{t−1}, β_t I); closed form q(x_t|x_0) = N(x_t; √(1−β̂_t)x_0, β̂_t I), β̂_t = 1−Π(1−β_i); reverse p_θ(x_{t−1}|x_t) = N(x_{t−1}; μ_θ(x_t,t), Σ_θ(x_t,t)); μ_θ(x_t,t) = (1/√α_t)(x_t − (β_t/√(1−α̂_t))ε_θ(x_t,t)); L_t = E‖ε − ε_θ(x_t,t)‖²_2; decoding = nearest neighbor in E (argmin over categories). Pipeline: numerics normalized, categoricals via learned embeddings, x_0 = embeddings ⊕ numerics + sinusoidal time embedding + label embedding, linear-projected; 500 diffusion steps, linear scheduler; up to 3000 epochs, batch 512, Adam, cosine LR, Glorot init; neurons ∈ {256,…,8192}, hidden layers ∈ {4,6,8,10,12}. Fidelity: column ω_col = 1−KS(x^d,s^d) numeric, 1−½TVD categorical, Ω_col = mean; row ω_row = 1−½|ρ(x^a,x^b)−ρ(s^a,s^b)| numeric pairs, 1−½TVD categorical pairs, Ω_row = mean; privacy DCR(s_n) = min_{x∈X} d(s_n, x), median over synthetic (lower better); utility Φ = (1/5)Σ Θ_i(S_train, X_test) over 5 classifiers (train on synthetic, test on real). Results (mean ± std, 5 seeds): Credit Default (30,000 rows) — column fidelity FinDiff 0.931±0.01 vs TVAE 0.920, CTGAN 0.872, TabDDPM 0.401; row fidelity 0.939 (best); utility 0.794 vs CTGAN 0.703, TabDDPM 0.709; privacy 1.474 (best); the paper claims utility trained on FinDiff synthetic (0.794) beats training on REAL data (0.706) by 8.4%. Philadelphia Payments — column 0.901, row 0.838 (best), utility 0.874 (best); one-hot baselines expanded to 6,124–7,830 dimensions and broke training on the full 238,894 rows. Fund Holdings (Bundesbank, proprietary) — column 0.764 (best); privacy TVAE 0.171 vs FinDiff 3.667 (the embedding model memorizes more on skewed numerics); TabDDPM column fidelity collapsed to 0.119. Ablation (Fund Holdings col/row): Standard scaler 0.534/0.824, Power (yeo-johnson) 0.552/0.889, Quantile Transformer 0.764/0.949 — quantile transform wins decisively on skewed numerics. Caveats: asymmetric tuning (FinDiff got exhaustive architecture search, baselines got SDV defaults — treat margins as optimistic); 'increasing embedding dimensionality did not result in performance enhancement' (D=2 chosen); no code link; Fund Holdings proprietary.

Voyager (Wang et al. 2023, arXiv:2305.16291v2) is an LLM-powered open-ended lifelong-learning agent for Minecraft built from three modules: automatic curriculum (GPT-4 proposes the next task conditioned on exploration progress + agent state, pursuing 'discovering as many diverse things as possible'; temperature 0.1 for diversity, 0 elsewhere); a vector-indexed skill library (every successfully self-verified action program stored in a vector DB keyed by the GPT-3.5 text-embedding-ada-002 embedding of its program description; top-5 relevant skills retrieved by embedding similarity to plan + environment feedback; complex skills compose simpler ones); and an iterative prompting loop with three feedback types per round — environment feedback, execution errors from the code interpreter, and self-verification (a separate GPT-4 critic judges from agent state + task whether the program succeeded and, if not, gives a critique with a completion suggestion) — looping generate → execute → feed back → refine until self-verification passes, giving up to the curriculum after 4 stuck rounds. Baselines: ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT; stack gpt-4-0314 + gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 + text-embedding-ada-002 (GPT-4 is 15× more expensive than GPT-3.5). Results: Voyager discovers 63 unique items within 160 prompting iterations — 3.3× more novel items than counterparts; travels 2.3× longer distances; unlocks wooden level 15.3× faster, stone 8.5×, iron 6.4×; Voyager is the ONLY method to unlock the diamond level. Generalization: consistently solves all novel tasks in a new world within a 50-iteration budget while baselines solve none; giving Voyager's skill library to AutoGPT also boosts AutoGPT (the library is a 'plug-and-play asset'). Ablations: replacing the automatic curriculum with a random one drops discovered items by 93%; self-verification is the most important feedback type (removing it drops items by 73%); Voyager without the skill library plateaus in later stages; GPT-4 obtains 5.7× more unique items than GPT-3.5 for code generation. Limitations: success is judged by the agent's own self-verification critic (no ground-truth oracle; critic precision/recall unreported — the headline claims inherit the critic's error rate); Minecraft's determinism flatters iterative debugging vs stochastic domains.

Experience Graphs ('Trellis', arXiv:2606.29823, 2026) argues that long-horizon agentic search should be stored as first-class, governed, queryable database state — an experience graph of artifacts, tool outputs, rewards, sibling comparisons, and causal lineage — rather than disposable logs/checkpoints. Core access patterns mapped to database operations: recovery = a query against the frontier; cross-session reuse = vector-seeded graph traversal; training-data extraction = a materialized view; agent replay = an as-of temporal query. Two-loop architecture: inner loop of skill-driven agent sessions + outer loop of RSI tree search over a persistent data substrate that 'renders agents stateless and serverless.' Design points: governed view maintenance, bi-temporal memory (valid-time + transaction-time), crash recovery via frontier queries, cross-user/cross-session governed sharing. The thesis line: 'databases made data reliable; experience graphs may make agents cumulative.' File-based memory (declarative facts, procedural skills, episodic logs) is diagnosed as capturing 'what an agent knows, not the reward-bearing experience graph of what its search tried.' No empirical content: the paper contains no experiments, tables, or baselines in the extracted sections — access-pattern claims are asserted, not measured; no cost/latency analysis; governance sketched, not specified; the 'stateless/serverless' vision assumes nonexistent infrastructure. The ledger's risk note: over-engineering the store before the discovery loop produces enough experience to need it — start with the minimal graph (nodes = attempts, edges = parent/derived-from, rewards = gate scores).

DeepSport (arXiv:2511.12908v2, Rice / UC Irvine / Georgia Tech, 2025) is the first end-to-end trained multi-sport multimodal LLM that reasons agentically over video — 'thinking with videos' by iteratively calling a frame-extraction tool — trained by SFT cold-start (Qwen2.5-VL-7B on DeepSport-CoT-15k for 1 epoch) plus GRPO reinforcement learning with a gated tool-use reward. Reasoning paradigm: trajectory τ = ((F_1,T_1,A_1),…,(F_n,T_n,A_n)) (Eq. 1); start with k=8 uniformly sampled frames with frame indices; per step: <think> reasoning, then either <tool_call>frame_extraction_tool(idx_start, idx_end)</tool_call> or terminal <answer>; redundant same-interval tool calls = format error. GRPO: group of G trajectories per prompt, advantage A_i = (r_i − μ_r)/σ_r (Eq. 2), clipped-ratio objective + β·KL(π_θ‖π_ref) (Eq. 3). Gated tool-use reward (Eqs. 4–8): R_acc(τ) = acc(τ) ∈ [0,1]; g_tool = 1 if tool used ≥ once; g_acc = 1 if acc ≥ 0.5; R_tool = 0.5·acc if g_tool=1 ∧ g_acc=1 (successful tool use), 0.03 if g_tool=1 ∧ g_acc=0 (curiosity bonus), 0 if no tool use; P_format = −0.05·(1 − g_fmt); R = g_fmt·(R_acc + R_tool) + P_format; invalid format collapses reward to −0.05. Training: video at 640×360, batch 32, 8 rollouts, 300 RL steps, up to 12,800 tokens/response, 8×H20 GPUs, 796 GPU-hours total. Distillation over 9 existing works → 10 data sources, 12 sports incl. American football (FineDiving, SoccerReplay-1988, FACTS, T3-Set converted to QA via templates); 15k LLM-filtered CoT trajectories (teacher Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking, judge DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp), 63k QA RL prompts, 6.7k QA test benchmark across four dimensions. Results (accuracy %, avg frames): DeepSport (14.39 frames) — 51.09 (recognition) / 43.82 (rules) / 24.74 (coaching) / 24.60 (commentary) / 40.08 overall vs GPT-5 (16f) 46.50 / 32.89 / 27.01 / 22.76 / 35.70 vs Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking (16f) 44.96 / 31.03 / 28.72 / 25.59 / 35.36 vs backbone Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct 16.98 — a +23.1-point lift on the same 7B backbone, beating GPT-5 overall while using fewer frames via selective re-watching; largest gains in Rule & Procedural Logic (43.82 vs 32.89 GPT-5); coaching/commentary remain weakest (24.74/24.60). Limitations: American football is one of 12 sports but results not broken out per sport (NFL capability unproven); the 0.5 accuracy gate and 0.03 curiosity bonus asserted, not ablated; LLM-as-judge filtering may select for judge-pleasing reasoning; 300-step RL phase short enough to question convergence.
equation: A_i = (r_i − μ_r)/σ_r ; R_tool = 0.5·acc if g_tool=1 ∧ g_acc=1 ; R_tool = 0.03 if g_tool=1 ∧ g_acc=0 ; R = g_fmt·(R_acc + R_tool) + P_format

claim: GITCO (github.com/birla-ai-labs/gitco) is a training-free, model-agnostic serving-time wrapper for frozen time-series foundation models (demonstrated on frozen TimesFM 2.5): a binary gate g(x) ∈ {0,1} predicts whether intervening on the context helps (intervene iff P(improvement|x) > τ; precision 78.0%, recall 57.6%; intervened on 24/53 datasets), and if so a router → probe → critic pipeline identifies the single most harmful context patch — the critic uses j* = argmax_j harmfulness(patch_j) (leave-one-patch-out influence proxy) — and repairs it with a 5-point simple moving average ỹ_{j*} = SMA_5(y_{j*}) over the harmful patch only, then forecasts with the repaired context. On 53 GIFT-Eval datasets (strict K=11 CV): total MASE improvement +1.032 summed vs frozen TimesFM 2.5; mean MASE reduction 1.95% across all 53 datasets, 4.30% among the 24 intervened; captured-improvement ratio 0.899 despite router classification accuracy of only 33.3%±28.4% (routing errors cost little because the improvement surface is flat). Limitations: single-patch assumption (a 2-anomalous-game stretch gets only one repair); SMA repair assumes point-anomaly structure and would destroy signal on a genuine regime shift (e.g., a new coach); the gate misses 42.4% of improvable cases; MASE-only evaluation with no probabilistic extension; GIFT-Eval is generic, not sports-structured.

A distributional-RL paper extends risk-sensitive RL beyond plain CVaR to static spectral risk measures (SRMs — convex blends of CVaRs such as Mean-CVaR), with the QR-SRM algorithm: SRM_ϕ(Z) = ∫_0^1 F_Z^{−1}(u) ϕ(u) du, ϕ non-increasing, ∫ϕ=1 (Eq. 3), equivalently SRM_μ(Z) = ∫_0^1 CVaR_α(Z) μ(dα) (Eq. 4) — convex combination of CVaRs (Kusuoka 2001); supremum representation SRM_ϕ(Z) = sup_{h∈H} {E[h(Z)] + ∫_0^1 ĥ(ϕ(u))du}, attained at closed-form h_{ϕ,Z}(z) = ∫_0^1 F_Z^{−1}(α) + (1/α)(z − F_Z^{−1}(α))^− μ(dα) (Eq. 6); objective max_π SRM_ϕ(G^π) = max_π max_h J(π,h), J(π,h) = E[h(G^π)] + ∫_0^1 ĥ(ϕ(u))du (Eq. 7). QR-SRM (Alg. 1): outer closed-form h_l from the initial-state return distribution (Eq. 6, novel vs Bäuerle & Glauner 2021); inner quantile-regression DRL on augmented MDP X:=X×S×C (S=[G_MIN,G_MAX] accumulated discounted reward, C=(0,1] discount factor), greedy rule a_{G,h}(x,s,c)=argmax_a E[h(s+cG(x,s,c,a))] (Eq. 10); Bellman iteration η_{k+1,l}=T^{G_l} η_{k,l} (Eq. 11). Convergence (Theorem 4.1): gap ≤ ϕ(0)cγ^{k+1}G_MAX (Eq. 13); J(π*_l,h_l) monotone increasing in l, lower-bounds the objective. Risk spectra tested: CVaR ϕ_α(u)=(1/α)1_{[0,α]}(u); WSCVaR ϕ_{α⃗,w⃗}=Σ_i w_i(1/α_i)1_{[0,α_i]}; exponential ERM ϕ_λ(u)=λe^{−λu}/(1−e^{−λ}); dual power DPRM ϕ_ν(u)=ν(1−u)^{ν−1}; interpretability via intermediate risk levels αξ_t^α and weights ξ_t^αμ(dα)/ξ (Eq. 9, Thm 5.1, Pflug & Pichler 2016 decomposition — explanation-only, never used to optimize). On three simulated environments only (American put option trading, mean-reversion trading, Windy Lunar Lander; multiple seeds): American option — QR-SRM(ϕ_α) finds the highest-CVaR_α(G) policy for each α∈{0.2,0.6,1.0}; lowering α 1.0→0.6→0.2 makes the policy more conservative (exercises sooner), raising CVaR_{0.2} but lowering CVaR_{1.0}; mean-reversion (Table 2) — QR-SRM(ϕ_{α=1}): CVaR_{1.0}=1.43±0.03, CVaR_{0.5}=0.03±0.04, CVaR_{0.2}=−1.36±0.09, beating QR-DQN (1.40±0.09, −0.24±0.17, −1.76±0.27) on all three and matching QR-CVaR; QR-iCVaR(α=0.5) is sub-optimal at CVaR_{0.5} (0.14±0.04 vs 0.27±0.03), confirming per-step risk measures misalign with static objectives; WSCVaR model ϕ_{α⃗_2,w⃗_2}, α⃗_2=[0.1,0.6,1.0], w⃗_2=[0.2,0.3,0.5] best on ERM_4.0/DPRM_2.0/WSCVaR rows (e.g., WSCVaR score 0.24±0.02 vs QR-DQN −0.18±0.16); Lunar Lander — QR-SRM(WSCVaR) achieves highest WSCVaR while improving CVaR_{0.2}/CVaR_{0.5} 'without a great impact on expected return.' A key failure: QR-CVaR collapsed on 3/5 Lunar Lander seeds; the authors attribute CVaR-only failures to 'Blindness to Success' (Greenberg et al. 2022) — ignoring the right tail — and weighting expectation alongside tail (Mean-CVaR/WSCVaR) fixes this while keeping tail protection. Assumptions: infinite-horizon discounted MDP, rewards bounded [R_MIN,R_MAX] with R_MIN≥0, exact return-distribution representation in the limit (acknowledged theory-practice gap).
equation: SRM_ϕ(Z) = ∫_0^1 F_Z^{−1}(u) ϕ(u) du ; SRM_μ(Z) = ∫_0^1 CVaR_α(Z) μ(dα)

claim: SymTorch (pip install torch-symbolic) automates symbolic distillation of trained PyTorch blocks into closed-form Pareto-front equations via forward-hook I/O recording and PySR evolutionary symbolic regression, demonstrated on GNNs, PINNs, and LLMs (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Llama-3.2-1B).
SymTorch symbolic-regression objective: select expression g from closed-form analytic expressions S minimizing summed MSE against block outputs.
equation: g* = argmin_{g in S} sum_i L(y_i, g(x_i))

claim: SymTorch Pareto-front equation selection score trades relative loss improvement against expression-tree node-count complexity.
Standard language-model perplexity definition used in SymTorch LLM speedup evaluation.
SymTorch recovered the 1-D heat equation with diffusivity alpha = 0.2 from a PINN trained on only 10 data points.

Qwen2.5-1.5B distillation: replacing 3 of 28 MLP layers via PCA+SymTorch gave an 8.3% token-throughput increase; the symbolic approximation contributed only ~1% of the perplexity increase while PCA dimensionality reduction was the dominant degradation source.

SymTorch recovered all four true interaction laws (gravity, spring, 1/r, 1/r^2) from a GNN's edge MLP, but symbolic regression directly on the raw dataset failed; the GNN decomposition reduces search from N^2 composite to 2N candidates, which is what makes recovery tractable.

LLM arithmetic distillation: the correct equation was present in the SR Pareto front for addition, multiplication, and Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion but was NOT selected as best; the LLM's learned operation approximates the true equation plus small epsilon systematic-error terms, and for counting 1s in binary strings the true equation was absent from the front entirely.

SymTorch's SLIME objective fits a local surrogate s to weighted squared errors on synthetic Gaussian points around x* plus neighbor points, with proximity kernel pi_x(z) = exp(-||x0 - x||^2 / sigma^2); training set = J nearest neighbors plus N_synthetic Gaussian points at half the neighbors' variance.
equation: s = argmin_{s in S} sum_{z in synthetic} pi_x(z)[f(z)-s(z)]^2 + M sum_{z in neighbors}[f(z)-s(z)]^2, pi_x(z) = exp(-||x0 - x||^2/sigma^2)

claim: PI-NDSR discovers symbolic equations for complex network dynamics by splitting them into node dynamics F and edge dynamics G: a physics-aligned graph neural ODE (PIND) denoises and interpolates noisy multi-trajectory observations into neural references F-hat/G-hat, then a coordinated two-population genetic search evolves F and G, freezing whichever population is closer to its reference.
Network dynamics decomposition: node state derivative equals intrinsic node dynamics F plus weighted sum of edge dynamics G over neighbors.
equation: dx_v(t)/dt = F(x_v(t)) + sum_{u in N_v} a_vu G(x_v(t), x_u(t))

claim: PI-NDSR coordination rule: each iteration computes distances d(F) and d(G) between populations and their neural references, evolves the population farther from its reference, and freezes the closer one.
equation: d(F) = sum||F - F_hat||^2, d(G) = sum||G - G_hat||^2

claim: PI-NDSR discovered equation for H1N1 influenza spread across countries/regions with aviation-route edges, with fitted constants a=0.0740, b=0.0015, m=-0.0041, c=9.9643; the form is physically sensible (zero growth at zero cases, sigmoid-modulated neighbor influence capturing travel aversion).
PI-NDSR achieved recovery probability 1.00 in all 8 synthetic settings versus TP-SINDy 0.15-1.0 (fails Wilson-Cowan entirely), SINDy 0-0.87, SymDL 0.15-0.87.

PI-NDSR had the lowest MSE (x10^-2, correct skeletons) in every setting, e.g. BA-SIS 0.312 versus TP-SINDy 0.434, SINDy 0.484, SymDL 0.979; and 100% recovery from SNR 70 dB down to 25 dB where TP-SINDy fell to 0% at 30 dB.
PI-NDSR ablations: removing interpolation drops recovery 1.0 to 0.81/0.86; removing coordination drops it to 0.31/0.47, making coordination the larger contributor to recovery.

The generalised signature-method framework unifies rough-path signature feature extraction as z_{i,j} = (transform composed with rescale composed with window_j composed with augment)(x) over augmentations, windows, transforms, and rescalings, where Sig^N(x) is the collection of iterated integrals of the path up to depth N.

The canonical signature pipeline (time+basepoint augmentation, hierarchical dyadic windows, signature depth at most 6, random forest) ranks in the top statistical clique on the UEA multivariate time-series archive, with no memory errors, while higher-ranked MUSE could not finish on 5/26 datasets with 500 GB RAM and HIVE-COTE has very high train/inference cost.

Across 8,569 dataset x variation x model combinations (26 datasets, 1,415 unique variations), hierarchical dyadic windows and signature-tailored augmentations (lead-lag, time, basepoint) are the dominant performance drivers; learnt projections and stream-preserving networks performed relatively weakly (authors note undertuning).

Signature-pipeline mean runtimes in seconds over UEA datasets: baseline augmentation+global window gave CNN 69.8, GRU 22.2, logistic 2.67, random forest 2.23; random projection + logistic ran in 0.86 s; learnt projections took 917 s (CNN) / 752 s (GRU).

Signature features grow geometrically in channel count d and depth N (combos producing more than 10^5 features were omitted from the study), lead-lag augmentation doubles channel count (d to 2d), and signatures are translation-invariant without basepoint augmentation, which creates a silent feature-duplication risk.

MARIE pairs decentralized per-agent local dynamics with a Perceiver centralized-aggregation module: a VQ-VAE tokenizer maps each agent's observation to K latents, and the per-agent trajectory becomes the token sequence tau^i = (..., x_{t,1}^i, ..., x_{t,K}^i, a_t^i, ...) (eq. 1).

MARIE's local dynamics Transformer predicts next observation tokens conditioned on the agent's own history plus aggregated global context features e_t^i (eqs. 2-4), and its Perceiver aggregation compresses the joint observation-action sequence into per-agent global-context vectors (eq. 5).

MARIE uses a discrete reward head with categorical outputs over M HL-Gauss-smoothed buckets where r-hat = E[R] (eq. 6, cross-entropy loss), and trains with joint dynamics loss L_Dyn = reward NLL + discount NLL + transition NLL (eq. 7) with Adam.
equation: L_Dyn = reward NLL + discount NLL + transition NLL

claim: MARIE was best or tied-best on 12/13 SMAC maps (median over 4 seeds): 3s_vs_5z 88.6 vs MAMBA 10.5 (all model-free baselines 0.0), corridor 47.1 vs MAMBA 21.1, 2c_vs_64zg 23.6 vs MAMBA 7.7; the exception was MMM where QPLEX 88.4 beat MARIE 25.0, hypothesized because short-horizon cooperation needs no imagination.

MARIE ablation: decentralized local dynamics plus Perceiver aggregation beats the centralized variant increasingly as agent count grows past 3; the centralized variant is competitive only at 2 agents (2s_vs_1sc).

Post-wave-2 integrity audit parsed all 772 arxiv-deep ledger files and reconciled them against the 750-line JSONL tracker: 755/772 files have a parseable verdict, 17 are notes/index files without verdicts.

Audit integrity catch: wave-2 commit 13b6a27c2 claimed the tracker went '485 to 605' but the tracker file was never updated (only 485 lines on disk); the tracker was rebuilt from wave-2 reader reports in audit commit 86f76c7.

Audit integrity catch: tracker entry 2603.04864v1 was recorded ADAPT but pointed at ledger 0212 whose actual verdict is REJECT and whose paper ID did not match; it was removed, and verified valuable count after audit is 579 (365 phase 1 + 214 phase 2) with 171 remaining to reach 750.

The doc specifies margin-density forecasting scored by CRPS, defined in prose as the integral over x of [F(x) - 1{x >= y}]^2 dx for forecast CDF F and observation y, and sets a graduation gate of CRPS improvement on at least 150 settled spreads versus a widened Gaussian baseline.
Conformal rank index k = ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)); if n < ceil(1/alpha) - 1, k exceeds n so intervals must be plus-or-minus infinity (fail-closed), banning all quantile clamping.

Jackknife+ uses zero data split and leave-one-out residuals, and its coverage guarantee is 1 - 2alpha (at alpha = 0.10 exactly 80% guaranteed, NOT 90%); the doc's worked example shows alpha=0.10, n=5 gives k = ceil(6 x 0.9) = 6 > 5, so clamped max-residual coverage is exactly 5/6 = 83.33% while reporting 90% confidence.

Generalized Venn-Abers fits dual monotonic isotonic regressions via PAVA on calibration data augmented with both hypothetical test labels, producing an epistemic multiprobability interval [p0, p1] with width Delta-p = p1 - p0; Delta-p > 0.20 means the market is flagged unpriceable and the engine fails closed with no position.

Shin devigging rejects proportional normalization because it severely overweights heavy favorites in extreme asymmetric markets; the power method only mildly dampens favorite-longshot bias with no theoretical foundation, while Shin solves a quadratic for the insider-trading parameter z and disproportionately removes vig from longshots.

Steam detection spec: RTS Kalman smoother feeds a cubic B-spline parameterization whose instantaneous curvature kappa(t) is monitored; the steam signature is an extreme global maximum in kappa(t) accompanied by a localized deceleration dip in trajectory velocity, and Hawkes processes are rejected for short-horizon odds archives because they overfit high-frequency noise and produce rampant false positives.

The doc cites Barber et al. (2020) for the result that bounded-length distribution-free confidence intervals for binary conditional probabilities are mathematically impossible without structural assumptions, meaning any per-pick uncertainty band is infinite or assumption-laden and the exchangeability assumption must be named on the product surface.

Audits of raw spatial event logs cited in the doc find that approximately 19% of frames contain state-transition inconsistencies, impossible telemetry, or corrupted formatting, motivating ingestion plausibility gates (e.g., flag player movement faster than 13 m/s as fatally corrupt).

Picks Intelligence doctrine defines confidence score bands: 80-100 Strong, 65-79 Moderate, 50-64 Lean, 35-49 Watchlist, 0-34 Withheld; scores below 50 must not surface as directional picks publicly, and a new model version has confidence capped at 70 until 30 picks are settled (fewer than 10 settled picks cannot surface confidence on any public surface).

Picks Intelligence minimum evidence requirements by pick type: SPREAD needs 1 Tier-1/2 plus 3 total sources, MONEYLINE 1+2, TOTAL 1+2, PROP 2+4, WATCHLIST 0+1; model disagreement above 15 confidence points is a risk factor, and two HIGH risk factors or Tier-5-only injury status or stale Tier-1 data escalate risk to VERY_HIGH.

Picks Intelligence win rate is defined as SETTLED_WIN/(SETTLED_WIN+SETTLED_LOSS) with PUSH/VOID excluded, displayed as W-L with a range timestamp and trailing windows (last 30/50/100), never blended across model versions, and requires at least 30 settled picks before public display.

Picks Intelligence enforces 8 forbidden claim classes on all surfaces: 'lock'/'guaranteed winner', 'risk-free'/'free money', 'sure thing', 'sharp money is on [side]' without Tier 1/2 backing, specific win rates without at least 30 settled picks at that version, 'verified inside information', 'our model knows something the market does not', and any implied non-public information access.

Skellam spread-rank v5.2.7 prices an independent Skellam cover probability into spread ranking for Poisson-valid sports (soccer, hockey, baseball): TeamGameLog rates feed Dixon-Coles (soccer) or Poisson (hockey/baseball) lambdas, and the same lambda plus the posted home spread emits skellam_cover rows as 2-way cover probabilities with push mass dropped and renormalized; skellamCoverFairValue two-way sums to 1 and is null on bad sport or degenerate lambda.

The v5.2.1 ranking law runs with independentWeight 0.7 against only skellam_cover rows; moneyline ranking ignores skellam_cover so an ATS cover probability is never treated as P(win). NFL and basketball spreads still rank by confidence; the Stern key-number mixture remains a separate module.

The NGS-replacement spec replaces three rule-based heuristic enrichers with measurements persisted in the NextGenStat table (grain player-week, unique on gsisId/season/week/seasonType/statType, written daily by the refresh-player-stats cron): passing fields include avgTimeToThrow (snap-to-release seconds), avgIntendedAirYards, avgCompletedAirYards, avgAirYardsToSticks, cpoe, aggressiveness (throws into tight windows); rushing fields include avgTimeToLos, pctAttemptsGte8Defenders, rushYardsOverExpected; receiving fields include avgCushion, avgSeparation, avgYac, avgYacAboveExpectation, catchPct.

Verified live NGS test pins: two QBs averaging 9.1 intended air yards recorded average time-to-throw of 2.799 s and 2.970 s, meaning the legacy heuristic's 4.0 s intermediate-timing constant is 35-43% above the measured band; the profile also inverted the ordering (deep 2.5 s below short 3.0 s, non-monotone) and wrongly defined pressure as 'seconds before snap' when time-to-throw is measured from the snap forward.

Pressure must be proxied, not measured: hurries are absent from both nflverse and the FTN subset, so the engine uses sack-and-hit rate from play-by-play as an explicit FLOOR proxy for pressure, and time-to-throw is not time-to-pressure.

Coverage exists only as opponent-aggregate exposure: per-receiver-week avgCushion and avgSeparation joined to the opponent defense's allowed aggregates via the schedule; no named-defender assignment exists in any platform source, so features must be named coverage_exposure_* (never per_defender_*) to avoid importing false certainty.

WR-vs-CB matchup features are built as differentials (receiver's normal separation/cushion versus the defense's allowed aggregate for the same week, plus pctAttemptsGte8Defenders for the run side) rather than hand-set priority matrices (WR to CB 95%, WR to LB 80%); the governing naming rule is that a measurement is produced by observing the world while a heuristic constant comes from judgment, and substituting the second while keeping the first's name breaks the track record.

Small-sample honesty pattern: the conformal-calibration module returns positive infinity below minN 20 rather than clamping (the correct pattern), while cqr.ts lines 12-15 clamp and is a known defect; small-sample intervals must refuse, not pretend coverage.

The Odds API is the primary live-odds source with markets h2h, spreads, totals across 7 verified sports (NFL, NCAAF, NBA, NCAAB, MLB, NHL, MLS); the freshness policy marks data older than 60 minutes as stale, records fetched_at on every ingestion run, and skips pick generation entirely on stale data with an alert, while every pick traces back to an ingestion run ID.

The public decision cockpit renders every published pick (and every no-pick) as a five-frame path (Board, Context, Signals, Gate, Verdict) evaluated by 6 gates (data freshness, sample size, brand safety, confidence threshold where marketDerivedEdge >= 50, activation status, public policy) and 3 verdict states (PUBLISHED, HELD, NO PICK), with failed gates rendered visibly (e.g., 'Pick blocked - weather data 87 min stale').

The Tier-1 validation bench prescribes walk-forward expanding-window cross-validation by season and week with random K-fold explicitly banned; scorers are log-loss and Brier for binary outcomes, CRPS for counts and yardage, PIT histograms, and calibration slope, all computed per prop family, with a non-zero exit code on regression.

The CLV referee runs simulated flat-stake closing-line value versus consensus close at decision time from the repo's own line archive; the doctrine states that a covariate improving log-loss but not CLV is 'describing the market, not beating it.'

The edge-mining lane (edge:mine) requires a pre-registered grid config checked into version control (adding cells requires a new version), hierarchical partial pooling, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the whole grid, season sign-stability, and minimum-effective-sample with design effects, emitting ranked HYPOTHESIS rows.

Every p-side covariate carries a provenance registry entry of the form provenance in {L0, L1, L2, L3, MARKET_GAME, MARKET_PROP} plus known_at, and the build guard fails if any MARKET_PROP feature reaches p or if any feature's known_at is later than decision time.

arXiv 2607.00164v1 (Cascade Research) trains a 7B LLM with RL using verifiable rewards to output calibrated NFL in-game win probabilities: the ideal target is eta(x) = Pr(win | x), the naive reward is r = 1 - (p - y)^2, and the proposed empirical-rate reward is r = 1 - (p - p-hat(x))^2; Brier score is strictly proper because among all functions of the state, its expectation is minimized uniquely by eta(x).

The paper's empirical-rate table bins training plays by score margin (14 bins, edges +/-1/+/-4/+/-7/+/-10/+/-14/+/-21) x time remaining (7 bins, edges 2/5/10/15/30/45 min) x pregame spread (9 bins, edges +/-0.5/+/-3/+/-7/+/-10), shrinking sparse buckets toward coarser parents with a hierarchical empirical-Bayes pseudocount M = 25: bucket = (w + M * p-hat_parent) / (n + M), applied global-to-downward.

Held-out 2024 (n=5185, Brier with 95% CI): Direct RLVR 0.1443 [0.1394, 0.1491] / ECE 0.0292 / MCE 0.0596 / accuracy 0.784 / resolution 0.1058; Masked-CoT 0.1522 / 0.0293 / 0.0684; DeepSeek-V4 zero-shot 0.1438 / 0.0430 / 0.0716; empirical-rate teacher 0.1432 / 0.0437 / 0.0993; live betting market 0.1355 / 0.0273 / 0.0824 / 0.799 / 0.1148.

Murphy decomposition finding: the 0.008 Brier gap between the direct RLVR model and the betting market is resolution, not reliability - the model is as well calibrated as the market but less sharp (resolution 0.106 vs 0.115); paired delta-Brier Direct-minus-Market is +0.0088 [0.0068, 0.0107], while Direct-minus-DeepSeek-V4 is +0.0005 (not significant).

Gradient-corruption finding: training the full chain-of-thought completion drove held-out Brier from 0.25 to 0.34 and ECE from 0.19 to 0.30; the masked-answer-span variant (gradients only on the final 'Probability: NN%' span) fixed reasoning consistency from 22.4% inconsistent (base CoT) to 4.4% (masked-CoT) under a blinded judge on 250 plays.

In-training held-out reward ablation (n=128): realized-outcome reward Brier 0.166 / ECE 0.10; half-half blend 0.181 / 0.121 (worse on both, reintroduces the outcome's noise); empirical-rate reward 0.154 / 0.050.

Adversarial flags on 2607.00164 recorded in the ledger: the method distills a lookup table and the trained model beats its own teacher on ECE (0.029 vs 0.044) with no explanation beyond 'smoothing' and no isotonic/spline smoothing baseline; checkpoint selection uses a fixed n=128 held-out sample (noisy); Cascade Research is not an established institution and the v1 preprint numbers are pending independent replication; the paper itself warns sparse or long-horizon events weaken both the reward and the market comparison.

The symbolic-regression tournament harness mandates affine calibration of every baseline before R-squared comparison: pred_cal = slope x pred + intercept, fit on train via least squares, applied to test; the motivating bug showed raw B2 R-squared of -0.2755 versus calibrated 0.0531, a 0.33 gap from scale mismatch alone.

Heavy-tailed targets get soft-target regularization before symbolic regression: soft_target_transform(y, beta=0.9) = median + beta x (y - median); the loss rule is log-cosh plus soft target for heavy-tailed targets and MSE only for bounded light-tail targets, with no invented auto-threshold.

The GBM ceiling probe gates symbolic regression into tiers: below 0.03 skip SR, 0.03 to 0.05 low-signal flag, 0.05 to 0.15 standard, above 0.15 SR plus structure diagnostic; if OLS R-squared is within 0.02 of the GBM ceiling, the signal is reported as 'primarily linear.' The gen-0 diagnostic runs a 1-generation probe (population 2000, parsimony 0.001) and flags attractor_suspect when the train-test gap exceeds 0.15.

The smooth-linear simplification test fits OLS on the same features as a discovered symbolic formula; if the smooth linear form wins or ties the discovered nonlinear formula (kink_is_decoration=True), the kink is decoration, not discovery; the row-alignment guard raises AssertionError on any row-count or index mismatch instead of silently comparing misaligned frames.

NFL Big Data Bowl 2026 trajectory task: the metric is mean Euclidean distance across predicted frames (10 fps tracking up to the pass moment, predicting (x,y) over ball flight of about 94 frames); the core portable representation predicts per-frame increments (dx, dy), applies torch.cumsum over frames to get cumulative displacement, anchors to the last observed position, and clips x to [0,120] and y to [0,53.3].

Repo1's winning ST Transformer config: input shape (B,10,167) to d=128, 6 pre-norm layers, 8 attention heads, 2 learned pooling queries, then a residual MLP 256 to 188 (94 frames x 2); best single model scored 0.547, and the near-uniform 4-model ensemble (ST 0.2517 / CNN 0.2517 / position-ST 0.2490 / GRU 0.2476) reached 0.541 on the public leaderboard, with the best 3-model combo (ST+GRU+CNN) at 0.540.

The TemporalHuber loss is a masked time-weighted Huber (delta=0.5) plus 0.01 times the mean of squared second differences, with time weight w_t = exp(-0.03t); the 'jerk' term is actually acceleration regularization focusing the loss on early frames.

Repo1 feature recipes: kinematics vx = s*cos(dir), vy = s*sin(dir), ax = a*cos(dir), ay = a*sin(dir); GNN-lite neighbor embeddings use K=6 nearest within a 30-yard radius with weights w = exp(-dist/8), normalized with ally/opponent split, producing 17 features; the geometric baseline sets momentum endpoint = position + velocity x t and required acceleration = 2 x displacement / t^2 clipped to [-10,10].
equation: vx = s * cos(dir), vy = s * sin(dir), ax = a * cos(dir), ay = a * sin(dir)

claim: Feature ablation ranking (847+ experiments, baseline CV 0.0750): geometric features +0.0045 (most important) beat GNN neighbor embeddings +0.0030, opponent features +0.0022, temporal +0.0018, lags +0.0015, route patterns +0.0012, and rolling stats +0.0008; 8+ layer transformers overfit (CV 0.0750 to 0.0755), window 10 was optimal (11+ no gain, 14 worse), and hidden 128 was optimal.

Augmentation and validation discipline from the report: horizontal flip gained +0.007 on the leaderboard, flip TTA +0.005-0.010, speed perturbation +0.003-0.004, and combined flip+speed+TTA +0.021 (0.568 to 0.547); the catastrophic TTA misfire (augmenting before scaling) cratered the leaderboard score 0.589 to 3.674, establishing the rule 'augment raw coords, recompute features, then scale'; training used seeds [42, 19, 89, 64] with 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by game_id_play_id and StandardScaler fit only on train folds.

The fictional-data honesty guard: an 11-test suite across two test files enforces that fiction may render only when the page discloses it, separating 'may fiction render' from 'may it rank'; the first draft reported 15 offenders with 3 false positives (e.g., /mlb is entirely real Lahman data), and the shipped guard maintains an allow-list of 10 pages, each re-checked that the disclosure still exists in source; non-vacuity was proven by injection (a scratch page rendering DFS_SLATE with no disclosure turned the suite red).

Two real honesty defects were found and fixed: the /fantasy/dfs page mislabeled real data as fake (a constant prop read 'Running on a sample slate' even after a licensed feed connected, because the note ignored the feed's own live flag), and the /fantasy/nba page carried a live-dot over invented players with no robots directive while its four sibling fictional slates all carried robots index:false (fixed with noindex plus an eyebrow 'fictional data' label and no live-dot).

The guard's stated unresolved blind spot: it reads page sources, not imports, so a component receiving fixture data as a prop from a module three levels down is only caught if the page itself names a fixture symbol; also recorded unresolved is /airwave rendering fictional personas behind a live-dot with the disclosure 120 lines further down, kept in LABELED_SURFACES because the disclosure is real and the page is a deliberate demo.

The ECE estimator postmortem derives that the expected binned ECE under perfect calibration is E[ECE | perfect calibration] = SUM_k (n_k / N) * sqrt(2/pi) * sqrt(SUM_i p_i(1-p_i)) / n_k, which is strictly positive and shrinks like 1/sqrt(n); simulated null ECE under perfect calibration (Beta-distributed forecasts, mean 0.67, 10 equal-width bins, 400 replications) reads n=100 -> 0.080-0.096, n=487 -> 0.039-0.043, n=1000 -> 0.027-0.031, n=2000 -> 0.019-0.022, n=5000 -> 0.012-0.014 - so the (n>=100, ECE<=0.05) floor pair was never jointly satisfiable and a perfect model reads about 0.09 at n=100.
equation: E[ECE | perfect calibration] = SUM_k (n_k / N) * sqrt(2/pi) * sqrt(SUM_i p_i(1-p_i)) / n_k

claim: The replacement debiased ECE estimator: debiased = SUM_k (n_k / N) * sqrt(max(0, g_k^2 - v_k)), where g_k = mean forecast - observed rate and v_k = SUM_i p_i(1-p_i) / n_k^2; deployed-version floors read the slice's seeded 5th-percentile bootstrap bound of debiased ECE (eceDebiasedCi90Lo, 200 resamples; null under 30 rows).
equation: debiased ECE = SUM_k (n_k / N) * sqrt(max(0, g_k^2 - v_k))

The corrected e-process certification uses a bet-specific composite null H0,i: p*_i <= b_i with b_i = 1/D_i (decimal odds), and an e-factor per bet with Ville's inequality P(sup E_n >= 1/alpha) <= alpha bounding the false-certification probability.

Price-space CLV is defined by de-vigging lock and close odds to no-vig probabilities and taking the difference, with both sides' decimal odds and millisecond timestamps recorded at lock and close; the audit specifies Shin de-vig, not proportional.

Same-slate dependence is corrected by effective sample size, and power analysis at one-sided alpha 0.05 and 80% power shows a 2% edge is not detectable in one MLB season at realistic volume: 3,844 picks needed at delta 0.02, 1,708 at 0.03, 615 at 0.05.

KL-based sample sizing for edge certification: D(0.60||0.524)=0.0114 implies log(20)/0.0114 ~ 263 picks, while D(0.55||0.524)=0.00135 implies ~ 2,220 picks; the skeptical prior of real post-vig edge in public MLB totals is ~0.05 and a posterior of ~0.5 on clean prospective data is required before operating on an edge claim.

The fixed break-even null of 0.524 is wrong because it assumes every bet is exactly -110; true break-even is bet-specific (-105 -> 0.5122, -120 -> 0.5455), and a fixed 0.524 inflates the certification rate so a losing 0.530 at -115 tests as skill.

Re-grading history after a bug fix destroys the e-process guarantee: certification probability can be driven arbitrarily high by re-grading until the path looks good, so historical ledgers must be frozen, fixes apply prospectively, and corrected history becomes a separate clearly-labeled audit stream.

The round-1 grouping-loss formula GL = (1/N) sum N_p Var(y|p) is wrong because it measures within-bin outcome variance (~0.25 Bernoulli noise); true grouping loss is the variance of the true conditional probability within a score bin, E[Var(P(Y=1|X)|S(X))] from Perez-Lebel, Le Morvan and Varoquaux 2023.

The GSE aggregator chain w_i = |p_i - 0.5| + 0.05 rewards extremity rather than reliability, the 0.03 dead zone discards small edges, and 0.484 attenuation plus 45% market re-anchoring forces p_final approximately equal to the market by construction; identified as the primary engineering cause of near-zero resolution, with logit-space regularized regression prescribed as the replacement.

Publication vs edge-claiming separation: publishing honest probabilities with no edge claim should be stratified across the full disagreement range so later CLV and resolution measurement stays unbiased, while edge-claiming uses a threshold on model-market disagreement chosen to maximize e-process log-growth; Bickel and Kim (2014) found little evidence of MLB over-under inefficiency, updating the 58.5% totals signal downward.

BUG1 fix: the Anscombe inverse offset must be 3/8 forward but 1/8 for the unbiased inverse (Makitalo-Foi 2011); the wrong 3/8 inverse biases run totals down by about 0.5, and field best practice is the exact Makitalo-Foi lookup table.

BUG2 fix: NB2 dispersion phi=12 is about 3.3x too high; empirical MLB variance-to-mean ratio ~2.15 implies phi ~ 3.7, the classic parameterization-mismatch symptom given NB dispersion is parameterized three incompatible ways (alpha vs theta=1/alpha vs phi) plus NB1-vs-NB2 confusion.

BUG3 fix: s^2=0.04 is 6x below the Anscombe Poisson floor of 0.25, so D_i must be 1/(4 n_i), not s^2/n_i; BUG4: MIN_GAMES_FOR_EMPIRICAL=8 is too low, and efron-morris-js.ts is an orphan commit not wired to HEAD.

NHL must not use NB2: empirical NHL goal dispersion ~1.01 is Poisson-exact over 52,540 team-matches, while MLB genuinely overdisperses at 2.21 with k ~ 3.8; forcing NB2 onto NHL inflates tail variance and systematically mis-prices NHL totals, so the engine must split per sport: NB2 for MLB, Poisson for NHL.

The Murphy Brier decomposition is stated as BS = REL - RES + UNC with live values UNC ~ 0.25 (fixed by a 50/50 world), REL ~ 0.004-0.02 (already excellent), and RES ~ 0.0048 (essentially zero); reaching the BS <= 0.22 target requires RES > ~0.03.

Under calibration, the Brier of a selective-publish set equals pi(1-pi) minus the variance of accepted forecasts, so reaching Brier 0.22 requires Var[P | accepted] >= 0.03; calibration eligibility floors are n >= 100, Brier <= 0.22, ECE <= 0.05, Murphy reliability <= 0.05, over 3 consecutive GREEN windows.

The monetization blocker is resolution, not calibration: RES ~ 0.0048 versus ~0.03 needed for Brier <= 0.22, driven by ~57 picks per day published near p = 0.5 collapsing the variance of published forecasts; the selectivePublishSweep delta sweep of |p - 0.5| thresholds (0 to 0.18) was never run against live settled data.

The selective-publish integrity condition states the conditional Brier of rejected picks should be ~0.25; above 0.25 means the system discards negative-EV picks (edge in fading them), below 0.25 is a STOP signal indicating metric gaming.

The seemingly promising totals ridge correlation r=0.490 (R^2=0.258) was diagnosed as the corr(X, Y-X) artifact: corr(p_entry, p_close)=0.40 implies corr(p_entry, Delta)=-0.51 by identity, and a ridge on p_entry alone matched it (r=0.503, R^2=0.284); moneyline grouped-CV gave r=0.091 with R^2=-0.002, a kill under the r>=0.15 rule.

Large Event Model (LEM) three-head architecture (arXiv:2402.06815v2): Type head in 42 to out 33 with hidden [256], LR 0.0010, batch 32, sigmoid; Accuracy head in 75 to out 2 with hidden [128], LR 0.0410, batch 1024, sigmoid; Data head in 77 to out 264 with hidden [64, 256, 256], LR 0.0063, batch 1024, relu; fine-tuning protocol is max 25 epochs with learning rate one-tenth of the original.

LEM validation weakness: simulated vs actual 2017-18 EPL standings averaged 3.4 positions of displacement (7-10 position misses on Burnley, Crystal Palace, West Ham, Huddersfield), with no held-out-season test, no comparison against a non-fine-tuned baseline, no uncertainty on simulated quantities, and validation run on the same season used for fine-tuning; GSE's acceptance gate is ADOPT only if fine-tuned team models beat Elo simulation by at least 1.0 win MAE on a held-out season AND beat the un-fine-tuned general model by at least 0.5 wins MAE.

Combinatorial Fusion Analysis enumerates (2^5 - 1 - 5) = 26 model subsets times 6 combination forms (score vs rank times AC/WCP/WCDS) = 156 ensembles, reduced to 52 keeping only diversity-strength weights; the selected LR+SVM+CNN rank-combination (ABE) reached 74.60% accuracy on the 2024 tournament vs the best public system's 73.02%, a 1.58pp gap equal to about 1 game out of 63, judged not statistically significant and noise-adjacent.

The transferable primitive from CFA is rank-space fusion of diverse model outputs, which is robust to miscalibrated probability scales, with diversity strength DS(A_j) computed from rank-score characteristic (RSC) functions as data-item-independent weights before ground truth arrives; GSE's adoption gate is rank-fusion only if it beats score-fusion on at least 2 of 3 NFL seasons backtested AND RSC diversity weights beat uniform weights.

Liu et al.'s TM-squared (TCDformer-based Momentum Transfer Model for Long-term Sports Prediction, arXiv:2409.10176v1) is a tennis-only model combining MODWT wavelet change-point detection with a trend/seasonal decomposition predictor; the ledger verdict is REJECT because its equations are garbled, its 80/20 train/test split is random rather than time-ordered (severe leakage), and its momentum-transfer premise was already tested and rejected in Garrett's own lab.

On 2023 Wimbledon men's singles (7,285 rows x 49 columns, 356,965 data points, 18 retained features), TM-squared reported 100-run average MAE 0.0389, MSE 0.0671, accuracy 0.9237, precision 0.9231, F1 0.9206 versus logistic regression 0.2126 / 0.2126 / 0.7874 / 0.7824 / 0.7871; however the random within-tournament split puts points from the same match on both sides, so the 92% accuracy is invalidated as a forecasting result.

The TM-squared paper's abstract claims MSE reduction of 61.64% and MAE reduction of 63.64% versus existing sports prediction models, but the ledger could not reproduce these from the paper's own Table IV (recomputed as 68.4% MSE and 81.7% MAE versus the best baseline logistic regression); quote only as a paper claim.

TM-squared detects change points with maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform (MODWT): the j-th jump location is l_j = arg max over t of ||W_{j,t}||, and the iterative k-th jump is l_k = arg max over t of ||W_{J,t}|| excluding previously found neighborhoods; momentum is defined with AHP-derived weights and a pairwise pressure matrix (e.g., Alcaraz-Zverev 4.78/0.21), though the reconstruction is uncertain due to garbled PDF extraction.
equation: l_j = arg max_t (||W_{j,t}||); l_k = arg max_t (||W_{J,t}|| | t not in union_{1<=i<=k} Omega_i); M_y(t) = m_{i,j} . SUM_z [delta_z(t).X_{i,z}(t) - delta-bar_z(t).X_{j,z}(t)]

claim: TM-squared's predictor decomposes momentum into a trend component x_t via multi-scale averaging filters with adaptive weights plus an MLP with RevIN, and a seasonal component x_s = M_y - x_t via wavelet attention; the final prediction is P(t+1) = x_t(t+1) + x_s(t+1), and the match winner is the argmax of total momentum with ties broken by historical rankings (Eq. 14).

Sun et al.'s 'Cracking the Black Box: Distilling Deep Sports Analytics' (KDD 2020, arXiv:2006.04551v4) trains transparent linear-model trees via mimic learning to reproduce a deep-RL action-value model in hockey/soccer, with Iterative Segmented Regression reaching tree-versus-deep correlation of 0.99436-0.99650 on action values; the ledger verdict is ADAPT as an interpretability and leak-auditing sidecar for a production probability engine.

In the black-box model, an action's impact is defined as the difference of action values between consecutive states, Q(S_t,A_t) - Q(S_{t-1},A_{t-1}), and the SARSA update minimizes the expected squared temporal-difference error E[(R_t + Q-hat(S_{t+1},A_{t+1}; theta_t) - Q-hat(S_t,A_t; theta_t))^2] with gradient step theta_{t+1} = theta_t - alpha . grad_theta L_t(theta_t).
equation: action impact = Q(S_t,A_t) - Q(S_{t-1},A_{t-1}); L_t(theta_t) = E[(R_t + Q-hat(S_{t+1},A_{t+1}; theta_t) - Q-hat(S_t,A_t; theta_t))^2]; theta_{t+1} = theta_t - alpha . grad_theta L_t(theta_t)

claim: The mimic learner uses leaf models y-hat = SUM_i (w_i . x_i) + b, splits that minimize weighted child y-variance with a minimum of 100 records per child, and pruning that minimizes E_v = argmin_w SUM_j (y_j - (w . x_j)) + lambda . R(w) where R is L0 for a smaller tree or L1 for better fidelity, pruning children when E_v < E_v1 + E_v2.
equation: y-hat = SUM_i (w_i . x_i) + b; E_v = argmin_w SUM_j (y_j - (w . x_j)) + lambda . R(w); prune children if E_v < E_v1 + E_v2

claim: The paper's novel action-replacement augmentation queries the black-box net for a soft label Q(S,A-prime) on a counterfactual action A-prime not equal to the observed action A (e.g., replacing a pass sequence with a shot), exposing the mimic tree to settings absent from real play.

The paper's fast split-point heuristics are Sorting+Variance Reduction, Sorting+T-test with Welch t-score (mu_1 - mu_2) / sqrt(sigma_1^2/N_1 + sigma_2^2/N_2), and Iterative Segmented Regression versus a Gaussian-Mixture baseline, with splitting criterion Variance(s) - [(N_{st}/N_s) . Variance(s_t) + (N_{sf}/N_s) . Variance(s_f)]; the T-test heuristic was worst on action values and Iterative Segmented Regression is the recommended default.
equation: Welch t-score = (mu_1 - mu_2) / sqrt(sigma_1^2/N_1 + sigma_2^2/N_2); splitting criterion = Variance(s) - [(N_{st}/N_s) . Variance(s_t) + (N_{sf}/N_s) . Variance(s_f)]

claim: Fidelity RMSE (mimic tree versus deep RL, test set): hockey shots action values Iterative Segmented Regression 0.01441 versus Null 0.13924; hockey passes action values 0.00964 versus 0.10808; soccer shots action values 0.00508 versus 0.13648; soccer shots impacts Sorting+Variance Reduction 0.01235 versus Null 0.11890; soccer pass impacts are the weak cell at correlation around 0.80-0.82 across all methods.

The mimic tree exposed an information leak in the original pipeline: frequent splits on event duration contradicted hockey expert knowledge, revealing a leak in the duration-feature extraction pipeline; per the paper, without an interpretable model such as the tree it is almost impossible to spot the spurious behavior from the black box.
Fidelity does not equal correctness: a mimic-learning tree can faithfully reproduce a biased black box, so high fidelity correlation does not validate the underlying model's correctness.

Pandey & Singh (2026) 'FailureAtlas: A Taxonomy of Failure Modes in Multi-Provider LLM Serving Infrastructure' (arXiv:2607.17525v1) proposes a 5x2 Layer-times-Detectability taxonomy (Network/Transport, Streaming/Protocol, State/Session, Model Behavior, Governance/Cost times Loud/Silent), with five populated evidence-verified failure modes, usable as a reliability audit instrument for a multi-provider LLM routing and agent stack.

Shared-state race condition: at 5 concurrent agent sessions the continuity preservation rate (CPR) was near perfect, but at 100 concurrent sessions CPR collapsed to about 28% (roughly a 72-point drop); the mechanism was a shared global history cache with a read-modify-write containing an async yield (the LLM call) and no lock, so a second writer silently overwrote the first's turn; every request returned HTTP 200, detected only via semantic-continuity metric drops.

Retry storm: 100 parallel agents with a fixed 1-second retry after a transient upstream 502 synchronized their retries and saturated the provider rate limit every window, so 25% of requests failed permanently despite only a momentary hiccup, while the provider billed for partial completions producing runaway spend for zero successes; mitigation is exponential backoff with jitter plus a global circuit breaker.

Redis semaphore leak (LiteLLM issue 20256, Loud): the error path bypassed the semaphore decrement (missing finally), stranding the active count in Redis; accumulated upstream errors drove the count to max_parallel_requests, causing a permanent HTTP 429 for that key with zero requests actually in flight, resolved only by a manual Redis flush.

SSE index collision (LiteLLM issue 33678, Silent): the SSE iterator reset its internal index counter per chunk, stamping every tool-call chunk index=0; the client concatenated independent tool args (e.g., two path fields) into a corrupted string saved into history, surfacing one turn later as a JSONDecodeError that misdirected debugging toward the network layer.

FailureAtlas structural findings: detectability is independent of layer; the Silent column is sparser (2 of 5 entries) but more dangerous; and the Model Behavior row is entirely empty (no evidence-grade entries found), which the paper treats as a finding about where observability tooling is weakest.

Event-loop blocking (LiteLLM issues 21033/24788): synchronous I/O inside an asyncio gateway blocks the whole event loop, and health checks roughly every 10 seconds turn it into persistent micro-outages; mitigation is async drivers in the critical path or run_in_executor.

Farkiani, Liu & Crowley (2025) 'Rethinking HTTP API Rate Limiting: A Client-Side Approach' (arXiv:2510.04516v3) proposes the Adaptive Token Bucket (ATB): a per-client local token bucket that on HTTP 429 reduces its local rate r to r times (1 - beta) where beta is the backoff factor, then slowly recovers r <- r + alpha per successful request (exact alpha and beta live in the code, not the paper); the oracle is a MILP minimizing total request completion delay subject to token-bucket capacity and FIFO ordering, usable only as an upper bound on small instances.
equation: on 429: r <- r . (1 - beta); per success: r <- r + alpha; token-bucket constraint: tokens consumed up to time t <= capacity + rate . t

claim: On a real search-API trace (avg 131K requests/day, 27K unique IPs) at the 800-request scale versus the wait-backoff baseline: ATB cut errors by 70.13% at 21.26% longer duration, and AATB (ATB plus aggregate UDP telemetry) cut errors by 93.23% at 27.62% longer duration with 276.25 telemetry messages; the paper's overall conclusion is ATB/AATB reduce errors 70.13%-97.3% at the cost of 11.7%-27.62% longer completion time.

ATB limitations: the uniform 1-token-per-request assumption breaks the fairness math under variable token costs (OpenAI-style), there is no adversarial-client analysis, and it was compared only against its own wait-backoff baseline rather than standard backoff-with-jitter or concurrency-limit approaches.

Susmann & D'Alessandro (2026) 'The Counterfactual Combine: A Causal Framework for Player Evaluation' (arXiv:2602.23233) gives a doubly-robust TMLE causal framework for player evaluation, demonstrated on all NFL field-goal attempts 2013-2023 via nflreadr: 11,523 attempts by 110 kickers raw, an analysis set of 46 kickers with at least 100 attempts yielding 9,786 attempts, with empirical FG success 85.3% and covariates kick distance, outdoor indicator, grass versus turf, temperature, wind speed, and final-30-seconds indicator.

The Counterfactual Combine defines three counterfactual estimands for the structural causal model Z=(X,A,Y) with X attempt covariates, A in {1..m} the player index, and Y in {0,1} success: direct standardization psi_a^direct = E[Y(a) | X in X-prime] which is league-table rankable; indirect standardization psi_a^indirect = E[Y(A*) | A=a] with P_{A*|X} = P_{A|X} which is NOT rankable (misuse warning citing Shahian et al. 2020); and performance above random replacement Delta-hat^b_rand_a = E-hat[Y | A=a] - psi-hat^rand_a.
equation: psi_a^direct = E[Y(a) | X in X']; psi_a^indirect = E[Y(A*) | A=a] with P_{A*|X} = P_{A|X}; Delta-hat^b_rand_a = E-hat[Y | A=a] - psi-hat^rand_a

claim: Theorem 1 (doubly robust): the TMLE estimator is consistent if either the propensity model or the outcome model converges, and is root-n asymptotically normal and efficient if both converge at o_P(n^{-1/4}); Wald confidence intervals come from the empirical efficient-influence-function standard deviation. Estimation fluctuates the initial estimate along a low-dimensional parametric submodel so (1/n) SUM D_P-hat*(Z_i) is approximately 0, then plugs in, with crossfitting required (10-fold NFL, 5-fold MLB); nuisance models are Super Learner ensembles (mean, glm, lightgbm) for both mu_P(a,X) and pi_P(a|X) under assumptions A1 no unmeasured confounders, A2 positivity, A3 intervention independence.

NFL kicker results: the top 3 by direct standardization are Evan McPherson, Tyler Bass, and Justin Tucker; Tyler Bass's standardized rate exceeds his observed rate, implying a harder-than-league-average attempt mix; Justin Tucker is statistically significantly positive on both the indirect and random-replacement contrasts; no kicker is significantly below zero on either contrast, consistent with selection (poor kickers do not stay in the league).

Efficient-influence-function structure: direct standardization weights residuals by inverse propensity, so a small propensity pi inflates variance, while indirect standardization weights by propensity itself; MLB propensity diagnostics (3,368,988 estimated propensity scores, mean 0.0119, 75% between 0.0110 and 0.0127) show some evidence of practical positivity violations that widen confidence intervals via the inverse weights, while the NFL data showed no pronounced violations.

MLB validation of the framework on 2025 regular-season baseballr data (163,664 at-bats by 673 players; analysis set 84 players with more than 150 games or 600 plate appearances, 40,107 at-bats, BA .260): top 5 standardized batting averages are Aaron Judge, Freddie Freeman, Bo Bichette, Vladimir Guerrero Jr., and Xavier Edwards; all 84 players' 95% confidence intervals contain their observed 2025 batting average.

Bhattacharjee, Thukral & Patil (2023) 'Early Churn Prediction from Large Scale User-Product Interaction Time Series' (arXiv:2309.14390v1) formulates churn as mapping 30 days of user-product interaction to 4 weekly churn probabilities with the training objective min over theta of SUM_i SUM_{j=1..4} (y_{ij} - g_j(theta; X_i))^2, and evaluates on ~10^6 users and ~10^8 transactions of proprietary Dream11 data (2018-2020).

Table 3 AUC per churn week W01-W04 (quoted exactly): LR 0.644/0.749/0.672/0.662; RF 0.640/0.775/0.699/0.687; GBT 0.646/0.773/0.703/0.694; CNN 0.797/0.705/0.686/0.675; ConvNeXt 0.835/0.751/0.729/0.717; Inception-ResNet 0.819/0.729/0.704/0.696; LSTM 0.800/0.742/0.727/0.721; Transformer 0.858/0.756/0.732/0.716; the headline claim is the Transformer beats the best classical model by about 6% on average, but classical RF/GBT beat it on week W02 (0.775/0.773 versus 0.756).

Churn metrics are TPR = TP/(TP+FN) and FPR = FP/(FP+TN), with AUC reported per week on ROC and PR curves, PR emphasized under 2-10x label skew; the label is y_{i,w}=1 iff user i has zero activity in week w.

Training cost at Dream11 scale: CNN about 6 hours and the 5-layer LSTM about 1M parameters versus the scaled-down encoder-only Transformer (8 self-attention blocks, about 1.8M parameters, no decoder) at about 13 hours on 4x Nvidia A10 GPUs with Adam lr 1e-4, global batch 16K, and 100 epochs; feature-engineering pipelines consume more than 70% of inference time at the 10^8 scale, which is the production motive for automated features.

Early-churn paper weaknesses: the train/validation/test split is a random user split (0.75/0.05/0.20), not time-ordered, over a 2018-2020 window that includes the COVID regime shift; the eleven shortlisted features are never individually named so the paper is not reproducible even in principle; the label of a full inactive week misses partial churn; and there is no calibration analysis under the 2-10x label skew.

Terawong & Cliff (2024, arXiv:2401.06086v1) trained XGBoost (binary:logistic with LogLoss, GridSearchCV 5-fold; colsample_bytree=1.0, eta=0.3, gamma=0, max_depth=6, subsample=1.0; n_estimators up to 1000 with early_stopping_rounds=10, halted at 452) as an imitation learner on the top-20% most profitable in-play bets (about 90k labeled actions) of scripted bettor-agents in the Bristol Betting Exchange horse-race simulator; the learner was significantly more profitable than every baseline including a Privileged private-information agent, largest p=0.0017 on Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney U-tests of per-agent profit distributions (profits non-normal per Shapiro-Wilk).

XGBoost imitation learner classification results: accuracy 0.88 overall; lay class precision 0.88 / recall 0.98 / F1 0.93; back class precision 0.85 / recall 0.41 / F1 0.56, with confusion 72,521 TN, 1,197 FP, 6,730 TP, 9,541 FN, so profitability comes from lay selectivity despite poor back-class recall; top features by F-score are distance (8,680), time (6,642), and rank (1,276).

The authors' own caution on the imitation-learning betting result: a lot of further development work and much more extensive testing would be required before real-money use; there is no real-data validation whatsoever, only the simulator.

Li et al. (2026, arXiv:2608.07932v2, ACM MM '26) SportsGrounder is a proposal-aided interleaved-grounding architecture for dense sports video VQA: OV-DINO object proposals with domain-guided top-K selection (K=15), Interleaved Grounding Fusion (IGF) weaving bbox coordinates plus visual semantics into global frame features, and Action-Aware Supervision (AAS) regularizing against language bias, trained with Mixed Preference Optimization (MPO); backbone InternVL3.5-2B with LoRA SFT 3 epochs plus MPO 1 epoch; no American football data in training.

SportsGrounder interleaves frame-by-frame H_vis = [Z_t^vit + Z_t^obj per frame], avoiding the naive-fusion O((T(N+K . L_box))^2) complexity explosion; the hybrid entity token is the text-embedding of the bbox string concatenated with the projected semantic vector.
SportsGrounder training losses: Eq. 10 L_SFT = L_vqa + lambda . L_act with lambda=0.1, and Eq. 12 L_p = -log sigma(tau log(pi_theta(y_c)/pi_ref(y_c)) - tau log(pi_theta(y_r)/pi_ref(y_r))).
equation: L_SFT = L_vqa + lambda . L_act, lambda=0.1; L_p = -log sigma(tau log(pi_theta(y_c)/pi_ref(y_c)) - tau log(pi_theta(y_r)/pi_ref(y_r)))

claim: SportsGrounder results on top-1 accuracy on 4-option multiple-choice QA: SoccerNet (26k QA, 17 action categories) 51.8 vs MiniCPM-V 4.0 47.5, InternVL3.5-2B 43.7, Qwen3-VL-2B 42.3, VideoLLaMA3-2B 38.6; FineSports basketball (24k QA, 24 action labels) 53.6 vs MiniCPM-V 48.2, InternVL3.5 44.8; SoccerNet subtasks Action 42.5, Team 71.2, Jersey 33.4 (MiniCPM-V wins at 37.8, OCR scales with params), Spatial 54.2.

SportsGrounder ablation: IGF-only baseline 47.2 overall / 38.4 Action; adding AAS gives 48.9 / 40.8 (+2.4 on Action); adding MPO gives 49.6 with Spatial 53.0 (+4.4 vs baseline); full model 51.8 / 42.5; absolute accuracies of 38-54% show dense sports VQA is hard with SOTA still wrong nearly half the time, so production use requires human-in-the-loop.
Prompt injection of bboxes as text consistently degrades Action accuracy across the SportsGrounder baselines (temporal-attention distraction), while visual-level fusion avoids the degradation.

Gao et al. (2026) 'BasketHAR' (arXiv:2604.17065v1) is a multimodal human-activity-recognition dataset from a single 90-minute basketball training session (waist-mounted MPU9250 9-axis IMU in a WT901 SoC at 200 Hz via UART; wrist heart-rate and skin-surface temperature via nRF51822 + Si1141 sensor at 1 Hz via Bluetooth), with 14 activity classes annotated by basketball-skilled students and each label verified by at least 2 annotators; the baseline is LoRA fine-tuning on ImageBind (freeze visual encoder, fine-tune text and IMU signal encoders), with inference as cosine similarity between input-signal features and textual label embeddings, taking the highest-similarity label.
BasketHAR alignment loss: Eq. (1) L = 1 - CosSim(.,.) and Eq. (2) L = sum of three modality-pair alignment losses (text-IMU, video-IMU, and a third pair), all hyperparameters set to 1.
equation: L = 1 - CosSim(.,.); L = sum of three modality-pair alignment losses, all hyperparameters = 1

claim: BasketHAR baseline results: overall accuracy multimodal alignment 78.11% versus CNN 72.91%, Random Forest 71.91%, LSTM 71.41%, SVM 70.27%, MLP 69.46%; macro average F1 0.69 for the multimodal method versus 0.57 for CNN; however per-class F1 for Run is 0.00 for all methods except CNN (0.12) and MLP (0.21), class imbalance is about 48:1 (Run 65 samples versus Bounce the Ball 3100), and the per-class counts sum to 11,235 versus the paper's Table 2 claiming 14,044 total samples at 200 Hz, an unexplained 2,809 discrepancy.

The BasketHAR paper's training-intensity numbers (average HR 142.77 bpm, peak 185 bpm, 90 abnormal HR records) come from an illustrative ChatGPT-4o-generated report, not independently confirmed dataset statistics; the paper has no cross-validation, no confidence intervals, no leave-one-subject-out protocol, an unstated volunteer count, and an unstated split methodology (leakage risk between adjacent windows).

Rahimian, Flisar, Sumpter (2025) 'Automated Explanation of Machine Learning Models of Footballing Actions in Words' (arXiv:2504.00767v1) is a 'wordalisation' pipeline converting an interpretable soccer xG model's numerical feature contributions into LLM-generated shot narratives using open Hudl-StatsBomb event data (110 columns per event) plus StatsBomb360, with separate logistic xG models per competition (EURO 2024 and 2022, NWSL 2018, FIFA 2022, FAWSL 2017, AFCON 2023) and an automated engagement-versus-accuracy evaluation.

Wordalisation model equations: Eq. (1) log-odds(x) = beta_0 + SUM_j beta_j x_j; Eq. (2) Contribution of x_j = beta_j . x-tilde_j where x-tilde_j = x_j - mu_j (mean-centered); Eq. (3) P(y=1|x) = 1/(1+e^{-log-odds(x)}); the SHAP explanation model is g(z') = phi_0 + SUM_i phi_i z'_i, and the key structural insight is that for the logistic model Eq. (1) is already a ready-made SHAP g, while SHAP-wordalisation for non-additive models (xGBoost) is an open challenge.
equation: log-odds(x) = beta_0 + SUM_j beta_j x_j; Contribution of x_j = beta_j . x-tilde_j, x-tilde_j = x_j - mu_j; P(y=1|x) = 1/(1+e^{-log-odds(x)}); g(z') = phi_0 + SUM_i phi_i z'_i

claim: Wordalisation synthesis layer: xG maps to percentile categories 'slim chance' (<25th pct, xG < 0.028), 'low chance' (<50th pct, < 0.056), 'decent chance' (<75th pct, < 0.096), 'high-quality chance' (<90th pct, < 0.3), 'excellent chance' (>90th pct, > 0.3); continuous features map to percentile bins, binary features to template sentences, and contributions are ranked by magnitude with only |contribution| > 0.1 log-odds included.

Wordalisation evaluation tradeoff: descriptive quality plus features plus contributions (Case 2) gives the highest accuracy on the two strongest features but low engagement, while full wordalisation (Case 4) gives the highest engagement and second-highest accuracy, the authors' recommended operating point; ablating the knowledge/answer steps (Case 3) is worse than full wordalisation, confirming the prompt-protocol steps matter, and raw numbers (Case 5) are the low-engagement baseline; dominant features overall are euclidean distance to goal and vertical distance to center.

The wordalisation xG model retains 11 features (squared distance to center; euclidean distance to goal; nearby opponents within 3 m; opponents in triangle; goalkeeper distance to goal; distance to nearest opponent; angle to goalkeeper; shot with left foot; shot after throw-in; shot after corner; shot after free-kick); dropped features were angle to goal (R=0.88 with angle to goalkeeper), distance to goalkeeper (R=0.81 with distance to goal), and angle to nearest opponent (p>0.05).

Duffield, Power, Rimella (2023) 'A State-Space Perspective on Modelling and Inference for Online Skill Rating' (arXiv:2308.02414v3) unifies Elo, Glicko, TrueSkill, SMC, and finite-state HMMs as approximate-inference schemes inside one factorial state-space model for time-varying skill, with filtering/smoothing/EM tooling demonstrated on WTA tennis 2019-2022 (tennis-data.co.uk, 0% draws), EPL football results/goals/timestamps (football-data.co.uk, 22% draws), international football, and classical chess (65% draws).

Q_S), with analytic eigendecomposition Q_S = Psi_S^T . Lambda_S . Psi_S giving O(S^2) filtering/smoothing after a one-off O(S^3) decomposition.
