claim: MaxIn-Elo results: 4x4 game - MaxIn-Elo has the highest convergence rate on both RR and cumulative regret, with regret 'close to 0'. Transitive games: MaxIn-Elo significantly outperforms all baselines on five games and achieves similar performance on the Triangular game; RR converges to 1 on four games; on the Transitive game RR reaches up to 0.6, on Elo game plus noise=0.1 RR up to 0.8; on the Elo game and noise=0.01/0.05 variants regret is close to convergence at around 500 rounds. Intransitive games: MaxIn-mElo has the lowest cumulative regret and the highest RR on all six games; RR reaches 1 except Blotto (top SSCC 99 plus low-rank rotation approximation). Hyperparameters: tau = 0.7n is the best starting point; gamma = 0.6 best top-1 on Elo games/Triangular (gamma = 0.4 'misidentifies the best player' on the Elo game); mElo dimension C = 8 best, 'performance drops when C = 16'; tau = 1 gives bad performance. Stated limitations: no contextual features, static skills assumed, top-1 focused not top-k. Hyperparameters were chosen 'with the best RR performance for each random seed', so reported margins are optimistic.

Rastogi, Balakrishnan, Shah, Singh (2021, arXiv:2006.11909v2) study minimax-optimal two-sample testing for ranked preference data, with the headline negative result that assuming BTL/Thurstone/SST buys nothing computationally over a model-free quadratic test. Theory setup: d items, per-pair counts k^p_ij, k^q_ij, win counts X_ij ~ Bin(k^p_ij, p_ij); simulations d=20, epsilon=0.05, random-design k ~ Bin(n,a). Real data: (1) Shah et al. 2016 MTurk crowdsourcing set - 6 experiments, 2017 ordinal + 1671 cardinal-converted-to-ordinal responses, d=74; (2) European football 2016-17 vs 2017-18 (EPL, Bundesliga, La Liga, Ligue 1), 15-17 common teams per league, d=67, 801 vs 788 comparisons, draws excluded; (3) Kamishima sushi preferences - 5000 total + 5000 partial rankings with demographics; no code released, Algorithms 1-4 fully specified in the paper.

Two-sample preference test: the unbiased-for-zero-under-null quadratic statistic T (Eq. 8) is T = SUM_{i,j} I_ij [k^q(k^q-1)(X^2-X) + k^p(k^p-1)(Y^2-Y) - 2(k^p-1)(k^q-1)XY] / [(k^p-1)(k^p-1)...(k^p-1)(k^q-1)(k^p+k^q)], rejecting when T >= 11d (general threshold d.sqrt(24(2-nu)/nu) for error nu); a permutation variant (Algorithm 2) gives sharp finite-sample Type I control; rank-breaking (random/disjoint-deterministic/complete) converts rankings to pairwise comparisons, then Algorithm 1 (Plackett-Luce, Theorems 7-8), with permutation Algorithm 4 controlling Type I error for the nonparametric marginal-probability model (Theorem 9). Sample complexity: testing needs only k = O(1/(d.epsilon^2)) comparisons per pair versus estimation's k = O(log d/epsilon^2), so testing is far cheaper than estimation.
equation: T = SUM_{i,j} I_ij [k^q(k^q-1)(X^2-X) + k^p(k^p-1)(Y^2-Y) - 2(k^p-1)(k^q-1)XY] / [(k^p-1)(k^p-1)...(k^p-1)(k^q-1)(k^p+k^q)]; reject when T >= 11d; general threshold d.sqrt(24(2-nu)/nu); testing k = O(1/(d.epsilon^2)) vs estimation k = O(log d/epsilon^2)

claim: Matching lower bounds: MST/WST/model-free critical radius epsilon^2_M > c/(kd) (Theorem 3, minimax optimal); parameter-based/SST information-theoretic lower bound epsilon^2_M > c/(kd^{3/2}) (Theorem 5); computational lower bound for SST at k=1: epsilon^2_M > c/(d(log log d)^2) under the planted-clique conjecture (Theorem 6), so no polynomial-time test beats the model-free rate; k <= 1 is impossible in general (minimax risk >= 1/2 for epsilon <= 1/2, Proposition 4).

Two-sample test empirical results: simulations show power-vs-scaling curves coincide across varied d, epsilon, a, confirming the predicted rate, with power identical under model-free, BTL, and SST data-generating models. Ordinal versus cardinal-converted-to-ordinal: REJECTED, p=0.003 combined (age p=0.001, taglines p=0.083, search p=0.187; spelling/distances/piano n.s.). European football 2016-17 vs 2017-18: FAIL TO REJECT, p=0.971 combined (EPL 0.998, Bundesliga 0.691, La Liga 0.67, Ligue 1 0.787), so no detectable shift in relative team strength across consecutive seasons. Sushi preferences: significant demographic differences (gender, age, region) detected in both ranking sets, competitive with Kendall/Mallows kernel tests. Limitations: the football analysis drops draws and uses at most 2 comparisons per pair, near the k>1 boundary with low power against small shifts; the test detects any shift with no attribution of which teams changed.

McGrath et al. (2026, arXiv:2512.08824v2) define 'command' (accuracy plus precision of in-rim landing location) from Sony Hawk-Eye 3D ball tracking for NBA free throws, plus launch-consistency ('touch') metrics and a 2D projectile physics model for error-robust launch regions. Data: Sony Hawk-Eye optical tracking (3D poses of players plus ball at 60 Hz), NBA regular-season free throws 2024-25 only (2023-24 discarded as noisier); pipeline 101,679 attempts -> 49,412 after outlier removal (>4 SD) -> 21,964 attempts across 72 players with at least 200 attempts; data and code proprietary, not shared.

Free-throw command and touch equations: Command C = 1 / (1 + mu^2 + sigma^2), where mu = mean landing distance from bullseye (2 in behind rim center per Marty 2018) and sigma = shot-to-shot SD of landing distance; range [0,1]. Touch (launch consistency): z^p_i = (sigma^p_i - mu_sigma_i) / sigma_sigma_i (per-component z-score vs league); r^p_i = 100% - Normalized(z^p_i); overall R^p = 100% - Normalized(z^p_theta + z^p_v) (position excluded because velocity/angle can compensate for positional error). Physics: 2D projectile, no drag/Magnus (<6% of ball weight at v=12 MPH, omega=2 rev/s); equations (5)-(7) map (v0, theta0) at fixed release (x0, z0) to rim-crossing position xf with zf = 10 ft; outcome bands swish / rim-contact / complete miss. Error suppression: perturb (v0, theta0) by player-empirical delta-v0, delta-theta0, compute the induced xf shift ('launch error propagation'); dark bands = error-suppressing launch regions. Shot optimization: loss L = 1/2(xf - xg)^2, xg = 5 1/12 ft (bullseye distance from baseline); gradient descent on (v0, theta0) to find the perfect-swish launch.
equation: C = 1 / (1 + mu^2 + sigma^2); z^p_i = (sigma^p_i - mu_sigma_i) / sigma_sigma_i; r^p_i = 100% - Normalized(z^p_i); R^p = 100% - Normalized(z^p_theta + z^p_v); L = 1/2(xf - xg)^2, xg = 5 1/12 ft; xf propto v0^2

claim: Free-throw command findings: league-average launch velocity 14.74 +- 0.33 MPH; angle 48.66 +- 2.99 deg; height 8.89 +- 0.42 ft. Split-half predictive validity (season split Nov 15, 2024, players with at least 50 attempts per half): early FT% -> late FT% r = 0.61; early command -> late FT% r = 0.67. Touch -> command r = 0.65; velocity consistency -> command r = 0.73; angle r = 0.35; position r = 0.17. Two players both at 86-87% FT% sit at the 95th vs 48th command percentile, i.e., equal binaries with very different attempt quality. Perturbations shift xf by up to about 1 ft; Player A delta-theta0 = 1.74 deg, delta-v0 = 0.28 MPH; Player B delta-theta0 = 1.11 deg, delta-v0 = 0.24 MPH. Swish band widest around 45-50 deg launch, narrowing beyond >55 deg or <40 deg; error-suppression dark bands near 46 deg (A) / 50 deg (B); higher velocity amplifies error propagation (xf proportional to v0^2). Command reliability floor: N >= ~50 attempts; tracking noise biases command in very small samples (unlike FT%). Authors' scope caveat: the framework may not extend to contested tasks because free throws are a 'closed task without defensive interference.'

Peng et al. (2025, arXiv:2511.07250v2) MVU-Eval is a 1,824-QA benchmark over 4,959 videos testing 26 multimodal LLMs on 8 multi-video understanding tasks (perception plus reasoning). Metric: zero-shot multiple-choice accuracy (exact option-letter match via regex extraction), overall and per-task; protocol 32 frames/video, longer side at most 720px, patch 28x28. Benchmark design: 8 tasks - Perception (Object Recognition 126, Spatial Understanding 179, Counting 227, Comparison 135) and Reasoning (Knowledge-Intensive Reasoning 281, In-Context Learning 164, Retrieval-Augmented Generation 339, Temporal Reasoning 373); average 4.7 videos/question, up to 13. Data sources: Kinetics-400, nuScenes, ScanNet, FineDiving (sports), YouCook2, Vchitect-2.0, DREAM-1K, plus 130 manually curated Kling.AI video-editing comparison samples; human faces and copyright-sensitive content excluded; benchmark to be released at github.com/NJU-LINK/MVU-Eval.

MVU-Eval QC pipeline: rule-based video-pair sampling -> auto QA generation (MLLM reject sampling plus templates; Jaccard similarity on captions for RAG pair sampling) -> leakage removal (content: strip descriptive text from options; format: regenerate until no-video accuracy approximately equals random chance) -> difficulty filtering (drop questions Gemini 2.5 Pro + Gemini 2.0 Flash + Qwen2.5-VL-72B all answer correctly) -> human verification (about 563 more removed) -> option rebalancing (final A 25.5%, B 25.8%, C 22.7%, D 20.4%). Yield: 4,187 -> 1,824 pairs (46% retained). Benchmark validation: no-video baseline 16.0% (below random 26.0%, models refuse to answer); human expert ceiling 93.6% via two-phase consensus (majority at least 3/5).

MVU-Eval results: overall best closed Gemini 2.5 Pro 58.4%; best open Qwen2.5-VL-72B 57.1%; human 93.6%; random 26.0%, a roughly 35-point gap to human, with most open models below 50%. Per-task bests: OR GPT-4o 54.7; SU GPT-4o 57.7; Counting Gemini 1.5 Pro 66.1; Comparison Qwen2.5-VL-72B 77.8; KIR Gemini 2.0 Flash 53.7; ICL Gemini 1.5 Pro 47.6; RAG Video-XL-2-8B 48.7; TR Gemini 2.5 Pro 83.1; no single model leads everywhere, so capabilities are imbalanced. Scaling: Qwen2.5-VL 3B->72B 46.2->57.1; InternVL3 8B->38B->78B 41.7->48.4->50.6; small Qwen2.5-VL-3B (46.2) beats larger LLaVA-OneVision-7B (40.4). Accuracy declines as video count rises; VideoLLaMA3-7B improves to 32 frames then degrades at 64 (token overload); resolution improves to 720, degrades at 960. Input format (Qwen2.5-VL-7B): native multi-video 51.9 vs multi-image 45.2 vs merged-video 44.6 (-7.3 pp for naive merging). Information ablation (VideoLLaMA3-7B): multi-video 47.5; text-description 41.0 (-6.5); multi-image 34.6 (-12.9); single-video 24.9 (-22.6); no-video 16.0 (-31.5). Failure modes: (1) object status/function; (2) spatial understanding across camera angles on the same vehicle; (3) domain knowledge plus filtering irrelevant videos; (4) temporal/causal 'what' vs 'why'; (5) instruction-following (LLaVA-Video-7B: >98% free-form paragraphs ignoring the option-letter instruction). The paper's motivating application is cross-angle sports analytics, but sports coverage is thin (FineDiving diving only), asserted not evaluated.

Baek & Yun (2026, arXiv:2508.13507v1): a badminton pipeline (YOLOv11x plus BoT-SORT tracking, ViT-Pose 17-joint poses, ST-GCN contrastive embeddings, two-layer Transformer shot/not-shot classifier) trained on 40 ShuttleSet singles videos (30 male / 10 female) and evaluated on one men's doubles match (1,698 frames) plus one women's doubles match (1,276 frames); verdict REJECT because the doubles 'validation' is two matches with the decision threshold tuned on the same eval data, so the transfer claim is unsupported and there is no transferable novelty. Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 on binary shot/not-shot.

Badminton tracking ID repair: constant-velocity extrapolation S(t_s+t) = S(t_s) + [S(t_s) - S(t_s-1)]t, with reassignment within 200 pixels (typical gaps <10 frames); the 200-pixel rule is resolution- and camera-dependent, not normalized, so it is brittle across broadcast setups.

Badminton singles-to-doubles results: Singles - ours (thr .50): accuracy .8617, precision .8977, recall .8973, F1 .8975; YOLO baseline (thr .57): .9876/.9880/.9874/.9877. Doubles (all) - ours (thr .86): .6686/.6311/.8124/.7104; men .7020/.6644/.8163/.7326; women .6389/.6028/.8182/.6941; YOLO baseline .5941/.5962/.5837/.5899. The authors frame it as 19.3% degradation (ours) vs 39.9% (YOLO), but thresholds were tuned per set, so the comparison is not clean; the doubles threshold (.86) was optimized on the same two matches used for evaluation, making the reported doubles numbers in-sample for the threshold; women's doubles accuracy is worse than men's (.6389 vs .7020) on a 30-male/10-female training split, an unexamined training skew.

Nguyen et al. (2025, arXiv:2507.09200v1) THYME is a SOTA video scene graph generation model combining hierarchical multi-scale spatial aggregation with cyclic temporal attention, evaluated on ASPIRe (ground-view) and the new AeroEye-v1.0 drone dataset. Data: ASPIRe - 1.5K videos, 1.6M frames, 833 object classes, 4.5K relation classes, 7 scenes; AeroEye-v1.0 (introduced here, built on AeroEye) - 2,260 videos, 261,503 frames, drone urban/suburban/rural, 56 object categories, >2M bounding boxes, 157 appearance + 128 situation predicates per box, about 752K position / 318K interaction / 178K relation annotations, aerial plus oblique plus ground viewpoints; baselines IMP, MOTIFS, VCTree, GPSNet, STTran, TEMPURA, HIG, CYCLO (the authors' own two predecessors, an honest self-comparison).

THYME architecture: (1) DETR detector gives per-frame object query embeddings q_i^{(t)}; (2) hierarchical aggregation F_t^{(l)}(S_i^{(t)}) = sigma(SUM_{S_j in N(S_i)} a_{ij}^{(t)} (W^{(l)} F_t^{(l-1)}(S_j^{(t)}) + b^{(l)})), with attention a_{ij}^{(t)} = softmax over dot-products of level-(l-1) features; (3) cyclic temporal refinement CA_{t'}(S_i) = SUM_{tau=0}^{T'-1} alpha_{t',tau}(S_i) V_{(t'+tau) mod T'}(S_i), where the modulo links the clip tail back to the head, then LayerNorm + FFN to a refined feature; (4) scene graph from gated fusion of DETR decoder self-attention relation representations across layers: G-hat = sigma(MLP_rel(SUM_k g_a^k elementwise R_a^k + g_z elementwise R_z)). Loss: focal loss per hierarchy level L(F_t^{(l)}) = -alpha_t(1-p-tilde_t)^gamma log(p-tilde_t); L_total = SUM_{l=1}^{L_h} L(F_t^{(l)}). Metrics: Recall and mean Recall at top-20/50/100 per interactivity type (standard VidSGG protocol). Five interactivity types: appearance (157 predicates), situation (128), position (135), interaction (142), relation (125), including sports-relevant predicates (approaching, overtaking, colliding, chasing, catching, dribbling, hitting).
equation: F_t^{(l)}(S_i^{(t)}) = sigma(SUM_{S_j in N(S_i)} a_{ij}^{(t)} (W^{(l)} F_t^{(l-1)}(S_j^{(t)}) + b^{(l)})); CA_{t'}(S_i) = SUM_{tau=0}^{T'-1} alpha_{t',tau}(S_i) V_{(t'+tau) mod T'}(S_i); G-hat = sigma(MLP_rel(SUM_k g_a^k elementwise R_a^k + g_z elementwise R_z)); L(F_t^{(l)}) = -alpha_t(1-p-tilde_t)^gamma log(p-tilde_t); L_total = SUM_{l=1}^{L_h} L(F_t^{(l)})

claim: THYME results: AeroEye-v1.0 R@20 - Position 15.52/mR 1.05 (CYCLO 13.52/0.75; HIG 12.51/0.85); Interaction 13.07/0.16 (CYCLO 12.61/0.14); Relation 16.03/0.95 (CYCLO 14.51/0.83); Appearance 16.52/0.68; Situation 5.53/0.61; R@100 - Position 42.03/2.15; Interaction 41.53/2.26; Relation 48.03/2.38. ASPIRe R@20 - Position 18.52/1.22 (CYCLO 16.32/0.97); Interaction 19.52/0.32 (CYCLO 15.27/0.20); Relation 21.02/1.12 (CYCLO 18.34/0.90); Appearance 18.23/1.07; Situation 6.57/0.26; R@100 - Position 50.05/2.53; Interaction 48.04/2.47; Relation 54.05/2.93. Ablations (AeroEye-v1.0): hierarchy 1/4 -> full: Appearance R@20 14.12->16.52, Position 12.32->15.52, Interaction 10.87->13.07, with gains plateauing at 3/4 depth; cyclic vs standard attention: Appearance 15.12->16.52, Position 13.42->15.52, Relation 14.03->16.03 (+1.4-2.0 pp R@20); temporal window 1/2 -> full is best, marginal from 3/4 -> full. Margins are 2-3% recall/mR over baselines with no confidence intervals or significance tests, possibly within run variance; mR@20 <1.1% on AeroEye-v1.0 means SOTA is 'least bad.'

Stevenson & Brewer (2019, arXiv:1903.07218v1): a Bayesian Gaussian-process model of cricket batsmen's career trajectories between innings; ledger verdict REJECT (superseded) as the earlier conference version of the journal paper 0604 already in the corpus; only two unique nuggets retained. Data: ESPNcricinfo Statsguru Test career scores; illustrative analyses of Kane Williamson's full Test career (career average 50.36 at the time) and the 'big four' (Smith, Kohli, Root, Williamson; ICC ratings as of 1 Aug 2018).

Cricket career-trajectory model equations: hazard-based survival likelihood P(X=x) = H(x) product_{a<x}[1-H(a)], with not-out scores treated as right-censored, P(X>=x); within-innings effective average mu(x) = mu_2 + (mu_1-mu_2)exp(-x/L); hazard H(x) = 1/(mu(x)+1); mu_1 = C.mu_2 (C~Beta(1,2)), L = D.mu_2 (D~Beta(1,5)); between-innings extension log(mu_{2t}) ~ GP(m, K) with squared-exponential kernel (scale sigma, length l); priors m~Lognormal(log 25, 0.75^2), sigma~Exp(10), l~Uniform(0,100); nu(t) = between-innings effective average via marginalization over scores; inference by nested sampling (Skilling 2006), C++ implementation, 1000 particles x 1000 MCMC steps per iteration.
equation: P(X=x) = H(x) product_{a<x}[1-H(a)]; mu(x) = mu_2 + (mu_1-mu_2)exp(-x/L); H(x) = 1/(mu(x)+1); mu_1 = C.mu_2, C~Beta(1,2); L = D.mu_2, D~Beta(1,5); log(mu_{2t}) ~ GP(m, K); m~Lognormal(log 25, 0.75^2); sigma~Exp(10); l~Uniform(0,100)

claim: Career-trajectory findings: Williamson did not consistently bat at his career average (50.36) until about 50 innings, supporting a 'finding your feet' adjustment period. Big-four next-innings predicted nu: Smith 62.5 (career avg 61.4, ICC 929), Kohli 57.4 (53.4, 903), Root 52.6 (52.6, 855), Williamson 51.2 (50.4, 847), with rank order matching ICC ratings; Smith is expected to outscore Kohli by 5.1 runs next innings, with 68.8% probability. Unique finding (form skepticism): the model 'appears to reject the idea of recent performances as having a significant impact on innings in the near future'; the effect of recent form varies greatly from player to player (citing Durbach & Thiart 2007's randomness result); the career shape supports the anecdotal arc of raw ability -> improvement with experience -> peak -> decline, with players taking different lengths of time to adjust. No formal predictive benchmark in this version (no LOOCV vs SMA like 0604); validation is illustrative only.

Ziyin Liu et al., 'Deep Gamblers: Learning to Abstain with Portfolio Theory' (arXiv:1907.00208v2): adds an (m+1)th 'reservation' (abstain) class to a classifier trained end-to-end with a Kelly-style portfolio objective, letting the model learn to say 'I don't know.' Data: SVHN (73,257 train / 26,032 test), CIFAR-10 (50,000 train / 10,000 test), CIFAR-100 and a cats-vs-dogs variant; VGG16-variant CNN backbone; all public image benchmarks, no sports data.

Deep Gamblers core objective: max_w SUM_i log[ f_w(x_i)_{j(i)} . o + f_w(x_i)_{m+1} ], where j(i) is the true label index, f_w(x)_{m+1} is the reservation (abstention) probability, and o > 0 is the reward hyperparameter. Reward-range property: meaningful rewards satisfy 1 < o < m; if o > m the network never abstains; if o < 1 it always abstains. Inference rule: abstain when the reservation probability exceeds the largest class probability; otherwise predict the argmax class. Practical caveat: low reward values required a cross-entropy warmup phase before the gambler loss was stable. Validation: coverage-vs-selective-error curves; baselines are softmax-response thresholding, Bayesian (MC) dropout, and SelectiveNet.
equation: max_w SUM_i log[ f_w(x_i)_{j(i)} . o + f_w(x_i)_{m+1} ]; 1 < o < m; o > m -> never abstain; o < 1 -> always abstain

claim: Deep Gamblers results: SVHN - at 95% coverage, selective error 1.36 +- 0.02; at 90% coverage, 0.76 +- 0.05, best among compared methods at low coverage. CIFAR-10: same pattern, Deep Gamblers wins at low coverage (high abstention), competitive elsewhere. The authors' stated trade-off: tuning o trades full-coverage error against low-coverage selective error; no single o dominates everywhere. Caveat: the method was never stress-tested under temporal distribution shift (vision data is i.i.d.; sports data drifts season to season).

Polson & Stern (arXiv:1604.03614v5) 'The Market for English Premier League Odds' calibrates a two-parameter Skellam (Poisson-difference) process to bookmaker correct-score odds matrices to represent the market's real-time outcome beliefs and trace 'implied volatility' during games. Data: 1,520 EPL games 2012-2016 (380/season) for calibration/efficiency; 18 EPL games Oct 15-22, 2016 (ladbrokes.com correct-score matrices, 238 score-difference outcomes) for the calibration diagnostic; Everton vs. West Ham Mar 5, 2016 (ladbrokes.com real-time odds scraped every 10 minutes) for the dynamic case study; scraped by the authors, not re-released.

Skellam market-model equations: score difference N(t) = N_A(t) - N_B(t) ~ Skellam(lambda^A t, lambda^B t), the difference of two independent Poisson processes. Calibration: (lambda-hat^A_t, lambda-hat^B_t) = argmin{D_E^2 + D_V^2} subject to lambda >= 0, matching the first two moments of vig-removed, score-aggregated market-implied probabilities. Moments: E[N(1)] = lambda^A - lambda^B; V[N(1)] = lambda^A + lambda^B. Conditional on lead l at time t: N(1) = l + Skellam(lambda^A_t, lambda^B_t). Implied volatility: sigma_IV,t = sqrt(lambda^A_t + lambda^B_t) (Black-Scholes analogy explicit). Zero-inflated draw variants exist (plain Skellam underestimates draws; type 2 with heavier vig on draws fits best). Time-varying log-linear extension: log(lambda^A_t) = alpha_A + beta_A X_{A,t-1} on in-game stats (possession, shots, corners, cards).
equation: N(t) = N_A(t) - N_B(t) ~ Skellam(lambda^A t, lambda^B t); (lambda-hat^A_t, lambda-hat^B_t) = argmin{D_E^2 + D_V^2} s.t. lambda >= 0; E[N(1)] = lambda^A - lambda^B; V[N(1)] = lambda^A + lambda^B; N(1) | lead l at t = l + Skellam(lambda^A_t, lambda^B_t); sigma_IV,t = sqrt(lambda^A_t + lambda^B_t); log(lambda^A_t) = alpha_A + beta_A X_{A,t-1}

claim: Skellam market findings: Skellam-implied probabilities track market-implied probabilities closely except for underestimating draws (fixed by the type-2 zero-inflated variant); Skellam log-odds have a heavier right tail than market log-odds (overprices extreme outcomes). On the 1,520-game efficiency test, binned home-win frequency approximately equals market-implied probability, so the market looks efficient; the Skellam curve with lambda-hat^A=1.5, lambda-hat^B=1.2 traces the win/draw probability relationship. Everton-West Ham case study: pre-game lambda-hat^A = 2.33, lambda-hat^B = 1.44; the 34' red card jumps implied volatility; Everton's win probability hit about 90% before West Ham's 78' goal; draw probability spiked to about 90% before the 90' winner; whole-game-normalized intensity rose through the game. NFL applicability note: scoring is not Poisson (drives have memory, 3/7-point chunks, clock effects), so the Skellam likelihood is wrong for the NFL, but the calibration architecture ports to a drive-based point process (Baker & McHale 2013, cited by the paper).

Szekely et al. (2023, arXiv:2303.05774): a machine-learning study of whether NFL Scouting Combine drills predict draft matriculation (at least 1 NFL snap) and career success (total NFL snaps). Data: draft classes 2013-2017; 1,973 prospects -> 805 with complete combine data (listwise deletion); six combine drills (40-yard dash, broad jump, bench press reps at 225, vertical jump, 20-yard shuttle, 3-cone drill); all positions pooled; 80/20 train/test split; code at github.com/bszek213/nfl_combine/tree/publish. No novel equations.

Combine study results: matriculation - random forest (944 estimators, min_samples_split=2, min_samples_leaf=2, max_features=3, max_depth=97, bootstrap; 10-fold CV selected) test accuracy 0.83 (CV 0.81); logistic 0.75, gradient boosting 0.77, SVM 0.76, tree 0.73. Career snaps - linear regression best (10-fold CV selected): CV RMSE 1,210.1, test RMSE 904.6, R^2 = 0.17 (SVM 1,298.8, GB 1,289.3, RF 1,276.0, tree 1,731.3). Feature-importance discrepancy: the 3-cone drill is MOST important for classification (getting drafted) but LEAST important for snaps (regression betas); broad jump is most important for snaps. Headline: combine drills predict getting INTO the league (83%) but explain only 17% of variance in career snaps, effectively a null result for success prediction. Limitations: listwise deletion (1,973->805) on an invite-only, range-restricted sample; snaps conflate special-teamers with starters; position-pooled (QBs with long snappers); no college production features; 2013-2017 classes only.

Pipping-Gamon et al. (2026, arXiv:2604.01491v1) produce opponent-adjusted player-level ratings for NFL offensive linemen (blockers) and pass rushers via ridge-regularized Bradley-Terry paired-comparison models on tracking data, with outcome severity (loss/win/hit/sack) as the richer target. Data: 2021 NFL regular-season player-tracking at 10 Hz from Hudl (proprietary, not replicable); analysis sample 153,138 blocker-rusher interactions across 33,283 pass plays in 266 games; 620 rushers, 348 blockers; double-team rate 42.7%; outcome frequencies loss 0.730, win 0.253, hit 0.0109, sack 0.0063; code at github.com/WhartonSABI/nfl-elo; nearest public substitute is NFL Big Data Bowl tracking releases / nflverse (lacks engagement labels).

Opponent-adjusted trench model: interaction distance d_{p,t} = sqrt((x_{p,t} - x_{QB,t})^2 + (y_{p,t} - y_{QB,t})^2). Binary ridge Bradley-Terry: logit P(Y_t=1) = alpha + r_{i(t)} - b_{j(t)} + delta D_t (Y_t=1 = rusher win under the 2.5 s distance rule); argmin_theta {-l(theta) + lambda||theta||^2_2}, lambda via CV on a log-spaced grid (lambda_min = 1.31x10^-4 win, 1.17x10^-4 severity). Severity multinomial: P(C_t=c) = exp(eta_{t,c}) / SUM_{c'} exp(eta_{t,c'}); eta_{t,c} = alpha_c + r_{i(t),c} - b_{j(t),c} + delta_c D_t; loss is the reference class. Severity weights anchored to EPA: w(o) = (EPA_no-pressure - EPA_o)/(EPA_no-pressure - EPA_sack); rounded weights w(loss)=0, w(win)=0.10, w(hit)=0.20, w(sack)=1.00 (from benchmarks: no pressure 0.233, hurry-only 0.019, hit-only -0.161, sack -1.856). Matchup baselines: smoothed player frequencies (prior strength m=25 win / m=50 severity); logit-average p-hat_ij^match = logit^{-1}((logit(p-tilde_i^(R)) + logit(p-tilde_j^(B)))/2). Rank AUC (Mann-Whitney form); Enrichment@K = precision@K / (n_+/n); uncertainty via end-to-end game-level bootstrap (B=1000).
equation: d_{p,t} = sqrt((x_{p,t} - x_{QB,t})^2 + (y_{p,t} - y_{QB,t})^2); logit P(Y_t=1) = alpha + r_{i(t)} - b_{j(t)} + delta D_t; argmin_theta {-l(theta) + lambda||theta||^2_2}; P(C_t=c) = exp(eta_{t,c}) / SUM_{c'} exp(eta_{t,c'}); eta_{t,c} = alpha_c + r_{i(t),c} - b_{j(t),c} + delta_c D_t; w(o) = (EPA_no-pressure - EPA_o)/(EPA_no-pressure - EPA_sack); w(loss)=0, w(win)=0.10, w(hit)=0.20, w(sack)=1.00; p-hat_ij^match = logit^{-1}((logit(p-tilde_i^(R)) + logit(p-tilde_j^(B)))/2)

claim: Trench-rating holdout results (model vs baseline log-loss): Win/Global 0.5568 vs 0.5636, improvement 0.0068, 95% CI [0.0047, 0.0093]; Win/Matchup 0.5568 vs 0.5582, improvement 0.0014, CI [0.0005, 0.0024]; Severity/Global 0.6319 vs 0.6395, improvement 0.0077, CI [0.0049, 0.0106]; Severity/Matchup 0.6319 vs 0.6333, improvement 0.0015, CI [-0.0000, 0.0031] (overlaps zero, directional only); abstract-reported relative reductions about 0.24% to 1.21%. All-Pro validation: the severity model leads AUC in 3 of 4 role/accolade slices; largest Delta-AUC = +0.150 (severity blocker, first+second team: 0.877 vs 0.727); enrichment@K improvements non-negative in every slice. Leaderboards (min 200 interactions), severity: rushers - Robert Quinn 0.543, T.J. Watt 0.531, Myles Garrett 0.493, Nick Bosa 0.430, Jaelan Phillips 0.429; blockers - Joe Thuney 0.258, Corey Linsley 0.255, Tytus Howard 0.250, Dion Dawkins 0.215, Halapoulivaati Vaitai 0.207.

Lopez & Bliss (2024, arXiv:2408.10867) 'Bye-Bye, Bye Advantage': Bayesian state-space estimation of rest-differential effects (MNF/Mini/Bye) in the NFL, testing whether the 2011 CBA (bye-week practice eliminated) killed the bye advantage and whether betting markets price rest correctly. Data: 5,679 NFL regular-season games, 2002-2023 (256/season 2002-2020, 272 in 2021/2023, 271 in 2022); game info from internal NFL sources (authors are NFL employees, disclosed); point spreads from nflreadR (aggregate of sportsbooks); 52 games (0.9%) dropped for unclassifiable rest (COVID/weather reschedules); rest edges: MNF 410 away/290 home, Mini 526, Bye 593; code plus data at github.com/ThompsonJamesBliss/restadvantageinamerfootball. Rest category definitions: MNF = at least 1-day diff with the disadvantaged team on at most 6 days rest; Mini = one team 9-11 days rest with at least 2-day diff; Bye = did not play the prior week.

Bye-advantage state-space model: E[Y_{s,ij}] = theta_{s,i} - theta_{s,j} + mu_{HA,s} + alpha_MNF.I(MNF) + alpha_Mini.I(Mini) + alpha_Bye.I(Bye) (Model 1; Model 2 splits alpha_Bye,pre.I(S<=2010) + alpha_Bye,post.I(S>=2011)). Team strength: theta_{(s,i)} ~ N(gamma.theta_{(s-1,i)}, sigma^2_teamstrength); home advantage trend: mu_{HA,s} = (alpha_HA_Trend.s + alpha_HA_Intercept).I(HA). Models 3/4 identical with Z_{s,ij} = pregame point spread as outcome. Priors: theta_2002 ~ N(0, sigma^2), sigma ~ HalfNormal(0,5^2), gamma ~ Uniform(0,1), rest alpha ~ N(0,5^2). Fit in Stan: 4 chains x 3000 iterations, 1000 burn-in, weakly informative priors; model comparison via LOO ELPD; posterior P(alpha_Bye,post < alpha_Bye,pre) computed directly.
equation: E[Y_{s,ij}] = theta_{s,i} - theta_{s,j} + mu_{HA,s} + alpha_MNF.I(MNF) + alpha_Mini.I(Mini) + alpha_Bye.I(Bye); theta_{(s,i)} ~ N(gamma.theta_{(s-1,i)}, sigma^2_teamstrength); mu_{HA,s} = (alpha_HA_Trend.s + alpha_HA_Intercept).I(HA)

claim: Bye-advantage results: bye effect on point differential - pre-2011 +2.21 pts/game (95% CI 0.61-3.80, P(>0)=99.6%, 'as beneficial as home field'); post-2011 +0.31 (CI -1.01 to 1.64, P(>0)=67.9%); P(decline)=96.6%. Market pricing of the bye (Model 4): +0.39 pre (CI 0.00-0.78) -> +0.97 post (CI 0.65-1.28), P(increase)=98.8%, so markets now OVERVALUE the bye by about 0.66 pts versus reality (+0.31). Mini: PD +0.48 (CI -0.65 to 1.57, n.s.); market -0.06 (P(>0)=31.8%). MNF: PD +0.14 (CI -0.86 to 1.18, n.s.); market +0.37 (CI 0.14-0.61, P=99.9%), so the market prices a nonexistent MNF edge. Home advantage 2023: PD +1.65, market +1.74 (markets near-perfect on HA); HA declined about 1 pt/game over the period. Postseason bye still real: 2011-2023, 34-10 SU (+7.34 avg PD), 21-22-1 ATS. Bye cover rates: 2002-2010 home 55.8%/away 56.9% -> 2011-2023 home 44.6%/away 52.7% (edge flipped to anti-bye).

Feng et al. (2022, arXiv:2206.09034v4) 'Towards Better Selective Classification' asks whether SOTA selective classifiers (SelectiveNet, Deep Gamblers, Self-Adaptive Training) win via their external selection heads or via a better classifier, and tests a cheaper recipe: discard the selection head, select by Softmax Response (max class probability), and add an entropy-minimization regularizer. Data: ImageNet100, ImageNet, ImageNetSubset (25-175 classes), StanfordCars, Food101, CIFAR-10; ResNet34/VGG16, 3-5 seeds; no sports data; code at github.com/BorealisAI/towards-better-sel-cls (builds on official SAT and Deep Gamblers implementations).

Selective classification equations: selective risk: min_{theta,psi} E[l(f_theta(x),y).g_psi(x)] s.t. E[g_psi(x)] >= c_target (Eq. 1). SelectiveNet loss: L = alpha(L_selective + lambda L_c) + (1-alpha)L_aux (Eq. 3); L_selective = (SUM l.g-bar)/(SUM g-bar). SAT loss: L = -(1/m)SUM[t_{i,y_i} log p_theta(y_i|x_i) + (1-t_{i,y_i}) log p_theta(C+1|x_i)] (Eq. 6); SAT moving target t_i <- alpha.t_i + (1-alpha).p_theta(.|x_i) with a (C+1)th abstain logit. Entropy regularizer: L_new = L + beta.H(p_theta(.|x)), beta=0.01 (Eq. 7). Recipe: (1) train any selective classifier; (2) discard its selection mechanism; (3) rank samples by Softmax Response g-bar(x) = max_u p_theta(u|x_i) (or -H); (4) calibrate tau on validation for target coverage.
equation: min_{theta,psi} E[l(f_theta(x),y).g_psi(x)] s.t. E[g_psi(x)] >= c_target; L = alpha(L_selective + lambda L_c) + (1-alpha)L_aux; L_selective = (SUM l.g-bar)/(SUM g-bar); L = -(1/m)SUM[t_{i,y_i} log p_theta(y_i|x_i) + (1-t_{i,y_i}) log p_theta(C+1|x_i)]; L_new = L + beta.H(p_theta(.|x)), beta=0.01; g-bar(x) = max_u p_theta(u|x_i)

claim: Selective classification results: ImageNet100 selective error at 80% coverage - SN 6.00 -> SN+SR 4.47; DG 5.21 -> DG+SR 4.52; SAT 5.20 -> SAT+SR 4.46; at 50% coverage - SN 1.05 -> 0.85; SAT 1.18 -> 0.88. SAT+EM+SR: StanfordCars 70% coverage 21.34 -> 15.84 (~26% relative); Food101 70% 4.89 -> 3.52 (~28% relative); ImageNet100 60% 1.72 -> 0.95; ImageNetSubset up to 85% relative improvement over vanilla SAT. ImageNet (SAT): 90% coverage 22.67 -> 21.57; 70% 13.88 -> 12.34 with EM+SR. Key negative result: SelectiveNet's own selection head catastrophically fails at low coverage (99.00% error at 10% coverage), evidence the external head is the failure mode. Fairness caveat (Jones et al. 2021): lowering coverage can magnify recall disparities across groups, relevant if a publish filter systematically withholds certain game types (e.g., divisional, bad-weather games).

Torres et al. (2026, arXiv:2607.24875v1) 'FinAbstain' is an explicit research PROPOSAL (not an executed study) for a selective financial-forecasting system: point-in-time multimodal retrieval, role-separated LLM agents, a composite hybrid uncertainty score, and an abstention controller, plus a preregistered evaluation blueprint; all results in it are labeled simulated, so what transfers is the architecture, the hybrid uncertainty score, and the dual-timestamp backtest-integrity rule. Planned data (not executed): S&P 100 constituents, 2015-2024, survivorship-aware; SEC EDGAR 10-K/10-Q/8-K, earnings-call transcripts, licensed news, OHLCV, MACD, RSI, moving averages, volatility.

FinAbstain uncertainty machinery: point-in-time evidence E_{i,t} = union_{m in M} {e^(m)_j : tau^pub_j <= t, tau^ing_j <= t} (publication AND ingestion timestamps at most t). Agent disagreement: D_{i,t} = (2/(A(A-1))) SUM_{a<b} JSD(p_{a,i,t} || p_{b,i,t}). Relevance-weighted contradiction: C_{i,t} = SUM_{j<k} r_j r_k q_{jk} / (SUM_{j<k} r_j r_k + eps). Hybrid uncertainty: U_{i,t} = sigma(w_0 + w_D D + w_C C + w_S S + w_R R + w_H H + w_G G), where S = 1 - sampling agreement, R = 1 - retrieval relevance (retrieval deficiency), H = predictive entropy, G = recent calibration gap; weights validation-fitted. Controller: y-hat = argmax_y p-bar(y) if U <= theta else abstain; theta selected on validation for minimum selective risk at minimum coverage c_min. Coverage Cov(theta) = (1/n) SUM g_theta; selective Risk(theta) = SUM g_theta l / (SUM g_theta + eps); ECE = SUM_b (|I_b|/n)|acc(I_b) - conf(I_b)|. Trading metrics: net return r^net = z_t r_{t+1} - kappa|z_t - z_{t-1}|, Sharpe, MDD, costs at 5/10/20 bps, block-bootstrap CIs.
equation: E_{i,t} = union_{m in M} {e^(m)_j : tau^pub_j <= t, tau^ing_j <= t}; D_{i,t} = (2/(A(A-1))) SUM_{a<b} JSD(p_{a,i,t} || p_{b,i,t}); C_{i,t} = SUM_{j<k} r_j r_k q_{jk} / (SUM_{j<k} r_j r_k + eps); U_{i,t} = sigma(w_0 + w_D D + w_C C + w_S S + w_R R + w_H H + w_G G); y-hat = argmax_y p-bar(y) if U <= theta else abstain; Cov(theta) = (1/n) SUM g_theta; Risk(theta) = SUM g_theta l / (SUM g_theta + eps); ECE = SUM_b (|I_b|/n)|acc(I_b) - conf(I_b)|; r^net = z_t r_{t+1} - kappa|z_t - z_{t-1}|

claim: FinAbstain numbers are all simulated (the paper's own label, NOT empirical findings): FinAbstain selective accuracy 0.688 at 72% coverage vs calibrated-no-abstention 0.606 at 100%; ECE 0.026 vs raw 0.128; Sharpe 1.08 vs 0.57; MDD 0.112 vs 0.171. Ablations (simulated): removing disagreement/contradiction/calibration each degrades selective accuracy and ECE; the 'no temporal filter' row was intentionally contaminated and excluded (demonstrating why scores alone cannot certify a backtest). These illustrate the intended hypothesis; they are not findings.

Gutierrez-Perez & Agudo (2025, arXiv:2504.10106) SoccerNet-v3D is a pipeline that mints 3D ball-localization annotations from broadcast plus replay soccer footage via field-line camera calibration (PnLCalib), multi-view triangulation, and a closed-loop bounding-box optimizer. Data: SoccerNet-v3 (33,986 images, 12,764 main+replay multi-view systems) -> SoccerNet-v3D (4,051 images; train 3,240 / test 811); ISSIA (six static synchronized 1920x1080 cameras, 25 FPS, 2-min sequence) -> ISSIA-3D (10,544 images; train 8,686 on cameras 3-6 / test 1,858 on cameras 1-2); about 10% manual re-annotation for box validation; code at github.com/mguti97/SoccerNet-v3D.

SoccerNet-v3D annotation equations: calibration quality JaC_gamma = TP_gamma/(TP_gamma+FN+FP) (Eq. 3), TP iff every pitch-segment point reprojects within gamma (% of image diagonal) of annotation, computed at gamma in {0.5, 1, 2}%, with acceptance gate JaC_0.5% > 0.75. Triangulation fusion: p = (1/N)SUM_{i,j}(p_ij | e_ij < tau) (Eq. 4), pairwise triangulations averaged over reprojection error e_ij < tau, with a parallax-angle beta caveat (small parallax gives high uncertainty). Monocular 3D from ball-size prior: p = R^T (phi p_c)/||p_c^+ - p_c^-|| + t (Eq. 7), phi = true ball diameter in meters (sphere prior). Box optimization: argmin_d ||p - R^T phi p_c/||p_c^+(d) - p_c^-(d)|| - t|| (Eq. 8), solved by local minimization; optimal d_opt centers the box on the 3D ray with width/height = d_opt. Baseline: YOLOv11-l 2D detection + PnLCalib + Eq. 7 monocular 3D.
equation: JaC_gamma = TP_gamma/(TP_gamma+FN+FP); p = (1/N)SUM_{i,j}(p_ij | e_ij < tau); p = R^T (phi p_c)/||p_c^+ - p_c^-|| + t; argmin_d ||p - R^T phi p_c/||p_c^+(d) - p_c^-(d)|| - t||

claim: SoccerNet-v3D results: box optimization vs about 10% manual re-annotation - IoU 0.57->0.66; size error 19.01%->7.27% of annotated diagonal. SoccerNet-v3D test (oracle calibration): YOLO_opt AP@0.5 0.81 vs YOLO_base 0.65; 3D MAE 0.81 m vs 15.3 m; MAE_% 5.5 vs 18.3; P_2m 0.30 vs 0.03. With estimated (non-oracle) calibration: MAE_m 4.2 m, P_2m 0.26. ISSIA-3D: YOLO_base AP@0.5 0.04 (total distribution-shift failure); YOLO_ISSIA (fine-tuned on generated boxes) AP@0.5 0.65, MAE_m 4.2 m, MAE_% 4.8, P_2m 0.35. Sensitivity: +-10% pixel-size variation -> 6-14 m 3D error (grows with camera distance); +-2% diagonal center shift -> only 0.6-1.6 m, so size error dominates. Filters: replay pairs with < 1 m camera displacement discarded as unreliable; calibration required JaC_0.5% > 0.75 (4,297 of 12,764 systems passed). The sphere prior (Eq. 7) is invalid for a prolate-spheroid football, blocking direct NFL reuse until an orientation-aware football shape prior is derived.

Duran, Laurent, Rushe & Ventresque (2025, arXiv:2502.09460v1) 'Metamorphic Testing for Pose Estimation Systems' introduces the MeT-Pose framework: a label-free QA protocol for pose estimators using metamorphic rules (input transformations with known output relations) to catch faults without keypoint ground truth. Data: PHOENIX (sign-language; 947,756 frames, dev subset 55,775 images, no keypoint ground truth); FLIC (human pose; 4,552 movie frames, 11 keypoints via Mechanical Turk; test subset 835 images); SUT is MediaPipe Holistic (BlazePose GHUM 3D) in deterministic static-image mode; code at github.com/MatoFD/MeT-Pose.

MeT-Pose rule definition: M = (M.trans, M.rel); img_mod = M.trans(img_orig); check the relation rel between the SUT outputs on the pair; pass iff Err_lmks < t_err. Err_lmks: infinity if landmarks are detected on only one of the pair; 0 if on neither; otherwise the MEDIAN of per-landmark L2_MP (Euclidean normalized: shoulder distance for body, iris distance for face, wrist-to-middle-finger-joint for hands). Rule families: Spatial (Id, Stretch, Mirror h/v/both, Rotation omega), Image quality (Res downscale, Gamma gamma, Bright a+m.v, Bilateral filter, Motion blur), Colour-space (Grey, hue rotation CWheel theta, per-channel scaling, zone-filtered Flt, Cfill). Subsumption: SubRate(M1,M2) = #(violating both)/#(violating M1), or 1 if M1 is never violated. Assumptions: transformations change only landmark positions (not which landmarks should be detected); there is no 'correct' global t_err, it must be user-set per application.
equation: M = (M.trans, M.rel); img_mod = M.trans(img_orig); pass iff Err_lmks < t_err; Err_lmks = inf if detected on one of pair only; = 0 if neither; = MEDIAN of per-landmark L2_MP otherwise; SubRate(M1,M2) = #(violating both)/#(violating M1)

claim: MeT-Pose results: body landmarks at t_err=0.2 (% images with at least 1 violation) - AllRels: PHOENIX 66.35, FLIC 83.83; SubRels: PHOENIX 25.08, FLIC 61.44; {Grey, Mirr_h}: PHOENIX 0.01, FLIC 43.11. Infinite errors (detection on only one image) persist even at high thresholds, always violations. Versus classic ground-truth testing on FLIC: at higher thresholds MeT-Pose finds MORE failures than classic testing (SubRels at t_err=0.2: MeT-Pose-only about 76.6% of stacked failures vs classic-only about 19.9%); MeT-Pose finds larger-magnitude errors that classic testing misses; partial overlap, each finds failures the other misses. Rule-subsumption matrices are strongly dataset-dependent (rules not redundant across domains); stronger motion blur does NOT cleanly subsume weaker blur (Holistic nonlinearity); most violating images fail only a small number of rules, so different rules expose different fault types. Hand landmarks (PHOENIX, Mirr_h/Grey) expose far more faults than body landmarks, so the rule/landmark subset must match the use case.

Oppel & Munz (2024, arXiv:2411.02954) IMUDiffusion is a DDPM adapted from images to synthesize multivariate IMU (accelerometer+gyroscope) time series, lifting a 4-class wearable human-activity classifier to macro F1 = 1.0 on 8/12 held-out participants; verdict REJECT because the stack has no IMU/wearable time series (NGS is RFID position data), though the minority-class-augmentation technique is noted. Data: Banos et al. benchmark (33 activities, 17 participants, 9 Movella IMUs; ideal placement, single thigh IMU, 4 classes: Walking 72.55+-16.42 s, Running 52.59+-5.03 s, Jump Up 11.12+-0.91 s [minority, 20 jumps each], Cycling 69.57+-15.66 s); 12 participants retained (PIDs 1,2,3,5,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,16).

IMUDiffusion architecture and training: forward diffusion x_{k,t} = sqrt(1-beta_{k,t}) x_{k,t-1} + sqrt(beta_{k,t}) eps, eps ~ N(0,I), t in {N | 0 < t < 3000}, k in {Acc, Gyro}; separate linear schedulers beta_Acc = 9e-4, beta_Gyro = 6e-4 (Eq. 2). Sinusoidal step embedding: TE_t = [sin(t/10000^{i/t_dim}), cos(t/10000^{i/t_dim})], t_dim = 128 (Eq. 1). T = 3000 diffusion steps (vs 1000 in Ho et al., needed for a smooth noise-to-motion transition); 3-block U-Net (Down/Mid/Up, 2 ResNet + 2 multi-head attention each, skip connections), base channels 32, downsampling along time only. Training: 4500 epochs, Adam lr 4e-4, smooth-L1 loss (beta_L1 = 1.0); about 8 min/class/participant training + 3 min per 128 sequences (RTX 3090); 78.4 GPU-hours total; 3840 synthetic sequences per class per LOSOCV step. Input: single right-thigh IMU at 50 Hz, 160-timestep windows (shift 40); STFT (Hanning, length 22, overlap 20) -> 12 freq bins x 80 time steps x 12 channels (6 axes x real/imag); per-axis standardization. Downstream classifier: CNN (3 conv 5x1 time-only kernels, MaxPool, 3 linear, dropout 0.3, L2 lambda=1e-4); LOSOCV over 12 participants; conditions 2 Sample (88 real sequences) / Full-Set / 2 Sample + all synth.
equation: x_{k,t} = sqrt(1-beta_{k,t}) x_{k,t-1} + sqrt(beta_{k,t}) eps, eps ~ N(0,I); beta_Acc = 9e-4, beta_Gyro = 6e-4; TE_t = [sin(t/10000^{i/t_dim}), cos(t/10000^{i/t_dim})], t_dim = 128

claim: IMUDiffusion results: 2 Sample Full Synth - macro F1 = 1.0 on 8/12 participants; exceptions PIDs 1, 3, 12, 13; PID 1 dropped BELOW 0.6, i.e., synthetic data hurt (idiosyncratic Cycling style misclassified as Jump Up; cluster analysis Fig. 8). Full-Set baseline: 1.0 on 6/12; synth lifted PIDs 2, 5, 9, 16 to 1.0, beating Full-Set. The conclusion claims at least 11 ppt improvement except PID 1; the abstract claims 'almost 30%' in some cases. Class-level: the 2 Sample baseline confused Running<->Walking in all 12 participants (Running->Walking in 12/12, Walking->Running in 9/12); with synth, confusion in only 1. Minority class Jump Up: zero misclassifications with synth. Dose response (Fig. 9): scores fluctuate +-0.3 with <1500 synth sequences/class (PID 14); <=0.15 at full dose, but 15-20% drops persist for some participants even at 100% dose. No GAN/VAE baseline run (asserted, not compared). UMAP: synth sequences form 2 tight clusters vs broad real-data spread, less visual diversity than claimed. The PID-1 lesson: synthetic augmentation degrades the most atypical subject, a direct caution for any synthetic-data use because synthetic data bakes in training-distribution bias, and atypical cases (e.g., injury-return players) are exactly where it hurts.

Huang et al. (2022, arXiv:2209.13154v1, ECCV 2022 SportsMOT workshop) 'Observation Centric and Central Distance Recovery on Sports Player Tracking' is a motion-first multi-object tracking pipeline (OC-SORT plus central-distance recovery plus sport-specific ReID post-processing) that took 3rd place on SportsMOT 2022 at HOTA 73.968. Data: SportsMOT (ECCV 2022 DeeperAction Challenge) - 45 training clips (basketball, soccer, volleyball) from Olympic Games, NCAA Championship, NBA games on YouTube; 720p, 25 FPS, official recordings, manually cut to avg 485 frames, no shot changes; evaluation on the challenge test set ranked by HOTA. Implementation: YOLOX-X detector (COCO-pretrained, fine-tuned 80 epochs, about 8 h on 4xTesla V100, ByteTrack recipe); OSNet ReID backbone, 10 epochs, Adam lr 0.0003. No explicit equations in the text.

Sports player-tracking pipeline config: detection confidence 0.1, IoU threshold 0.3, track threshold 0.7, max tracklet age 30 frames. Central distance recovery: re-run recovery with Euclidean distance between detection centers and tracklets' last observations when IoU recovery fails (fast players' boxes do not overlap); thresholds basketball 200, soccer 80, volleyball 80. Soccer post-processing: three greedy association rounds; disappear/reappear location gating scaled by time gap (<100 frames -> 100; 100-500 -> 250; >500 -> 400), then appearance cosine distance < 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 per round; tracklet embeddings averaged over frames. Basketball: hard 10-identity cap, EMA appearance updates, re-entry by argmax cosine similarity. Volleyball: cap 12, distance-only reassociation < 400, no appearance. Final step: linear interpolation over gaps.

Sports-tracking results: HOTA went OC-SORT baseline 67.107 -> +central distance recovery 71.764 -> +ReID post-processing 73.968 (3rd place, SportsMOT 2022); final HOTA 73.968, AssA 63.460, DetA 86.316, MOTA 94.832, IDF1 78.271, IDS 2754, Frag 3592; association (63.5) is well behind detection (86.3), so association is the hard part. Leakage flag: the central-distance thresholds were 'based on the evaluation performance on the Sportsmot testing set', i.e., test-set tuned, so the reported HOTA is optimistic. The paper's 'football' is soccer and there is no shot-change handling, so the pipeline as written breaks at every broadcast cut.

Clare, Jamil, Morcrette (2021, arXiv:2103.14430): ResNets that output a 100-bin softmax predictive distribution for weather variables, combined via a shallow CRPS-trained stacking network. Data: WeatherBench / ERA5 reanalysis (1979-2018, 5.625 deg grid), variables Z500 and T850, 3- and 5-day horizons; baselines from Scher & Messori, 'dressed ERA', operational IFS literature values; compute about 12h per ResNet, about 30 min stacking, on RTX6000 (2 GPUs, 48GB).

Binned-softmax distribution architecture: binned softmax PDF p_k = exp(z_k)/SUM_j exp(z_j) over K=100 bins. CRPS on binned CDFs: SUM_bins (CDF_forecast - CDF_obs)^2 x bin width. Stacking: shallow net (two 36-unit ReLU layers + softmax) over concatenated 100-bin member outputs, trained minimizing CRPS on a separate stack split. The paper's within-1sigma/2sigma containment check divides SD by sqrt(100), a misuse of the standard-error formula; the ledger warns DO NOT import it.
equation: p_k = exp(z_k)/SUM_j exp(z_j); CRPS = SUM_bins (CDF_forecast - CDF_obs)^2 x bin width

claim: Stacked-weather results (2017-2018 test): Z500 CRPS 211 (3-day), 1500 (5-day); T850 1.22 (3-day), 1.69 (5-day). Scher & Messori Z500 benchmarks: 526 and 707, so the stacked model beats them substantially. T850 references: dressed ERA 1.44/1.18, operational IFS 0.98, so the stacked model (1.22/1.69) lands between. Within-1sigma containment: 64.7%, 71.2%, 67.3%, 71.2%; within-2sigma: 93.6%, 94.0%, 94.0%, 94.2%, roughly Gaussian-consistent, mildly under-dispersed at 1sigma. Nominal 95%/99% intervals from the paper's flawed CI formula contained only about 14-20% of outcomes.

Landsgesell, Knoll, Wenzel (2026, arXiv:2603.08206v5): how tabular foundation models (realTabPFNv2.5 vs TabICLv2) rank under proper scoring rules (CRPS, CRLS, interval score), and how fine-tuning with scoring-rule losses induces different inductive biases. Data: about 20-23 OpenML regression datasets (house_prices, Bike_Sharing_Demand, california_housing, nyc-taxi-green-dec-2016, etc.), each subsampled to at most 3000 instances, 5-fold CV; synthetic toy datasets (X~Uniform(-4,4) with 25% heavy outliers); fine-tuning code adapted from TabPFN GitHub (PR PriorLabs/TabPFN#689 added CRPS loss, Dec 2025); the 'scoringBench' benchmark is not yet released.

Proper scoring-rule equations: CRPS(F,y) = integral (F(z)-1{y<=z})^2 dz; beta-energy S_beta(F,y) = E_F||X-y||^beta - 1/2 E_F||X-X'||^beta, beta in (0,2) (beta=1 gives CRPS, beta=2 gives MSE-equivalent). CRLS(F,y) = -integral log|F(x)+1{y<=x}-1| dx; interval score S_alpha = (u-l)+(2/alpha)(l-y)1{y<l}+(2/alpha)(y-u)1{y>u}. Power-Bregman objectives (eqs. 20-23, incl. Itakura-Saito p=-1, Poisson/KL p=0); tail-weighted wCRPS (eqs. 24-26, w=(1-u)^2 left / u^2 right). Fine-tuning: lr 1e-5, weight decay 0.1, 600 epochs, early-stopping patience 20, 20,000 ctx+query samples.
equation: CRPS(F,y) = integral (F(z)-1{y<=z})^2 dz; S_beta(F,y) = E_F||X-y||^beta - 1/2 E_F||X-X'||^beta, beta in (0,2); CRLS(F,y) = -integral log|F(x)+1{y<=x}-1| dx; S_alpha = (u-l)+(2/alpha)(l-y)1{y<l}+(2/alpha)(y-u)1{y>u}

claim: Scoring-rule fine-tuning results: beta(1.8)-energy fine-tuning vs baseline - CRPS +2.76%+-6.38% (61/23/6 W/L/T); IS95 +2.24%+-13.86%; MAE +4.28%. CRLS fine-tuning: CRLS +2.27%+-7.00% (79/18/3); IS95 +3.87%+-13.15%. TabICLv2: CRLS +6.01%+-10.95% (84/19/2); IS95 +5.14%+-14.18%. 'No model best in all metrics indicating complex trade-offs.' Toy ranking reversal: Model B (outlier) ranks 1 at beta=0.2 but 4 at beta=2.0; Model A (bias) ranks 2 at beta=0.2, 1 at beta=1.073 and 2.0. Merkle et al. cited: Spearman correlation between Brier- and log-score forecaster rankings only 0.15. Weighted-CRPS XGBoost beats TabICL 14.1% (left tail) / 17.7% (right tail), 15/20 wins. Caveats: early-stopping metric = training objective (acknowledged confound); high std (gains dataset-dependent); log score numerically unstable as f-hat(y)->0; all scoring rules fail to elicit tail-region properties where data are absent.

Chatzidimitriou & Tserpes (2026, arXiv:2609.03790v2): a landmark-based framework for injury-session discrimination when monitoring is minute-resolution but injury labels exist only at athlete-session level (elite women's football, SoccerMon 2020). Data: SoccerMon 2020 (elite Norwegian women's football) - 3,743 athlete-sessions from 48 athletes; modeling cohort 2,259 Team A athlete-sessions from 27 athletes, with all 22 positive sessions arising from just 5 athletes; public code repo linked, raw data not redistributed.

Landmark injury-session protocol: landmark representation X_{a,s,1:l} = within-session monitoring observed no later than landmark l, with landmarks at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 min; the estimand is P(injury-associated session | X_{a,s,1:l}), which is session-level, never minute-level. Feature sets: PRE (14 contextual), CUM (30 expanding summaries), DYN (33 short-horizon dynamics); CUM+DYN (63) is primary. Models benchmarked: logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, TabPFN; augmentation conditions NONE / SMOTE / CTGAN. Metrics: ROC-AUC, PR-AUC with athlete-cluster bootstrap CIs; robustness via leave-one-positive-athlete-out, 100 alternative negative-athlete fold allocations, equal-athlete weighting.
equation: X_{a,s,1:l} = within-session monitoring observed no later than landmark l; estimand P(injury-associated session | X_{a,s,1:l})

claim: Injury-session results: primary CUM+DYN logistic regression ROC-AUC across 10-60 min landmarks: 0.499, 0.557, 0.607, 0.428, 0.402, 0.367 - non-monotonic, near or at chance at later landmarks; the pattern persists on the fixed 2,104-session 60-min common cohort. TabPFN: 0.692 at 30 min; improves later-landmark discrimination vs logistic regression but does not consistently beat Random Forest. PRE+DYN: 0.784 at 20 min (PRE alone about 0.70), but paired contrasts vs CUM+DYN include zero at every landmark; PRE has substantial missingness plus unverified same-day sleep timing, treated as sensitivity, not evidence. Synthetic augmentation is condition-specific, not universal: RF benefits at 30-min SMOTE / 40-min CTGAN; logistic regression shows little benefit and several negative CTGAN contrasts; CTGAN shows distributional drift without near-duplicate memorization. Core stated limitation: only 5 positive athletes, so inferential precision is fundamentally limited; leave-one-positive-athlete-out confirms fragility. The ledger's protocol takeaway: never smear game-level injury labels across sub-game time units; use player-game as the unit with features frozen at weekly checkpoints and player-disjoint folds.

arXiv:2508.07136v2 introduces DTVW (Diversity-driven Time-Varying Weights): a Bayesian forecast-combination method where inter-model forecast disagreement enters the latent weight dynamics as a predictive prior, estimated by particle filtering. Data: author-designed complete/incomplete model simulations; monthly real US IRAC oil prices 1973:01-2024:08 (eval 1992:01-2024:08, from Aastveit et al. 2023 / Garratt et al. 2019 extensions); quarterly BEA GDP growth + PCE inflation 1960:Q1-2009:Q4 (eval 1970:Q1-2009:Q4). No public code (builds conceptually on the DECO Matlab toolbox).

DTVW combination equations: diversity div^l_{k,t,h} = SUM_i(yhat^l_{k,t+h} - yhat^l_{i,t+h})^2 / SUM_i SUM_j(yhat^l_{i,t+h} - yhat^l_{j,t+h})^2. Latent dynamics: x^l_t = theta^l_{0,t} + theta^l_{1,t} x^l_{t-1} + theta^l_{2,t} div^l_{t,h} + eps^l_{1,t}; theta_t = theta_{t-1} + eps_{2,t}; softmax maps latents to simplex weights w^l_{k,t}. Estimation: particle filter, N=1000 particles, ESS-triggered resampling (Billio et al. 2013 style). Initialization: two-stage grid search minimizing CRPS - coarse over [-10,10]^2 (step 2), fine (step 0.5); tuned inits: (7,7) incomplete-sim, (-3,4.5) oil, (-2,9) macro. Point forecasts converted to densities via Metropolis-within-Gibbs (1000 draws after 5000 burn-in).
equation: div^l_{k,t,h} = SUM_i(yhat^l_{k,t+h} - yhat^l_{i,t+h})^2 / SUM_i SUM_j(yhat^l_{i,t+h} - yhat^l_{j,t+h})^2; x^l_t = theta^l_{0,t} + theta^l_{1,t} x^l_{t-1} + theta^l_{2,t} div^l_{t,h} + eps^l_{1,t}; theta_t = theta_{t-1} + eps_{2,t}; softmax -> simplex weights w^l_{k,t}

claim: DTVW results: the estimated diversity coefficient theta_2,t is consistently positive across all sims and empirical apps; in misspecified settings theta_1,t (history) turns negative, i.e., the model distrusts historical signals and leans on diversity. Simulation 1 (true model present): DTVW gains over TVW - 1.56% RMSFE, 2.70% CRPS, 20.83% LS. Simulation 2 (true DGP absent): DTVW reductions vs TVW - 2.43% RMSFE, 15.01% LS, 10.57% CRPS; TVW over-concentrates on the best-RMSFE model while DTVW upweights the second model (best in LS/CRPS). Oil: DTVW best at all horizons, DM 1% significant - 1-step: RMSFE 1.337 vs TVW 1.507 (11.3% gain), LS 0.643 vs 0.849 (24.3%), CRPS 0.511 vs 0.598 (14.5%); 3-step LS gain 33.5%, CRPS 17.8%; 6-step LS 33.2%, CRPS 18.1%. PCE: DTVW RMSFE 0.227 vs TVW 0.252; LS -0.914 vs -0.639; CRPS 0.088 vs 0.106. GDP CRPS 0.301 vs 0.300, a near-miss because initialization was grid-searched on PCE CRPS (authors' own caveat). BMA performs worse than the no-change baseline on probabilistic oil forecasts; BMA_roll beats BMA. During the 2008-09 oil shock, point forecasts deteriorated while density forecasts stayed strong. Caveats: the initialization grid search was tuned on evaluation CRPS (flatters reported gains); particle-filter cost; no public code; point-metric fragility under abrupt breaks.

Choi (2014, arXiv:1403.8125, v4): maximum drawdown (MDD) and its consecutive recovery (R) as portfolio ranking criteria vs cumulative past return, across monthly momentum and weekly contrarian equity portfolios. Data: KOSPI 200 (Jan 2003-Dec 2012, Korea Exchange); SPDR US sector ETFs XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY (Jan 1999-Dec 2012, Bloomberg); S&P 500 (Jan 1993-Dec 2012, Bloomberg); Ken French data library (factors); no code. Design: 6-month/6-week estimation, 10 decile baskets (KOSPI, S&P 500), 3 baskets (ETFs), equally weighted, dollar-neutral long-short, overlapping 1/6 rebuilt monthly (weekly); no transaction costs.

Drawdown path decomposition: MDD = max_tau(max_{t<tau}(P(t) - P(tau))) on log-prices; recovery R = R(t*,T), the log-return from the end of MDD formation to period end; path decomposition C = PP - MDD + R (pre-peak, drawdown, recovery). Seven ranking rules: C (1,1,1 benchmark); M (0,1,0); R (0,0,1); RM (0,1,1); CM (1,2,1); CR (1,1,2); CMR (1,2,2). Risk model: ARMA(1,1)-GARCH(1,1) with classical tempered stable (CTS) innovations for VaR/CVaR/Sharpe; Carhart four-factor regression (MKT, SMB, HML, MOM) on S&P 500.
equation: MDD = max_tau(max_{t<tau}(P(t) - P(tau))); R = R(t*,T); C = PP - MDD + R

claim: Drawdown-momentum results: KOSPI weekly contrarian - benchmark C L-W 0.0731%/wk (sigma 2.8417%); R rule 0.1455%/wk (sigma 1.7567%), about 2x return at about 40% lower vol; R strategy daily VaR95 1.149%, CVaR95 1.391% (lowest of all); strategy MDD 30.09% vs benchmark 33.66%. KOSPI monthly momentum: benchmark C W-L 1.3305%/mo (sigma 6.8258%); CM 1.4330%/mo (sigma 7.0357%, lowest kurtosis); R rule worst at monthly scale (0.3740%/mo). S&P 500 Carhart: weekly contrarian - only significant alpha is R L-W: alpha = 0.1373%/wk (5%); benchmark alpha = -0.0071 (insignificant). Monthly momentum: M W-L alpha = 0.8273%/mo (5%, largest); benchmark alpha = 0.2169 (insignificant). Pattern stated: 'drawdown = trend information, recovery = reversion information' - MDD-based rules dominate at monthly scale, recovery rules at weekly scale. Limitations: no transaction costs (weekly contrarian turnover understated); 7 rules x 3 universes x 2 horizons = multiple-comparison concern; sample ends 2012; equities only.

Herculano (2026, arXiv:2602.21173v1): Bayesian parametric portfolio policies (BPPP) - placing shrinkage priors on linear policy coefficients and Bayesian-averaging via Laplace approximation at the MAP. Data: six Fama-French factors as allocatable assets; 242 signals (212 Open Source Asset Pricing predictors + 30 factor-specific); July 1963-December 2023; 120-month initial training window; 605 monthly OOS observations (1973M8-2023M12); no code stated.

BPPP mechanism: policy form w_t = theta^T x_t (weights linear in signals); Bayesian layer p(theta|data) proportional to p(data|theta) p(theta); Laplace approximation N(theta_MAP, H^{-1}) with H the Hessian at the MAP; marginal likelihood disciplines shrinkage strength (instead of cross-validation). PPP baseline: theta estimated by maximizing in-sample expected mean-variance utility (gamma = 2, 5, 10); transaction costs tested at 10 bps and 50 bps.
equation: w_t = theta^T x_t; p(theta|data) proportional to p(data|theta) p(theta); Laplace approximation N(theta_MAP, H^{-1})

claim: BPPP results (full-period OOS): PPP Sharpe 1.05 / max DD -37.21% / turnover 9.54; BPPP Sharpe 1.32 / max DD -24.50% / turnover 6.03; market 0.74. Net Sharpe at 10 bps: PPP 0.96, BPPP 1.25; at 50 bps: PPP 0.60, BPPP 0.99. CE gain BPPP-PPP: 142 bp (gamma=2), 184 bp (gamma=5), 255 bp (gamma=10). Crisis Sharpe - GFC: BPPP 0.56 vs PPP 0.33; COVID: BPPP 0.89 vs PPP 0.66. BPPP-vs-market Sharpe difference 0.579, bootstrap SE 0.103, t=5.61, p<0.001. Limitations: 242 signals on 60 years of equity data is the ideal shrinkage case (sports signals are fewer/noisier); linear policy class; Laplace quality asserted not diagnosed; equity frictions differ from bet frictions; single asset universe.

Li et al. (2024, arXiv:2411.06391, Renmin/Peking/KAUST): CausalStock - an end-to-end framework pairing an LLM-based Denoised News Encoder (5-dimension scoring rubric) with lag-dependent temporal causal discovery and a functional causal model for news-driven stock movement prediction. Data: six public benchmarks, chronological splits, US+China+Japan+UK - ACL18 (US, Yahoo Finance+Twitter, train 2015/10/01, test 2016/01/01); CMIN-US (110 stocks, train 2018/01/01-2021/04/30, test 2021/09/01-2021/12/31); CMIN-CN (300 stocks); KDD17 (50 stocks, 11 price feats); NI225 (51 stocks); FTSE100 (24 stocks). No code stated; LLM prompts fully specified in Appendix A.

CausalStock mechanism: the Denoised News Encoder has an LLM score each news text on 5 dims - correlation (0-10), sentiment polarity (-1..1), significance/importance (0-10), potential price impact (0-10), duration of impact (0-10) - forming a 5-dim vector embedded per stock-day. Temporal causal graph G = [G_1,...,G_L] in R^{L x D x D}, G_{l,ji}=1 iff X_{t-l}^j -> X_t^i; lag-dependent posterior p(G|X_{<T}) = p(G_1|X_{T-1}) product_{l=2}^L p(G_l|G_{l-1}, X_{T-l}). Variational posterior q_phi(G) = product of Bernoullis per edge with logits coupled across lags by 3-layer MLPs h_u, h_v; Gumbel-softmax gradients; separate causal weight graph G-hat for causal degree. FCM: y_T^i = f_i(Pa_G^i(<T)) + z_T^i, z_T^i ~ N(0,(sigma^i)^2); output through logistic sigmoid. Loss: L = (1/D)(-ELBO + lambda.BCE), lambda = 0.01. Hyperparams: lr 1e-5, lag L=5, price-encoder hidden 4, batch 32, news w=20 words / l=10 news per day; trained on 4x Tesla V100. Investment simulation: top-3 predicted stocks equal weight, daily rebalance; APV^t = product(1+r^i), Sharpe ratio.
equation: G_{l,ji}=1 iff X_{t-l}^j -> X_t^i; p(G|X_{<T}) = p(G_1|X_{T-1}) product_{l=2}^L p(G_l|G_{l-1}, X_{T-l}); y_T^i = f_i(Pa_G^i(<T)) + z_T^i, z_T^i ~ N(0,(sigma^i)^2); L = (1/D)(-ELBO + lambda.BCE), lambda = 0.01; APV^t = product(1+r^i)

claim: CausalStock results: news-driven ACC/MCC - ACL18 63.42+-0.0039/0.2172 vs best baseline CMIN 62.69/0.2090; CMIN-US 54.64/0.0481 vs 53.43/0.0460; CMIN-CN 56.19/0.1417 vs 55.28/0.1110. No-news: KDD17 56.09/0.1235 vs DTML 53.53/0.0733 (+2.56pp); NI225 53.01/0.0640; FTSE100 52.88/0.0534. Investment sim: ACL18 SR 0.369/APV 1.32 vs CMIN 0.357/1.24, market 0.107/1.07. Ablations (ACL18 ACC): w/o TCD 51.08 (MCC 0.0102, so the causal module carries about 12pp and removal collapses to coin-flip); w/o news 58.10; lag-independent 59.19 (-4.23pp vs full); variable-dependent TCD 63.50 but O(L.D^4) vs O(L.D^2), rejected as impractical. News encoders: GPT-3.5 denoised 63.42 > Llama denoised 62.82 > FinGPT denoised 61.92; denoised beats raw embeddings for the same LLM. Causal strength = G circle-times G-hat; Spearman corr(market value, causal strength): ACL18 0.7939 (p=0.006), FTSE100 0.8909 (p=0.0005). Example denoised scores: AAPL 5G-delay news -> sentiment -0.7, impact 9; TSLA delivery milestone -> sentiment +0.7. Limitations (authors' Appendix E): no time-varying graph; Bernoulli captures edge existence only; 'accurate prediction implies reliable causal graph' asserted not proven; LLM scoring used models with cutoffs after some test periods (possible indirect leakage, paper does not address).

Hamilton, Tawn, Firth (2025, arXiv:2312.13619v2, accepted in Statistical Science): a synthesis of the many independent theoretical routes to the Bradley-Terry model (odds transitivity, Luce choice, MaxEnt, discriminal processes, hazards, Poisson scoring, network/spectral forms) plus assumption-failure diagnostics. No new datasets, no empirical validation, no code; the 'results' are the derivations themselves. Illustrative references to standard paired-comparison applications (chess, sports).

Bradley-Terry synthesis routes: BT pairwise probability P(i beats j) = pi_i / (pi_i + pi_j), pi_i > 0. Luce choice: P(i chosen from S) = pi_i / SUM_{j in S} pi_j. Gumbel discriminal process: Y_i = log pi_i + eps_i, eps_i iid Gumbel -> logistic BT; Weibull/Frechet variants give generalized forms. MaxEnt: the BT likelihood is the entropy-maximizing distribution under mean-win constraints (retrodictive criterion). Quasi-symmetry: win-matrix structure yielding BT-type stationary distributions (fair-bets/PageRank connection). Extensions: Rao-Kupper and Davidson tie models; multi-competitor Plackett-Luce forms. Assumptions made explicit: pairwise outcomes independent conditional on worths; worth scale one-dimensional and static; no order-of-comparison effects; ties excluded unless a tie model is adopted.
equation: P(i beats j) = pi_i / (pi_i + pi_j), pi_i > 0; P(i chosen from S) = pi_i / SUM_{j in S} pi_j; Y_i = log pi_i + eps_i, eps_i iid Gumbel

claim: BT synthesis conclusions: multiple historically independent routes (Thurstone-Mosteller, Bradley-Terry 1952, Zermelo 1929, Luce 1959, Plackett 1975) converge on the same functional form, stated as the unifying claim explaining the model's robustness across domains. The existing research map mentioned Bradley-Terry only as an inventoried catalog entry (not deeply researched); the 64-ID dedup set contains no BT derivation paper, so this ledger fills that gap. It complements (does not duplicate) applied BT papers in the same wave (0889 PlackettLuce package, 0890 MaxEnt multi-outcome BT, 0891 luck+depth BT, 0892 dynamic BTL). Limitation: failure diagnostics are discussed in principle but not demonstrated on a real sports dataset with a worked remediation; practitioner translation (what to change when a diagnostic fails) is left to the reader.

SMOGS (arXiv:1806.06696v1): models basketball passing as a non-homogeneous spatio-temporal Poisson process with multiplicative latent sender/receiver factors (u_i^T v_j) estimated by MCMC, and reads a win/loss 'fragmentation vs. overlap' signature off the latent factors. Data: first public SportsVu college-basketball optical tracking dataset (one NCAA D-I team's home games, Dec 2014 - Jan 2015, players anonymized by random ID; 25 Hz snapshots) via three merged XML sources (Boxscore, Play by Play, Sequence Optical); synthetic validation dataset (2 games, 8 players, about 10,000 observations) generated from the model; Hoff et al. R package amen (no code repo stated; dataset download link not given).

SMOGS model equations: pass hazard (6): theta_{i,j}(t) = lim_{eps->0+} P(Y_{i,j}(t) | H(t)) / eps. Full model (10): log(theta_{i,j}(t)) = X_{i,j}(t)^T beta_{i,j} + u_{i,g}^T v_{j,g} + eps_{i,j}(t), with latent term (8): z_{i,j,g}(t) = u_{i,g}^T v_{j,g} + eps_{i,j}(t); R = 2 latent dimensions, game-specific. Preliminary AME (5): log-odds(y_{ij}=1) = beta_d x_d + r_i + s_j + u_i^T v_j + eps_{ij} (fit with Hoff's R package amen). Thin-plate-spline spatial smoother (11): min SUM_k ||n-tilde_k - xi-bar_i(c_k)||^2 + lambda integral_S ||partial^2 xi-bar_i / partial s^2||^2_F ds, lambda by GCV, on 1 ft x 1 ft half-court tiles. 5-dim dyadic covariate W_{i,j}(t): baseline constant; dribble-started indicator; log distance from i to nearest defender; j's closeness rank to i (1-4); passing-route openness (Cervone metric); spatial effects normalized to integrate to 1. Inference: Metropolis-within-Gibbs (Gibbs for beta, U_g, V_g columns; Metropolis for theta intensities); standard multivariate normal priors.
equation: theta_{i,j}(t) = lim_{eps->0+} P(Y_{i,j}(t) | H(t)) / eps; log(theta_{i,j}(t)) = X_{i,j}(t)^T beta_{i,j} + u_{i,g}^T v_{j,g} + eps_{i,j}(t); z_{i,j,g}(t) = u_{i,g}^T v_{j,g} + eps_{i,j}(t); log-odds(y_{ij}=1) = beta_d x_d + r_i + s_j + u_i^T v_j + eps_{ij}

Real data (Table 2): Latent beats Covariate-only: train LL -679.33 +- 114.51 vs -917.89 +- 220.41; held-out LL -58.52 +- 11.20 vs -64.68 +- 12.59. Win/loss signature (Figures 1, 4, interpretive only, no classifier): in the win, starters' sender/receiver effects cluster together ('more overlap, more active teamwork'); in the loss, effects lie farther from origin and ball movement is 'fragmented'. No numeric accuracy/AUC for win/loss prediction; conclusions rest on a handful of games (about 2 months of one team's home games). The 90/10 in-game split means held-out LL is not a true out-of-game test; game-specific latent factors cannot predict a future game (no carry-forward mechanism).

The statistical base (V1) of the ledger's soccer exact-score study is a dynamic GAS model of attack/defense strength and vulnerability with half-life 1,440 days, attack gain 0.04, vulnerability gain 0.02, plus a Dixon-Coles correction with rho = -0.05 on the score matrix.
equation: tau_{xy}(lambda_H, lambda_A, rho), rho = -0.05; half-life h = 1,440 days; gains g_a = 0.04, g_v = 0.02

claim: V1 validation on 5,330 soccer matches (2022-23 through 2024-25) achieved 0.9855 1X2 log loss, 0.5876 Brier, 0.2004 RPS, and 52.8% accuracy.

In the ledger's 150-match 2025-26 EPL dev replay, LLM reranking (V4) improved exact-score Top-1 from 15/150 (10.0%) to 22/150 (14.7%) and Top-3 from 40/150 (26.7%) to 46/150 (30.7%), but McNemar tests vs V1 (Top-1 p=0.2295, Top-3 p=0.3075) were not statistically significant, and V4 did not outperform V1's native 1X2 decision (80/150, 53.33% accuracy).

Failure modes in the replay: no 0-0 result ever appeared in the Top-3 (all 150 root verdicts selected a first goal, never predicting 0-0, so 0-0 was structurally unsolved); among 14 actual 1-1s, V4 placed 1-1 first 4 times and in the Top-3 ten times; high-total (>=4 goals) matches hit only 4/43 exact.

The ledger's verdict is REJECT for LLM reranking of engine outputs (in-sample design: the first 100 of the 150 dev matches explicitly informed V4's design; closed-weight LLM may have memorized outcomes per the authors' own caveat), while the audit architecture is adopted: frozen hash-verified artifacts, strict evidence cutoffs, schema validation of LLM outputs, and separating candidate coverage from reranking quality.

Candidate coverage: the V1 Top-10 held the true score in 116/150 (77.3%) matches; V4 anchors expanded theoretical coverage to 127/150 (84.7%, +11), but an added anchor entered the final Top-3 in only 3 matches and none was an exact hit.

Yeung, Sit & Fujii (2023) factorize football match events jointly as f(...) = product over i of f_t(t_i|H_i) * f_z(z_i|t_i,H_i) * f_m(m_i|t_i,z_i,H_i), with the t->z->m forecast order chosen by grid search; history encoding uses the trailing 40 events -> embeddings + positional encoding -> transformer encoder -> a 31-dimensional history vector H_i.
equation: f(\cdot) = \prod_i f_t(t_i|H_i)\cdot f_z(z_i|t_i,H_i)\cdot f_m(m_i|t_i,z_i,H_i), seqlen=40, H_i \in R^{31}

claim: The NMSTPP model is trained end-to-end with Adam on the loss L(theta) = sum_i [10 x RMSE_{t_i} + CEL_{z_i} + CEL_{m_i}], weighting the time RMSE ten times the two cross-entropy terms.

Holistic Possession Utilization Score (HPUS) is built from HAS = sqrt(E(Zone|H) * E(Action|Zone,H)) / t with t floored at 1, where E(Zone|H) = 0*P(Area_0) + 5*P(Area_1) + 10*P(Area_2) and E(Action|Zone,H) = 0*P(poss loss) + 5*P(dribble/pass) + 10*P(cross/shot); HPUS = sum_i phi(n+1-i) * HAS_i with exponential decay phi(x) = exp(-0.3(x-1)); HPUS++ restricts to possessions ending in attack.
equation: HAS = sqrt(E(Zone|H)\cdot E(Action|Zone,H))/t, E(Zone|H) = 0\cdot P(Area_0) + 5\cdot P(Area_1) + 10\cdot P(Area_2), E(Action|Zone,H) = 0\cdot P(\text{poss loss}) + 5\cdot P(\text{dribble/pass}) + 10\cdot P(\text{cross/shot}), HPUS = \sum_i \varphi(n+1-i)\cdot HAS_i, \varphi(x) = exp(-0.3(x-1))

claim: NMSTPP validation total loss was 4.40 vs fine-tuned Seq2Event-Transformer 4.48, Uni-LSTM 4.51, Modified Seq2Event 4.57, and AR(2)+transition-prob 6.98; NMSTPP was best on zone CEL (2.04) and action CEL (1.33) and tied best RMSE_t (0.10) with only 79K parameters and 49 minutes of training.

HPUS correlated -0.78 with final 2017/18 Premier League ranking and 0.92 with both goals and xG without using any goal data; dependent t->z->m heads beat independent heads (4.40 vs 4.44 total loss), and 20-zone discretized features matched raw (x,y) features (RMSE_t 0.10, action CEL 1.33 both) with better explainability.

Class imbalance was handled with weight_i = n_samples / (n_classes x n_samples_in_class_i) plus a post-hoc dribble weight x1.16 tweak; the ledger flags that the 0/5/10 HAS weights and 0.3 phi decay are hand-chosen rather than tuned.

Thomas et al. model each team's scoring as competing Cox processes h(X,t) = h_0(t) * h_1(X) with flat baseline h_0(t) = 1, giving scoring rates lambda^h = exp(r^h + sum_p(X_p^h omega_p + X_p^a delta_p)) and lambda^a = exp(r^a + sum_p(X_p^a omega_p + X_p^h delta_p)), where (omega_p, delta_p) are player p's offensive/defensive contributions (zero = average); MESH = omega_p - delta_p.
equation: h(X,t) = h_0(t)\cdot h_1(X), h_0(t)=1, \lambda^h = exp(r^h + \sum_p(X_p^h \omega_p + X_p^a \delta_p)), \lambda^a = exp(r^a + \sum_p(X_p^a \omega_p + X_p^h \delta_p)), MESH = \omega_p - \delta_p

claim: Estimation used a Laplace-Gaussian prior pdf f(x|lambda,sigma^2) proportional to exp(-sigma^2 lambda^2/2 - lambda|x| - x^2/(2 sigma^2)) with partial pooling by position, fit by Gibbs/Metropolis MCMC in R+C++ taking 60 processor-hours for 200k outcomes x 2600 covariates; the penalized path chose Lasso lambda=8 out-of-sample and pair-interaction lambda_pair=8.5 (247 nonzero of 2000 pair params).

Out-of-sample doubled negative log-likelihood ordered Score < Team < Player models in all five NHL seasons (totals 76416 / 76397 / 76087); only 37 of 1,592 players had 95% CIs excluding zero for net MESH (36 positive, 1 negative), with leaders Datsyuk 0.463, Crosby 0.388, H. Sedin 0.355; rating 0.1 corresponds to about 0.3 goals/game differential.

Offense and defense estimates are roughly uncorrelated; forwards carry offensive variability; skater defensive variability is much smaller than offensive (goalie absorbs defense); centers affect defense more than defensemen do; pair chemistry showed best Boyes-McClement +0.393, worst Kovalchuk-White -0.545 (wiping out their positive individuals), and adding pairs flipped #1 from Datsyuk to Crosby.

Home-ice advantage was confirmed every season and scoring rates were elevated (both teams) when the game was not tied; limitations include flat baseline hazard discarding within-shift dynamics, power plays excluded, player ability constant over five seasons (no aging), and pair selection with no uncertainty quantification.

Dynamic Rank Centrality (Algorithm 1): (1) time-neighborhood N_delta(t) = {t' : |t-t'| <= delta/T}; (2) union graph G_delta(t); (3) locally averaged win fractions ybar_ij(t) = |N_ij,delta(t)|^{-1} sum y_ij(t'); (4) Rank Centrality transition matrix P-hat(t) (eq. 2.5), normalization d_delta(t) >= d_max; (5) leading left eigenvector pi-hat(t) as the time-varying strength estimate.
equation: N_\delta(t) = \{t' : |t-t'| \leq \delta/T\}, \bar{y}_{ij}(t) = |N_{ij,\delta}(t)|^{-1} \sum y_{ij}(t'), \hat{P}(t) \text{ Rank Centrality transition matrix}, \hat{\pi}(t) = \text{leading left eigenvector}

claim: Speed: n=100, T=150: DRC 13.2±0.19s vs kernel-MLE 65.99±5.97s; n=400, T=100: DRC 59.58±2.28s vs MLE 551.54±56.71s — roughly 5-10x faster (eigenvector vs optimization) at equal accuracy on synthetic benchmarks.

On NFL 2009-2015 (32 teams, 16 rounds/season), DRC strength-Elo correlations for 2011-2015 were 0.425/0.518/0.284/0.478/0.414 vs kernel-MLE 0.092/-0.237/-0.337/-0.026/0.002; Kendall rank correlations with Elo ranks were low for all methods (-0.201 to 0.245).

Fantasy integer program: max Z = sum_j c_j x_j + sum_j c_j y_j (captain doubles), subject to sum x = 11, sum v_j x_j <= 83.5 (budget net of reserves), sum y = 1, y <= x, position min/max, at most 3 players per real team; robust variant uses box uncertainty U = {c_j in [cbar_j - d_j, cbar_j + d_j]} with max_{x,y} min_{c in U} sum c_j (x_j + y_j).
