claim: In the FPL 2023/24 estimator bake-off (train GW1-26, evaluate GW27-38), the hybrid estimator scored the single best week (83 pts, GW27) and Monte Carlo 82 (GW27) plus best in GW30 and GW33, while linear-weighted average (w_i = i/sum j) was the most consistent, posting the top score in 5 gameweeks, more than any other method.

Robust min-max versions did NOT beat deterministic (except robust ICT, roughly tied) - box robustness added nothing empirically; the ICT objective beat EGI-EGC by a wide margin; ARIMA(0,1,1) was the most stable ARIMA while linear regression and ARIMA were weakest overall.

Emergent behavior across all strong estimators: every top method chose a 3-5-2 formation; Ollie Watkins appeared in every team; keepers were picked from weak defenses (save volume); expensive chalk (Salah, Haaland) was mostly excluded on value; evaluation dropped weeks with any missing player data entirely (selection bias flaw) and omitted covariance/stacking.

Weighted hybrid rating Omega(p) = sum omega-hat_i(p) mu_i(p) with |omega| normalized to 1 and sign kept, where weights come from a logistic regression Logit(Y-hat) = I + sum omega_i mu_i + epsilon (binary) or proportional-odds (ordinal); F(p) = sum l_i(p) mu_i(p) is the factor-rating form with loadings l.

Omega was best overall in all 12 dataset x setup cells vs Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill: Halo Slayer all-setups Omega 63.0 vs Elo 61.4; Halo CTF Omega 66.6 vs Elo 63.9; CS:GO top-tier Omega 67.0 vs TrueSkill 57.2 (systems collapse, ~10-point gap); PUBG top-tier NDCG Omega 79.2 vs Elo 71.7.

Example construction: CS:GO Support = 0.669590 x KillAssist + 0.330410 x FlashAssist; Omega_CS:GO = 0.552309 x Skill + 0.276699 x Experience + 0.170992 x Support; factor loadings include CS:GO Skill = Damage 0.3871 + KD 0.2707 + Accuracy 0.1838 + WinRate 0.1585.

Experience carried 22-32% of the regression weight in all four games (CS:GO 0.2767, PUBG 0.2833, Halo-Slayer 0.3202, Halo-CTF 0.2190); negative features (betrayal, suicide) got tiny weights; team rating = MAX of member ratings (star-player model) disagrees with the 0934 chain's sum aggregation and was never reconciled.

EventGPT context block: c = (pID_{1:22}, minute, h_{g'}, a_{g'}, h_{r'}, a_{r'}), 22 on-pitch player IDs plus match minute and cumulative goals/red/yellow home/away; event tokens v_t = (h_t, e_t, x_t, y_t, delta_t, o_t, rOBV_t) with residual on-ball value rOBV_t = E[sum_{tau=t}^{T_episode} OBV_tau | state at t, player p_t]; training loss L = -sum_{t=1}^{T} log P(v_{t+1} | c, p_{1:t}, v_{1:t}) with teacher forcing; player ID conditions predictions but is NEVER predicted, enabling counterfactual substitution.
equation: c = (pID_{1:22}, minute, h_{g'}, a_{g'}, h_{r'}, a_{r'}, h_{y'}, a_{y'}), v_t = (h_t, e_t, x_t, y_t, \delta_t, o_t, rOBV_t), rOBV_t = E[\sum_{\tau=t}^{T_{episode}} OBV_\tau | \text{state at } t, \text{player } p_t], L = -\sum_{t=1}^{T} \log P(v_{t+1} | c, p_{1:t}, v_{1:t})

claim: Next-event results (h up, e up, x/y down, t down, a up, rOBV down): LEM 85.20%/74.07%/9.01/8.11/1.37/90.51%/0.014; LEM Transformer 96.05%/80.42%/7.15/7.08/1.40/86.92%/0.008; EventGPT 94.12%/82.91%/4.30/4.31/1.11/92.87%/0.009 - event type +2.5pp over LEM Transformer, spatial MAE roughly halved, rOBV MAE 0.009 (second best).

Counterfactual case studies: in Haaland's Man City context Isak's predicted rOBV 3.76 (own OBV 4.94) exceeded Haaland's own sim 2.71 (~GT 2.59), while Haaland dropped to 1.37 in Hojlund's Man Utd context; elite finishers' value collapses in weaker systems, and Haaland placed in Arsenal defensive contexts scored 2.35/1.42/1.98/1.37 vs original-player sims 5.19/3.63/5.14/8.78 - value is context-shaped, not label-shaped.

t-SNE of EventGPT player embeddings shows clean role clusters (CB/FB dense, wing-backs intermediate, AM/winger/FW sub-clusters) with no positional labels used in training; limitations include unvalidated substitution fidelity vs actual transfers, acknowledged positive bias (Saka sim 18.59 vs GT 15.72), and player embeddings learned on the same players in test (interpolation, not zero-shot).

Standard Glicko equations quoted in the paper: E_A = 1/(1+10^{-(R_A-R_B) g(RD_B)/400}); g(RD) = 1/sqrt(1+3 RD^2/pi^2); RD_A' = 1/sqrt(1/RD_A^2 + 1/d^2); d^2 = 1/(g(RD_B)^2 E_A (1-E_A)); r_A' = r_A + g(RD_B)(S_A-E_A)/sqrt(1/RD_A^2 + 1/d^2).

The logistic scale was recalibrated by grid search over Brier/MAE/log-loss/ECE to d = 85 for Test cricket (vs chess default 400), giving E_A = 1/(1+10^{c(R_B-R_A)/d}); d=85 beat d=400 by 17% on Brier (0.1601 vs 0.1929), 10.52% on log-loss (0.5946 vs 0.6645), 10.33% on MAE, 13.56% on ECE.

Home and toss effects were added as additive rating adjustments, e.g. E_{i,home} = 1/(1+10^{-(R_i-R_j+h_{i,j}) g(RD_j)/85}), combined via the Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copula E = F(H)G(T)[1+omega(1-F(H))(1-G(T))] with omega = -0.5436 (from Spearman rho = -0.1812 = omega/3), selected over Gaussian/Frank/Plackett by AIC.

Margin-of-victory-scaled update uses S_A = (1+MOV)/2 (win), (1-MOV)/2 (loss), 1/2 (draw) with MOV_i = ((R_i-R_min)/range_R)^{beta_i} * ((W_i-W_min)/range_W)^{1-beta_i} + I_i*(E4P_i+ERM_i)/TR_i, fed into r_A' = r_A + g(RD_B)((1+/-MOV_i)/2 - E_A)/sqrt(1/RD_A^2 + 1/d^2); the ledger notes Table 17 MOV values exceed 1 (e.g., 1.886), breaking the probabilistic interpretation of (1+MOV)/2.

Results: winner predicted correctly in 44 of 56 non-drawn matches (~78.6%) in the WTC 2021-23 test window; Spearman rank correlation 0.9624 between the Glicko ranks and ICC ranks; home advantage 82 home wins vs 41 away wins (Pearson chi2 p = 3.386e-7); toss 75 wins after winning toss vs 50 after losing (p = 0.002399); bootstrap (100 permutations) average coefficient of variation 0.44%, SD ~0.436 rating points.
Draw predictor D_{alpha,A,B} = alpha(1-E_A-E_B) + (1-alpha)|E_A-E_B| with (alpha,q) = (0.6, 0.67); alpha in [0.55, 0.6] correctly flags 9 of 12 test draws in the top 33-35% quantile.

Bayesian Predictive Decision Synthesis (BPDS) mixture: f(y|x) proportional to sum_{j=0:J} pi_j(x) alpha_j(y|x) p_j(y|x, M_j), where pi_j(x) are decision-dependent model probabilities (weights vary over the decision space, incorporating past predictive fit AND past decision outcomes) and alpha_j(y|x) are outcome-dependent calibration functions.

Entropic (exponential) tilting: alpha_j = exp{tau(x)' s(y,x)} with bounded score functions, solving E_f[s(y,x)] = m_f(x) (target expected score) via tau(x) per candidate decision x; equivalent reweighted-mixture form f(y|x) = sum pi-tilde_j(x) f_j(y|x, M_j) with f_j = alpha_j p_j / a_j and pi-tilde_j = k(x) pi_j a_j.

Case study findings: expected utility of BPDS exceeded BMA in virtually every period (graphical, no formal test), substantially higher pre-financial-crisis and similar after; BPDS predictive mixtures are less dispersed than BMA (BMA more heavy-tailed, especially at long horizons); both typically recommended larger rate changes than policymakers actually implemented.

Importance-sampling ESS of the tilted mixture stayed 90-95% pre-COVID (small, desirable tilting), collapsed during the COVID recession but recovered with decisions still 'sensible'; mixture ESS stayed above individual-model ESS throughout - ESS collapse is a feasibility diagnostic for whether a target expected score is realistic.

Wald statistical decision framework: states of nature s, sampling distributions Q_s, statistical decision functions phi(psi); evaluation by maximum regret max_s E_s[R_s(phi)], not Bayes risk; clinical normalization U(A,0)=1, U(A,1)=0, U_B in (0,1) gives threshold rule p_x* = 1 - U_B: choose B iff p_x > p_x*.
equation: R_s[\varphi(\psi)] = |(1-p_s) - U_B| \cdot e[p_s, \varphi(\psi), U_B], p_x^* = 1 - U_B

claim: Hoeffding regret bound for the sample-mean rule: max_s E_s[R_s(n/N)] <= delta + max[(1-p_m) - U_B, U_B - (1-p_M)] * exp(-2 N delta^2), with a bounded-variation pooled-sample extension using exp[-2(N_0+N_1) delta^2].

Exact weighted-estimator minimax-regret results (Table 1): (N_0,N_1)=(10,10): 0.030 at w=0.751; (5,15): 0.034 at 0.863; (15,5): 0.023 at 0.752; (20,20): 0.021 at 0.858 - optimal weights favor own-group sample but borrow substantially from the other group; one-observation max regret has closed form 1/4 * max[(1-U_B)^2, U_B^2].

Wald decision criteria without data: (1) max_{c in C} integral w(c,s) d pi (subjective average welfare); (2) max_{c in C} min_{s in S} w(c,s) (maximin); (3) min_{c in C} max_{s in S}[max_{d in C} w(d,s) - w(c,s)] (minimax regret); as-if optimization c[s(psi)] in argmax_{c in C} w[c,s(psi)] acts as if the estimate were the true state.

Hodges-Lehmann (1950) minimax-regret predictor for [0,1] outcomes: (mu_N sqrt(N) + 1/2)/(sqrt(N) + 1); missing-data midpoint predictor E(y|delta=1)P(delta=1) + 1/2 P(delta=0) with max regret 1/4[P(delta=1)^2/K + P(delta=0)^2].

The midpoint predictor beats the sample-average-of-observed-outcomes when all distributions are feasible: max MSE ~1/4 the size at observability <=0.8 (Table 1A N=100: 0.1952 at P(delta=1)=0.1 vs Table 2A 0.7779), ~1/2 at 0.9; identification (bias) dominates imprecision when observability <0.7.

Utah juvenile-sentencing example: max regret of mandate-confinement (a) = 0.45 vs mandate-no-confinement (b) = 0.55, so (a) minimizes maximum regret, yet the empirical-success rule picks (b) because 0.41 > 0.23 - as-if optimization selects the MMR-inferior treatment.

TVCalib segment reprojection loss (Eq. 2): L = (1/|S|) sum_c d_mean(undistort_psi(x^(c)), pi_phi(s^(c))) - mean point<->line / point<->point-cloud distance per segment, NDC-normalized; point-line distance (Eq. 1): d(p, s-hat_line) = |det((pi_phi(X_1)-pi_phi(X_0)); (pi_phi(X_0)-p))| / |pi_phi(X_1)-pi_phi(X_0)|.

Composite score CS = (1-e^{-4 CR}) * sum_t w * AC@t with w=[0.5,0.35,0.15], t in {5,10,20}px, AC@t = TP/(TP+FN+FP); optimizer AdamW lr 0.05, weight decay 0.01, 2000 steps, one-cycle; self-verification reject at loss > tau=0.019.

On SN-Calib-test-center with ground-truth segmentation, TVCalib(tau) achieved AC@5/10/20 = 68.7/88.0/96.1, CR 92.8, CS 76.9 vs HDecomp baselines (53.7/77.5/88.4, CS 65.1); with predicted segmentation AC@5 drops 68.7->57.6 - segmentation quality is the bottleneck, not the calibration optimizer; ledger verdict REJECT (domain-disjoint from sports prediction).
Joint lens-distortion learning improves WC14 AC@5 from 64.4 to 68.4 but causes trivial FoV-explosion local minima on low-FoV SN-Calib samples (CR 92.3->78.3).

Exhaustive consistent score for alpha-prediction intervals (4.6): S_exh(A,y) = alpha mu(A) - mu(((-inf,y] x [y,inf)) intersect A); normalized mixture form (4.8): S_mu = (1-alpha) mu(((-inf,y] x [y,inf)) \ A) + alpha mu(A \ ((-inf,y] x [y,inf))).

Theorem 4.16: the SHORTEST alpha-prediction interval (alpha in (0,1)) is NOT elicitable in either the selective or exhaustive sense - the first non-degenerate nowhere-elicitable set-valued functional; governance rule: never target 'tightest calibrated interval'.

Theorem 3.7: for functionals with the proper-subset property, selective and exhaustive elicitability are mutually exclusive - quantiles are selectively elicitable, hence never exhaustively; interval sets can never be scored selectively, and mixing modes invalidates comparisons.

Coverage-only evaluation (V_sel = 1{y in [x_1,x_2]} - alpha) is an identification function, not a score - it cannot rank intervals; quantile endpoints ARE elicitable via pinball loss; discrete outcomes (e.g., integer NFL totals) break singleton-quantile regularity - consistency survives but strict consistency degrades.

Elementary scores S_u give Murphy diagrams: plot mean score difference Delta(u) over a parameter grid u in U; variant dominance must hold under every consistent scoring function; the ledger's numeric gate promotes a challenger engine only if its Murphy curve lies at/below the incumbent's on >=95 of 100 elementary-score grid points plus DM significance.

LASSO (alpha=0.1722 via 10-fold CV) and OLS on Syracuse solar-panel data: LASSO MSE default 5.5436, 60%-train 5.5045, alpha=0.001 -> 5.4459; OLS full-data 5.4248, 60/40 split 5.4147; top-25-feature model MSE 5.4968 - model differences tiny and likely noise, units unstated; the study never ran the with/without-weather ablation its title promises and used random 60/40 splits on time-ordered data (invalid for forecasting = train/test leakage).
Ledger verdict REJECT: methodologically weak (random splits on autocorrelated time series, no weather-value ablation, unclear units) and domain-disjoint from sports; superseded by ledger 1302.

CNN sentiment classifier augmented with sentiment/emotion lexicon-embedding channels and attention over lexicon channels (SC-EAV and NC-EAV variants, with/without attention); training-vocabulary lexicon coverage only 11.53% (SemEval) and 9.20% (SST), with coverage gaps handled by zero/default vectors.

SemEval SC-EAV: 63.8 vs baseline 61.6 (cited systems 63.3, 63.0); SST SC-EAV/NC-EAV: 48.8% vs baseline 47.5% (strongest cited 49.6% still beats it); lexicon models substantially more stable across embedding sizes: baseline run-to-run SDs 0.8491, 1.1909 vs lexicon-model SDs 0.4208, 0.5764.

VADER on article text plus DistilBERT on headlines with log-odds transform log(p/(1-p)); lagged sentiment + lagged price features (lag-3 focus); OLS/ridge/lasso/elastic-net; temporal split train 2021-01-01 to 2023-08-31, test 2023-10-01 to 2024-02-22, September 2023 discarded as buffer.

Baseline (lag-3 price-only) RMSE: 134.85; DistilBERT lag-3: linear 128.78, ridge 128.74, lasso 223.45, elastic net 133.79 - about 4.5% RMSE reduction from sentiment with ridge; the lasso blowup to 223.45 signals multicollinear, fragile features; flaws include weekend forward-fill muddying the weekend boundary and a price-LEVEL target (RMSE 134.85 on index ~22,000 = 0.6%) making gains economically meaningless vs returns/direction.

Causal-ICM rank-2 intrinsic coregionalization GP: f^e(x) = u_1(x); f^o(x) = rho f^e(x) + sqrt(1-rho^2) u_2(x); u_1, u_2 ~ GP(0,k) independent; rho in (0,1) selected by 5-fold CV over {0.0, 0.1, ..., 1.0} minimizing weighted held-out experimental error; proven variance bound V^e(x*) >= (1-rho^2) * V^e_De(x*) - borrowing shrinks uncertainty by at most a rho-tied factor.
equation: f^e(x) = u_1(x), f^o(x) = \rho f^e(x) + \sqrt{1-\rho^2} u_2(x), V^e(x^*) \geq (1-\rho^2)\cdot V^e_{De}(x^*)

claim: Tennessee STAR validation RMSE: Causal-ICM 6.29; experimental GP 6.36; observational GP 7.47; experimental grounding GP 6.38; RF 6.27 (essentially tied - headline advantage is simulation robustness, not a real-data win); Integrative HTE 11.84; under misspecification Causal-ICM RMSE 2.586 (1.513) vs GP exp 3.422 (2.186) vs Integrative HTE 21.883 (3.330).

rho sensitivity: RMSE minimized near rho=0.8 (0.305), rising at rho=1.0 (1.095) where confounding is no longer absorbed; RBF kernel 0.822 (0.651) beats Matern variants; out-of-support MSE 1.071 (0.722) vs Integrative HTE 3.153 (0.919) vs Kallus GP 43.461 (42.069); runtime 4.56s vs Integrative HTE 6.01s per 100 datasets.

Per-position (8 positions) Lasso: (alpha-hat, beta-hat) = argmin sum(y_i - alpha - sum beta_j x_ij)^2 + lambda sum|beta_j| (lambda 0.004-0.01, 5-fold CV then raised to force 10-15 features); Random Forest: y-hat_RF = (1/n_trees) sum y-hat_tree_k (100 trees, max depth 6); target log market value; normalization x_ij = (x_ij - xbar_j)/max(x_j); CV R^2 = 1 - MSE_cv/VAR(y).

With league-average-value: Lasso CV-R^2 GK 48.5%, FB 55.4%, CD 57.7%, CDM 60.0%, CM 61.5%, AM 55.9%, WG 57.4%, FWD 58.0%; RF 53.8%/54.1%/58.1%/61.2%/61.5%/52.8%/54.3%/57.4% (Lasso ~ RF, honest headline); without league-average-value R^2 drops to ~35-44% - the league anchor contributes roughly 20 points of R^2.

Top features everywhere: league_avg_value, total_minutes_on_field, age (age_sq negative); long-pass volume has NEGATIVE coefficient for CBs/DMs (modern build-up preference); goals scored not selected for forwards (collinear with touches-in-box/linkup features); Golden Boy: predicted top-13 included 9 of the jury's top-10 with Kendall correlation 0.38 vs present-value-vs-jury 0.24 - the model beats the current market at matching expert judgment.

Data-replication method: outputs ordered C_1 < C_reject < C_2; each point replicated twice into R^{d+1}: [x;0] and [x;h]; replica 1 discriminates C_1 vs {C_reject,C_2} with high cost on C_2 errors; replica 2 discriminates {C_1,C_reject} vs C_2 with high cost on C_1 errors; one binary classifier on 2l replicated points with non-intersecting boundaries; prediction rule (C_1,C_1)->C_1, (C_2,C_1)->reject, (C_2,C_2)->C_2.

Loss L = 0 correct, w_r reject, 1 error; empirical risk = w_r * R + E with 0 <= w_r <= 1 (w_r = C_low/C_high) and the constraint w_r < 0.5 (above that, random guessing beats rejecting); rejoSVM outperformed all comparators (two-independent-classifiers, post-hoc threshold, Fumera embedded-reject SVM, Frank-Hall-style ordinal) over the FULL w_r range on all six datasets; the authors admit the Fumera baseline may have been misused, and w_r is still a hyperparameter so the 'no thresholds' claim is partial.

Markov score recursion: V(s) = q(s) V(T1(s)) + (1-q(s)) V(T2(s)); deuce D(q) = q^2/(q^2+(1-q)^2); Elo update R_{i,t+1} = R_{i,t} + K_{i,t}(S_{i,t} - q_{i,t}) with K_{i,t} = 250/(m_{i,t}+5)^0.4; Elo gap d -> serve edge e = clip(alpha*d, -0.15, 0.15), alpha grid-searched (selected 1.3e-4).

Bayesian shrinkage of live serve rate toward the Elo prior: theta-hat = (n/(n+k)) theta_live + (k/(n+k)) theta_prior; selected kappa = 640/160/40 at 25/50/75% match progress (shrinkage weakens as evidence accumulates).

Trace hybrid stacks [p_Markov, p_shrink, logit(p_Markov), logit(p_shrink), p_shrink - p_Markov, live features] in HistGradientBoostingClassifier; on the tennis test set it posted accuracy 0.7606/0.8215/0.8834 at 25/50/75% progress (77.84% all-points) with log loss 0.4753/0.3530/0.2002 - highest accuracy and lowest log loss in every column vs all four baselines; Trace's largest lead over baselines is mid-match (~40-70% progress).

Serve-shrink Markov: 0.7564/0.7946/0.8720 accuracy with log loss 0.5142/0.4266/0.2842 - beats Elo-asymmetric Markov on log loss at every checkpoint despite similar accuracy (better probability quality); HGBM alone was weak early (0.6944 acc at 25%, below symmetric Markov) but the strongest single model late (75%: acc 0.8738, log loss 0.2299).

Negative Binomial GAM: log(Shots) ~ s(Diff.S) + s(Diff.RC) + Home + s(Diff.WP) + s(GM|Half=1) + s(GM|Half=2) + s(Team) + s(season), with GCV for spline df, extreme bins |score|>3->+/-3, |RC|>2->+/-2, minute 45+->45, team/season random-effect smooths; neutral-baseline adjustment multiplies output by e^{-(eta_hat_s - eta_hat_0)} for score differential s, e^{-(eta_hat_rc - eta_hat_0)} for red-card differential, e^{-gamma_hat} for away->home, with 95% CIs from GAM Bayesian posterior covariance; NO adjustment for win-probability differential (don't penalize strength) or minute.
equation: \log(Shots) \sim s(Diff.S) + s(Diff.RC) + Home + s(Diff.WP) + s(GM|Half=1) + s(GM|Half=2) + s(Team) + s(season), \text{adjust} \times e^{-(\hat{\eta}_s - \hat{\eta}_0)}

claim: Multiplicative context coefficients: trailing teams shoot x0.70-0.90; leading teams x1.10-1.75; up a man x0.75 (down 1), x0.40-0.70 (up 2+); down a man x1.7-1.9 (down 1), x2-3 (down 2+); concrete adjustments: Bordeaux 31 shots -> 13.8 [12.5,15.1] (2-man advantage while trailing); Bayern 15 -> 31.9 [30.1,33.7] (12th-minute red card, led throughout); Real Madrid 40 -> 60.7; PSG 18 corners -> 9.5.

Adjusted stats correlate more with points earned than raw: shots 0.787 vs 0.718; corners 0.737 vs 0.603; significantly beat raw stats in forecasting future score differentials (paired t-test, Holm p<0.01 all leagues); but the forecasting gain was marginal in magnitude: RMSE reduction 0.004-0.04 goals/game (1.5-15.2 goals over 380 games), statistically significant but practically small per the authors' own admission.

Predictive LOSOCV per-game totals: shots MAE 3.24-3.53/game (27-28% of mean), R^2 21-31%; corners MAE 1.9-2.1 (40% of mean), R^2 17-22%; season-level: 8/10 strongest positive adjustments were league winners, 8/10 strongest negative were relegated teams.

The paper is a two-page conceptual note with no data, no estimation, no validation, and no transferable method: three hypothetical teams split $6M across Offence/Defence/Goalie (Montreal 1/1/4; Boston 2/2/2; New York 3/3/0), each pair playing 9 head-to-head matchups of the three numbers; the constructed tallies BOS over MTL 6-3, NY over BOS 6-3, MTL over NY 5-4 form an intransitive cycle (NY > BOS > MTL > NY) built by construction, not estimated; verdict REJECT.

SVR objective: (w*,b*) = argmin_{w,b} (C/N) sum_i V_epsilon(y_i - (x_i w + b)) + ||w||^2_2 with epsilon-insensitive loss V_epsilon; grid over kernel {RBF, sigmoid, linear, polynomial}, C in {0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0}, epsilon 0.05-0.25, gamma {0,0.05,0.1,0.15}, degree {2,3}; best SVR (RFECV, C=0.25, epsilon=0.25, linear kernel): RMSE 7.759 / MAE 6.221 / MRE 0.448 (all test cases).

RFECV kept only 4 features: age, years pro, passing attempts (last 10), successful passing 2-pt conversions (last 10) - touchdowns dropped, flagged by the author as suspicious (symptom of correlated features + small data); the author's own verdict: 'the errors were still very high. For example, the MAE of the best prediction was more than 6 points, which can make a difference in most Fantasy Football games.'

Portable EWMA feature proposal: S_t = alpha G_t + (1-alpha) S_{t-1}, replacing last-game/last-10-average feature pairs; methodological holes: no baseline of any kind (not even 'repeat last week's score'), test = one season, QB-only, MRE defined with prediction (not actual) in the denominator.

Plackett-Luce joint likelihood for listwise preference rankings: P_psi[sigma^(1) >> ... >> sigma^(K)] = product_{k=1}^{K} exp(r-hat_psi(sigma^(k))) / sum_{j=k}^{K} exp(r-hat_psi(sigma^(j))), with segment reward r-hat_psi(sigma) = sum_t r-hat_psi(s_t, a_t), trained via negative log-likelihood.

Best PL config (K=4) achieved 86% mean final success rate (Drawer Open 86±3.7, Door Close 48±19.3, Button Press 41±18.4), matching the Oracle baseline on Drawer Open; BT-Kwise K=5 hit 89±7.1 on Drawer Open; no single ranking size or formulation dominates universally; verdict REJECT - robotic manipulation with zero sports-relevant claim, data, or transfer path.

SIDO per-minute ally impact: Delta = beta_0 + b_c + b_p + epsilon_g, Delta = sum_a (Y_ag - E[Y_ag]) (per-player ally differential, summed over teammates); model: gold_pg = beta_0 + b_c + b_p + epsilon_pg (Eq. 1); priors: beta_0 ~ N(0,1); b_c ~ t_3(0,phi), b_p ~ t_3(0,tau); phi,tau ~ HalfC(0.5); sigma ~ HalfC(0.3).
equation: \Delta = \beta_0 + b_c + b_p + \epsilon_g, \Delta = \sum_a (Y_{ag} - E[Y_{ag}]), gold_{pg} = \beta_0 + b_c + b_p + \epsilon_{pg}

claim: Champion proficiency: delta_pc = (1/n_pc) sum(Y_pg - beta-hat_0 + b-hat_c) (Eq. 3); SIDO (solo) measures player skill vs champions-as-cohort baselines; b_p for allies/enemies isolates teammate/opponent effects; enemy metric is -b_p; ally model fitted only to solo-queue games with friends.

SIDO separates pros from non-pros across ALL roles (most FDR-significant 0-7, 7-15 min); gold differential predicts winners 69%/79%/83% (0-7/7-15/15-25 min); discrimination (player SIDO): 0.77 vs BA 0.87 (gold), 0.30 vs Plus-Minus 0.00 (ally) - Plus-Minus has no discriminative power in LoL.

Conservative attribution: player-ally model overlap is attributed to the ally (players get only the solo component), avoiding inflated skill claims; independence model: intraclass correlation between champion proficiency and ally/enemy model player effects is minimal.

Elo-as-SGD with home-field offset eta: theta_{k+1} = theta_k + beta [y_k - sigma(x_k^T theta_k + eta)]; optimal constant step: beta_{o,k} ~ 1/2 [(1-1/M)/(2v) + hbar^2/hbar + 2 hbar^2 (k-1)/(M-1)]^{-1}; convergence requires 0 < beta < [(1-1/M)/(2v) + hbar^2/hbar]^{-1} with rule of thumb beta < 2v; time constant tau1 ~ (M-1)/(2 beta hbar); MSD: dbar_k = alpha2^k (dbar_0 - dbar_inf) + dbar_inf, dbar_inf = beta hbar (M-1)/[2(hbar - beta hbar^2)].

Empirical Elo finding: optimal beta=0.87 converges within a single season, while FIFA/FIDE-scale beta=0.1 does not; optimal beta ~0.93-1.09 corresponds to K_opt ~160-190 Elo points (divide by s' = 400/ln 10 ~ 173.7); estimated per-season eta 0.06-0.77, v 1.2-3.7.

MaxIn-Elo: UCB h(x_t,y_t) = rbar_{x_t} - rbar_{y_t} + gamma ||e_{x_t} - e_{y_t}||_{V_t^{-1}}; selection (x_t,y_t) = argmax_{(x,y) in S x S} ||e_x - e_y||_{V_t^{-1}}; rating update r_x^{t+1} <- r_x^t + eta (o_xy^t - p-hat_xy^t); cumulative regret R(T) = sum [r*_{x*} - 1/2(r*_{x_t} + r*_{y_t})] with high-probability bound O(n log T sqrt(T)) w.p. >= 1-10/T.
equation: h(x_t,y_t) = \bar{r}_{x_t} - \bar{r}_{y_t} + \gamma\|e_{x_t} - e_{y_t}\|_{V_t^{-1}}, r_x^{t+1} \leftarrow r_x^t + \eta(o_{xy}^t - \hat{p}_{xy}^t), R(T) = \sum[r^*_{x^*} - \frac{1}{2}(r^*_{x_t} + r^*_{y_t})]

claim: mElo with intransitivity terms: p-hat_xy = sigma(r_x - r_y + c_x^T Omega c_y); findings: MaxIn-Elo achieved highest top-1 rank-recovery (RR) and near-zero cumulative regret; RR up to 0.6 (Transitive game) and 0.8 (Elo game + noise 0.1); ablations: gamma=0.6 best top-1 (gamma=0.4 misidentifies the best), tau=0.7n best, C=8 best.

Caveat: hyperparameters were grid-searched on the evaluation metric itself (RR/cumulative regret), so reported numbers are optimistic; the method targets best-model identification under active sampling, not passive rating accuracy.

Two-sample ranking test: H_0: P=Q vs H_1: (1/d)|||P-Q|||_F >= epsilon; statistic T = sum_{i,j} I_ij [k^q(k^q-1)(X^2-X) + k^p(k^p-1)(Y^2-Y) - 2(k^p-1)(k^q-1)XY] / [(k^p-1)(k^q-1)(k^p+k^q)], reject when T >= 11d; minimax upper bound epsilon^2 >= c/(kd).
equation: H_0: P=Q \text{ vs } H_1: (1/d)|||P-Q|||_F \geq \epsilon, T = \sum_{i,j} I_{ij}[k^q(k^q-1)(X^2-X) + k^p(k^p-1)(Y^2-Y) - 2(k^p-1)(k^q-1)XY]/[(k^p-1)(k^q-1)(k^p+k^q)], \text{ reject when } T \geq 11d

claim: Computational lower bound for SST at k=1: epsilon^2 > c/(d(log log d)^2) under planted-clique conjecture - assuming SST/BTL structure buys nothing statistically; and k <= 1 is impossible in general (minimax risk >= 1/2 for epsilon <= 1/2).

Empirical applications: MTurk ordinal-vs-cardinal comparison REJECTED with p=0.003 (elicitation format changes measured preferences); European football 2016-17 vs 2017-18 FAIL TO REJECT with p=0.971 (no detectable team-strength shift across seasons).

Cricket career batting model: survival hazard P(X=x) = H(x) prod_{a<x}[1-H(a)]; mean function mu(x) = mu_2 + (mu_1 - mu_2) exp(-x/L); H(x) = 1/(mu(x)+1); mu_1 = C mu_2, L = D mu_2; log(mu_{2t}) ~ GP(m, K) squared-exponential kernel.

Findings: Williamson didn't bat at career average (50.36) until ~50 innings; big-four next-innings predicted: Smith 62.5 (61.4), Kohli 57.4 (53.4), Root 52.6 (52.6), Williamson 51.2 (50.4); Smith 68.8% probability to outscore Kohli by 5.1 runs; the model REJECTS recent-form significance for elite batsmen.
Ledger verdict REJECT (superseded): better covered by ledgers 0904/1151; no portable innovation beyond standard GP-on-log-mean regression.

Deep Gamblers objective: max_w sum_i log[ f_w(x_i)_{j(i)} * o + f_w(x_i)_{m+1} ] - portfolio-theory-inspired classification with a reservation (abstain) class; reward-range property: 1 < o < m (o > m -> never abstain; o < 1 -> always abstain); inference rule: abstain when reservation probability exceeds max class probability.

SVHN selective classification: 95% coverage selective error 1.36 +/- 0.02; 90% coverage 0.76 +/- 0.05; low reward needs cross-entropy warmup to avoid degenerate abstention; never stress-tested under temporal shift; for GSE abstention must mean 'edge is small', not 'model confused' - a portfolio-construction question, not a calibration one.

Skellam live EPL framework: N(t) = N_A(t) - N_B(t) ~ Skellam(lambda^A t, lambda^B t); P(N(1)=x | lambda^A, lambda^B) = sum_k P(W_B=k-x | lambda^B) * P(W_A=k | lambda^A); E[N(1)] = lambda^A - lambda^B, V[N(1)] = lambda^A + lambda^B; calibration (lambda-hat^A_t, lambda-hat^B_t) = argmin {D_E^2 + D_V^2} s.t. lambda >= 0 from the vig-removed correct-score odds matrix.
equation: N(t) = N_A(t) - N_B(t) \sim Skellam(\lambda^A t, \lambda^B t), P(N(1)=x|\lambda^A,\lambda^B) = \sum_k P(W_B=k-x|\lambda^B)P(W_A=k|\lambda^A), E[N(1)] = \lambda^A - \lambda^B, V[N(1)] = \lambda^A + \lambda^B

claim: Even-team draw probability: P(N(1)=0 | lambda, lambda) = e^{-2 lambda} I_0(2 lambda); implied volatility sigma_IV,t = sqrt(lambda^A_t + lambda^B_t) (Black-Scholes analogy); Skellam-implied ~ market-implied except draw underestimation (fixed by type-2 zero-inflated variant); Skellam overprices extreme scorelines.

Market-efficiency test: 1,520-game binned home-win frequency ~ market-implied probability (no detectable edge); Everton-West Ham: pre-game lambda-hat^A=2.33, lambda-hat^B=1.44, red card jumps implied vol; caveat: NFL scoring is not Poisson - the framework needs scoring-process substitution for American football.

Combine data (RF classifier, 944 estimators): matriculation test accuracy 0.83; snaps linear regression best: CV RMSE 1210.1, test RMSE 904.6, R^2 = 0.17 - combine explains only 17% of career-snap variance (effectively null for career success); 3-cone is the most important feature for matriculation but the LEAST important for snaps (scouts overweight it); broad jump is most important for snaps.

Limitations: listwise deletion 1973->805 on an invite-only sample, positions pooled, no college production controls; verdict ADAPT as a negative prior - use combine numbers as noise-discounted tiebreakers, not as inputs.

Kalshi market-updating: p_it = (bid_it + ask_it)/2 (midpoint price); benchmark q_it = Pr(Y_i=1 | I_it) via cross-fit logit; efficient-updating regression Delta p_it = alpha + beta Delta q_it + Gamma X_it + eta_it; Gap_it = Delta q_it - Delta p_it; drift p_{i,t+h} - p_it = alpha_i + delta_t + rho Gap_it + epsilon_{i,t+h}.
equation: p_{it} = (bid_{it}+ask_{it})/2, q_{it} = Pr(Y_i=1|I_{it}), \Delta p_{it} = \alpha + \beta\Delta q_{it} + \Gamma X_{it} + \eta_{it}, Gap_{it} = \Delta q_{it} - \Delta p_{it}

claim: Findings: beta = 0.630 (no controls) / 0.638 (controls), H0:beta=1 rejected p<0.001 (10pp benchmark change -> ~6.4pp market move - systematic underreaction); clutch beta ~0.51; net-of-benchmark rho = 0.379/0.414/0.459/0.458/0.484 at h=1/2/5/10/15 min (predictable drift).

Executable-style returns (buy ask/sell bid) NEGATIVE - midpoint drift is absorbed by trading costs; salience/illiquidity moderator lambda_it = 1 + alpha_S*Salience + alpha_L*Illiquidity + alpha_SL*Salience*Illiquidity: salience reduces underreaction, illiquidity increases it.

Risk-constrained Kelly: constraint sum_i p_i W_i^{-lambda} <= 1 on terminal wealth per outcome; worked example (p=(0.50,0.30,0.20), q=(0.45,0.35,0.30), overround 1.10, gamma=1, lambda=2): unconstrained cash .9091, stake .0909, R(0)=1.01 violated; constrained s*=.3794, z1=1.1433, c*=.9394, W1*=1.0740, x1*=.0606 (~33% stake cut); support invariance: constrained and unconstrained share the likelihood-ratio prefix support in overround markets.
Calibration reduces to a one-dimensional root-find on the log scale via KKT; file caveat: the constraint is a mathematical convenience with thin economic interpretation.

One-event implicit-cash solver: s*_i = (p_i - c* pi_i)_+; W*_i = max(c*, p_i/pi_i); KKT condition E[1/W*(I)] = 1; c* = (1-P_A)/(1-Q_A); exact parlay theorem: x*_gamma = prod_{l:gamma_l=0} c*_l * prod_{l:gamma_l != 0} s*_{l,gamma_l}, terminal wealth factorizes W*_x(I) = prod_l F_l(I_l), V_par = sum_l E[log F_l(I_l)]; ticket active iff every selected leg is active in its one-event problem.
equation: s^*_i = (p_i - c^*\pi_i)_+, W^*_i = \max(c^*, p_i/\pi_i), E[1/W^*(I)]=1, c^* = (1-P_A)/(1-Q_A), x^*_\gamma = \prod_{\ell:\gamma_\ell=0} c^*_\ell \cdot \prod_{\ell:\gamma_\ell\neq0} s^*_{\ell,\gamma_\ell}

claim: Whitrow asymptotics: x^sim_j(epsilon) = x^ind_j(epsilon) - Lambda_j alpha_j epsilon^3 + O(epsilon^4) = (1 - Lambda_j epsilon^2) x^ind_j(epsilon) + O(epsilon^4), Lambda_j := sum_{k != j} a_k^T C_k^{-1} a_k; quartic value loss 0 <= V_par(epsilon) - V_sing(epsilon) = O(epsilon^4); binary check vs Thorp: f_1 = m_1(1-m_2^2)/(1-m_1^2 m_2^2); independence is load-bearing - correlated legs break the factorization; perturbative results need the low-edge regime.
equation: x^{sim}_j(\epsilon) = x^{ind}_j(\epsilon) - \Lambda_j\alpha_j\epsilon^3 + O(\epsilon^4), \Lambda_j := \sum_{k\neq j} a_k^T C_k^{-1} a_k, f_1 = m_1(1-m_2^2)/(1-m_1^2m_2^2)

claim: Localized conformal prediction: weights w_i(x) proportional to H(x, X_i) (Gaussian kernel or k-NN); the naive version Q_{1-alpha}(sum_i w_i(x) delta_{E_i}) is INVALID and can undercover arbitrarily badly; the valid version uses an adjusted data-dependent level alpha-tilde(x); finite-sample marginal coverage >= 1-alpha under exchangeability.
equation: w_i(x) \propto H(x, X_i), Q_{1-\alpha}(\sum_i w_i(x)\delta_{E_i}) \text{ (naive: INVALID)}

For crowdsourced binary classification where workers may abstain and some are spammers, the optimal reliability weight for worker w is W_w = [(W-M)*mu^n + (M_A / (2^N (1-m)^N))*delta(n-N)]^-1, where W is total workers, M is total spammers, mu = E[correctness given a definitive answer], m = E[skip probability], n is the number of definitive answers the worker submitted, and delta is the Dirac delta penalizing the worker cohort that answered everything.

Spammers who complete all microtasks with random guesses (M_A) concentrate in the always-answer cohort, so the Dirac delta(n-N) term in the optimal worker weight specifically discounts them; the honest-crowd-optimal weight W_w = mu^(-n) upweights large-n workers, which makes it degrade sharply as completing spammers grow.

In Monte Carlo simulations with W=50 workers and 14 of 50 being spammers, the spammer-robust reliability-weighted voting rule beat both honest-crowd-optimal weights and simple majority vote across crowd quality mu in (0.5, 1); at mu=0.5 (pure noise) all three rules merged and no weighting could help.

The spammer model in Li & Varshney (arXiv:1710.09901) splits spammers into two types via a Shah & Zhou 'double or nothing' payment mechanism: M_A spammers complete ALL microtasks with random guesses while M_0 spammers skip ALL microtasks, and the M_A/M_0 counts are jointly estimated by MLE from observed counts of workers who answered everything (W_{N+G}) and skipped everything (W_0) using G=3 gold-standard questions.

Abstention (skip) behavior is a reliability signal in crowdsourced classification: workers who abstain when unsure carry higher weight than always-answering low-edge workers, who are statistically spammer-like and deserve a multiplicative discount in ensemble voting.

In two-stage score-based abstention (Mao, Mohri, Zhong, arXiv:2310.14770), the predictor h is frozen after stage-1 training and only the rejector r is learned in stage 2 using the exponential surrogate loss Phi(t) = exp(-t) on the rejector scores.

Two-stage abstention (logistic loss on the predictor, exponential loss on the learned rejector) achieved lower abstention loss than single-stage cross-entropy surrogates on all three vision datasets: CIFAR-10 3.22% +/- 0.04% vs CE mu=1.0 4.48% +/- 0.10% and CE mu=1.7 3.62% +/- 0.07%; CIFAR-100 9.54% +/- 0.07% vs 10.40% and 14.99%; SVHN 0.93% +/- 0.02% vs 1.61% and 2.16%.

The ranking of single-stage surrogate losses L_mu (generalized cross-entropy with parameter mu) flips across datasets: mu=1.7 beats mu=1.0 on CIFAR-10 but loses on CIFAR-100 and SVHN, showing single-stage surrogate choice is dataset-dependent, which favors the two-stage approach.

Two-stage abstention surrogates enjoy both realizable H-consistency and Bayes-consistency with the excess abstention risk bounded by a concave function Gamma of the excess surrogate risk, which single-stage cross-entropy surrogates lack in general; the paper also casts defer-to-human as a special case of abstention.
equation: excess abstention risk <= Gamma(excess surrogate risk)

claim: GTA-Net (Yuan & Zhou, arXiv:2411.06725) lifts 2D to 3D human pose with a Joint-GCN for local joint graphs, a Bone-GCN for the global skeletal graph, and a hierarchical-attention-augmented TCN using causal and dilated 1D convolutions; the GCN layer update is H^(l+1) = sigma(D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2} H^(l) W^(l)) with adjacency A' = A + I.

In GTA-Net's temporal module, causal convolution is y_t = sum_{i=0}^{k-1} w_i * x_{t-i} and dilated convolution is y_t = sum_{i=0}^{k-1} w_i * x_{t-i*d}; the causal-only structure means no future frames are used, making it suitable for real-time pose estimation on live footage.

GTA-Net's scaled dot-product attention uses e_ij = (h_i W_q)(h_j W_k)^T / sqrt(d_k), alpha_ij = softmax(e_ij), h'_i = sum_j alpha_ij h_j, with residual connections Z = Y + X, trained with MSE loss L = (1/N) sum_t (Z_t - Y_hat_t)^2.

GTA-Net achieved 41.8 mm MPJPE (Protocol #1, mid-hip aligned) and 32.2 mm (Protocol #2, rigid-transformation aligned) on Human3.6M averaged over 15 actions with CPN-detected 2D keypoints, versus prior bests of 42.8 mm and 32.4 mm; with ground-truth 2D keypoints it reached 35.1 mm and 22.3 mm.

In GTA-Net's ablation, removing the attention-augmented TCN caused the largest MPJPE degradation (Human3.6M 32.2 to 39.3 mm; HumanEva 15.0 to 22.1 mm; MPI-INF-3DHP 48.0 to 52.4 mm), followed by removing Joint-GCN (38.1/21.2/50.6) and Bone-GCN (37.8/20.8/50.1); the paper's prose claim of outperforming across all metrics on zero-shot MPI-INF-3DHP (PCK 95.2%, AUC 70.8%, MPJPE 48.0 mm) is contradicted by its own Table 3 showing Yu et al. at 98.19/76.53/31.36.

In a one-million-replications-per-cell simulation study (Sziklai, Biro, Csato, arXiv:2103.06023v4), a five-round Swiss tournament beats knockout at recovering the true strength ranking (measured by inversion count) with probability 0.6350 at skill=1, 0.9044 at skill=5, and 0.9379 at skill=10; under empirical calibrations the probabilities are 0.5598 (chess), 0.6676 (soccer), 0.7095 (tennis).

Realistic seeding improves tournament ranking efficacy (inversion-count fidelity to true strengths) by at most about 3%, far less than intuition suggests, so format choice dominates seeding choice for ranking fidelity.

TVCalib (Theiner & Ewerth, arXiv:2207.11709v2) reframes soccer broadcast-frame field registration as direct camera calibration, optimizing the segment reprojection loss L = (1/|S|) sum_{c in S} d_mean(undistort_psi(x^(c)), pi_phi(s^(c))) with point-to-line distance d(p, s_hat_line) = |det((pi_phi(X_1) - pi_phi(X_0)); (pi_phi(X_0) - p))| / |pi_phi(X_1) - pi_phi(X_0)|, where the pinhole model is P = K * R * [I | -t].
equation: L = (1/|S|) sum_{c in S} d_mean(undistort_psi(x^(c)), pi_phi(s^(c)))

claim: TVCalib's combined calibration score is CS = (1 - e^{-4CR}) * sum w * AC@t with weights w = [0.5, 0.35, 0.15] over accuracy thresholds AC@5, AC@10, AC@20, where AC@t = TP/(TP+FN+FP) and CR is the completeness ratio.

On SN-Calib-test-center with ground-truth segmentation, TVCalib reached AC@5/AC@10/AC@20 of 68.7/88.0/96.1 with CR 92.8 and CS 76.9, versus the best homography-decomposition baseline at 53.7/77.5/88.4 (CR 80.3, CS 65.1); with predicted segmentation TVCalib dropped to 57.6/81.7/93.2, showing segmentation quality is the pipeline bottleneck.

TVCalib's optimization uses AdamW (lr 0.05, weight decay 0.01, 2000 steps, one-cycle schedule) with multiple initializations (center/left/right) and argmin-loss selection plus self-verification rejection when the loss exceeds tau = 0.019; joint lens-distortion learning improved WC14 AC@5 from 64.4 to 68.4 but caused FoV-explosion local minima on low-FoV samples (CR 92.3 to 78.3).

The class I_alpha of alpha-prediction intervals is exhaustively elicitable with the explicit consistent scoring function S_exh(A,y) = alpha*mu(A) - mu(((-inf,y] x [y,inf)) cap A), equivalently in normalized mixture form S_mu = (1-alpha)*mu(((-inf,y] x [y,inf)) \ A) + alpha*mu(A \ ((-inf,y] x [y,inf))), so engines' interval forecasts can be ranked with a rigorous consistent score instead of ad-hoc coverage-plus-width penalties.
equation: S_exh(A,y) = alpha*mu(A) - mu(((-inf,y] x [y,inf)) cap A)

claim: The shortest alpha-prediction interval SI_alpha for alpha in (0,1) is NOT elicitable in either selective or exhaustive mode (Theorem 4.16 of Fissler, Frongillo, Hlavinova, Rudloff, arXiv:1910.07912v2) — the first non-degenerate example of a set-valued functional elicitable nowhere — so 'report the tightest calibrated interval' is not a legitimate scoring target, and non-elicitability extends to minimal-volume prediction regions.

For functionals with the proper-subset property, selective and exhaustive elicitability are mutually exclusive (Theorem 3.7): quantile forecasts can never be scored in exhaustive mode and interval sets can never be scored selectively, so interval backtests must use the exhaustive interval score rather than pinball loss on endpoints, which scores a different functional; coverage-only evaluation (1{y in [x1,x2]} - alpha) is an identification function, not a score, and cannot rank intervals.

Quantile endpoints of prediction intervals ARE elicitable via pinball loss, fixed-constant endpoints and midpoints are elicitable, and the elementary-score mixture representation of interval scores admits Murphy diagrams (Ehm et al. 2016): a variant whose Murphy curve dominates everywhere wins under every consistent scoring function, giving a score-choice-robust model-comparison gate.

The solar-power weather study (arXiv:1802.03913v1, REJECT verdict) is an evaluation anti-pattern: it validated a time-ordered forecasting problem with a random 60/40 train/test split (train/test leakage via temporal autocorrelation), never ran the with-weather versus without-weather ablation its title promised, and reported MSE values (LASSO 5.5436, OLS 5.4248) with unstated units.

A lexicon-integrated CNN sentiment classifier (Shin, Lee & Choi, arXiv:1610.06272v2) combining word embeddings with a parallel lexicon-embedding channel (six sentiment lexicons) plus attention over lexicon channels (SC-EAV) reached 63.8 vs a 61.6 plain-CNN baseline on SemEval and 48.8% vs 47.5% on SST, with lexicon coverage of only 11.53% of training vocabulary (SemEval) and 9.20% (SST), so most signal came from a minority of tokens.

The lexicon-augmented sentiment CNNs were substantially more stable run-to-run than the plain CNN baseline across embedding sizes: standard deviations 0.4208 and 0.5764 versus 0.8491 and 1.1909 for the baseline, so the stronger finding than the ~2-point accuracy gain is stability across retrains.

Adding lag-3 DistilBERT headline sentiment (log-odds transform log(p/(1-p))) plus VADER body-text sentiment features to a lag-3 price-only baseline cut Nifty 50 movement-prediction RMSE from 134.85 to 128.74 with ridge regression (about a 4.5% reduction), while lasso blew up to RMSE 223.45, signaling unstable multicollinear features under L1.

The Nifty 50 news-sentiment study (Dasgupta & Satpati, arXiv:2412.06794v1) used a single temporal split (train Jan 2021-Aug 2023, test Oct 2023-Feb 2024, September 2023 discarded as buffer) but had target and validation flaws: a price-level target made RMSE reductions economically meaningless (134.85 on an index near 22,000 is about 0.6%), and a weekend forward-fill design left the target flat on weekends while features were not.

Causal-ICM (Dimitriou et al., arXiv:2405.20957v3) fuses a small unconfounded randomized-trial source with a large confounded observational source for CATE estimation via the rank-2 intrinsic-coregionalization multi-task GP: f^e(x) = u_1(x); f^o(x) = rho * f^e(x) + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * u_2(x), with u_1, u_2 drawn independently from GP(0, k) sharing base kernel k, and the single borrowing parameter rho in (0,1) selected by 5-fold CV.
equation: f^o(x) = rho * f^e(x) + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * u_2(x)

claim: Causal-ICM's posterior variance has a proved lower bound V^e(x*) >= (1 - rho^2) * V^e_De(x*), so borrowing from the biased observational source shrinks uncertainty by at most a rho-tied factor; its confounding-function posterior is eta(x*)|X,y ~ N(m^e(x*) - m^o(x*), V_eta(x*)).

On the Tennessee STAR validation (422 randomized + 2,593 observational observations), Causal-ICM achieved RMSE 6.29, essentially tied with random forest at 6.27, beating experimental GP (6.36) and observational GP (7.47); under misspecification in multivariate setting 2 it won decisively at 2.586 versus 3.422 (GP exp) and 21.883 (Integrative HTE), and at n_obs=2000 it improved to 0.934 while Integrative HTE degraded to 1.576.

Causal-ICM's borrowing parameter rho minimized validation RMSE near rho=0.8 (0.305), rising at rho=1.0 (1.095) where confounding stops being absorbed; an RBF base kernel (0.822) beat Matern 3/2 and 5/2 kernels, and out-of-support MSE was 1.071 versus 43.461 for the Kallus grounding GP.

Per-position Lasso ((alpha_hat, beta_hat) = argmin sum(y_i - alpha - sum beta_j x_ij)^2 + lambda sum |beta_j|) and random forest (100 trees, max depth 6) models predicting log market value two years ahead from per-minute-normalized stats plus a league-average-value anchor achieved CV-R^2 of 48.5%-61.5% across 8 soccer positions on 12,133 players; without the league-average anchor R^2 dropped to roughly 35-44%, so the anchor contributed about 20 points of R^2.
equation: (alpha_hat, beta_hat) = argmin sum(y_i - alpha - sum beta_j x_ij)^2 + lambda sum |beta_j|

claim: In the soccer future-value study (Baouan et al., arXiv:2212.11041v1), the top predictors of a player's market value two years ahead were league-average value, total minutes played, and age (age-squared negative); long-pass volume had a NEGATIVE coefficient for center-backs and defensive midfielders (modern build-up preference), and raw goals scored was not selected for forwards because it was collinear with touches-in-box and linkup features.

On the Golden Boy 2022 young-talent test, the soccer value model's predicted top-13 included 9 of the jury's actual top-10, with Kendall correlation of predicted-vs-jury 0.38 versus present-value-vs-jury 0.24, showing the model beat the current market at matching expert judgment of young talent.

The Data Replication Method (Sousa & Cardoso, arXiv:1011.3177v3) learns a classification-with-reject (abstain) region using a single standard binary classifier: treat outputs as ordered C1 < C_reject < C2, replicate each training point twice into R^{d+1} as [x;h] and [x;0], and train one binary classifier on the 2l replicated points whose intersection with each replica subspace yields two non-intersecting decision boundaries.

In the data-replication reject-option method, prediction works by classifying both replicas: (C1,C1) means C1, (C2,C1) means reject/abstain, (C2,C2) means C2; the SVM mapping (rejoSVM) adds (1/2)(b2-b1)^2/h^2 to the objective for unique thresholds, the K-class extension uses 2(K-1) replicas with K-1 reject regions, and the empirical risk is w_r * R + E with rejection cost 0 <= w_r <= 1 (above 0.5 random guessing beats rejecting).
equation: empirical risk = w_r * R + E, 0 <= w_r <= 1

claim: rejoSVM outperformed all comparators over the full w_r rejection-cost range on SyntheticI, SyntheticII, binary BCCT (960 breast-cancer observations, 30 features), SyntheticIII, SyntheticIV, and 4-class BCCT per the paper's accuracy-reject curve figures (no tabulated numeric values); SVM-based methods beat NN-based methods overall.

For risk-controlled selective prediction (RCPS), the threshold rule is tau* = min{tau_k : R_hat(tau_k) + C_k(n,delta) <= alpha}, and the nine-family ablation (Basu, arXiv:2603.08907) found Learn-Then-Test (LTT) is the single largest improvement: on MASSIVE at alpha=0.10, LTT+Hoeffding achieved 94.0% coverage versus 73.8% for Hoeffding+union (27% relative gain) with the correction shrinking from 0.079 to 0.046.

Transfer-Informed Betting (TIB) warm-starts a WSR betting bound with a data-rich sibling market's risk profile via mu_hat^TIB_t = w_t * R_hat_source + (1 - w_t) * mu_hat_t with w_t = n_eff/(n_eff + t) and default n_eff=50; its wealth stays a supermartingale (valid for all source-target divergences), verified machine-checked in Lean 4 (18 lemmas, 0 sorry), with convergence |UCB_TIB - UCB_WSR| = O(n_eff/(n_eff + n)).

The cross-domain selective-prediction ablation yields a bound-selection recipe by calibration size: n_cal >= ~500 use WSR+LTT; 120 <= n <= 500 use LTT+Empirical Bernstein; n <= ~120 use TIB warm-started from a sibling market; empirically LTT was feasible at n=150 (62.1% +/- 8.6%) while Hoeffding+union was infeasible until n=400, giving a rule of thumb of about 120 verified examples per domain for LTT versus about 350 for Hoeffding.

Across 8,650 real forecast experiments (FRBP Survey of Professional Forecasters, 1968-2019), the crowd mean beat ALL individuals in only 1.7% of experiments and beat most individuals (xi <= 1/2) in 66.8%; by contrast, a virtual unbiased forecaster crowd matched on (N, diversity) beat all in 16.3% and beat most in 99.8%, so an unbiased crowd is roughly 10x more accurate than the economists' crowd.

Reia & Fontanari (arXiv:2008.01485) found crowd diversity is POSITIVELY correlated with collective error (Spearman rho = 0.31 short, 0.25 medium, 0.14 long range — more diverse crowds are LESS accurate), skewness has no association with signed collective error (contradicting the augmented-quincunx model), and an unbiasedness test (two-tailed p = 1 - erf(|<g> - G|/sqrt(2*delta/N))) showed 85% of the 8,650 collective predictions have p < 0.05, i.e., professional economists' forecasts are biased.

For layperson wisdom-of-crowds experiments (paper strip, bean bag, book pages, candy jar), the probability a random participant beats the crowd ranged from 15% (paper strip) to 38% (book pages), and short-range forecasts were about 3x more accurate and 4x less disperse than long-range forecasts.

Bayesian Predictive Decision Synthesis (Tallman & West, arXiv:2405.01598) combines models via relaxed entropic tilting: choose tilted model probabilities minimizing KL(tilted || BMA) subject to improving the expected decision score (expected utility of the portfolio decision under a target-return constraint), where 'relaxed' caps how far the tilt can move — overweighting models that are good for the downstream decision, not just good one-step forecasters.

In the BPDS FX experiment (daily log returns of nine currencies, 2001-2021; 27 VAR x volatility-discount x target-return model/decision pairs), greedy forward selection with a 0.95 correlation bar and 0.9995 state discount selected 7 of 27 pairs; reported example annual Sharpe values showed wide dispersion (individual models 2.21, 0.21, 1.98; discounted BMA with alpha=0.8 at 2.17, 0.23, 0.88), with the paper claiming BPDS-tilted combinations improve decision scores over plain BMA.

Wheatcroft's GAP rating system (arXiv:2001.09097) maintains 4 ratings per team per statistic — home attacking H^a_i, home defensive H^d_i, away attacking A^a_i, away defensive A^d_i — with predicted home attacking output S_hat_h = (H^a_i + A^d_j)/2, away S_hat_a = (A^a_j + H^d_i)/2, and the differential S_hat_h - S_hat_a as the outcome-model regressor; ratings update via H^a_i <- max(H^a_i + lambda*phi_1*(S_h - (H^a_i + A^d_j)/2), 0) with lambda, phi_1, phi_2 in (0,1) fit by least squares across previous seasons.

In the soccer GAP study on 143,672 matches across 22 European leagues, predicted off-target shots were far more predictable than the headline statistics (GAP MAE 1.86 vs sample-mean 3.77), and predicted goals alone added NO information beyond market odds (AIC -5,617.8 vs odds-only null -5,619.1); the most informative predicted statistics were shots off target, then corners, then shots on target, illustrating the principle that a statistic's information content equals its importance times its predictability.

The GAP paper fed predicted stat differentials plus market-odds-implied probability into an ordinal logistic outcome model log(p_hat_h/(p_hat_d + p_hat_a)) = alpha_hat + sum beta_hat_i V_i and measured genuinely out-of-sample mean profit of +1.85% (level stakes) and +5.01% (Kelly stakes, CI +3.38 to +6.76) for the best predicted-stat combos with odds included, though cumulative profit curves showed the edge decaying in recent seasons across all 22 leagues as markets absorbed the information.
equation: log(p_hat_h/(p_hat_d + p_hat_a)) = alpha_hat + sum beta_hat_i V_i

claim: The soccer coaching decision-support paper (Beal et al., arXiv:2003.10294, REJECT verdict) modeled pre-match tactics as a Bayesian game (payoff u = weighted result probability: win 2, draw 1, loss 0) with best-response, spiteful (minimize opponent payoff), and minmax optimization; its formation prediction reached 96.21% accuracy (precision 0.9867, recall 0.9135) and best-response tactics showed a +16.1% model-vs-model win-probability boost (p=0.0001), but it used non-time-ordered random CV splits (deployment leakage) and never calibrated probabilities or tested against odds.

The generalized Kelly paper (O'Brien et al., arXiv:2003.02743) derives the optimal stake fraction when binary outcomes are temporally correlated as a Markov chain of memory depth m: the memory-1 model is P(X_k = 1 | X_{k-1}) = omega_0 + omega_1 * X_{k-1}, the optimal constant fraction over horizon n is K_n = 2*(E[H_n]/n) - 1 where E[H_n]/n = lambda_n * p_0 + (1 - lambda_n) * p_infty with p_0 = omega_0 + omega_1*x_{-1}, p_infty = (omega_0 - omega_1)/(1 - 2*omega_1), and lambda_n = (1/n)*(1 - (2*omega_1)^n)/(1 - 2*omega_1).

In the paper's numerical example (memory depth 1, x_{-1}=1, omega_0=0.55, omega_1=0.20, n=2), classical Kelly expected log growth was about 0.053 while correlation-aware constant-fraction expected log growth was about 0.082 and time-varying fractions about 0.088, a roughly 55% ELG gain from accounting for correlation under the true model — though gains were computed under the true model, estimated parameters shrink them, and the binary even-money structure does not directly cover American-odds sports bets.

Preference-centric bandits (Tatli et al., arXiv:2504.20877v2) replace expected reward with a preference metric U_h(F) = integral h compose F d_lambda, a signed Choquet integral of the arm's full CDF, and learn the optimal mixture alpha_star in argmax_{alpha in Delta^{K-1}} U_h(sum alpha_i F_i) of arms rather than the best single arm; Theorem 2 says convex distortion h favors a solitary arm while Theorem 3 says for every strictly concave h there exists an instance whose optimum is a strict mixture.

For Gini-deviation risk (h(u) = u(1-u)) on a two-arm Bernoulli bandit Bern(p)/Bern(1-p), an even mixture strictly beats either arm alone: U_h(1/2 F_1 + 1/2 F_2) > max(U_h(F_1), U_h(F_2)), which formalizes why a strictly concave risk criterion (e.g., CVaR on a portfolio) can prefer spreading stake across several picks instead of all-in on the best single pick.

The preference-centric bandit algorithms achieved regret rates of O(K sqrt(T)) (PM-ETC-M) and O(sqrt(KT)) (PM-UCB-M) for Gini deviation ignoring polylogs; PM-UCB-M selection uses A_{t+1} = argmax_i (t * a_t^U(i) - tau_t^U(i)) with 1-Wasserstein confidence balls, and at T=60k PM-UCB-M average regret was about 0.004-0.008 versus uniform sampling's 0.010-0.020 (numeric replication gate: PM-UCB-M regret <= 50% of uniform's, decreasing over T in {20k, 40k, 60k}).

The SDWPF dataset (Zhou et al., arXiv:2208.04360v2, from the Baidu KDD Cup 2022) is the largest public spatial wind-power forecasting benchmark at release: 4,727,520 ten-minute records from 134 wind turbines over 245 days with 13 columns (wind speed, temperatures, nacelle direction, blade pitch, status flags, spatial coordinates); the paper's baseline scored RMSE 47.08, MAE 37.56, and a combined RMSE/MAE score of 42.32 over K=195 test predictions on the 288-step (48-hour) forecasting task.

The PART tennis injury-readiness framework (REJECT verdict, duplicate of ledger 0772) on a 9-player collegiate cohort showed weak discrimination: XGBoost injury-classifier AUC 0.64 +/- 0.01 (accuracy 0.74, injury F1 0.43) with self-reported questionnaire labels, while the physical-capability LSTM reported an implausible R^2 = 0.993 (RMSE 0.749, MAE 0.248), which the ledger flags as a leakage/target-construction concern — a standing validation rule that any model with R^2 near 1.0 must be treated as leakage until proven otherwise.

A survivorship-bias-free audit of 5,467 verified pre-match Nigerian sports-betting influencer wagers (~$4.8M tracked against Stake.com slip URLs, July 2023-Aug 2025) found an overall win rate of 10.39%, collective influencer ROI of -25.24%, and a follower flat-staking simulation ROI of -38.27%; by odds segment, Low (<10) lost 10%, Medium (10-100) netted a loss, and High (>100) lost 74%.
equation: ROI = (Total Payout - Total Stake) / Total Stake

claim: In the influencer-wager audit, no simulated staking strategy was profitable (Flat, Inverse S=C/O, Square Root S=C/sqrt(O), Fixed Return S=P/(O-1)); Fixed Return was least bad, then Inverse, then Square Root, Flat worst; ANOVA showed the strategy effect was significant (p = 2.12e-7) but the tipster effect was not (p = 0.1246), meaning no influencer was statistically superior, and the affiliate commission formula (0.03 * Wagered / 2) * Commission Rate pays on wagering volume rather than accuracy.

For Kelly-optimal (log-utility) sizing on a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dx_i = (a_i - b_i * x_i)dt + sum_j sigma_{i,j} dW_t^j, the optimal fraction vector is f_t* = R^{-1} c_t (R = sigma sigma^T, equivalently the maximizer of F(x) = c_t^T x - (1/2) x^T R x), and for a single asset f_t* = (mu_t - r)/sigma^2 with mu_t = a - b*log(S(t)) + 0.5*sigma^2, a dynamic fraction that rises as the price falls below its mean-reverting level.

In the OU-Kelly framework (Lv & Meister), estimation sensitivity at r=0 is: a 1% overestimation of volatility has about the same effect on the optimal fraction as a 2% underestimation of drift, so calibration budget belongs on sigma first; under global correlation structure the total optimal fraction over n correlated assets collapses to (mu_1(t) - r)/sigma^2, meaning n strongly correlated assets behave like one asset and total stake must be capped at the single-asset fraction rather than summed.

The covariate Bradley-Terry model (Ting Yan, arXiv:2507.22472) gives P(i beats j) = exp(beta_i - beta_j + Z_ijk^T gamma) / (1 + exp(beta_i - beta_j + Z_ijk^T gamma)) with Z_ijk = -Z_jik, reducing to Agresti's home-field model when Z=1 indicates i at home; merit estimates converge at ||beta_hat - beta*||_inf = O_p(sqrt(log n / n)) while covariate coefficients converge at ||gamma_hat - gamma*||_2 = O_p(sqrt(log n) / n).
equation: P(i beats j) = exp(beta_i - beta_j + Z_ijk^T gamma) / (1 + exp(beta_i - beta_j + Z_ijk^T gamma))

claim: The CBTM paper's Figure 1 shows that fitting plain Bradley-Terry when the truth has a covariate effect produces l_inf merit error that grows with gamma and does NOT shrink as n grows (permanent non-vanishing bias), while CBTM error stays small and shrinks; on NBA 2018-19 (1,230 games), the home-advantage coefficient was gamma_hat = 0.45 (SE 0.065, p = 2.1e-12), decisively significant, and the merit ordering reproduced East playoff seeding exactly.

CBTM Corollary 1 gives a separability gate for published rankings: the top-K teams are exactly recovered when the merit separation Delta_K = beta*_{K-1} - beta*_K >> sqrt(log n / n); the paper also supplies a closed-form incidental-parameter bias correction gamma_hat_bc = gamma_hat - N^{-1/2} Sigma_hat^{-1} B_hat and notes 95% CI coverage for merit gaps collapses for far-apart pairs under wide merit ranges (e.g., n=200, coverage 13.00% for pair (0,100)), so controlling ||beta*||_inf is necessary for valid inference.

Sparse Bayesian time-varying-parameter models (Fruhwirth-Schnatter & Knaus, arXiv:2207.12147v1) use the non-centered parameterization beta_{jt} = beta_j + sqrt(theta_j) * beta_tilde_{jt} with beta_tilde_{jt} = beta_tilde_{j,t-1} + u_tilde_{jt}, u_tilde_jt ~ N(0,1), which converts variance selection (is theta_j = 0?) into coefficient selection (is sqrt(theta_j) = 0?), making it amenable to shrinkage priors (horseshoe, triple gamma, discrete spike-and-slab) and per-coefficient MCMC classification into zero, fixed, or dynamic.

In the sparse TVP review's US-inflation application, MCMC slab choice materially affected inference: the hierarchical Student-t slab had about 20% move acceptance between fixed/dynamic states versus under 5% for Gaussian and fractional slabs with visible chain dependence, and the Lasso prior over-shrank by classifying EVERY coefficient as zero while discrete spike-and-slab discriminated (e.g., treasury-bill coefficient P(dynamic|y)=0.86, commodity index P(fixed|y)=0.78, Dow Jones P(zero|y)=0.61).

Cutting et al. (arXiv:2507.08921v1) modeled Polymarket 2024-election odds with Bayesian Structural Time Series y_t = Z_t' alpha_t + epsilon_t, epsilon_t ~ N(0,H_t); alpha_{t+1} = T_t alpha_t + R_t eta_t, and used the variance-ratio interpretation: tau^2 = 0 gives mean-reverting Gaussian noise while sigma^2 -> 0 gives a random walk — a transferable per-game tau^2/sigma^2 ratio classifier for distinguishing informed line moves (steam) from public churn.
equation: y_t = Z_t' alpha_t + epsilon_t; alpha_{t+1} = T_t alpha_t + R_t eta_t

claim: In the Polymarket-vs-polls election study (ADAPT only for the BSTS methodology, not the n=1 result), from Oct 18, 2024 onward Polymarket's 95% predictive intervals no longer crossed the 50% line while polling's intervals always straddled it; Polymarket price series were random-walk-like (tau^2 > 0, fanning intervals) versus polling being Gaussian noise about a mean (tau^2 ~ 0, flat intervals), but the October Trump surge coincided with a single actor's roughly $30M in wagers across multiple accounts plus wash-trading accusations, so the headline 'markets beat polls' may partly reflect a whale's thumb on the scale.

Piotrowski & Schroeder's Kelly-in-parimutuel-framing paper (arXiv:physics/0607166v1) derives the no-short optimum: if p_1*IN_2 > p_2*IN_1, bet only the mispriced side with l_1* = p_1 - (IN_1/IN_2)*p_2 and l_2* = 0, and under Laplace indifference l_1* = p_1 - p_2; the fixed-odds Kelly form is f* = (b*p_hat - (1 - p_hat))/b = (p_hat - q)/(1 - q) for decimal odds b with q the de-vigged implied probability, used only when p_hat > q.

The Piotrowski & Schroeder Kelly paper's core qualitative result is that Kelly profit on bookmaker wagers equals profit-on-unpopularity (seer's profit) minus Shannon entropy, with maximal growth E(z) = -sum p_k ln(IN_k/(IN_1+IN_2)) - S where S = -sum p_k ln p_k, E(z) >= 0 always and E(z) = 0 iff p_1*IN_2 = p_2*IN_1 (pool-implied probabilities match true probabilities); the ledger cautions the paper's parimutuel zero-margin formulas do not describe US fixed-odds sportsbooks and its exact-knowledge assumption means raw Kelly on noisy probability estimates overbets, hence fractional Kelly.
equation: E(z)(l_bar_1, l_bar_2) = -sum_k p_k ln(IN_k/(IN_1 + IN_2)) - S

claim: The sports-intelligence LLM/VLM QA benchmark (Yang et al., arXiv:2406.14877v1) measured a large human gap on hard multi-hop sports scenario reasoning: best models scored 79.37/73.17 (single-hop easy/hard) and 44.49/29.11 (multi-hop easy/hard) versus human 96.63/96.02/94.90/91.84; all four best advanced configurations used chain-of-thought prompting, GPT-4o led single-hop while GPT-4 led multi-hop, and six-month progress was +4.5%/+7.0%/+10%/+7%.

On video-based sports QA, a task-specific Auto-Focus Transformer baseline scored 59.2/59.1 overall versus general VLMs at 19.28-31.52 with GPT-4 judge scores of only 1.49-1.92 out of 5, especially weak on Temporal (8.82-16.23) and Counterfactual questions; the paper's four-class text error taxonomy is (A) domain-knowledge errors, (B) inaccurate recall, (C) context/nuance confusion, (D) reasoning errors, with advanced-scenario errors dominated by class C and video errors by lack of domain knowledge.

EDGE (arXiv:2608.20511) is a binned directed calibration test for probabilistic binary classifiers: group residuals r_g = (o_g - e_g)/sqrt(V_g) with o_g = sum y, e_g = sum pi_hat, V_g = sum pi_hat(1-pi_hat) over G=10 equal-frequency groups, project them onto a k<=3 orthogonal-polynomial shape basis Z as S = r' Z (Z'Z)^{-1} Z' r = ||P_Z r||^2, with null S ~_dot sum lambda_j chi^2_{1,j} where lambda_j are eigenvalues of (Z'Z)^{-1} Z' Omega Z (Satterthwaite approximation S ~= c * chi^2_nu).

EDGE-poly 3 held nominal size (realized 0.047-0.051 at alpha=0.05, null p-values Uniform) and at n=1000 led or tied rival binned tests in 19 of 22 detectable miscalibration scenarios with median relative power gain of about 27% over the better of HL/EF (e.g., cloglog link 0.77 vs 0.40 HL vs 0.50 EF; omitted quadratic 0.62 vs 0.41), cost 8.1 ms/call at n=1000, and had 0% failure versus Stukel's refit failing to converge in 20-28% of sparse samples — but omnibus tests beat it on rough 4-cycle oscillation (1.00 vs 0.52) and sawtooth (0.95 vs 0.11) departures.

The interval-score ROC framework (arXiv:2607.28178) compares interval forecasters via the IS-ROC curve beta |-> (MS^P(beta), MAD^P(beta)) — mean interval width vs mean absolute miss distance across coverage levels — with interval score IS^P(alpha,beta) = MS^P(beta) + (2/alpha) MAD^P(beta) and iso-score lines MAD = -(alpha/2) MS + (alpha/2) IS.

For tunable interval predictors, calibration is g(alpha) = argmin_beta IS(alpha,beta) = MS(beta) + 2/alpha * MAD(beta) with a tangent method for convex curves and convex-hull/step calibration for non-convex ones; quantile-level recalibration tilde_tau = g(2*tau)/2 for tau <= 1/2 transforms the whole predictive distribution, and global convex-hull ensembling selects the per-coverage-level best sub-model (isotonic regression restores nesting).

In the in-game win-probability study on 41,642 NCAA basketball games (Maddox, Sides, Harvill, arXiv:2204.11777), five estimators were compared on Brier score: MLE 0.1453, Stern probit 0.1452, fixed-prior Bayes 0.1451, dynamic Bayes 0.1450, adjusted dynamic Bayes 0.1284 — an 11.4% relative Brier improvement came essentially entirely from blending a time-weighted pre-game win probability with the in-game estimate (2019-20: 0.1397/0.1398/0.1396/0.1396/0.1261).

The Stern (1994) Brownian-motion in-game win-probability formula tested in the paper is p_tilde = Phi((l + (1-t*)mu)/sqrt((1-t*)sigma^2)) with home edge mu ~ 5-6 points and mu/sigma in [0.12, 0.39]; the dynamic-beta-prior variant used strong priors (up to beta(19,1)/beta(1,19)) only in extreme differential cells while preserving comeback mass early, and raw MLE produced pathological cells (Drexel's 34-point comeback yielded p=1 cells) that Bayesian pseudo-counts smoothed.

The forecast-combination paper (van Eijk & Ghosh, arXiv:2503.20082) trains a linear pool y_hat_t(omega,omega_0) = omega_0 + sum_j omega_j x_{t,j} with omega on the simplex directly on 0-1 beat-the-consensus losses: hit target tilde_y_t = I(y_t > y_hat_t(bar_omega)), Bernoulli NLL hit loss, and win rate Pr(|R_t|<1) where R_t = (y_t - y_hat_t(omega,omega_0))/(y_t - y_hat_t(bar_omega)), using a Cauchy-CDF surrogate (1/L) sum_t p_t(lambda) * [(1/pi) arctan((z_t - z_0)/gamma_hat) + 1/2] with z_t = |R_t| - 1 optimized by COBYLA, preferred over logistic as a tighter indicator approximation.

On I/B/E/S analyst forecasts (23 large-cap tech companies, 36 quarterly revenues 2015-2023, rolling L=12 windows, time-ordered), direct win-loss optimization (NLP/COBYLA) achieved 79.2% hit rate and 68.7% win rate versus QP 79.7%/61.2% and Bayesian 82.4%/62.7%, with best single NLP lambda=0 at 83.2%/71.9% against benchmarks of naive 39.7%/17.0% and AKAnomics 66% hit; time-discounting evidence was weak (Bayesian posterior mean lambda ~ 0.098, best NLP at lambda=0, 'setting lambda=0 would possibly provide the best forecasts').

The coupled acute:chronic workload ratio has a hard ceiling of 4.0 by construction: if an athlete is inactive 3 weeks then records workload WL1 in week 4, ACRatio = WL1/(WL1/4) = 4 regardless of WL1 magnitude, so the metric cannot discriminate spike sizes at the top end; the uncoupled ratio (acute excluded from the chronic denominator) removes both the ceiling and the spurious acute-chronic correlation.

The IOC's acute:chronic 'sweet spot 0.8-1.3 / danger zone >1.5' guidance rests on three small studies (n=28 cricket fast bowlers, n=53 Australian footballers, rugby league) where the apparent risk increase was driven entirely by points at ACRatio=2.0 with no apparent relationship below 2.0; apparent low-ratio injury risk is an artifact of time-mismatch bias (athletes injured early in a weekly block accumulate less acute load), and EWMA implementations carry an initial-value bug (with lambda<0.5 the time-0 weight exceeds later days) requiring about 50 burn-in days.

Inverse optimization on 9 seasons of NFL 4th-down decisions (Sandholtz, arXiv paper via nflfastR 2014-2022) recovers each coach's implicit risk preference as a quantile tau minimizing average Hamming loss min_{tau in [0,1]} (1/N) sum_j 1(a_j != a*_j(sigma_j, q^pi-bar_tau)) between observed decisions and tau-optimal decisions, where q^pi-bar_tau(sigma,a) = Q_tau[V^pi-bar(sigma,a)] = inf{x : tau <= F_{V^pi-bar}(x|sigma,a)} is the tau-quantile of next-state value under a fixed league-average continuation policy.

NFL coaches behave as if optimizing LOW quantiles of next-state value (conservative risk preferences) in both field regions and nearly every win-probability range versus the 4th Down Bot reference; tau_hat_1 - tau_hat_2 (opponent half minus own half) > 0 with 95% CIs excluding 0 until WP >= 0.8, meaning coaches are clearly more risk-tolerant in the opponent's half at low-to-mid win probability; league risk tolerance increased over 2014-2022 in every WP x region cell, and in a performance regression (N=622 cells) beta_1(tau_hat) = 0.769*** (SE 0.138, partial R^2 0.048), so higher tau is associated with more average points gained, consistent with the ~0.4 wins/year cost of excessive conservatism (Yam & Lopez 2019).
equation: AvgPointsGained_{ijkell} = beta_0 + beta_1 tau_hat_{ijkell} + beta_2 Elo_{ij} + beta_3 1(ell=Own) + epsilon

claim: Truncated-normal EMOS (Thorarinsdottir & Gneiting 2010) post-processes wind-speed ensembles with predictive law N_0^infty(mu, sigma^2) and link functions mu = a + b_H^2 f_bar_H + b_L^2 f_bar_L, sigma^2 = c^2 + d^2 S^2, where f_bar_H, f_bar_L are ensemble-group means, S^2 is combined-ensemble variance, and squared coefficients enforce nonnegative weights; parameters are fit by minimum-mean-CRPS (closed-form CRPS for the truncated normal) per lead time.

On ECMWF operational dual-resolution wind-speed ensembles (50-member 9 km + 100-member 36 km, 8,726 SYNOP stations, July 2023-May 2024), EMOS post-processing considerably reduced the differences between configurations (replicating Baran et al. 2019): all EMOS variants beat raw forecasts on CRPS/QS/MAE/RMSE at nearly all lead days, local EMOS was best for days 1-6, and raw dual-resolution (100,50) never beat pure high-resolution (0,50) significantly — adding high-res members to 50 low-res gave monotonic CRPSS gains of about 10% (32 members), 7% (16), 5% (8) at day 1, decaying with lead time.

For wind-speed ensemble post-processing, the EMOS truncated-normal advantage vanishes at high-wind thresholds: at 10 m/s and 15 m/s Brier scores the truncated normal lacks tail weight, so log-normal or truncated GEV laws are suggested; the skill score used is S = (S_bar_ref - S_bar_F)/(S_bar_ref - S_bar_perf) (Murphy 1973, positively oriented), and significance came from 95% CIs via 2,000 stationary-bootstrap block samples.

SportsSum2.0's three-step game-summarizer (select -> rewrite -> fluency-aware MMR rerank) converts live commentary into news: the reranker is MMR(D,R) = argmax_{d_i in D-R} [lambda_1 * info(d_i) + lambda_2 * flu(d_i) - lambda_3 * max_{d_j in R} sim(d_i, d_j)] with lambda = (0.6, 0.2, 0.2), info from the commentary-importance selector, flu = 1 - perplexity(d_i)/eta (GPT-2), and sim = BERTScore, greedily selected to an article-length budget.
equation: MMR(D,R) = argmax_{d_i in D-R} [lambda_1 * info(d_i) + lambda_2 * flu(d_i) - lambda_3 * max_{d_j in R} sim(d_i, d_j)]

claim: SportsSum2.0's lexical+semantic pseudo-labeler scores candidate commentaries in a [h_i, h_i+3] timeline window as S(r_i, c_j) = lambda * BERTScore(r_i, c_j) + (1-lambda) * ROUGE(r_i, c_j) with lambda = 0.7, and it consistently beat the semantic-only pseudo-labeler; the best three-step model (Bert2bert) scored ROUGE-1/2/L 48.13/20.09/47.78 vs SportsSUM baseline 44.73/18.90/44.03 (+2.8 avg points), and in human evaluation the cleaned dataset's largest gain was on fluency — dataset noise degrades generation quality.
equation: S(r_i, c_j) = lambda * BERTScore(r_i, c_j) + (1-lambda) * ROUGE(r_i, c_j)

claim: On Kalshi NBA winner contracts (1,438 games, 409,512 contract-minutes, Apr 2025-May 2026), markets underreacted to public play-by-play information: the efficient-updating regression Delta p_it = alpha + beta Delta q_it + Gamma X_it + eta_it gave beta = 0.638 (H0: beta=1 rejected, p<0.001), meaning a 10pp benchmark win-prob change moved the market only about 6.4pp, with clutch situations updating worst (beta ~ 0.51).
equation: Delta p_it = alpha + beta Delta q_it + Gamma X_it + eta_it

claim: The residual updating gap Gap_it = Delta q_it - Delta p_it predicted future price drift with net-of-benchmark coefficients rho = 0.379/0.414/0.459/0.458/0.484 at horizons h=1/2/5/10/15 minutes (all significant): a 10pp gap implied 2.0pp drift at 5 min and 4.6pp net of benchmark changes, rising to 4.8pp at 15 min; salience reduced underreaction while illiquidity increased it, but executable returns (buy ask / sell bid) were NEGATIVE — midpoint drift is absorbed by bid-ask costs, so predictable drift is not a frictionless edge.
equation: p_{i,t+h} - p_it = alpha_i + delta_t + rho Gap_it + epsilon

claim: The risk-constrained Kelly paper (arXiv:2604.11577) adds a CRRA risk constraint sum_i p_i W_i^{-lambda} <= 1 and proves a support-invariance result: in overround markets (sum q_i > 1), constrained and unconstrained optimizers share the same likelihood-ratio-prefix support (sorted by p_i/q_i), so risk constraints change only the cash level and stake magnitudes, never which outcomes are staked; calibration reduces to a one-dimensional root-find on the log scale for scalar s* via the KKT system.

In the risk-constrained Kelly worked example (p=(0.50,0.30,0.20), q=(0.45,0.35,0.30), overround 1.10, gamma=1, lambda=2), the constrained optimum cut the example stake from 0.0909 to 0.0606 (a one-third reduction, s*=0.3794, c*=0.9394) while keeping identical active support; the paper has no empirical validation (single hand-picked ternary event) and gamma/lambda are free parameters with no calibration guidance.

For optimal parlay wagering on independent events (arXiv:2603.26620), the exact Kelly ticket-book is an outer product: x*_gamma = prod_{ell: gamma_ell=0} c*_ell * prod_{ell: gamma_ell != 0} s*_{ell,gamma_ell} with terminal wealth factorizing as W*_x(I) = prod F_ell(I_ell) and growth V_par = sum E[log F_ell(I_ell)]; a ticket is active iff every selected leg is active in its one-event problem (Cor. 3.2), so no optimal parlay contains a singly inactive leg.

Whitrow asymptotics (Theorem 4.2) show the singles-only restriction costs only quartic growth: 0 <= V_par(epsilon) - V_sing(epsilon) = O(epsilon^4), and simultaneous singles stakes equal isolated Kelly through second order with only a cubic shrinkage correction x^sim_j(epsilon) = (1 - Lambda_j epsilon^2) x^ind_j(epsilon) + O(epsilon^4) where Lambda_j := sum_{k != j} a_k^T C_k^{-1} a_k; the binary cross-check versus Thorp's two-bet formula gives f_1 = m_1(1-m_2^2)/(1-m_1^2 m_2^2) expanding to f_1 = m_1 - m_1 m_2^2 + O(epsilon^5).

Localized conformal prediction (Leying Guan, 2023, JMLR) weights calibration scores by a localizer w_i(x) proportional to H(x, X_i) (e.g., Gaussian kernel or k-NN weights) so prediction intervals are valid marginally and tighter where the test point's neighborhood is predictable; the naive plug-in quantile Q_{1-alpha}(sum_i w_i(x) delta_{E_i}) is INVALID and can undercover arbitrarily badly, so the valid version uses a data-dependent adjusted level alpha-tilde(x) computed from the weighted calibration distribution, preserving finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability.

In Guan's localized conformal prediction experiments (Example 4.1, nominal 95% intervals), localization narrowed intervals at equal coverage under heteroskedasticity: setting A 0.95/2.77 -> 0.94/2.27 (~18% narrower), C 0.95/4.26 -> 0.95/3.15 (~26% narrower), B nearly unchanged (0.95/3.14 -> 0.95/3.01), and D with no gain (0.94/3.81 -> 0.94/3.86); the method costs O(n) per test point, and effective sample size (sum w)^2/sum w^2 diagnoses when localization starves the calibration set.

A Bayesian hierarchical linear model of squash home advantage (Greengard & Takriti, arXiv:2506.09287, PSA World Tour Dec 2018-Mar 2024) is y ~ Normal(a_rank1 - a_rank2 + h*b, sigma_y) with b in {-1,0,1}, h ~ Normal(0, 0.5), sigma_y, sigma_a ~ Normal^+(0,2), and ranking-slot ability prior a_j ~ Normal(beta*(j-1) + gamma*sqrt(j-1), sigma_a) with top-rank ability fixed at 0 for identification, fit by MCMC in Stan; the country-specific extension adds h_country ~ Normal(0, 0.2).

Estimated squash home advantage was +0.40 games for men and +0.30 games for women (SE ~0.10), giving evenly-matched home win probabilities of about 58% and 56% (Phi(0.4/1.9)=0.58, Phi(0.3/1.8)=0.56); the mean ability gap between adjacent top-20 ranks was about 0.15 games, so home advantage is worth roughly 2-3 ranking slots, and Egypt's home effect (0.45 men) was measurably larger than England's — venue/crowd heterogeneity is real.

Dynamic Bayesian Regression Quantile Synthesis (Kobayashi et al., arXiv:2603.11474v1) combines multiple models' quantile forecasts as p(y_t|Phi_t,H_t) = integral alpha(y_t|f_t,Phi_t) prod_j h_{tj}(f_{tj}) df_t via the asymmetric Laplace synthesis y_t = F_{tau,t}' theta_{tau,t} + epsilon_{tau,t} with epsilon ~ AL(tau, sigma_{tau,t}), random-walk weights theta_{tau,t} = theta_{tau,t-1} + w_t (discount delta_tau), and gamma-beta random-walk scale sigma; the AL density is alpha_tau(epsilon|sigma) = tau(1-tau)/sigma * exp{-rho_tau(epsilon/sigma)} with rho_tau(u) = u(tau - I(u<0)).

The factor extension FDRQS shares combiner weight dynamics across N series via theta_{itj} = lambda_{ij}' u_{tj} with L=5 latent factors under a multiplicative gamma process prior (delta_{1j} ~ Ga(2.5,1), delta_{ell j} ~ Ga(3.5,1)); on global GDP growth-at-risk it won outright with relative cumulative quantile-weighted CRPS of 0.757 at h=4 versus 0.897 (univariate DRQS) and 0.796 (best single agent DQLM1), and kept the smallest scores after the 2020 COVID shock while univariate methods deteriorated.

Evaluation in the quantile-synthesis paper used quantile-weighted CRPS_t^{(m)} = integral_0^1 2 (I{y_t < Q_hat_t(tau)} - tau)(Q_hat_t(tau) - y_t) nu(tau) dtau with weightings nu in {1, tau^2, (1-tau)^2}, relative cumulative score RCS < 1 meaning beating the benchmark, and PIT uniformity; agent weight dynamics showed DQLM3 credibly negative at tau=0.1 in the US inflation study (hedge behavior — corrective agents add value) with posterior agent correlations emerging only under extreme 2020Q3 stress.
