equation: CRPS_t^{(m)} = integral_0^1 2 (I{y_t < Q_hat_t(tau)} - tau)(Q_hat_t(tau) - y_t) nu(tau) dtau

claim: For lasso-based forecast combination across a 20-point lambda grid, BIC-posterior weights are w_m = exp(-0.5*BIC_{lambda_m}) / sum_m exp(-0.5*BIC_{lambda_m}) with BIC_{lambda_m} = n*log(Loss_{lambda_m}) + df_{lambda_m}*log(n) (df = nonzero count); on monthly log-realized variance of 10 stock indices (2000-2016), the lambda-grid combination slightly improved MAFE at all horizons but the Model Confidence Set (75%, 5000 bootstraps) retained BOTH combined and non-combined ordered lasso at every horizon — the combination gain was NOT statistically significant (honest negative result).

In the realized-variance lasso study, ordered lasso (monotone non-increasing lag coefficients via PAVA) dominated with the lowest MAFE at all horizons (h=1: 0.514; h=2: 0.599; h=3: 0.639; h=6: 0.698), and a horizon pattern emerged: univariate models won at h=1,2 (best AFE for 8/10 indices) while multivariate spillover models won at h=3 (8/10) and h=6 (7/10) — lean specs for short horizons, cross-entity structure for long horizons.

Using instrumented-mouthguard head kinematics from 3,852 real impacts (3,805 non-concussive + 47 concussive across 203 athletes), linear acceleration dominated rotational measures as a concussion predictor: held-out AUPRC a=0.65 [0.27,0.90] versus alpha=0.36 [0.12,0.67] and omega=0.35 [0.07,0.67] (random classifier 0.01), with logistic risk functions P(concussion) = logit^{-1}(beta_0 + beta_1*a [+ beta_2*omega or beta_2*alpha]); 50% risk thresholds were a=100 g, alpha=8.3 krad/s^2, omega=40 rad/s (decision thresholds a=78.7 g, alpha=5874.2 rad/s^2, omega=29 rad/s).

In the mouthguard concussion study, the a+alpha model gave odds ratios OR_a = 2.3 [1.5-3.6] (significant) and OR_alpha = 1.3 [0.81-1.9] (not significant); LASSO beta coefficients ranked a=0.91 > omega=0.842 > alpha=0.380 with dominance R^2 of a=0.108, omega=0.065, alpha=0.061; concussive impacts showed regional brain strain MPS95 of 0.28-0.48 versus 0.04-0.09 for non-concussive (p<0.0001); all four youth concussions were missed (recall 0 for every model), showing the kinematics framework does not generalize to developing brains.

On 63,000 over-level records from 1,751 ODIs with over-by-over data, the cricket Duckworth-Lewis-Stern rain rule had 78.12% accuracy on all overs (83.74% excluding the first 20), while supervised ML beat D/L at every over: 10th over 72.23% vs 80.97% (Bagging+Naive Bayes), 20th 79.20% vs 82.80% (NN), 30th 85.90% vs 87.45% (NB), 40th 88.42% vs 88.98% (NN); a PSO-optimized resource table (mu=10, c1=2, c2=2.5, 50 generations, fitness = classification accuracy) raised 0-50 over accuracy from 79.25% to 80.25%, with dropping the monotonic-decrease constraint giving even higher accuracy.

The cricket D/L study's Unpredictability Index (D/L formula failure percentage at the 40th over per team) ranked Sri Lanka 18.18% (chasing wins), India 20.37% (chasing losses, 'collapses'), England 21.95% (defending wins), and Australia 20.41% (defending losses) — per-team model-failure profiling as a diagnostic for systematic mispricing; limitations include no cross-validation, accuracy-only evaluation (no calibration/log-loss), and exclusion of rain-interrupted matches (selection bias).

AskSport (arXiv:2503.21067v1) uses a thin BM25 top-10 retrieval over the QASports corpus plus a RoBERTa extractive reader returning top-3 answers with (confidence, source title, source URL), where reader confidence = softmax over start/end span logits; on three hand-picked example questions confidences were 0.64-0.80, and the 0.7978 top confidence on the unanswerable opinion question ('best player') is disqualifying evidence that raw softmax confidences are uncalibrated and must never be displayed as reliability signals.

In the optimal-online-bookmaking paper (Tal & Sabag, arXiv:2506.16253), a bookmaker posting odds over T rounds on K outcomes can guarantee worst-case loss L*_T,K = T + (largest root of P_{T,K}), where the characterizing polynomial is P_{T,K}(x) = sum_{m=0}^{K} binom(K,m) (-T)^{overline{K-m}} x^m (rising factorial); the binary case gives L*_{T,2} = T + sqrt(T) (regret exactly sqrt(T)), the ternary case L*_{T,3} = T + 2 sqrt(T) cos[(1/3) arccos(1/sqrt(T))], and regret scales as Theta(sqrt(T)) with a K-dependent constant from the largest root of the K-th Hermite polynomial (asymptotically 2 sqrt(K)).

The optimal online bookmaker strategy is opportunistic: recompute the largest root of the characterizing polynomial after every suboptimal/non-decisive bet, otherwise post static optimal odds — static odds posting is strictly suboptimal; for the binary case the overround is Gamma_t = sum_k 1/gamma_t(k) with normalized offered probability r_t(k) = 1/(Gamma_t * gamma_t(k)), and the largest root is computable to precision epsilon in O(K log(1/epsilon)) time.

The screening-rent equilibrium paper (Zang, Andrade, Nakajima, arXiv:2609.20017, grounded in Polymarket transaction data of 588M trades and $67B volume) gives a no-pickoff screening floor (Lemma 1): a two-sided YES quote is pickoff-proof iff YES ask >= 1/2 + sigma and YES bid <= 1/2 - sigma, with executable premium s_D >= s_D^floor equivalent mu_F - mu_D and the screening band s_D in [s_D^floor, s_bar_D).
equation: YES ask >= 1/2 + sigma; YES bid <= 1/2 - sigma

claim: In the Polymarket transaction sample (738,393 trades across 275 Bitcoin 5-minute up/down markets, ~24h, $10.38M notional), makers earn at resolution not on the spread: 91.4% of persistent makers' profit arrived at settlement (<9% pre-settlement), makers made +$45.3K versus retail -$66.7K, one-sided edge was +$70K buying vs +$2.6K selling, and positions resolved favorably 56.8% of the time; regime-conditional pooled mid-band gaps flipped from +0.043 (longshot)/-0.037 (favorite) to +0.225/-0.071 in trending markets and -0.205/+0.066 in flippy markets.

The multi-outcome set premium decomposition is premium = [sum_j mid_j - 1] + sum_j (ask_j - mid_j), with the set premium coefficient on log n equal to +0.060 per log n (p<0.001), 96% of it in the committed-markup term, plus a NO-side replication premium of +0.048; fees in the studied market were 1.8% taker and 0% maker.

Lehoczky's extended drawdown formula (proved via excursion theory in Salminen & Vallois, arXiv:2411.18374) gives the joint Laplace transform of the drawdown time theta_delta = inf{t >= 0 : M_t - X_t > delta} and the running max at that time: E_x[exp(-alpha theta_delta - beta M_{theta_delta})] = [psi_alpha(x)/psi_alpha(x or (delta+l))] integral c_alpha(y;delta) exp(-beta y - integral b_alpha(z;delta) dS(z)) dS(y), where psi_alpha/phi_alpha are the fundamental solutions of d/dm d/dS u = alpha u, with the hitting-time Laplace E_x[e^{-alpha H_y}] = psi_alpha(x)/psi_alpha(y) for x<=y and phi_alpha(x)/phi_alpha(y) for x>=y.

For the Lehoczky/Malyutin drawdown framework, drawdown is D_t = M_t - X_t, maximum drawdown D^-_t = max_{s<=t}(M_s - X_s), and the only directly implementable case is Taylor's Brownian-with-drift specialization (Example 3.9, Eq. 3.15): the general formulas need the scale function S, speed measure m, and fundamental solutions of the bankroll diffusion (unknown for real weekly wagering), Laplace transforms must be numerically inverted (mpmath/scipy), and the diffusion of log bankroll is only an approximation of discrete weekly wagering with no estimation error or transaction costs.

The Independent Chip Model (ICM) validation study on 10,000+ poker tournaments (Juho Kim, arXiv:2506.00180v1, REJECT verdict for GSE) found ICM is roughly valid but systematically miscalibrated by stack size: P_i(1st) = chips_i/sum chips underestimates the probability that a large stack wins and overestimates the probability that a short stack cashes, partly because large stacks are large because they are skilled (skill-homogeneity violation); the finding has no fantasy-sports translation since DFS has no chip stacks, eliminations, or ICM analogue.

Learning-to-defer (arXiv:2006.01862) minimizes the system loss (1 - r(x))*ell(h(x), y) + r(x)*ell_exp(m, y) — model loss when not deferred plus expert loss when deferred — and uses a convex, Bayes-consistent cost-sensitive generalized cross-entropy surrogate whose minimizer is the Bayes-optimal classifier-rejector pair, where the rejector explicitly models P(expert correct | x).

The learning-to-defer paper beat confidence-threshold routing on CIFAR-10 (surrogate routes to the expert exactly on the expert's competent classes) and on hate-speech detection with an AAE-dialect-biased expert reached 92.91 +/- 0.17 versus 92.42 +/- 0.40 for the confidence baseline and 93.22 +/- 0.11 for oracle routing — capturing most of the oracle's routing gain — and crucially learned NOT to defer the dialect subpopulation the expert was biased against, a bias-audit template.

Empirical-Bayes (James-Stein) shrinkage on Bradley-Terry-Luce team-strength MLEs uses gamma_hat_JS = (I - Sigma(Sigma+A)^{-1}) gamma_hat_MLE + Sigma(Sigma+A)^{-1} u, with inversion-free shrinkage R_hat = (I + A S)^{-1} where S = N*J(gamma_hat_MLE, D) or N*I(gamma_hat_MLE, D) (observed/expected Fisher, no Sigma inversion), prior covariance A_ii = gamma_hat_{MLE,i}(1-gamma_hat_{MLE,i})/(n(n+1)), A_ij = gamma_hat_{MLE,i}gamma_hat_{MLE,j}/(n+1), and shrink target u_i = 1/n.

On the semi-synthetic NFL 2016 schedule (256 games, 32 teams, known ground-truth skills), James-Stein shrinkage with expected Fisher reduced parameter MSE by 51% (alpha=0.51) and pairwise-probability error by 12%; on real NFL2016, win% MSE fell from 0.0591 to 0.0491 (-16.8%, parametric blocked bootstrap) and matchup Brier MSE fell up to -9.2% with parametric bootstraps, while non-parametric bootstraps gave only about -1% because they cannot resample single-occurrence matchups; on NBA2016 (82 games) gains were smaller (win% MSE -9.1%, matchup <1%), showing seasons with more games need less shrinkage.

NBA2Vec (arXiv:2302.13386) trains 8-dimensional dense player embeddings for 1,551 NBA players with p(outcome | O1..O5, D1..D5) = softmax(W_2 * ReLU(W_1 * [e_bar_off; e_bar_def] + b_1) + b_2), where e_bar is the mean of the 5 player embeddings (permutation invariance via averaging), a 128-unit ReLU hidden layer, softmax over 23 play-outcome classes, and cross-entropy loss (equivalent to KL divergence vs empirical outcome distributions).
equation: p(outcome | O1..O5, D1..D5) = softmax(W_2 * ReLU(W_1 * [e_bar_off; e_bar_def] + b_1) + b_2)

claim: NBA2Vec achieved mean validation KL divergence of about 0.3 on the final 25 playoff games (5,102 plays) of ~3.7M NBA plays through 2017; KL plateaus at about 30 plays per lineup matchup; embeddings cluster recognizable roles and correlate significantly with rebounds, assists, and 3P rates; and the matchup optimizer found Nene as 5th man vs the Warriors death lineup gave 37.3% series win probability versus Trevor Ariza 34.4% and Carmelo Anthony 33.4%.

The flexible marked spatio-temporal Hawkes-style point process (Narayanan, Kosmidis & Dellaportas, arXiv:2103.04647v3) decouples mark excitation from event timing: L(Ftn | zeta, theta) = prod_i g(ti | Fti-1; zeta) f(mi | ti, Fti-1; theta) {1 - G(T | Ftn; zeta)}, with the mark PMF f(mi | ti, Fti-1; theta) = [delta_{mi} + sum_{tj<ti} alpha* e^{-beta(ti-tj)} gamma_{mj->mi}] / [1 + sum_{tj<ti} alpha* e^{-beta(ti-tj)}] and alpha* = epsilon*beta/mu.
equation: f(mi | ti, Fti-1; theta) = [delta_{mi} + sum_{tj<ti} alpha* e^{-beta(ti-tj)} gamma_{mj->mi}] / [1 + sum_{tj<ti} alpha* e^{-beta(ti-tj)}]

claim: On 2013/14 EPL touch-ball data (500,000+ events, 30 composite marks, 3 pitch zones), excitation dominated the event sequence: the 95% HPD for exp(alpha) was (451.35, 642.54), meaning prior events carry about 500x the weight of background in the mark PMF; the mark-pair x zone-specific decay model M_beta achieved the best held-out log predictive density (-21,342.57 versus first-order Markov -21,898.31), and corner->shot excitation persisted longer than corner->pass (beta (0.16,0.44) vs (1.34,2.36)); home advantage lived in conversion/ability parameters rather than background rates, and the M_beta simulator predicted '>=1 home shot in next 30s' with AUC 0.67 vs moving-average baselines at 0.48-0.50.

AI Feynman 2.0 (Udrescu et al., arXiv:2006.10782) defines mean error-description-length per candidate as d_k = (1/N) sum_i d_ki with Pareto dominance meaning f_a dominates f_b iff simpler AND more accurate; after each module merge (n1*n2 combinations) it prunes all Pareto-dominated candidates, and the Pareto-optimal count grows only logarithmically with total candidates.

AI Feynman 2.0 discovers compositional substructure by training a neural network on the mystery function and examining gradient properties to find arbitrary n-ary modules (e.g., the (v1+v2)/(1+v1*v2) relativistic velocity-addition module was found, then recursion ran on the reduced variable); it improved noise robustness by 1-3 orders of magnitude over v1 (added noise shifts the best formula 'straight upward' in the Pareto plane rather than breaking discovery), and its normalizing-flow + symbolic-regression lane maps samples of an unknown distribution f to a normal and then symbolically regresses the estimated density — the first SR method for 'given samples, find the distribution's symbolic form.'

OneBM (IBM Research, arXiv:1706.00327) enumerates joining paths p = T_0 -c1-> T_1 ... -ck-> T_k => c (T_0 = main table) via DFS to MaxDepth (simple paths only, forward-only vs backward-allowed, one-to-one vs multiple path types, redundant paths removed via canonical forms), builds per-entity relational trees T^e_p grouped by depth-d nodes, applies type-appropriate transforms (time series -> avg/max/min/sum/count/var, recent(k), FFT, discrete wavelet, autocorrelation; categorical sequence -> count/distinct/high-correlated subsequences), and enforces temporal safety by only collecting data generated before the prediction cutoff timestamp to avoid mining leakage.

OneBM reached the top 16-24% of three Kaggle competitions with zero hand-crafted features: KDD Cup 2014 (OneBM+XGBoost 81st, AUC 0.59696, top 17% untuned), Grupo Bimbo (RMSLE 0.48681, rank 326 = top 16% of 1,969 teams, top correlated features were demand-series aggregates: mean 0.454, min 0.414, max 0.392, recent(1) 0.385), and Outbrain click prediction (linear ensemble 0.65078, rank 227 = top 24%, 77% of the best human score 0.70); runtimes were 0.3h, 2.8h, and 32.7h respectively.

HiT-JEPA (arXiv:2507.00028) is a hierarchical (point -> segment -> trajectory) self-supervised trajectory embedding: T^(1)=Conv1D(T); T^(2)=MaxPool1D(Conv1D(T^(1))); T^(3)=MaxPool1D(Conv1D(T^(2))) (channel doubles, length halves per level, d=256), per-level Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (context encoder, EMA target encoder, 1-layer Transformers, 8 heads; M=4 masks, masking ratios 10-30%), with a top-down attention spotlight A^(l-1) <- (A^(l-1) + sigma tilde-A^(l)) (sigma learnable) and loss L = lambda L^(1) + mu L^(2) + nu L^(3) with lambda=0.05, mu=0.15, nu=0.8.

HiT-JEPA achieved the lowest self-similarity mean ranks across 5 of 6 trajectory datasets (T-Drive mean rank 1.040-1.041 across DB sizes, 1.031-1.038 across distortion rates 0.1-0.5) and the lowest mean ranks in zero-shot transfers (Porto-trained to Tokyo/NYC check-ins and ocean-vessel data); fine-tuning beat T-JEPA by +12.6% on T-Drive (+6.4% on GeoLife), with Hausdorff +14.7% and discrete Frechet +19.9% relative gains; ablations showed 1 encoder layer per level best (2-3 layers overfit) and the reader flagged leakage caveats (self-similarity queries are odd/even splits of the same trajectory, inflating ~1.0 ranks).

TrajFM (arXiv:2408.15251) uses learnable relative-spatial rotary attention (STRPE): q_i = R_{Phi(x_i,y_i)} W_q e_i, k_j = R_{Phi(x_j,y_j)} W_k e_j, Phi(x,y) = W_Phi(x||y), theta_k = 10000^{-2k/d}, so that q_i^T k_j = e_i^T W_q^T R_{Phi(x_i,y_i)-Phi(x_j,y_j)} W_k e_j — attention depends only on relative displacement, making it region-agnostic; L=2 layers, d=128, with per-point spatial/temporal/POI-text modalities.
equation: q_i^T k_j = e_i^T W_q^T R_{Phi(x_i,y_i)-Phi(x_j,y_j)} W_k e_j

claim: TrajFM's masking-and-recovery pretraining unifies all downstream trajectory tasks as masking patterns with zero retraining: modality masking (mask spatial/temporal of a point, recover at same step), sub-trajectory masking (replace <p_s,...,p_e> with a mask point, append start token, recover autoregressively), loss = sum MSE (spatial/temporal) + BCE (end token) with L^s_i = (x_hat_i - x_i)^2 + (y_hat_i - y_i)^2; it was superior in region transfer (train Chengdu -> test Xi'an and vice versa, sometimes beating in-domain), with ablations showing STRPE > vanilla Transformer and optimal L=2, d=128 (larger L 'overly complicated and harder to train').

AdaER (arXiv:2308.03810v2) for continual learning selects replay examples by an interference score from a virtual one-step-ahead classifier: theta' = theta - alpha nabla_theta l(f_theta; B_t) (one SGD step on the new batch without replay), s(m) = l(f_{theta'}(x_m), y_m) - l(f_theta(x_m), y_m), where higher s(m) means more forgotten by the new batch; it maintains a class-entropy-balanced buffer with importance-aware eviction (remove the least-important example by the C-CMR score, protecting the most-forgotten).

AdaER achieved Split-MNIST 89.6% accuracy (+3.7% over ER) and Split-FMNIST 74.0% (+6.3%), best overall versus all 9 baselines; on Split-CIFAR10 backward transfer was +4.4 versus -19.9 for ER (positive backward transfer = later tasks help earlier ones) with forgetting 18.0 (28.0% lower than MIR); growing the buffer M from 50 to 200 lifted GEM accuracy by 49.9% but AdaER by only 2.5%, showing AdaER is far less buffer-size-sensitive.

Adaptive Deep Kernel Learning (arXiv:1905.12131v2) learns a family of task-conditioned deep kernels k_ADKL(x,x';z_t) := k_rho(phi_theta(x;z_t), phi_theta(x';z_t)) where the task embedding z^t = psi_eta(D^t_trn) = w(Concat(mu^t_xy, sigma^t_xy)) is a permutation-invariant DeepSets encoder (each input-target pair encoded then mean/std pooled), the conditional input embedding is phi_theta(x;z_t) = o(Concat(u'(x), z_t)), and an InfoNCE meta-regularizer (Eq. 12) pushes train-task embeddings to be informative.

In the ADKL experiments (sinusoids: 5,000 tasks; Binding: 7,620 tasks; Antibacterial: 3,842 tasks), ADKL-KRR and ADKL-GP consistently beat R2-D2 and CNP on all three collections, with the ADKL-vs-R2-D2 gap being the pure effect of test-time kernel adaptation; all deep-kernel methods beat non-DKL with as few as 15 support samples, a linear base kernel generalized better than RBF (RBF's shared length-scale resists task adaptation), and InfoNCE meta-regularization (gamma in {0.1, 0.01}) helped in most configurations versus gamma=0.

Conservative Q-Learning (Kumar et al., arXiv:2006.04779) minimizes min_Q max_mu alpha(E_{s~D,a~mu}[Q(s,a)] - E_{s~D,a~pi_beta}[Q(s,a)]) + (1/2)E_{s,a,s'~D}[(Q - B_hat^{pi_k} Q_hat^k)^2] + R(mu), so the learned Q-values lower-bound the true policy value (Theorem 3.3), enabling safe policy improvement from fixed logged data; the CQL(H) variant uses alpha E_{s~D}[log sum_a exp(Q(s,a)) - E_{a~pi_beta}[Q(s,a)]] in place of the max_mu term.
equation: min_Q max_mu alpha(E_{s~D,a~mu}[Q(s,a)] - E_{s~D,a~pi_beta}[Q(s,a)]) + (1/2)E[(Q - B_hat^{pi_k} Q_hat^k)^2] + R(mu)

claim: CQL on D4RL benchmarks: on Gym MuJoCo it beat prior methods by 'large margins, sometimes as much as 2-3x' on multi-policy/complex datasets; on Adroit it was the only method family improving over behavioral cloning, attaining 2-9x the scores of the next-best offline RL method; on AntMaze it was the only method making meaningful progress on medium/large mazes; on Franka Kitchen it exceeded 40% success on all tasks as the only method beating BC; on offline Atari with 1% of DQN replay it achieved 36x and 6x the return of the best prior method on Q*bert and Breakout respectively.

Using a pretrained GPT-2 (frozen, W = W_0 + BA with low-rank LoRA update, rank r << d) as the Decision Transformer backbone (arXiv:2411.17900, offline trading policies from A2C/DDPG/PPO/TD3/SAC expert trajectories on 29 DJIA stocks, 2009-2020, evaluated 2020-07-01 to 2021-10-29) gave DT-LoRA-GPT2 return/drawdown/Sharpe of 43.72+/-2.04% / -8.42+/-0.57% / 1.76+/-0.08 versus expert 34.69/-9.12/1.60, DT-LoRA-Random 38.66+/-0.43/-9.42+/-0.18/1.80+/-0.02, and CQL 48.00+/-3.75/-9.32/2.23+/-0.10 — pretrained init consistently beat random init (43.72 vs 38.66 on A2C; 47.98 vs 42.88 on DDPG), while value-based CQL remained the strongest baseline on raw return/Sharpe.

GameNGen (Valevski et al., arXiv:2408.14837) repurposed pretrained Stable Diffusion v1.4 as a real-time DOOM engine predicting next frames at 20 FPS on one TPU; its stability recipe is training always teacher-forced while adding conditioning noise augmentation so training sees corrupted conditioning and learns to recover, preventing autoregressive 'sampling divergence'; it reached next-frame PSNR 29.4 (comparable to lossy JPEG), human raters chose the real game at near-chance rates (58%/60% on short clips, 50% after 5-10 min of play), context ablation showed big gains from 1 to 2 frames then rapid asymptote (~3s history), and health/ammo tallies persisted far beyond the 3s conditioning window.

Quantitative probing (Grunbaum, Stern, Lang, arXiv:2209.03013) is a model-agnostic validation framework for causal discovery: quantitative domain-knowledge expectations about non-target effects (probes) are stated before analysis, a probe counts as a hit when |tau_hat_probe - tau_probe| <= epsilon_probe, and the fraction recovered (hit rate) judges whether the learned graph and target-effect estimate can be trusted; a failed probe triggers reexamination of the graph, estimation, or expectations.

In 1,378 simulation runs (random DAGs, n=7 nodes, p_edge=0.1, m=1,000 samples, FGES discovery + linear-regression ATEs), mean absolute/relative target error and mean structural Hamming distance went approximately linearly to 0 as probe hit rate approached 1; 14 runs had perfect hit rate 1.0 yet absolute target error >= 0.2, caused by disconnected graphs (probes in one component, target in another) — filtering to connected graphs (653 runs) left only 4 such cases, so probes must be in the same connected component as (ideally close to) the target.

TabRepo (Salinas & Erickson 2024, arXiv:2311.02971) is a dense repository of 786,000 precomputed model evaluations (1,310 configs x 200 datasets) enabling offline AutoML analysis and zero-shot portfolio learning via greedy complementarity selection: j_1 = argmin E_i[l_{i,j_1}]; j_n = argmin E_i[min_{k<=n} l_{i,j_k}] (Caruana-style greedy complementarity).

TabRepo's greedy zero-shot portfolio (ensemble) achieved normalized error 0.365 with rank 168.7 and 6275.5s fit versus AutoGluon 0.389/208.2/5583.1s, AutoSklearn2 0.455 (14415.9s fit), LightAutoML 0.466, and FLAML 0.5+ (4h budget, 200 tasks); CatBoost dominated with defaults while FT-Transformer and LightGBM were runners-up, 4h tuning + ensembling improved every family, ensembling let LightGBM match CatBoost, and no single model was best everywhere — supporting season-conditioned model selection.

Data Shapley valuation (Ghorbani, Zou, Esteva, arXiv:2104.08312) is defined axiomatically (null-element, symmetry, linearity) as phi(z) = sum_{i=0}^{N-1} sum_{s subset of N-{z}, |s|=i} [v(s U {z}) - v(s)] / C(N-1, |s|), equivalently phi(z) = E_{pi~Pi}[v(s_pi^z U {i}) - v(s_pi^z)], with exact linear-time KNN-Shapley via dynamic programming (Jia et al. 2019) on KNN in pre-logit representation space; Active Data Shapley (ADS) pre-selects the top 2-10x batch (30% CIFAR-10, 20% CINIC-10/Tiny ImageNet, 10% large noisy pools) before running a diversity-based batch AL method on the subset only.
equation: phi(z) = sum_{i=0}^{N-1} sum_{s subset of N-{z}, |s|=i} [v(s U {z}) - v(s)] / C(N-1, |s|)

claim: Active Data Shapley (ADS) gave 2.6-8x speedup of the diversity step across methods/datasets (~6x average, ~6.4x curated, gains growing with pool size since diversity methods are ~O(n^3)) with first-iteration accuracy preserved or improved (BADGE+ADS 64.3/95.4/70.4 vs BADGE 63.9/95.0/70.4 on Cheap-10/SVHN/CINIC-10); in noisy regimes (80% Beta-noise-corrupted SVHN-extra, Cheap-10 web-scraped pool, CINIC-10 domain shift) ADS-Coreset was best; optimistic max-over-classes aggregation (Shapley(x^u) := max_c Shapley((x^u, y_c))) beat mean/weighted-mean.

Flow with FlorDB (Garcia et al., UC Berkeley, arXiv:2408.02498v2) is a systems position paper on 'hindsight logging' — record cheap execution state, compute arbitrary new metadata post-hoc across pipeline versions via record-replay, resolving the metadata-first vs move-fast tension via the ABCs of context (Application, Behavioral, Change); it reports zero numerical results (no experiments, baselines, or metrics), and the reader noted caveats including that 'sufficient execution state' for arbitrary future queries is asserted not bounded and it does not address point-in-time feature correctness.

LakeVilla (Gotz, Ritter, Giceva 2025, arXiv:2504.20768v2) adds three composable per-transaction features to lakehouse OTF protocols non-invasively: LV[R] recovery (file-based markers reserve snapshot versions, transaction sublogs + undo/redo adapt to concurrent changes instead of aborting), LV[CT] complex multi-table transactions (marker-based conflict/deadlock detection; LV[R,CT] gives global serializability), LV[I] isolation via a global version log with atomic validation (R1-R3: read-set freshness, write-set conflicts, version distance); headline overhead is 2% on YCSB writes and 2.5% on TPC-DS reads, LV[I]'s global version log adds ~4 ms per read/write, LV[R] had zero aborts versus rising Spark abort rates at 1->64 clients, and LV[CT] commit latency stays flat ~1s up to 32 tables.

Warm-start genetic programming for alpha mining (Ren, Qin, Li, arXiv:2412.00896) seeds GP from a single known-effective alpha's structure and restricts crossover to structure-preserving subtree swaps (offspring structure = parent structure by construction; generation 1 = point mutation only; tournament selection + restricted crossover or point mutation; elitism; duplicate individuals rejected).

Warm-start GP on Chinese A-shares (2020-2021 mining, 2022 fit, 2023-01 to 2024-10 backtest, 5-day holding, VWAP, 0.6 permille cost, 10 Alpha101 seeds): structure-constrained random alphas had P(IC > 0.03) > 13% (3x the unconstrained density); 10 Alpha101 seeds enhanced out-of-sample IC 0.015->0.047, RankIC 0.019->0.078, ICIR 0.15->0.43, RankICIR 0.17->0.60 (out-of-sample IC 0.047 exceeded in-sample 0.034); warm-start beat traditional GP by >1% IC and ~1% RankIC out-of-sample; the top-10 warm-start alphas had avg |Spearman| = 0.60 vs 0.87 for traditional GP (seven traditional runs produced identical factors — no diversification), and backtest annual return/Sharpe at size 10 was WS_LR 0.484/0.937 vs GP_LR 0.024/0.052 vs Alpha101_LR -0.083/-0.231.

TabSyn (Zhang et al. 2023, arXiv:2310.09656) generates mixed-type tabular data via two stages: a tabular VAE (column tokenizer d=4; 2-layer Transformer encoder/decoder D=128; beta-VAE loss L = l_recon + beta l_kl with adaptive beta: betamax=0.01, beta <- 0.7 beta on recon-loss plateau, floor betamin=1e-5) plus latent VE-SDE score diffusion (z_t = z_0 + sigma(t) epsilon; score-matching loss L = E||epsilon_theta(z_t,t) - epsilon||^2; 5-layer SiLU denoising MLP); its Proposition 1 proves the linear noise schedule sigma(t) = t makes Euler one-step reverse error exactly 0, giving best quality at <20 NFEs (vs STaSy 50-200, TabDDPM ~1000).

TabSyn on six tabular datasets: column density error avg 1.08% vs best-baseline avg 14.52% (86.0% error reduction claimed; News: 1.64 vs STaSy 6.89, TabDDPM 78.75); pair correlation error avg 1.73 vs TabDDPM 5.34 (67.6% reduction); MLE (XGBoost trained on synthetic, tested real) avg gap to Real-trained 7.23% (TabDDPM 19.14%, SMOTE 9.39%; Adult AUC 0.915, Shoppers 0.920, Magic 0.938); ablation showed latent space is the key (TabSyn-DDPM 1.02/2.15 beats TabDDPM-in-data-space 1.75/3.01); Adult sampling 1.784s vs TabDDPM 28.92s (93% reduction) with same hyperparameters on all 6 datasets, no per-dataset tuning; unconditional TabSyn as inpainting imputer beat XGBoost-on-real on 4/6 tasks (Default AUC 87.2 vs 77.0); DCR privacy 51.20%/52.90% (50% = ideal, no memorization).

Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023, arXiv:2303.11366v4) learns via verbal reinforcement with no gradient updates: triad of Actor M_a (CoT/ReAct), Evaluator M_e (scores the trajectory; exact-match / heuristics / LLM-as-judge), Self-Reflection M_sr (writes textual lesson); loop r_t = M_e(tau_t); sr_t = M_sr({tau_t, r_t}, mem); mem <- mem U {sr_t}, |mem| <= Omega (Omega = 1-3; 3 for AlfWorld/HotPotQA, 1 for programming).

Reflexion results: AlfWorld ReAct+Reflexion solves 130/134 (ReAct-only converges at 22% hallucination rate with no long-term recovery; Reflexion eliminates almost all possession-confusion failures); HotPotQA +20% over baselines, retry-only baselines solve ZERO new failed tasks on later trials at temperature 0.7, self-reflection adds 8% absolute over episodic memory alone; HumanEval Python pass@1 91.0 (Reflexion) vs GPT-4 80.1 vs previous SOTA 65.8; ablation on hardest-50 HumanEval Rust: full Reflexion 0.68, reflection WITHOUT grounded signal 0.52 (worse than 0.60 baseline — reflection without a trustworthy evaluator is actively harmful), test-gen only 0.60 (no gain).

A 2025 theory paper on statistical limits of self-improving agents (arXiv:2510.04399) proves utility-driven self-modification preserves PAC learnability iff the policy-reachable model family is uniformly capacity-bounded (sup VC(H_reach) < infinity) — unbounded capacity turns learnable tasks unlearnable — and proposes a Two-Gate promotion policy: accept a self-modification iff validation margin >= tau AND capacity proxy B(Z_new) <= K(m) (sample-size-dependent cap), with capacity bounds enforced GLOBALLY since per-axis budgets allow multiplicative emergent capacity explosions; the ledger's operational proxy is B = (# free parameters) + (# engineered features) + (rule count x avg conditions) with cap K = 2 x training seasons.

CLIP (Radford et al., ICML 2021, arXiv:2103.00020v1) trains dual encoders (ResNet or ViT image encoder + Transformer text encoder) with an InfoNCE-style symmetric cross-entropy over the N x N image-text similarity matrix with learnable temperature tau (init 0.07, logits clipped <= 100) on 400M web image-text pairs (32 epochs, batch 32,768; RN50x64 took 18 days on 592 V100s); zero-shot transfer works by using the text encoder as a hypernetwork generating classifier weights from language, with a cosine-similarity classifier on L2-normalized inputs/weights, no bias, temperature scaling.

CLIP achieved ImageNet zero-shot 76.2% top-1 (matching supervised ResNet-50 with 0 of its 1.28M labels) and 95% top-5 (matching Inception-V4), improved prior zero-shot from 11.5% to 76.2% on ImageNet, reduced aYahoo error by 95%, more than doubled SUN 23.0->58.5, beat a supervised linear classifier on ResNet-50 features on 16/27 datasets, and prompt engineering + ensembling gave ~+5 points average across 36 datasets ('A photo of a {label}.' +1.3% ImageNet; 80-variant ensemble averaged in embedding space +3.5%) — roughly the gain of 4x compute, 'free' when amortized; known weaknesses: polysemy breaks transfer, bag-of-words behavior on compositional/spatial relations, and zero-shot cosine similarities are uncalibrated probabilities.

ProbFM (2026, arXiv:2601.10591v1) is a probabilistic time-series foundation model with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma deep evidential regression head emitting calibrated uncertainty decomposed into aleatoric vs epistemic components in a single forward pass: p(mu,sigma^2|m,lambda,alpha,beta) = N(mu|m,sigma^2/lambda) x InvGamma(sigma^2|alpha,beta), network outputs (m,lambda,alpha,beta) with lambda,alpha,beta > 0 via softplus; aleatoric uncertainty = beta/(alpha-1), epistemic = beta/((alpha-1) x lambda), total predictive variance = beta/(alpha-1) x (1 + 1/lambda).
equation: aleatoric = beta/(alpha-1); epistemic = beta/((alpha-1) x lambda)

claim: ProbFM's crypto position-sizing experiment: DER-based strategy Sharpe 1.33 vs MSE baseline 0.90, Sortino 2.27 vs 1.52, Calmar 3.04, win rate 0.52; DER was competitive on accuracy with better-calibrated uncertainty than Gaussian NLL on LSTM-backbone comparisons; the reader flagged that experiments are LSTM-scale (no 100M+ parameter TSFM demonstration — 'foundation model' in the title outruns the evidence), the Gaussian likelihood is misspecified for skewed sports outcomes, and miscalibrated epistemic uncertainty is worse than none for abstention decisions.

CVaR learning (Wang, Kallus & Sun, arXiv:2302.03201) defines CVaR_tau(X) = sup_{b in R}(b - tau^{-1} E[(b-X)^+]) = E[X | X <= F_X^{dagger}(tau)] for continuous X (tau=1 gives expectation, tau->0 gives essential infimum), CVaR-RL is equivalent to a robust MDP under worst-case transition perturbation; minimax lower bounds are MAB >= (1/24e) sqrt((A-1)K/tau) and RL >= (1/24e) sqrt(S(A-1)K/tau) for tau in (0,1/2) with Bernoulli rewards — CVaR learning is strictly harder than risk-neutral by a sqrt(tau^{-1}) factor.
equation: CVaR_tau(X) = sup_{b in R}(b - tau^{-1} E[(b-X)^+])

claim: The paper's Bernstein-UCB (per-arm pessimistic shortfall mu_hat_k(b,a) = (1/N_k(a)) sum_{i<k} (b-r_i)^+ 1[a_i=a]; bonus Bon_k(a) = sqrt(2 tau log(AK/delta)/N_k(a)) + log(AK/delta)/N_k(a); optimistic CVaR f_hat_k(b,a) = b - tau^{-1}(mu_hat_k(b,a) - Bon_k(a)); pull argmax_a f_hat_k(b_hat_{a,k}, a)) improves Tamkin et al.'s CVaR-UCB suboptimal tau^{-1} dependence to tau^{-1/2}, with matching minimax-optimal upper bounds MAB <= 4 sqrt(tau^{-1} A K) L + 16 tau^{-1} A L^2 (L = log(AK/delta)) and RL <= O-tilde(tau^{-1} sqrt(SAK)) improving Bastani et al. 2022 by S sqrt(H); it is purely theoretical with zero empirical validation.

SINDy (Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics) with control fits x_dot(t) approx = Theta^T phi(x,u) via the sparse problem min_Theta ||X_dot - Phi(X,U) Theta||^2_2 + lambda^2 sum_i ||Theta_i||_0, with the STLS iteration converging in <= n_phi steps to a LOCAL minimizer — no guarantee of true structure even with correct bases in the library; it is scored with BFR = max(1 - sum(y_k - y_hat)^2/sum(y_k - y_bar)^2, 0) [%] and RMSE computed on open-loop simulation.

Ugolini et al.'s benchmarking study (arXiv:2403.00578v1, three nonlinear-identification benchmarks with unobserved states and hard non-smooth nonlinearities) found: pick-and-place BFR 76% (94% with better threshold) for 2nd-order derivative-coordinate SINDy versus 75 PWA and 83 jump models, while naive 1st-order SINDy (y_dot = -111.16 y + 133.73 u - 3.48 y u) missed all key dynamics; Bouc-Wen showed structurally CORRECT models scoring WORSE on test metrics than structurally wrong HPO models (only the Ideal variant reproduced the hysteresis cycle); cascaded tanks: hidden-SINDy Poly 93.24/0.55 vs NN-ARX 95.10/0.47 (slightly better but uninterpretable) vs linear ARX 86.55/0.77 — linear ARX beat naive nonlinear SINDy — with the core finding that test-metric-optimal != structurally correct and validation RMSE preferred the polynomial model (0.356) over the physics-informed sqrt model (0.383).

ERBench (Kahlmeyer et al. 2026, arXiv:2606.09276) is the first benchmark for equation-discovery algorithms scoring symbolic recovery of known ground-truth laws instead of in-domain fit: Symbolic Recovery Rate f_hat = f iff sympy proves f(x)-f_hat(x)=c_0 or f(x)/f_hat(x)=c_1 (sympy timeouts count as failures, strict lower bound), Jaccard Index JI = |S_true intersect S_pred| / |S_true union S_pred| over unique subexpression sets, and normalized Tree Edit Distance TED = dist/(|T_true| + |T_pred|) via Zhang-Shasha.

ERBench on a 1,000-formula secret set (6 algorithms x default hyperparams x 5 runs): PySR is the only method with non-trivial recovery, 0.29 +/- 0.04; DSR, E2E, Operon 0.00; gplearn 0.05 +/- 0.01; linear baseline 0.00; JI: PySR 0.49 +/- 0.02, DSR 0.28, linear 0.25 (complex methods barely beat linear on parsimony-adjusted partial credit); TED: PySR 13.4, linear 14.6, gplearn 45.2; PySR has near-perfect recovery at 1-3 operators but near-zero beyond 13 operators, uniform sampling adds ~10% over diverse distribution, and pre-trained transformers (E2E) collapse outside pre-training domains — problem complexity, not data scarcity, is the principal bottleneck.

NFS (Gu, Vosoughi & Prioleau 2021, Dartmouth, arXiv:2102.06024v3) is a neural feature selector for multivariate time series: each of d univariate streams goes through its own temporal CNN then an aggregating CNN; importance score per stream = batch-norm affine scale alpha_i (no extra parameters), z_out^i = alpha_i z_norm^i + beta_i; training objective L = sum l(f(x,W),y) + gamma sum_i |alpha_i|, gamma = 0.001 (l = MSE or cross-entropy; L2 coefficient 0.01 on weights); selection retains top-k alpha_i.

NFS on four multivariate time-series datasets (every model trained 5x and averaged): OhioT1DM (5/19 streams) NFS+LSTM RMSE 17.50 vs full 17.80 vs AgnoS 19.52 vs published SOTA NPE+LSTM 17.80; Favorita (5/15) delta=2d MAE 4.441 vs 4.877 full vs 5.044 AgnoS; PhysioNet 2012 (16/37) NFS+t-LeNet AUC 0.9179 vs 0.9045 full vs 0.9032 AgnoS vs GRU-D 0.8424 (+0.075 over prior SOTA), best on all 7 downstream models; Face Detection (32/144) NFS+MCDCNN accuracy 0.636 vs 0.629 full vs 0.598 AgnoS vs SNN 0.57, best on all models; consistent pattern: NFS >= full-set on every model/dataset (pruning never hurts, usually helps) and supervised gradient selection beats unsupervised AgnoS.

The Neural Game Engine (Bamford & Lucas 2020, arXiv:2003.10520) is a modified Neural GPU — state as a 2D grid (W_s,H_s,C_s) with one vector per tile, 3x3 convolutional kernel banks U,U',U'' masked to the 4-neighborhood (no diagonals), per frame a CGRU cell iterated n times to produce the next state, decoded to O_{t+1} and reward r_t, with 2D diagonal gating (state split 5 ways, fixed-kernel convolutions copy tile info to neighbors); the key property is that changing (W_s,H_s) changes zero parameters, giving unbounded size generalization.

Neural Game Engine results on 10 deterministic GVGAI games (1.28M frames per experiment, evaluation rollouts vs the true engine up to 500 steps x 10 repeats): size generalization from 10x10 training to 30x30/50x50/70x70/100x100 gave max E_mse 7.5-8.3e-6 with F1 = 1.0 everywhere over 500 steps (zero degradation at 100x the cells); most games reached F_t = 1.0 and F_r = 1.0 (perfect pixel and reward prediction); iteration ablation showed n=2 reaches very high rollout accuracy vs 5 hand-built GVGAI levels while n=1 plateaus much lower (multiple iterations are vital for non-local interactions); failures: aliens (stochastic enemies, partial observability) min F_t = 0.73, clusters reward completely unlearned.

Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR, Romano/Patterson/Candes 2019, arXiv:1905.03222): E_i = max(q_{alpha_lo}(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_{alpha_hi}(X_i)), alpha_lo = alpha/2, alpha_hi = 1 - alpha/2; calibration quantile = ceil((1-alpha)(|I_2|+1))-th largest of {E_i}; interval C(X_{n+1}) = [q_{alpha_lo} - Q_{1-alpha}, q_{alpha_hi} + Q_{1-alpha}] with guarantee P{Y_{n+1} in C} >= 1 - alpha under exchangeability; the audit's central thesis is 'eliminate fake tightness' — fail-closed (emit infinite intervals or No-Bet) when the calibration sample is too small to certify the nominal quantile, never clamping the quantile to the largest observed residual.

The conformal audit's mandatory hand computation for n=5, alpha=0.10: inflation (1-alpha)(1+1/n) = 1.08; rank k = ceil(6*0.90) = 6 > n=5, so the quantile at level >1.0 is +infinity and the system must refuse/No-Bet; the minimum n for an alpha=0.1 guarantee is ceil(1/alpha)-1 = 9; clamping k to n=5 yields max residual with true coverage 5/6 ~ 83.33% (a 6.67% under-coverage defect) while claiming 90% — explicitly banned as 'fake tightness'; Jackknife+ guarantees 1 - 2*alpha (80% at alpha=0.10), split conformal requires delta >= 1/(n+1) or infinite sets/abstain, and for binary moneylines CQR is invalid — use Venn-Abers multiprobability bounds [p0,p1] with refusal when p1-p0 > 0.20, plus ECE > 0.05 fail-closed and n >= 30 before public performance displays.

LEAP (arXiv 2609.01337, Chen et al., Sep 2026) replaces a monolithic LLM forecast with evidence-isolated elicitation plus deterministic tempered Bayesian aggregation; the task schema is T = (q, tfreeze, tau, O) and the posterior is P(theta|E) proportional to P0(theta) times the product over i in R of Pi(ei|theta) under a conditional independence assumption repaired by dependency clustering on canonicalized dependency keys.
equation: T = (q, tfreeze, τ, O);  P(θ|E) ∝ P0(θ) ∏_{i∈R} Pi(ei|θ)

claim: LEAP's continuous aggregation update is tau_post = tau0 + eta * sum_{i in R} tau_i, mu_post = (1/tau_post)(mu0*tau0 + eta * sum_{i in R} mu_i*tau_i), with per-evidence leave-one-out contribution Delta_j = mu_post - mu_post^(-j).
equation: τpost = τ0 + η Σ_{i∈R} τi;  µpost = (1/τpost)(µ0τ0 + η Σ_{i∈R} µiτi);  Δj = µpost − µpost^(−j)

claim: LEAP's discrete aggregation is: single-choice log pi_post(k) proportional to alpha * log pi0(k) + eta * sum_{i in R} w_i * log L_i(k) with softmax and Delta_j = pi_post(k_hat) - pi_post^(-j)(k_hat); multi-choice logit pi_post(k) = logit pi0(k) + eta * sum_{i in R} w_i * l_i(k) with Delta_j = sum_k |pi_post(k) - pi_post^(-j)(k)|.
equation: log πpost(k) ∝ α log π0(k) + η Σ_{i∈R} wi log Li(k), softmax;  Δj = πpost(k̂) − πpost^(−j)(k̂);  logit πpost(k) = logit π0(k) + η Σ_{i∈R} wi ℓi(k);  Δj = Σ_k |πpost(k) − πpost^(−j)(k)|

claim: LEAP's scoring rules are Brier = (1/N) sum_i (1/K_i) sum_k (p_ik - y_ik)^2, Spherical = (1/N) sum_i (sum_k p_ik*y_ik) / sqrt(sum_k p_ik^2 * sqrt(sum_k y_ik^2)), NCRPS_i = min(1, CRPS_i / max(|v_i|, 1)), and ECE as the gap between top-option confidence and empirical accuracy.
equation: Brier = (1/N) Σ_i (1/Ki) Σ_k (pik − yik)²;  Spherical = (1/N) Σ_i (Σ_k pik yik)/√(Σ_k p²ik √(Σ_k y²ik));  NCRPSi = min(1, CRPSi/max(|vi|,1));  ECE = gap between top-option confidence and empirical accuracy

claim: LEAP's fixed likelihood maps use continuous observation relative SDs {0.08, 0.18, 0.45} by type times tier multipliers (A 0.80, B 0.95, C 1.15, other 1.10) times strength (strong 0.85, weak 1.20) times reliability (high 0.85, low 1.15) times target_match times recency, clamped to [0.03, 1.25]; discrete likelihoods are support 0.90 / oppose 0.08 / neutral 0.12 (direct), verifier 0.99/0.01, fallback 0.85/0.12/0.35; role weights w_i in [0.05, 1.5] and eta = 1.0 by default.

LEAP beat Monolithic on all 5 base models with FutureX gains of 3.6-18.1 points and Spherical gains of 2.5-15.1 points, while Brier improved on only 3 of 5 models; calibration improved with ECE 0.1840 to 0.0876, Adaptive ECE 0.1765 to 0.0912, and overconfidence 0.3167 to 0.1500 (roughly halved); the ablation showed removing the prior (0.6427/0.2808/0.2134) fell below Monolithic (0.6512/0.2689/0.1840), making the prior the single most important component.

LEAP costs about 2x tokens per task (11,508 vs 5,733) with p95 latency 27.8s vs 12.1s; eta sensitivity is flat (0.5 -> 0.7181, 1.0 -> 0.7284, 2.0 -> 0.7210 FutureX) and linear opinion pooling (0.6808) loses to LEAP (0.7284); safeguards include dependency clustering with 85.3% retained and outlier rejection |mu_i - mu_0| > 4*sigma_0 for continuous observations.

The V8 pro-bettor model process checklist (from Rob Pizzola / Circles Off) requires seven mandatory ordered steps for shipping any sports prediction model: beatable market, data inventory, leakage review, preregistration, walk-forward versus closing line, honest-negative writeup, and ship criteria; a model that skips a step does not ship.

The ship criteria are all of: 0 leakage-probe failures, holdout Brier better than market baseline, holdout log-loss better than market baseline, passes W1 calibration gates, positive CLV on sealed holdout, thesis block present, known limitations stated, no 'any'/fake data/imputed finals, and reproducible (seeded, deterministic under V4 replay); leakage probes cover future-Elo contamination, current-week snap-share exclusion, and sign-convention, with chronological splits only (random splits forbidden), post-kickoff fields never entering features, and missing values staying null.

Isotonic calibration applies only if it improves holdout Brier; the cited discipline from sjpagano reports held-out 2025 numbers of Brier 0.1613, log loss 0.4831, AUC 0.8459, and ECE 0.0331, and the checklist holds that if the model cannot beat the closing line on holdout, the honest answer is a negative result, which is itself a deliverable.

The build handoff's V6 specifies 12-game trailing SOS-adjusted offensive/defensive ratings with prior-season Bayesian blending where weight w ramps 0 to 1 over about 6 weeks, a generalized Poisson for touchdowns that is under-dispersed with lambda < 0, separate field-goal/safety/XP/OT models, 5,000 Monte Carlo sims, and about a 10% home-field bump that is fit rather than hardcoded.

Expected value in the handoff is ev = p * decimalOdds - 1, emitted only when EV exceeds threshold AND the W1 calibration gate passes; the W1 gate applies isotonic only when holdout Brier improves (sjpagano's held-out 2025 numbers: Brier 0.1613, log loss 0.4831, AUC 0.8459, ECE 0.0331), and the W2 walk-forward benchmark cites benbr11's 65.9% versus about 66% closing-market parity.

V1 leakage probes detect three anti-patterns: future-Elo (a feature value that changes when future games are included means it leaked), current-week snap-share (features computable only from strictly earlier weeks, the TreMatt03 pattern), and sign-convention (predicted sign must match market sign convention, per urwishpatel2003's 86%-backtest bug); V4 deterministic replay requires one shared StrategyFn for live and replay paths, seeded RNG, byte-identical decision journals, and SKIPPED_NO_MARKET fail-closed (never invent prices).

GSE's computation conventions: EPA/EP are nflverse-shipped (nflfastR multinomial logistic regression on down, distance, field position), not re-estimated; a play is successful iff EPA > 0 (verified 100% match on pass/run plays); filters are season_type == 'REG' and play_type in ('pass','run'), excluding qb_kneel and qb_spike (453 kneels + 82 spikes in 2025); garbage time is Q4 with win probability > 0.95 or < 0.05 (removed 3,702 plays in 2025, 11.2%, and 238 in 2026 Week 1, 12.4%).

A dropback is defined as pass_attempt == 1 OR qb_scramble == 1 (sacks count as attempts), with 17,626 dropbacks in 2025; a designed rush is rush_attempt == 1 AND scramble == 0 AND kneel == 0; the explosive-play rate is dropback >= 15 yards OR designed rush >= 10 yards (4for4 convention); stuff rate is designed rushes with yards_gained <= 0.
equation: dropback = (pass_attempt == 1) OR (qb_scramble == 1);  designed rush = (rush_attempt == 1) AND (scramble == 0) AND (kneel == 0);  explosive = (dropback ≥ 15 yds) OR (designed rush ≥ 10 yds);  stuff rate = designed rushes with yards_gained ≤ 0

The NFL Big Data Bowl 2026 Prediction task (8,147 entrants, $50k prizes, Sep 2025 to Jan 2026) asked for post-throw player (x,y) per frame predicted from pre-pass NGS tracking plus targeted receiver identity and ball landing location, scored by RMSE = sqrt(1/(2N) * sum((x_true - x_pred)^2 + (y_true - y_pred)^2)) in yards; self-reported leaderboard scores were schubert-tom 0.518 (top 5%), shevchenko9liza 0.534, xxremsteelexx 0.540, with the best single model at 0.547 (6-layer ST transformer).

The winners' consensus techniques were delta (displacement) prediction over absolute coordinates, ball-landing conditioning via FiLM gates, LOS-centered/mirrored coordinate normalization, physics-informed losses (velocity/accel caps, direction-cosine loss, boundary and momentum penalties), horizontal-flip augmentation (most effective per 847-experiment ablations), test-time augmentation adding 0.005-0.010 on the leaderboard, up to 20-fold CV, and position-specific models; ball-landing features dist_to_ball and speed_toward_ball dominated feature importance at about 20% each in one analysis.

The Big Data Bowl dataset is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial), so a commercial product cannot train directly on the competition data while methods transfer; honest negatives reported include that dropping detected anomalies hurt (-0.14%), DBSCAN found no meaningful clusters, and Shapley-Flow duplicated plain SHAP (ARI=0.97); the reusable MIT-licensed repos are XxRemsteelexX and shevchenko9liza.

The bitemporal system tracks each observation's observedAt (when the thing happened) and recordedAt (when it entered the system) as TwinObservation invariants: recordedAt >= observedAt; foldObservationsAsOf supports three modes: 'transaction' (recordedAt <= asOf), 'evidence' (observedAt <= asOf), and 'both' (default), with a test-pinned case where 'both' and 'transaction' select identical sets.

The bitemporal fold law is latest observedAt wins, ties broken by latest recordedAt, full ties by later input position; the system never calls Date.now() (asOf is always a parameter), has 138+ tests, applies freshness decay at reconstruction point, and composes no-observation as unknown; it was motivated by an incident where /nflverse returned OOM-500 while /api/health stayed healthy.

arXiv:2412.03190v1 (Bhaskar et al. 2024, 'Node Classification With Integrated Reject Option') introduces the NCwR-Cost loss: a (K+1)-class cost-based reject loss l_ce^d(f(h), e_y) = -log f_y(h) - (1-d)*log f_{K+1}(h), consistent with the l_{0d1} loss, where small d prefers rejection and d=1 reduces to standard cross-entropy; it is backbone-agnostic and was evaluated on Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, ILDC, Thyroid, and Pima graphs.

The NCwR-Cov (coverage-constrained, SelectiveNet-style) baseline from arXiv:2412.03190v1 optimizes selective risk r(f,g|S_n) = [(1/n) sum l(f(h_i),y_i) g(h_i)] / phi(g|S_n) with coverage phi(g|S_n) = (1/n) sum g(h_i) and objective E(f,g) = r(f,g|S_n) + lambda Psi(c - phi(g|S_n)), Psi(a) = max(0,a)^2, lambda=32, final loss E = alpha E(f,g) + (1-alpha) E(f), alpha=0.5; the brief reports cost-based rejection beats this coverage-constrained head because cost rejects hard/boundary examples first while coverage constraint rejects arbitrary (sometimes easy) examples, e.g. whole classes 3-4 at 50.4% coverage, and NCwR-Cov optimization is unstable (high variance).

Measured results from the NCwR paper per the brief: NCwR-Cost on Cora gives d=0.5 -> 95.8 +/- 0.05 accuracy at 42.6 +/- 0.02 coverage and d=0.85 -> 87.2 +/- 0.06 at 90.5 +/- 0.07 coverage; Citeseer d=0.5 -> 91.6 +/- 0.12 at 9.7 +/- 0.05; on the real high-stakes ILDC legal task (7,593 Indian Supreme Court cases), NCwR-Cost d=0.25 -> 87.24 +/- 2.45 accuracy at 67.00 +/- 3.30 coverage and NCwR-Cov at coverage 0.5 -> 97.55 +/- 0.62 accuracy; cost-based rejection beats the Softmax-Response baseline at all coverage levels on all datasets.

Wang et al. (2018) 'The Advantage of Doubling' (arXiv:1803.02940v1, NBA double-team study on 875,412 SportVU possessions): dueling-CNN Q-learning policy (NBNet) with MDP state s_t = court config, 20 discrete actions (stay home or double leaving one of 19 regions open), reward = negative points {0,-1,...,-5} undiscounted; optimal values Q*_pi(s,a) = max_pi E[G_t | s_t=s, a_t=a], V*(s) = max_a Q*(s,a), A*(s,a) = Q*-V*, TD loss L = sum_i sum_t [Q*(s_t^i,a_t^i) - (r_t^i + V*(s_{t+1}^i))]^2 with double Q-learning; raw 90.6% doubling rate tamed to 29.29% (vs 33.92% observed) by suppressing doubles unless Q-margin over man-to-man >= 0.2.

From 'The Advantage of Doubling' findings: 4.8% of possessions contain a double team (range 3.8% Portland - 6.7% Milwaukee); doubling yields significantly lower offensive FG% but significantly higher foul rate; doubled ball handlers shoot only 6.2% of the time and pass-out-of-double beats keeping the ball; best-vs-double John Wall 1.07 ppp doubled vs 0.89 not, worst guard Lou Williams 0.68 vs 0.95; best tandems Lowry+Valanciunas 0.64 pts/poss allowed, Rubio+Towns force turnovers on 21.4% of doubles; learned policy: better to leave the open man in the paint than in the back, more hesitant to double stars, more willing to double role players; q_avg vs points correlation -0.08 (p<0.001) with clustering in [-1,0] vs mean reward ~-1.4 showing upward Q-learning bias (acknowledged).

Mahmudlu, Karakus & Arkadas (2025) 'What If They Took the Shot?' (arXiv:2511.23072v1): hierarchical Bayesian xG model eta_ij = alpha + (beta + gamma_i)^T x_ij with player-specific finishing deviations gamma_i ~ N(mu_i, Sigma) shrunk toward Football Manager 2017 priors; partial-pooling shrinkage gamma*_i ~ [tau_i^2/(tau_i^2+sigma^2)] gamma_hat^MLE_i + [sigma^2/(tau_i^2+sigma^2)] mu_i; inference via PyMC NUTS (4 chains x 2,000 warmup + 2,000 sampling, target acceptance 0.95).

From the 'What If They Took the Shot?' paper: counterfactual xG_B(A) = sum_i sigma(alpha + (beta+gamma_B)^T x_i), delta_xG_{B<-A} = xG_B(A) - xG_A(A) -> E[delta_xG], Pr(delta_xG>0), HDI_95%; FATS (Fit-Adjusted Transfer Score) = sum_c w_c Pr(delta_xG_c > 0) with w_c = target team's empirical context shares. On 9,970 shots by 148 players (StatsBomb 2015-16 top-five leagues): Berardi->Sansone delta_xG = +2.2; Lewandowski->Dortmund +6.49 (Pr=0.92, FATS=0.85); XGBoost benchmark importance: defenders in triangle 27.6%, shot distance 18.3%, shot angle 14.2%.
equation: \Delta xG_{B \leftarrow A} = xG_B(A) - xG_A(A), \quad \text{FATS} = \sum_c w_c \Pr(\Delta xG_c > 0)

claim: Cavus & Biecek (2022) 'Explainable expected goal models for performance analysis in football analytics' (arXiv:2206.07212v2): aggregated ceteris-paribus profiles g_AP^j(z) = (1/k) sum_{i=1}^k f(x_i^{j|z}), population form g_AP^j(z) = E_X^{-j}[f(X^{j|z})], a semi-global per-player/per-team what-if explainer sitting between local CP profiles and global PDP. Trained on 315,430 shots (33,656 goals, ~10.66%) from 12,655 matches over 7 seasons; the ORIGINAL-data random forest has better Brier (0.051) and log-loss (0.173) than the headline 'winning' ROSE-over-sampled model (Brier 0.071, log-loss 0.270), whose metrics are inflated by evaluating on over-sampled test data.
