Sakaori & Abe (2026) 'Gibbs Sampling for Bayesian Generalized Poisson Matrix Factorization' (arXiv:2609.12468v1): GP pmf p(y) = eta(eta+xi y)^{y-1} exp(-(eta+xi y))/y!, restricted to 0<xi<1 (overdispersion only); GPMF mean E[y_ij]=s_ij with variance s_ij(1+theta_i)^2 (theta-param) or s_ij/(1-xi_i)^2 (xi-param); hierarchical latent model n_ijk | w_ik,h_jk,xi_i ~ Poisson((1-xi_i)w_ik h_jk), y_ij | n_ij,xi_i ~ Borel-Tanner(n_ij, xi_i), W,H ~ Gamma, xi_i ~ EBeta; closed-form Gibbs updates with the novel trick of an infinite-mixture representation of EBeta as a mixture of Beta(alpha,beta+m) (gamma>=0) or Beta(alpha+m,beta) (gamma<0) with recursive weights truncated at M=200, cheaper than SIR. Verdict in brief: REJECT - no prediction mechanism, no sports forecasting result.

From the Bayesian GPMF paper's simulation results: Bayesian GPMF beats GPMF-MLE on MSE in all settings with gains growing in dispersion (xi=2/3: W-MSE 84.1 vs 251 random-init / 335 NNDSVD; S-MSE 2.66 vs 7.61); 95% credible-interval coverage S ~ 0.954-0.966, xi ~ 0.934-0.953 (near nominal); finite mixture M=200 matches SIR(L=1000) accuracy with less compute (4706s vs 6202s on M5 MacBook); EPL pressing application: xi largest for Watford/Swansea/Chelsea/Spurs (volatile pressing), smallest for Leicester (stable). Zero predictive accuracy numbers for any sports outcome - retrospective description only.

Pipping-Gamon & Wyner (2026) 'The Blown Lead Paradox: Conditional Laws for the Running Maximum of Binary Doob Martingales' (arXiv:2601.18774v4): models live win probability as a Doob martingale p_k = E[Y | F_k] with path maximum M_N = max p_k; for symmetric games (p_0 = 1/2), P(M_lambda >= 2/3) = 1/2 - half of all evenly matched games should see the eventual loser reach >=67% win probability, and half of three-player winners dipped to <=20% WP at some point.

From the Blown Lead Paradox paper: the two-player eventual-loser path-maximum CDF for p_0 >= 1/2 is F_{M_lambda}(x) = 0 on [0,1-p_0), 1 - (1-p_0)/x on [1-p_0, p_0), 2 - 1/x on [p_0,1), 1 at x=1; applied to the Eagles' 78.4% peak WP in Super Bowl LVII, F_{M_lambda}(0.784) = 2 - 1/0.784 ~= 0.7245, so P(M_lambda >= 0.784) ~= 0.2755 - mildly unusual but far from extraordinary under correct calibration, contradicting the 'collapse' narrative.

Dominitz & Manski (2025) 'Comprehensive OOS Evaluation of Predictive Algorithms with Statistical Decision Theory' (arXiv:2403.11016v3) argues ML's K-fold/CTF evaluation should be replaced by Wald's statistical decision theory: decision criteria are Bayes risk min_c integral L(c,s) d pi, minimax min_c max_s L(c,s), and minimax regret min_c max_s [L(c,s) - min_d L(d,s)]; binary-choice regret decomposes as R_{c(.)s} * |L(a,s) - L(b,s)| - error probability times loss magnitude; for MSE regret = V_s[p(psi)] + {E_s(y) - E_s[p(psi)]}^2.

From the Dominitz & Manski position paper: Manski & Tetenov (2016), N=145/arm - the empirical-success (ES) rule has max regret 0.01 vs one-sided z-test 0.05, with ES regret peaking at effect size ~+/-0.03 (error prob ~0.35); the cancer example shows the unconventional reversed test (alpha=0.20, beta=0.05) has 4x smaller max regret (1/5 yr) than the conventional test (4/5 yr); referenced critique that naive 90% CIs in Bates, Hastie & Tibshirani (2024)'s sparse-logit n=90/p=1000 example actually miscover 31% and need ~1.6x widening.

Xenopoulos, Coelho & Silva (2021) 'Optimal Team Economic Decisions in Counter-Strike' (arXiv:2109.12990v1, 6,538 CSGO demofiles Apr 2020-Apr 2021): OSE_T = sum_r (W_{T,r} - O_{T,r})^2 over rounds for team T - the per-team optimal-spending-error decision-quality metric valuing round-by-round equipment buy decisions by the WP delta of actual vs optimal buy; weighted log-loss: logistic 0.793, XGBoost 0.739, NN 0.736, OHE-map XGBoost 0.730 (winner); observed round win rates: Eco 3%, Low Buy 27%, Half Buy 34%, Hero Low Buy 25%, Hero Half Buy 48%, Full Buy 59%; OSE correlates with round win rate at r = -0.45 (confounded with competition tier).

From the CSGO buy-decision paper: CT eco rounds had predicted-optimal buy of low/half buy in >90% of cases with ~3% average lost WP per suboptimal eco; second round after losing the pistol: actual T buys 27% eco / 10% low / 63% half vs optimal 0% / 0% / 100%; the brief flags the fatal associational-causal flaw that counterfactual buy substitution into an associational WP model is not a causal estimate (buy choice correlates with team strength), so the OSE ranking may reflect who teams face rather than decision quality.

Manski (2019) 'Statistical inference for statistical decisions' (arXiv:1909.06853v1) is the superseded draft of the Wald SDT framework (superseded by arXiv:1912.08726v4): ES-rule max-regret bounds from Manski & Tetenov (2016) for K arms with outcome range M and n/arm are (2e)^(-1/2) M (K-1) n^(-1/2) (tighter for K=2,3) and M (ln K)^(1/2) n^(-1/2) (tighter for K>=4); the finite-sample curiosity (Prop. 2) is that under its assumptions there is no MMR advantage to large sample size - one observation per treatment is as good as the full sample when p is known.

Zemzoumi & Abouaomar (2026) 'Sim2Win' (arXiv:2607.26061v1, StatsBomb open data, 1,411 team-match rows, 178 teams, ~706 matches across 11 competitions): four engineered ratios PE = ball recoveries/(pressures+epsilon), SQ = xG/(shots+epsilon), D = passes/(possession events+epsilon), C = fouls + 3*yellows + 5*reds; shifted 5-match rolling profiles xbar(t,m) = (1/5) sum_{i=1}^5 x(t,m-i) with no leakage; volatility/momentum features sigma_xG (5-match std), M_xG = xGbar_last3 - xGbar_last5. In-distribution 80/20 holdout: CatBoost 60.90% acc / 0.9289 log loss / 0.7268 AUC (selected), XGBoost 56.39% / 0.9271 / 0.7406 (best AUC), LogReg 55.64% / 0.9207 (lowest log loss - best calibrated but linear), TabPFN 41.35% (worst).

Sim2Win ablation and validation results: rolling window 3 -> -4.11% acc, window 7 -> -3.93% (window 5 is the key choice); without xG volatility -1.66%, without contextual -1.21%, without engineered ratios only -0.15% (AUC rises 0.683->0.691); raw unshifted per-match features +7.10% acc is pure leakage, reported only as a diagnostic upper bound; LOCO (leave-one-competition-out) mean CatBoost acc 55.4% / AUC 0.704 vs ELO 0.567 / Pi-Rating 0.551 / GAP 0.548 - 21/21 AUC wins and 19/21 accuracy wins (authors' asymmetry caveat: ratings warmed up only on training competitions); Draw F1 = 0.238 on holdout - a structural trade-off no config exceeds 0.40.

Kang et al. (2026) 'DIAMOND: An LLM-Driven Agent for Context-Aware Baseball Highlight Summarization' (arXiv:2506.02351v1): WE(s) = W_s/N_s; WPA = WE_after - WE_before; LI = |delta WE|/Avg(|delta WE|); scoring maps WPA to 1-60 importance bands (>=0.15 abs WPA + late/crucial = 40-60; 0.05-0.15 = 20-39; <0.05 = 1-19) with LLM narrative adjustment +1 to +20 and Leverage Index correction delta R = R_WPA - R_LI giving top rank-difference plays up to +20 points decreasing 1/rank. On 5 KBO games: DIAMOND P 0.814 / R 0.886 / F1 0.848 vs WPA-only 0.635/0.716/0.673 vs NAVER AI 0.818/0.292/0.429; ablation: Preparation+Decision stages give +9.2pp F1 over WPA-only, Reflection adds +2.8pp.
equation: WPA = WE_{\text{after}} - WE_{\text{before}}, \quad LI = \frac{|\Delta WE|}{\text{Avg}(|\Delta WE|)}

claim: Chatterjee & Barber (2026) (arXiv:2609.13100) propose rankECE_n(f) = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^{n-1} (Y_{pi(i)} - Z_{pi(i)})(Y_{pi(i+1)} - Z_{pi(i+1)}) with Z sorted ascending - a tuning-free calibration-error estimator with data-adaptive bins of size 2; theory: rankECE(f) = 0 iff f is perfectly calibrated (n>=4), which binned ECE lacks; rankECE(f) <= l2-ECE(f); rankECE_n ->p l2-ECE as n->inf; under H0, sqrt(n) rankECE_n(f)/sqrt(E[Z^2(1-Z)^2]) ->d N(0,1) giving an asymptotic miscalibration test.

rankECE empirical results: the rankECE/l2-ECE ratio -> 1 rapidly with n and stays substantially closer to 1 than any binECE(K) at moderate n (K=10 collapses on oscillatory functions; K=n/20 shows persistent positive bias); sentiment experiments (4 HF models, Amazon+Yelp): rankECE consistently closest; tests control type-I error at 0.05 with asymptotic power comparable to SKCE-U; rankECE tests run in ~0.02-0.03 ms vs SKCE-U's 3-60 ms (M4 MacBook); plug-in decision rule excess risk vs best M-piecewise-monotone-transformed rule bounded by rankECE(f) + sqrt(8(M+1)/n).

Demartino, Egidi & Torelli (2024) (arXiv:2405.10247) test a Bayesian Bradley-Terry-Davidson posterior-median log-strength-difference covariate in goal-based Poisson models and ML result-forecasters for international football (2018-2023): Davidson draw model p_ij^W = exp(psi_i)/Z, p_ij^D = exp(gamma+(psi_i+psi_j)/2)/Z, p_ij^L = exp(psi_j)/Z; double Poisson log(lambda_1n) = theta + att_{h_n} + def_{a_n} + (phi/2) omega_n, log(lambda_2n) = theta + att_{a_n} + def_{h_n} - (phi/2) omega_n with omega_n = MAD-normalized rank-points difference, x_MAD = (x-M(x))/M(|x-M(x)|).

From the Bayesian BTD paper: FIFA vs BTD normalized-strength correlation is high (WC Pearson 0.90, Spearman 0.88, Kendall tau 0.69; AFCON 0.91/0.89/0.74); Brier score findings - 2022 World Cup knockout: BTD beats FIFA on all models (e.g. Diag.Infl. 0.510 vs 0.530, RF 0.461 vs 0.493) while FIFA marginally better in heterogeneous group stages; 2023 AFCON knockout: Diag.Infl. 0.677 (BTD) vs 0.681 (FIFA); the paper's interpretation is BTD wins when teams are similar in ability. Adversarial notes: no significance testing of tiny Brier gaps, knockout test sets only ~16 matches, possible pooled-window lookahead (BTD fit on 2018-2023 rather than strictly pre-match).

Jiao, Hu & Yan (2019) (arXiv:1908.05745): Bayesian marked spatial point process for NBA shot charts with shot-location intensity lambda(s_i) = lambda_0 exp(X^T(s_i) beta) as a non-homogeneous Poisson process on a 50x35 one-foot grid (X = 10 NMF basis shot types), and make/miss mark model m(s_i)|Z ~ Bernoulli(theta(s_i)) with logit theta(s_i) = xi lambda(s_i) + Z^T(s_i) alpha - the fitted location intensity enters as a covariate with coefficient xi; priors lambda_0 ~ G(0.01,0.01), beta,xi,alpha ~ N(0,100); inference via Metropolis-within-Gibbs, 60k iterations, 20k burn-in, thin 10.

From the Bayesian marked-spatial-point-process paper (2017-18 NBA shot charts, top-50 shooters): 40/50 (80%) of shooters favored the intensity-dependent mark model and all estimated xi > 0 ('accuracy higher where attempts are more frequent'), with intensity x shot-type interactions all insignificant; Curry was the famous counterexample - intensity-INDEPENDENT preferred (DIC 2379.2 vs 2391.3); Durant, Harden, James all favored xi != 0; Ward clustering of 51 players from fitted coefficients into 5 shot-pattern groups (e.g. Curry/Harden/James: fewer long/mid 2s, more 3s especially left-wing). The ledger's NFL port: test xi per QB with >=200 attempts on NGS target locations, fit per player, never pool (Curry counterexample).

Wattanachit et al. (2022) (arXiv:2202.11834, CDC FluSight 27 models, 3 test seasons): the beta-transformed linear pool (BLP) F_BLP(y) = B_{alpha,beta}(sum_m omega_m F_m(y)), f_BLP(y) = (sum omega_m f_m(y)) * b_{alpha,beta}(sum omega_m F_m(y)) with alpha,beta > 0 - a 2-parameter warp that fixes the linear pool's proven overdispersion (alpha=beta=1 recovers LP). Overall test mean log score: BMC2 -3.02 (best) > BLP -3.03 > LP -3.06 > EW-BMC2 -3.13 > EW-BLP -3.13 > EW-LP -3.26; equal weights strictly fail in train and test; BMC2 uses 2x BLP's parameters but only marginally beats it, so BLP is the practical recommendation.
equation: F_{BLP}(y) = B_{\alpha,\beta}\left(\sum_m \omega_m F_m(y)\right), \quad f_{BLP}(y) = \left(\sum_m \omega_m f_m(y)\right)\cdot b_{\alpha,\beta}\left(\sum_m \omega_m F_m(y)\right)

claim: From the FluSight ensemble paper: BLP/BMC2 most calibrated at 1-week-ahead (lowest Cramer distances) but calibration degrades with horizon; honest negative - beta methods corrected LP overdispersion but introduced systematic under-prediction in test (PIT CDF below diagonal across all values, worse at longer horizons and in the severe 2017/18 season); guardrail proposed: regularize (alpha,beta) toward (1,1) with penalized MLE log-score - lambda*[(alpha-1)^2 + (beta-1)^2], lambda via leave-one-season-out CV, since the under-prediction pathology is worse in heavy-tailed/extreme regimes.

Berthelot et al. (2025) (arXiv:2510.01810), anti-doping biological-passport work: interpretable intra-individual Z-score statistics T_n^(0) new-observation test = (X_n - Xbar_{n-1})/(sigmahat_{n-1} sqrt(1+1/(n-1))) ~ Student(n-2) under H0; T_n^(1) = max leave-one-out studentized deviation (single abnormal observation); T_n^(2) = max over all intervals I of |Xbar_I - Xbar_Ibar|/(sigmahat_{n,I} sqrt(1/|I|+1/(n-|I|))) (abnormal consecutive subsequence, change-point style); T_n^(3) multivariate Mahalanobis = (n-1)/(nd) * max_i Mahalanobis(X_i - Xbar_{n,-i}); T_n^(4) DevianLM extension = max external studentized residuals under a Gaussian linear model with designs A (intercept), B (+seasonality), C (+drift).

From the Z-score biological monitoring paper (3,936 French soccer players 2006-2019, 1,683 cyclists 2003-2014): T_n^(2) detects far above the 5% nominal rate - ferritin 26.67% cycling / 18.67% soccer, IGF1 35.97% cycling; among status-switchers ferritin T_n^(2) 89/158 (56.33%), IGF1 96/135 (71.11%); multivariate T_n^(3) over {erythrocytes, hemoglobin, hematocrit}: amateurs 53/604 (8.77%), professionals 27/160 (16.88%); malfunctioning-device hemoglobin sequences 4.45% soccer / 4.75% cycling (near nominal); KS normality p-values for chosen transforms all tiny (ferritin soccer 6.79e-16) except osteocalcin (0.841), so the 5% nominal rate itself may be miscalibrated.

Seong et al. (MIT CSAIL/GIST 2024) (arXiv:2405.11802): LatentCF - latent-space counterfactual optimization computing the minimal personalized joint-motion edit flipping a stroke-quality classifier to expert level: z <- AE-Encode(x); loop y_pred <- C(AE-Decode(z)), loss <- CE(y_pred, y'), z <- Adam(z, loss, alpha) until y_pred >= tau or max_iter. On MultiSenseBadminton (7,763 swings, 25 players): Transformer stroke classifier 5-fold forehand acc 85.12 (BalAcc 85.67, F1 85.22) vs LSTM 84.29/84.84/84.40; LatentCF vs 1NN validity 1.0 for all, proximity L1 3.41 vs 5.43-5.54, L2 0.58 vs 0.91-0.92, DTW 3.39 vs 5.36-5.42, Fréchet Pose Distance 0.33 vs 0.69-0.71 - LatentCF wins on every proximity/plausibility/motion metric.

Lakatos (2026) (arXiv:2609.07512), post-processing 50-member ECMWF forecasts at German stations: EMOS links mu = a + b^2 fbar, sigma = c^2 + d^2 S (minimum-CRPS estimation, Gaussian for temperature, truncated normal for wind); altitude-aware linear pool (ALP): separate combination weight per altitude group (<300 m, 300-700 m, >=700 m), F_ALP,t,s(y) = what_{t,g(s)} F_1,t,s(y) + (1-what_{t,g(s)}) F_2,t,s(y); core transferability rule - EMOS-L best at observed stations (CRPSS 14.7 vs DRN) but worst at unobserved (negative skill, largest generalization gap), while semi-local/regional EMOS-R wins at unobserved; Transformer the only ML model positive at unobserved on the non-extended set; GNN-Geo degrades badly at unobserved (oversmoothing; Feldberg 1,490 m failure - geographical graph ignores elevation).

Wang et al. (WSDM '22) (arXiv:2111.12535): KES - knowledge-corpus-enhanced sports commentary summarizer retrieving from a structured corpus (14,724 player passages, 523 team articles) via NER + entity linking (NLev(entity,title) = Lev/max-len, linking thresholds lambda_p=0.2, lambda_o=0.25) and fusing knowledge embeddings into an mT5 rewriter: input embedding z_k = LN(z_token + z_pos + z_seg + z_know) with learnable segment embeddings {[Player],[Team],[Time],[Other]} and z_know = averaged RoBERTa-[CLS] sentence embeddings of linked passages. On K-SportsSum (7,854 Chinese commentary-news pairs): KES ROUGE-1 48.79 / ROUGE-2 21.04 / ROUGE-L 47.17 vs SportsSUM 44.89/19.04/44.16 (+3.7 avg); ablations: remove segment embeddings -0.53, remove knowledge embeddings -0.72, both -1.71, PGN rewriter -2.92. Caveat: implicit fusion hallucinates - KES injected 'De Yang is 1.7 meters' when his actual height is 1.8 m, so the ledger requires a per-fact entailment filter.

Nechepurenko (2026) (arXiv:2604.27041): the Signal Credibility Index (SCI) classifies prediction-market price jumps into informed updating vs liquidity pressure vs disagreement vs concentrated manipulation: logit ell_t = log[p_t/(1-p_t)]; persistence PR(t,w) = |ell_t - ell_{t-w}| / sum_{tau=t-w+1}^{t} |ell_tau - ell_{tau-1}| in [0,1] (=1 iff monotone); two-sidedness TS_s = 1 - |B_s - S_s|/(B_s + S_s) (0 = one-sided consensus, 1 = balanced disagreement); flow concentration HHI_s^flow = sum_j (|Delta v_{j,s}| / sum_j' |Delta v_{j',s}|)^2; SCI_s = PR_s (1-TS_s) (1-HHI_s^flow) in [0,1].

From the SCI paper (Monte Carlo, 48 five-min bins per 4-hour path, eight DGPs): Exp 1 AUC = 0.984 (95% CI [0.981,0.986]) with Youden-optimal tau* = 0.27 (TPR 0.92, FPR 0.05); component means informed: PR 0.50, TS 0.11, HHI 0.04, SCI 0.451; liquidity: 0.22/0.17/0.10/0.163; disagreement: 0.14/0.97/0.02/0.005. Headline failure mode (whale_informed, label 1): mean SCI 0.231, P(SCI>tau*) = 0.376 -> Type II error; coord_manip_broad (label 0): mean SCI 0.399, P(SCI>tau*) = 0.827 -> Type I error. Exp 3 (8-DGP): logistic regression AUC 0.908 > SCI 0.847, with LR coefficients beta_PR = +6.29, beta_{1-TS} = +3.99, beta_{1-HHI} = -4.84 - concentration positively associated with informed updating, opposite the SCI's weighting.

arXiv:2503.17927 (2025) derives fractional Kelly from the CLT asymptotic variance of the log-growth rate as a sizing method: asymptotic Sharpe SR_r(f) = g_r(f)/sqrt(upsilon_r(f)) where g_r(f) is per-bet log-growth and upsilon_r(f) its asymptotic variance; ridge objective Ri_r(f,gamma) = g_r(f) - gamma*upsilon_r(f) - every gamma>0 yields a below-full-Kelly optimizer, and varying gamma traces a growth-vs-volatility efficient frontier with the 'fraction' indexed by a risk-aversion parameter, replacing the ad-hoc half-Kelly rule. Worked Bernoulli example (p=.75 even money): full Kelly f*=.5 -> growth ~.13, SR ~.27; fractional f=.25 -> growth ~.10, SR ~.43 (~20% growth sacrifice for ~60% Sharpe improvement).

Nakakita, Toyabe, Nakatsuma & Hoshino (2026) (arXiv:2507.18404): first rigorous convergence theory for the ancillarity-sufficiency interweaving strategy (ASIS) in Bayesian hierarchical panel models y_it = alpha_i + epsilon_it, alpha_i ~ N(mu_alpha, sigma_alpha^2), epsilon_it ~ N(0, sigma_epsilon^2). Theorem 1: the SA (centered) and AA (non-centered) geometric rates sum to 1 - if one mixes well the other necessarily mixes poorly. Corollary 1 (decision rule): SA converges faster if sigma_epsilon^2 < sigma_alpha^2 T; AA converges faster if sigma_epsilon^2 > sigma_alpha^2 T, with T = observations per group.
equation: \text{SA faster if } \sigma_\varepsilon^2 < \sigma_\alpha^2 T, \quad \text{AA faster if } \sigma_\varepsilon^2 > \sigma_\alpha^2 T

claim: From the ASIS MCMC paper: Theorem 2 - under ASIS interweaving (SA->AA and AA->SA sweeps each iteration), the global mean mu_alpha chain is approximately IID when tau_alpha^2 N is large (diffuse prior limit); MCSE of mu_alpha (x1e-5, smaller better, ASIS best in every setting) - e.g. Table 5 on real US cigarette panel data (48 states x 11 years): SA 8.673, AA 8.232, ASIS 3.072 (x1e-3) - ASIS ~2.7x lower MCSE than either single scheme; cost note: ASIS roughly doubles per-iteration work so wall-clock wins are smaller than MCSE ratios.

Benjamin Lucas (2024) (arXiv:2403.03862v1): plain single-parameter Elo audit of CFP selection-committee decisions across every 4-team CFP season (2014-2023): p_A = 1/(1+10^((R_B - R_A)/400)), update R_A* = R_A + 25*(O_A - p_A) with K fixed at 25, all teams init 1500, no margin-of-victory, no home-field term, no preseason prior, no recency decay. 2023 selection-day ranks: committee picked Elo 1st (Michigan 2174), 5th (Texas 2050), 6th (Alabama 2039), 13th (Washington 1883) while Florida State was 11th (1951) - the paper calls 2023 the largest Elo-vs-committee disagreement; the committee never selected the Elo top four in any season.

Sawczuk et al. (2022) (arXiv:2212.10904v1): smooth Expected Possession Value (EPV) surface for rugby league via Bayesian Mixture Model: 33 centres (30 field of play, 3 in try area), each a 5-Dirichlet probability vector over possession outcomes (converted try, unconverted try, penalty goal, drop goal, no score); P(s;x,y) = sum_k z_k(x,y) P_k(s) with z_k by bilinear interpolation among 4 surrounding centres; EPV(x,y) = sum_s P(s;x,y)*Points(s) with Points = {6,4,2,1,0}. On 138 matches of the 2021 Super League (99,966 attacking actions): highest field-of-play EPV^mu = 1.73 at centre (50,100); top AE player ratings (points per match above expected): Player 276 (Full Back) 8.21, player 19 (Winger) 6.67.

Mao, Mohri, Zhong (2023) (arXiv:2310.14772) on predictor-rejector multi-class abstention: calibration-gap lemma C*_Labs(H,R,x) = 1 - max{max_{y in H(x)} p(x,y), 1-c}; conditional risk C_L(h,r,x) = sum_y p(x,y) L(h,r,x,y). Table 1 abstention loss: SVHN - Mozannar 1.61%+/-0.06%, Cao 2.16%+/-0.04%, single-stage P-R 2.22%+/-0.01%, two-stage P-R 0.94%+/-0.02%; CIFAR-10: 4.48%/3.62%/3.64%/3.31%; CIFAR-100: 10.40%/14.99%/14.99%/9.23%. Two-stage P-R wins on all three and beats two-stage score-based on CIFAR-100 (9.23% vs 9.54%); on CIFAR-10 it achieves the lowest accepted-set error (2.69%+/-0.05%) at a LOWER rejection ratio (22.83%+/-0.21%) than Cao (28.27%+/-0.18%) - better selection, not just more abstention.

arXiv:1912.05642v4 on locally scale-invariant proper scoring rules: scaled CRPS S1^sta(P,y) = - E|X-y| / E|X-Y| - 0.5 log(E|X-Y|) is a special case of the standardized kernel score with h(x) = -0.5 log(x) and g(x,y)=|x-y|; generalized proper kernel scores S_g^h(P,y) = h(E[g(X,X')]) - E[g(X,y)], proper for any increasing concave h and negative-definite kernel g. Local scale invariance: a proper rule S on location-scale family Q_theta (theta=(mu,sigma)) is locally scale invariant iff its scale function satisfies s(Q_theta) sigma^2 = s(Q); Proposition 1 - log score and Dawid-Sebastiani score are locally scale invariant, CRPS and Hyvarinen are not; every standardized kernel score with h(x) = -0.5 log(x) is locally scale invariant; simultaneously robust + locally scale invariant is conjectured impossible.

From the scale-invariant scoring-rules paper: SCRPS and the log score select the true scale parameter far more often than CRPS and Hyvarinen in 500 stochastic-volatility simulations (CRPS/Hyvarinen pulled toward high-volatility observations); on 227 pedestrian-count street segments, removing the ~20 highest-mean observations halves the average CRPS while SCRPS is much less sensitive - average CRPS weights by predictive scale; GSE's target uncertainty scales differ radically (QB passing yards sigma~60, receptions sigma~2.5, game totals sigma~14), so under average-CRPS ranking high-variance targets dominate engine selection. Explains why the log score identified the true system more efficiently than Brier/RPS - its efficiency comes exactly from local scale invariance.

Koch (2018) (arXiv:1803.07041v6), pure actuarial theory on spatial risk measures: normalized spatially aggregated loss L_N(A,P) = nu(A)^(-1) integral_A C_P(x) nu(dx), spatial risk measure R_Pi(A,P) = Pi(L_N(A,P)); proved diversification orders: expectation 0, variance -2, VaR -1, expected shortfall -1 (under CLT + mixing assumptions on max-stable/Brown-Resnick/Smith fields); asymptotic spatial homogeneity of order -gamma: R_Pi(lambda A,C) = K1(A,C) + K2(A,C)/lambda^gamma + o(1/lambda^gamma) as lambda->inf. Brief verdict: REJECT - no data, no experiments, no code, no operational path to value; replaced by ledger 1303 for the weather/spatial-extremes lane.

Kumar et al. (2019) (arXiv:1908.08147v1), descriptive study of sentiment in ~0.15M Facebook posts and 1.13B reactions across five news channels (CNN 33,324 posts; NPR 18,266; Fox 26,525; Economist 24,272; NYT 47,522): post/comment sentiment correlations CNN 0.97, Fox 0.98, Economist 0.95, NYT 0.97, NPR 0.93 (claimed p<.05); Fox negative posts 40%, NPR positive 43% / negative 28%. Brief verdict: REJECT - purely descriptive, no predictive task, no held-out evaluation; critique: correlations ~0.95+ are likely artifacts of the normalized engagement metric and common audience, and p<.05 on N~1e5 correlations is meaningless. Replacement: ledger 1308 (few-shot LLM topic+stance pipeline for live sports-event social data).

Trotter (2024) (arXiv:2412.10298v1) predicting sports broadcast viewership from 72h pre-event Reddit engagement (PullPush API, capped at 100 results/query): features = total posts/comments/scores in 72h + mean TextBlob + mean VADER sentiment + sport one-hot; target log1p(viewership); Gradient Boosting Regressor reported test MAE 1.27M, RMSE 2.33M, R^2 = 0.99. The ledger's central flaw: R^2=0.99 is an artifact of a random split on time-ordered data (same season/sport in train and test) plus sport one-hot + Super Bowl outliers (~100M+ viewers) making it mechanical - the model learns 'Super Bowl = big', not buzz->viewership; rebuild prescription: temporal split (train <=2023, test 2024), held-sport-out validation, hierarchical sport/team random effects instead of raw one-hot.

arXiv:2409.00629 'Upselling in Online Fantasy Sports' (Dream11): an 8-week randomized live experiment (2024-01-01 to 2024-02-28) with four upsell intensity arms (1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, 2x deposit-offer discount multipliers); supervised comparison weighted-F1: heuristic 0.736, LightGBM regressor 0.758, LightGBM classifier 0.804, focal-loss classifier 0.852; S/T/X/R CATE learners with XGBRegressor, fixed propensity 0.5, 1,000 Hyperopt trials. Results: upselling raised per-transaction value +5.6%, but the most aggressive 2x arm showed a 4.8% transaction decline and conversion fell ~2.1% overall; offline-derived CATE policy estimated 10.7% revenue uplift (no online A/B validation reported); new-user 1x arm reported 2.1% conversion improvement.

arXiv:2307.02188 'G-score Fantasy Basketball': replaces the Z-score draft ranking with a G-score adding each player's own period-to-period variance to the valuation denominator - counting stats: G = (muM(q) - muM) / sqrt(sigmaM^2 + kappa*tauM^2); turnovers: G = (muM - muM(q)) / sqrt(sigmaM^2 + kappa*tauM^2); percentage stats: G = (muA/muA(p))*(muR(q) - muR) / sqrt(sigmaR^2 + kappa*tauR^2). kappa estimated ~= 1.04 on 2022-23 NBA weekly data (player's own variance counts ~as much as cross-player variance). In 1,000 simulated seasons per draft seat (12-team, 13-player, 20-week H2H): G-score drafter vs Z field won 32.5% Most Categories / 21.4% Each Category (baseline 1/12 = 8.33%); Z vs G field won 0.4%/0.5%. Contest-type insight: variance should be penalized in cash-style valuations but rewarded in GPPs (sign flip on the tau term).

(2020) (arXiv:2005.04020v2): three-agent minimalist physics simulator of soccer ball-possession intervals mapped onto a Wiener process with drift and absorbing barrier - Fokker-Planck (sigma^2/2) d^2p/dx^2 - mu dp/dx = dp/dt with absorbing p(d_0,x_b;t)=0; first-passage-time density g(tau) = (x_b/sqrt(sigma^2 2 pi tau^3)) exp(-(x_b - mu tau)^2/(2 sigma^2 tau)). Kelly-formula typo verified in the 1197 ledger against the arXiv LaTeX source: the paper prints f_i = max((o_i + p~_i - 1)/(o_i - 1), 0) but correct Kelly for decimal odds is f_i = max((o_i * p~_i - 1)/(o_i - 1), 0) - the '+' in the numerator must be a multiplication; implemented verbatim the printed formula bets on negative-edge outcomes (e.g. o=2, p~=0.4 gives f=1.4 instead of 0) and overbets positive edges (o=2, p~=0.6 gives f=1.6 instead of 0.2).

Billings & Del Barco (2017) (arXiv:1707.00529v1): simulation study of the Labouchere negative-progression cancellation staking system on fair coin flips - bet = first+last of sequence (or sole element), win removes both ends, loss appends bet size, terminates on empty sequence or insufficient capital; completion-time exponential fit f(x) = 10^6 * e^(-0.131x) (R^2=0.86884, 10M-round sim). Findings: win rate rises with bankroll (371/1000 wins at $4 bankroll -> 1000/1000 at ~$40k); $4,000 bankroll grows near-linearly for ~6,000 bets then loses everything to one streak; only infinite capital profits, finite capital is eventually ruined. Methodological defects flagged: g(x) = 0.1*e^(-0.131x) presented as a 'probability' but integrates to 0.763 (not a density); termination probability rho(x) self-contradictory; Wald homogeneity test invalidly applied to two R^2 values. Verdict in brief: REJECT - confirms no staking system beats fair odds.

Limitations: SDS hyperparameters tuned on the test season, one season only, Betegy probabilities an unexamined black box, no significance testing. The brief adapts it strictly as negative-control research evidence for a singles-first stance, never to promote parlays.

Voracek & Orabona (NeurIPS 2025) (arXiv:2505.22422v2): STaR-Bets - sequential target-recalculating betting-based confidence intervals for the mean of a bounded [0,1] variable achieving statistically optimal width up to a 1+o(1) factor. Testing-by-betting: wealth W_i^m = W_{i-1}^m (1 + ell_i (X_i - m)) with ell_i in [-1/(1-m), 1/m]; reject H0(m): E[X]=m if W_n^m >= 1/delta (Markov); non-rejected m's form a (1-delta)-CI. Kelly-style oracle constant bet ell* = S/V with S = sum(X_i-m), V = sum(X_i-m)^2; target |ell*| = sqrt(2 log(1/delta)/V). Theorem 8: for all X in [0,1] with variance sigma^2 > 0, alpha,delta in (0,1), c > 0, there exists n_0 in O(c^-4) such that for n >= n_0, Alg. 3 rejects every m <= xbar_n - sigma sqrt((2+c) log(1/delta)/n) with probability >= 1-alpha; Corollary 9 gives CI width optimal up to 1+o(1) - the first such finite-time guarantee for a betting CI.

From the STaR-Bets paper: STaR-Bets (Alg. 4) ell = sqrt(2(log(1/delta) - lgW)/((n-t+1)vhat)) ^ 1 uses wealth-still-needed log(1/delta) - log W_t and rounds-left n-t, stopping once the target is hit and betting aggressively near the deadline if behind; Prop. 4/Cor. 5: STaR-Hoeffding rejects whenever vanilla Hoeffding does, so CIs are never wider, sometimes strictly narrower. Simulations (n in {8,...,256}, 1,000 reps, delta=0.05): on Beta(5,1) STaR-Bets approaches the undercovering T-test as n grows; on Bernoulli(0.3) it ~matches optimal randomized Clopper-Pearson, beats standard CP at small n, far beats Hedged-CI at large n; beaten competitors: Hoeffding, empirical Bernstein, Hedged-CI, standard CP, PMBSS.

Oesting & Naveau (2020) (arXiv:2003.05854v1): max-stable processes with unit Frechet margins and data-driven spectral functions built from ensemble forecast fields for coherent spatial extreme-precipitation simulation. Five models: A - max-linear on all N forecast maps; B - max-linear on max-spectral functions above the empirical 90%-quantile threshold (N(u)=1819 maps); C - Reich-Shaby (2012) construction with nugget alpha in (0,1); D - max-linear mixture Y(s) = max{a*Y_noise(s), (1-a)*Y_B(s)}; E - classical Brown-Resnick with anisotropic power variogram plus nugget (5 parameters: sigma^2, b1, b2, theta, beta). Fit = minimize RMSE of model-implied pairwise extremal coefficients vs empirical F-madogram estimates. Results on 110 Meteo-France stations (fall 1980-2017, 190 block maxima): Model A fails (dry days should not build basis functions); B overstates dependence for strongly dependent pairs (missing nugget); C and D capture observed pairwise coefficients well; triplewise out-of-fit RMSE: C=0.154, D=0.137, E=0.167; the 5-parameter E cannot capture non-stationarity by construction.

On 40,747 games / 1,306,515 scoring events (NBA, CFB, NFL, NHL): arcsine laws hold well in NBA and NHL, football fits weaker (discrete 3/7-point scoring); NBA: 10-point lead ~90% safe with 7.87 min remaining, 18 points at halftime likewise ~90% safe; NBA diffusion D ~= 0.0391 points^2/sec, Peclet ~= 0.77, persistence p = 0.360 (scoring runs have memory), 9.37 lead changes/game; NFL context: ~7.75 scoring events/game vs NBA's ~93.6 - the diffusion approximation is weakest where football needs it.

Eliades & Papadopoulos (2024) (arXiv:2406.15760v1), 'ICM Ensemble with Novel Betting Functions for Concept Drift': Inductive Conformal Martingale S_n = prod_{i=1}^n f_i(p_i), updated online as S_n = S_{n-1} * f_n(p_n), with nonconformity alpha_j = -p~_j (negative posterior of true label) and smoothed p-value p_j = (|{alpha_i>alpha_j}| + U_j*|{alpha_i=alpha_j}|)/(j-k), U_j ~ U(0,1); betting functions satisfy integral_0^1 f_i(p) dp = 1, f_i >= 0, so E[S_{n+1}|history] = S_n under exchangeability. Ville's inequality: P(exists n: S_n >= C) <= 1/C; alarm at S_n > 100 -> reject exchangeability at 1% significance. CAUTIOUS betting function: h_n = 1 if S^{n-1}/min_k S^{n-k} <= epsilon else f_n, epsilon = 100, window W = 5000. Theorem: under uniform p-values, any betting function f != 1 gives S_inf = 0 a.s. Results (10-ICM ensemble, 10% noise): STAGGER 0.949, SEA 0.920, ELEC 0.768, AIRLINES 0.651; kNN-alone generally lowers performance and often fails to detect many changes.

Pozdnyakov (2025) (arXiv:2501.10302), 'Martingale Approach to Gambler's Ruin Problem for Correlated Random Walks': ruin probability for symmetric 2-state correlated random walk alpha = [B - 1 + (1/2)*1/(1-p)] / [A + B - 2 + 1/(1-p)], where p = persistence P(win|win), A = profit target, B = bankroll (unit stakes); arbitrary initial law alpha = [B - 1 + pi_1/(1-p)] / [A + B + (2p-1)/(1-p)]; sanity checks: A=B -> alpha=1/2; p=1/2 -> alpha=B/(A+B) (classical); p->1 -> alpha->1/2 (first flip decides); B->inf -> alpha->1. With persistence p > 1/2, the 1/(1-p) terms inflate ruin probability vs the i.i.d. classical value; the ledger notes GSE's existing ruin/drawdown math (ledgers 1749-1752) all assumes independent increments - a gap this closes exactly. Limitation: unit stakes only, increments +/-1, 'likely unsuitable for Markov chains with more than three states'.

Besalu (2021) (arXiv:2102.07738v1), 'The Dependent Chip Model (DCM)' - verdict in brief: REJECT, disqualified per the full-text rule because ar5iv returned only the abstract page (abstract-only reads are excluded); from the abstract: DCM recursively explores a multiplayer Texas Hold'em game tree assuming all players have equal skill but different survival prospects from their stacks, and awards MORE to top podium positions and LESS to lower ones than ICM (DCM_podium_top > ICM_podium_top, DCM_podium_bottom < ICM_podium_bottom); poker deal-making (chopping prize pools) has no DFS application; superseded in-lane by ledger 1761 (SCO).

Madras, Pitassi & Zemel (2018) (arXiv:1711.06664), 'Predict Responsibly': adaptive learning-to-defer - jointly train a predictor and a deferral policy pi(x) routing each input to the model or the downstream decision maker, minimizing joint system loss over (predictor, deferral policy, fixed DM), learning the human's competence map (where the human is biased defer less; where the human is strong defer more), fairness measured on system decisions with Pareto fronts of system accuracy vs fairness (each point the median of five runs). On semi-synthetic COMPAS and Heritage Health with simulated DMs: adaptive deferral dominates fixed-deferral and no-deferral baselines on the accuracy-fairness frontier; in the inconsistent-DM regime the human flips 30% of the selected subgroup's predictions, yet the joint system still improves over the model alone; in the highly-biased regime the system learns to defer less to the biased human on the affected subgroup - fairness gain comes from routing, not changing the human. Limitations: simulated (not real) humans; non-stationary human not handled (paper assumes a fixed decision maker); no exact effect sizes.

Geenens & Cuddihy (2017) (arXiv:1701.07555v2), 'Robust Analysis of Second-Leg Home Advantage in UEFA Football': Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression p_hat_h(x) = sum K((x-X_i)/h) Y_i / sum K((x-X_i)/h) (Gaussian kernel, h_0 = 0.525 by AIC) with predictor X = log(C_2/C_1) (log-ratio of team strength indices) and three pointwise 95% CIs for p(0) on local equivalent sample size n*h*f_hat_h(x)/R(K): Wald-type, conditional Wilson, conditional Agresti-Coull; bandwidth chosen by a novel bootstrap selector (B = 5,000 resamples) maximizing estimated coverage. Simulation coverage at nominal 95% (n=1000): Wald 0.860, Wilson 0.958, Agresti-Coull 0.961 (n=250: Wald 0.796, Wilson 0.940, AC 0.939); coverage-optimal bandwidth (~0.86) exceeds estimation-optimal h_0 (0.525).

On 48 PMLB regression datasets x 5 draws of 250 training rows = 240 experiments: QLattice-BIC won the most first places (77/240 all-configs; 132/240 best-config-per-family, over half), best non-SR = Lasso alpha=0.1, worst = decision tree; interpretable-only: QLattice-BIC best in 184/240, Lasso 49; weighted scoring: QLattice-BIC 644 (unchanged rank order), per-family weighted GB 821, RF 787, Lasso 511. Caveats: vendor-authored (Abzu employees), 'typical hyperparameters' may handicap ensembles, overlapping test sets -> correlated experiments, no significance testing, no time series or regime-structure datasets.

Hollmann, Muller & Hutter (2023) (arXiv:2305.03403v5, NeurIPS 2023), CAAFE: an LLM acts as a code generator that iteratively proposes semantically meaningful pandas features from dataset context - prompt (dataset description, feature names, dtypes, missing-value %, 10 sample rows, CoT instructions, worked example) -> LLM generates pandas code adding exactly one column (with '# Feature name', '# Usefulness:', '# Input samples:' comments) -> execute -> fit classifier, evaluate on D'_valid (10 random validation splits; keep iff mean(Delta accuracy, Delta ROC AUC) > 0) -> repeat 10 iterations; execution safety via syntax parse + pandas-operation whitelist + error feedback loop. On 14 tabular classification datasets (<=2,000 samples; 10 OpenML + 4 post-Sept-2021 Kaggle): TabPFN mean ROC AUC: no FE 0.798 -> CAAFE(GPT-3.5) 0.806 -> CAAFE(GPT-4) 0.822; mean rank 13.9 -> 12.9 -> 9.78; improvement on 11/14 datasets; the +0.024 jump is 71% of the improvement from switching logistic regression (0.749) to random forest (0.783); baselines (TabPFN mean AUC): DFS 0.791, AutoFeat 0.796, FETCH 0.796, OpenFE 0.798; GPT-3.5 improves only 6/14 - model quality is load-bearing; tic-tac-toe: 0.888 -> 0.987 -> 1.000 in two iterations; semantic-blinding ablation: hiding feature names + description drops GPT-4 CAAFE 0.822 -> 0.800; cost: avg 4:43 min/dataset (90% LLM code generation), 7.4% faulty-code rate all recovered via error feedback. Risks: LLM proposes from names - 'spread_close'-style semantic leakage possible; GPT-4 invented gendered features on a fake doctor/nurse dataset (bias demo).

Li et al. (2024) (arXiv:2406.12913), T-JEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for trajectory similarity - predicts masked trajectory segments in representation space, not data space, plus AdjFuse, a learnable 3x3 neighborhood-fusion module stabilizing embeddings under low/irregular GPS sampling. AdjFuse: softmax over node neighborhood N(i) union {i}: w'_j = exp(w_j)/sum_{k in N(i) union {i}} exp(w_k); h-tilde = sigma(sum w'_j*h_j + b); residual h'_i = h_i + W-tilde*h-tilde. JEPA: target encoder E_{theta-bar} (EMA of context encoder); M=4 targets resampled with replacement, masking ratios {10%,20%,30%}, successive sampling prob p=50%; context mask p_gamma in [85%,100%]; predictor = 2-layer Transformer decoder (8 heads); loss = SmoothL1(predicted, target) summed over positions; encoders = 3-layer Transformer (4 heads), learnable positional encoding, d=256. On Porto (1.7M trajectories), T-Drive (10,357 taxis), GeoLife (182 users), FourSquare-TKY (573,703 check-ins)/NYC (227,428): T-JEPA beats TrajCL on self-similarity mean rank in 4 of 5 datasets (T-Drive +0.114, GeoLife +0.158 mean-rank units; TrajCL better on Porto by 0.044); sparse check-ins: TKY 6.88x better than t2vec, 2.92x better than TrajCL; distortion: 1.62x/10.92x/3.04x/2.53x better on T-Drive/GeoLife/TKY/NYC, Porto 0.073 worse; removing AdjFuse -> downsample mean rank 6.7, 74% worse. Caveats: no code link; NYC/TKY gains on tiny DBs (147/500); single-agent trajectories only.
equation: w'_j = \frac{\exp(w_j)}{\sum_{k\in N(i)\cup\{i\}}\exp(w_k)}, \quad \tilde{h} = \sigma\left(\sum_j w'_j\cdot h_j + b\right), \quad h'_i = h_i + \tilde{W}\cdot\tilde{h}

claim: Jiao et al. (2023) (arXiv:2303.05000): two learned-representation approaches to vehicle-trajectory anomaly detection - supervised contrastive encoder (F: 1-D conv + map graph -> 128-D -> CL encoder -> 32-D latent; NCE (M+1)-way softmax L_ij = -log[exp(s_ni^T s_nj/tau)/(exp(s_ni^T s_nj/tau) + sum_m exp(s_ni^T s_am/tau))]; L = 1/(N(N-1)) sum_{i,j!=i} L_ij; SVM on 32-D latent for online detection) and unsupervised semantic-latent-space autoencoder (latent partitioned into intention (3 classes), aggressiveness, residual; discriminators regularize each partition; semantic loss Loss_sem(z,g) = -sum_{i=1}^3 g_intent log z_intent + (g_agg - z_agg)^2; decoder with smooth-L1/Huber; anomaly score = reconstruction error vs threshold). On Argoverse 1 (30K+ scenarios) and Argoverse 2 (anomalies synthesized via white-box PGD attacks - not real-world): supervised CL 'significantly' improves over baselines on both datasets (exact AUC numbers figure-rendered, not text-recoverable); unsupervised semantic-AAE beats OC-SVM and TS2Vec. Limitations: synthesized anomalies stay within the attack family; intention/aggressiveness are driving-specific; no online latency measured despite 'online detection' framing; no code link.
equation: L_{ij} = -\log\left[\frac{\exp(s_{ni}^T s_{nj}/\tau)}{\exp(s_{ni}^T s_{nj}/\tau) + \sum_m \exp(s_{ni}^T s_{am}/\tau)}\right], \quad L = \frac{1}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i,\,j\neq i} L_{ij}

claim: Tang et al. (2025) (arXiv:2502.16789v2), AlphaAgent: LLM-agent framework mining financial 'alphas' with three decay countermeasures - originality enforcement: factor f_i parsed into AST T(f_i), similarity s(f_i,f_j) = max_{t_i subset T(f_i), t_j subset T(f_j)} {|t_i| : t_i ~= t_j} (eq. 5), penalize similarity to the existing alpha zoo; hypothesis-factor alignment: each factor must be semantically consistent with an explicit market hypothesis h (LLM-scored); complexity control: Rg(f,h) = alpha_1*SL(f) + alpha_2*PC(f) + alpha_3*ER(f,h) (eq. 4) - symbolic length, free-parameter count (window lengths), novelty/alignment term; symbolic assembly from primitives (dev success 0.83 vs 0.75 without; token efficiency 1.00 vs 0.81); LightGBM (max depth 4) on base alphas (intraday/daily return, 20-day relative volume, normalized daily range) + mined alphas forecasting next-day returns; backtest top-50 by predicted return, drop lowest 5. On CSI 500 and S&P 500 (train 2015-2019, val 2020, test 2021-01-2024-12): best in ALL 10 reported columns - CSI 500: IC 0.0212 (next TRA 0.0198), ICIR 0.1938, AR 11.00% (next LSTM 4.96%), IR 1.488 (next 0.6225), MDD -9.36% (best); S&P 500: IC 0.0056, ICIR 0.0552, AR 8.74% (next 2.75%), IR 1.0545, MDD -9.10% - using only GPT-3.5-turbo while RD-Agent used GPT-4, so the regularization, not the LLM, drives the edge. Ablation: factor-modeling constraints raise hit ratio 0.29 vs 0.16 (+81%). Limitations: only 5 evolutionary rounds per trial; OHLCV-only; slippage/market impact absent; turnover undisclosed; LLM alignment scoring uncalibrated.

Si et al. (2025) (arXiv:2504.04798), TabRep: tabular diffusion whose CatConverter encodes any categorical as a point on the unit circle - CatConverter(c,K) = [cos(2*pi*c/K), sin(2*pi*c/K)] (Eq. 12), 2 dims, parameter-free, decoding = nearest of K circle points (out-of-index impossible; OOI casting to index 0 at 5-20% rates). Singular-point geometric theory: one-hot's minimal n-singular points scale sum_{n=2}^{K}(K choose n) = 2^K - (K+1), with conditional score variance Var(g|x) = (alpha_t^2/sigma_t^4)*(n-1)/n (Eq. 10) - strictly positive and increasing in n; CatConverter collapses this to ONE minimal K-singular point (circle center), K 2-singular points, NO n-singular hyperplanes for 2<n<K. Unified continuous diffusion on concat[quantile-transformed numerics, CatConverter categoricals]: DDPM loss E||grad log q - grad log p_theta||^2 (Eq. 13); Flow Matching E||v_theta(z_t) - (eps - z_0^CC)||^2 (Eq. 14), Euler ODE sampling. On 7 UCI tabular datasets (MLE via XGBoost AUC/RMSE): TabRep best on all 7, first method to beat Real-trained downstream quality on 3 datasets (Default 0.782 vs Real 0.770; Stroke 0.869 vs 0.852; News RMSE 0.814 vs 0.842); representation bake-off: OneHot-DDPM collapses on Adult (0.476 AUC), TabRep best; ordering is load-bearing (lexicographic vs random: Adult AUC 0.913 vs 0.776); TabRep-Flow is cheapest (Adult total 2031s vs CoDi 24049s) and best at 8 NFEs. High-cardinality toy (1,000-category feature): TabRep-Flow RMSE 0.4812 ~= TabSYN 0.4775 vs TabDDPM 0.8253 - use Flow, not DDPM, for high-cardinality fields. Caveats: beating Real is partly a denoising/regularization artifact; CatConverter imposes an arbitrary circular order on nominal features; OOI casting injects systematic bias toward index 0.

SakanaAI (2025) (arXiv:2504.08066), AI Scientist v2: end-to-end agentic system producing fully AI-generated manuscripts via progressive agentic tree search - each node = a code checkpoint with an evaluation score; a dedicated Experiment Manager agent selects the best-performing node after each of 4 experimentation stages using a dedicated LLM evaluator with explicitly articulated criteria, then branches/refines from it (replacing linear refinement); replication discipline: after each stage the manager launches multiple replications of selected best experiments to report statistics (mean +/- std); hypothesis-first proposals: structured proposal (hypothesis, predicted direction, falsification condition, exact backtest spec) BEFORE code runs, proposals without a falsification condition rejected without running. Results: one of three manuscripts submitted to the ICLR 2025 workshop 'I Can't Believe It's Not Better' achieved average reviewer score 6.33/10 (6,6,7), roughly top 45% of submissions, exceeding the average human acceptance threshold - the paper's claim of 'the first instance of a fully AI-generated paper successfully navigating a peer review' (that paper found no significant improvement, occasionally harmful, from explicit compositional regularization on synthetic arithmetic-expression datasets); the other two manuscripts were not accepted; v1's reviewer was itself an LLM (NeurIPS scale 2-6, max 6.0). Internal inspection: the system 'occasionally introduced inaccuracies in citations' and 'sometimes lacked the detailed methodological rigor' for leading conferences; the 'best manuscript per seed' selection step is human-in-the-loop.

Jaegle et al. / DeepMind (2021) (arXiv:2103.03206v2), the Perceiver: a Transformer distilling arbitrary high-dimensional multi-modal inputs into a fixed-size latent array via iterative asymmetric cross-attention - cross-attention with latent queries Q in R^{N x D}, K,V in R^{M x C}, N << M gives O(MN) instead of O(M^2); total architecture cost O(MN + LN^2) (L = depth); Fourier position features [sin(f_k pi x_d), cos(f_k pi x_d)], k-th band f_k from K equally spaced frequencies between 1 and mu/2 (Nyquist), x_d in [-1,1], concatenated with raw x_d -> encoding of size d(2K+1); modality encodings concatenated (not added) for low-dimensional dense modalities; latent array re-queries input with up to 8 cross-attend modules; optional weight sharing; ImageNet config: 8 cross-attends, 512 latents x 1024 channels, 64 Fourier bands, ~45M parameters with weight sharing; video dropout: zero the video stream with 30% probability per example. Results: ImageNet top-1 78.0 vs ResNet-50 77.6 vs ViT-B-16 77.9; permuted ImageNet: Perceiver 78.0 vs ViT 61.7 vs ResNet 39.4 (robustness to loss of grid structure); AudioSet mAP: tuned A+V 44.2 vs late-fusion SOTA 46.2; video dropout alone lifted spectrogram model 39.9 -> 43.2 (>3% mAP); ModelNet40 top-1: 85.7 vs PointNet++ 91.9. Limitations: test-set snooping on ModelNet40; 'with great flexibility comes great overfitting' - weight sharing gave ~10x parameter reduction needed on ImageNet.

Gygli et al. / UNC (2017) (arXiv:1707.08559v1), video highlight prediction from joint modeling of visual features and live audience chat reactions on esports streams: metrics P = |S_gt intersect S_pred|/|S_pred|, R = |S_gt intersect S_pred|/|S_gt|, F = 2PR/(P+R) x 100% (Eq. 1-2); models: V-CNN (pretrained ResNet-34 frame features), V-CNN-LSTM (LSTM over image features, unfolded 16 steps), L-Char-LSTM (character-level 3-layer LSTM over all chats in next W_t seconds; best W_t = 7s), L-Word-LSTM (vocab 10,019), joint lv-LSTM = concat(F_v, F_l) -> 2-layer MLP; chat encoding trick: chats concatenated with a stop character, the NUMBER of stop characters encodes chat count (model can learn to use volume); positive-label heuristic: only the last 25% of frames in each highlight clip labeled positive. On 321 League of Legends championship Twitch videos (spring 2017; NALCS English 218, LMS Traditional Chinese 103; ground truth = community-created highlight clips matched to timestamps): dev F-scores: L-Char-LSTM 41.5 vs L-Word-LSTM 19.2 - character-level beats word-level by 22.3 points on internet slang; V-CNN 64.0, V-CNN-LSTM 68.3, joint lv-LSTM 74.8 (P 0.77, R 0.72) - combination is best; test NALCS 74.7 vs video-only 72.2 vs chat-only 43.2; LMS 70.0 vs 69.2 vs 39.7; chat works better in English (43.2) than Traditional Chinese (39.7). Caveats: uses FUTURE chat (next 7s) - fine for post-hoc highlight generation, NOT real-time prediction; ground truth biased toward popular teams/spectacular plays.

SFF authors (2026) (arXiv:2606.08578v1), Smoothed Full Fine-tuning: interpolate pretrained weights with a fresh random initialization before fine-tuning - Theta_3 = alpha*Theta_1* + (1-alpha)*Theta_2, Theta_1* = pretrained weights, Theta_2 = fresh random initialization, alpha in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9} selected on validation. Intuition: pretrained weights sit in a sharp minimum of the pretraining loss; interpolating toward random init moves the start out of the sharp basin while retaining most pretrained knowledge, settling in a flatter minimum of the target loss; cost is one extra forward-free arithmetic op. Across 8 large time-series models (Timer, TimesFM, MOMENT, UniTS, Moirai, Chronos, TTMs, Sundial) x 9 forecasting benchmarks: SFF reduces MSE by 3% on average and up to 6.5% vs ordinary full fine-tuning, gains consistent across architectures (not architecture-specific); best alpha varies by dataset/model, the 4-point grid suffices. Caveats: with small validation windows alpha selection itself can overfit (prefer alpha = 0.5-0.7 fixed or nested validation); 3% average gain may drown in season-to-season variance - needs multi-season aggregation; no probabilistic-metric evaluation (MSE only).

arXiv 2609.07617 ('Forecasting the Winner of a Live Tennis Match'), verdict ADAPT: Bayesian pseudo-count shrinkage of live in-game rates toward pre-game priors - theta-hat = (n*r + kappa*pi)/(n + kappa), pi = prior (Elo-based serve prob), r = observed in-match rate, n = observed sample, kappa = pseudo-count selected per match-progress checkpoint (kappa = 640/160/40 at 25%/50%/75%); Elo: q_{i,t} = 1/(1 + 10^((R_{j,t} - R_{i,t})/400)), R_{i,t+1} = R_{i,t} + K_{i,t}(S_{i,t} - q_{i,t}) with K_{i,t} = 250/(m_{i,t} + 5)^0.4, all players start 1500; Trace hybrid: feature vector [p-hat_M(s), p-hat_S(s), logit(p-hat_M), logit(p-hat_S), p-hat_S - p-hat_M, z(s)] -> HistGradientBoostingClassifier, logit(p) = log(p/(1-p)); evaluation: log loss L = -(1/N)*sum[y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)] as primary selection metric, strictly chronological splits (train 2011-2021, val 2022, test 2023-2024). On Jeff Sackmann data (1.5M 'point states', 8,222 outcome labels): Trace accuracy 0.7606/0.8215/0.8834 and log loss 0.4753/0.3530/0.2002 at 25/50/75% - best in every column; serve-shrink barely beat Elo-asymmetric Markov on accuracy (77.68% vs 77.56% all-points) but consistently won on log loss (calibration over accuracy); pure-HGBM was worse than symmetric Markov early (0.6944 vs 0.6851 at 25%) but beat every Markov model on log loss at 50% (0.3788) and 75% (0.2299) - live features dominate structure late. Caveats: '25% progress' uses ex-post total point count; three models per checkpoint (not one deployable model); single 473-match validation year; no CIs.

Wang et al. (2018) (arXiv:1803.02940v1), 'The Advantage of Doubling': NBA double-team study with a rule-based double-team detector plus a dueling-CNN Q-learning policy (NBNet) over SportVU tracking. MDP: state s_t = court config at second t; actions = 20 discrete (stay home, or double leaving open one of 19 court regions); reward = negative points {0,-1,...,-5}, undiscounted; Q*_pi(s,a) = max_pi E[G_t | s_t=s, a_t=a], V*(s) = max_a Q*(s,a), A*(s,a) = Q*-V*; TD loss L = sum_i sum_t [Q*(s_t^i,a_t^i) - (r_t^i + V*(s_{t+1}^i))]^2 with double Q-learning + cached target net; NBNet = dueling CNN on 17-channel 47x50 court image (trajectories with exponential time decay, causal per-player shooting-% channels) + 93 flat features; q_avg(i) = (1/T_i) sum_t Q*(s_t^i, a_t^i) possession-quality summary; post-processing: double actions suppressed unless Q-margin over man-to-man >= 0.2 (tames raw 90.6% doubling rate to 29.29% vs 33.92% observed). On 875,412 possessions (643,147 after dropping transition; RL subset 22,695 Cavs offensive possessions): 4.8% of possessions contain a double team (3.8% Portland - 6.7% Milwaukee); doubling -> significantly lower offensive FG% but significantly higher foul rate; doubled ball handlers shoot only 6.2% of the time; best vs double: John Wall (1.07 ppp doubled vs 0.89 not), worst guard Lou Williams (0.68 vs 0.95), worst-affected forward Kevin Durant (0.99 vs 0.90); best tandems: Lowry+Valanciunas 0.64 pts/poss allowed, Paul+Jordan 0.70, Thompson+Green 0.74, Rubio+Towns force turnovers on 21.4% of doubles; learned policy: better to leave the open man in the paint than in the back, more hesitant to double stars, more willing to double role players.

Mahmudlu, Karakus & Arkadas (2025) (arXiv:2511.23072v1), 'What If They Took the Shot?': hierarchical Bayesian xG model with player-specific finishing deviations shrunk toward Football Manager 17 priors, extended to counterfactual transfer evaluation (FATS score). Hierarchical: eta_ij = alpha + (beta + gamma_i)^T x_ij, gamma_i ~ N(mu_i, Sigma) (FM-informed prior means); partial pooling gamma*_i ~= [tau_i^2/(tau_i^2+sigma^2)] gamma-hat^MLE_i + [sigma^2/(tau_i^2+sigma^2)] mu_i; inference PyMC NUTS, 4 chains x 2,000 warmup + 2,000 sampling (8,000 draws), target acceptance 0.95, max tree depth 10; counterfactuals: xG_B(A) = sum_i sigma(alpha + (beta+gamma_B)^T x_i), Delta xG_{B<-A} = xG_B(A) - xG_A(A) -> E[Delta xG], Pr(Delta xG>0), HDI_95%; FATS (Fit-Adjusted Transfer Score) = sum_c w_c Pr(Delta xG_c > 0), w_c = target team's empirical context shares. On StatsBomb 2015-16 top-five-leagues data (9,970 shots by 148 players): MCMC convergence all 25 reported parameters R-hat < 1.1 (max 1.004, mean 1.001), bulk ESS mean 5,340, BFMI 0.77-0.85; player log-odds posterior means: one-on-one Aguero +1.48, Suarez +1.43; distance Bale/Robben >+1.7; penalty area Higuain +1.79, Bale +1.78; Berardi->Sansone: Delta xG = +2.2 (Berardi baseline 4.0 xG on 75 shots); Vardy->Giroud swap: Giroud->Vardy(Leicester) E[Delta xG] = -7.25, Pr(Delta xG>0) = 0.07, FATS = 0.10; Lewandowski->Dortmund +6.49, Pr = 0.92, FATS = 0.85; retrospective: model flagged latent finishing ability of Immobile and Belotti during underperforming spells; Sansone's EUR13M transfer to Villarreal followed. Flagged inconsistency: Pogba-B.Fernandes counterfactual placed in Serie A 2015-16 in one section, labeled 'Manchester United 2021' in another.

Dave Cliff (2021) (arXiv:2105.08310v1), 'BBE: Simulating the Microstructural Dynamics of an In-Play Betting Exchange via Agent-Based Modelling': design paper for a betting-exchange simulator with a limit-order-book-style matching engine plus a heterogeneous bettor-agent population. Race step dynamics: d_c(t + delta t) = d_c(t) + S_c(t, f_r, d); preference-modulated step S_c(t, f_r) = (k - |f_r - p_c|) * U(d_min, d_max), k > 0; blocking (Eq. 1): S_c(t, f_r, d) = R_c(t,d)*P_c(f_r,p_c)*delta(v_c) if Delta_c(t) > theta_c+; else R_c(t,d)*delta_min, Delta_c(t) = distance to nearest competitor ahead; exchange: price-time priority matching, partial fills, cancellable pre-race bets, all unmatched bets cancelled at race start, ~5% commission on winnings only. Bettor agent taxonomy (sophistication continuum): RP(d) rational predictors (d i.i.d. dry-run simulations per timestep), Linex (linear extrapolation of mean speed over last N seconds), LW (Leader Wins), UD (Underdog), BTF (Back The Favourite), RB (Representative Bettor - favorite-longshot bias + human stake clustering on multiples of 2/5/10), ZI (Zero Intelligence noise); minimum population bound B >= 4DN for D distinct prices on both sides across N competitors. No real data used (simulator design); calibration to real Betfair data explicitly future work. Structural numbers: N=5 -> nonempty-market probability under random one-bet bettors 0.038; N=10 -> ~=0.0004. (Note: staking-simulation methodology only; no wagering recommendations.)

claim: Winning team write-up of Kaggle 'March Machine Learning Mania' 2014 (arXiv:1412.0248v1): spread-calibrated logistic market model ensembled with a KenPom efficiency model, plus a 10,000-simulation skill-vs-luck analysis. M1 (spread model): logit(Pr(y_g=1)) = beta_0 + beta_1*spread_g on 65,043 games over 12 seasons (Las Vegas spreads from covers.com); M2 (efficiency model): logistic regression on adjusted per-100-possession offensive/defensive efficiencies + neutral-site indicator, selected from 11 candidate fits (best test log-loss 0.487 adjusted+neutral vs 0.538 unadjusted; neutral indicator +0.013); ensemble S1 = 0.75*M1 + 0.25*M2, S2 = 0.25*M1 + 0.75*M2 (weight direction from 2008-2013 tournament log-loss, optimum 0.69 on M2/0.31 on M1). Results: S2 won Kaggle 2014 with log-loss 0.52951 (1st of 433); S1 would have placed 4th (0.54107); correlation between entries 0.94. Luck quantification (10,000 simulated 2014 tournaments x 5 'true' probability scenarios): if S2 were truth, S2 median rank 14, P(win) 11.65%, P(top-10) 44.47%; under median-of-top-10 as truth, P(win) ~= 2% for both; under all-coin-flip, neither ever won; 332-348 unique winners of 433 across simulations (~20% of entries never winnable). Holy & Cerny (2026) (arXiv:2604.09143v1), score-driven rating system generalizing classical Elo into a unified GAS/DCS framework handling arbitrary outcomes (win/loss, margin of victory, win/draw/loss, full rankings). Core update: r_{t+1}^(i) = r_t^(i) + K * nabla_i(r_t; y_t), nabla_i = partial ln f(y_t | r_t) / partial r_t^(i) (the score of the outcome likelihood), K > 0 the K-factor; classical Elo recovered exactly iff the link is logistic (Prop. 1), Elo's original normal-CDF link only approximately score-driven; margin of victory via Skellam on point differences: Poisson rates lambda_A = exp(alpha(r_A - r_B)), lambda_B = exp(-alpha(r_A - r_B)), scores nabla_A = alpha(y_t^(A) - y_t^(B) - 2 sinh(alpha(r_t^(A) - r_t^(B)))), nabla_B = -nabla_A; win/draw/loss via ordered probit (plus draw-free-parameter Skellam-with-thresholds variant); full rankings via Plackett-Luce: nabla_i = alpha(1 - sum_{p=1}^{y_t^(i)} exp(alpha r_t^(i)) / sum_{q=p}^{m_t} exp(alpha r_t^(q-th))). Proven fairness: zero expected score E[nabla_i|r_t] = 0 (Prop. 2); zero-sum sum_i nabla_i = 0 per outcome, so no rating inflation (Prop. 3, requires outcome distribution be a function of rating differences only); score decreasing in own rating under strict log-concavity (Prop. 4); reversion of ratings toward unobserved true skill s_t when skill != rating (Prop. 5). Recommendations: random-walk dynamics on ratings (not mean-reverting - mean-reversion is 'unfair by construction'); keep home advantage OUT of the rating itself to preserve fairness. No empirical results - pure theory, proofs of Props. 1-5 only.

Homography math from the Mendez deep-dive: a 3x3 projective matrix H with 8 degrees of freedom maps points as p_t = H * p_i (homogeneous coordinates, append 1) and p_i = H^-1 * p_t in the inverse direction; 4 point pairs minimum (8 equations, 8 unknowns), overdetermined systems via library least-squares.

Direction discipline: OpenCV's findHomography(templatePoints, imagePoints) - source=template, dest=image - yields H_template->image, which warpPerspective needs for the overlay; the measurement direction GSE needs is H_image->template (pixels -> field meters); never flip the correspondence order to match the tutorial.

The DLT colinearity math: each correspondence stacks two rows into design matrix A (2n x 9) and solves A*h = 0, ||h||=1 via SVD; for colinear inputs the rows of A span fewer than 8 dimensions (nullspace dim >= 2) and the condition number kappa(A^T A) = lambda_max/lambda_min -> infinity; near-colinear inputs (parallel yard lines) give small but nonzero lambda_min - the solver returns a matrix whose fitting-point reprojection error looks fine while extrapolation meters away explodes - so a post-fit residual check alone is insufficient and the guard must measure geometric spread before solving.

The implementable colinearity guard (checkCorrespondenceGeometry): need >= 4 correspondences; 2D spread test on both src and dst point sets via 2x2 covariance eigenvalues l1 >= l2 >= 0 - if l2/(l1+eps) < 1e-3 (DERIVED) throw DegenerateCorrespondencesError 'colinear-src'/'colinear-dst', with absolute-scale backstops sqrt(l2) < 8 px src / 0.5 m dst (DERIVED) -> 'insufficient-spread' and a convex-hull-area backstop; the canonical template is 120 x 53.3 px (1 px = 1 yd) with NFL hash marks at 18 ft 6 in from each sideline (college = 40 ft apart).

Wang et al. (2018, arXiv:1803.02940v1) model NBA double-teaming as an MDP: state s_t = court configuration at second t, actions = 20 discrete (stay home, or double leaving open the man in one of 19 court regions) restricted to a feasible set, reward = negative points scored {0,-1,...,-5} undiscounted so cumulative reward = terminal reward.

Optimal Q/V/advantage: Q*_pi(s,a) = max_pi E[G_t | s_t = s, a_t = a]; V*_pi(s) = max_a Q*_pi(s,a); A*_pi(s,a) = Q*_pi(s,a) - V*_pi(s); TD loss L = sum_i sum_t [Q*_pi(s_t^i, a_t^i) - (r_t^i + V*_pi(s_{t+1}^i))]^2 trained with double Q-learning and a periodically cached target network; policy pi*(a|s_t) = 1 iff a = argmax_{a in A_t} Q*_pi(s_t, a).

NBNet is a dueling CNN: 17-channel 47x50 image input (1 court-region channel, 11 trajectory channels with exponential time decay, 5 offensive-player shooting-% channels computed causally from pre-game data) plus 93 flat features (shot/game clock, quarter, binned heights/weights); double-team actions were suppressed unless their Q exceeded man-to-man Q by >= 0.2 (validation-tuned), taming the raw 90.6% doubling rate to 29.29% (vs. 33.92% observed per-second rate).

Doubling trade-off measured over 875,412 possessions: significantly lower offensive FG% but significantly higher foul rate; doubled ball handlers shoot only 6.2% of the time; best vs. the double: John Wall (1.07 ppp doubled vs. 0.89 not), worst guard Lou Williams (0.68 vs. 0.95); best tandems Lowry+Valanciunas 0.64 pts/possession allowed, Paul+Jordan 0.70; Q-values predict outcomes weakly: q_avg vs. points correlation -0.08 (p < 0.001), showing classic Q-learning upward bias acknowledged by the authors.

The rule-based double-team detector (>=2 defenders within a radius of the ball handler, persisting >=2 consecutive windows) agreed with humans at 72.3%/73.2% vs. human-human agreement 64.2% on 100 possessions; the NFL transfer spec ('Double-or-Die') sets reward = -EPA with actions {rush 4, blitz 5, blitz 6+, bracket WR1, bracket WR2, ...}, feasibility masking, and a dueling network on NGS 2019-2024.

equation: η_{ij} = α + (β + γ_i)ᵀx_{ij}; γ_i ~ N(μ_i, Σ), Σ = diag(σ_1²,…,σ_17²)
