Prediction (5 future points): Chengdu — UniTraj(ft) MAE 28.78 / RMSE 32.44 vs TrajFM 77.82/80.48, DeepMove 36.31/39.10; zero-shot best on all three datasets. Classification: GeoLife — UniTraj(ft) 78.8%, head-only 71.3%; Grab-Posisi — UniTraj(ft) 79.3%, head-only 64.2%. Generation: Chengdu density error 0.0039 -> 0.0037 (5.1% reduction); cross-city Chengdu->Xi'an 0.0171 -> 0.0152 (11.1%). Data study: MAE decreases with scale; full 2.45M slightly higher MAE than curated 1M (quality > raw scale at margin). Encoder blocks: MAE ~40 at 2 -> ~10 at 8, no gain beyond 8; mask ratio 50% best (5-10% under-trains, 75% destroys context).

ATSCC (KAIST 2024, arXiv:2407.20028): self-supervised contrastive trajectory encoder where positive pairs are defined by geometric segmentation (iterative Ramer-Douglas-Peucker significant points) instead of data augmentation; causal Transformer encoder supports real-time monitoring of incomplete, variable-length trajectories. Ledger verdict ADAPT — most reproducible paper in the lane (public code + data); football analog: WR trajectory 'significant points' ARE the route breaks; needs careful RDP eps tuning (football is adversarial/discontinuous, not waypoint-driven). Code: github.com/petchthwr/ATSCC; data: huggingface.co/datasets/petchthwr/ATFMTraj.

ATSCC method: iterative RDP — significant points recursively where max perpendicular distance d(x_{i,k},x_{i,s},x_{i,e}) = ||x_{i,k}-x_{i,s}|| if x_{i,s}=x_{i,e}, else |(x_{i,e}-x_{i,s})x(x_{i,s}-x_{i,k})|/||x_{i,e}-x_{i,s}|| exceeds eps; each timestep gets a segment ID upsilon_{i,t}. Per-step features (9): ENU (x,y,z), directional unit vector (u^x,u^y,u^z), polar (r, sintheta, costheta). Causal Transformer: 12 layers, d=768, FFN 3072 (GELU), 12 heads, dropout 0.35, NoPos (no positional encoding); binomial timestamp masking p=0.2 before input projection (mimics missing states); representation dim 320. Soft Nearest Neighbor loss: L_snn = -E[log sum_{j:upsilon_i=upsilon_j} exp(z_i^T z_j/tau) - log sum_{k:upsilon_i!=upsilon_k} exp(z_i^T z_k/tau)] — positives = same segment (within/across instances); positives excluded from negative sum. Batch: 16 trajectories x ~500 steps ~= 8,000 representation vectors per update.
equation: L_snn = −E[log Σ_{j:υ_i=υ_j} exp(z_iᵀz_j/τ) − log Σ_{k:υ_i≠υ_k} exp(z_iᵀz_k/τ)]

claim: ATSCC data: four manually labeled airport datasets from AIPs (labels for evaluation only): Incheon RKSI arrivals + departures (ADS-B/Opensky 2018-2023), Stockholm Arlanda ESSA arrivals (SCAT + flight plans), Zurich LSZH arrivals; resampled every 5 s, cleaned, smoothed, scaled. Findings: ATSCC outperforms ALL baselines (SPIRAL, TCN-AE, TF-AE, T-Loss, TNC, TS-TCC, TS2Vec, InfoTS) in SVM accuracy on all four datasets; largest gains on Incheon arrivals (complex 4-parallel-runway config); departures slightly easier (straighter). Clustering (NMI/ARI): ATSCC best — label-faithful representations without label supervision. Exact accuracy/NMI/ARI numbers are table-rendered and not text-recoverable from the read — only rankings and qualitative margins were captured.

Jouyon et al. (2023, arXiv:2304.01239) extend online distillation (ARTHuS: fast student trained on a slow frozen teacher's pseudo-labels) with continual-learning methods for cyclic domain shifts, benchmarked on day/night driving video segmentation. Ledger verdict ADAPT — maps to GSE as a teacher-student weekly update where the monthly full-history teacher distills soft targets into a fast weekly student, with MIR replay + RWalk regularization preserving cyclic (seasonal-regime) knowledge.

Online-distillation methods: replay buffer selection f_S in {FIFO, Uniform, Prioritized, MIR (maximally-interfered retrieval)} x update f_U in {Uniform, Prioritized}; regularizers MAS, LwF, ACE, RWalk (Riemannian walk: EWC-style Fisher penalty sum_i F_i(theta_i - theta*_i)^2 + parameter-distance penalty). Best: MIR+ACE and MIR+RWalk. Metrics: mIoU, mIoU-NDS, FWT (forward transfer), BWT (backward transfer), Final-BWT (retention across cycles), on 20- and 40-sequence streams.

Online-distillation findings: MIR+ACE (20/40 seq) mIoU 25.6/25.5, BWT 30.8/29.4 — best overall; MIR+RWalk Final-BWT 30.1/30.8 — best retention. Baseline FIFO no-CL: mIoU 23.4/24.2, BWT 17.7/13.9, Final-BWT 21.9/19.9; uniform replay alone nearly matched the best combos (mIoU 25.5/25.0, BWT 30.6/28.8). Memoryless 18.4/19.4; MAS 14.0/14.0 and LwF 15.7/15.9 — both WORSE than memoryless; RWalk alone 18.3/19.3 (regularizer-only weak). Baseline forgets at the second cycle's domain shift (Fig. 3); MIR+RWalk stays stable. Robust claim per ledger: 'MIR-family replay + light regularization >> baseline,' not 'ACE beats RWalk' (25.6 vs 25.5 vs 25.2 mIoU within noise). Data: long untrimmed driving videos (day/night, city/countryside alternations), concatenated into 20- and 40-sequence streams; code: github.com/Houyon/online-distillation-cl.

ALPaCA (Harrison, Sharma & Pavone 2018, arXiv:1807.08912v2): meta-learn a neural basis phi(x;w) plus a matrix-normal prior over last-layer weights offline, then do analytic Bayesian linear regression online via recursive least squares (Woodbury), replacing gradient-step adaptation. Ledger verdict ADAPT — after each game the engine posterior over team-strength latents updates in closed form, O(n_phi^2), with no refit.

ALPaCA model: y-hat_t = K^T phi(x_t;w) + eps, eps ~ N(0,Sigma_eps); prior p(K) = MN(K-bar_0, Lambda_0^{-1}, Sigma_eps). Online updates (Woodbury): Lambda_t^{-1} = Lambda_{t-1}^{-1} - (1+phi_t^T Lambda_{t-1}^{-1} phi_t)^{-1}(Lambda_{t-1}^{-1} phi_t)(Lambda_{t-1}^{-1} phi_t)^T; Q_t = phi_t y_t^T + Q_{t-1}; K-bar_t = Lambda_t^{-1} Q_t; predictive variance Sigma_{t+1} = (1+phi_{t+1}^T Lambda_t^{-1} phi_{t+1})Sigma_eps. O(n_phi^2) per update vs O(n^3) kernel GP. Offline meta-loss: minimize expected KL equivalent to expected NLL of analytic posterior over random horizons (Eqs. 10-12).

ALPaCA findings: Sinusoid (MAML testbed) — one sample gives 'a good estimate of the sinusoid nearly everywhere'; within five samples estimated variance drops to nearly zero; ALPaCA beats MAML on MSE at all context sizes; MAML 'performs poorly with a single sample.' Hopper 12D handled with 32 basis functions; 'performance did not noticeably change with a larger number of basis functions'; kernel GPR 'prohibitively slow' (Fig. 11 timing). Lane-change (real human data, 19 participant pairs, 1105 episodes @10Hz): improvement near-linear, not early-rapid — attributed to bimodal transition data; in many cases MAML 'fails to adapt, and furthermore, gives no indication of its uncertainty.' No exact scalar NLL/MSE tables — claims are curve-based. Gaussian noise with known Sigma_eps assumed; t-distribution relaxation analytically available but numerically unstable to backprop. Code: github.com/StanfordASL/ALPaCA.

Dabney, Ostrovski, Silver & Munos (2018, arXiv:1806.06923) — Implicit Quantile Networks model the full return quantile function Z_tau(x,a) for arbitrary tau~U([0,1]) via a tau-embedding, trained with quantile Huber loss; the paper also introduces distortion risk measures (CVaR, Wang, CPW) for risk-sensitive policies. Ledger verdict ADAPT — IQN critic for stake sizing plus CVaR(0.25) policy distortion as a drawdown-aware Kelly alternative.

IQN loss: quantile Huber loss rho^kappa_tau(delta) = |tau - 1{delta<0}| * L_kappa(delta)/kappa; L_kappa(delta) = 1/2 delta^2 if |delta| <= kappa else kappa(|delta| - 1/2 kappa); pairwise TD-errors delta_ij = r + gamma Z_{tau'_j}(x', pi(x')) - Z_{tau_i}(x,a), N=N'=32. Tau-embedding: phi_j(tau) = ReLU(sum_i cos(pi i tau) w_ij + b_j), dim 64, elementwise-multiplied with state features. Risk-sensitive policy: pi_beta(x) = argmax_a E_{tau ~ beta}[Z_tau(x,a)] for distortion beta (CVaR, Wang, CPW).

IQN findings on ALE Atari-57 (200M frames, 30 random no-op starts; 6-game subset for risk experiments; no code stated): human-normalized mean/median/human-gap — IQN 1019%/218%/0.141 (5 seeds) vs QR-DQN 864%/193%/0.165, C51 701%/178%/0.152, Rainbow 1189%/230%/0.144 (2 seeds); 'At 100M frames IQN reached QR-DQN at 200M frames.' Risk-averse policies improved over risk-neutral on Asterix and Assault ('very significant advantage'); CVaR(0.1) lost performance on QBert and Space Invaders; risk-seeking Wang(1.5) 'significantly underperforms' on 3 of 6 games; CPW ~= risk-neutral. Quantile crossing not explicitly prevented; policy distortion applied post-hoc while training maximizes the mean.

Dreamer (Hafner, Lillicrap, Ba & Norouzi 2019, arXiv:1912.01603): learn a latent world model (RSSM representation + transition + reward models) and learn behaviors purely in latent space by backpropagating analytic gradients of lambda-return value estimates through imagined trajectories. Ledger verdict ADAPT for the latent-dynamics machinery as an NFL game simulator; the actor-critic policy half is replaced with Monte-Carlo pricing.

Dreamer components: representation p(s_t|s_{t-1},a_{t-1},o_t); transition q(s_t|s_{t-1},a_{t-1}) (RSSM: deterministic recurrent core + stochastic state); reward q(r_t|s_t). Lambda-return target: V_lambda(s_tau) =d (1-lambda) sum_{n=1}^{H-1} lambda^{n-1} V_N^n(s_tau) + lambda^{H-1} V_N^H(s_tau). ELBO terms: J_R^t = ln q(r_t|s_t); J_D^t = -beta KL(p||q) + observation reconstruction.

Dreamer findings on DeepMind Control Suite (20 visual control tasks; 5x10^6 environment steps, 5 seeds; code at danijar.com/dreamer, TensorFlow Probability; DMC open source): after 5M steps, Dreamer average performance 823 across tasks vs PlaNet 332 vs D4PG 786 (D4PG needed 10^8 steps). Compute: ~33h per 10^6 env steps on 1x V100 + 10 CPUs vs 11h PlaNet, 24h D4PG-to-similar. Ablation: pixel reconstruction beat contrastive (solved ~half the tasks) and reward-prediction-alone (insufficient) for representation learning. RSSM produced accurate 45-step open-loop predictions given only actions (Fig. 5). Limitations noted: continuous Gaussian latents blur multimodal futures; DMC dynamics are smooth/Markovian unlike football's regime breaks (injuries, halftime, garbage time).

GNS — Graph Network-based Simulators (Sanchez-Gonzalez et al., DeepMind/Stanford, 2020, arXiv:2002.09405): encode-process-decode over a particle graph with M rounds of learned message passing, trained single-step, rolling out thousands of timesteps across fluids/rigid/deformable materials. Ledger verdict ADAPT — players as particles, interactions as message passing; the natural inductive bias for NGS tracking data (22 interacting agents).

GNS: G^0 = Encoder(X); G^{m+1} = MessagePass(G^m), m=0...M-1; Y = Decoder(G^M); X_{t+1} = Integrator(X_t, Y). Training: single-step L2 loss on predicted accelerations with input noise corruption. Key empirical findings: the MAIN determinants of long-term rollout performance were (1) number of message-passing steps M and (2) training-data noise corruption — NOT other hyperparameters.

GNS findings: one GNS model was SOTA vs prior learned simulators (DPI, CConv) across fluids, rigid solids, deformable materials (particle physics datasets Water-3D, Goop-3D, Sand-3D, rigid/deforming solids; exact MSE numbers figure-based, not extracted). Generalizes from thousands of training particles/timesteps to different initial conditions, thousands of timesteps, and >=10x particle counts at test time. Stated limitation: football players have intent/assignments/adversarial objectives — message passing captures interaction but not strategic intent; GNS predicts positions, so GSE needs a discrete event head (scores, turnovers).

Ganesh et al. (2023, arXiv:2304.05294) — multidata causal discovery: run PC_1/PCMCI in multidata mode over an ensemble of time series (260 tropical-cyclone cases as ensemble members) to find a single sparse causal-driver set, which then feeds simple MLR/RF models that generalize better than correlation- or XAI-selected features. Ledger verdict ADAPT — ensemble = team-seasons, causal drivers replace GSE's hand-built feature stack.

Multidata causal method: M-PC_1 / M-PCMCI (tigramite) in multidata mode — samples pooled across ensemble via sliding windows; only time-lagged predictors considered; alpha_PC significance threshold as the sparsity knob (more stringent alpha -> fewer, more reliable features). Metric: R^2 (1 perfect, 0 one-std-dev error). Assumptions: common causal structure across the ensemble; within-series stationarity. Code: tigramite multidata (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.7747255).

Multidata causal findings on 260 Western Pacific tropical cyclones 2001-2020 (lifetime >6 days to landfall); ERA5 reanalysis (25km, 3-hourly) + IBTrACS best tracks; split 150 train / 55 val / 55 test (test = recent years 2017-2020): test R^2 — causal-MLR wind 0.80 (31 features), Pmin 0.89 (17f), precip 0.62 (90f); causal-RF wind 0.78 (17f), Pmin 0.88 (26f), precip 0.62 (123f). Non-causal RF on all 3978 features: train 0.93/0.88/0.75 but val 0.77/0.74/0.65, test 0.89/0.79/0.58 — overfits; causal models match/beat it with 17-123 features. Lagged-correlation MLR: train up to 0.96, val 0.85/0.81/0.69 — 'selects sets of predictors that perform very poorly.' Causal MLR systematically beats the tuned LSTM (PyTorch, Optuna) on all targets; M-PC_1 slightly beats XAI selection, edge largest for <50-feature models. M-PCMCI ~= M-PC_1 at 6h min-lag but 'drastically deteriorates' at 1-day min lag. Absolute test gains modest (wind: causal-MLR 0.80 vs non-causal-RF 0.79) — the win is sparsity + validation robustness, not a blowout.

Salinas et al. (2023, arXiv:2305.03623): replace the Gaussian-process HPO surrogate with a conformalized quantile-regression (CQR) surrogate that models heteroskedastic objective noise; multi-fidelity reduces to the 'trivial' trick of training on each config's last-fidelity observation plus async successive halving. Ledger verdict ADOPT — unifies GSE's HPO loop with its conformal calibration program on one calibrated-uncertainty stack.

CQR-HPO method: CQR surrogate — quantile regression over config space, conformalized on held-out configs; EI acquisition with 20 fantasy samples for pending async evaluations. Normalized regret = (y_t - y_min)/(y_max - y_min); average rank; critical diagrams; calibration error. Multi-fidelity: train ANY single-fidelity surrogate on last-fidelity-per-config observations + async successive halving (fidelity = training seasons). Data: 13 tasks from FCNet, NAS-Bench-201, LCBench (airlines, albert, covertype, christine, Fashion-MNIST), NAS301 via YAHPO; 4 async workers.

CQR-HPO findings: at n=1024 — RMSE: GP 0.58, QR 0.37, CQR 0.37; calibration error: GP 0.11, QR 0.04, CQR 0.03; runtime: GP 20.03s, QR 2.23s, CQR 2.16s (~10x faster than GP). CQR+MF shows 'statistically significant improvements over ASHA at all times and over all other model-based multi-fidelity methods after 50% and 100% of budget'; ablation: QR+MF 'much worse than CQR+MF' — the conformal correction drives the gain. Caution: CQR is WORSE calibrated than GP at small n (n=16: calibration error 0.13 vs GP 0.06); the edge needs n>=256. The naive last-fidelity extension of REA/GP/BORE/QR also beats ASHA on average rank/regret (except REA).

Guillory & Bilmes (2009, arXiv:0905.2997, UW technical report) — a pure-theory paper extending greedy active learning to non-uniform query costs, >2 answers, and non-uniform priors: ask the question maximizing the shrinkage-cost ratio Delta_i(S,pi)/c_i, with logarithmic approximation guarantees. Ledger verdict ADAPT — theoretical license for GSE's value-per-dollar charting-acquisition rules; no experiments, no code.

Cost-aware active learning: shrinkage Delta_i(S,pi) = pi(S) - sum_j pi(S^j)^2/pi(S); greedy rule: maximize Delta_i(S,pi)/c_i. Tree cost: C(T,pi) = sum_h pi(h) c_T(h); collision probability CP(v) = sum_z v(z)^2. Theorem 2: C(T^g,pi) <= 12C* * ln(1/min_h pi(h)) — approximation quality independent of costs ('surprising... does not depend on the costs themselves'). Theorem 4: C(T^g,pi) <= O(C* * ln(n * c_max/c_min)); Theorem 5/6: eps-approximate greedy costs only 1/(1-eps) factor. Data: none — no datasets, no experiments; 'twenty questions' motivating examples (document length proportional to labeling time, parse-tree fragments, parallel labelers).

Cost-aware active learning quantitative claims are approximation factors: 12*ln(1/min pi) (Theorem 2), O(ln(n*c_max/c_min)) (Theorem 4), 12/(1-eps)*ln(1/min pi) (Theorem 5); prior baseline Dasgupta 2004's 4*ln(1/min pi) for binary unit-cost. Only paper in its related-work table with k>2 answers AND non-uniform costs AND non-uniform prior. Assumes finite realizable hypothesis class, unambiguous questions, known pi/costs — bounds don't transfer directly to deep models; version-space quantities intractable for deep nets (hence ledgers 2002-2004's gradient/MC-dropout approximations). Agnostic (non-realizable) extension stated as open; no batch-diversity analysis.

LST-Bench (Camacho-Rodriguez et al., Microsoft, 2023, arXiv:2305.01120v3): a benchmark for log-structured tables (Delta, Iceberg, Hudi) capturing long-running-deployment behavior (degradation from file accumulation, maintenance resilience, concurrency, time travel) with a new stability metric S_DR. Ledger verdict ADAPT — informs GSE's Delta-vs-Iceberg choice and gives a quantitative lake-maintenance doctrine.

LST-Bench method: stability metric S_DR = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n (M_i - M_{i-1})/M_{i-1} (degradation rate over phase iterations; reciprocal for higher-is-better). Framework: tasks -> sessions -> phases -> workload; WP1 Longevity, WP2 Resilience (Optimize phases), WP3 Read/Write Concurrency, WP4 Time Travel. Metadata layouts: Delta = commit log + checkpoints every 10 txns; Iceberg = metadata file -> manifest lists -> manifests; Hudi = commit timeline + nested metadata table. Code: github.com/microsoft/lst-bench/ (open source).
LST-Bench data: TPC-DS dbgen at SF100 (100GB) and SF1000 (1TB) on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2; Spark 3.3.1 / Trino 420 clusters (1 head + 16x E8as v5); Delta 2.2.0, Iceberg 1.1.0, Hudi 0.12.2.

LST-Bench findings: SF1000 Spark TPC-DS — Delta 511K QphDS (2.7->5.2h, 92% degradation); Hudi-CoW 262K (6.2->6.5h, 5%); Hudi-MoR 112K (23->24h, 6%); Iceberg-CoW 549K (2.7->4h, 45%); Iceberg-MoR 493K (2.9->5h, 73%). File accumulation degrades performance up to 6.8x without maintenance. Engine effect: Spark default writes up to 200x per partition -> 5x+ API calls; Trino creates up to 40x fewer files; baselines ~2x faster on Trino; Spark DML caused 2.4x degradation vs Trino-written files (confirmed by cross-reading). Optimize impact: Delta SU latency drops 2.3x and 2.6x; Iceberg-CoW 1.5x/1.8x; Iceberg-MoR 2.2x/3.2x; Hudi needs no Optimize. S_DR: Hudi <0.07 (most stable, read-intensive); Iceberg up to 0.89 (least stable); Hudi reads ~6x more data (trades stability for raw speed). Time travel: no significant latency/storage overhead vs latest-version queries. CoW beats MoR for read-heavy workloads across the board. All numbers are untuned out-of-the-box defaults (2023 versions); TPC-DS is OLAP, not an ML feature-table workload.

Kakushadze, Lauprete & Tulchinsky (2015, arXiv:1601.00991) disclose 101 real WorldQuant production alphas as explicit executable formulas, plus empirical characterization of their return distribution, pair-wise correlations, and dependence on volatility/turnover. Ledger verdict ADOPT — the formulaic-alpha operator grammar and 'alpha as code' mining blueprint are directly portable to GSE signal discovery; anchor reference for the lane.

101-alphas operator grammar (Appendix A): delay, correlation, covariance, rank, mean, std, min, max, sum, product, scale, ts_rank, signed power, decay_linear, industry neutralization, etc., over OHLCV/VWAP/fundamentals. Example: alpha = -ln(today's open / yesterday's close) (delay-0 mean reversion). Empirical scaling: R_i ~ sigma_i^0.76 (alpha return scales with realized volatility, fitted exponent ~=0.76); turnover log-factor regression on pair-wise correlations has poor explanatory power.

101-alphas findings on proprietary WorldQuant production data (per-alpha Sharpe, turnover, cents-per-share, realized volatility; 101x101 covariance matrix), window Jan 4 2010-Dec 31 2013; inputs daily OHLC, volume, VWAP, market cap, GICS/BICS/NAICS/SIC; formulas published, raw data proprietary: mean (median) pair-wise correlation of the 101 alphas: 15.9% (14.3%) — low, so large alpha counts don't imply redundancy. Average holding period ~0.6-6.4 days; alpha returns strongly correlated with volatility (exponent ~=0.76) with NO statistically significant dependence on turnover. Caveats: 101 were hand-picked for simplicity from a much larger pool (selection/survivorship); production Sharpe/turnover self-reported; 2010-2013 window; alpha decay likely; no multiple-testing accounting for the search space behind the 101.

FactorEngine (arXiv:2603.16365): a program-level knowledge-infused factor mining framework for quantitative investment. It casts factors as Turing-complete code programs with three separations (LLM macro logic revision vs. Bayesian micro parameter tuning; directional vs. hyperparameter search; LLM vs. local compute), plus multi-agent bootstrapping of factor programs from unstructured research reports with explicit leakage control. Ledger verdict ADAPT — the report-to-program bootstrapping maps directly to GSE's sports-report/text corpus.

FactorEngine method: fitness weights alpha=beta=gamma=1 (Eq. 2, 4) — unweighted, admittedly arbitrary. Predictive metrics: IC/ICIR/RankIC/RankICIR; portfolio metrics: AR/IR/MDD/SR (excess over benchmark). Search config: 200 and 400 iterations, one factor per iteration; 2 islands, migration every 7 iterations; init with 5/10 alphas or reports; backbone Gemini-2.5-Pro (ablations on Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite, GPT-4o). Three separations: (1) LLM macro logic revision + Bayesian micro parameter tuning; (2) LLM-guided directional search vs. Bayesian hyperparameter search; (3) LLM calls reserved for logic, everything else local. Knowledge-infused bootstrapping: extraction->verification->code-generation pipeline over pre-2017 financial reports only; experience knowledge base learns from failure trajectories. Integration: mined factors merged with Alpha-158 into LGBM; top-50 assets held 5 days. Baselines: GPLearn, LGBM, LSTM, Transformer, TRA, AlphaAgent, RD-Agent-Quant, Alpha-158.

FactorEngine data: Qlib full-market data; CSI300/CSI500 evaluation. Train 2008-01-2014-12, validation 2015-2016, test 2017-01-2024-12. OHLCV only. Financial research reports published before 2017 (knowledge-infused bootstrapping pool; no test-period overlap).

FactorEngine findings: CSI300, 400-iteration, FE-report-2 best in all 8 columns: IC 0.0474 (Alpha158 0.0299, AlphaAgent-2 0.0314), ICIR 0.3185, RankIC 0.0475, RankICIR 0.3146, AR 18.99% (Alpha158 8.40%, RD-Agent-2 9.17%), |MDD| 12.61%, IR 1.6001, SR 1.0093. CSI500: FE-report-2: IC 0.0536, ICIR 0.4140, AR 8.36%, IR 0.6719, SR 0.2945 (best or near-best). FE-report > FE-alpha at both budgets (report knowledge beats hand seeds); FE beats AlphaAgent and RD-Agent (2043/2051-class baselines) on every metric. Ablation: Bayesian micro-search -> best program score 0.38 vs 0.25 without, steeper improvement trajectory. Limitations: Gemini-2.5-Pro trained on post-2017 data may smuggle future knowledge (authors acknowledge); only 200/400 iterations; Turing-complete programs risk overfitting more than symbolic forms; no complexity-vs-performance curve shown.

Fair Tab Diffusion (arXiv:2404.08254): a latent diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data with multivariate classifier-free guidance (label + regime attributes), a security gate preventing sensitive guidance from distorting the label distribution, and a tunable balancing dial that rebalances the joint outcome x regime distribution from empirical to uniform. Ledger verdict ADAPT the machinery (not the fairness framing) as GSE's rare-regime synthetic NFL data generator — regime attributes = weather severity, rest category, prime-time, division game, dome/altitude; the balancing dial is the controlled way to oversample tail NFL regimes.

Fair Tab Diffusion equations: multivariate guidance (Eq. 6): eps-bar(z_t,c,S) = eps-hat(z_t) + w_g(gamma(z_t,c) + sum_i mu(c,s^(i);w_s,lambda)(eps-hat(z_t,s^(i)) - eps-hat(z_t))), with warm-up gamma:=0 if t<delta, momentum nu_{t+1} = beta nu_t + (1-beta)gamma_t. Security gate: mu = phi where |eps-hat(z_t,c) - eps-hat(z_t,s)| < lambda, else 0; phi = max(1, w_s|eps-hat(z_t,c) - eps-hat(z_t,s)|). Balancing dial (Eq. 8): y_k^balanced = y_k + d_k*i/10, i in [0,10], d_k = y-bar - y_k (deviation of joint cell k from uniform). Guided x-hat_0 estimate for discrete features (Eq. 7); loss L_T = L_G + (1/C)sum_i L^(i) (Gaussian + mean multinomial VLB terms). Fairness metrics: DPR = min/max selection rates across groups; EOR = min of TPR/FPR ratios across groups, both in [0,1]. Backbone: MLP encoder + U-Net + Transformer posterior; numericals via quantile transform; categoricals one-hot. Code: github.com/comp-well-org/fair-tab-diffusion.

Fair Tab Diffusion data: Adult (48,842 rows, 14 attrs; train 22,611), Bank Marketing (45,211 rows, 16 features; train 22,605), COMPAS (train 8,322); 50/25/25 train/val/test; all via OpenML (links in paper's Appendix A).

Fair Tab Diffusion findings (the paper's claims, 3 random seeds): fidelity (Table 2, density/correlation error, lower better, means): TabSyn 1.5%/4.1% best; Ours 11.9%/18.3% — worse than TabSyn/TabDDPM (4.1%/6.6%) but competitive with STaSy (13.1%/17.4%); SMOTE 2.2%/4.8% but DCR shows copying. MLE AUC (Table 3, means): Real 89.1%; TabSyn 86.0%; TabDDPM 85.6%; Ours 84.7% (only 1.3% below TabSyn despite rebalanced distribution); DCR Ours 35.5%. Fairness (Table 4, means, higher better): Ours DPR/EOR 68.4%/71.4% vs Real 46.2%/40.2%, FairCB 56.0%/54.4%, all SOTA diffusion <50% (TabSyn 43.8%/38.6%). Composite score (0.5*AUC + 0.25*DPR + 0.25*EOR) optimal at balancing level 10 (Adult, Bank) / 9 (COMPAS). Appendix Table 7: sampling a training-size synthetic set takes 1213.9s for Ours vs 2.7s TabSyn, 25.1s STaSy, 118.9s TabDDPM — the paper's backbone is slow; the machinery should be ported onto a fast backbone.

Darwin Godel Machine (arXiv:2505.22954): a self-improving coding agent that iteratively rewrites its own code, keeping an archive of ALL generated variants (not just winners — 'stepping stones'), selecting parents proportional to performance score x number of children with codebase-editing functionality, and evaluating via staged cheap-to-expensive protocols (10 tasks to verify editing ability, then 50, then 200 if >40% on the 60-task subset and top-2 in archive). Ledger verdict ADAPT the archive/parent-selection/staged-evaluation design into signal discovery; the self-modifying-agent machinery itself is overkill. Self-modification FM: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New); 80 iterations. Code: github.com/jennyzzt/dgm.

Darwin Godel Machine findings: SWE-bench 20.0% -> 50.0% over 80 iterations (best DGM agent comparable to checked open-source SOTA, below closed-source); Polyglot 14.2% -> 30.7% on full benchmark (subset 14.0% -> 38.0%), 'far surpasses Aider' despite starting below it. Ablations: DGM w/o self-improve and DGM w/o open-ended exploration both underperform — 'both components are essential.' Key qualitative finding: 'many paths to innovation traverse lower-performing nodes' — the final best agent's lineage includes two performance dips; innovations (e.g., node 24) trigger explosions of follow-on innovations. Transfer: FM swap preserves gains (19.0% -> 59.5% with Claude 3.7 Sonnet); Python-trained agent transfers to unseen languages 'substantially outperforming both the initial agent and Aider.' Cost: single SWE-bench run ~2 weeks + 'significant API costs.' Authors' caveat: SWE-bench is 'likely included in the training sets of FMs.'

ImageBind (arXiv:2305.05665): one joint embedding space across six modalities (image, text, audio, depth, thermal, IMU) using images as the binding modality with only image-paired training data — emergent alignment between never-co-paired modalities falls out. Ledger verdict ADAPT: bind NGS tracking, broadcast video, commentary audio, and injury-report text into one shared space via image-paired contrastive learning, enabling zero-shot cross-modal retrieval without paired tracking-text data. Encoder recipe: per-modality Transformer (ViT); image+video share one temporally-inflated ViT; image/text can initialize from CLIP with image encoder frozen.

ImageBind equation: symmetric InfoNCE over image-paired (I,M) pairs: L_{I,M} = -log[exp(q_i^T k_i/tau)/(exp(q_i^T k_i/tau) + sum_{j!=i} exp(q_i^T k_j/tau))]; q_i = f(I_i) image embedding, k_i = g(M_i) modality embedding, both normalized; symmetric total L_{I,M} + L_{M,I}; tau = learned temperature; all other batch items are negatives. Audio: 2s 16kHz -> 128-bin mel-spectrogram -> Transformer; IMU: 1D conv (kernel 8) -> Transformer.

ImageBind findings (emergent zero-shot, Table 2): IN1K 77.7, Places365 45.4, Kinetics-400 50.0, MSR-VTT 36.1, NYU-D 54.0, SUN-D 35.1, AudioSet 17.6, VGGSound 27.8, ESC 66.9, LLVIP 63.4, Ego4D 25.0 (random-chance: ESC 2.75, VGGS 0.32; supervised SOTA e.g. ESC 97.0, IN1K 91.0). Emergent ESC 66.9 ~= AudioCLIP's supervised 68.6. Text->audio retrieval on Clotho (R@1/R@5/R@10): ImageBind 6.0/28.4/42.3 vs supervised AVFIC 8.4/38.6/-, 'double the performance of AVFIC despite not using any text pairing for audio.' Few-shot: audio encoder beats self-supervised AudioMAE by ~40% top-1 at <=4-shot. Ablations: temporally aligned video-audio pairs > unaligned; stronger image encoder improves audio+depth (ViT-H: ESC 60.3 vs ViT-B 56.7); smaller depth encoder better on small (image,depth) data (ViT-S 30.7 vs ViT-B 26.7 on SUN).

Skating-Mixer (arXiv:2203.03990): pure-MLP multimodal architecture for long-sequence action quality assessment processing figure-skating videos clip-by-clip, carrying a learnable [MEM] token through a Memory Recurrent Unit (MRU) with linear (not quadratic) complexity. Memory-Mixer updates: [CLS]_t concat [MEM]_{t-1} -> [MEM]_t (skip connections mitigate vanishing/exploding gradients without LSTM gates). Ledger verdict ADAPT as game-level recurrent modeling — treat a game as the long video, quarters/drives as clips, carrying a persistent [MEM] 'game-state' token forward. Front-ends: TimeSformer (video) + AST (audio).
equation: [MEM]_{t−1} → two bottleneck MLPs → A_t^{prev}, V_t^{prev}; Ã_t = [A_t^{prev} A_t] + PE_a, Ṽ_t = [V_t^{prev} V_t] + PE_v

claim: Skating-Mixer equations: Eq. 1 — memory-conditioned clip features: Ã_t = [A_t^{prev} A_t] + PE_a, Ṽ_t = [V_t^{prev} V_t] + PE_v, where A_t^{prev}, V_t^{prev} come from two bottleneck MLPs applied to [MEM]_{t-1}; PE_a/PE_v positional encodings. CLS Mixer (Eq. 2): C̃ = [CLS_1 ... CLS_T] + PE_c -> averaged and concatenated with [MEM]_T -> linear layer -> score. Audio-Mixer/Video-Mixer: separate MLP-Mixer blocks (token-mixing + channel-mixing MLPs) fuse along time per modality; Multimodal Mixer: [CLS] concat Â_t, V̂_t -> cross-modal mixing. Bi-directional variant averages forward/backward [CLS] and [MEM] for scoring.

Skating-Mixer findings: Fis-V (500 videos, 400/100 split; TES+PCS labels): MSE TES 19.57 / PCS 7.96 (best; S-LSTM 22.31/10.21, MS-LSTM 22.64/9.84); Spearman TES 0.68 / PCS 0.82 (S-LSTM 0.57/0.74). FS1000 (1000+ videos, 8 program types, 7 scores: TES, PCS, SS, TR, PE, CO, IN): MSE TES 81.24 / PCS 9.47 (S-LSTM 83.79/10.90); Spearman across 7 metrics 0.88/0.82/0.80/0.81/0.80/0.81/0.81 — best on every metric vs C3D-LSTM, MSCADC, M-LSTM, S-LSTM, MS-LSTM, M-BERT. Efficiency: MLP-Mixer gives linear vs Transformer quadratic complexity — trainable on small datasets where ViTs 'hardly' work. Limitations: single [MEM] vector is a narrow bottleneck (information loss unquantified); no memory-vs-clip-averaging ablation; judge-score bias unexamined.

Mix, Don't Pick (arXiv:2606.09912): under a fixed pretraining budget, the choice of synthetic time-series generator is first-order for time-series foundation model zero-shot performance, and a simple equal-weight mixture over generator families matches or beats picking the best single generator. Metrics: nCRPS = CRPS/CRPS_seasonal-naive, nMASE likewise, geometric mean over 97 dataset-horizon tasks (<1 beats naive); paired bootstrap over the 97 tasks. Design: fix corpus size (1M x 1024 windows) and budget; vary generator or mixture; train Chronos-T5-Mini and Moirai-Small from scratch; zero-shot on GIFT-Eval. Ledger verdict ADAPT the equal-weight-mixture recipe for GSE's synthetic sports pretraining corpus after designing sports-native generators. Code: github.com/birla-ai-labs/mix-dont-pick.

Mix Don't Pick findings (11.2B-point pool; 11 generator families: ARIMA, ETS, fBm, SDEs, GARCH, chaotic systems, TimeSynth, TSI, StepFunction/Waveform, KernelSynth): generator choice is first-order — CRPS varies 1.6x across generators for Moirai-Small and 2.1x for Chronos-T5-Mini under identical budgets. Rankings don't transfer across architectures: KernelSynth best for Moirai-Small (CRPS 0.734 / MASE 1.049); ETS catastrophic for Chronos (CRPS 1.976 / MASE 2.694); real reference 0.814/1.149 (Moirai), 0.791/1.061 (Chronos). Equal-weight Mixed11 matches/beats the best single generator for both architectures. Real+synthetic strongest overall but optimal ratio architecture-dependent. Limitations: 1024-length windows vs 17-game seasons (untested); GIFT-Eval has no sports datasets; small-budget scaling untested.

Long-run reward CVaR maximization for MDPs (arXiv:2312.01586): the risk-seeking side of CVaR-MDPs grounded in prospect theory's loss frame — the long-run right-tail CVaR optimum is attained by a stationary randomized policy requiring at most one randomization (mixing <=2 actions), computed via two linear programs (one for optimal VaR y*, one dual LP for optimal stationary randomized policy x*(i,a) with flow-balance). Ledger verdict ADAPT as a principled 'drawdown regime' rule: when underwater, the rational risk-seeking response is a computed mixture of exactly two stake/action levels, not ad-hoc chasing. Right-tail CVaR_alpha(xi) = (1/(1-alpha)) int_alpha^1 VaR_q(xi) dq; alpha=0 degenerates to ordinary long-run average MDP; known tabular MDP required. (2): CVaR_alpha(xi) = min_y {y + (1/(1-alpha))E[xi-y]^+}; y* = VaR_alpha(xi); (42): J*_beta = max_d [CVaR^d + beta eta^d].

CVaR-MDP structural results: (a) limsup optimum = liminf optimum via two opposing optimality inequalities, attained within stationary randomized policies — the limit need not exist (Example 1: limsup +2, liminf -2); (b) counterexample (3-state/3-action) where NO stationary deterministic policy is optimal — contrary to risk-neutral and risk-averse MDPs; (c) Theorem 2: optimal stationary randomized policy exists requiring at most one randomization. Computation: max-min saddle point via von Neumann minimax -> two LPs (Eqs. 38/39). Mean-CVaR extension (Eq. 42) same two-LP structure.

CVaR-MDP numerical findings (constructed MDP examples, no real datasets): Example 2 (alpha=0.7): optimal randomized CVaR* = 93.24 vs best deterministic 92.6675 (gap ~0.57, ~0.6%); policy d*(3|1)=d*(1|2)=1, d*(1|3)=0.0255, d*(3|3)=0.9745 — single randomization suffices. Limitations: requires known tabular MDP (no learning theory); toy-scale numerics; right-tail CVaR maximization is the opposite of what a bankroll usually wants — fenced to drawdown regime only; LP size grows with |SxAxS|; no robustness analysis for kernel misestimation.

Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics with Conformal Prediction (arXiv:2507.11739): integrates conformal prediction with Ensemble-SINDy to give distribution-free coverage guarantees for time-series prediction intervals, library feature importance (LOCO/LOCO-path), and uncertainty intervals on discovered equation coefficients. Ledger verdict ADOPT — every published equation and forecast gets honest uncertainty intervals holding even under non-Gaussian noise. Coverage: P(Y_{n+1} in C_alpha(X_{n+1})) >= 1-alpha (Eq. 4); split-CP interval C_alpha = [f-hat - q_{1-alpha}, f-hat + q_{1-alpha}] (Eqs. 5-6); CP-PID long-run coverage (1/T) sum err_t = alpha + o(1) (Eq. 7). SINDy: X-dot = Theta(X) Xi; Xi = argmin ||X-dot - Theta Xi-hat||^2_2 + lambda||Xi-hat||_0 (Eq. 3); Ensemble-SINDy: B bootstrap resamples -> B fits -> median aggregation + inclusion-probability thresholding. EnbPI: s_t^(b) = |y_t - f-hat_b(x_t)| (Eq. 8); C_{n+1} = [f-bar - q_{1-alpha}, f-bar + q_{1-alpha}] (Eqs. 9-10); sliding calibration window of size l_r. CP-PID: q_{t+1} = eta g_t (P) + r_t(sum g_i) (I) (Eq. 11), g_t = err_t - alpha — no exchangeability needed, bounded scores only. LOCO-path: T_j = sum_lambda ||Xi^(-j)(lambda) - Xi(lambda)||_1 (Eq. 14). Predator-prey ground truth: x-dot_1 = alpha x_1 - beta x_1 x_2 + w_1; x-dot_2 = delta x_1 x_2 - gamma x_2 + w_2; [alpha,beta,gamma,delta] = [1, 0.1, 1, 0.1] (Eq. 19). Code: github.com/urban-fasel/SINDyCP_tutorials.

SINDy conformal findings (fully synthetic reproducible: stochastic predator-prey incl. gamma-noise variant; Lorenz; hyperchaotic Rossler with 2+ positive Lyapunov exponents; quadrupole boson Hamiltonian; 100 repeated noise realizations): time-series prediction — EnbPI and CP-PID both achieve the 90% target coverage in the low-data regime with narrow intervals; CP-PID starts wide then converges; EnbPI oscillates conservatively around target; longer horizons (10 steps) and chaotic systems still hit target coverage with wider intervals. Feature importance: LOCO, LOCO-path, inclusion probabilities stabilize rapidly in low-data regime; true active terms score higher than irrelevant library terms. Coefficient uncertainty (Figure 5): standard E-SINDy intervals cover true coefficients (alpha=1, beta=-0.1, gamma=-1, delta=0.1) under low Gaussian noise but FAIL under larger noise, gamma noise, or process noise; feature-CP intervals are wider but cover truth across all noise types. Appendix: feature-CP vs WENDy and BSINDy over 100 realizations.

Unsupervised Feature Construction for Anomaly Detection in Time Series (arXiv:2501.07999v2): the window -> tsfresh -> tabular-detector pipeline (Isolation Forest on tsfresh auto-constructed features) beats raw sliding-window vectors, Wilcoxon-significant across 5 datasets. Seven-step pipeline: (1) sliding windows W in {32, 64, 128, 256}; (2) F windows into tabular DB; (3) horizontal normalization within windows (IF needs none); (4) tsfresh 'Efficient' (q=777 features; missing-value columns at small W dropped); (5-7) Isolation Forest or LOF (PyOD 1.1.3, defaults) -> window anomaly prediction. Evaluation: window labeled anomalous if any anomaly point inside; AUC per series from confidence scores; Wilcoxon signed-rank paired comparisons. Ledger verdict ADAPT: W=32 for intraday odds moves, W=8 games for EPA windows; top-1% of trailing-4-week anomaly score -> 'shock' event, cross-checked against news/weather as a prior-reset trigger.

Anomaly-feature findings (5 public benchmarks, 387 series: SVDB 76 ECG series, NAB 46, AIOPS 2018 13, NormA 5, UCR Archive 2020 247): Isolation Forest — tsfresh features beat raw windows in all 16 dataset x window cells, 14/16 statistically significant (e.g., SVDB/W=32: p=1.522e-12; UCR/W=128: p=1.792e-32); non-significant: SVDB/W=256 (p=0.1161), NAB/W=32 (p=0.05059). Headline: UCR AUC 0.586 -> 0.746 (+36%) with tsfresh. LOF: FE best in only 4/16 cells, 2 significant — no consistent benefit for distance-based detectors. Critical diagrams: IF-FE ranked first on 3 of 4 datasets; on UCR LOF-TS (raw) still best. Caveats: offline train-on-all protocol doesn't measure future generalization; window labeling inflates anomaly mass; tsfresh's 777-dim blowup hurts distance-based models; W grid fixed, not tuned.

OS2FSU — Online Sparse Streaming Feature Selection with Uncertainty (arXiv:2208.01562v2): the only online streaming feature selection method treating missingness as first-class — LFA imputation of sparse streaming features, then fuzzy-logic-regulated significance thresholds plus neighborhood-rough-set dependency scoring to absorb imputation uncertainty. Phase I: buffer Bs=15 features into matrix B (M x Bs); factorize R-hat = PQ^T minimizing L(P,Q) = 1/2||W o (R-PQ^T)||^2_F + (lambda/2)(||P||^2_F + ||Q||^2_F) (Eq. 1) via SGD, W masking observed entries; completed B-hat = PQ^T. Phase II: (a) Fisher's-z/G^2 relevance; (b) Markov-blanket redundancy; (c) trapezoidal fuzzy membership lets threshold mu float in [0.01, 0.1] instead of fixed 0.01/0.05; fuzzy-relevance features scored by gamma_{F-hat_j}(C) = |R-low_G D|/|U| (Eq. 7), top |SF|/2 added. Hyperparameters Bs=15, lambda=0.01, eta=0.00001. Ledger verdict ADAPT for GSE's gappy features (NGS-derived, props, injury designations).

OS2FSU findings (6 real datasets: mfeat-factors 217x2000, SMK-CAN-187 19993x187, lung 3312x203, USPS 256x9298, COIL 241x1500, Isolet 617x1560; train sparsified theta=0.1-0.9, test complete; KNN+SVM+RF average accuracy, 5-fold CV; baselines LOSSA, fast-OSFS, SAOLA, OSFASW, SFS_FI on zero/mean-filled data): theta=0.1 — OS2FSU best on 6/6 (D1 90.05 vs LOSSA 83.95; D6 73.25 vs 50.66, +22.6 pp); average 82.46 vs LOSSA 73.39 (+10.29 pp runner-up, +19.81 pp last). D1 across theta: best at every theta 0.1 (90.05) to 0.9 (61.05); flat-to-improving for theta<=0.6 then drops rapidly (77.47 at 0.8) — imputation error dominates past 60% missingness. Wilcoxon (alpha=0.1, R_m<=2, N=6): R^- = 0 at nearly all theta<=0.7 vs every competitor. Selection size: moderate 16.73 features avg (LOSSA 8.97) — fuzzy band admits useful marginal features. Caveats: test-complete flatters imputation; accuracy collapses past theta=0.6 for ALL methods; fuzzy band and top-|SF|/2 heuristics lack ablation; exponential redundancy subsets fine at |SF|~17 only; classification-only.

2026-09-13 calibration proposal v5.3.0 (status PROPOSED, supersedes v5.2.7; 2026-10-01 audit: NOT implemented, NOT part of shipped v5.3.0 — consumed by the 2026-09-27 narrative_contract promotion, PR #954 merged 2026-09-29): five interlocking engine moves — calibrated confidence (confidence = round(calibrated_p x 100) from regularized logistic regression on full factor vector; features per pick: consensus, depth, edge, movement, rest, form, quality, H2H, venue, uncertainty, cross-market, schedule stress); stronger thresholds (Premium = conjunction of calibrated confidence >= cutoff AND shrunk edge >= min_edge AND beat-vector agreement AND prop alignment >= neutral AND dataQualityScore >= bar; cutoffs refit from backtested CLV/ROI where marginal CLV/ROI turn durably positive); beat desk (classify injury/lineup/scheme/motivation/weather/off-field -> entity-resolve -> polarity x magnitude -> freshness decay half-life ~24-48h, injury slower -> trust tiers T1 official to T4 Reddit volume-gated with tipster-leaderboard updating; unresolved high-magnitude negatives block Premium); prop alignment (prop-implied vs pick-implied game-script similarity; conflicted -> penalty + human review; anti-circularity guard); context matrix (travel, non-linear rest differential, O-vs-D unit matchups, coaching/scheme — learned weights, rest x altitude and injuries x spread interactions).

2026-09-13 proposal's three verified facts about the then-current engine: displayed confidence was a heuristic market-echo composite (scoring.ts:551 sums consensus, depth, edge, movement, rest, form, quality, H2H, venue, uncertainty, cross-market, schedule stress, +10 base) while the board ranked on rankingP (0.7 weight) — two different truths on one card; thresholds were static vibes (70 -> Premium) with no fit to realized outcomes; beat writers/reporter news/pressers/Reddit sentiment had zero ingestion and the DB had no prop market, so cross-market consistency was unchecked (game_signals shadows at BLOCKED_MISSING_SOURCE). Founder override 2026-09-13 killed the 4-8 week shadow period ('we're way too far behind'); layers ship behind CALIBRATION_ADJUSTMENTS_ENABLED kill switch, backtested before shipping.

WorldGym (arXiv:2506.00613, Quevedo et al. 2025): tests whether a learned world model (latent Diffusion Transformer on robot video) can serve as an offline policy-evaluation environment — scoring arbitrary control policies with rankings that correlate with real-world performance. Policy value rho(pi) = E[R(s_H, g)] (eq. 1); world-model estimate rho-hat(pi) via Monte Carlo rollouts in learned model T-hat with learned reward R-hat (eq. 2); multi-task POMDP with sparse {0,1} rewards; GPT-4o as VLM judge with partial-credit criteria (0/0.5/1). Ledger verdict ADAPT — the corpus's only ledger addressing evaluation rather than simulator construction. Data: Open-X Embodiment (Bridge, RT-1, VIOLA, Berkeley UR5, Google Robot); Kim et al. (OpenVLA) first-frames, 10 trials x tasks. Code: world-model-eval.github.io.

WorldGym findings: real-vs-world-model success rates Pearson r = 0.78 (p < 0.001) per task; mean rates differ by 3.3% on average. Point estimates: RT-1-X 18.5% real vs 15.5% world-model; Octo 20.0% vs 23.8%; OpenVLA 70.6% vs 67.4%. Rankings preserved across RT-1-X < Octo < OpenVLA, Octo-Small 1.5 < Octo-Base 1.5, OpenVLA v0.1 < OpenVLA 7B, and checkpoints 2K->18K / 10K->60K. OOD: OpenVLA confused carrot-vs-orange by proximity; distracted by on-screen carrot image in 15% of trials; 'pick red/blue' color classification — OpenVLA 100%, others near chance. Compute: days of real eval vs <1 hr on a single GPU. Caveats: realistic object interaction weak; earlier abstract reported in-distribution underestimation / OOD overestimation (same off-distribution pathology as ledger 2211's MuZero finding); no uncertainty quantification on rho-hat(pi).

NFL concussion protocol (compiled 2026-09-21 from official NFL/NFL-NFLPA documents; sections labeled [CONFIRMED]/[REPORTED]): game-day flow C1-C7 — No-Go signs (LOC, ataxia, confusion, amnesia) -> automatic no-return for rest of game; ataxia added Oct 2022 (post-Tua Tagovailoa investigation), replacing 'gross motor instability' and eliminating the 'alternative explanation' loophole. Five-step Return-to-Participation: 1 Rest/Recovery -> 2 Light Aerobic -> 3 Continued Aerobic + Strength -> 4 Football-Specific (strictly non-contact) -> 5 Full Contact/Clearance; advance only after tolerating all current-step activities without symptom recurrence; regression on recurrence. Final clearance = Head Team Physician decision confirmed by the Independent Neurological Consultant (INC). Neurocognitive testing must complete before contact; abnormal -> retest typically at 48h. Once diagnosed, player may not return to that game ('Madden Rule'). No set timeframe; daily monitoring through entire protocol. No-contact activities allowed with abnormal neurocognitive testing; contact barred until back to baseline OR Team Physician determines non-concussion cause. Concussion is an absorbing state until INC confirms: a concussed player 'practicing Friday' is at most Step 3-4. Observable leak: DNP (concussion) -> LP (concussion) maps to Steps 1-4; 'Full' + no game designation after concussion = Step 5 complete, INC confirmed.

CARDS_SHARE_CORE_WIRING (docs/data/CARDS_SHARE_CORE_WIRING.md): a 10-card implementation deck (SC1-SC10) for a 'share core' props stack — team-week usage matrices -> masked Dirichlet-multinomial share fits over targets/carries -> per-player volume marginals via Beta-Binomial x team-trials mixture -> shadow-mode walk-forward validation against incumbent per-player NB models. Masked Minka fixed-point (psi = digamma): n_i = sum_{j active} x_ij; A_i = sum_{j active} alpha_j; alpha_j <- alpha_j * (sum_{i active j} [psi(x_ij + alpha_j) - psi(alpha_j)]) / (sum_{i active j} [psi(n_i + A_i) - psi(A_i)]); init 2x mean observed share floored 1e-3; alpha floor 1e-6; tol 1e-9; budget 500; non-convergence -> KernelError NO_CONVERGENCE (never degrade). Per-player marginal (SC5): X_i | N=n ~ BetaBinomial(n, alpha_i, A-alpha_i); mean = E[N]*s_i; variance = sum_n pmf_N(n)*n*s_i(1-s_i)*(A+n)/(A+1) + s_i^2*Var(N) (law of total variance). Activity mask: player is a column iff offSnaps >= 1; targets>0 or rushAtt>0 with offSnaps=0 -> refuse the ENTIRE team-week. Teammate correlation (SC8): Cov(X_i,X_j | n) = -n*s_i*s_j*(A+n)/(A+1) (i!=j); unconditional Cov = s_i*s_j*[Var(N) - (A*E[N] + E[N^2])/(A+1)]. Alpha exposure-offset projection (SC6): s_i^fit = alpha_i/A; s'_i proportional to s_i^fit*(eNext_i/eHist_i)^beta (beta default 1); alpha'_i = A*s'_i with concentration preserved; fail-closed whole-projection refusal on missing exposure. Data class CROWN (INTERNAL for SC1-SC5, CROWN for SC6-SC10). Scrape wave-2 results (2026-09-12, founder-pasted extract JSON; wiring map): 71 feature inventory items, 567 data columns, 34 verbatim formulas, 12 pricing observations, 4 calibration claims, 39 export/API paths, 17 paywalled features — organized into Tier 1 factor-engine inputs, Tier 2 optimizer/props-board parity, Tier 3 methodology/calibration, Tier 4 competitive intel/alerts, with a numbered wiring priority. Verbatim formulas: Sprint Speed = 'feet per second in a player's fastest one-second window' on individual plays; best ~2/3 averaged for seasonal figure; MLB average 27 ft/sec (range ~23 poor to ~30 elite). Hit Probability assigned from exit velocity and launch angle of each batted ball, based on outcomes of comparable historic balls in play. Expected season metrics accumulate expected outcomes of each batted ball with actual strikeouts, walks and HBPs. Pass Over Expected Difference = Actual - Expected (RBSDM). Series Conv % = TD / 1st Down / FG / Punt / TO outcome percentages. EPA/play = how much a QB raises or lowers his team's scoring expectation on each pass play. Rushing YOE = actual yards minus what an average back would gain from the same situation. Pressure % = share of opposing dropbacks where this defender recorded a sack or QB hit. VORP tooltip: 'Multiply by 2.70 to convert to wins over replacement.' EV50 = avg of hardest 50% of batted balls; Hard Hit % = 95 MPH+; Bolts = runs at or above 30 ft/sec. Factor inputs wired: underlying: { barrelPct, hardHitPct, ev50, xwOBA, sprintSpeed }; matchupSplit: { vsMan, vsZone, vsLightBox, vsStackedBox, sampleSize }; consensus: { overCount, underCount } — with the rule NEVER fabricate; absent = factor does not fire. Expected book profit decomposes as E[pi(s)] = (1+phi)Q(s) - phi, where pi(s) is book profit at spread s, Q(s) is home-team share, and phi is the price parameter (phi=0.1 at standard -110 odds).
Home-team share decomposes into book pricing and outcome probabilities: Q(s) = b_{h,L}(s)P(M<s) + b_{v,L}(s)P(M>s), with b the home/away book prices and M the margin.

The assumption-light identity: Q(s) = 1/2 + 2*theta(s)*lambda(s) + 2*F_m(s)*Fbar_m(s)*delta(s), separating the hold (1/2), shading×lean (theta*lambda), and outcome covariance (F_m*Fbar_m*delta) terms.

Substituting gives the reconstructed-profit expression E[pi(s)] = (1-phi)/2 + 2(1+phi)[theta(s)*lambda(s) + F_m(s)*Fbar_m(s)*delta(s)]; the structural model is Y = X + epsilon + V for the bookmaker price and M = X + U for the margin.

The promotion gate's non-asymptotic lower confidence bound is LCB(delta) = d-bar - s_d*sqrt(2*ln(2/delta)/n) - (b-a)*7*ln(2/delta)/(3(n-1)), where s_d is the sample standard deviation of the paired differentials, n the sample size, and the range width (b-a)=2 for Brier-score differentials in [-1,1]; promotion requires LCB(0.05) > delta_prac = 0.002 with N_min = 500 paired events and a coverage floor of 0.95.

Leg 2 of the promotion gate requires CLV non-inferiority via a Welch one-sided test with epsilon = 5 basis points, at least 100 graded CLV picks per side, plus a 200-pick anti-flap burn-in before a promotion decision can be reversed.

The masked Minka update for Dirichlet-multinomial share parameters is alpha_j <- alpha_j * (sum over active i of [psi(x_ij + alpha_j) - psi(alpha_j)]) / (sum over active i of [psi(n_i + A_i) - psi(A_i)]), where psi is the digamma function, x_ij the observed count, n_i the trials, and A_i the sum of alphas.

Per-player pmf: pmf(k) = sum_{n >= k} trialsPmf(n) * exp(logChoose(n,k) + logBeta(k+alpha_i, n-k+A-alpha_i) - logBeta(alpha_i, A-alpha_i)). Conditional variance Var(X_i|n) = n*s_i*(1-s_i)*(A+n)/(A+1) and covariance Cov(X_i,X_j|n) = -n*s_i*s_j*(A+n)/(A+1); unconditional Cov = s_i*s_j*[Var(N) - (A*E[N]+E[N^2])/(A+1)].
equation: pmf(k)=\sum_{n\ge k} trialsPmf(n)\cdot\exp(\log Choose(n,k)+\log Beta(k+\alpha_i,n-k+A-\alpha_i)-\log Beta(\alpha_i,A-\alpha_i))

claim: Exposure offset: s'_i proportional to s_i^fit * (eNext_i/eHist_i)^beta with beta = 1, scaling fitted shares by the ratio of next-game to historical exposure. The shadow harness SC10 evaluates Brier/log-loss at lines k+0.5, CRPS via K1, randomized PIT via K2, and 2000 joint draws via K11.

Parlay ratio R = P_exec / P_ind where P_ind = product over legs of p_j. Median parlay inflation is about 3% per leg (beta-hat_1 approximately 0.029, R^2 approximately 0.94); median R rises from 0.991 at 2 legs to 1.305 at 11 legs.

AFCON 2019 nested Poisson regression (verdict: ADAPT for correlated in-play scoring): (2.1) log mu_A(Elo_O) = alpha_0 + alpha_1*Elo_O; (2.2) log nu_B(Elo_O) = beta_0 + beta_1*Elo_O; combined lambda_{A|B} = (mu_A(Elo_B) + nu_B(Elo_A))/2; (2.3) log lambda_B(E_A, G_A) = gamma_0 + gamma_1*E_A + gamma_2*G_A, where the simulation realizes the stronger team's goals G_A first, then the weaker team's goals conditional on them.

AFCON goodness-of-fit: chi_T = sum (x_i - mu-hat_i)^2 / mu-hat_i; p-values averaged 0.476 for (2.1) (Namibia 0.048, the only poor fit), 0.67 for (2.2), 0.33 for (2.3); Nigeria (2.1) deviance null 71.36 vs residual 66.39, p=0.03, a significant lack of fit. Generalized Poisson (phi approx 1) and negative binomial were checked and discarded.

HiveMind (verdict: ADAPT as a single egress proxy for concurrent agent API calls): AIMD concurrency control c_{t+1} = min(C_max, c_t + alpha) if mean latency <= L_target, else max(C_min, c_t*beta), with alpha=beta=0.5 defaults (equation reconstructed, uncertain per the brief).
equation: c_{t+1} = \min(C_{max}, c_t + \alpha) \text{ if } \bar{\ell} \le L_{target};\ \max(C_{min}, c_t\cdot\beta) \text{ otherwise}

claim: HiveMind primitives: circuit breaker opens if e/n >= tau with n >= N (N=20, tau=0.50), half-open after T_cool=10 s with a single probe; retry delay d_k = min(d_max, d_base*2^k + U(0, d_base)) with d_base=1 s, d_max=30 s, Retry-After header overrides. Provider profiles (RPM/TPM/maxC/L_target): Anthropic 50/80K/5/3000ms, OpenAI 60/150K/10/2000ms, Google 60/100K/8/2000ms, Ollama 1000/10M/2/10000ms. Token budget warns at 85% and checkpoint-stops at 100%. Priority ordering: priority level > estimated token cost (shortest-job-first) > creation-time FIFO, with a dependency DAG and cycle detection.

HiveMind evaluation results: failure rates Direct -> HiveMind: micro-10 100%->10%, micro-20 100%->10%, micro-50 100%->0%, replay-11 73%->18%, stress 100%->10%, latency-spike 100%->0%; wasted tokens reduced 96-97%. Ablation on replay-11: transparent retry is the most critical primitive (no retry: 63.6% fail; admission-only: 81.8% fail). Real-world: Ollama 10/10 both modes, HiveMind 7% faster (28.5 vs 30.5 s), proxy overhead <3 ms/request. Cost at 10 runs/day: Haiku $0.35->$0.01/day (97%), Sonnet $1.31->$0.05 (96%), Opus $6.55->$0.24 (96%). Code: MIT, github.com/jayluxferro/hivemind.

Face2PPG real-time remote photoplethysmography (verdict: REJECT for GSE - no camera/biometric inputs): pipeline is face detection/alignment -> geometric ROI -> RGB-to-CIE-Lab -> 12 s rolling buffer -> 61-tap FIR band-pass -> FFT/Welch spectral HR estimation, main loop 33 ms targeting 30 fps. Color science: L* = 116*f(Y/Y_n)-16, a* = 500*[f(X/X_n)-f(Y/Y_n)], b* = 200*[f(Y/Y_n)-f(Z/Z_n)].

Face2PPG results (MAE +/- std / PCC): Server Multiregion - LGI-PPGI 4.5+/-3.3/0.57, COHFACE 8.0+/-4.4/0.06, UBFC1 0.9+/-0.4/0.96, UBFC2 0.9+/-0.9/0.98; RT Config 1 - 6.4+/-6.8/0.45, 10.8+/-5.5/-0.04, 1.4+/-0.5/0.80, 4.7+/-4.6/0.72. Honest failure: COHFACE PCC approx 0.06/-0.04/-0.01 - the method fails on compressed video; no comparison against standard rPPG baselines (POS/CHROM/DeepPhys).

Narya (Garnier & Gregoir 2021, verdict: ADAPT for NFL play valuation as a complement to EPA/WPA): Expected Discounted Goal V^pi(s) = E_{tau ~ pi_theta}[R(tau)|s] with cumulative discounted reward R(tau) = sum_n gamma^n r_{t_n}; policy gradient nabla J = E[sum_t nabla log pi_theta(a_t|s_t) R(tau)].

Narya RL training: PPO + Impala with lr 0.000343, gamma=0.993 (about 0.5 weight at 100 frames), 8 parallel envs, batch 1024, clipping 0.08, entropy 0.003, GAE 0.95, grad-norm clip 0.64; trained in the Google Research Football simulator with 50M steps vs easy bot, 50M vs medium, then 2x50M self-play - zero real match data. Homography X_2 = H X_1 (h_33=1) solved via 28 keypoint masks; REID ResNet-50 embedding (dim 751) with Kalman tracklets.

Narya results: homography IoU 0.908/0.921 (mean/median) vs best Citraro 0.939/0.955; SSD detection mAP 74.6 (player AP 89.9, ball AP 59.3); keypoint IoU/F1 0.882/0.91. Agent goal difference: 8.14 vs easy bot, 4.7 vs medium, 5.3/4.8 in self-play. EDG finding: assist/goal value split 35%/65% versus 10%/90% in EPV/VAEP - value much more uniformly distributed; EPV and EDG always agree on action-impact sign; EDG rates a pass negatively where VAEP rates it positively when 2 opponents press the receiver.

MuyBridge (Bradshaw et al. 2026, verdict: ADAPT for NFL broadcast metric localization): segment center c_s = p^{prox}_s + rho_s(p^{dist}_s - p^{prox}_s); whole-body center of mass C = (sum m_s c_s)/(sum m_s) with m_s sex-specific de Leva mass fractions. Camera ray d_{f,j} proportional to K^{-1}[u,v,1]^T; robust range z-tilde_f = median of sparse depth samples at keypoints; anthropometric range t^{size}_{f,k} = L_k/||d_{f,i}-d_{f,j}||; depth anchoring (alpha,beta) = argmin sum w_f(alpha z-tilde_f + beta - t^{anchor}_f)^2.
equation: C = \frac{\sum m_s c_s}{\sum m_s},\ c_s = p^{prox}_s + \rho_s(p^{dist}_s - p^{prox}_s)

claim: MuyBridge results: vertical center-of-mass error 33-41 mm across regimes; depth axis dominates - running 166/187 mm (mean range 4.4 m, 3D MAE 187, AbsRel 3.6%), track-and-field 117/185 mm, skating 672/707 mm (10.1 m, 6.6%). Baselines absolute 3D MAE run/T&F/skate: MuyBridge 187/185/707 vs MeTRAbs-S 224/120/231, CameraHMR 392/180/534, NLF 52/209/646; root-relative: 45/118/76 vs MotionAGFormer 45/79/90 (with ground-truth scale). Jump height 62 mm MAE, r=0.84, +12 mm bias (n=719). Reference center of mass is markerless-computed, not motion capture - a stated limitation.

MuyBridge ablations: constant range -> 721/235/1890 (kills it); no ground-contact -> 355/808/1220; no keypoint-depth -> 387/316/939; flight-phase error 1.5-2.3x worse than contact (7.0-8.7% vs 3.6-5.6% of range). Deployment: pose 63 FPS (15.58 ms), depth 2.86 Hz, full pass 638.4 mJ, 946 MB model on iPhone 15. Data: AthletePose3D (~1.3M frames, 8 athletes); pose trained on COCO-WholeBody + HICO-DET; depth on ~1.2M synthetic pairs (Hypersim + Virtual KITTI 2). Code: github.com/Abradshaw1/Muybridge.

Off-screen player imputation (Choi 2026, verdict: ADAPT the B4 method and simulated-viewport benchmark into the NGS-replacement lane): B4 role-anchored centroid voting c-hat(t) = (1/|V_t|) sum_{i in V_t} (p_i(t) - off_i(t-)); off_i(t) <- EMA[p_i(t) - c-hat(t)] with EMA weight 0.1/step; fewer than 3 voters falls back to B2, no stored offset to B1. Ladder: B0 ignore; B1 last-seen with decay w = e^{-Delta t/tau}, tau=8 s; B2 formation anchor; B5 fixed template; B3 = B2 + EMA offsets + velocity extrapolation blended with e^{-Delta t/1.5s}.
equation: \hat{c}(t) = (1/|V_t|) \sum_{i\in V_t} (p_i(t) - off_i(t^-));\ w = e^{-\Delta t/\tau},\ \tau=8\text{ s}

claim: Imputation results at viewport width W=44 m (~14.6-15.0 of 22 visible): B0 hidden-zone MAE 26.9/25.6/25.1 pp and control-share error 13.4/12.5/11.1 pp -> B4 hidden MAE 13.3/12.2/13.8, share error 4.7/4.5/4.7, position error 11.6/10.0/9.7 m (best in all three matches; B0-vs-B4 confidence intervals never overlap). B5 fixed template is the clearest negative result (position 22.7/20.7/21.9 m, worse than any dynamic anchor); B3E has the worst position error among dynamic variants (15.7/15.2/16.3 m). Data: Metrica Sports open sample (3 matches, 22 players + ball at 25 fps, evaluated at 5 fps); games 1-2 development, game 3 held out. Code: github.com/nowayfootball/offscreen-impute.

Occlusion stratification for B4 median position error: <=2 s: 3.3-3.7 m; 2-9.6 s: 7.2-8.9 m; >9.6 s: 15.6-16.9 m; 50-57% of hidden (frame, player) samples lie beyond 9.6 s. Held-out game 3: B2/B3V edge B4 on share error by 0.3 pp (4.4 vs 4.7), 95% CI [-0.4,+1.3] - unresolved at this sample size. Space-creation index SCI = Delta_own + Delta_opp: >=+12 space creation, +4..+12 weak progression, <+4 dead possession; a broadcast case study (n=2 windows, no ground truth) moved SCI by 15.6-17.2 points, flipping verdict classes - a sensitivity result, not an accuracy claim.

DAG-Net (Monti et al. 2020, verdict: ADAPT for NFL trajectory forecasting): VRNN with encoder q_phi(z_t|x_{<=t},z_{<t}) = N(mu_z,t, sigma^2_z,t), decoder p_theta(x_t|x_{<t},z_{<=t}), prior from h_{t-1} alone, GRU h_t = phi^rnn(x_t,z_t,h_{t-1}), trained by sequential ELBO on relative displacements (Delta x, Delta y). Goal conditioning: g^i_t is a one-hot grid cell the agent will land in (from ground-truth sliding window); Goal-Net g'_t = phi^goal(g'_{t-1}, d_{t-1}, h_{t-1}); ELBO gains -sum_k g^k_t log(g'^k_t). Refinements: g-hat_t = W(g'_t || g-tilde_t) (goal GNN); h-hat_t = H(h_t || h-tilde_t) (interaction GNN with distance-based adjacency). Hyperparams: GRU-64, latent-32, 2 attentive GNN layers x 4 heads per graph; sports training lr 1e-3, batch 64, 300 epochs.

DAG-Net SportVU NBA results, ADE/FDE in feet (10 observed -> 40 predicted): attack 8.98/14.08 vs STGAT 9.94/15.80, Social-Ways 9.91/15.19, Weak-Supervision 9.47/16.98; defense 6.87/9.76 vs best baseline 7.05/10.56 - best in all four cells. Long-term (20 obs; ADE): 2.09/4.58/6.66 (attack) vs C-VAE 3.95/5.80/7.08. Stanford Drone: 0.53/1.04 vs STGAT 0.58/1.11. Metric ADE = sum_i sum_t dist / (|P|*T_pred). Ablation: the goal-conditioning drives most of the gain (Vanilla VRNN attack 9.41/15.56 -> DAG-Net 8.98/14.08). Limitations: training sees full ground-truth sequences (protocol mismatch vs inference); goal-prediction accuracy never measured separately; no confidence intervals.

Bayesian variable selection for metric reliability (McShane et al. 2009, verdict: ADAPT as a metric-reliability screen for NFL advanced stats): y_ij ~ Normal(mu + alpha_i, w_ij*sigma^2); alpha_i | gamma_i=1 ~ Normal(0,tau^2); alpha_i | gamma_i=0 ~ Normal(0, 0.01 tau^2); p_1 ~ Uniform(0,1) (data-driven automatic multiple-testing control per Scott & Berger). Signal proxies: p-hat_1 (posterior mean fraction of signal players) and negative entropy -H = (1/m) sum[gamma-hat_i log gamma-hat_i + (1-gamma-hat_i) log(1-gamma-hat_i)]. Gibbs: 60,000 iterations, 10,000 burn-in, thinning every 50, full analytic conditionals.

MLB metric-reliability results on the Kappelman 2009 (Fangraphs) database (8,596 player-seasons / 1,575 players, 1974-2008; 50 offensive metrics): 33/50 metrics show signal, 17 essentially none. Best: K/PA, Spd, ISO, BB/PA, GB/BIP (discipline/speed/power); BABIP lands high-signal, contradicting Studeman (2007a). Top posteriors: ISO population mu-hat=0.142 vs McGwire 0.320 (SD 0.010), Bonds 0.304; BB mu-hat=0.087 vs Bonds 0.204; Spd mu-hat=4.11 vs Coleman 8.55; K-rate mu-hat=0.166 vs Cust 0.388; all gamma-hat_i=1.00. Lasso% vs p-hat_1 agree on normal metrics (36/50) but disagree on 14 skewed ones (Lasso attributes more signal - the authors argue theirs is more cautious). PCA: only ~8 PCs exceed permutation null (49 metrics); about 6-7 significant PCs among the 32 high-signal metrics - only six or seven truly different metrics among those 32. Limitations: retrospective only (no forward test); era pooling 1974-2008 without era terms; metric-by-metric fits ignore cross-metric dependence.

BoRaEM (Shejole et al. 2026, verdict: ADAPT for fusing heterogeneous prediction sources into one Bradley-Terry team-rating layer): P(w>l;s) = sigma(beta_s(r_w - r_l)) with beta=1 ideal, beta=0 spammer, beta=-1 adversarial. EM: E-step kappa_i = tanh(eta_i/2)/(2 eta_i), eta_i = beta_{s_i}(r_{w_i}-r_{l_i}); M-step beta_s = (sum d_i)/(2 sum kappa_i d_i^2) closed form; rewards via H r = b, sum r = 0 (conjugate gradient); Polya-Gamma omega_i ~ PG(1,0). Identifiability: center rewards + unit-RMS normalization with compensatory beta rescaling each iteration; beta clipped to [-1,1]; rewards init 0, beta init 0.8. Theory: M-step as rank-1 matrix sensing min ||A(beta r^T)-u||^2 with RIP when N >= C*MK/delta^2*ln(2/eta); every local minimum near-global; EM monotonically increases likelihood.

BoRaEM results: FaceAge (IMDB-WIKI-SbS: K=9,150 items, M=4,091 workers, N=250,249 comparisons): accuracy 79.21% / weighted 87.36% / tau=0.5795 / 6.55 s - best, narrowly ahead of HBTL (79.20/87.35/0.5793, 83.1 s) and plain BT (79.01/87.20/0.5754, 0.89 s); BoRaEM is 10-25x faster than competence-modeling competitors. Spammer injection 0%->44.4%: BoRaEM/HBTL/HTCV remain best across all four archetypes; BARP/BT/RC degrade substantially. Synthetic: competence-modeling methods stable at all N; BoRaEM more robust than CrowdBT at sparse N < 4000. Limitations flagged in the brief: synthetic draws come from the fitted model (best-case); real-data gains over plain BT are tiny (+0.20%); the beta in [-1,1] adversarial regime is not operative for analyst sources (use beta in [0,1]); RIP needs uniform sampling that NFL reality lacks; the method optimizes rank, not calibrated probabilities - it needs a separate logistic calibration step. Code: github.com/KaustubhShejole/BoRa_EM.

Mult-DPO (Zhu et al. 2026, verdict: REJECT - GSE has no LLM-alignment lane; the Plackett-Luce machinery is already inventoried): multinomial surrogate p_MN(Omega_x) = k! * product_{e in E^p} w(e|x)/W with W = sum_E w, O(k) vs k! (2^k via inclusion-exclusion) for the marginalized Plackett-Luce; theorems p_PL >= p_MN and 1 <= p_PL/p_MN <= (1 + A/B)^{k-1}; corollary L_PL-DPO <= L_Mult-DPO with gap <= (k-1)*log(1 + A/B). Loss: L = -beta sum_{E^p} log(pi_theta/pi_ref) + k log sum_E (pi_theta/pi_ref)^beta + C.
equation: p_{MN}(\Omega_x) = k! \cdot \prod_{e\in E^p} w(e|x)/W;\ 1 \le p_{PL}/p_{MN} \le (1 + A/B)^{k-1}

claim: Mult-DPO results: NDCG@{5,15,20} on Qwen2.5-0.5B, Goodreads: 0.0947/0.1292/0.1406 vs LiPO(BT) 0.0862/0.1198/0.1294, S-DPO 0.0762/0.1105/0.1192, vanilla DPO 0.0389/0.0558/0.0622; MovieLens-10M: 0.0650/0.1001/0.1103 vs LiPO 0.0622/0.0980/0.1100; Reddit-V2: 0.1097/0.1101/0.1154 vs LiPO 0.0963/0.1020/0.1060. Mult^2-DPO beats binary Mult-DPO everywhere: about 12% NDCG@5 gain at 0.5B (0.0732 vs 0.0650) on MovieLens-10M; scale-study gains flatten 1.5B->7B. Bound empirically verified (L_Mult-DPO >= L_PL-DPO in training dynamics on the <=3-positive subset); hard negatives improve NDCG. Limitations: the MN surrogate is not a ranking distribution (authors' admission); per-dataset beta selection is vague; total domain mismatch for GSE. Code: github.com/yaochenzhu/Mult_DPO.

ProSkill (Mazzamuto et al. 2026, verdict: REJECT - no sports data, no sports method, no transfer path): annotation protocol is Swiss-tournament pairing (similar current scores, no repeat matchups) -> crowdsourced pairwise skill comparisons (16,372 pairs, 551 MTurk workers, 5 judges/pair majority vote) -> Elo aggregation E_A = 1/(1+10^{(R_B-R_A)/400}) to continuous scores. Benchmark results: global ranking best CoFInAl Spearman rho=0.59 on Meccano; USDL I3D 0.12-0.38, VideoMAE 0.19-0.43 across datasets; pairwise best AQA-TPT + VideoMAE on EgoExo4D at 0.79 accuracy, worst RAAN + I3D on IKEA at 0.45. Crowd agreement: IKEA 0.724, EgoExo4D 0.716, Assembly101 0.705, Epic-Tents 0.699, Meccano 0.666 - substantial label noise. Limitations: targets are circular (Elo derived from the same pairwise labels); no expert gold standard; no lightweight/non-deep baselines. Code/data: fpv-iplab.github.io/ProSkill.

IRT + Glicko-2 classifier benchmarking (Cardoso et al. 2025, verdict: ADAPT - fit IRT difficulty/discrimination to games and rank engine versions by Glicko-2 tournaments): 3PL P(U_ij=1|theta_j) = c_i + (1-c_i)*(1/(1+e^{-a_i(theta_j-b_i)})) with difficulty b_i, discrimination a_i, guessing c_i per test instance. True-Score TS_j = sum_i P(U_ij=1|theta_j); Birnbaum two-step ability estimation (catsim) with instances sorted by difficulty into 10 ascending groups; Principle of Consistent Order (getting a hard item right while missing easier ones penalizes ability). Glicko-2 tournament: each dataset one rating period, round-robin, chess scoring 1/0/0.5, initial 1500 / RD 350 / volatility 0.06. Data: OpenML-CC18 (60 of 72 datasets; 11 largest excluded as too slow; Pc4 excluded - ltm non-convergence); 120 MLPs + 12 classifiers + 7 artificial anchors; decodIRT tool at osf.io/wvptb/files.

IRT benchmarking findings: only 16.66% of datasets have mean difficulty >0, 3.33% >1 - about one sixth of the benchmark is truly challenging; over 90% positive discrimination. Difficulty-discrimination inversion: the hardest bin (mean difficulty 0.63) has mean discrimination -2.44; the easiest (-1.99) has 20.09. Negative-discrimination pathology: on ilpd, negative-discrimination instances let the pessimal classifier outscore the optimal one on True-Score; dropping them restores ordering. Glicko-2 results (increasing-discrimination): optimal 1799.001, SVM 1734.361, MLP 1700.412, RF 1697.411, KNN 1690.538; (increasing-difficulty): RF 1709.253, SVM 1708.006, optimal 1628.72 - ordering is tournament-schedule dependent. Metadata: MajorityClassPercentage correlates with guessing deviation (0.26) and discrimination deviation (0.29); ClassEntropy correlates highly with all item-parameter SDs.

Modified Glicko-2 for soccer clubs (Shelopugin & Sirotkin 2023, verdict: ADAPT the modifications to an NFL Glicko-2 team-strength model): Skellam PMF p(k,mu1,mu2) = exp(-(mu1+mu2))*(mu1/mu2)^(k/2)*I_k(2 sqrt(mu1 mu2)). Draw-aware expectation E(mu,mu_j,phi_j,d,s) = exp(g(phi_j)(mu-mu_j)) / (1 + exp(g(phi_j)(mu-mu_j)) + exp(d+s)), where s is the LightGBM draw probability and d is a bias term correcting Poisson underestimation of draws (Dixon-Coles style).

Modified Glicko-2 home update: mu' = mu + phi'^2*g(phi_j)*(s_j - E(mu+h, mu_j, phi_j, d, s)) with separate home advantage h_p for the pandemic period (Mar 2020-Jun 2021) and constraint h > h_p. Promotion initialization: r(mu_init+mu_new, phi, sigma) if promoted (mu_new<0), else r(mu_init, phi, sigma); season-start drift r(mu+mu_l, phi+phi_s, sigma) on league change; post-season global-mean normalization as an anti-inflation step. All params {mu_init, mu_new, mu_l, phi_s, h, h_p, phi, sigma, d} fit per league by minimizing match-outcome log-loss.

Modified Glicko-2 test results on 60,091 season-blocked matches (2021/22-2022/23, trained 2010/11-2020/21 on ~366,000 proprietary flashscore.com matches): modified Glicko-2 log-loss 0.5832 vs LightGBM 0.5896, CatBoost 0.5931, original Glicko-2 0.5949 - best, delta about 0.0064 vs LightGBM (~1.1% relative), no SEs/CIs reported. Interpretation table: rating diff 0 -> 35.7/28.6/35.7 (win/draw/loss); 100 -> 49.9/25.7/24.3; 200 -> 63.8/20.5/15.7; 500 -> 90.5/6.0/3.5; 800 -> 98.1/1.2/0.7. Summer-2023 tables: Man City 2237.7 (top Europe), Palmeiras 1961.0 (top South America); league averages England 2118.8, Germany 2069.9, Brazil 1868.4, Argentina 1779.9. Limitations: draw-probability s comes from a LightGBM trained on the same matches (no leakage firewall); no ablation of which modification drives the gain; within-season stability is assumed but contradicted by roster churn. Code: github.com/andreyshelopugin/GlickoSoccer.

Multimodal Bradley-Terry with latent stance (Newman 2022, verdict: ADAPT for NFL team strength with play facets auto-weighted by inferred informativeness): p_uv = lambda_u/(lambda_u+lambda_v) with lambda_u = e^{s_u}; stance likelihood P(sigma_r|lambda) = lambda_u^{sigma_r} lambda_v^{1-sigma_r}/(lambda_u+lambda_v); observation model P(x_r|sigma_r,q_t) = q_t^{sigma_r}(1-q_t)^{1-sigma_r}, where q_t = P(dominant party wins an interaction of type t).

Newman multimodal-BT EM: E-step pi_r = lambda_{u_r} q_{t_r} / (lambda_{u_r} q_{t_r} + lambda_{v_r}(1-q_{t_r})); M-step q_t = sum delta pi / sum delta; lambda_i = sum[pi delta_u + (1-pi) delta_v] / sum_u A_{iu}/(lambda_i+lambda_u) (Zermelo-style), renormalized by geometric mean. MAP variant uses logistic prior P(s) = 1/((e^s+1)(e^{-s}+1)) (uniform prior on dominance-vs-average probability). Sign-flip invariance (lambda -> 1/lambda, q -> 1-q) handled by post-hoc inversion.

Newman results: synthetic Spearman R^2 (multimodal/traditional) at M=5000, T=5: 0.88/0.83 (q in [0.5,1]), 0.83/0.53 (q in [0.25,1]), 0.88/0.42 (q in [0,1]) - multimodal wins hugely when some types signal subordination. 2015 NFL application (32 teams, 36,030 play-level interactions across 5 play types - run/pass/sack/punt/FG - with NO success information, only play-type choices): inferred rank scores vs win fraction R^2=0.453, p<0.0001; valences show rushing plays and field goals signal dominance (q_t>0.5) while passing plays, sacks, and punts signal subordination (q_t<0.5); bottom-10 teams averaged 620 pass plays vs 504 for top-10. Runtime 11 s on a circa-2022 laptop. Limitations: in-sample description, not a backtest; the passing-subordination finding is largely a game-script artifact (trailing teams pass more; no score/clock controls); single season; false independence assumption (drives are correlated). Code: supplementary at doi.org/10.1098/rspa.2022.0517.

Variance-aware Elo (Düring, Fischer & Wolfram 2021, verdict: ADAPT the variance-corrected update, reject the full PDE machinery): microscopic update R_i^* = R_i + gamma(S_ij - b(R_i - R_j)) with b(z) = tanh(nu z), S_ij in {-1,1}. The portable Jensen correction (Eq. 6): <S_ij> approximately b(theta_i-theta_j) + 1/2 b''(theta_i-theta_j)(sigma_i^2+sigma_j^2) =: b(theta_i-theta_j) + K(theta_i-theta_j, sigma_i, sigma_j), where K is odd in its first argument and even in the other two; team strength is a random variable with mean theta and variance sigma^2 from lineup/injury fluctuations.

Elotype rating findings: outcome variance Var[S_ij] approximately (b'(theta_i-theta_j))^2 (sigma_i^2+sigma_j^2). Qualitative law: high-sigma teams get rated toward the middle; weak teams over-perform / strong teams under-perform expectations. Synthetic simulations (N=200 teams x 23 players, m=11 lineups; N=500 players, 10^6 steps): ratings converge to mean strength only for theta in [6,8] at larger sigma; larger sigma collapses ratings toward the mean (all about 7 regardless of theta); stationary bias - theta<5 systematically under-perform, theta>5 over-perform relative to rating (the Jensen term bends theta=R). nu sensitivity (sigma=2): nu=1 -> total collapse to about 7 (diagonal lost); nu=0.1/0.01 recovers the theta=r diagonal, nu=0.01 much slower - nu must be small (chess uses nu approximately 1/400). Convergence theorem (homogeneous sigma): E(t) <= E(0) exp(-2 w_min(L + sigma^2 L_2)t) when b + sigma^2 b'' is monotone; for tanh this needs 1 + nu^2 sigma^2(4 - 6 sech(z nu)^2) > 0. Zero real-data validation; mean-field theorems assume N->infinity and all-play-all, not the NFL (32 teams, structured schedule).

Bayesian Bradley-Terry for NCAA hockey (Whelan & Wodon 2020, verdict: ADAPT the Hessian posterior-uncertainty machinery and Bayes-factor evaluation protocol into the ratings/verification stack): BT theta_ij = e^{lambda_i}/(e^{lambda_i}+e^{lambda_j}) = logistic(lambda_i - lambda_j); log-likelihood = sum_i v_i lambda_i - 1/2 sum_{i,j} n_ij ln(e^{lambda_i}+e^{lambda_j}); Ford iteration for the MLE. Priors: Haldane (improper); generalized logistic f proportional to product Gamma(2 eta)/Gamma(eta)^2 * 1/[(1+e^{lambda_i})^eta (1+e^{-lambda_i})^eta] (MAP = MLE with 2 eta fictitious half-win/half-loss games vs a zero-strength team); Gaussian N(0,sigma^2).

Hessian posterior approximation: H_ij = -n_ij theta-tilde_ij theta-tilde_ji + delta_ij sum_k theta-tilde_ik theta-tilde_ki - prior term; covariance = H^{-1} (Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse for Haldane's degenerate direction l^{(1)}). Bayes factor B_12 = P(O|M_1)/P(O|M_2); tossup M_0: P(O) = 2^{-n_O}; B_mle,0 = product 2 theta-hat_{w_g l_g} - each correct call multiplies by up to 2. Posterior predictive via N=20,000 Gaussian Monte Carlo draws; importance-sampling reweighting was unstable on the 59-dof posterior (weight outliers up to 0.00686 vs mean 0.00005 - an honest negative result). Data: NCAA D-I men's hockey game results (collegehockeynews.com); 60 teams, ~30-40 games/season; tournaments 2003-2019 (17 tournaments x 15 games = 255 evaluation games). Code: gitlab.com/jtwsma/bradley-terry.

Hockey evaluation findings: the 2019 tournament cumulative Bayes factor vs tossup ended slightly below 1 - the American International upset of St. Cloud State wiped out all gains from correct calls. Cumulative 2003-2019: BT/KRACH clearly preferred over the win-ratio model, which beats tossup; 255 games separate BT from win-ratio but cannot distinguish Haldane vs logistic(eta=1) priors. Cornell (KRACH 415.3) vs Quinnipiac (93.30): single-game - point 81.7%, Gaussian 80.0%, IS 81.5-81.8%; best-of-three series - point 91.1%, Gaussian 88.2%, IS 89.5-89.9% - uncertainty induces correlation across games (a loss revises the strength gap downward), so point estimates materially overstate series probabilities. Limitations: no home-field term; the NFL has only 17 games/season (wobblier estimates, needs stronger priors); IS instability; Bayes-factor comparisons need many games.

FFORMA (Montero-Manso et al.) fuses time-series forecasters with meta-learned weights: for series n and model m, weight w_m(f_n) = exp(p_m(f_n)) / sum over models of exp(p_m(f_n)), where p_m(f_n) is the output of an XGBoost model trained on series meta-features f_n for that model; the XGBoost custom loss uses gradient G_nm = w_nm (L_nm - Lbar_n) and Hessian H_nm approx w_nm (L_nm (1 - w_nm) - G_nm), with Lbar_n = sum_m w_m L_nm the weighted loss of the ensemble.
equation: w_m(f_n) = exp(p_m(f_n))/Σ exp(p_m(f_n)); L̄_n = Σ w_m L_nm; G_nm = w_nm(L_nm − L̄_n); H_nm ≈ w_nm(L_nm(1−w_nm) − G_nm)

claim: The M4-competition evaluation metric OWA (overall weighted average) is defined as OWA = 1/2 * (MASE/MASE_Naive2 + sMAPE/sMAPE_Naive2), i.e. half the sum of the model's MASE and sMAPE each relative to the Naive2 baseline's MASE and sMAPE.

On 100,000 M4 time series, Cawood & van Zyl (2022) found median OWA and Schulze ranks: FFORMA ranked 1 (median OWA H 0.318, W 0.529, M 0.602, Y 0.491, Q 0.580), ES-RNN ranked 5, simple averaging (AVG) ranked 7, Theta ranked 11; hourly frequency showed the largest gap (FFORMA 0.415 vs AVG 0.847, roughly 2x better). Median improvements of FFORMA over ES-RNN were Hourly 0.059, Weekly 0.017, Monthly 0.037, Yearly 0.056, Quarterly 0.030.

The ensemble hierarchy on M4 data was: gradient-boosted ensembles beat neural-network ensembles generally, and weighted averaging (FFORMA, FFORMA-N) beat model selection (FFORMS-R/G) beat stacking (NN-STACK), except in the regime where all base learners perform similarly - daily frequency was the exception, where NN-STACK (median 0.646) was the best and described as 'stacking the only successful ensemble when all base learner performances are similar' (NN-STACK failed badly on hourly: 1.427 on 414 series with horizon 48).

Xie et al.
