claim: Flamingo-80B results: OKVQA 0-shot 50.6 (SOTA 43.3 16-shot); VQAv2 0-shot 56.3 (SOTA 38.2 4-shot); COCO CIDEr 0-shot 84.3 (SOTA 32.2); MSVDQA 0-shot 35.6 (SOTA 35.2) - few-shot SOTA on numerous benchmarks without task-specific fine-tuning; fine-tuned Flamingo set new SOTA on VQAv2, VATEX, VizWiz, MSRVTTQA and HatefulMemes. Limitations: dev-set model-selection bias disclosed (5/16 benchmarks), web-noise unquantified, likelihood-scored close-ended eval can flatter results, and zero sports data was in training - NFL film transfer is untested.

TimesFM (Google, 2024) is a decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting: f maps y_{1:L} to yhat_{L+1:L+H} with input patching (patch 32 -> tokens via InputResidualBlock), token t_j = InputResidualBlock(patch Hadamard mask) + PE_j, causal stacked Transformer, output patches (128) decoded autoregressively, and random patch masking exposing all context lengths 1..512. Training loss is TrainLoss = (1/N) sum_j MSE(yhat, y) (Eq. 5) - point forecasts only, quantile heads future work; sizes 200M (20L/1280d/16h) / 70M / 17M; training took 16 TPUv5e x 2 days for the 200M model; random masking r in [0, p-1] of the first patch. Assumes univariate only, no covariates, MSE Gaussian noise, context <= 512. Pretrained on ~100B+ timepoints (Google Trends ~22k queries ~0.5B pts, Wikipedia pageviews ~300B pts, 3M synthetic series of ARMA/seasonal sines/trends with change-points/steps, M4, Electricity, Traffic, Weather); evaluated on Monash (18 datasets), Darts (8 series) and Informer ETT (ETTm1/m2/h1/h2); code: only llmtime referenced (planned open weights release).
equation: f: y_{1:L} → ŷ_{L+1:L+H}; t_j = InputResidualBlock(patch ⊙ mask) + PE_j; ŷ_{pj+1:pj+h} = OutputResidualBlock(o_j); TrainLoss = (1/N)Σ_j MSE(ŷ, y)

claim: TimesFM results: Monash (scaled MAE, geometric mean) TimesFM best overall, slightly better than but within significance of N-BEATS, outperforming supervised DeepAR and improving on llmtime (GPT-3.5) by >25%; Darts within significance of best (llmtime, seasonal ARIMA); Informer ETT TimesFM best with supervised PatchTST within significance. Ablations: performance improves monotonically with size/FLOPS; synthetic data addition helps (Fig 3d). Limitations: MSE-only training (no calibrated uncertainty - unsuitable as-is for a picks engine), no covariates (weather/injuries/lines not consumable), context 512 points vs NFL's 17-game seasons (needs cross-season design), and results were relative rankings from figures with no absolute MAE tables.

A base-rate-honest benchmark of LoRA-adapted TimesFM on equities (base google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch; LoRA rank 32/alpha 64/dropout 0.05; context 512/horizon 128; variants zero-shot, pooled LoRA, per-sector LoRA; baselines always_up, random-walk, persistence of last return sign, AR(1) direct; splits expanding walk-forward folds train <=2019/<=2021/<=2023, test 2020-2022/2022-2024/2024-2026; held-out tickers ~80/20 per sector, seed 42 fixed; per-series log+z-score on pre-target history only; run_meta.json reproducibility manifests with two-run bit-identical gate) found a negative result: an apparent ~80% directional accuracy was base-rate artifact (base rate ~0.70 in the 2014+ bull window; the fine-tuned model scored below it - the ~80% was base-rate, not skill); pooled LoRA showed no directional skill over the base rate at any horizon on either universe (excess accuracy centered on zero, negative at 6-month horizon); per-sector adapters were significantly worse than pooled (Diebold-Mariano p<0.001 on held-out S&P 500 at h=128) - specialization hurt; fine-tuning's only measurable benefit was significant point-error reduction versus zero-shot TimesFM, which still did not beat naive baselines and conferred no tradeable directional edge (better CRPS does not imply better pick P&L). Data: NASDAQ-100 (100 stocks + QQQ, 10 sectors) and S&P 500 (501 stocks + 11 SPDR ETFs), daily split/dividend-adjusted closes 2005-01-01 to 2026-01-01, frozen checksum-verified artifacts. Limitations: single seed 42, NASDAQ-100 sector strata too thin, equities are not sports (market efficiency differs).

A risk-sensitive MDP framework directly optimizes the long-run CVaR of per-period costs: CVaR(X) = E[X | X >= F_X^{-1}(alpha)] = (1/(1-alpha)) integral_alpha^1 F_X^{-1}(gamma) dgamma (loss convention). Since CVaR breaks the dynamic-programming principle (time inconsistency), the authors derive a sensitivity-based CVaR difference formula, a Bellman-type local optimality equation (necessary and sufficient for local optima, only necessary for global), and a policy-iteration algorithm (Algorithm 1) that alternates policy evaluation (long-run CVaR) and difference-formula improvement, provably converging to local optima in the mixed-policy space; a mean-CVaR objective CVaR(c_t) + beta*eta(c_t) adds a beta risk-attitude knob. A pseudo-CVaR with fixed threshold y linearizes the sensitivity analysis; deterministic policies are optimal for minimization in the risk-averse case. Assumptions: finite state/action spaces, infinite-horizon average-cost, known transitions, bounded costs, unichain policies.
equation: CVaR(X) = E[X | X ≥ F_X^{−1}(α)] = (1/(1−α))∫_α^1 F_X^{−1}(γ)dγ; Mean-CVaR = CVaR(c_t) + β·η(c_t)

claim: On a constructed 60-state portfolio MDP (10 market conditions x 6 risky-asset percentages; actions = next-period risky % in {0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.55, 0.7, 0.85}; transaction cost 0.45%; riskless 0.01%/day; CVaR level alpha=0.66/0.75; no real data), policy iteration converged in 2-3 iterations from any start, but different starts landed on one of two local optima (global CVaR 4.43 vs local 12.58) - the landscape is non-convex so multi-start is needed. Table 3 (mean, std, CVaR of costs): CVaR-global (-37.55, 37.91, 4.43); CVaR-local (-92.37, 94.77, 12.58); random (-150.41, 205.21, 50.38); mean-optimal (-311.65, 322.20, 45.17) - the mean-optimal policy had ~10x worse CVaR than the CVaR policy. Mean-CVaR (beta=0.22, alpha=0.75): objective converged to 3.38 by iteration 3; higher beta was visibly more aggressive; two local optima existed at beta=0.4. Limitations: only local-optimum convergence is guaranteed; toy MDP with hand-specified transitions; no learning theory; no comparison to simpler baselines like fixed-fraction staking.

The MDL (minimum description length) equation-selection score (Eq. 1) is L(D) = -log(L(theta-hat)) + k*log(n) - (p/2)*log(3) + sum_j log(c_j) + sum_i^p (1/2*log(I_ii) + log(|theta-hat_i|)) in nats, where -log L(theta-hat) is the Shannon-Fano residual term, k*log(n) is the structure term for k nodes from n operators plus sum log(c_j) for integer constants, and the remaining terms encode parameter precision; lower is better and model probability is proportional to exp(-L(D)). Optimal parameter precision is Delta_i = (12/I_ii)^{1/2} with I the observed Fisher information (likelihood-vs-precision tradeoff); the Bayesian connection (Eqs. 2-4) shows MDL equals -log posterior under a Laplace approximation with function prior -log P(f_i) = k*log(n) + sum log(c_alpha). An alternative function prior is the Katz back-off prior learned from a training set of domain equations (operator-combination probabilities, language-model style), a drop-in replacement for k*log(n).
equation: L(D) = −log(ℒ(θ̂)) + k·log(n) − (p/2)·log(3) + Σ_j log(c_j) + Σ_i^p (½·log(I_ii) + log(|θ̂_i|)); Δ_i = (12/I_ii)^{1/2}

claim: Exhaustive Symbolic Regression (Bartlett et al. 2024) generates EVERY function up to a complexity cap (guaranteeing no candidate is missed): all tree templates by arity, decorated with all operator permutations, deduplicated via simplification rules (tree reordering, parameter permutation, reparametrization invariance, parameter combination), max-likelihood parameter fit per unique function via nonlinear optimization, broadcast to equivalent variants via transformation Jacobians. Cost: ~200 CPU-hours at complexity 10 (exponential scaling; typical cap ~10, ESR 2.0 targeting ~13 in Julia). On the SRBench benchmark (Penn ML Benchmarks, feynman_I_6_2a, 10^5 datapoints from an unknown univariate function), ESR alone found the true generator y = theta1*theta0^{x^2} (theta0=0.6065, theta1=0.3989 ~ 1/sqrt(e), 1/sqrt(2pi) - a standard normal; exact params give MSE = 3x10^-33) at complexity 7 via a sharp MSE cliff, while all five stochastic algorithms (PySR, DataModeler, FFX, QLattice, Operon) missed it (Operon found only an overparametrized complexity-11 version).

MDL-ranked domain equations: cosmology MDL winners were H^2(z) = theta0(1+z)^2 (cosmic chronometers) and H^2(z) = theta0(1+z)^{1+z} (supernovae), both complexity 5 below Friedmann's 7, preferred over Friedmann H^2(z) = H0^2(Omega_Lambda + Omega_m(1+z)^3) by 7.12 nats (probability ratio 1240) and 4.91 nats (probability ratio 136); 38 (CCs) / 36 (SNe) functions beat the literature standard, and both winners share the Friedmann Taylor expansion to O(z^2) (data: 32 cosmic-chronometer points + 1590 Pantheon+ SNe Ia with covariance). On the galaxy radial acceleration relation, many ESR functions beat MOND's 'Simple'/'RAR' interpolating functions, but P(g_obs -> const as g_bar -> 0) ~ 1 over all functions and mock-data controls showed the data cannot discriminate even if MOND were true. Inflation: MDL winner exp(-exp(exp(exp(phi)))) (complexity 6); with the Katz prior trained on Encyclopaedia Inflationaris, winners were theta0(theta1 + log(phi)^2) (set A) and theta0 phi^{theta1/phi} (set B); literature models ranked 1272 (Starobinsky), 8697 (quadratic), 10839 (quartic) out of the exhaustive list (3 CMB numbers from Planck: A_s = (0.027 +/- 0.0027) M_pl, n_s = 0.9649 +/- 0.0042, r < 0.028 at 95% CL).
equation: H²(z) = H₀²(Ω_Λ + Ω_m(1+z)³); g_obs = ν(g_bar/a₀)g_bar; φ̈ + 3Hφ̇ + V′(φ) = 0

claim: Bennett & Clarkson (2022, arXiv:2207.11486v1) replaced hand-chosen rolling windows or grid-searched exponential decay with a learned forgetting (sample-weighting) mechanism trained by gradient descent via bi-level optimization on validation loss. Weighted ERM is Rhat_t(theta) = sum_{tau=1}^{t-1} alpha_{|t-1-tau|} * L(f(X_tau;theta), Y_tau) with weights from a forgetting mechanism alpha(i;eta) parameterized by eta; two mechanisms: (3) exponential decay alpha(tau;eta) = exp(-eta1 tau) (GradExp) and (4) mixed decay alpha(tau;eta) = exp(-eta1 tau - eta2 tau^2 - eta3 log(tau+1)) (GradMixedDecay). The bi-level problem is min_eta g^U(eta, theta-hat) subject to theta-hat in argmin_theta g^L(eta,theta), where g^U is validation loss on the most recent T-t* samples and g^L the alpha-weighted training loss; implicit differentiation (Gould et al. 2016, Lemma 3.1) gives partial theta-hat / partial eta_i = -(nabla^2_theta g^L|theta-hat)^{-1} * partial/partial eta_i nabla_theta g^L|theta-hat, requiring g^L twice continuously differentiable - incompatible with tree models like LightGBM unless weights are fit on a differentiable surrogate then frozen. Training: 5 restarts from random init, 50 epochs SGD each.
equation: R̂_t(θ) = Σ_{τ=1}^{t-1} α_{|t-1-τ|}·L(f(X_τ;θ), Y_τ); α(τ;η) = exp(−η₁τ) (GradExp); α(τ;η) = exp(−η₁τ − η₂τ² − η₃log(τ+1)) (GradMixedDecay); ∂θ̂/∂η_i = −(∇²_θ g^L|θ̂)^{−1}·∂/∂η_i ∇_θ g^L|θ̂

claim: On synthetic data (4 settings x 192 Monte Carlo runs from Kuznetsov & Mohri 2020, t=1..3000, eps_t ~ N(0,0.05^2): FixedRegime abrupt change points, RandomWalk gradual drift theta_t = 1 - t/1500, RandomRegime stochastic switching, Stat no-shift; features X_t = (Y_{t-1}, Y_{t-2}, Y_{t-3}), no-intercept linear; split train 1..2875, validation 2876..2975, test 2976..3000) and real financial data (19 years of daily log-returns for 50 NYSE equities; Task 1 Fama-French 3-factor risk model Y_t^(i) - RF_t = theta_t^(i)' X_t with X_t = (1, MR_t, SB_t, HL_t); Task 2 next-day |return| for 15 ETFs from 5 lagged absolute returns; expanding time-series CV: 6 years training, 150-day validation, next 150 days out-of-sample), GradMixedDecay was best in 4 of 6 datasets (FixedRegime, RandomWalk, Factor, Vol) and near-best in RandomRegime and Stat; GradExp approximately equaled GridSearchExp (gradient matches grid search where grid search is feasible, enabling the 3-parameter mechanism grid search cannot afford). In the no-shift control (Stat), Stationary (2.54 x10^-3) won - forgetting only helps under actual shift; the Vol column (GradMixedDecay 8.76 vs Stationary 8.77 x10^-5) was a tie, not a win; the paper's real-data Wilcoxon significance stars are overstated because correlated time series violate the independence assumption. NFL-scale caveat: NFL seasons are ~17 games, so the effective-sample-size tradeoff bites much harder than in 19 years of daily data, and the 'validation = most recent data' assumption breaks under abrupt mid-validation regime change (exactly when forgetting matters most).

A three-stage LSTM pipeline estimated the 3D trajectory of a bouncing ball from 2D monocular tracking using a camera-independent ray parameterization: each 2D track point (u,v) is back-projected to a 3D viewing ray r(s) = c + d s from camera center c and direction d (from extrinsics E and intrinsics f, p_x, p_y), with c = psi(E^{-1}[0,0,0,1]^T) and d = psi(E^{-1}[u-p_x, v-p_y, f, 0]^T), psi = dehomogenization; each ray is reparameterized as two intersection points with two perpendicular planes - the ground plane (y=0) and a vertical plane (z=0) - dropping always-zero coordinates to get P = (p_ground, p_vertical) in R^4, so camera location/orientation/focal length drop out. Stage 1 (EoT network, LSTM^eps): 3 bidirectional LSTMs with shortcut connections + 3 FC layers on temporal differences DeltaP_t = P_{t+1} - P_t (shift invariance), outputting eps_t in [0,1], the probability the ball ends its trajectory. Stage 2 (height prediction): forward LSTM^f and backward LSTM^b predict height differences Delta h^f_t / Delta h^b_t accumulated from h^f_0 = 0 / h^b_N = 0, combined by ramp sum h_t = (1-w_t) h^f_t + w_t h^b_t with w_t = (t-1)/(N-1); height (1 DOF, camera-independent) uniquely determines the 3D point via ray intersection r^y_t(s*_t) = h_t, guaranteeing reprojection consistency; a bidirectional LSTM^height refines absolute heights. Stage 3 (LSTM^refine): 3 BiLSTMs predicting residual deltas (delta x_t, delta y_t, delta z_t) on reconstructed 3D coordinates, ResNet-style. Losses: L_eps = -(1/N) sum_t [gamma eps^gt_t log eps_t + (1-gamma)(1-eps^gt_t) log(1-eps_t)] (weighted BCE); L_3D = (1/N) sum_t ||(x,y,z)^gt_t - (x,y,z)^final_t||^2_2; L_B = (1/|Y|) sum_{y in Y} y^2 for below-ground points; total L_Total = lambda_eps L_eps + lambda_3D L_3D + lambda_B L_B with (10, 1, 10). Trained solely on PhysX/Unity simulation.
equation: r(s) = c + ds; P = (p_ground, p_vertical) ∈ R⁴; h_t = (1−w_t)h^f_t + w_t h^b_t, w_t = (t−1)/(N−1); L_Total = λ_ε L_ε + λ_3D L_3D + λ_B L_B, (λ_ε, λ_3D, λ_B) = (10, 1, 10)

claim: Ball-trajectory results: tennis landing (Real TrackNet, vs SynthNet): landing accuracy 87.21%, F1 0.807, landing error 0.63 m vs SynthNet's 3.58 m - a ~5.7x reduction in landing error. Single-launch trajectories (distance NRMSE): ours 0.03 +/- 0.002 (~0.6 cm RMSE on that dataset) vs Shen et al. 2016 (0.11 +/- 0.01) vs Mocanu et al. 2017 (1.02 +/- 0.03). Noise robustness: at +/-25 px input noise (1664x1088 resolution), ours degraded to ~0.05/0.07/0.09/0.11 at 5/10/15/20/25 px vs Shen 0.64 and Mocanu 1.20 +/- 0.42 at +/-25 px - degrades minimally. Parameterization ablation (Synthetic->Real Mocap/IPL, NRMSE): the proposed p_ground+p_vertical input + height output (0.05/0.09/0.01 synth, 0.68/0.74 real) beat naive pixel-input + xyz-output (14.13/0.31/0.70 synth, 11.68/2.45 real) - the representation is the decisive ingredient, with naive 3D regression overfitting badly (large synth->real gap). Component ablation: removing LSTM^height exploded error (synth Mocap 0.05 -> 6.26); removing LSTM^refine raised errors across datasets (synth Mocap 0.05 -> 0.10, real IPL 0.74 -> 1.84); EoT flags mattered most on Tennis/IPL where player-induced direction changes are less predictable. Stated assumptions: first and last frames lie on the ground (y=0), camera intrinsics+extrinsics known, camera high enough that no viewing ray is parallel to either plane, and each 'trajectory' begins when a force is applied and ends before the next force or rest; sim-to-real caveats: simulation ignored spin, aerodynamics (Magnus) and court/turf friction, and unusual trajectories degraded.

Five calibration papers were ranked for frozen deterministic models (calibrate outputs, no MODEL_VERSION bump to evaluate): (1) Variable-Based Calibration - Kelly & Smyth (decision tree on one variable, per-leaf calibrator; fixes the recorded defect 'no code path conditions calibration on sport'); (2) Foulley football forecast verification (reliability, Brier decomposition, discrimination); (3) Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability - Barber, Candes, Ramdas, Tibshirani (recency-weighted quantiles for temporal drift; nfelo's 2009-2024 close-game ATS was 55.06% but 2024 alone was 45.3%); (4) Dirichlet calibration - Kull et al. The frozen GSE NFL prediction model replayed against 27 seasons (1999-2025 regular season) of nflverse closing lines: 6,967 in-range games -> 15,939 settled picks (SPREAD 6,967, TOTAL 6,967, MONEYLINE 2,005), results 8,246 W / 7,401 L / 292 P. Break-even win rate at -110 is 110/210 = 52.381%. Headline: 15,647 decisive picks at 52.700% win rate, 95% CI [51.92%, 53.48%], z = 0.799 vs break-even - not statistically significant (z < 1.96); blended 52.7% win rate looks above break-even but is an artifact of mixing markets (moneyline picks were heavy favourites ~-350 paying ~0.29 units vs 0.91 at -110). Per-market ROI (units staked): SPREAD 48.86% win / ROI -6.53% (n=6778, push 189); TOTAL 49.49% / ROI -5.44% (n=6868, push 99); MONEYLINE 76.71% / ROI -1.96% (n=2001, push 4); overall ROI -5.48%, roughly the size of the vig. Confidence bands: 70-79 (n=3,770, 48.33%, ROI -7.52%) vs 65-69 (n=9,693, 49.47%, ROI -5.46%) vs 60-64 (n=183, 51.37%, CI [44.17%, 58.50%], ROI -1.91%) - higher confidence gave worse results (mildly anti-informative); premium band (70-79) vs free band (65-69) two-proportion z = -1.19, p = 0.235 (not significant, point estimate the wrong way); no 80+ band exists (the engine essentially never emits confidence >= 80) and almost the whole board sits in 65-79; confidence decides the paywall (70-79 = PREMIUM paywalled, 65-69 = FREE), so no evidence paywalled picks outperform free ones - directly challenging the paid tier's premise. Era splits flat and negative: 1999-2005 n=3,454, 48.90%, ROI -6.49%; 2006-2012 n=3,494, 49.86%, ROI -4.70%; 2013-2019 n=3,517, 49.22%, ROI -5.93%; 2020-2025 n=3,181, 48.70%, ROI -6.93% - no golden age, no decay; 2025 alone n=630, 53.968%, CI [50.08%, 57.86%], z=0.797 - interval equally consistent with losing money and a large edge. The corpus was genuinely out-of-sample (nothing fit on it; weights heuristic; isotonic layer fit on live 2026 picks). Structural caveats: entry line == closing line by construction (all picks MATCHED_CLOSE; no CLV visible); book depth synthetic; Edge Index/grade ladder untestable; the synthetic-book reconstruction priced every spread/total pick at -110 (offeredProb(-110) = 0.5238, symmetric de-vig fairProb = 0.5000, rawEdge = -0.0238 for every pick), so all 13,646 spread/total picks land in one Edge Index band (every pick grades LEAN - a reconstruction artifact). A spread-sign bug was caught via zero pushes: pre-fix 36.0% on a 139-pick sample (50 W / 89 L / 0 P), post-fix 49.3% with 5 pushes.

The design-to-react governance protocol (doctrine only, no shipped-component evidence recorded) defines five sequential translation stages with audits: Stage 1 design-token audit (colors map to DESIGN.md tokens, no hardcoded hex, 4px spacing multiples), claim-governance audit (source freshness disclosure, confidence scores carry 'not a guarantee' context, forbidden vocabulary: lock / guaranteed / sure thing, win-rate claims carry window + model version, 'Entertainment purposes only' on public pick surfaces), access-control audit (premium data gated; cockpit-only marked), accessibility pre-check (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 body, visible focus states, text alternatives for dataviz); Stage 2 mandatory component pre-declaration with import contract (colors via CSS custom properties only, no new npm dependencies); Stage 3 token/paywall/claim compliance per render block with the canonical correct pattern being server-side tier resolution (isPro prop from a validated server component), never client-side useSession() checks; Stage 4 test tiers (unit, integration incl. gated components hiding confidence score for FREE tier, accessibility, claim governance); Stage 5 typecheck + lint + full test run, visual regression at 1280px and 375px vs mockup, hex-drift check via grep -E '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}' (must return zero). Banned patterns: hardcoded hex via style=, casino-green color, eslint-disable/@ts-ignore in pick components, client-only paywall checks, unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML with pick data, hard-coded win rate without <WinRateBadge>; any component displaying pick data, confidence scores, or market data always gets operator review before production.

arXiv 2609.23158 (KAUST, Sep 19, 2026): 77 GHz FMCW radar chest snapshots (single chirp T = 102.4 µs, 256 fast-time samples, ~7.5 cm range resolution, INRAS radarbook 2 GHz bandwidth, 2 Tx / 16 Rx, 1 m standoff) classifying pre- vs post-exercise physiological skin states via Wavelet Scattering Transform (analytic Morlet/Gabor wavelets, invariance scale 128 samples, Q = [2,1], [4,1], [8,1]) on 15 university-level ultimate frisbee athletes (125 single-chirp samples per subject per condition -> 3750 total; WST tensor 25 paths x 8 temporal windows -> 3750 x 200 feature matrix). Headline: feedforward NN mean accuracy 91.55% with 95% CI [84.27, 98.83]% in leave-one-subject-out (LOSO); full LOSO table: NB 76.35 ± 15.98 [68.26, 84.43]; SVM 80.32 ± 15.85 [72.30, 88.34]; KNN 77.87 ± 14.55 [70.50, 85.23]; Kernel 85.07 ± 13.90 [78.03, 92.10]; NN 91.55 ± 14.39 [84.27, 98.83]; random 10-run CV (leakage-prone) ran higher: NB 89.84 ± 1.52, SVM 92.16 ± 1.12, KNN 90.29 ± 0.87, Kernel 96.51 ± 1.11, NN 99.28 ± 0.56 - the NN CV->LOSO drop (99.28 -> 91.55) evidences within-subject leakage in random CV. Feature-order contributions by |t|-statistic ranking: zeroth-order S0 ≈ 67.9%, second-order ≈ 24.4%, first-order ≈ 7.6% - low-pass signal energy/amplitude stability dominates; WST beats raw-signal baseline; Q = [4,1] best tradeoff. Gate verdict: 0/3 -> REJECT (no transferable GSE input stream, task, or edge). Adversarial findings: n = 15 subjects with 250 highly correlated chirps/subject; LOSO CI 14.6 points wide - some held-out subjects plausibly near chance; no ground truth (no corneometry, skin temperature, sweat electrolytes, body-mass loss); 125-chirp 'selection procedure' never specified; post-exercise subjects were panting/shifting at 1 m standoff - classifier may detect 'exhausted moving person vs calm resting person,' not skin permittivity; 2-hour ambient drift unreported; t-statistic interpretability admits non-independent samples (inflates |t|); single-sport population, demographics unspecified. Transferable lesson only: group-out (LOSO) validation over random CV to kill within-subject leakage, and order-contribution analysis to check whether a model is learning the claimed mechanism or a confound.

From the skin-state radar ledger (arXiv 2609.23158), the FMCW radar received signal model is r(t) = Σ_{l=1}^{L} α̃_l e^{j2π(fc + Bt/(2T))(t−τ_l)} + n̄(t) (1), with τ_l = 2R_l/c and n̄(t) ~ N(0, σ²); after demodulation x(t) = Σ_{l=1}^{L} α̃_l e^{j2πfcτ_l} e^{j2π(Bτ_l/(2T))t} + n(t) (2); in beat-frequency form x(t) = Σ_{l=1}^{L} α_l e^{j2π(2BR_l/(cT))t} + n(t), 0 ≤ t ≤ T (3), where α_l = α̃_l e^{j4πfcR_l/c} and beat frequencies f_bl = 2BR_l/(cT) are estimated by range FFT; Hamming windowing is xw(t) = x(t) · w(t) (4); and the skin–air reflection coefficient is Γ ≈ (1 − √ε*) / (1 + √ε*) with ε* the local complex permittivity. Assumptions: normal incidence, L point targets, AWGN, quasi-static target over the 102.4 µs chirp.

The frozen (Fable FV-003) 'operational epistemic twin' architecture contract defines a deterministic read-time composition law over evidence for capability states (motivated by the production incident where /nflverse OOM-500ed while /api/health said healthy). Composition law: (1) Node X = unavailable if own unavailable, or ANY hard dep composes unavailable; (2) else gated (with gate provenance chain) if own gated or any hard dep gated - intentional darkness propagates as intent, never as outage; (3) else unknown if own unknown or any hard dep unknown - ignorance is contagious through hard edges; (4) else degraded/stale (max rank; union of tags/reasons) if own or any hard dep carries rank 1, or any SOFT dep composes to ANY non-healthy state - including a soft dep that composes unknown (missing/expired evidence), which caps the dependent at degraded; soft dep contributes exactly one capped 'degraded' tag, its specific tag granularity never propagates; soft deps never gate, never unknown-ify, never disable; (5) else healthy. Three orthogonal axes: Severity healthy(0) · degraded(1) · stale(1) · unavailable(2) (degraded/stale share rank 1 as distinct tags - impairment vs freshness); Certainty evidenced · unknown (unknown is not a severity; a node can never be more certain than its least-certain required evidence); Intent open · proof_gated · owner_gated (founder-gated ≠ outage; modal provenance records WHICH gate). Evidence decay: every evidence ref carries observedAt + freshness horizon; past-horizon severity evidence decays to unknown automatically - gating does NOT decay (a gate stays gated even if not re-read). The 2026-09-28 deep read of the fantasy variance model (packages/prediction-engine/src/fantasy-variance.ts) built on production Neon player_game_stats (32,894 player-weeks) proves the posted McCaffrey spot-check (proj=417, floor=313, ceiling=584) is a label leak with an impossible band: Falsifier 1 (symmetry check) - band symmetric in CV by construction, so floor + ceiling = 2*proj must hold; posted 313+584 = 897 vs 2*417 = 834 - fails (midpoint 448.5, not 417); Falsifier 2 (CV split) - CV implied by floor = 1 - 313/417 = 0.2494, by ceiling = 584/417 - 1 = 0.4005, gap 0.1511 - no single CV produces the pair; label-leak proof - McCaffrey's realized 2025 PPR total = 416.6 over 17 games, posted 'projection' = round(416.6) = 417, a number a model fit on seasons < 2025 cannot emit. Fitted-as-specified projections for McCaffrey: 16 remaining games -> proj 233.5 / floor 116.1 / ceiling 350.9; 17 -> 248.0 / 123.3 / 372.8; 18 -> 262.6 / 130.6 / 394.7 - never reaches 417. Method: recency weight with 6-week half-life (exponential decay); Empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the positional mean via reliability = n/(n+8) applied to both rate and CV; band from shrunk CV: floor = proj*(1-CV), ceiling = proj*(1+CV).

PROVEN calibration path floors: Brier <= 0.22, ECE <= 0.05, settled n >= 100 (eligibility), independent coverage >= 40% to win bestScore, separation = mean p|win minus mean p|loss must be > 0, and GREEN streak needs K=3 consecutive green calibration runs; bestScore = argmax of Murphy RES among kinds with separation > 0, n >= 50, coverage >= 40%.

Murphy decomposition of the Brier score: REL = reliability (calibration error component, lower better); RES = resolution (ranking power, higher better). Isotonic and Platt maps cut REL only; RES stays flat - maps do NOT raise resolution.

CQR coverage defect quantified: the code rank = ceil((1 - alpha) * (n + 1)) - 1, clamped via Math.min(Math.max(rank, 0), n - 1); at n=5 and alpha=0.1 the clamp silently returns the largest score, so the function reports 90% coverage while delivering 83.33%. The fix is to return +Infinity below minN (pattern already in conformal-calibration.ts:174).

rankingP defect in ranking-prob.ts: rankingP = 0.7 * trueProb + 0.3 * (confidence / 100); when trueProb is missing or non-finite it falls back to confidence only, and confidence reaches the ordering three ways (30% weight always, entirely when trueProb absent, twice more as terminal fallback in sort-key.ts). Market-offset logistic head safety property: give the head a fixed offset term per row (coefficient pinned at 1, never penalized or updated); identity property - as lambda -> infinity, a head with the market logit as offset must reproduce the market probability exactly. This guarantees heads shrink toward the MARKET rather than the base rate (the naive code shrank toward the base rate).

An SRS variant takes each game's spread, adjusts for HFA (2.5 pts used), and iterates SRS to solve team ratings (transitive spreads).

HFA reference values: ~0.62 spread points (2021 market, per PFF); 2.5 pts used in the SRS variant. The notes' blend for Baldwin's Team Tiers chart is explicitly an inference, not his exact formula: predicted home margin = r_h - r_a + HFA; convert American odds to no-vig implied probabilities; de-vig futures within each market; jointly solve latent ratings to fit spread-implied margins plus futures-implied neutral-field win probability (via margin-to-win logistic). The weighting of game lines vs futures is unknown.
equation: predicted home margin = r_h − r_a + HFA

The bridge logistic-regression model was fit on 6,955 pre-2025 games (36 earlier games skipped for a missing prior feature) and scored on 285 sealed 2025 games, with all 285 emitting probabilities and none clamped. Its 2025 Brier against home wins is 0.2237, versus the spread-bucket table's 0.2120 on the same 285 games - the bridge loses by 0.0117 Brier points. The acceptance rule: any new model must beat both numbers on the same sealed set with leak-free priors and unclamped outputs.

Coefficient signs were discovered via homeSign (sign of each fitted coefficient), not hand-assigned: Dome and neutral came out negative (against home win probability), while scoring and rest features came out positive (favoring the team with the rest/scoring edge). The bridge is explicitly 'not a claim about a book'.

Team implied total derived from odds: team_implied_total = total/2 - signed_spread/2. This odds-derived game-script feature is flagged as a standard replicable input.

@SamHoppen 'How the game was won' (confirmed nflfastR feed, inferred categorization): single-game WPA/EPA decomposed into 10 mutually exclusive facets - Pass Off, Run Off, Pass Def, Run Def, Takeaways, Giveaways, Off Pen, Def Pen, Special Teams, Other. Sanity checks: total EPA additive over plays; WPA should telescope to approximately final WP minus initial WP if every play is assigned exactly once (each play's WPA = WP_after - WP_before from the team's perspective).

Creator rate formulas (inferred): motion_rate = motion-tagged eligible offensive plays / offensive plays; screen_rate and play_action_rate = screen/PA plays / relevant pass/dropback plays; no_huddle_rate = no-huddle snaps / offensive snaps; rpo_rate = RPO-tagged plays / charted offensive plays; under_center_rate = qualifying under-center offensive snaps / qualifying offensive snaps; under_center_epa_per_play = total EPA on qualifying under-center plays / count; target_share = player targets / team targets; tprr = targets / routes run; yprr = receiving yards / routes; first_read_share = first-read targets / team first-read targets.

PFF grading system (confirmed): every player/play graded -2 to +2 in 0.5 increments (0 = expected), position-specific rubrics, situational adjustment, converted to 0-100 facets. Inferred Shauncore denominators: pff_positive_grade_rate = count(grade > 0 on eligible QB pass plays) / eligible graded QB pass plays; pff_negative_grade_rate = count(grade < 0) / same denominator; zero-graded plays stay in the denominator but in neither numerator.

Speed estimation chain from All-22 screenshots: per-screenshot yard calibration from full-field white-line spacing (worked example: 5 yards ≈ 410 units, so 1 yard ≈ 82 units); Euclidean distance d(p,q) = sqrt((q1-p1)^2 + (q2-p2)^2); worked example (DeSean Jackson): 215.5 units / 0.2 s x (1 yd / 82 units) = 12.8 yd/s = 26.2 mph. The authors explicitly note this reads high vs Next Gen Stats, so use only for relative comparisons (Jackson 22.4 mph vs Maurice Harris 19.3 mph in the first 0.6 s off the line). The paper never smooths trajectories - improvement path: Savitzky-Golay or Kalman before differencing.
equation: 215.5 units / 0.2 s × (1 yd / 82 units) = 12.8 yd/s = 26.2 mph

claim: Formation classification from jersey-color coordinate features (Sloan 2018): Level 1 (QB position) - CART 86.5%, Naive Bayes 67.5%, SVM 56.1%, k-NN 49.8%, Logistic Regression 42.9%; CART report: Center P 0.82 / R 0.92, Shotgun 0.90 / 0.84, Pistol 0.50 / 0.12 (Pistol starved of training data). A tuned CART beat SVM/k-NN/LR at both levels on this small coordinate-feature dataset - cheap classical baselines can precede learned models.

Camera-follow drift correction: save the frame-1 highest point of a full white line as a reference anchor and adjust later frames against it. LOS standardized to a 1-99 scale (own 1 = 1, through opponent's 20 = 80). Stage 1 geometric standardization: Hough line transform over screenshots, heuristic filter keeps long full-field white yard lines, LOS = yard line nearest the offensive line, camera rotation from LOS direction and its perpendicular via an arccosine formulation.

Worked coach-tendency and scheme-tendency mining: McVay 2015 was ~60% more likely to run on 1st-&-6+ on his own half with 2+ minutes left; Singleback Ace Pair Slot splits - 65% of runs right, 81% of passes short, 4.6 yds/pass vs 2.5 yds/run. Throughput: formations for a full game (~50 offensive plays) in under 5 minutes.

Author-stated limitations: small training set; jersey-color RGB fragile to shadows/sunlight; no RFID ground truth (data not publicly released due to NFL rights - the method is replicable only on GSE's own footage).

The 1891 brief is a historical placeholder/pointer on catastrophic forgetting in neural networks (McCloskey & Cohen 1989; Ratcliff 1990): sequential training overwrites prior task weights - the foundational motivation for EWC and continual-learning methods covered in the companion briefs.
