ViViT-B 16x2 fine-tuned with focal loss L_FL = -(1-p_y)^gamma log(p_y), gamma = 1.6, alpha_risky = 0.6 / alpha_safe = 0.4, detects risky head-first spearing tackles in football practice video: best config (photometric-only augmentation, Run15) reached risky-class recall 0.67, risky F1 0.59, accuracy 0.67 on 733 dummy-tackle clips.

The ViViT tokenization and layer equations used: z_0 = [x_cls; E p_1; ...; E p_N] + E_pos; z'_l = MSA(LN(z_{l-1})) + z_{l-1}; z_l = FFN(LN(z'_l)) + z'_l; Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V with d_k = 64. A Taguchi L18 design reduced 54 augmentation combos to 18 runs, applied post-split only to training folds of the minority class.

The new model gained +8.4 pp risky recall over the prior C3D baseline (0.67 vs 0.583) at a cost of -9.9 pp safe recall; duplication-only rebalancing reached only 0.54 risky recall, and geometric perturbations (rotations/flips) hurt because spatial body-configuration cues are the safety signal. Limitations: dummy tackles not live tackles, FPOC manually marked, risky recall 0.67 means ~1 in 3 dangerous tackles missed.

XGBoost on 12 weeks of pre-season Fitbit data predicted collegiate volleyball players' season hit% binarized at 0.2 (coach threshold): best phase combination (55 days) reached accuracy 0.8645, F1 0.7549, AUROC 0.8236; Phase 3 alone (9 days) collapsed to F1 0.2273. Top features by F-test: HRV (F=86.279), breathing rate (F=60.780), total sedentary time (F=46.942).

The dossier's verdict is REJECT: N=14 with only 3 positives, F1=0.75 rests on SMOTE synthesized from n=3 real minority subjects, feature-selection timing relative to LOSO folds is unstated, and physiology signs are counterintuitive (poor performers had higher sleep efficiency, 92.5 vs 82.6) — a cautionary case study in reproducibility traps.

GATv2-TCN predicts next-game-day player performance on dynamic per-game-day complete graphs of players (both teams, >=10 minutes): GATv2 attention e(g_i,g_j) = a^T LeakyReLU(W[g_i||g_j]), alpha_ij = softmax over neighborhood, h_i = sigma(sum_j alpha_ij W g_j) with 4 heads and 32-dim output, followed by temporal convolution over t0=10 prior representations.

On 691 NBA games (2022-10-18 to 2023-01-20, 582 players): GATv2-TCN RMSE 2.222, MAE 1.642, MAPE 0.513, CORR 0.508 — best RMSE/MAE/CORR vs ASTGCN (2.293/1.699/0.455/0.453), TCN, DeepVAR, N-BEATS; no CIs or significance tests stated. Spectral GNNs (GCN/ChebyConv) fail on these cluster graphs because of block-diagonal Laplacians with repeated eigenvalues — the paper's justification for GATv2.

The paper's 59-wager Underdog Fantasy case study (35/59 correct, 59.3% hit rate) is a single day with no walk-forward, no ROI, and no vig accounting — flagged by the dossier as a textbook anecdotal profitability claim; target ambiguity: 13 stats collected but the final output dim is stated as 6 with the exact 6 predicted metrics unstated.

The Conway-Maxwell-Poisson pmf p(x|lambda,nu) = lambda^x / ((x!)^nu Z(lambda,nu)) generalizes Poisson: nu<1 gives overdispersion, nu>1 underdispersion, nu=1 recovers Poisson. The modified Sarmanov joint (eq. 8) is f(x_1,...,x_d) = {prod f_i(x_i)}{1 + C(d,2)^-1 sum_{j<k} delta_{jk} phi_j(x_j) phi_k(x_k)} with exponential kernel phi_i(x) = e^{-omega x} - Psi_i.

Applied to Premier League 2018-2021 (1,140 matches): home advantage exp(gamma_1) posterior mean 1.249 (95% CI 1.055-1.455, ~25% home goal surplus with crowds) vs 1.146 without crowds, P(gamma_2<0) = 0.97; dispersion nu_1 = 0.818 +/- 0.063, nu_2 = 0.756 +/- 0.065 (overdispersed); delta = -1.767 +/- 0.355 with 99% CI excluding 0 (negative home-away goal dependence, empirical corr -0.162).

PSIS-LOO could not decisively choose the COM-Poisson model over plain Poisson (6917.2 +/- 32.6 vs 6938.4 +/- 71.6); the paper uses full-sample fit plus PSIS-LOO with no train/test split and ignores team strength — flagged as the failure mode to avoid when porting the distributional construction to joint NFL low-count event modeling (explosive plays, red-zone trips).

Merritt & Clauset (2013) on 1,279,901 scoring events across 40,813 games: NFL scoring tempo is memoryless — inter-arrival correlation C(n) = (sum_k (t_k - <t>)(t_{k+n} - <t>)) / sum_k (t_k - <t>)^2 is ~0 at all lags in all four sports — and NFL tempo MLE is lambda-hat = 0.00204/s, i.e. 7.34 events/game with 490.2 s/event.

The lead-size-conditioned scoring Markov chain: P_{L,L+k} = Pr(r scores | L) * Pr(point value = k); P_{L,L-k} = (1 - Pr(r scores | L)) * Pr(point value = k); prediction = P^n * S_0 summed over L>0 (r wins). Lead-size scoring slopes: CFB +0.005 probability per point of lead, NFL +0.002 per point (CFB effect ~2.5x NFL); NBA is negative (restoring force).
equation: P_{L,L+k} = Pr(r scores | L) * Pr(point value = k)

claim: Winner-prediction AUC: CFB/NFL exceed 60% after one scoring event and 80% by three events; the Markov chain beats the leader-wins heuristic in all sports and was ~10% more accurate than SBR moneylines after 20% of events (small non-systematic sample, caveated). Three-phase tempo: early dip, middle stable/Poisson, end-of-period sharp spike (NHL end-game rate exceeds 3x the game mean, attributed to pulled goalies).

CS:GO win-probability-added per action: V(a(i,t)) = Y-hat(i,t+1) - Y-hat(i,t) in [-1,1], normalized to the acting player's team (the damaged player gets -V); player WPA = sum over rounds. XGBoost WP model (100 estimators) beat CatBoost and logistic regression on a time-ordered split: log loss 0.5353, Brier 0.1842, AUC 0.7913.

Metric evaluation battery (Franks et al.): stability = month-to-month correlation, independence = correlation with KDR, discrimination = top-10 rankings. On n=479 players: WPA stability 0.40 / KDR-independence 0.73; WPA was significantly more stable than ADR (p=0.0029), KAST% (p=0.0392), Rating 2.0 (p=0.0268) but NOT significantly more stable than KDR (p=0.3594) — the paper overclaims on that comparison.

Feature importance ranked team equipment value first, then HP remaining on both sides; bootstrap (100 resamples of each player's rounds) gave mean-WPA/round SDs of 0.0038-0.0041; a ZywOo headshot in a 1-vs-2 with 13 HP produced +67% win probability. Limitations: only damage events credited, adjacent ticks are near-duplicates, no team-strength control.

Component-wise MLP neural Granger causality: h_1(t) = sigma(sum_{k=1..K} W_1^k x_{t-k} + b_1); x_{t,i} = W_L h_{L-1}(t) + b_L + e_{t,i}; objective min_W sum_{t=K+1..T}(x_{t,i} - g_i(x_{(t-1):(t-K)}))^2 + lambda sum_j Omega(W_{:j}^1) with group sparse group lasso Omega on first-layer weights per input series; Granger strength is read off first-layer weight magnitudes.
equation: min_W sum_{t=K+1..T}(x_{t,i} - g_i(x_{(t-1):(t-K)}))^2 + lambda sum_j Omega(W_{:j}^1)

claim: On 16 pitcher-batter pairs (27-joint mocap): share of total causality ngc_pp ~49% (pitcher internal), ngc_bb ~31% (batter internal), ngc_pb ~19% (pitcher->batter), ngc_bp ~1% (batter->pitcher); asymmetry ngc_pb/(ngc_bb + ngc_pb) = 0.38, i.e. ~38% of batter movement is generated from pitcher movement. Lag indices: l_pp = 0.13 +/- 0.01 s, l_bb = 0.07 +/- 0.04 s, l_pb = 0.49 +/- 0.06 s (matches ~0.50 s ball travel time at 76.8 mph).

MANOVA on in-field rate: F(1,14) = 10.9, p < .01, eta^2 = 0.60; follow-ups: ngc_pp F=9.4, p<.01, eta^2=0.40; ngc_bp F=32.1, p<.01, eta^2=0.69 despite being ~1% of total causality (flagged as likely anticipatory movement, not genuine influence). Sensitivity warning: hyperparameter tuning targets a chosen variable-usage-rate band (0.25-0.50), making detected-link density substantially a tuning artifact.

Weighted dynamic prior (eq. 10): beta^att_{i,tau} | beta^att_{i,tau-1}, phi_att,tau ~ N(beta^att_{i,tau-1}, 1/phi_att,tau) — period- and type-specific commensurate priors that adaptively control how much attack/defence strength information is borrowed from the previous half-season. Spike-and-slab hyperprior (eq. 11): phi_{k,tau} ~ N^+(100,0.1)(1-p_l) + N^+(0,5) p_l with p_l = 0.99 fixed (spike at 100 = borrow everything, slab = forget).

On Bundesliga/EPL/La Liga 2020/21-2024/25 with six goal-count likelihoods: weighted dynamic consistently beats Owen (2011) and Egidi baselines but gains are modest (Brier deltas ~0.002-0.02; e.g. Bundesliga bivariate-Poisson last-3-rounds Brier 0.678 vs 0.683 vs 0.687). It converges 32-55% faster than the baselines (R-hat ~1.00, bulk ESS 3000-5000). No betting simulation, no covariates, no ROI analysis.

Clegg & Cartlidge's replication of the WikiBuzz tennis mispricing study confirmed the regression (WikiBuzz beta-hat_3 = 0.009 +/- 0.004) but showed most Bet365 profits came from one erroneous 5.50 quote (true market max 2.10): removing the Hercog bet flipped PM ROI from 17.29% to -7.36% and absolute return from 1.24 to -0.50. Kelly staking used was f*_ij = max(p~-ij - (1-p~-ij)/b_ij, 0) with bankroll reset to 1 per bet.

The one surviving strategy (competitive matches, model probability in [0.4,0.6], no RankDist) kept ROI 29.38% -> 12.44% after removal (263 bets, overround 7.01%, p_bs = 0.002 via the Wunderlich-Memmert 100,000-trial random-betting bootstrap), but the edge died after Feb 2020: re-estimated Feb 2020-Aug 2023 (13,913 player-matches), WikiBuzz beta-hat_3 = 0.001 (0.004), p = 0.837 — both insignificant.

Three operational QA rules adopted from the paper: (1) an odds-sanity filter (drop/flag book quotes above cross-book best by >3 SD of the best-minus-mean spread, plus z-score consensus outliers) before backtest data is written; (2) the 100k random-betting bootstrap as a mandatory significance screen (never publish a strategy with p_bs > 0.05); (3) cap fractional Kelly at <=0.25x full Kelly — full Kelly amplified one bad data row into 39.3% of bankroll on a single 5.50 quote.

The dossier's verdict on Gasteratos et al. (2024, arXiv:2412.12990v2) is REJECT: the perspective piece on human action recognition contains no experiments, datasets, models, equations, or quantitative results — only qualitative descriptions of technique families (two-stream CNNs, 3D CNNs, transformers, event cameras, synthetic data, RL) — so there is nothing implementable to extract.

Tahir/Egidi/Torelli (2026) model EPL 2015/16 through shot-level logistic xG: logit(p) = beta_0 + sum beta_j X_j, p-hat_i = 1/(1+exp(-eta_i)), with xG_team,match = sum p_i over team shots. Three GLM variants compared by AIC: Base 5354.47, Interaction 5357.31, Granular 5261.82 (delta-AIC >= 90 favors granular). Team strengths = first-half per-match xG rates normalized by league means; second half simulated as Poisson matches, 1,000 simulations.

Mid-season ex-ante title probabilities: Arsenal 49.0%, Man City 26.6%, Tottenham 5.4%, Leicester 16.7% (avg simulated rank 3.12, P(top 4) > 80%); Leicester was the largest positive outlier vs simulated mean but still in the upper tail, ranked 4th in mid-season xG while leading on points. Full-season fit: Spearman rho 0.837 (points), R^2 0.758, RMSE 7.624 points; the paper's own critique: Poisson small-sample exaggerates extremes and there is no holdout for the xG model.

Rugby penalty-kick decision framework: EPlineout = beta-hat_0 + beta-hat_1*meter_line + beta-hat_2*Card_Diff + beta-hat_3*WinPct_Diff (linear regression on next-score value); P(make | d, theta) = logit^-1{beta_0 + f(d,theta)} (2D GAM spline in distance and angle); EPkick(d,theta) = Pmake*3 + (1-Pmake)*EPmiss(d,theta); the indifference frontier is traced by DeltaEP(x,y;dtouch) = EPlineout(xLO) - EPkick(x,y) = 0, with regret R = EPoptimal - EPactual.

Fitted lineout EP regression: intercept 3.2545 (SE 0.2093, p<2e-16), meter_line -0.0586 (SE 0.0044), Card_Diff 0.8802 (SE 0.3052, p=0.00397), WinPct_Diff 0.6503 (SE 0.3430, p=0.058). Case study (13 NZ vs South Africa decisions): total regret R = 1.39 points, proportion optimal decisions 0.46; most wrong decisions sat near the indifference frontier. Authors' own critique: EP is not win probability, and there is no held-out validation of either surface.

V3 video super-resolution: basis B_i(x,y,t) = a_i sin(omega_i.(x,y,t) + phi_i); reconstruction V-hat(x,y,t) = sum_i B_i; anti-aliasing scale xi(omega_i,sigma) = exp(-||omega_i||^2/(8 pi^2 sigma^2)). Trained on Adobe240 with random continuous spatial scales U(1.2,4); V3 (13.7M params) hit Vid4 26.76/0.818 PSNR/SSIM and GoPro Center 32.93/0.922; V3-Large (20.6M) reached 33.09/0.925.

Limitations acknowledged: regression oversmoothing (fine detail hallucinated as smooth), only bicubic-downsampling degradation tested (real broadcast H.264 artifacts, interlacing, motion blur untested), no per-pixel uncertainty, 1.27 s/clip not real-time. The dossier's hard rule: synthetic detail must never be treated as measured tracking data — enhanced frames quarantined from measurement pipelines.

TOTNet ball tracking uses a visibility-weighted loss L = w_v * (BCE(P_x, T_x) + BCE(P_y, T_y)) over visibility levels v in {0,1,2,3}, with fully-occluded frames getting normalized Gaussian targets T_x[j] = (1/Z_x) exp(-(j-T_x)^2/(2 sigma^2)) instead of one-hot heatmaps. On the new occlusion-rich TTA table-tennis set, fully-occluded RMSE fell 37.30 (prev SOTA WASB) -> 12.31 (TOTNet) -> 7.19 (optical-flow variant).

Ablation on TTA full-occ RMSE: baseline 29.57 -> +WBCE 24.43 -> +augmentation alone 54.26 (augmentation alone hurts) -> WBCE+aug 12.31 -> +optical flow 7.19. Caveats: the visibility weights w_v and sigma are unreported (loss not reproducible from paper), baselines are author re-implementations, tennis full-occ test is n=5, and TOTNet is heavier and slower than WASB (8.65M params / 28.08 FPS vs 1.48M / 33.44 FPS).

Chen Jia Wei's tennis-doubles dissertation pipeline: standardized annotation taxonomy + React/Flask annotation tool + transfer-learned classifiers. Pose-GCN propagation: H^(l+1) = sigma(D^(-1/2) A D^(-1/2) H^(l) W^(l)) on a 17-node skeleton graph. Detection stack: GroundingDINO zero-shot phrase grounding -> YOLO-Pose per box, fine-tuned on 10-30 annotated frames per player.

Tracking accuracy (NCAA 952-frame rally): only GroundingDINO+YOLO-Pose achieved identity support (P1 100%/P2 100%/P3 69.8%/P4 64.3%, 1436 s) vs YOLOv11+DeepSORT (P4 0.1%) and Florence-2 Large (P4 0.0%). Classification: formation Double-Image CNN accuracy 94.28%/87.57% (AUC 99.25%/96.92%) on pro/NCAA; pose-GCNs trained from scratch mostly underperform (serve-vs-nonserve GCN AUC 42.72%/57.22%, worse than random on pro) — the paper's conclusion is that transfer-learned CNNs beat from-scratch GCNs on tiny data.

Feiz et al. (2025) four-stage multi-person 3D pose pipeline: confidence-weighted triangulation [mu_1(P_11-u_1 P_31); ...] [x,y,z,1]^T = 0 with mu_j = mean detection confidence of camera j (SVD solve), then SMPL kinematic optimization, then multi-person physics-based iLQR trajectory optimization with objective min_u sum_t w_1 L_reg + w_2 L_p + w_3 L_v + w_4 L_collision, weights (0.001, 10, 0.1, 20).
equation: min_u sum_t w_1 L_reg + w_2 L_p + w_3 L_v + w_4 L_collision

claim: Physics refinement gains: e_MPJPE 41.2 -> 38.4, foot-height error 16.4 -> 8.1, foot-planar-velocity error 2.2 -> 0.3; CHI3D penetration 114.9 -> 18.7. Limitations: requires calibrated cameras (NFL broadcast cameras lack calibration), four-stage + iLQR far from real-time, physics metrics partly self-referential, and the Hi4D extreme-interaction case was worse than baselines (penetration 67.2 vs 51.1/39.8) due to coarse convex-hull collision geometry.

Lai et al. (2024): a fine-tuned VideoMAE ViT (16 frames, 224x224, lr 5e-5, 10 epochs) on raw video reached 90% accuracy on fine-grained fencing actions (95% CI [0.8812, 0.9187]; per-class F1 0.84-0.98) and 83.25% on boxing punch types, vs 64.8% for a pose-estimation-based baseline on fencing. Preprocessing equations only: X_sub = {x_i | i = k*T/N}; X_std = (X-mu)/sigma.

Caveats: -5 pp accuracy on home (non-competition) videos (domain shift on quality/lighting/occlusion — exactly broadcast-film conditions); split ratios unstated with no bout-level de-duplication stated (near-duplicate frames could inflate accuracy); conflicting annotations systematically excluded (selection bias); assumes pre-clipped single-action inputs with no detection/localization stage. New public FACTS fencing dataset: 6,400 clips across 8 labels.

Prakash et al. (2024) NHL broadcast tracking-by-detection: each frame is a bipartite graph with nodes combining 512-D OSNet appearance embeddings and homography-projected footpoints p_i = H_i(f_l, f_r) (bottom-mid of bbox via 3x3 homography), edges Delta r^id_ij = [L1 distance, cosine similarity] and Delta p_ij = [L1, L2]; a 6-layer message-passing network predicts frame-to-frame identity links with sigmoid focal loss summed over L iterations; inference prunes edges below xi = 0.9.

Broadcast test with ground-truth detections: IDsw 1056 -> 151 and IDF1 71.8% -> 95.1% vs the Hockey MOT baseline; but with real Faster R-CNN detections the IDsw gain evaporates (453 vs 431), keeping only the IDF1 edge (71.3% vs 62.9%). Ablation: adding homography cut video-5 IDsw 53 -> 13; MPN depth sweep overfits sharply beyond L=6 (L=14: 388 IDsw / 43.3 IDF1).

Pelechrinis & Goldsberry (2021) on 750 games of 2016-17 NBA tracking data: corner threes hit 38.8% vs 34.7% above-the-break (4.1 pp gap, ~12 pts/100 shots); a distance-only logistic model predicts only ~1.8 pp of the gap — distance explains less than half. Trajectory clustering: k-means on 4-s pre-shot (x,y) shooter+defender trajectories (25 Hz), 10 clusters via the gap statistic, cluster coherence via radius of gyration r_C = sqrt((1/||C||)*sum(x_i-x_C)^2).

Mechanism evidence: >90% of corner 3s are assisted vs just above 70% for above-the-break; a FIBA natural experiment (three-point-line geometry difference only 28% of NBA's) still shows a 16 pts/100-shots gap, supporting assist-generated openness over geometry. Nash equilibrium of the commit-vs-help defensive game: expected equilibrium distance d-hat ~= 13 ft vs observed 12.3 ft — means match but shapes differ (bimodal mixed strategy vs empirical normal-like), evidence defenses deviate from equilibrium.

An LSTM RNN (2 stacked layers, 64 hidden units/layer, peephole connections, dropout 0.6, Adam lr 0.005) on raw 0.5-second SportVu ball trajectories (X, Y, Z + game clock, 25 Hz, 12 timesteps) classifies NBA three-point attempts as make/miss and beats static feature-engineered classifiers (elastic-net GLM, GBM) at every distance except 2 feet from the basket, on >20,000 attempts from 631 games of 2015-16.

AUC by distance (RNN vs GBM vs GLM): 2 ft 0.93/0.942/0.875; 4 ft 0.906/0.848/0.848->GLM collapses; 8 ft 0.843/0.719/0.558 — the RNN holds up far from the basket while the GLM collapses to near-random. Limitations per the file: 80/20 random split (no chronological or player holdout), deliberately unoptimized baselines, shooter/defender context ignored.

The dossier's verdict on the hockey momentum-causality pipeline (logistic event weights -> XGBoost xG -> 32-dim event embeddings + single-layer 50-unit LSTM -> PCA + K-means momentum chains -> X-Learner ATE) is REJECT for the causal claim: the treatment is defined from a composite score that includes the outcome model (circularity), overlapping 30-second windows violate independence, random splits leak same-game sequences, and the data are proprietary and unverifiable.

Reported numbers (kept only as the salvageable architecture reference): XGBoost xG test accuracy 71.2%, AUC 0.85, precision 0.36, recall 0.42 at ~2% goal base rate; LSTM val accuracy 82.6%; X-Learner ATE 0.10688 with 95% CI 0.05002-0.17436 and p-value 1.43e-52 — flagged by the dossier as a dependence-ignored artifact, not strength. Only the sequence-embedding architecture is salvageable, as a predictive drive-momentum feature, never a causal claim.

Per-team Markov Decision Processes over soccer possessions (375 states: 22x17 offensive-half grid + defensive-half + 3 absorbing): P(s,a,s') = Pr[S_{t+1}=s'|S_t=s,A_t=a]; pi(shoot|s) = c_s^shot/c_s by counts; E[goals|pi] = sum_s E[shots in s|pi]*P(s,shoot,s_goal) with expected visits from the fundamental matrix N = (I-Q)^-1. The dossier's verdict is REJECT for GSE — soccer shot policy has no NFL transfer path and the Markov counterfactual machinery duplicates existing 4th-down literature.

Substantive results: model fit MAE of state values vs empirical in [0.013, 0.015] across 17 teams; season-goals estimate avg relative error 11.38%; high-volume long-distance shooters converted 6.5% on 416 long shots vs 2.1% goal rate on 4,455 non-shooting touches in the zone; long-distance shots declined ~20%/season from 2013/14 to 2018/19; a targeted 10% increase in long-distance shooting yields ~+0.5 goals/season (worked example: +1 goal would have kept Bournemouth up in 2019/20).

LEAP replaces a monolithic LLM forecast with per-evidence-item isolated LLM calls emitting likelihood parameters, combined via a deterministic tempered conjugate-Bayesian update: posterior P(theta|E) proportional to P0(theta) prod_{i in R} Pi(ei|theta); continuous update tau_post = tau0 + eta*sum tau_i, mu_post = (mu0*tau0 + eta*sum mu_i*tau_i)/tau_post; single-choice log pi_post(k) proportional to alpha log pi0(k) + eta*sum w_i log L_i(k); per-item LOO auditability via Delta_j = mu_post - mu_post^(-j).
equation: tau_post = tau0 + eta*sum tau_i; mu_post = (mu0*tau0 + eta*sum mu_i*tau_i)/tau_post

claim: On 347 constructed forecasting tasks across 5 base models: FutureX gains monolithic->LEAP of DeepSeek-V3.2 0.4895->0.6701, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite 0.6004->0.7069, Grok-4.20-Fast 0.6533->0.7503; external frameworks macro-average Brier -16.5 (0.4806->0.3157); calibration on GPT-5.4-mini halved (ECE 0.1840->0.0876, overconfidence 0.3167->0.1500). Ablation: removing the prior drops FutureX below monolithic (0.6427 vs 0.6512) — the prior is the load-bearing component. Cost: 11,508 tokens/task vs 5,733; median latency 10.4s vs 6.2s.

The finite-sample conformal coverage guarantee P_{Y,X,D_cal}(Y in C_M(X;D_cal)) >= 1-alpha (eq. 1) is marginal over calibration sets, so in the realistic single-calibration deployment workflow small calibration sets can yield conditional coverage far below nominal with high probability. Empirical protocol (split conformal, alpha=0.1): with m=10, 19% of calibration sets deliver <85% conditional coverage vs nominal 90%; at m=200 the shortfall essentially disappears. The Vovk-2012 conditional bound is vacuous at small m.

The critique does not hold for learn-then-test (Angelopoulos 2025), PAC confidence sets (Park 2019), or risk-controlling prediction sets (Bates 2021); exchangeability is assumed and distribution shift is untreated. The dossier verdict is ADAPT as QC for conformal/CQR calibration: GSE's calibration windows are inherently small (weekly slates, short seasons), exactly the regime where marginal guarantees mislead — add a conditional-coverage audit with a minimum-m sizing rule from the Vovk bound.

The proposed Balance score g(q;p) satisfies |g(q;p)| = |q-p| (Eq. 11), so |average Balance| approximates true ECE ONLY if sign(q-p) is constant over the whole range — the dossier's verdict is REJECT because signed errors cancel across oppositely miscalibrated regions: a model +5% miscalibrated on favorites and -5% on underdogs scores ~0 on Balance, the failure mode ECE's absolute value was designed to avoid.

The paper's legitimate complaint stands: ECE with bins M in [5,100] can reverse the ranking of two overconfident models while |Balance| preserves it, and |Balance| approaches true ECE with far fewer samples than ECE (which needs >500 samples). But the Balance score is not a proper scoring rule. At most adopt a one-line signed mean (predicted - empirical) per calibration slice as a supplemental diagnostic next to existing ECE/LRD dashboards.

Under sublinear-expectation theory with simultaneous mean-shift (eta) and variance-regime (G-normal) uncertainty, infinite-family min-max/min-min optima collapse to two classical normal LSEs; the practical moving-block estimator scans overlapping blocks B_l, fits OLS per block, takes coefficients from the min-MSE block (k-hat = argmin_l sigma-hat_l^2, beta-hat = beta-hat_{k-hat}) and min/max block-mean/variance as uncertainty bounds (mu-hat_low = min_l mu-tilde_l, mu-hat_bar = max_l mu-tilde_l) — strongly consistent and robust to contamination.

Contamination benchmark (T=200) MSE of beta-hat: scenario 1 — MM 0.0205, LSE 0.2075, R-LSE 0.0228; scenario 6 (50% contamination) — MM 1.6230 (breakdown), LSE 0.7033, R-LSE 0.1667. S&P 500 AR(1) real data: R-LSE F significant at 1% in 18/20 rolling years vs LSE in 1/20 (e.g. 201607-201707: R-LSE R^2 0.3269/F 59.98 vs LSE R^2 0.0311/F 3.97). Caveat: block length must satisfy n<n0 with unknown n0, and an NFL team-season T (~17) is underpowered — pool across teams/plays.

The Biometrika theory paper proves assumptionless finite-sample oracle inequalities in KL divergence for maximum regularized likelihood estimators Lambda-hat in argmin_{Lambda in L}{-log f_Lambda(X) + r*u(Lambda)} (eq. 1) for any definite positively-homogeneous regularizer (l_q including non-convex q in (0,1), nuclear norm) with no sparsity/restricted-eigenvalue assumptions: d(Lambda-hat) <= r*u(Lambda*) + r*u(-Lambda*). Lasso specialization gives a penalty bound sqrt(log p/n)*||beta*||_1 (1/sqrt(n) rate, optimal sans further assumptions). The dossier verdict is REJECT — pure math with no data, no simulations, and no implementable sports application.

The T-score symmetrized ratio T(a,b) = (2-b/a)1{a>=b} + (a/b)1{b>a} maps discrete basketball scores to a continuous dominance measure; modeling its in-game evolution as a Brownian T-process yields a closed-form real-time win probability PW_t = 1 - Phi((c-T_*(t,a,b))/sqrt((1-t)(tau^2+sigma^2))) with tau^2 = sum alpha_i^2 (eq. 5.2), and sensitivity dPW_t/dS_i = phi(.)*alpha_i/sqrt((1-t)(tau^2+sigma^2)) (eq. 5.3).

Intervals on Fire (IoF): the union of intervals where Delta_mT/Delta > delta (delta = fourth-largest per-game rate of change); X-index X_delta^{k,j} = player court time during IoF; STATS X = h(X) with h(x) = delta*x. Player-eval example (Chiba Jets playoff loss): PCS top Togashi 0.2091, STATS X top Edwards 0.059 (PCS only 0.0858) — rank orders differ across PCS/PTS/EFF/PER, i.e. total statistical output differs from dynamic contribution.

The dossier flags: no WP accuracy metric anywhere (no Brier, no calibration curve, no baseline); the T_* anchor is explicitly ad hoc; delta is arbitrary per game; the TFS-vs-win-rate correlation rho=0.989 is in-sample circular (alpha_0 fitted on the same outcomes). Adoption gate proposed: adapt the Brownian closed-form WP to drive-aggregated nflverse data only if holdout Brier is within 0.0005 of the nfl4th grid on 2023-2024, calibrated in all deciles.

Made and missed NBA field-goal locations for three players are jointly modeled as two correlated log-Gaussian Cox processes sharing a spatial baseline: log lambda_j(s; z_i) = alpha_0(s) + z_i^T beta_j(s), j=1 (made), 2 (missed), with spatially varying coefficient surfaces beta_j on a Karhunen-Loeve-truncated GP prior (L=15 components, retained variance >0.8; kernel hyperparams a=0.25, b=1.5; inverse-Gamma(5,5) variance priors; 15,000 MCMC iterations, 10,000 burn-in via MALA + Gibbs).
equation: log lambda_j(s; z_i) = alpha_0(s) + z_i^T beta_j(s)

claim: JSVLGCP attained the lowest negative posterior log-likelihood for LeBron and Jordan (comparable to best for Curry; exact NPLL values not printed — the headline claim rests on figures). Limitations: only 2 binary covariates (home/away, opponent strength), conditional independence of shots given the field ignores hot-hand structure, and the NFL analog is sparser (~100-150 targets/player/season) with public nflverse lacking full 2D receiver coordinates.

Phelan & Whelan (2017) hierarchical Bayesian Bradley-Terry for MLB team strength: sigma ~ Gamma(2N, 2N/sigma-hat^2); lambda|sigma ~ N(0,sigma^2 I); V|lambda ~ Bradley-Terry(exp{lambda}) (Eq. 22), where sigma-hat^2 is the previous season's estimated log-strength variance via the MAP approximation sigma-hat = sqrt(sum lambda-hat_i^2/N) (Eq. 18). Prediction via posterior predictive p(V-tilde|V) = integral p(V-tilde|lambda)p(lambda|V) dlambda (Eq. 23).

2017 mean absolute rest-of-season win error, Bayes vs MLE: Apr 15 — 8.82 (6.58) vs 24.65 (17.34); May 1 — 7.31 (6.17) vs 12.49 (10.39); Jun 1 — 4.72 (4.87) vs 6.90 (4.27); tied by Sep 15 (1.75 vs 1.83). Averaged 2011-2017, Bayes matches or beats MLE for the entire season in both error and variability. The Bayesian ranking shrinks toward actual records and avoids MLE's 0/1/undetermined probability pathologies.

SoccerGuard runs a 90-scenario grid (3/5/7-session input windows x 1/3/7-day output horizons x imbalance treatments x 5 models: logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, SVC, LSTM) on the public SoccerMon dataset (4,448 data points, 37 players, 43 injury points, ~1% event rate). Example scenario I-58 (random forest): precision 0.623 but TPR 0.014, F1 0.027, AUC 0.618 — high precision while catching only 1.4% of injuries.

Headline findings: 5-session input improves F1 by 40.91% vs 3-session input; 7-day output horizon improves F1 by 336.36% vs 1-day horizon. The file flags serious flaws: 43 injury events spread over 90 scenarios x 45 Monte Carlo rounds (multiple-comparison minefield), Monte Carlo random splits on longitudinal data leak future sessions into training, and no hyperparameter tuning — precision-without-TPR reporting on rare events is treated as noise-mined until re-validated.

Wang & Pleimling (2019) on pure-chance online gambling logs (roulette, crash, dice, jackpot; 0.3M-19.2M bet logs per dataset): wager sizes are log-normally distributed at aggregate (e.g. Crash C1 mu=1.647/sigma=2.226), gamblers predominantly use negative progression — after a loss they most often increase wagers (dataset F: 0.560 increase vs 0.061 decrease), after a win more likely to decrease — and player-selected odds follow a truncated shifted power-law with exponents below 2 (Coinroll alpha=1.423), i.e. gamblers overweight low-probability win chances.

The dossier's verdict is REJECT: the paper is descriptive statistical physics only — no predictive model, no holdout, data available only from the authors on request, and zero transferability to NFL sports betting. The wager-size CCDF log-normal fit uses P(x) = [Phi((ln(x+1)-mu)/sigma) - Phi((ln(x)-mu)/sigma)] / [1 - Phi((ln(x_min)-mu)/sigma)] with x_min via KS-distance minimization and model selection by Akaike weights.

Zech & Wood (2013) infer time-varying discrete-state offensive/defensive team strengths from soccer scorelines with a Markov Random Field trained by EM + loopy belief propagation: EM objective Q(theta,theta^old) = sum_Z P(Z|X,theta^old) ln P(X,Z|theta) (Eq. 1), with BP message reordering reducing cost to O(NK^2) (Eq. 2). Emissions are freely parameterized discrete conditionals (not assumed Poisson) — discovered distributions deviate from Poisson notably on 0/1 goals.

The paper's own rolling out-of-sample test (EPL 2005-2012, cumulative net log-likelihood) shows the model substantially beats a naive constant-rate baseline but UNDERPERFORMS both Elo and William Hill implied probabilities — stated explicitly — and 8 identical-training runs converge to different optima (non-convexity). The dossier's verdict is REJECT: loses to Elo on its own benchmark; the authors concede a continuous-state extension is needed, which the corpus already covers.

Pitcan (2026) tests whether a structural Dixon-Coles football model adds information beyond the de-vigged closing price in Serie A (7,220 matches, 19 seasons): the fitted logarithmic-opinion-pool weight is w-hat = 0.000 on validation (p^{(w)}_i proportional to (p^M_i)^{1-w}(p^S_i)^w, Eq. 8), with log loss monotone increasing in w on [0,1] on both validation and test — a genuine boundary solution, i.e. the model adds nothing beyond the market.

Head-to-head (n=2,660): market (Shin de-vigged) RPS 0.1905 [0.1856, 0.1957], log-loss 0.9620, accuracy 54.8% vs Dixon-Coles RPS 0.1972, log-loss 0.9858, accuracy 53.4%; paired RPS difference market-minus-model +0.0067, 95% CI [0.0046, 0.0088]; the market wins RPS in all 7 test seasons. Shin margin removal: p_i(z) = (sqrt(z^2 + 4(1-z)*pi_i^2/Pi) - z) / (2(1-z)) (Eq. 1), root by bisection; fitted z over 17,479 complete books: median 0.017, max 0.061.

The paper's constructive contribution is match leverage: L_m = P(Omega|win m) - P(Omega|lose m) (Eq. 9), the change in season-objective probability between winning and losing a fixture, estimated by post-hoc conditioning on one season simulation — e.g. Fiorentina on 1 Mar 2026: Lecce away L=0.073 vs Inter home L=0.033 (2.25x leverage, gap ~8 MC SEs). Dixon-Coles specification used: log lambda = gamma + alpha_h - delta_a, log mu = alpha_a - delta_h (Eq. 2) with age-weighted likelihood w(Delta t) = exp(-xi*Delta t), xi=0.002/day (half-life 347 days) (Eq. 5).

Rezaei & Samadi (2026) test whether recent Elo-rating history contains signal beyond the current rating: K=6 lagged monthly Elo differences per match are whitened (x-tilde = Sigma-hat_X^{-1/2}(x-x-bar)); SIR kernel M-hat_SIR = sum_c pi-hat_c x-bar_c x-bar_c^T; SAVE kernel M-hat_SAVE = sum_c pi-hat_c (I_K - Sigma-hat_c)^2; top d=2 eigenvectors give scores z = B^T x-tilde, fed into a Poisson goal regression with home advantage and scoring-rate covariates.

Combined RPS on 128 World Cup matches (2018+2022): SIR d=2 0.127 (acc 0.688); SAVE d=2 0.127 (acc 0.680); SIR d=1 0.129; current-Elo Poisson 0.212; ARIMA-Elo 0.213; ensemble 0.209 — every SDR model beats every non-SDR baseline, with the first direction carrying almost all the gain. Caveats: only 128 test matches, and SDR models were trained on a richer sub-population (WC-qualified teams only), so part of the gap may be population selection rather than the trajectory signal.

Kumar et al. (2025) dual-threshold conformal prediction for autonomous perception: nonconformity s_i = -log p_i(y_i) (Eq. 2); conformal threshold q-hat_conf = Quantile({s_i}, (n+1)(1-alpha)/n) (Eq. 3) giving prediction sets C-hat(X) = {y : -log p(y) <= q-hat_conf} with coverage >= 1-alpha (Eq. 4); a second abstention threshold q-hat_abs = argmax_tau {TPR(tau) - FPR(tau)} — Youden's J on the calibration set (Eq. 5) — with abstain iff -log p(y) > q-hat_abs (Eq. 7).

ImageNet1K results: abstain-detection AUC 0.993 -> 0.995 (moderate->heavy rain), fog 0.9704 -> 0.9865, beating STARNet and likelihood methods; coverage stays near target (fog 90.0% -> 91.1%); abstention scales adaptively with perturbation severity, 13.5% -> 63.4% overall. Caveats: should_abstain labels derive from the authors' own severity protocol (mildly circular), conformal coverage is marginal not conditional, and the authors disclosed LLM text-polishing.

Williams, Schliep, Fosdick & Elmore (2024) build a Bayesian hierarchical mixture (L=J=10 latent clusters; shot counts | w_i ~ Multinomial(N_i, p_{w_i}) (Eq. 1); makes | z_i ~ Binomial(N_i^k, q_{z_i}^k) (Eq. 2); Dirichlet(alpha) priors on selection profiles, Beta(1,1) on accuracy; Gibbs 10k iterations, 3k burn-in) of NBA players' shot-selection and shot-accuracy profiles on 2.6M attempts (2008-09 through 2020-21), then define Expected Points Above Average (EPAA) = E[points(player i, N-tilde_i)] - E[points(average team, N-tilde_i)] at fixed volume N-tilde=8000, as a full difference-of-means posterior.
equation: EPAA = E[points(player i, N-tilde_i)] - E[points(average team, N-tilde_i)]

claim: EPAA captures unique offensive efficiency: Pearson correlations EPAA-PER 0.246, EPAA-BPM 0.238, PER-BPM 0.915; no meaningful correlation between EPAA and proportion of team shots taken (high-EPAA low-volume players like Joe Harris and Kendrick Nunn exist); 2020-21 top team expected points: Nets ~=120/game. MCMC reported no convergence issues.

Borgohain, Ackermann & Loaiza-Maya (2022) horse-race a variational BNN (2 hidden layers x 4 ReLU units, mean-field Gaussian VI, ELBO = E_q[log p(y|w,x)] - KL(q(w)||p(w)), ADAM) against a standard NN plus ex-post calibration (beta, isotonic, logistic/Platt) on 20 UCI binary tabular datasets with test log-loss: average ranks (lower better) BNN 2.0952, beta 2.6667, uncalibrated NN 2.7619, logistic 3.1905, isotonic 4.2857.

Friedman statistic 23.13, p = 0.000119 (methods differ overall), but post-hoc Wilcoxon-Holm shows only BNN vs isotonic is significant — BNN vs beta, vs uncalibrated, vs logistic are NOT. The file's honest read: calibration is usually enough; the abstract-level claim overstates the statistics. Dataset-level examples: Image Segmentation BNN log-loss 0.012053 vs uncalibrated 0.410117; Landsat BNN 0.065981 vs 0.549391.

Turtel et al. (2026) train GPT-OSS-120b with Dr. GRPO using five strictly proper scoring rules as terminal rewards on 8,041 binary news-event forecasting questions: S_log = y log p + (1-y)log(1-p) (1); S_Brier = -(p-y)^2 (2); S_spherical (3); beta family S_{alpha,beta}(p,y) = -y*integral_p^1(1-q)w(q)dq -(1-y)*integral_0^p q w(q)dq with beta-density weights at (2,8) (weights low-p region) and (8,8) (weights near 0.5) (4-5). Training: rank-32 LoRA, K=8 rollouts, advantage A_i = S_m(p_i,y) - (1/K)sum_j S_m(p_j,y), no KL penalty (7).

Pooled-5 results: log-loss-trained is best calibrated (ECE 0.0434) and best log score (-0.5132); Brier-trained has best Brier (0.1648) and best AUC (0.7511); Beta(8,8) is worst on ECE (0.0954). Bias-information-noise (BIN) decomposition: Brier-trained has the largest information contribution (3.70); log-trained has the largest positive noise contribution (2.60) with near-unit posterior probability of lower noise than every other variant. Headline lesson: proper rules share the same population incentive but are NOT interchangeable as training objectives.

Christopher D. Long's expository derivation (arXiv:2603.13581v1) of the exact closed-form full-Kelly staking rule for a single event with M mutually exclusive outcomes: maximize sum p_i*log(c + x_i/q_i) subject to c + sum x_i = 1 (p_i subjective probs, q_i = 1/O_i state prices, c cash reserve, x_i stakes). Fixed-support cash: c_A = (1 - P_A)/(1 - Q_A) with P_A = sum_{i in A} p_i, Q_A = sum_{i in A} q_i; canonical stakes x_i-star = (p_i - c-star*q_i)_+ (stake only where subjective prob exceeds cash-scaled state price).

Greedy support selection: sort edge ratios r_i = p_i/q_i descending and expand the support while r_{k+1} > c_k (proved optimal); terminal wealth W_i-star = max(c-star, p_i/q_i). The ledger's acceptance gate requires the greedy support to match brute-force optimal support on 1,000 random synthetic markets (M in {4,...,20}) in 100% of cases with objective value to 1e-9. Assumptions noted: p_i known exactly (no estimation error), single event only, fixed prices, no stake limits, full Kelly only.

Multi-Scale Graph WaveNet for wind-speed forecasting (Rathore et al. 2021, arXiv:2109.15239v1): a learnable adjacency A = Softmax(E*E^T) over weather-station node embeddings E discovers station-to-station influence from data instead of using geographic distance, combined with dilated 1-D causal convolutions (exponentially increasing dilation up to 8, residual + skip connections, inception-style multi-scale stack) forecasting 6-, 12-, 18-, 24-hour horizons.

On real wind-speed measurements from five Danish cities (Esbjerg, Aalborg, Aarhus, Odense, Roskilde, 2000-2010), the method outperformed state-of-the-art wind-speed forecasting on all four horizons by 4-5%. Limitations per the ledger: only five stations in one small flat country, hourly-scale data with gust extremes unmodeled, no exogenous NWP features, and the learned adjacency may overfit small networks.

Rivian/VW Group selective-prediction certification paper (arXiv:2609.22048): instead of asking whether a granted reliability certificate is valid, it asks whether finite calibration data can produce a certificate at all — certificate availability is exactly computable via the binomial inversion identity UCP(E,n;gamma) <= alpha iff FBin(E;n,alpha) <= gamma, where FBin(k;n,p) = sum_{i=0}^k C(n,i)p^i(1-p)^{n-i}. Availability: pi(n,r;alpha,gamma) = FBin(e*;n,r) with e* = max{k: FBin(k;n,alpha) <= gamma}; pi=0 if no k certifies.

Sample-size arithmetic (tau=0.90, familywise delta=0.05, true error 0.05, 80% availability): 179 calibration examples for 1 group; 450 each for 50 groups; raising true error 0.05->0.09 explodes the requirement to 13,407 per group. Selective error is R(t) = P(C=0 | A_t=1) with R(t) <= alpha = 1-tau. Shift warning: under 30% label-prior shift, monitoring detects only 11.3% of a 2.5% conditional shift within 2,000 probes — all guarantees hold for the certification distribution only.

Eckford & Moffett (arXiv:2104.14277v2) prove proportional (Kelly) betting is exactly optimal single-letter coding in an information-theoretic investment game: wealth evolves as W_{n+1} = W_n*<s(y_n), r_{z_n}> with growth rate G = sum_{x,y} p(x,y)*log<s(y), r_x>, and the linear lower bound on the rate-distortion function R(D) >= H(X) - D - Lambda* holds with equality iff the bettor uses proportional betting (T = P_{x|y}, i.e. betting conditional outcome probabilities = Kelly in this notation).

Converse result: every optimal single-letter code corresponds to a Kelly-betting investment game (-(1/c)E[d(x,y)] = Lambda* - H(X|Y), satisfied by diagonal R with r_{xx} = e^{d_0(x)/c}, s_x = p(x|y)). Limitations: finite alphabets, known px, and capacity-achieving input assumptions rarely hold in sports betting; real fractional-Kelly staking means the equality condition essentially never holds exactly — the bound is a diagnostic, not an operating point.

Under data scarcity, what drives conformal prediction coverage is the diversity of the calibration set — the p95-p5 spread of nonconformity scores — not how many rare events it contains: support width R^2=0.85 vs rare-event count R^2=0.02 (~50-fold gap), with residual rare-count correlation ~= 0 after diversity matching. The diversity-maximizing selector (argmax over N-subsets of p95-p5 of |forecast error|) raised 6-month recession-probability coverage 67.8%->81.4% where Mondrian, shift-robust, and extreme-value conformal baselines failed.

Calibration proposition: coverage deficit Delta = G(Q_G(1-alpha)) - G(Q-hat_C(1-alpha)); coverage fails when the calibration (1-alpha) quantile falls short of the test distribution's. Selector cost: interval width 10.6->32.6 points while still short of 90%. Mondrian dropped coverage 67.8%->61.0% even with oracle labels; a probit model reached ~97% coverage only with intervals 40-335x wider than the target range (vacuous). Cross-country validation: rho(diversity) 0.45-0.66 vs rho(rare) 0.02-0.23.

Bayesian two-part model of soccer chance creation on 2016/17 Premier League (380 fixtures, ~32,000 events, Stratagem Technologies Analyst data, proprietary): (A) block-structured Poisson counts N^j_{t_r,k} ~ Pois(lambda^j_{t_r,k}) with lambda = exp{theta^j_{t_r} - theta^{opp}_{t_r} + delta_{home}*gamma_{t_r} + alpha*G + beta*R} (sum-to-zero on theta), plus (B) topic-model-style categorical/GMM composition of assist/chance players and locations (8-component GMMs with means fixed at k-means centroids); fit by blocked Gibbs sampling in PyMC3 (2000 iterations + 100 burn-in) with monthly online refits.
equation: lambda = exp{theta^j_{t_r} - theta^{opp}_{t_r} + delta_{home}*gamma_{t_r} + alpha*G + beta*R}

claim: Posterior chance-creation ability theta: MCI t_6 0.465, LIV t_3 0.414, CHE t_6 0.384; relegated SUN t_6 -0.531, t_1 -0.296; home effect gamma positive in all 6 blocks, rising at end of first half and end of match. Case study LIV-CRY 23/4/17: model predicted 1 CRY chance in each of blocks t_3, t_5 vs actual 2 each. Caveat: no out-of-sample predictive scoring reported (no Brier/log-loss) — the paper is descriptive, not predictive.

Basketball plays as team-specific non-stationary MDPs (arXiv:1812.05170): state = ballcarrier x 6 regions x open/contested (~180 states/team); shot-clock-sliced transition probability tensors with P(s,a,s') = exp(lambda)/sum exp(lambda) and hierarchy lambda~N_8(zeta^{position},Sigma_lambda), zeta~N_8(omega^{region/defense},Sigma_zeta), omega~N_8(0,Sigma_omega); shot policy pi = expit(theta_{t_n}); make model Make(s) = expit(mu^{(x,y)} + I(open)*xi^{(y)}); reward R = 3*Make or 2*Make. Estimated in Stan with multi-level shrinkage and AR(1) temporal covariance on 155,656 NBA plays.

Held-out log-likelihood (higher better, empirical -> location -> position -> player shrinkage): policy pi -36808 -> -21553; transitions P -17299 -> -13478; rewards R -5956 -> -4540 — player-specific shrinkage is best on all three, with temporal autocorrelation rho-hat_theta = 0.94. Cavaliers counterfactuals (300 sims each): cutting contested mid-range 70% and doubling 3PA rate moves EPPS 1.038->1.089 and EPPP 0.923->0.973; Irving->James passes -90% changes Irving shots +18% and James -13% with negligible team change.

Combined forecast errors are often strongly autocorrelated (54% in the 1969 Bates-Granger example, overlooked for 55+ years); the two-step correction f^{CZZ}_{T+h|T} = f^{ZZ}_{T+h|T} + gamma*e^{ZZ}_{T|T-h} with default gamma = 0.5 (estimated gamma-hat = argmin_gamma sum[y - (f + gamma*e)]^2, bound -1<gamma<1) delivers gains exceeding the original combination gains: UNEMP corrected-mean relative RMSFE 0.47-0.51 vs OLS-optimal 1.03 — mitigating the forecast combination puzzle. The one-step GLS variant y_{t+h} = sum w_j f_{j,t+h|t} + gamma(y_t - sum w_j f_{j,t|t-h}) + xi beats the two-step.

Empirical results: corrected EW on the Bates-Granger motivating example MSFE 103 vs 150 (-31% correction gain vs -20% combination gain); UNEMP mean+gamma0.65 MSFE 0.0729 (relative 0.4663); OLS-optimal+gamma0.5 -41%; CPI gamma=0.5: -30% in 2022-2025. Failure mode: with COVID in-sample the correction hurts (UNEMP 1.16-1.53) via outlier propagation — skip correction after |e_t| > 3-sigma weeks; hist-optimal gamma (0.4-0.54) performs ~= fixed 0.5. Theorems 1-2: the corrected forecast weakly dominates in conditional and unconditional MSE.

Keller's optimal-running model extended with terrain, carbohydrate oxidation, and fatigue: state ODEs dv/dt = f - g*sin alpha - v/tau - c*v^2; dx/dt = v; dE/dt = sigma - f*v + (zeta/m)*N(t) - Q; dQ/dt = K*f*v (fatigue proportional to work rate); dN/dt = k*N(1-N/M) logistic oxidation with N(t) = (1/M + (1/N_0-1/M)e^{-kt})^{-1}. Optimal control result (Theorem 1): max force only at the start and on steep uphills, near-constant power elsewhere (bang-bang + singular arcs, Hamiltonian switching function linear in f).

Predicted elite finish times on five 2023 Golden Trail World Series races within 0.51-13.3%: Zegama 0.51% (3:35:34 vs 3:36:40), Mont-Blanc 3.45%, Dolomyths 10.03% (optimistic, loose-rock switchbacks unmodeled), Pikes Peak 9.93% (optimistic), Mammoth 13.3% (pessimistic). Parameters: M = 2.32e-2 g/s, k = 1.353 1/s, K = 6e-5 1/s, sigma-hat = 27 m^2/s^3; oxidation logistic fit R^2 = 0.9459. Limitations: no recovery term in dQ/dt, continuous running differs from intermittent football, no injury outcome, weather/surface unmodeled.

Wind-tunnel aerodynamic analysis of FIFA World Cup balls: 7-parameter drag fit C_D(v)|_{Sp=0} = (a-b_min)/(1+exp[(v-v_c)/v_s]) + b_min + drag-rise term (Eq. 5); spin-dependent C_D(Re,Sp) = C_D|_{Sp=0} + b*Sp (Eq. 7); lift fit C_L^fit(Sp) = alpha*Sp^beta with (alpha,beta) = (1.15, 0.83) at Re = 333,793 (Eq. 8); air density rho = pM/RT (Eq. 10) with barometric p = p_0[1 - Lh/T_0]^(gM/RL) (Eq. 11); flight ODE d^2r/dt^2 = -g j-hat - (rho*A*v^2/2m)[C_D v-hat - C_L(s-hat x v-hat)] (Eq. 12) integrated with 5th-order Cash-Karp Runge-Kutta.

Quantified effects: the Jabulani's unpredictable region is ~=15-24 m/s vs 10-17 m/s for other balls, with transition lift ~= (24/17)^2 ~= 2x the Brazuca's (explaining its erratic behavior); altitude variation (Brasilia 1,200 m vs sea level, 25-m kick at 34 m/s) changes ball flight by 82.0 cm for the Jabulani and 49.0 cm for the Brazuca; temperature variation gives 16.6-24.5 cm; air-density variation reaches up to 23%. Coefficients are soccer-ball-specific and do not transfer to a tumbling football; no wind in simulations; humidity ignored.

A CNN post-processor trained on only 15 six-hourly reports of a single typhoon (Soudelor, Taiwan 2015) beats the raw 20-member WEPS ensemble and an FCN on 24-h precipitation via three transferable tricks: (1) temporal-interpolation data augmentation (linear interpolation between consecutive reports + noise injection, 2x(2N-1) total reports); (2) dynamic storm-relative features (TC center lon/lat, grid-TC distance, TC-passed indicator); (3) recency-weighted CRPS loss with 1:2:4 weights on the three most recent reports. Gaussian CRPS: CRPS = sigma*{z*(2Phi(z)-1) + 2phi(z) - 1/sqrt(pi)}, z = (y-mu)/sigma.

CNN-all was best of five on CRPSS across the landfall reports 6-11 on plain grids and closest to observed frequency for P(precip > 200 mm); ablation shows CNN-dyn and CNN-aug each beat plain CNN with CNN-all best overall. Failure modes: the FCN beats all CNNs on mountain grids in some reports (terrain-locking the CNN kernels smooth out); Gaussian reference beats post-processing for light rain (gains only in the >80 mm regime); the 24-h accumulation design arrives a day late — not real-time deployable as designed.

SoccerRAG (arXiv:2406.01273): extractor -> validator -> SQL-agent -> few-shot-SQL-RAG pipeline answering natural-language queries over a multimodal soccer archive (550 games, Whisper-transcribed commentary, Labels-v2 event annotations, player info in SQLite). The controlled ablation proves the validator is the crucial component: full pipeline GPT-3.5 scored 9/10 correct vs the standalone SQL agent at 0/10 (GPT-3.5 pipeline-1) and 2/10 (pipeline-2); GPT-4 full pipeline 8/10.

Pipeline mechanics: (1) LangChain LLM feature extractor -> schema-defined JSON; (2) validator with string-match/Levenshtein entity resolution vs the DB plus auxiliary abbreviation tables, asking the user on ambiguity; (3) LangChain SQL agent; (4) SQL RAG with top-K=2 human-crafted SQL exemplars retrieved by FAISS over question embeddings; query difficulty quantified via Halstead metrics (n1, n2, N1, N2, volume V, difficulty D, effort E). Limitations: only 10 questions in the ablation, subjectively scored; LLMs truncate large list outputs; documented LLM laziness (subset returns, premature stops).

On 2,560 NFL games (2002-2011), line difference LD = (Favorite-Underdog margin) - |closing line| (Eq. 3) fits Normal(0, 13.588): mean -0.009, sd 13.588, chi-squared not statistically different from Gaussian — yielding the closed-form spread-to-win-probability map Pr(win|p) = Phi(p/13.588) (Eq. 4, Stern 1991 method), e.g. p=7 -> 69.6%. Calibration: p=1: model 0.529 vs actual 0.509; p=3: 0.587 vs 0.581; p=5: 0.644 vs 0.597; p=7: 0.697 vs 0.689.

Break-even win rate at -110: 100*WR = 110(1-WR) gives WR = 0.5238 (Eq. 1). Home teams won 57% straight-up but covered only 48.9% ATS (z=-5.977 vs 0.5238); home favorites 816-888 ATS (47.9%, z=-4.002). Home underdogs: the abstract claims 53.5% ATS but the paper's own Table 1 shows 409-396 = 50.8% (discrepancy noted in the file; 53.5% matches the pick-em row 15-13); the historical decay series is 58.1% (1973-79) -> 52.5% (1981-96) -> ~50.8% — the file says expect the edge dead unless re-tested at >=52.38% on 2012-2025.

Line movement distribution: >2,000 of 2,560 games moved <=1 point, 1,548 moved <=0.5, ~20% moved >1 point, ~10% moved >=2 points; opening vs closing MSE not significantly different; movement peaks in Week 1 and Week 17. Division winners: the model picked >=75% correctly every season (retrospective, ties counted favorably). Favorites ATS: 1,194 covered, 412 won SU but didn't cover, 853 lost outright, 101 pushes — favorite ATS loss rate 51.5%.

A Monte Carlo drawdown-quantile framework (arXiv:2608.00127) shows standard Brownian-motion formulas materially understate tail drawdown risk for non-Gaussian return archetypes: at Sharpe 1 and 3-year horizon, the 90th-percentile max drawdown is 1.87 (Gaussian), 1.98 (trend), 2.00 (market-neutral), and 2.48 (mean-reversion/short-vol, ~33% worse than Gaussian). Brownian benchmark: max-drawdown median 1.16, 90th percentile 1.89 annual-vol units. Four statistics tracked: maximum drawdown, maximum loss, final negative time, longest recovery time.

Method: 250 trading days/year Brownian motion; 16,000 independent paths with fixed seed for archetypes (modest for 90th-percentile tail claims); the paper recommends stationary block bootstrap and Hurst-exponent stress scenarios (H=0.5, 0.6, 0.7) for real use. Caveat: a pick-return process of discrete -110 wagers with time-varying edge matches none of the archetypes exactly — stylized inputs only.

Kelly growth-optimal portfolio paper (arXiv:1009.3753) on proportional transaction fees: the fee-inclusive rebalancing condition is f[W(1+fr)-alpha*X] = fW(1+r)-X (Eq. 8) with transfer volume X_{r>0} = Wrf(1-f)/(1-alpha*f); the headline finding is that partial rebalancing (transfer only a fraction epsilon of the required amount each period, heuristic T ~= 1/epsilon) beats intermittent rebalancing (resize every T periods) at both fee levels studied, and the same pattern holds under GARCH(1,1) correlated returns.

Under fees the interior-optimal rebalancing period T*>1 (constant rebalancing is no longer optimal); the paper's exact claim is that optimal growth rates are achieved for epsilon inside (0,1], outperforming the optimal intermittent values for both studied alpha. No single headline number — results are in figures (growth rate vs T, vs epsilon curves). The ledger maps the standard -110 vig (~4.55%) to the paper's fee alpha for a stake-smoothing rule: epsilon-damped stake updates s_t = s_{t-1} + epsilon(s*_t - s_{t-1}).

Pure theory paper (arXiv:1902.04256) on selective prediction in a fully adversarial setting: a predictor that pre-commits which future window of the sequence to predict (Algorithm 1's dyadic scheme) achieves expected squared loss O(1/log n) — Lemma 2.1: for integer k >= 1, Algorithm 1 achieves expected squared loss <= 1/k on any sequence of length 2^k — and the bound is tight with matching lower bound Omega(1/log n) (resolving Drukh's 2013 open question). Theorem 1.4: L-smooth statistics w.r.t. earth mover's distance achieve expected absolute loss O(L/sqrt(log n)).

Explicit lower bound (Section 2.3): for any predictor A there exists a binary length-n sequence with expected squared loss >= 1/64. Operational takeaway stated in the file: the adaptive version (choosing the window after seeing data) gains only a constant factor over the pre-committed scheme — so if a backtest shows adaptive week-skipping winning by a large margin, that diagnoses overfitting in the adaptive rule, not genuine signal.

Selective prediction on ranked outputs (arXiv:2608.14683) proves a feasibility ceiling: selective accuracy <= min(1, p/c) (Eq. 2), where p = base accuracy and c = coverage — recalibration or rescoring cannot beat it. Score decomposition (Eq. 3): s_i(x) = a(x) + r_i(x) — a shared case-level term plus a candidate-specific residual — so the top-two margin s_1 - s_2 = r_1 - r_2 cancels a(x); Eq. (5) shows no zero-sum contrast over candidates can recover the discarded case-level information.

Empirical results on 10,374 real patient cases (Phenopacket Store v0.1.27, 780 diagnoses): eight small LLMs achieve at most 4.6% Recall@1 on ultra-rare diseases, so at 10% coverage even perfect confidence ranking cannot reach 50% selective accuracy (ceiling min(1, 0.046/0.10) = 46%); Exomiser: top-two margin selects 10% of cases at 29.0% accuracy vs 13.3% overall while the top score provides no reliable gate. Proposition 1 (unidentifiability): the better gate (margin vs top score) needs labeled data or an intervention — it cannot be determined from unlabeled scores.

GCN-WP (arXiv:2207.13191): a semi-supervised graph convolutional network representing an entire esports league as a graph — one node per team-game, undirected edges to the opponent's node and to the team's previous-game node (BuildLeagueGraph, Algorithm 1), homogeneous network justified by delta (team-minus-opponent) features, label timing offset by c convolutions to avoid leakage. GCN layer: f(L^{(n)},A) = sigma(D-hat^{-1/2} A-hat D-hat^{-1/2} L^{(n)} W^{(n)}), A-hat = A + I; Chebyshev-polynomial filters (degree 1) also tested.

Test on LCS 2020 (trained on LPL, validated on LCK — cross-league transfer): GCN-cheby 1-layer + delta features accuracy 0.619 (best) vs SCOPE (Elo) 0.597 vs RF lookback-5 + delta 0.578 +/- 0.012; GCN-cheby 2-layer 0.568; raw features 0.541. Delta features beat raw everywhere; 1-layer beats 2-layer (wider neighborhoods pull in opponents-of-opponents noise); Chebyshev beats spectral on delta (0.619 vs 0.551) — opposite of Kipf & Welling's original finding. Central weakness: accuracy only, no probabilities, no calibration.

AFBART (arXiv:2503.07789): Adaptive Functional Bayesian Additive Regression Trees — fully nonparametric function-on-scalar regression estimating NBA players' 2-D shot-intensity surfaces: y_i(s) = sum_k beta_k(x_i) phi_k(s) + epsilon_i(s), with phi_k data-adaptive orthonormal basis functions (matrix orthonormality constraint for identifiability, mixture-of-normals prior with thin-plate-spline roughness penalty) and beta_k(x) = sum_t g(x; T_t, M_t) (50-tree BART ensemble); posterior sampling via Gibbs/Metropolis-Hastings MCMC (Algorithm 1); defaults 20 basis functions, 50 trees.

Simulation (3 cases x 2 noise levels): AFBART had the lowest RMSPE, MIS, and MCRPS in all 6 settings — e.g. Case 1 low noise RMSPE 0.07 vs FBART 0.68 vs BFOSR 13.38 vs LLR 20.31; Case 3 (realistic surfaces) RMSPE 0.34 vs 0.69/0.90/3.02. Real-data 4-fold CV on NBA 2017-18 (191 players, >400 FGA): AFBART lowest on both RMSPE and MCRPS (exact CV numbers blanked in extraction — ordering only verifiable). Variable importance top 5 (posterior mean splitting proportions): position, block %, steal %, games played, 3-point attempt rate.

AI Feynman (arXiv:1905.11481): physics-inspired symbolic regression that recursively combines a neural network's discovered symmetries/separabilities with dimensional analysis, polynomial fitting, and brute-force search. Separability recombination: y = y'*y''/c_num (multiplicative; additive analog y = y' + y'' - c_num); symmetry threshold epsilon_sym = 7 x NN validation error (~7-sigma, near-zero false positives); NN: 6 hidden layers (3x128 + 3x64), softplus, 100 epochs, lr 0.005, batch 2048, Adam weight decay 1e-2, FastAI 1-cycle; polynomial fit degrees 0-4.

On the Feynman Database for Symbolic Regression (100 equations from the Feynman Lectures + 20 bonus, 100,000 synthetic points per mystery, max 2h CPU per mystery): basic set AI Feynman solved 100/100 vs Eureqa 71/100 (the paper also restates Eureqa at 68% in Section IV — both figures are the paper's own claims); bonus set 18/20 (90%) vs Eureqa 3/20 (15%), with the biggest gains on the most complicated mysteries where NN-discovered symmetry/separability eliminates variables before brute force. Limitation: sports quantities lack physical units (kills the dimensional-analysis module) and have regime structure rather than symmetries.

LLM-SRBench (arXiv:2504.10415): a memorization-proof 239-problem benchmark for LLM-based scientific equation discovery — LSR-Transform (111 problems) rewrites known models in unfamiliar forms, LSR-Synth (128 problems) injects novel terms with held-out OOD test sets. Headline: the best system manages only ~31.5% symbolic accuracy (LLM-SR + GPT-4o-mini on LSR-Transform); on Transform, LaSR leads numerical accuracy (Acc_0.1, NMSE) while LLM-SR leads symbolic; on LSR-Synth materials the advantage inverts; all methods degrade ID->OOD.

Memorization diagnosis: error-curve analysis of plain LLM sampling on 100 Feynman problems vs bench problems — sharp drops + low symbolic error = recitation, gradual curves = genuine search; LSR-Transform is substantially harder than Feynman at matched node counts, including the simplest [0-15]-node band. DataBlind (no data) performs poorly, so data is necessary and priors insufficient; GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-8B consistently beat GPT-3.5-turbo (smaller/less-opinionated models explore better). Metrics: symbolic accuracy, Acc_tau, NMSE, OOD NMSE, efficiency; complexity controlled by expression-tree node count.

Khurana et al. (IBM, arXiv:1709.07150) RL feature engineering: a transformation graph (DAG of dataset nodes x transforms) compactly enumerates compositional feature search — root D_0, hierarchical nodes D_j = T(D_i), sum nodes D_{i,j} = D_i + D_j, a height-h complete graph over t transforms having ~t^{h+1}-2 nodes. MDP: state s_i = (G_i, b_ratio) with 9 factors (node accuracy, transform avg reward, times-used on path, recency of gains, depth, budget fraction, feature-count ratio, is-selector, data types); reward = best-accuracy improvement of G_{i+1} over G_i; Q-update w <- w + alpha(r + gamma*max Q - Q)*f with alpha = 0.05, gamma = 0.99, epsilon-greedy epsilon = 0.15.
equation: w <- w + alpha(r + gamma*max Q - Q)*f

claim: On 48 training + 24 non-overlapping test datasets: 23.8% median error reduction over base at B_max = 100 steps; RL policies 4-8x more efficient than handcrafted BFS/DFS/global at finding the optimal node; RL1 (action-dependent weights) more data-efficient than RL2. Standouts: Amazon Employee 0.712->0.806; Bikeshare DC 0.393->0.798; feature selection as a graph transform improves final gain by 51%; h_max = 4 optimal for the majority, h_max = 6 deteriorates (over-composition). Different algorithms yield different optimal features — FE is model-dependent.

START (arXiv:2211.09510): self-supervised trajectory representation learning with spatiotemporal domain structure — Stage 1 TPE-GAT road-network attention e_ij = (h_i W_1 + h_j W_2 + p^trans_ij W_3) W_4^T with transfer probabilities p^trans_ij = count(v_i->v_j)/count(v_i); Stage 2 TAT-Enc time-aware encoder x_i = r_i + t_{mi(t_i)} + t_{di(t_i)} + pe_i (minute-of-day + day-of-week embeddings) with interval-decay attention TA_h = softmax(Q_h K_h^T/sqrt(d') + Delta-tilde) V_h, learned decay delta'_{ij} = 1/log(e + |t_i - t_j|). Pretraining: span-masked recovery (mask consecutive spans l_m=2, p_m=15%) + NT-Xent contrastive (tau=0.05), L^pre = 0.6*L^mask + 0.4*L^con.

Results: best on all metrics on Beijing taxi and Porto datasets across travel-time estimation, ID classification, and detour similarity vs 8 baselines (exact Table II values figure-rendered, qualitative only); BJ-pretrained START fine-tuned on GeoLife beats Geolife-pretrained START (cross-city transfer works, unlike Trembr whose transfer is worse than baseline). Efficiency: 25.8 s to encode 100,000 trajectories on RTX 3090; deep similarity is O(d) vs O(L^2) classical — >=10x faster per query than DTW/LCSS/Frechet/EDR.

GenMove (arXiv:2501.13347): one masked conditional diffusion model unifying mobility-trajectory generation, recovery, and prediction — mask conditioning e_co = e_all ⊙ m (conditional observation), e_ta^0 = e_all ⊙ (1-m) (task target); five mask strategies (Random/recovery, Terminal/prediction, Complete/generation, Sequential, Circadian) mixed by adjustable ratios; user embedding p_u = LSTM_phi(h_u) with flow-based controller p_u = f_xi(r_u); classifier-free guidance eps-tilde_theta = (1+omega)eps_theta(e_ta^t,t|e_co,p_u) - omega*eps_theta(e_ta^t,t|e_co,empty); training loss L(theta) = E||eps - eps_theta(e_ta^t,t|e_co,p_u)||^2 with 1000 diffusion steps and a 4-layer 8-head Transformer noise predictor on 128-dim embeddings.

Results: generation ~13% average improvement over baselines (TimeGEO, MoveSim, VOLUNTEER, PateGail, DiffTraj) across JSD metrics; recovery ~6% improvement on Distance; next-location prediction only close to the best baseline (the paper honestly admits generality costs single-task peak performance); long-term prediction (8 steps) significantly outperforms all baselines with the gap widening with horizon; zero-shot on unseen users: Accuracy@5 +18% (scarcity-constrained) and ~+20% (long-term 8-step); optimal mask ratio 0.8, not 1.0 — multi-task training helps single tasks.

Kirkpatrick et al. (2017) Elastic Weight Consolidation: L(theta) = L_B(theta) + sum_i (lambda/2)*F_i*(theta_i - theta*_{A,i})^2 (Eq. 3) — anchor each weight to its task-A value with stiffness proportional to the diagonal Fisher information F_i, derived from the Bayesian update log p(theta|D) = log p(D_B|theta) + log p(theta|D_A) - log p(D_B) (Eq. 2) with a Laplace approximation giving a diagonal Gaussian posterior whose precision is the Fisher diagonal. Fisher is approximated as E[grad log p grad log p^T] (diagonal only); EWC is linear in parameters and examples, unlike ELLA which inverts parameter-dim matrices.

Permuted MNIST: plain SGD catastrophically forgets task A at the switch while uniform L2 preserves A but cannot learn B; EWC learns B while holding A, and dropout-SGD degrades after ~2 permutations while EWC scales to many tasks with only modest error growth. Atari: plain DQN total human-normalized clipped score stays < 1 (learns at most 1 game); the EWC agent learns multiple games (10 games, EWC activated per game after 20M frames). Fisher overlap (Fig 2C): similar tasks share weights at all depths; dissimilar tasks subdivide early layers but share layers near the output.

The paper's stated chief limitation (Fig 3C): inverse-Fisher-shaped perturbations are least harmful, but nullspace perturbations hurt as much — the method is overconfident about which parameters are unimportant. The ledger's GSE port: per-feature importance-weighted anchoring sum_i (lambda/2)*w_i*(s_i - s*_i)^2 with w_i = normalized per-feature importance (mean |SHAP| or split gain) in weekly GBM refits, a cosine-overlap diagnostic of per-feature importance vectors across regime strata (early/mid/late/playoff) setting per-feature lambda, and flooring all w_i at small epsilon as the overconfidence guard.

Cheng et al. (2019) 'Few-shot Learning with Meta Metric Learners' (arXiv:1901.09890v1): an LSTM meta-learner learns the optimizer for a task-specific Matching Network, combined with a two-stage auxiliary-task retrieval procedure that ranks historical tasks by cross-accuracy on the target and keeps the top-s as D_aux; ledger verdict ADAPT.
Matching-network attention is α(x̂,x_i,θ) = exp(f(x̂)·g(x_i)) / Σ_j exp(f(x̂)·g(x_j)) with prediction P(y|x̂,S) = Σ_i α(x̂,x_i;θ) y_i — a trainable k-NN that handles arbitrary class counts.
equation: α(x̂,x_i,θ) = exp(f(x̂)·g(x_i)) / Σ_j exp(f(x̂)·g(x_j)); P(y|x̂,S) = Σ_i α(x̂,x_i;θ) y_i

claim: The LSTM-as-optimizer update is c_t ← R((∇ℒ_t, ℒ_t); Θ), θ_t ← c_t, with c_t=θ_t, c̃_{t+1}=−∇ℒ(θ_t), forget gate=1, input gate=learning rate.
equation: c_t ← R((∇ℒ_t, ℒ_t); Θ); θ_t ← c_t; c̃_{t+1} = −∇ℒ(θ_t); forget gate = 1; input gate = learning rate

claim: Auxiliary-task retrieval procedure (Sec. 3.2): train a per-task matching network M^i on merged task data, score each by cross-accuracy acc_{i→target} on the target's combined data, and take the top-s as D_aux; 1-shot multi-task needs D_aux because meta-test cannot supply gradients.

Sentence Classification Service multi-task results: 1-shot FCE — Meta Metric-learner 58.13% vs Meta-learner LSTM 56.98% vs Matching FCE (+additional data) 54.24% vs basic 53.59%; 5-shot — 74.54% vs 72.54% vs 70.28%.

Omniglot: 1-shot 95.79% vs Matching FCE 95.84% (approximately tied); 5-shot 98.83% vs 98.65% vs LSTM 97.22%. Amazon Reviews: 1-shot 49.38% vs Matching FCE 47.18% (about 2pp gain over second-best); 5-shot 60.82% vs 54.64% (over 5pp improvement on the matching network).
Paper's own warnings: adding unrelated auxiliary data decreases performance, and cross-accuracy scores are 'usually low but their relative magnitudes could reflect relatedness.'

Dabney et al. (2018) 'Distributional Reinforcement Learning with Quantile Regression' (arXiv:1710.10044, QR-DQN): a distributional RL critic that learns the full return distribution via quantile regression without a fixed return support; ledger verdict ADAPT.
The return distribution is represented as Z_θ(x,a) = (1/N) Σ_{i=1}^N δ_{θ_i(x,a)}, where each θ_i estimates a fixed quantile τ̂_i = (τ_{i−1}+τ_i)/2 with τ_i = i/N; experiments use N=200 quantiles.
QR-DQN loss is the quantile Huber loss ρ^κ_τ(δ) = |τ − 1{δ<0}| · ℒ_κ(δ)/κ applied to pairwise TD-errors δ_{ij} = r + γθ_j(x′,π(x′)) − θ_i(x,a).
Proposition 2 of QR-DQN: Π_{W1}T^π is a γ-contraction in d̄_∞ (the maximal ∞-Wasserstein metric): d̄_∞(Π_{W1}T^πZ_1, Π_{W1}T^πZ_2) ≤ γ d̄_∞(Z_1, Z_2).

On ALE Atari-57 at 200M frames with the best-agent protocol, QR-DQN achieved mean/median human-normalized scores of 915%/211% with 41 games above human and 54 games above DQN, vs C51's 701%/178% with 40/50 — 'qr-dqn outperforms all previous agents in mean and median human-normalized score.'

QR-DQN authors' sobering note: 'Even at 200 million frames, there are 10% of games where all algorithms reach less than 10% of human,' and they flag Double-DQN-style overestimation bias as unaddressed future work.

Hafner et al. (2023/2024) 'Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models' (arXiv:2301.04104, DreamerV3): a recurrent state-space world model whose single fixed hyperparameter configuration outperforms tuned per-domain experts across 150+ tasks; ledger verdict ADAPT for the robustness toolkit (categorical latents, symlog/twohot, KL balancing, continue predictor).

DreamerV3 RSSM world model: h_t = f_φ(h_{t−1}, z_{t−1}, a_{t−1}); z_t ~ q_φ(z_t|h_t,x_t); ẑ_t ~ p_φ(ẑ_t|h_t); r̂_t ~ p_φ(r̂_t|h_t,z_t); ĉ_t ~ p_φ(ĉ_t|h_t,z_t) (continue flag); x̂_t ~ p_φ(x̂_t|h_t,z_t).
equation: h_t = f_φ(h_{t−1}, z_{t−1}, a_{t−1}); z_t ~ q_φ(z_t|h_t,x_t); ẑ_t ~ p_φ(ẑ_t|h_t); r̂_t ~ p_φ(r̂_t|h_t,z_t); ĉ_t ~ p_φ(ĉ_t|h_t,z_t); x̂_t ~ p_φ(x̂_t|h_t,z_t)

claim: DreamerV3 world-model loss (Eq. 2): L(φ) = E_{qφ}[ Σ_t (β_pred L_pred + β_dyn L_dyn + β_rep L_rep) ] with β = (1, 1, 0.1); L_dyn and L_rep use max(1, KL[…]) — free bits clipped below 1 nat (≈1.44 bits) — with stop-gradient KL balancing.
equation: L(φ) = E_{qφ}[ Σ_t (β_pred L_pred + β_dyn L_dyn + β_rep L_rep) ], β = (1, 1, 0.1)

claim: DreamerV3 robustness transforms: symlog(x) = sign(x)·ln(|x|+1); symexp(x) = sign(x)·(exp(|x|)−1); symexp-twohot loss L(θ) = −twohot(y)^T log softmax(f(x,θ)) — categorical cross-entropy regression that is scale-invariant.
equation: symlog(x) = sign(x)·ln(|x|+1); symexp(x) = sign(x)·(exp(|x|)−1); L(θ) = −twohot(y)^T log softmax(f(x,θ))

claim: DreamerV3 on Minecraft: the first algorithm to collect diamonds from scratch without human data or curricula — at 100M steps diamonds were found in 0.4% of episodes; 100% of Dreamer agents obtained at least one diamond vs 0% of baselines.

DreamerV3 ablations: the world-model KL objective is the most important component, followed by return normalization and symexp twohot. Compute costs: Minecraft 100M steps = 8.9 GPU-days at 200M params; DMLab 100M steps = 2.9 GPU-days (single Nvidia A100 per run); model sizes 12M–400M params.

Xu et al. (2026) 'TacticGen: Grounding Adaptable and Scalable Generation of Football Tactics' (arXiv:2604.18210, association football): a multi-agent Diffusion Transformer with agent-wise self-attention for player-player cooperative/competitive dynamics plus context-aware cross-attention over game context, ball, and temporal sequence; ledger verdict ADAPT for its prediction→generation framing.

TacticGen inference-time classifier guidance: x_{t−1} ∼ p(x_{t−1}|x_t) tilted by ∇ log p(objective | x_t) — generation is steered toward objectives specified by rules, natural language, or neural evaluators without retraining.
equation: x_{t−1} ∼ p(x_{t−1}|x_t) tilted by ∇ log p(objective | x_t)

claim: TacticGen trained on 3.3M+ annotated events and 100M tracking frames from top-tier soccer leagues, claiming SOTA precision in player-trajectory prediction with scaling consistent with scaling laws; an expert case study with Birmingham City FC staff confirmed realistic, strategically valuable tactics (exact numeric tables were not extracted in the ledger).

TacticGen is positioned against TacticAI (corner-kick set pieces only) and TacEleven/GenTac (tied to curated text-to-trajectory conditioning sets); TacticGen handles open-play continuous dynamics with free-form inference objectives.

Ahmad, Shadaydeh et al. (2021) 'Causal Inference in Non-linear Time-series using Deep Networks and Knockoff Counterfactuals' (arXiv:2109.10817): DeepAR probabilistic forecasting plus in-distribution knockoff interventions as a scalable nonlinear causal-discovery arm that beats PCMCI/GPDC head-to-head; ledger verdict ADAPT.

The causal significance score is CSS_{i→j} = ln(MAPE_j^i / MAPE_j) — the log ratio of forecast error with vs without the knockoff intervention — with a hypothesis test on mean CSS > 0 across realizations.

Knockoff intervention method (Barber & Candès 2015): generate knockoff samples X̃_i that are in-distribution and exchangeable with X_i, substitute X_i with its knockoff, and reforecast — keeping the intervention on-distribution instead of out-of-distribution.

On synthetic series, DeepAR-Knockoffs had the best F-score across the nonlinearity coefficient β, beating VAR-GC (whose linearity assumption fails) and PCMCI/GPDC; DeepAR-OutDist suffered a high false discovery rate and the lowest F-score, while PCMCI, DeepAR-Mean, and DeepAR-Knockoffs all kept FPR well-controlled.

On real Danube river-discharge data, VAR-GC and PCMCI reported false causal links (extreme rainfall events violate stationarity) while DeepAR-Knockoffs correctly discovered the expected links except a single false link.

The paper's cost caveat: better performance from DeepAR-Knockoffs comes with higher computational load from deep networks, especially for large multivariate time series. Evaluation metrics used: FPR = FP/(FP+TN); F-score = TP/(TP + 0.5(FP+FN)).

Egelé et al. (2023) 'Is One Epoch All You Need For Multi-Fidelity Hyperparameter Optimization?' (arXiv:2307.15422): random search over HP configs, evaluate each at minimum fidelity (1 epoch), select top-K=3, train only those to max fidelity (100 epochs); ledger verdict ADAPT as the mandatory baseline every multi-fidelity scheduler must beat.

On HPOBench (Naval Propulsion tabular regression), the final test RMSE of the 1-Epoch policy ≈ the 100-Epochs policy (curves converge to the same point), but 1-Epoch uses 40× fewer training epochs: 200×1 + 3×100 = 500 epochs vs 200×100 = 20,000 epochs.

SHA uses ~10× fewer epochs than 100-Epochs but still 4× more than 1-Epoch; Hyperband uses slightly more than SHA; SHA/HB/LCE 'do not differ significantly from each other' in final RMSE — all similar to each other, all costlier than the trivial 1-Epoch baseline.
Mechanism finding: learning curves show a few dominant curves; good vs bad models are separable in the first epoch; the ranking of GOOD models stabilizes after ~5 epochs while bad models stay noisy.

Morato, Andriotis, Khademi (2025) 'ConBatch-BAL: Batch Bayesian Active Learning under Budget Constraints' (arXiv:2507.04929, Delft University of Technology): two deployable budget-constrained batch acquisition heuristics — dynamic thresholding and greedy knapsack — that reached accuracy targets with 20–80% fewer active-learning iterations than random; ledger verdict ADAPT.
ConBatch-BAL constrained batch objective (Eq. 2): argmax_{x₁:ₙ⊆D_pool} a({x₁,…,xₙ}, p(ω|D_train)) subject to c(x₁,…,xₙ) ≤ c_max and n ≤ n_max.
equation: argmax_{x₁:ₙ⊆D_pool} a({x₁,…,xₙ}, p(ω|D_train)) s.t. c(x₁,…,xₙ) ≤ c_max, n ≤ n_max

claim: Batch-BALD acquisition (Eq. 4): 𝕀(y₁:ₙ; ω | x₁:ₙ, D_train) = ℍ(y₁:ₙ|x₁:ₙ,D_train) − 𝔼_{p(ω|D_train)}[ℍ(y₁:ₙ|x₁:ₙ,ω,D_train)] — the mutual information between batch predictions and model parameters.
equation: 𝕀(y₁:ₙ; ω | x₁:ₙ, D_train) = ℍ(y₁:ₙ|x₁:ₙ,D_train) − 𝔼_{p(ω|D_train)}[ℍ(y₁:ₙ|x₁:ₙ,ω,D_train)]

claim: Dynamic thresholding (Alg. 1): at step i admit only candidates with cost c(x) ≤ c_th,i = c_max,i / (n_max − (i−1)); the threshold adapts as remaining budget shrinks. Both heuristics are equivalent to greedy Batch-BALD in the infinite-budget limit.

With distance cost on build6k/nieman17k/mnist6k: ConBatch-BAL reached accuracy targets with 20–43% fewer AL iterations than random on build6k and 50–80% fewer on nieman17k; under a 100-m batch constraint random failed to reach 71% accuracy on nieman17k within 800 iterations; on mnist6k both strategies hit 97% in <400 iterations vs >600 for random under the 100-m budget.

Under the 2-km constraint ConBatch-BAL outperformed the unconstrained random baseline on all datasets (average unconstrained batch travel ≈ 25 km); under area_cost, greedy beats dynamic thresholding on build6k/nieman17k because thresholding starves the expensive-but-informative area, while on mnist6k diversity lets thresholding win.

Eswararaj, Nellipudi, Kollati (2025) practitioner benchmark of Delta Parquet, Iceberg, and Hudi on synthetic automotive telemetry (100 vehicles × 2,000 records × 30 days ≈ 200,000 records, Apache Spark 3.3.0 on AWS EC2 m5.4xlarge); ledger verdict ADAPT — Delta for the Spark-centric ML workload, Hudi rejected, Iceberg as fallback if a second engine enters.

Measured lakehouse numbers: ingestion time (min) Delta 13.5, Iceberg 14.1, Hudi 9.7; query latency (sec) Delta 4.8, Iceberg 3.2, Hudi 6.4; storage (GB) Delta 88, Iceberg 76, Hudi 91; throughput (records/sec) Delta 123,456, Iceberg 119,034, Hudi 153,870; compaction (min) Delta 3.1, Hudi 2.2 (MoR mode), Iceberg N/A.

Critical fairness flaw in the Delta/Iceberg/Hudi benchmark: Delta ran on optimized Databricks Runtime 11.3 while Iceberg/Hudi ran on vanilla Spark — Delta's numbers were flattered, yet Iceberg still beat Delta on query latency (3.2 vs 4.8s) and storage (76 vs 88 GB). Single runs with no variance on a toy dataset, from a practitioner journal rather than a top-venue peer-reviewed source.

Benchmark author insights: Hudi had the fastest ingestion (incremental/upsert); Iceberg had the best query latency and ~13% less storage; Hudi's async compaction outpaced Delta; the case-study recommendation was Hudi for real-time ingestion, Iceberg for batch analytics, and Delta for ML lifecycle — possibly combined.

Duly et al. (2024) 'AlphaForge: A Framework to Mine and Dynamically Combine Formulaic Alpha Factors' (arXiv:2406.18394v5): a generative-predictive factor miner producing a 100-formula 'factor zoo' plus dynamic per-time-step re-selection/re-weighting combination (Mega-Alpha) on trailing factor performance; ledger verdict ADAPT.

AlphaForge Stage 1 mining: predictor P is trained to map formula one-hot encoding x ∈ {0,1}^{D×S} to fitness with L_P = sqrt((1/n) Σ_i (P(x_i) − fitness(x_i))²); generator G is trained to maximize predicted fitness via x = M(G(z)), z ~ N(0,1)^Q, with a diversity penalty between sampled formulas, adding qualified formulas until TargetFactorNum = 100.
equation: L_P = sqrt((1/n) Σ_i (P(x_i) − fitness(x_i))²); x = M(G(z)), z ~ N(0,1)^Q

claim: AlphaForge Stage 2 dynamic combination: at each time t re-score zoo factors on trailing-window IC, ICIR, RankIC; select top-N (best N=10 of 100); fit fresh OLS on latest data: Mega-Alpha_t = Σ_{j∈top-N_t} w_{j,t} f_j — a linear (not nonlinear) combination for overfitting control, justified by factor-performance momentum (Ehsani & Linnaaimaa 2022).

AlphaForge factor-pool size is non-monotonic in {1,10,20,50,100} with a peak at 10 — 'at any given time, approximately 10 factors capture the most relevant price information.' The Mega-Alpha composition changes day to day (only 5 of 10 factors carried from Day 1 to Day 2; factor #3 flipped weight from −0.00014 to +0.00168).
