The 'World-Class Sports Probability Engine Corpus Audit' prescribes CQR with a quantile-clamping ban, Generalized Venn-Abers for binary moneylines, decoupling latent performance from market pricing, and anytime-valid E-processes for edge testing; 155 of 278 Table-3 rows were GSE-relevant, 123 of 278 flagged sheet_inflated=Y.
CQR non-conformity score: E_i = max(q̂_{α_lo}(X_i) − Y_i, Y_i − q̂_{α_hi}(X_i)); conformal rank index k = ⌈(n + 1)(1 − α)⌉.

Quantile-clamping defect: at α=0.10, n=5 → k=⌈6×0.9⌉=6>5, forcing the empirical quantile to +∞; clamping to n=5 delivers true coverage n/(n+1) ≈ 83.33% while presented as 90% → a 6.67 percentage-point under-coverage defect ('fake tightness'). Fail-closed rule: when n < ⌈1/α⌉ − 1, emit infinite intervals [−∞, +∞] or abstain via the No-Bet block; Jackknife+ gives ≥ 1 − 2α coverage without a calibration holdout.

Generalized Venn-Abers: dual isotonic regressions produce multiprobability bounds [p_0, p_1]; interval width (p_1 − p_0) is the epistemic-uncertainty measure, with an example No-Bet gate at p_1 − p_0 > 0.20 (a policy choice, not derived). Loss shift: BCE → Brier loss 'drastically optimizes baseline point-estimate calibration' per NCAA-data evaluations; parameter estimation error scales as d/n.

Target-leakage rule: closing lines/near-game odds used as team-strength input features = severe target leakage; a pure performance engine derives signal only from play-by-play efficiency, spatial tracking, and box-score aggregates, with market dynamics living in a separate Hawkes subsystem; arXiv 2010.12508 is direct evidence for profitability by decorrelating predictions from consensus pricing.

Aoki, Assunção & Vaz de Melo (2017) arXiv:1706.02447v1 'Luck is Hard to Beat': a cross-sport study of skill-vs-luck in sports outcomes; GSE verdict ADAPT — take the schedule-preserving random null (skill coefficient φ) as a regime diagnostic for the engine's irreducible error floor; reject the dated in-sample NBA roster model and the circular team-removal procedure.

Skill coefficient: φ = (s² − σ²_{2k}) / s², where s² = observed variance of season-end standings and σ²_{2k} = expected standings variance under a Monte Carlo null replaying the actual schedule with outcomes drawn from observed home/tie/away frequencies; φ ∈ (−∞, 1]; φ≈0 means standings are fully explained by chance; the 95% null interval comes from the 2.5th/97.5th Monte Carlo percentiles.

Cross-sport luck findings (270,713 BetExplorer matches, 1,503 seasons, 198 leagues, 84 countries, Jan 2007–Jul 2016): skill-dominated seasons — basketball 100%, volleyball 99.39%; pure-luck-compatible — handball 17.95%, soccer 7.13%. Average team removal to reach the random interval: basketball 50%, volleyball 40%, handball 14%, soccer 19%/20%. NBA: 17–25 of 30 teams must be removed before standings look random; φ > 0.95; EPL ≈ 0.77; Primera División 0.80; Série A 0.63; Algerian Division 1 2014–15: φ = −1.93 (negative, unexplained).

NBA underdog win probabilities 2012–2016 (mean): P(U)=0.36; away underdog 0.27; home underdog 0.45; away underdog vs removed elite 0.19; home underdog vs removed elite 0.17. The NBA model's skill-wins correlation of 0.7399 is in-sample and circular (wins were the fitting target); no held-out log-loss/Brier, no Elo/odds baseline. Season-length confound: the NFL's 17-game season mechanically looks more luck-like than the NBA's 82 games.

Radiance field per timestep: F_t(x,d; Θ_t) = MLP(γ(x), γ(d); Θ_t) with ~12.7M params per timestep (~48.8 MB); volume rendering: Ĉ(r,t) = ∫ T_t(s) σ_t(r(s)) c_t(r(s),d) ds, T_t(s) = exp(−∫ σ_t du); loss: L(Θ_t) = Σ_i Σ_{r∈R_i} ‖Ĉ(r;Θ_t) − C(r)‖² + κ‖Θ_{t+1} − Θ_t‖².
equation: F_t(x,d; Θ_t) = MLP(γ(x), γ(d); Θ_t); Ĉ(r,t) = ∫ T_t(s) σ_t(r(s)) c_t(r(s),d) ds; T_t(s) = exp(−∫ σ_t du); L(Θ_t) = Σ_i Σ_{r∈R_i} ‖Ĉ(r;Θ_t) − C(r)‖² + κ‖Θ_{t+1} − Θ_t‖²

claim: Synthetic novel-view results: DWS PSNR 34.28/LPIPS 0.027 vs 4DGS 28.17/0.08, D-3DGS 18.45/0.139; Soccer Penalty Kick 33.81/0.028; CMU Panoptic Baseball Bat 29.43/0.066 (D-3DGS/4DGS/ST-GS all failed). Memory per timestep: 48.8 MB vs 3DGS random-init 91 MB / GT-points 77 MB + ~6.2 GB point-cloud folder; per-timestep 3DGS would be 200–300 MB per step (20–30 GB per 100 frames).

Bibliometric SLR + BERTopic survey of 204 journal articles (2002–2024, Web of Science/SSCI) on AI and analytics in sports; verdict REJECT — no predictive model, no measured effect, no transferable technique. Four extracted themes by prominence: (1) performance modelling, (2) physical and mental health, (3) social media sentiment analysis, (4) tactical tracking. PRISMA funnel: 598 articles → 539 journal → 459 by research area → 339 after JCR-2025 5-year IF ≥ 2.0 filter → 204 after academic binary coding (135 excluded).

ATP Grand Slam point-prediction study (Wimbledon + US Open men's singles, 2016–2020, 709 matches, Jeff Sackmann point-by-point data, 57 features, LR/RF/AdaBoost/XGBoost vs naive serve-prior); verdict REJECT — honest negative result: every ML method matches or underperforms the naive baseline.

Tennis descriptives: server point-win rates 73.2% (first serve), 57.2% (second serve), 64.8% overall; 68.19% (AD) / 68.15% (deuce) of successful first serves went close to sidelines vs 29.04% / 30.3% for second serves. First-serve 10-fold CV: all four ML models accuracy = 73.2% (equal to baseline), recall 0.0% — the models never predict the returner. Second-serve CV: XGBoost 53.0%, AdaBoost 52.8%, RF 53.0%, LR 52.7% vs baseline 57.2% (all ~4 pp below).

ATP XGBoost-gain feature importance: the strongest features were score/state features (P1SetsWon, P2SetsWon, P2BreakPointWonA/P2BreakPointMissedA, ranks, surface); accumulated serve/return features had no significant influence. The paper's own conclusion: public summary features cannot beat the serve prior; Hawk-Eye spatiotemporal data exists but is not public — a cautionary citation that point-level prediction with public summary features degenerates to the prior.

MambaMOT: a learned Mamba (selective state-space) motion predictor replacing the Kalman filter in tracking-by-detection MOT pipelines, with MambaMOT+ adding a trajectory-embedding head that merges fragmented tracklets in O(N) via cosine similarity + hierarchical clustering (vs O(N²) Siamese mergers); verdict ADAPT — take the MambaMOT+ O(N) tracklet merger; defer to sibling paper 0063 (MambaTrack, SportsMOT HOTA 72.6 vs MambaMOT+ 71.3) for the motion model itself.

MambaMOT SSM: y(t) = C·h(t); h(t) = A·h(t−1) + B·x(t). Cosine embedding loss: L_cos(i,j) = 1 − cos(f_i,f_j) if i=j; max(0, cos(f_i,f_j)) if i≠j; L_total = L_pred + L_cos with L_pred = L_giou + L_mse. Tracklet merging: per-tracklet embeddings → cosine similarity → hierarchical clustering with temporal-50-frames / spatial-50-pixels veto gates.
equation: y(t) = C·h(t); h(t) = A·h(t−1) + B·x(t); L_cos(i,j) = 1 − cos(f_i,f_j) if i=j; max(0, cos(f_i,f_j)) if i≠j; L_total = L_pred + L_cos

claim: DanceTrack test: MambaMOT HOTA 55.5, MambaMOT+ 56.1 vs ByteTrack 47.3 (+8.2 HOTA for MambaMOT); SportsMOT test: MambaMOT+ 71.3 vs ByteTrack 62.0; inference 28.8 FPS on a single GPU (real-time) vs <10 FPS for transformer trackers like MOTR.

Bayesian predictive-density study of the time until the r-th goal in NHL hockey (unrestricted gamma waiting-time vs ancillary-information-restricted version); verdict REJECT. Waiting-time model: X|λ ~ Gam(r, λ), pdf p_λ(x) = x^{r−1} e^{−x/λ} / (Γ(r) λ^r), x > 0. KL prediction error on 2016–17: pe(q̂_1) = 0.04 vs pe(q̂_0) = 0.45 — the restricted estimator wins ~11× under KL.

Ancillary information (past points / specialist opinion as an order restriction) shifts the predicted 3rd-goal time later: mode 17.92 → 28.13, mean 28.35 → 33.12, P20 14.38 → 19.06, P50 26.62 → 32.82, P90 50.30 → 53.48.

Kernel-resident MCP tool-governance gateway (~286K lines of Rust) forcing every agent tool call through six layers in fixed order: schema validation (0.10 µs), trust-tier check (1.15 µs), per-agent token-bucket rate limit (0.02 µs), adversarial regex prefilter DFA (7.50 µs), ProbeLogits semantic gate (358/332/556 ms per classification on Qwen2.5-7B/Llama 3 8B/Mistral 7B), constitutional policy match (1.83 µs); Blake3-hashed audit chain (0.73 µs) in a 4 MB ring buffer (~30K records); FAIL-CLOSED: if the inference engine is unavailable, all tool calls are denied system-wide until recovery. Verdict ADAPT for the portable 6-layer pattern + ProbeLogits primitive + fail-closed audit chain.

ProbeLogits score: s = logit(Dangerous) − logit(Safe) at the verbalizer position, calibration bias subtracted, scaled by alpha; threshold s > 0 rejects (equations reconstructed from garbled PDF, flagged uncertain). Graduated response: deny when ANS and p > 0.90; LogWarn band [0.70, 0.90]; below 0.70 proceed; production default alpha = 0.9.
equation: s = logit(Dangerous) − logit(Safe); threshold s > 0 reject

claim: Governed-MCP evaluation: Custom-101 full pipeline F1 = 0.789 (accuracy 84.2%, precision 0.769, recall 0.811; TP 30, FN 7, FP 9, TN 55); ablation — no ProbeLogits F1 = 0.357 (TP10/FN27; ΔF1 = −0.432: hand-rule firewalling admits 27/37 dangerous calls), so the semantic layer is load-bearing. HarmBench non-copyright block rate: 99.0% / 98.0% / 98.7% (Qwen2.5-7B / Llama 3 8B / Mistral 7B). ToxicChat: ProbeLogits-Llama-3 F1 0.679 vs Llama Guard 3 0.675 (parity, +10.5 pp recall, 2.4–3.4× lower latency).

SportSQL: an interactive system answering arbitrary natural-language questions over live sports data — entity resolution (mentions → DB ids before SQL generation) → schema-only LLM SQL generation (LLM sees the schema, not the data), executed read-only → just-in-time materialized views for expensive temporal queries → verified visualizations (Matplotlib/Seaborn plotting code must reproduce the query dataframe byte-for-byte before rendering); verdict ADOPT for GSE's nflverse/odds tables. Code: https://github.com/coral-lab-asu/SportSQL.

DSQABench results (1,793 questions from 180 base templates × 3 rephrasings): Gemini 2.0 Flash — string EM 76.23, table correctness 0.64, completeness 0.76, overall 0.69; GPT-4o — EM 80.48, correctness 0.70, completeness 0.81, overall 0.75. By primitive: single Retrieve 100%, Order 97.6%, Calculate+Compare 96.3%, Retrieve+Filter+Calculate 22.3%, Compare+Order 30.3%, Manipulate/join 15.4%; by primitive count: one 93%, two 67%, beyond three ≈50% — compositional join/aggregation queries are the bottleneck.

Market-maker/market-taker study proving a strictly inferior price-predicting model can generate systematic profits via a decorrelation training objective that penalizes agreement with the market; verdict in source: ADOPT the MSE* decorrelation objective. Ideal loss: MSE*_Ω(R,M,T) = (1/|Ω|) Σ_i (t_i − r_i)² + γ·(t_i − r_i)(m_i − r_i), γ > 0; betting-adapted: MSE*_Ω(R,M,T) = E[(T − R)² − γ·(T − M)²] with m_i = bookmaker probabilities from odds; γ trades accuracy vs decorrelation. Kelly wealth-growth decomposition: W_G = D_KL(R||M) − D_KL(R||T); positive Kelly returns ⟺ XENT_Ω(R,T) < XENT_Ω(R,M).
equation: MSE*_Ω(R,M,T) = (1/|Ω|) Σ_i (t_i − r_i)² + γ·(t_i − r_i)(m_i − r_i), γ > 0; W_G = D_KL(R||M) − D_KL(R||T)

claim: Decorrelation results on NBA 2006–2014 (9,093 games, Pinnacle closing odds margin ≈2.5%): without odds feature, γ=0.4 gives W_sharpe = 1.74±0.14 (best; accuracy 67.15, below bookmaker's 69±2.5); with odds feature γ=0.4 gives 1.49±0.10; unif staking never profitable (best −0.39±0.22). Model–market Pearson correlation: 0.87 (no-odds) vs 0.95 (with-odds) — the odds feature raises correlation. Simulation: at Corr(T,R)=0.85, raising Corr(T,M) from 0.85→0.95 drops W_sharpe from 11.15% to −1.73% at fixed accuracy; Theorem: for unbiased estimators, Corr[T,M|R] = −1 maximizes essential profitability; fractional Kelly benefits from decorrelation while full Kelly is blind to it. Caveat: decorrelation can hurt if the model is already superior to the market.

Exact MCMC sampler for target distributions π(x) ∝ p₀(x)e^{s(x)} where the score s(x) is only accessible through stochastic pairwise-preference judges following the Bradley–Terry model; verdict in source: ADAPT as a DFS slate sampler with a BT-consistent scoring judge, not raw LLM votes. N-vote acceptance rule: α_N(x,x′;K) = min{1, r₀(x,x′)·K/(N−K+1)}; exact for every integer N ≥ 1, Peskun–Tierney optimal among exact rules with the same proposal and N queries. BT pairwise probability: p_J(x≺x′) = σ(s(x′)−s(x)); ideal oracle: α*(x,x′) = min{1, r₀(x,x′)·p/(1−p)} with r₀ = p₀(x′)q(x|x′)/[p₀(x)q(x′|x)]; multi-judge: α = min{1, r₀·∏_i K_i/(N−K_i+1)}.

Pref-MH results: image generation 63.6% preference success vs 7.4% Pointwise-MH vs 4.5% base (aesthetic 6.395/6.289/6.287); molecule design: QED 0.698±0.002, SA 0.781±0.001, diversity 0.899±0.001; R-hat → 1, ESS grows with chain length for all N ≥ 1. Theorem: no exact oracle-based BT-MH implementation exists with fixed sampling budget. Key assumption: judge votes follow Bradley–Terry (transitive latent scores, independent votes, stationary judge); exactness evaporates under non-BT judges.

Nguyen & Yurko (2026) Bayesian 'step-and-turn' generative framework for NFL ball-carrier movement evaluation: models step length and turn angle from 10 Hz NFL Big Data Bowl 2025 tracking (weeks 1–9 2022, 5,400 RB run plays), then ghost-simulates an 'average player' (H=100 hypothetical steps per frame, new random effect from N(0, τ²), other 21 players fixed) to compute yards-vs-ghost value metrics; verdict in source: ADAPT as a 'Ghost Score' RB evaluation module. Step length: s̃_ijt ~ N(μ^(SL)_ijt, σ²), μ^(SL) = α_0^(SL) + Xβ^(SL) + u_j + v_k; u_j ~ N(0, τ²_u), v_k ~ N(0, τ²_v); turn angle: φ_ijt ~ von Mises(μ^(TA)_ijt, κ_ijt), log κ_ijt = γ_0 + γ_1 s_ijt + w_j. Play value: ℓ̂_ijt = Σ_{l=10}^{110} l·P(L_ijt = l | X_ijt) (CatBoost); frame δ^(h)_ijt = ℓ̂_ijt − ℓ̂^(h)_ijt; Yards success rate = (1/H)Σ_h 1(δ^(h)_ijt > 0); Explosiveness = 1(ℓ̂_ijt > q_0.95(ℓ̂^(h)_ijt)). Code: https://github.com/qntkhvn/nflstepturn.

Ghost-score leaderboards (weeks 1–9 2022, ≥70 attempts): Yards success rate top 5 — Josh Jacobs 0.542, Miles Sanders 0.539, Travis Etienne 0.527, Dameon Pierce 0.512, James Robinson 0.507; bottom 5 — Michael Carter 0.446, A.J. Dillon 0.448, Cordarrelle Patterson 0.450, Raheem Mostert 0.453, Christian McCaffrey 0.457. Explosiveness top 5 — Etienne 0.118, Aaron Jones 0.095, Kenneth Walker 0.093, Sanders 0.092, Antonio Gibson 0.089; bottom 5 — Tyler Allgeier 0.035, Jamaal Williams 0.044, Dillon 0.050, David Montgomery 0.054, Carter 0.054. Step-length vs turn-angle random-effect correlation r = 0.279; Jonathan Taylor = least variable turn angle (matches 'straight-ahead runner' scouting).

EPFL student project (Rimbot, Jaggi & Barba, 2025) predicting bouldering-climbing move order ('beta') from unordered holds: all three prediction models fail — seq2seq predictions 'not even holds'; autoregressive Transformer collapsed to always outputting the padding token; simplified Transformer 35% accuracy on a length-14 sequence but only 2 non-padding tokens correctly predicted ('results look pretty random'); paper's own conclusion: 'not satisfying and would require more research'. Verdict: REJECT — no transfer path to GSE.

Chiang & Denes (2023) predicting table-tennis winners from TTNet video-capture stats (Tokyo 2020 Olympics + Bundesliga); verdict in source: ADAPT the feature-engineering pattern (paired advantage differentials + leave-one-match-out aggregates), not the sport or numbers. Features: RANKDIFF (zeroed when both players ranked >100), BALANCE = (|SA| + |SRA| + |FHA|) / 3 with SA = serve-minus-receive win %, SRA = short-minus-long-rally win %, FHA = forehand-minus-backhand win %; target y_i = {1 if P wins; −1 if P loses}. Portable template: advantage-differential matchup features (e.g., pass-vs-run EPA diff, home/road split diff) + BALANCE-style well-roundedness = mean of absolute differentials; RANKDIFF tail-saturation (clip/zero tiny rating differences between closely-rated teams); LOO-aggregate leakage audit.

Table-tennis results (with caveats — headline numbers use post-match in-match features, leaky): test accuracy/F1 — LR 0.722/0.706, MLP 0.694/0.703, sigmoid-SVM 0.694/0.621, RBF-SVM 0.667/0.600; ablation with vs without derived features (validation acc/F1): LR 0.699/0.705 vs 0.631/0.668, SVM-RBF 0.700/0.677 vs 0.500/0.591, MLP 0.696/0.708 vs 0.639/0.683 — all models worse without derived features; RF Gini: RANKDIFF most important; exclude-target-match aggregates (test): LR 0.639, RF 0.667, MLP 0.667 (61–67%) — comparable to live-feature numbers, taken as evidence against overfitting.

Ötting, Michels, Langrock & Deutscher (2021), the first study of live-betting market reaction at the stakes level (not odds level): a state-space model of 1 Hz bookmaker stakes (aggregated to 15s intervals, 306 Bundesliga 2018/19 matches, 274,778 intervals, 969 goals) testing whether bettors overreact to surprising news; verdict in source: ADAPT the ARX-ZAGA state-space design to NFL in-play odds-velocity proxies. Observed stakes y_t ~ ZAGA(μ_t, σ, π_t): f(y_t) = π_t if y_t=0; (1−π_t)h(y_t) if y_t>0; μ_t = exp(α_0 + g_t); g_t = φ g_{t−1} + η_t, |φ|<1; final ARX(1) state: g_t = φ g_{t−1} + β_1·halftime_t + β_2·ginidiff_t + Σ_{j=3}^{5} β_j·(1/goalteam^{(j)}_t) + σ_g η_t for surprising/slightly/un-surprising goals; surprise bins by pre-goal odds: >4.00 surprising, 2.00–4.00 slightly, <2.00 unsurprising.
equation: g_t = φ g_{t−1} + β_1·halftime_t + β_2·ginidiff_t + Σ_{j=3}^{5} β_j·(1/goalteam^{(j)}_t) + σ_g η_t

claim: Live-market reaction results: baseline φ̂ = 0.985 [0.984, 0.986] (strong serial correlation in latent activity); news effects: β̂_surprising = 0.531 [0.494, 0.567], β̂_slightly = 0.218 [0.176, 0.261], β̂_unsurprising = 0.034 [0.001, 0.067] — surprising-goal effect >15× the unsurprising effect, so bettors overreact to surprising news even though odds already shortened. β̂_ginidiff = −0.094 (activity rises as the match becomes MORE uncertain than at kickoff); eloteam α̂_1 = 0.439 (better teams attract more money); ΔAIC = 217,117 in favor of the state-space formulation over no-state regression; model checks: predicts no stakes in 7.3% of intervals vs true 7.2%, correctly predicts 96.5% of intervals where stakes were placed. Limitations: no out-of-sample test; single bookmaker, single season.

Macdonald (2012) regression-based adjusted plus-minus for NHL skaters via ridge regression on shift-stint outcomes, fitting on high-frequency proxy outcomes (shots, Fenwick, Corsi) rescaled to expected goals per 60 minutes for stability; verdict in source: REJECT for NFL — the shift-stint design needs per-play full lineups that nflverse lacks (near-total collinearity among fixed 11-man units); portable sub-ideas (ridge APM) already standard.

Kramov & Bauzha (2016): a hobbyist hardware build log for a ~$20 remote heart-rate telemetry device (PPG sensor → ATmega8 → Bluetooth HC-05 → Arduino Uno → Ethernet ENC28J60 → browser WebSocket/JSON); verdict: REJECT unconditionally — no mathematical model of any kind, no signal-processing equations, no validation, no error model, zero quantitative results (no accuracy figure, no Bland-Altman, no latency, no packet loss, no sample size). Arrhythmia 'detection' is simple threshold deviation with zero measured true/false positives; hardware stack is obsolete (HC-05 Bluetooth 2.0, ATmega8, ENC28J60); the stated '38,600 baud' is nonstandard (38,400 is standard).

Price, Cai, Shen & Hu (2022): a hierarchical causal model identifying team-level and league-level home-field advantage via paired home/away differencing (the return fixture cancels the neutral-field nuisance parameter), applied to 2020–21 EPL; verdict in source: ADAPT — the differencing trick transfers to NFL division games. Match model: Y_{i,j} = α_{i,j} + β_i + ε_{i,j}; return fixture: Y_{j,i} = −α_{i,j} + β_j + ε_{j,i}; paired cancellation: Y_{i,j} + Y_{j,i} = β_i + β_j + ε_{i,j} + ε_{j,i}; linear system H β + ε = Y; OLS β̂ = (HᵀH)⁻¹HᵀY; league effect Δ̂ = Σ_i β̂_i/n; hierarchy β_i ~ N(Δ, σ²). Causal definition: β_i = E_j{Y*(δ_i=1,δ_j=0) − Y*(δ_i=0,δ_j=0)}; assumptions (A1) SUTVA, (A2) ignorability (auto-holds: schedule pre-determined), (A3) non-monotonicity. Validated with a 1,000-replicate Monte Carlo.
equation: Y_{i,j} = α_{i,j} + β_i + ε_{i,j}; Y_{i,j} + Y_{j,i} = β_i + β_j + ε_{i,j} + ε_{j,i}; β̂ = (HᵀH)⁻¹HᵀY; Δ̂ = Σ_i β̂_i/n

claim: HFA findings (EPL 2020–21, 380 games, 11 per-game stats): 7 of 11 statistics significant at α=0.05, ALL offense-side (XG 0.232/0.092/0.011; Successful Key Passes 0.489/0.237/0.039; Touches in Box 2.253/1.043/0.031); defensive stats (interceptions, blocked shots) and the referee proxy (yellow cards) NOT significant; goals showed no significant HFA. Raw that season: 144 home wins (37.89%) vs 153 away wins (40.26%) — no raw home win edge — yet causal offensive effects remain positive. Teams with most significant team-level effects: Fulham, Brighton, Newcastle, Wolves — all bottom-half finishers (Fulham relegated): weaker teams retain larger home advantage. Caveats: 2020–21 was a COVID season (empty/reduced crowds — may explain no officiating/goal-level HFA); single season, n=20; NFL schedules aren't double round-robins (only division pairs give clean home+away).

Mendes-Neves et al. (2025): under the 2023 Springer Soccer Prediction Challenge's results-only-data constraint, forecasting match outcomes by modeling distributions of shot quantity and quality from ELO ratings, then Monte Carlo-simulating games; verdict in source: ADAPT the architecture (latent event distributions → simulation) to NFL play-count and EPA distributions. ELO: ELO_{i(t+1)} = ELO_{it} + K(O_{ijt} − P_{ijt}); P_{ijt} = 1/(1 + 10^{−(ELO_{it}−ELO_{jt})/a}); K=32, a=400, initial rating 500. Quantity: Quant_H = N(μ_quant, σ_quant²); Quality: Qual_H = N(μ_qual, σ_qual²); simulation: hs = [S_1..S_N], S ~ Qual_H, N ~ Quant_H; Home Goals = Σ_{i=1..N} I(hs_i > X_i), X_i ~ U(0,1). Two-stage pipeline: mean regressor from (ELO_H, ELO_A), then a second-stage model on residuals for σ. Code: https://github.com/nvsclub/SpringerSoccerChallengeCode.
equation: ELO_{i(t+1)} = ELO_{it} + K(O_{ijt} − P_{ijt}); P_{ijt} = 1/(1 + 10^{−(ELO_{it}−ELO_{jt})/a}); Home Goals = Σ_{i=1..N} I(hs_i > X_i), X_i ~ U(0,1)

claim: Distribution-simulation results: validation RPS — LR 0.215, KNN 0.213, DT 0.215, RF 0.213; test RPS 0.201 vs bookmaker 0.198 (worse than bookmakers); RMSE 1.58/1.64; MAE 1.65/1.66. Betting rentability: Strategy 1 (1 unit when bookmaker odds > model estimate) −0.8% absolute (+4.8% over the −5.6% bookmaker-margin baseline); Strategy 2 (stake = 1/forecasted odds) +1.1% absolute (+6.7% over baseline). Systematic draw underestimation: boosting draw likelihood by 27% improves RPS marginally; challenge finish within 5% of top entries. Limitations: profitability on an unaudited window; normal assumption mis-specified for skewed count data; quantity/quality independence assumed not tested.

Walsh & Joshi (2024): two identical NBA pipelines differing only in model selection metric (accuracy vs classwise-ECE) compared on season ROI, testing whether calibration — not accuracy — should select sports models; verdict in source: ADOPT as direct mandate — select on guarded classwise-ECE, size with fractional Kelly. Kelly: k = (pb − q)/b (p = model probability, q = 1−p, b = odds−1); perfect calibration: P(Ŷ = Y | P̂ = p) = p ∀ p ∈ [0,1]; classwise-ECE: (1/k)Σ_i Σ_j (|B_{j,i}|/n) |y_i(B_{j,i}) − p̄_i(B_{j,i})|, k classes, m=20 equal-width bins, with an 80%-nonempty-bins guard (violated → ECE set to 1) blocking the 'predict the base rate' degenerate. Pipeline hygiene: drop one of each Spearman-|ρ|>0.7 pair; season-to-date average differences vs opponents; two-sample KS tests at 1% on validation vs training drop drifted features; first 10 games per team-season are feature-burn only; chronological splits (CV explicitly rejected for sports).
equation: k = (pb − q)/b; P(Ŷ = Y | P̂ = p) = p ∀ p ∈ [0,1]; classwise-ECE: (1/k)Σ_i Σ_j (|B_{j,i}|/n) |y_i(B_{j,i}) − p̄_i(B_{j,i})|

claim: Calibration-selection results (NBA 2018/19, $10,000 start): fixed $100 — calibration SVM $13,244.51 (ROI 32.45%) vs accuracy SVM $10,556.29 (ROI 5.56%); eighth-Kelly — calibration SVM $13,692.86 (ROI 36.93%) vs accuracy SVM $2,409.66 (ROI −75.9%). Summary: calibration-driven SVM — 87.55% games bet, 38.8% won, accuracy 64.27%, classwise-ECE 4.46%, max ROI 36.93%; accuracy-driven SVM — 89.89% games bet, 38.46% won, accuracy 64.62%, classwise-ECE 5.03%, max ROI 5.56%. Mechanism: the accuracy-driven model's value-bet predictions clustered at probability extremes (variance 0.036 vs 0.034) — overconfident value bets self-destruct under Kelly. Limitations: single season, no ROI significance test; both branches converged on SVM so the contrast is confounded by differing feature subsets (6/8 differ); 80% guard 'somewhat arbitrary' (authors' words); NBA moneyline only.

Xu, Wei, Wells & Aryal (2026): Temporal Feature Distillation (TFD) + Temporal Gated Scale (TGS) module for label-efficient Precise Event Spotting (frame-accurate event detection) in tennis/figure skating/diving video via teacher-student EMA over unlabeled video; verdict: REJECT — video event-spotting for precision sports, no consumer in GSE's current stack (no video pipeline). Alignment loss: L_align = ‖F_s − F_t‖² (student vs teacher temporal feature maps); total L_TFD = L_sup + λ(t)·L_align, λ(t) cosine-ramped 0→1 over ten epochs after a five-epoch supervised warm-up. At 10% labels, mAP (Tennis/FS_Comp/FS_Perf/FineDiving): 80.19/38.29/50.29/52.87 — best in 14 of 16 dataset×fraction settings. TGS ablation (Tennis, 10% labels): ViT-Tiny 10.96 → +TGS 44.77 (+33.81); ViT-Small 46.32 → +TGS 68.39 (+16.83); +TFD → 80.19.

Dream11 industry paper on FENCE, a deployed production pipeline detecting users who create multiple fantasy-sports accounts to circumvent per-user contest-entry limits, at 190M+ user scale, in batch (historical graph: Random Forest-predicted + heuristic shared-attribute edges → Alternating connected components) and real-time (1-hop Redis neighborhood lookup on registration, 4-second SLA) modes; verdict recorded: REJECT for GSE — anti-fraud/account-integrity, no transfer to prediction, calibration, or DFS-optimization lanes. Automated-flow precision 96.7%, training recall 55.2%; manual-review precision 70.2%, recall 86.4%; automatic-action threshold cluster score > 0.95; relative 86% decrease in false-positive volume after deployment. No public data/code (unverifiable).

NODE baseball-pitching study: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations learning the low-dimensional dynamical structure of full-body pitching and predicting the full motion from only its initial segment, without predefined order parameters or stationarity assumptions; verdict: ADAPT — the method (transformer-encoded latent space + neural-ODE flow from ~8% initial conditions) is portable to NFL tracking trajectory forecasting. Equations: dẑ(t)/dt = f_θ(z(t), t) (3-layer MLP, 2 hidden × 128, tanh); L = λ_recon L_recon + λ_KL L_KL (λ_recon = 1.0, λ_KL = 1×10⁻³); R²(t) = 1 − SS_res(t)/SS_ori(t). Architecture: transformer encoder (3 layers, 8 heads, dim 256, causal mask) maps x_{0:T−1} ∈ R^{T×45} to K=12 latent points in d=3; z_0 encodes ~first 8% of motion; MLP decoder (2 hidden × 256 ReLU) reconstructs 45-D joints. Code: https://github.com/takamido/NODE_baseball_pitching.
equation: dẑ(t)/dt = f_θ(z(t), t); L = λ_recon L_recon + λ_KL L_KL; R²(t) = 1 − SS_res(t)/SS_ori(t)

claim: NODE pitching results (lab mocap, 8 collegiate pitchers, 16 cameras @ 200 Hz, 15 joints → 45-D, 968 pitches): mean RMSE 66.1 ± 15.7 mm over the full prediction interval; mean R² 0.46 ± 0.20 over the entire motion, 0.49 ± 0.20 over the second half — ~50% of variance in the latter half of the motion explained from only the initial ~8% of the sequence. NODE prediction mitigates late-phase error growth the training-mean baseline suffers. Limitations: reconstructed motions are more stereotyped than ground truth (~50% of variance dropped — deterministic model averages away functional variability); no cross-pitcher evaluation (per-pitcher models only); expert-only sample; point predictions, no uncertainty.

CausalTraj: a temporally-causal, likelihood-based multi-agent trajectory forecaster fixing the incoherence of per-agent-scored models — learns the true joint distribution of multi-agent futures via a per-timestep Mixture-of-Gaussians on displacements, SOTA on joint metrics (minJADE/minJFDE) with competitive per-agent accuracy; verdict: ADAPT — port the causal MoG stack + joint-metric evaluation protocol to NFL tracking, with richer player–ball covariance than their block-diagonal assumption. Causal factorization: p(X_{P+1:T} | X_{1:P}) = ∏_{t=P}^{T−1} p(X_{t+1} | X_{1:t}); per-timestep ΔX_{t+1} = X_{t+1} − X_t, output mixture of M=8 Gaussians: p(ΔX_{t+1} | X_{1:t}) = Σ_m π_{t+1,m} N(ΔX_{t+1}; μ, Σ), covariance block-diagonal per agent via Cholesky factors L_{t,m,n} = [[exp(ℓ¹¹),0],[ℓ²¹,exp(ℓ²²)]], Σ̂ = LLᵀ. Loss: L_NLL = −E_t log Σ_m π̂ N(Y_t; μ̂, Σ̂) plus entropy regularizer L_ent = −(1/log M) Σ_m π̂ log(π̂+ε); total L = L_NLL − λ_ent L_ent, λ_ent = 0.05. Code: https://github.com/wezteoh/causaltraj.
equation: p(ΔX_{t+1} | X_{1:t}) = Σ_m π_{t+1,m} N(ΔX_{t+1}; μ, Σ); L = L_NLL − λ_ent L_ent, λ_ent = 0.05

claim: CausalTraj results: Football-U (yards, 20-frame, k=20) joint minJADE20/JFDE20 = 1.12/2.68 vs MoFlow 1.16/2.82, MoFlow joint-obj 1.19/2.87, Sports-Traj 3.66/3.46 (per-agent: MoFlow slightly ahead 0.16/0.27 vs 0.16/0.31). NBA SportVU 4.0 s joint: 1.38/2.57 (best) vs LED 1.63/2.99, MoFlow 1.69/3.31, GroupNet 2.12/3.72; per-agent 4.0 s: MoFlow 0.71/0.87 best. Basketball-U joint: 0.97/1.77 vs MoFlow 1.18/2.30. Ablation (Basketball-U joint): full 0.97/1.77 → no spatial-relation encoder 0.99/1.81 → single Gaussian 1.03/1.86 → component-mean sampling 1.05/2.13. MoFlow's joint-objective loss variant barely moved joint metrics — loss changes alone don't learn joint structure. Failure modes: ball carried with unrealistically large ball–player gap, ball–boundary collisions (traced to block-diagonal covariance: no cross-agent covariance within a component).

Unsupervised temporal segmentation of sports movement into biomechanical phases (demo: javelin throw — steps, drive, throw, recovery) from video pose sequences without frame-level labels, via a two-stage pipeline: Adaptive ST-GCN denoising autoencoder (3 Adaptive ST-GCN blocks, Chebyshev order 7, 64-d → MLP to 40-d latent; L_total = L_MSE + λ_vel L_vel) then structured unbalanced optimal transport over latent 'phase prototypes' (visual cost = cosine distance between latent embeddings; fused Gromov-Wasserstein temporal-structure term + Kantorovich appearance term + KL relaxation toward a prior; frame label = rowwise argmax of the transport plan) with a pseudo-label cross-entropy loop; verdict: ADAPT — transferable recipe for unsupervised NFL play-phase segmentation, rebuilt without the paper's phase-count oracle K. Critical assumption: K is fixed to the known ground-truth phase count — a phase-count oracle, a hard blocker for NFL. Javelin dataset: 211 videos (111 men/100 women), MMPose 16-joint MPII skeletons. Released: https://github.com/Bikudebug/Javelin_Throw_Dataset.

Unsupervised segmentation results (test vs manual annotations): Ours 71.02 mAP / 74.61 F1 / 48.01 mIoU / 64.04 MoF vs TOT 33.32/33.70/20.21/34.90, TOT+TCL 39.30/50.03/41.32/50.87, CTE 54.82/62.74/50.58/63.42, ASOT 60.20/57.55/41.80/61.19. mIoU (48.01) markedly lower than F1 (74.61) — frame classification strong, boundary localization weak (matters for timing-sensitive applications like snap/release timing). Limitations: K-oracle untested without oracle; global Hungarian alignment inflates operational realism (offline/transductive); no CIs or significance tests; one sport, 211 videos.

Silent-Impact study: can tennis shots be detected and classified from IMU data on the passive (non-dominant) wrist — where there is no impact jerk — at accuracy comparable to dominant-arm sensing, so users can wear the smartwatch they already own; verdict: REJECT — recreational-wearable tennis shot tracking has no transfer path to NFL prediction or analytics. Results: classification (5-fold, participant-grouped) — passive arm 88.2 ± 2.0% vs dominant 90.1 ± 3.0% (gap only 1.9%; Ganser FCN baseline passive 81.4% vs dominant 90.5%, gap 9.1%); frequency-band attention (Fourier bands 0–4 Hz whole-body / 5–20 Hz arm swing / >20 Hz impact vibration, per Ji & Pachi 2005, Khusainov et al. 2013) improved passive-arm performance +6.8% vs the FCN but added nothing on the dominant arm (−0.4%). Detection: MS-TCN passive accuracy 95.6%, F1 86.0% vs threshold-peak baseline passive 77.8%/37.6%; dominant 98.5%/94.8%. Data: 20 recreational players, Xsens DOT IMUs both wrists @120 Hz, 6,000 shot sequences, 368 minutes of rallies (2,259 shots). Public: https://github.com/jyp0802/Silent-Impact.

Dissertation testing Multimodal LLM (VideoLLaMA2, LoRA fine-tuned) tennis video understanding — single-event action classification then the harder unsolved task of full event-sequence identification in a rally — and whether traditional CV detectors or vision-encoder fine-tuning close the gap; verdict: ADAPT the 'structured-CV-features-as-text-in-the-prompt' hybrid pattern (edit score 76.0 vs benchmark 82.1) as the portable lesson; raw MLLM video reasoning is too weak to use directly. Normalized segmental edit score (Lea et al. 2016): Edit Score = (1 − (event additions, deletions or replacements needed) / (number of events in longer label)) × 100. Data: FineTennis (F³Set, arXiv:2504.08222) — 7,445 train / 2,271 test rally videos from Grand Slams, 56 event types. Code: https://github.com/bigcrushes/videollama2_tennis.
equation: Edit Score = (1 − (event additions, deletions or replacements needed) / (number of events in longer label)) × 100

claim: Tennis MLLM results: single-event (8 epochs): e1 0.96, e2 0.73, e3 0.83, e4 0.72, e5 0.96, overall 0.41. Rally edit scores (10 epochs): default 34.4 → 32-frame sampling 39.7 → oracle event count in prompt 49.8 (diagnostic) → self-predicted count 30.0 (pipeline collapsed). CV-feature fusion: 32-frame default 39.7 → bboxes drawn in video 18.2 (halved — drawn lines break the vision encoder) → bboxes in prompt 61.3 → bboxes + court corners + ball coords in prompt every 2 frames 76.0 (approaching the 82.1 benchmark) → 17 keypoints every 20 frames + court + ball 50.7. STC connector alone: 0.018 (random-level — connector features near-useless). CLIP fine-tuned separately then reloaded into VideoLLaMA2: single-event 0.55 (10 ep)/0.56 (6 ep); sequence task 54.6 (up from 39.7). Qualitative: strong textual pattern learning (serve start, near/far alternation), poor video understanding.

SpineTrack + SpinePose: a dataset with nine vertebral keypoints (C1, C4, C7, T3, T8, L1, L3, L5, sacrum — existing datasets collapse the spine to a single rigid segment) and a teacher–student distillation model extending RTMPose estimating fine-grained 2D spine pose in unconstrained in-the-wild images without degrading standard body-pose performance; verdict: ADAPT — spine-curvature keypoints are a novel biomechanical feature source for QB throwing-mechanics / OL posture analysis, banked as a future CV idea (GSE has no video-pose pipeline today). Loss (Eq. 9): L_total = α L_pos + β L_distill + γ_1 L_structure + γ_2 L_spine (ablations: α=5, β=2.5, γ_1=0.1, γ_2=0.5); L_pos = Σ_{k∈K_student} KL(p_{s,k}, g_k) (KL vs GT heatmaps); L_distill = Σ_{k∈K_body} KL(p_{s,k}, p_{t,k}) (distill Body8 teacher); L_structure = (1/(π|B|)) Σ_b |Δφ_b|, Δφ_b = atan2(sin(φ^p_b−φ^g_b), cos(φ^p_b−φ^g_b)) (bone-angle orientation penalty); L_spine = MSE({s_i}, {s̃_i}), s̃_i = s̃_{i−1} + w_i(s_i − s̃_{i−1}), w_i = 1 − 0.5σ(α(‖s_i − s̃_{i−1}‖ − T)) (differentiable smoothing dampening abrupt spinal bends). Data: SpineTrack-Unreal (~25k synthetic frames, UE5) + SpineTrack-Real (33k+ annotations from COCO/YogaPose); 50,962 images, 58,766 annotated humans, 35 keypoints.
equation: L_total = α L_pos + β L_distill + γ_1 L_structure + γ_2 L_spine; L_pos = Σ_{k∈K_student} KL(p_{s,k}, g_k); L_distill = Σ_{k∈K_body} KL(p_{s,k}, p_{t,k}); L_structure = (1/(π|B|)) Σ_b |Δφ_b|

claim: SpinePose results: SpineTrack Spine AP — SpinePose-s 89.6 (AR 90.7), -m 91.4 (92.5), -l 91.0 (92.2), -x 89.3 (91.0); same-family baselines score 0.0 on spine (they lack the keypoints). Retention: SpinePose-l COCO AP 75.2 / AR 79.5 vs RTMPose-l 76.9/81.5; Halpe26 77.0/81.1 vs 78.4/82.9 — spine extension costs ~1.5–2.1 AP points. Ablation (SpinePose-l, COCO/Halpe26/SpineTrack AP): no-distill 69.6/72.2/87.0 → +distill 70.8/73.2/87.3 → +distill+spine-smooth 74.7/76.6/88.7 (spine smoothness adds +3.9/+3.4 on benchmarks — surprising, attributed to 'rule-based knowledge' preventing interference) → all losses 75.2/77.0/88.4 (best on all three). NFL caveats: helmets/pads/jerseys occlude torso landmarks entirely — pads likely defeat the visual cues; GT bboxes at validation (real detector performance lower); 10-epoch fine-tune only credible via Body8 teacher init.

Group2Int: an end-to-end diffusion framework for multi-agent trajectory prediction that conditions generation on team-level tactic labels via classifier-free guidance and models group interaction as a cooperative game, using a learned Banzhaf Interaction to capture each agent's cooperation tendency toward potential tactics; also releases an NBA SportVU extension with human-annotated tactics as a new joint trajectory+tactic benchmark; verdict: ADAPT — closest published analog to what NFL tracking-based live win-probability and prop pricing needs; port requires swapping human-annotated basketball tactics for NGS scheme labels and scaling from 11 to 22 agents. Key equations: g_i = [a_i; c_{i,m(i)}], G = f_ϕ(X,L); classifier-free guidance f_ε(y,G) = f_ε(y,A) + s_g·(f_ε(y,G) − f_ε(y,A)), s_g = 0.1; DDPM reverse, 100 diffusion steps; L_dist = min_s ‖Y − Ŷ_s‖₂ (variety over S=20 samples); Banzhaf learner f(·) = γ_o(SA(γ_ctx(A))) predicts N×k agent–tactic matrix, supervised by masked-attention heuristic I_B^j = (S_a2t + S_t2a)/2; w_j = Fusion(Ĝ_j, I_pred^j) → GAT+MLP tactic head, top-k via argmax, focal loss γ=4.0; total L = L_noise + L_dist + η·L_unc + α·(L_tactic + β·L_bi), game factor 0.001.
equation: f_ε(y,G) = f_ε(y,A) + s_g·(f_ε(y,G) − f_ε(y,A)), s_g = 0.1; L_dist = min_s ‖Y − Ŷ_s‖₂; I_B^j = (S_a2t + S_t2a)/2; L = L_noise + L_dist + η·L_unc + α·(L_tactic + β·L_bi)

claim: Group2Int results: NBA SportVU (minADE/minFDE, k=20 best-of-20): 1 s: 0.19/0.29; 2 s: 0.39/0.59; 3 s: 0.61/0.86; 4 s: 0.84/1.17 — beats LED by 9.5% (1 s ADE) and ~5.6% (4 s ADE; LED 0.89/1.24). TeamTrack-soccer (ADE/FDE at 1.2/2.4/3.6/4.8 s): 0.23/0.45, 0.58/1.10, 1.00/1.89, 1.48/2.72 — beats LED 15.4% ADE / 9.6% FDE at 4.8 s. TeamTrack-basketball: beats LED 14.4% ADE / 30.3% FDE at 4.8 s. Tactic prediction Top-1/2/3/5: 60.23/81.15/90.53/96.79 vs Pooling* 55.22/75.82/86.05/94.67, finetuned Llama3-8B* 38.17. Ablation denoising (4 s): MLP 5.28/8.71, query-based 1.24/1.63, diffusion 0.84/1.17. Ablation Banzhaf: no-BI Top-1 58.44 vs team-level 60.09 / scene-level 60.23 (~+2 pp). Ball has highest Banzhaf interaction (~0.285) for both teams. Data: 90,618 sequences × 30 frames (11 agents), 16 tactic labels from 25 trained humans, 8,238 JSON entries + .npy trajectories, 70/30 split. Limitations: 70/30 split not stated game-disjoint (sequence-level splits leak); primary task conditions on observed tactic labels — production must recognize tactics first (recognition gap); best-of-20 flatters generators; Banzhaf 'supervision' is a masked-attention heuristic, not a game-theoretic oracle.

A four-spike plan for AWS work (Amplify fit review, AWS gate enforcement via apps/web/lib/fable/aws-gates.ts, a SageMaker model-card template mirror, a Clean Rooms contract checklist), all local and zero-cost; standing rule: all spikes stay local unless the owner explicitly approves live AWS work. Not engine-actionable beyond a checklist; included as a program-completeness record.

Spec for the GSE B2B sports intelligence API: three v1 endpoints (/api/v1/probabilities, /api/v1/openapi, /api/v1/signals) with x-api-key auth and fail-closed key-tier scoping — a bare key exposes only FREE data, premium rows require an explicit opt-in ':premium' key suffix (case-insensitive suffix; constant-time key compare; fixed a leak where any key holder received Pro-gated confidence for PREMIUM items). Rate limits: ~60/min (signals), ~30/min (probabilities), Postgres-backed durable limiter; modelConfidence = 0–100 UX composite; signal payload carries claimPosture 'experimental_research_grade_not_verified_roi' while performance is unpublished; free public embed at /embed/edge-index/[gameId].

A 221-byte archive banner stating the ops/archive directory is non-canonical history and operators must use CANONICAL.md + the production /cockpit as the system of truth — explicit rule: do not update archived files as if they were current law. Procedural marker only; included for program completeness.

A Cox-process (doubly stochastic Poisson) framework can jointly model soccer match events (home/away goals, home/away red cards) and random referee stoppage-time lengths with state-dependent intensities, and its log-likelihood is strictly concave when regressors are linearly independent, making MLE a unique, convex optimization problem.

The parametric log-likelihood of the joint event model is l(xi) = -sum_j[int_0^T exp(sum_i xi^j_i psi^j_i(r))dr - sum_l(sum_i xi^j_i psi^j_i(t^j_l))] + sum_k[U^k sum_i xi_i phi_i - exp(sum_i xi_i phi_i) - ln(U^k!)], where T = 90 + U_1 + U_2 and U_k are stoppage minutes.
Log-linear event intensities take the form ln lambda^j(t) = sum_i xi^j_i psi^j_i(t) and log-linear stoppage-time means ln pi_k = sum_i xi_i phi_i.

On 3,039 Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A matches (2015-2022), a red card reduces the receiving team's goal intensity by 30.48% while multiplying the opponent's goal intensity by 1.4385; losing by one goal raises goal rate by 10.11% and losing by two raises it 21.24%.

The fitted full model (G4S5R) predicts 27.48% draws vs 27.42% observed, substantially better calibrated than a static Maher model's 24.46%/27.32% on 27.92% observed, and beats simpler models on result and exact-score predictive log-likelihood from minute 30 onward via 100,000-scenario forward simulation per match.

A hybrid video-tracking architecture combining a costly accurate detector (Faster-RCNN run once every 'jump' frames as supervisor/auto-initializer) with a cheap per-frame tracker (KCF every frame inside an ROI) and SSD refinement achieves both speed and accuracy: per-player average IoU overlap 0.600-0.653, 84.98-91.75 fps, AUC 0.600-0.660, vs Faster-RCNN alone at ~45ms/frame and AUC 0.32.

In the hybrid tracker, drift correction should only adjust the fast tracker's box when it diverges from the supervisor detector for more than 3 consecutive frames; correcting at first disagreement was found experimentally unstable.

Per-frame precision is defined as average IoU overlap phi = (ground-truth box intersect tracked box)/(union), success threshold IoU > 0.5, and the OPE curve is the percentage of frames above threshold across thresholds with AUC as its integral over [0,1].

From sparse event-only soccer data (positions known only at ball events), mini-batch K-means (K=200) over 660,848 movement vectors (start/end positions, time, speed, possession flag) builds per-player normalized cluster histograms whose cosine distances yield similar-player comps; uniqueness is the sum of distances to 5 nearest neighbors U_i = sum_{j=1}^{M} d_ij.

Player consistency across time periods is measured as C_i^k = (1/N) sum_t D(c_i^k, c_i^t), the average distance between the period-k profile and all other periods' profiles; on 2012/13 La Liga Opta data Messi scored uniqueness 0.860 / consistency 0.30 vs Cristiano Ronaldo 0.55 / 0.51.

A regularized adjusted plus/minus (APM) rating for CS:GO regresses match score differential on a design matrix of +1/-1/0 participation indicators (ResultDiff_i = sum_j X_ij beta_j + eps_i, X_ij in {+1,-1,0}) with ridge, elastic-net, and hierarchical Bayesian variants using a standardized box-score Rating2.0 as prior mean.

On 2018-2023 HLTV CS:GO matches, Pearson p-values for predicted-vs-true plus/minus correlation were ridge 0.57 (non-significant), Bayesian 0.03323, logistic 2.092e-05, elastic logistic 2.2e-16; the paper reports no correlation magnitudes, MAE, log-loss, or calibration, making the predictive evidence uninterpretable, and its random 80/20 split leaks rosters across train/test.

Per-team 2-state hidden Markov models with covariate-driven transition probabilities gamma_ij^(p) = exp(eta_ij^(p))/sum_k exp(eta_ik^(p)), eta_ij^(p) = beta_0^(ij) + sum_l beta_l^(ij) x_l^(p), predict NFL run/pass play calls at 0.715 weighted out-of-sample accuracy on 2018 (vs ~0.67 pbp-only baselines, 58.4% naive pass baseline), ranging 0.602 (Seattle) to 0.779 (New England).

The HMM play-call match likelihood follows the forward-algorithm form L = delta P(y_{m,1}) Gamma^{(m,2)} P(y_{m,2)} ... Gamma^{(m,P_m)} P(y_{m,P_m)} 1, and one-step-ahead forecasting uses likelihood-with-candidate over likelihood-without (Zucchini et al. 2016) with argmax as the class forecast.

Across 51 physical-AI benchmarks, mean pairwise Spearman correlation is 0.487 (all positive); median benchmark has roughly half its variance reconstructible from the other 11 (leave-one-model-out ridge R^2), and collapsing just two substitute pairs moves 22 of 51 models by >=3 ranking places.

Benchmark redundancy can be audited with three tools: uniqueness = 1 - LOO R^2 (ridge regression of each benchmark on the rest), greedy utility U(b|S) = g(b)*(1 - R^2(b~S)) where g(b) is the Gini coefficient of the score distribution, and Bradley-Terry ranking P(i>j) = sigma(r_i - r_j) with Elo_i = 1500 + 400*r_i/ln(10).

A single principal component explains 55.2% of the 12-benchmark suite variance and tracks general vision-language capability at Spearman rho=0.952; residualizing on it halves mean pairwise correlation from 0.487 to 0.250.

A two-stage adaptive prediction protocol combines offline nonlinear-least-squares base fitting under KL-quantified distribution shift with an online meta layer aggregating N parallel models by exponential loss weighting: y_{t+1}^{pred} = sum_i w_{t,i} y_{t+1,i}^{pred}; w_{t+1,i} = w_{t,i} exp(-lambda l_t) / sum_j w_{t,j} exp(-lambda l_t).

Per-model projected LMS updates take the form beta_hat_{t+1,i} = Pi_D{beta_hat_{t,i} + phi_t/(d + m_t^2)*(y_{t+1} - beta_hat_{t,i}^T phi_t)} with discount accumulator m_{t+1} = gamma*(...), gamma in (0,1); the two-stage error decomposes as J_T <= J_mis + J_opt + J_est (mismatch + optimization + estimation, Theorem 18).

In simulation, meta-LMS average prediction error lies strictly below single-model LMS and fixed-parameter baselines across the horizon even when the offline estimate fails to converge, though the superiority claim is visual only with no exact error values or confidence intervals stated.

A CNN regressing pixel displacement from a basketball's center to its vertical ground projection, lifted to 3D via calibrated camera geometry, achieves MAPE 1.25+-0.11 m vs 2.88+-0.22 m for the diameter-based depth baseline on DeepSport, with best crop size 256 px (MAPE 1.04+-0.11).

The Murphy calibration-refinement decomposition states E[S(P,X)] = UNC - RES + REL, with empirical REL = S(p) - S(x_hat), RES = S(x 1_N) - S(x_hat), UNC = S(x 1_N); Brier skill score follows as BSS = 1 - BS/BS_ref = (RES - REL)/UNC.

Yates' Brier decomposition is E[S] = UNC - 2Cov(P,X) + Var_X[E_P(P|X)] + E_X[Var_P(P|X)] + [E(P)-E(X)]^2, and the likelihood-base form is E[S] = Var(P) - Var_X[E_P(P|X)] + E_X[(E_P(P|X) - X)^2]; logistic calibration logit[Pr(X_i=1)] = alpha + beta logit(p_i) with Wald/LR tests of alpha=0, beta=1 diagnoses over/under-forecasting shapes.

On 384 UCL group-stage matches, the Poisson-ELO model achieved Brier skill 24.8% on home wins (odds: 29.5%), 1.4% on draws ('unforecastable', near-climatological), and 21.2% on away wins; logistic calibration showed over-forecasting of home wins (alpha_hat=-0.259, p=0.030); discrimination C-statistics were HWIN 0.795 vs odds 0.820, AWIN 0.789 vs 0.820.

Structured-prediction consistency theory defines a calibration function H_{Phi,L,F}(eps) := inf_{f in F, q in Delta^k} delta_phi(f,q) s.t. delta_l(f,q) >= eps, giving the connection R_Phi(f) < R*_{Phi,F} + H_check(eps) => R_L(f) < R*_{L,F} + eps; averaged SGD with step gamma = 2D/(M sqrt(N)) needs sample complexity N* = 4D^2 M^2/H_check^2(eps).

The paper reports zero numerical results (pure theory): some task losses make learning harder than others, with exponential-in-output-size constants separating tractable from intractable task losses; classical 0-1 loss is ill-suited to structured prediction.

BoxMind recommends boxing tactical adjustments via the strategy gradient G_b = d y_hat/d I_{b,ind} (gradient of predicted win probability w.r.t. the 18 technical-tactical indicators), ranking the top-5 positive-gradient indicators; the fused BoxerGraph model hit 69.8% test accuracy (+9.5pp over best baseline) and 14/16 correct at the Olympics.

BoxMind's multi-task loss is L_total = alpha*L_MSE(I_hat_curr, I_GT) + beta*L_CE(y_hat, y_GT) with CE weight 1 and indicator weight 0.02; the latent time-variant embedding is E_b(t) = sum_{c=0}^{C-1} E_b^{(c)}*t^c and fusion is F_match = MLP_fusion(I_{b,ind} (+) E_b(t) (+) I_{o,ind} (+) E_o(t)).

Nonlinear age transforms Age.30 = |age - 30| and Age.int = 0 if 28 <= age <= 32 else min(|age-28|, |age-32|), entered as player differences alongside Elo, materially improve tennis prediction: RF with Points+Rank+Age.30+Elo reached 0.820 classification accuracy and Brier 0.151 on 2022 Grand Slams (5,013 matches, 47 tournaments, 2011-2022).

Under a rolling 12-tournament window, linear tennis models degraded sharply (classification ~0.647, Brier 0.293) while random forest with enhanced features held up (0.789 / 0.659 / 0.165); expanding-window best linear Brier was 0.153, spline Elo+Age.30 0.149.

The continuous-time within-play NFL valuation framework routes an expected-yards ball-carrier model through an RFCDE conditional density into expected points: E[g(Y*_{t,i}|F(X_{t,i}))] = integral g(Y*_{t,i}|F(X_{t,i}))*f_hat(Y*_{t,i}|F(X_{t,i}))*dX_{t,i}; the paper warns plugging point estimates into nonlinear EP/WP is biased. Ball-carrier models: E[Y*_{t,i}|F(X_{t,i})] = E[Y_{t,i}|F(X_{t,i})] + current yard line.

On NFL Big Data Bowl tracking data (6 weeks 2017, 1,075,720 frames), an LSTM (2 layers x 50 units, 20% recurrent dropout) had the lowest leave-one-week-out CV RMSE for ball-carrier expected yards at every point across the carry; XGBoost feature importance top-2 were closest-defender distance (defense1_dist_to_ball) and ball-carrier speed, with 9 Voronoi tessellation features as OL blocking-quality signals.

An exponential frequency fit frequency(N) ~= b*e^(-rN) on annual MLB HR totals predicted >50% chance of Bonds's 73-HR record falling within 5 years and >80% within 10 years; the prediction was falsified (no 74+ HR season since 2006), showing the parameter-stationarity assumption failed (steroid-era inflation).

Isotonic Bradley-Terry alternates rate learning argmin (1/|D_tra|) sum phi(sigma(r_i - r_j), y_ij) with sub-gradient descent and learning the link sigma by isotonic (monotone PAV) regression instead of assuming logistic; the isotonic link is the polyline connecting unique sorted (r_i - r_j, sigma_hat_ij) pairs constrained to non-decreasing, sigma(-u)=1-sigma(u), in [0,1], with closed-form inner solution = group mean and training error never increasing.

On synthetic Cauchy-link (misspecified) data, isotonic BT beat logistic BT on test win-prob error in most cells (e.g., n=25, N=1: 0.3956+-0.0474 BT vs 0.3689+-0.0489 IBT), with gains largest at small n,N (regularization effect) and large n,N (misspecification mitigation); IBT also withholds judgment via exact ties (sigma_hat=0.5) on undecidable pairs, improving Kendall's tau.

A Bradley-Terry tournament over pairwise algorithm comparisons (win if NDCG@10 higher; ties add 0.5 each; Pr(i>j) = p_i/(p_i+p_j), estimated by Zermelo MLE iteration p'_i = sum_j W_ij/sum_j (W_ij+W_ji)/(p_i+p_j)) yields more consistent rankings than mean/sum aggregation: triplet-ratio consistency BT 0.510 vs Mean 0.488, mean Kendall's tau BT 0.567 vs 0.542, and BT stays ~0.6 until >70% of comparisons are missing.

The transitive-triplets consistency ratio 1/((n choose 3)*D - missing) * sum_d sum_{i1!=i2!=i3} I{i1^d > i2^d > i3^d} measures ranking consistency robustly to missing comparisons (unlike mean Kendall's tau); a covariate-adjusted BT P(i>j|x) = sigma(beta_{i0}-beta_{j0}+<x,beta_i>-<x,beta_j>) with fusion penalty predicts rankings on unseen datasets, hitting top-1 at 0.28 vs 0.02 for naive mean.

An empirical Elo tuning protocol enumerates candidate experience-based K-factor schedules and game-count cutoffs, computing rating histories under each and selecting via a logistic classifier on pre-match rating differences; the recommended schedule is K_i = 60 if n_i <= 5; 30 if 5 < n_i <= 10; 16 if n_i > 10.
equation: K_i = 60 \text{ if } n_i \leq 5; \; 30 \text{ if } 5 < n_i \leq 10; \; 16 \text{ if } n_i > 10

claim: The standard Elo expected score and update are E_A = 1/(1 + 10^{(R_B - R_A)/400}) and R' = R + K_i(S - E); on 4.64M real Ludo games four K configs tied at F1 0.548-0.554 (accuracy gaps 0-30 points ~52%, near random), but the tuner was fit and evaluated in-sample, a data-snooping flaw.

GoalNet builds a graph neural network over event-centric soccer graphs (22 players as nodes, interactions as edges) predicting change in expected threat (Delta xT), distributing it as xT_v = (||h_v^(L)|| / sum_u ||h_u^(L)||)*Delta xT; GCN propagation is H^(l+1) = sigma(A H^(l) W^(l)) and graph attention is alpha_uv = exp(LeakyReLU(a^T[W h_u^(l) || W h_v^(l)]))/sum_w exp(...).

TransGoalNet achieved validation MSE 0.0001-0.0002 for Delta xT prediction (vs GAT 0.0006-0.0110), surfacing hidden facilitator players like Idrissa Gana Gueye and Xhaka's progressive pass as the decisive xT gain; however there is no test set, no holdout, and the embedding-magnitude attribution axiom is validated only qualitatively.

Spectral ranking via the top eigenvector of the skew-symmetric pairwise-difference matrix has relative l-infinity error bounded by SNR^{-1} (Theorem 3.2), and leave-one-out analysis reduces sample complexity under the Erdos-Renyi Outliers model from Omega(n^{4/3} log^{3/2} n) to Omega(n log n); the normalized variant divides by D = diag(|H| 1_n) before eigen-decomposition.

The maximum per-item displacement rho_infinity = max_i (1/(n-1))*(# order violations involving item i) explodes when true scores are close (inverse minimum-separation dependence), and the normalized algorithm's lambda^{-8} factor is nearly vacuous; simulations show SNR=1.7 gives relative error ~0.2 and max displacement ~0.15.

Rankability of a ranking instance is diagnosed by r = f(k, |P|, tau, beta): k = distance of dominance matrix D_bar from perfectly rankable, |P| = number of optimal rankings, tau = Kendall-tau diameter of the optimal set, beta = new position-weighted indecision-location measure penalizing fractional entries further from the diagonal and lower in the ranking; 98% of 50 LOLIB IO instances have more than one optimal ranking.

A Bayesian hierarchical model y_g ~ t_nu(a_diff(g) + eff_diff(g) + ha(g), sigma_y) with random-walk team ability decomposes English Premiership Rugby margins into ability, effort (tries share of scoring attempts), home advantage, and heavy-tailed luck (nu ~ Gamma(9,0.5), 4 chains x 2500 iterations in Stan); posteriors: beta_effort = 3.114 [1.574, 4.639], beta_home = 0.324 [-0.028, 0.657], nu = 13.011 [5.445, 25.335].

Tango variance decomposition on the rugby data gives Var(Luck) = 0.01136364, Var(Performance) = 0.03798835, Var(Effort) = 0.01563645, Var(Ability) = 0.01098826 (effort, luck, ability contribute roughly equal thirds), but the effort result is target-contaminated because the effort proxy is computed from the same game it explains.

Spatial allocative efficiency: an NBA lineup is efficient if players' FG% ranks match their FGA-rate ranks, scored by Lineup Points Lost LPL_i = sum_j v_i*xi_ij*(A*_ij - A_ij) (optimal shot vector A*_i from rank-matching permutation preserving total attempts); each LPL point costs 0.62 actual points (theta posterior mean -0.62, 95% HPD (-1.08, -0.17)).

A permutation test over 500 random allocations per starting lineup shows NBA lineups minimize LPL beyond random (GSW, POR p-hat = 0.000; SAC 0.442 worst); Houston lost ~1 point/game to misallocation (most efficient), Washington >3 points/game (least); 10% of 2016-17 games were decided by <=2 points.

Player LPL contribution is PLC_ij = LPL_i * (A*_ij - A_ij)/sum_j|A*_ij - A_ij| (positive = undershooting, negative = overshooting); the game-level regression is Score_abg = mu + alpha_a + beta_b + gamma*I(Home_ag) + theta*TGLPL_ag + eps_abg.

For ranking K items via adaptively chosen pairwise comparisons, epsilon-greedy policies with saddle-point pair selection D(theta) = max_{lambda in Delta} min_{theta-tilde: r(theta-tilde)!=r(theta)} sum lambda^{i,j} D^{i,j}(theta||theta-tilde) (KL divergence between comparison-outcome distributions) and optimal stopping rules attain the asymptotic Bayes-risk lower bound as comparison cost c->0.

Lemma 5 gives an exponential MLE deviation bound for sequential ranking: P_theta(sup_{n<=t<=m} ||theta_hat^{(t)}-theta|| >= eps_1) <= e^{-Omega(n eps_lambda^2 eps_1^4)} * O(m^K) for n eps_lambda^2 eps_1^4 -> infinity, usable as a 'ratings have converged' sample-complexity diagnostic (though vacuous at NFL scale where K=32 breaks the O(m^K) term).

DeepHit neural survival network outputs a PMF over discrete time bins for the first-hitting-time of injury (trained with combined log-likelihood + ranking loss) and forecast time-to-injury from longitudinal athlete data at C-index 0.762 (chronological) with a 21-day input window and 7-day horizon on 4,449 player-date observations; leave-one-player-out IQR was 0.192, with best player 0.974.

On next-day injury classification baselines, XGBoost reached AUC 0.876 (F1 0.429, precision 1.000, recall 0.271) and RF AUC 0.779 (F1 0.533); rolling-average features beyond one day degraded badly and were abandoned; global importance leaders were average running speed, soreness, monotony, prior injury count, and subjective missingness.

In-play bettors' relative stakes follow a beta-inflated state-space model y_t ~ BEINF(mu_t, sigma, p, q) with state g_t = phi g_{t-1} + beta*vaepdiff_{t-1} + omega eta_t; estimated phi_hat = 0.968 [0.964, 0.971] shows strong persistence of market sentiment, and bettors overweight late in-game momentum (the VAEP effect rises rapidly in the second half).

Bookmakers' live win probabilities barely respond to VAEP (in-play momentum) swings: 'changes in the win probability are almost exclusively resulting from the time remaining' (HSV vs Werder case study), while bettors bet momentum; a tied-at-half momentum threshold strategy yielded mostly negative mean returns (some substantially below the ~5% vig), indicating momentum overreaction by bettors.

A player kernel k(z,z') = sigma^2 z^T z' relates matches through shared players (lineup vector z with +1/-1/0 by outcome) as Gaussian-process classification, P(u>v) = 1/(1+exp[-(s_u-s_v)]); on national-team soccer it matched betting odds log-loss (Euro 2008: PlayerKern 0.969 vs Elo 0.910 vs Odds 0.979; Euro 2016: 1.067 vs 1.102 vs 1.020) and was more consistent across tournaments than Elo.

Draws in the player-kernel model use the Rao-Kupper form P(u>v) = 1/(1+exp[f(x)-alpha]), P(draw) = (e^{2alpha}-1)P(u>v)P(v>u); the dual/match-space view avoids estimating one skill parameter per player when players outnumber matches (P > N).

A down-aware continuous play-success measure is progress(down, togo, gained) = 0 if down in {3,4} and gained<togo; (gained/togo)^down if down in {1,2} and gained<togo; 1 if gained>=togo (linear on 1st down, quadratic on 2nd down); RBF SVR regressing it achieved MAE 0.1351, RMSE 0.2332 on 177,245 NFL plays (2009-2014).
equation: \text{progress}(down, togo, gained) = \begin{cases} 0 & down\in\{3,4\}, gained<togo \\ (gained/togo)^{down} & down\in\{1,2\}, gained<togo \\ 1 & gained\geq togo \end{cases}

claim: On play-success classification, RBF SVM reached accuracy 66.65% (precision 67.62%, recall 63.75%, F1 65.63%); ANOVA F-tests ranked togo (16146.92), down (6690.42), and pass (2927.44) as top features, while team-identity one-hots showed a million-fold spread (NE 48.01 vs MIA 0.00005), indicating team-identity memorization rather than insight.

Training a forecaster with reward r = 1 - (p - p_hat(x))^2 against a state-conditioned empirical win rate p_hat(x) (empirical-Bayes bucketed teacher: p_hat = (w + M*p_hat_parent)/(n + M), M = 25 pseudocounts) beats training against realized outcomes (r = 1 - (p - y)^2): held-out NFL in-game WP Brier 0.1443, ECE 0.0292 vs market 0.1355/ECE 0.0273, and the trained model was better calibrated than its own teacher (ECE 0.029 vs 0.044).

Three static estimators (direct model, DeepSeek-V4 zero-shot, empirical-rate teacher) converge at Brier ~0.143-0.144 while trailing the market by the same 0.008 gap, showing the gap is resolution/information, not calibration; reward-target ablation: empirical rate 0.154/0.050 vs realized outcome 0.166/0.10 vs blend 0.181/0.121; full-completion CoT training decalibrated the model (Brier 0.25->0.34, ECE 0.19->0.30).

For distributional regression with a reject option, the optimal rule at a fixed exactly-controlled rejection rate eps is Gamma*_lambda(X) = F*_X iff ent(F*_X) <= lambda, else reject, with lambda_eps = G_ent^{-1}(1-eps); average-CRPS decomposes as CRPS-bar(H,K) = ent(K) + Div(H,K) with ent(K) = integral K(u)(1-K(u))du and Div(H,K) = integral (H(u)-K(u))^2 du.

The semi-supervised plug-in for the reject rule tracks target rejection rates almost exactly even with only 20% unlabeled data (eps=0.5 -> r_hat=0.50+-0.04), and Airfoil DRF error fell from 1.53+-0.05 at eps=0 to 0.78+-0.09 at eps=0.9; rejection-rate control is distribution-free: E[|r(Gamma_hat_eps) - eps|] <= C N^{-1/2}.

Modern neural networks are systematically miscalibrated (ECE grows with depth/width; BatchNorm increases miscalibration even as accuracy improves); single-scalar temperature scaling q_hat_i = max_k sigma_SM(z_i/T)^(k) with T fit on validation NLL is the preferred post-processing fix, e.g., CIFAR-100 ResNet-110 ECE 16.53% -> 1.26%, without changing accuracy since T does not change argmax.

ECE = sum_m (|B_m|/n) |acc(B_m) - conf(B_m)| and MCE = max_m |acc - conf|; the NLL-vs-accuracy disconnect (CIFAR-100 test error 29%->27% while NLL overfits) explains why good pick accuracy can coexist with terrible probability-based sizing; more weight decay monotonically improves calibration past the accuracy optimum.

Weighted conformal predictive systems restore nominal coverage under covariate shift by weighting calibration conformity scores with the estimated test-vs-calibration covariate likelihood ratio w_hat(x) = dP_test/dP_cal: Q_hat(y|x_{n+1}) = sum_i p_i^w(x_{n+1})*1{C_i <= C(x_{n+1},y)}, with normalized weights p_i^w proportional to w_hat(x_i); the ratio is estimated via a probabilistic test-vs-calibration classifier.

Under covariate shift on the Airfoil UCI data, unweighted conformal predictive system coverage collapses below nominal while WSCPS restores average coverage to the desired 80% and slightly improves (lowers) CRPS; the method assumes only P(X) changes (P(Y|X) invariant) and the probabilistic-validity claim (Conjecture 3.5) is empirically supported but unproved.

Gaussian-process regression on log(days-to-first-injury) with composite dynamic-time-warping kernel k(x_i,x_j) = exp(-gamma*DTW(x_i,x_j)), K = 1/2[k_train + k_match], achieved LOOCV concordance correlation ccc 0.95-0.98 from T down to T-12 days before injury, best MAE ~11 days (mean 91.7, median 49.5) minimized at T-3; significant recovery-time covariates were recurrence 6/6, phase of play 6/6, body part 5/6, diagnosis 5/6.

On weekly GPS-based injury classification, supervised PCA (screening by univariate |x_j^T y|) was the best method by Cohen's kappa (Approach A: kappa 0.21+-0.04, acc 88.8%, precision 0.55, recall 0.33) while RF/SVM/GP/MLP/k-NN all scored ~0; every classifier sat at the ~66.4% majority-class baseline for recovery-time classification, with best kappa = RF 0.256; all datasets were club-confidential, not released.

On 15,455 FRBP Survey of Professional Forecasters contests, the median crowd estimate beats ALL participants with odds 0.026 vs 0.015 for the mean (~1.7x better), and the median beats the majority by construction while the mean beats the majority in only 67% of contests; median beats mean head-to-head in 50.4% of contests with their errors correlating r=0.98.

Skewness vs collective crowd error shows Pearson r = 0.03 (no meaningful correlation), debunking the error-cancellation (unbiased estimates) explanation of crowd accuracy; mean relative errors: mean 0.20+-0.01, median 0.19+-0.01, winners 0.15+-0.01, random forecaster 0.22+-0.01, ARIMA 0.31+-0.01 (ARIMA beats a random expert in only 35% of contests).

Model-free contextual-bandit feature screens rank features by heterogeneous treatment effect across arms rather than outcome correlation: HIE: FI_HIE(x) = sum_b (N_b/N)*(P_{w_b}(Y=1) - P_{w*}(Y=1)) with w_b = argmax per-bin arm; HDD: FI_HDD(x) = sum_b (N_b/N)*D_b(P_{b_1},...,P_{b_k}) - D(P_1,...,P_k); combined FI(x) = alpha1*hat FI_HIE(x) + alpha2*hat FI_HDD(x), min-max normalized.

HIE/HDD feature screening took 2.7s per trial (10 features x 50,000 samples) vs LinUCB 647.3s (~240x faster) and CohortMAB 82.5s (~30x), and matched or beat model-embedded selection on downstream contextual-bandit reward on both synthetic (CausalML HTE generator) and a 600,000-sample Roblox recommender experiment, though no p-values or CIs were stated.

The decoupled Kelly portfolio problem has computational cost NT vs T^N for the coupled problem: decoupled return R_avg = sum f_i*exp(E[ln(1+f_i X_i)]) - 1 (Eq. 10) vs coupled R_c = exp(E[ln(1+sum F_i X_i)]) - 1 (Eq. 11), which requires an N-dimensional integral; the combined Kelly-Markowitz objective adds a variance penalty with constraint sum f_i^2 = 1.

On 10 stocks solved by differential evolution, the Markowitz model converged to the same portfolio at all risk parameters P in {0.1,...,0.9} (stock X_10 ~0.55 weight, all others at the 0.05 lower bound); decoupled Kelly matched MV at P=0.3 and 0.5 but mis-converged at P=0.9 (lower return AND higher risk - a possible local-maximum trap), with no out-of-sample test and no transaction costs.

A tweet sentiment classifier (word2vec + random forest) for Microsoft hit 70.18% sentiment accuracy (n-gram+RF 70.49%; logistic 62.42%), at the 70-79% human-concordance boundary from literature, and logistic regression on 3-day aggregate sentiment predicted next-day stock direction at 69.01% (LibSVM 71.82% on 355 daily instances, ~36 test points = +-15pp noise); the direction split was not stated as time-ordered, so lookahead leakage is likely.

The Bayesian Market Maker (BMM) converges tightly in equilibrium yet adapts to shocks: Gaussian-shock simulations (matched spread) gave BMM profit +2081.35 vs LMSR -2457.30, RMSD 2.92 vs 5.38; post-convergence RMSD_eq strongly favors BMM (LimitedInformation: 0.93 vs 14.56); but under adversarial uniform shocks BMM max loss was 50,183.77 vs 8,384.42 - BMM is NOT loss-bounded (~6x LMSR's bound of b*ln2 = 8664.34).

BMM's shock adaptation uses a consistency index C(history) = L(mu_t, 2 sigma_t) - L(mu_t, sigma_t) where L(mu,sigma) = integral N(v;mu,sigma)*prod_{i=1}^{W}(Phi(z^+_i,v,sigma_eps) - Phi(z^-_i,v,sigma_eps)) dv; if C > 0, sigma_{t+1} = 2 sigma_t (window W is the master adaptability/convergence tradeoff knob); the LMSR spot price is rho(q_t) = e^{q_t/b}/(1+e^{q_t/b}).

On 16 NBA seasons (~18,000 games), single-feature strength summaries beat box-score Four-Factors features: best dynamic Elo (depth 2) AUC 0.7117, accuracy 0.6736; historical Elo (20% offseason regression, HFA=40, K=30) AUC 0.7117, accuracy 0.6721; the Elo update is R <- R + K*(outcome - 1/(1+10^(-(R_opp-R+HFA)/400))).

A five-stage NFL OL evaluation pipeline (to-side minus not-to-side differential stats as teammate controls; k-means k=7; per-cluster salary distributions) explains cap value at adj. R^2 = 0.50 (intercept 5,399,261; stuff% differential -82,247, p=0.012; yds/attempt differential +382,197, p=0.045; sack% -2,516, p=0.023), and current-year PFF rating was NOT significant - differential stats beat PFF for salary explanation; flagged undervalued: John Jerry (NYG G 2014, $795,635), Mike McGlynn (KC G 2014, $1,037,594).

In the agent-based tournament model P_j(t) = a*T_j + (1-a)*L_j(t) fitted to 13 Olympics' 100m results, best-fit parameters are men a=0.96 (sigma_T=0.15), women a=0.94 (sigma_T=0.14): random luck accounts for ~4% of performance for men and ~6% for women at the Olympic level, a strong lower bound for less controlled domains like team sports.

The luck-share moment identity: the difference of two subsequent runs has symmetric triangular distribution on [-(1-a), (1-a)] with SD = (1-a)/sqrt(6), which estimates the luck share without the full agent-based model; lucky-streak analysis shows of 1000 simulated final winners, 852 were moderately lucky (L>0.5) in all 6 rounds and 232 very lucky (L>0.75) in all 6.

Elo is online gradient descent on convex log-loss with a regret bound: OGD with eta_t = D/(G sqrt(t)) gives Regret_T <= (3/2)GD sqrt(T), so (1/T)Regret_T <= C sqrt(N/T) with eta_t = sqrt(N/t); the sparsity rule is t/N < 1000 -> Elo wins (regret dominates), t/N > 1000 -> model capacity can win - NFL at N=32, T~=285/season (t/N ~= 9) is extreme-sparse, licensing Elo-family ratings only.

The Bradley-Terry model is rejected as the data-generating process on all 8 real datasets tested (all p < 10^-4, most < 10^-10), including chess, tennis, Go, and LLM Arena; Elo2k (vector ratings, p_t = sigma(u_i^T v_j - u_j^T v_i)) has a non-convex loss with no OGD guarantee, and Elo-family was best or tied on all 6 sparse datasets (e.g., tennis CE loss 0.6242 vs pairwise 0.6820).

A Bernstein Quantile Network (BQN) turns a single deterministic weather forecast into a calibrated probabilistic one without an ensemble: quantile function Q(tau) = sum_{j=0}^{d} theta_j C(d,j) tau^j (1-tau)^{d-j} (d=16, sorted theta => monotone), achieving CRPS 1.622 vs naive 1.921 vs EMOS 1.700 (CRPSS 0.156 vs naive), with joint multi-lead-time training plus lead-time embeddings beating per-lead partitioning.

All models degrade at forecast tails and cannot invent tails they haven't seen (Feb 2021 Texas cold event was out-of-distribution with CRPSS collapse in low winter percentiles); adding a 2nd ensemble member gives a sharp CRPSS jump even with postprocessing, with diminishing returns after.

In a suspense/surprise model of European football matches, per-minute surprise is the Euclidean magnitude of the shift in home/draw/away win probabilities from one minute to the next, summed over all 90 minutes.

Per-minute suspense is the square root of the expected squared deviation of next-minute beliefs (p_{t+1}^j) from current beliefs (p_t^j), where the expectation weights the two goal-scoring states (home scores next, away scores next) by their probabilities, summed over all 90 minutes and over the three outcomes.

For binary classification with a bounded abstention budget δ, the Bayes-optimal rule abstains exactly where posterior ambiguity is largest, predicts ±1 outside that region, and randomizes on boundary shells where the ambiguity CDF jumps.
equation: γ_δ = sup{γ>0 : P_X(|η(X)−1/2|≤γ) ≤ δ}; abstain where |η(x)−1/2| < γ_δ, randomize with c_0=(δ−δ_1)/(δ_2−δ_1) on boundary shells

claim: The paper decomposes plug-in abstention error into a stochastic term and a discretization term: the stochastic error shrinks with the effective sample count n·μ_min in each histogram cell.
equation: e_S(h,x)=√(32 log(nμ_min)/(n μ_min h^D)); e_D = sup-cell variation of η

claim: A hierarchical player→frame→segment voting pipeline (YOLOv3 pixel stream + OpenPose skeleton stream) automatically clips table-tennis rally highlights from full broadcasts: a k-frame window is 'playing' when its mean Boolean playing score exceeds a threshold, and consecutive segments merge when their gap is under Δt.
equation: Pr_play(s) = (1/k) Σ_i Bp_i > Prc (Eq 5–6); merge if (t_begin^{i+1} − t_end^i) < Δt (Eq 8)

claim: On 10 table-tennis broadcasts (~640k frames), the 3-level voting cascade reached rally-level precision/recall 96.4%/96.2% (YOLOv3) and 95.7%/87.3% (OpenPose) versus ~80% frame-level accuracy before voting; OpenPose was 2.39× slower than YOLOv3 (paper prints 1.39×, flagged as suspect).

The MediaEval 2022 Sport Task benchmark on TTStroke-21 table-tennis video defines two subtasks: (1) stroke classification of trimmed clips into 20 stroke classes plus non-stroke, scored by global + per-class accuracy; (2) temporal stroke detection from untrimmed video, scored by COCO-style temporal mAP over 20 IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95 plus frame-wise temporal IoU.

Benchmark reference results: classification best 74.2% global accuracy (long-tail-aware SWIN) versus ResNet-50 68.8% and baseline 20.4%; detection best frame-wise IoU 0.247 (YOLOv5) versus baseline 0.144, with the detection baseline's mAP unbeaten in 2021 — long-tail-aware training was the decisive factor in fine-grained sports classification.

A probabilistic match-classification model for low-scoring sports computes, for each team under each result (W/D/L), the simulated prize probability, then defines gain from offensive play G = P(prize|W) − P(prize|D) and loss L = P(prize|D) − P(prize|loss avoided); the (G,L) position relative to the indifference threshold yields six match classes (competitive, unimportant, offensive-incentive, defensive-incentive, collusion-vulnerable, asymmetric) and an incentive strength κ equal to distance from indifference.
equation: κ = distance from indifference; G = P(prize | W) − P(prize | D); L = P(prize | D) − P(prize | loss avoided)

claim: Simulation over 500 pre-final-round scenarios × 1,000 final-round outcomes found that incomplete round robins produce fewer unimportant matches but more offensive and more defensive/collusion-vulnerable matches than complete round robins, and identified collusion-vulnerable fixtures (mutually beneficial draws) where standard form analysis fails.

DYNAMO (DYnamic Non-stAtionary local M-estimatOrs) estimates time-varying causal graphs for non-stationary time series without stationarity, faithfulness, or constant-Gaussian-noise assumptions: x_t := f(Pa(x_t), ε_t; θ(τ_t)) with τ_t = t/T, fitted by kernel-localized M-estimation ℒ_t(ϑ) = (1/Th) Σ_l ℓ(x_l, Y_{l−1}; ϑ) K_h(τ_l − τ_t); the linear case is NOTEARS with trace-exponential acyclicity penalty H(W)=tr(e^{W∘W})−d.
equation: ℒ_t(ϑ) = (1/Th) Σ_l ℓ(x_l, Y_{l−1}; ϑ) K_h(τ_l − τ_t); H(W)=tr(e^{W∘W})−d

claim: Applied to 1.6M Wyscout events from 760 EPL matches, home-field advantage collapsed in empty stadiums (2020-21 home win 37.9% vs away 40.3%) and returned with crowds (2021-22 home win 43.0%, +9 points over away); DYNAMO-predicted minute-level XG beat DYNOTEARS and raw XG on goal-prediction MSE for all four studied teams (e.g., Arsenal 2021-22: 0.00079 vs 0.00106 vs 0.00111, ≈29% improvement).

DFS tournament payout design fits an ideal power-law curve π_i = E + (P1 − E)/i^α (E = entry fee as minimum payout, P1 = first prize), where the exponent α is found by binary search on the budget equation because the right-hand side is strictly decreasing in α.
equation: π_i = E + (P1 − E)/i^α; B − N·E = Σ_{i=1..N} (P1 − E)/i^α (B = total prize pool, N = paid places)

claim: The power-law ideal fit real tournaments with average p-value .237 (not rejected); the four-stage production heuristic deployed at Yahoo ran under 1.5 seconds on the hardest contests, and on a 125,000-winner DraftKings contest produced cost 78.7k in 1,700 ms with zero extra winners.

A MaskGIT-based deep generative model for minute-by-minute wind vectors (Time VQ-VAE tokenization + masked token-wise NLL training) explicitly fails on extreme winds — no generated day exceeded the 22.7 m/s training max in 50,000 synthetic days (3 exceedances) while observations exceeded 20 m/s 28 times — so the paper was REJECTed for sports use: nonparametric generative wind simulation cannot supply the tail regime that would matter for weather/totals modeling.

LiveQA is a timeline-aware sports QA dataset built from live NBA broadcast text: 1,670 games/documents, 1,786,616 sentences, 117,050 quizzes (per-document averages 1,069.83 sentences, 70.09 quizzes), with a question-type taxonomy of comparison / calculation / inference / tracking — reusable as an event-tracking/evaluation harness even though the 2020-era reader baselines are dated.

Predicting Tommy John (UCL) surgery from rookie-season stats of 8,503 MLB pitchers (826 positive / 7,677 negative, 47 Stathead features K-best-reduced to 13): MLP reached ROC-AUC 0.6740, besting Decision Tree 0.6329, Random Forest 0.6143, XGBoost 0.6068, KNN 0.5702, and Naive Bayes 0.5463 — a portable protocol for NFL player-availability modeling, with heavy reproducibility gaps (no feature list, split years, or hyperparameters).

A five-page workshop proposal for an adaptive time-varying structural causal model to detect regime changes in energy markets contains zero empirical content — no dataset, no experiment, no results — and its 'competitive forecasting performance' claim is unsupported by any table, figure, or metric; verdict REJECT, nothing transfers.

FanCric, a six-LLM-agent pipeline (Supervisor → Researcher → Career Profiler → Form Assessor → Strategizer → Selector → Evaluator) for fantasy cricket lineups, was tested on one IPL match against 12.7M real crowd entries: FanCric averaged 528.55 points (58.6 percentile, 80% win rate, best team 644 = 96.3 percentile) versus a prompt-engineering baseline at 512.9 (50.4 percentile, 70% win rate) — but the Selector used GPT-4o against the baseline's GPT-4o-mini, so model strength confounds the architecture effect.

A coverage-constrained abstention (reject) objective for imbalanced classification maximizes selective accuracy max_{f,q} P(f(x)=y | a(x) ≤ θ) with loss L_t = r̂(f,q|E_t) + λΨ(c − φ̂(q|E_t)) and Ψ(b)=max(0,b)², where empirical selective risk r̂ = Σ ℓ(f(z),y)(1−q(z)) / (|E|·φ̂) and empirical coverage φ̂ = (1/|E|) Σ (1−q(z)); an auxiliary full-sample BCE term (weight 1−α) keeps the model seeing rejected samples.

For aggregating Blackwell-ordered experts' probability forecasts, the precision scheme weights experts proportional to φ(x) = 1/(x(1−x)) when the two forecasts are close (|x₁−x₂| ≤ 0.4) and proportional to √φ(x) when far apart, snapping to 0/1 at extremes and 1/2 on (0,1)/(1,0).

For conditionally independent experts, the average-prior aggregation scheme applies the Bordley Bayes formula with a dummy prior μ̂ = (x₁+x₂)/2 (variant: μ̂ = 0.49(x₁+x₂), plus 0.02 if the sum exceeds 1); the minimax regret for the Blackwell-ordered setting is ≈0.022542.
