Rest coefficient is live: +0.41 margin points per extra rest day, fitted on 544 games, replacing the crude rest_diff/7 proxy that treated a week of rest as a full signal.
Weather signals are zero: wind -0.14 total points per mph (se 0.16) and temperature +0.03 per degF (se 0.04) on 349 outdoor games, both inside one standard error - no signal, unused.

Referee-crew signal fails: 2024 crews with |mean|>se applied to 2025, n=113, r=-0.093 vs home win, slope -0.0101 (se 0.0103) - the slope does not clear, so named crews stay out of the edge; fourth-down go rate walk-forward r=-0.014 is noise, unused.
Honesty discipline rule for signal claims: a coefficient inside one standard error (or positive when negative is expected) is zero, and a weight without a row is a lie.

Fitted offensive-line absence calibration on 1,069 team-weeks (2024-2025): tackle_out (129 games) costs -2.61 used points (se 0.91, multiplier -0.1132); tackle_dnp (87) costs -1.72 (se 1.20, multiplier -0.0746); tackle_limited (154) costs -1.15 (se 0.90, multiplier -0.0498); interior OL out (+0.95, se 0.98) and backup tackle out (-0.52, se 1.58) are zeroed because one is positive and the other inside one se.

The input for OL absence adjustment is practice-participation status (whether the starting tackle practiced; doubtful pooled with out; a questionable tag alone is not input), not the official injury tag.

Six anytime-TD usage analysts recovered verbatim: (1) THE GOAL LINE - who gets the ball inside the 5; (2) THE RED ZONE - real share inside the 20 vs general workload; (3) THE SCRIPT READ - game-flow effect on scoring chances; (4) THE LONG SCORE - goal-line vs distance scorer repeatability (a distance-only scorer needs a broken play, not a play call); (5) THE SOFT SPOT - which position the defense gives up TDs to; (6) THE QB VULTURE - QB sneak/designed-run cannibalization of short TDs.

Wiring constraints for usage-derived probabilities: red-zone/goal-line shares must be computed point-in-time (prior games only, no peeking); edge only when the usage model disagrees with the market AND walk-forward tests support it; every TD output needs an evidence card (what usage, when known, from where, how fresh, what the market priced).

Withhold rule: if the pregame model and the devigged moneyline differ by more than 0.08, the game is WITHHELD (not a side) - Week 3 2026 had 10 association-only, 6 withheld, 0 insufficient; ASSOCIATION_ONLY means premises name the same outcome and agree but interference is not cleared, so it is an association, not a live edge.

Measured: forward Brier 0.2524 on 33 settled 2026 games (fit on 7,240 pre-2026 games, 2026 results excluded from fit); the largest Week 3 model-market divergences were PHI@CHI 0.336 (model 0.699, market 0.363) and KC@MIA 0.302 (model 0.475, market 0.173) - both withheld.

Fail-closed quantization rule: the conformal quantile now fails closed when rank exceeds n instead of returning +Infinity; the port was verified by transpiling with esbuild and running against hand-computed values (36/36 pass).

CV rotation deskew recipe: estimate roll angle via phi = arccos(v_axis dot e_x) with the sign from the cross product (v_axis x e_x)_z, rotate the image by -phi; per-frame pixels-per-yard comes from detected adjacent full-field 5-yard line spacing, serving as an independent label-free homography validator (cross-check H's local scale vs measured, reject bad fits that pass reprojection on mislabeled points).

Formation classification result (Ajmeri & Shah 2018, Sloan): a CART classifier on coordinate features reached 86.5% QB position (Center/Shotgun/Pistol) and 72.3% formation accuracy over 29 classes from All-22 film at 5 fps.
Documented limitation: jersey-color tracking breaks under shadows/sunlight RGB variance - do not hard-code one HSV range; use adaptive thresholds or per-frame white-point normalization.

License verdict RESEARCH-ONLY: the-playmakers repo carries an MIT badge hyperlinked to a LICENSE file that does not exist (GitHub API license field null, no LICENSE in any of 5 commits) - the badge is aspirational/broken, so no code/figures may be copied; the wr-finder dataset on Roboflow has explicit CC BY 4.0 and is USABLE with attribution.

Training-recipe value: a YOLOv8 NFL pre-snap position detector on 503 annotated images (8 classes: CB, FB, LB, QB, RB, Safety, TE, WR) reports mAP@0.5 = 0.759 (best class WR 94.2% precision), setting the detector-v2 acceptance bar; process fix adopted is a DATASET_LICENSES.json sidecar with a CI test failing if any training dataset lacks an explicit license entry.

Trust infrastructure pattern: deny-by-default network policy (a policy.yaml declaring every allowed host, port, verb, and binary) structurally enforces hard rules like draft-never-send - policy as code, not convention.
Sack-prop veto: sack props are deliberately NULL because pressure-to-sack conversion has R^2 < 0.005 - a metric-honesty standard, not a signal.

Early-season props-consensus method: base rates use 100% 2025 full-season means (0% blended Week 1), script-adjusted volume via 2025 dropback rates by win-probability bucket, with a garbage-time correction filtering ~11% of plays.

Turnover-luck regression screen: actual minus expected INTs - CLE +7.11 and LV +7.74 thrown over expected (positive regression) vs CHI +7.22 takeaways over expected (negative regression, not repeatable) - feeds DST and offense regression screening.
NGS feed physics sanity gates: test_no_teleport requires hypot(dx,dy) <= 12.0*dt + 0.5, speed cap <= 12.0 yd/s; causality test requires zeroing frame_id > t changes outputs by < 1e-6.

NGS uncertainty calibration gates (mandatory before downstream consumption): ECE_regression = sum_b (n_b/N)*|RMSE_b - mean_sigma_b| over 10 equal-count bins must be < 0.15 yards; coverage at Mahalanobis <= 1 (expect 0.393) and <= 2 (expect 0.865) within +/- 5 percentage points.

NGS internal-only doctrine (standing, CI-fenced): NGS data and metric names are never on any public surface - NGS signals get their own calibrated weight and are backtested like every other signal family, but only derived judgments ship.

Two-source verification matrix: every slate claim is tagged CONFIRMED (two independent sources), SINGLE, DIRECTIONALLY CONFIRMED, UNVERIFIED, or DOWNGRADED, with conflicts explicitly named and unresolved rather than smoothed.

Referee significance finding: across 1,886 games and simultaneous significance testing of all 17 officials, only Alan Eck's low penalty rate (10.9 per game, fewest in NFL) survives as a strong signal; all other crew splits are suggestive or not significant and must be labeled as such.

MNF totals pattern: the under is ~71% (25 overs, 56 unders, 1 push) from 2020-2024; MNF over rate was ~42.6% in 2019-2024; MNF totals are set ~1 point higher than the Sunday early slate (45.6 vs 44.6), so the under bias is partly inflated expectations - a line-setting effect, not just scoring.

Crew total leans: Shawn Smith +1.7 pts vs closing total (largest over-lean in the dataset, not significant), Adrian Hill -1.0 pt (strongest under lean of any Week 2 crew), Brad Rogers +1.3 pts with 13.1 flags/game driving extensions.
Reuse rule: absent license = no license, so method-level learning only with no code reuse; MIT repos only are reusable with attribution.
JOINT_MODEL_REQUIRED rule (from nfl-edge-finder): a joint/composite model must refuse unless all legs evaluate on the same Monte Carlo draws - directly relevant to any joint-probability layer.

Partner outreach honesty rules: no fake audience claims, no fake revenue claims, no unsupported performance claims, no live links until approval, and every outreach must explain the evidence-first posture.
Market calibration baseline: the closing line as a predictor achieved Brier 0.2111 and ECE 0.0180 over 5,281 games - the bar the GSE model's calibration must beat.

assessEdge protocol: independent estimators must diverge from the book AND agree with each other before any edge is assessed; industry context is that long-run win rates above ~55-57% at -110 are vanishingly rare and 65%+ advertised claims are almost always manipulated or small-sample.

Rejected as tout-funnel behavior: 'place bet at DraftKings' buttons, embedded sportsbook checkout, and bet-slip deeplinks (make-betting-frictionless mechanics) - at most an honest affiliate disclosure link, founder-gated; on-brand builds include calibration-by-confidence analytics and the PropPick extension.
License posture: AGPL/GPL repos are learn-don't-integrate (e.g., freemocap AGPL-3.0, firecrawl AGPL-3.0); all repos verified via the GitHub API rather than README claims.

Four-dimension source risk rubric (quality / licensing / reliability / manipulation): an unconfirmed ToS automated-access status is treated as PROHIBITED, and Scores24 classified ORANGE (owner approval required, no automated access) with a six-step path to GREEN; scraping Scores24 is a P1 violation in the repo.

Source-graph integrity rule: do not present blocked, metadata-only, fixture-backed, license-required, or partner-required data as active; blocked sources stay isolated in rights/activation/outreach queues with a fallback source and expected next action.

Open gaps confirmed: active, legally usable data coverage remains smaller than the seeded source universe (546 seeded sources), and backtesting/model proof are scaffolded with fixtures and need historical production predictions.

Jarvis deterministic synthesizer (ADR 002): a pure function answering 'is the platform launch-ready?' with no LLM call and no wall-clock-dependent inputs (purity enforced by test: no I/O, no fs, no fetch, no Date.now(), no Math.random(), no top-level await) so the same inputs always produce the same auditable output; LAUNCH_READY requires zero safety warnings.

JARVIS_VERSION discipline: the version is bumped on every rule change with tests and changelog updated, so no rule drifts silently - the same discipline applies to calibration rule changes, which must leave an audit trail naming the version that produced each assessment.

Trust tiers for data: CONFIRMED (two independent free sources agree), SINGLE_SOURCE, DISPUTED - settlePendingPicks only grades via trusted finals; DISPUTED finals HOLD and unmatched finals stay PENDING, never settled blindly.

Cross-source agreement mechanism: join ESPN and henrygd NCAA scores by stable team abbreviation plus date proximity (+/- 1 day), reporting agreement, disagreement, and coverage gaps as first-class outputs.

Honesty-contract decision rule: a test failure asserting a product HONESTY contract is repaired in the CODE; a failure asserting a design detail the owner deliberately replaced is reconciled in the TEST with the changing commit named; no guard is weakened and no gate is flipped.

Memory-state lifecycle: candidate -> confirmed -> repeated_pattern, with conflicted, stale, superseded, rejected, expired states; a contradicting memory must NOT silently overwrite a confirmed one - it creates a conflicted state for owner review; candidates require confirmation, repeated evidence, or explicit owner approval.

Decision-ledger schema: decision_title, decision_summary, decision_type, rationale, evidence, alternatives_rejected, owner, decision_date, revisit_date, outcome, status, source_refs - every major owner decision creates both a ledger entry and a linked memory event.

FAILED_CLOSED evidence discipline: a validation run without a reproducible immutable receipt records FAILED_CLOSED and is never promoted, and historical failed receipts stay labeled failed; the CONFIRMED_CREDITS_ONLY rule admits a provider only on a fresh, covering, sufficient snapshot - a stale snapshot fails closed ('no receipt, no snapshot; stale snapshot, no credit admission').

Skill coefficient from Aoki, Assuncao & Vaz de Melo (2017, arXiv:1706.02447v1): phi = (s^2 - sigma^2_{2k}) / s^2, where s^2 is observed variance of season-end standings scores and sigma^2_{2k} is expected standings variance under a Monte Carlo null replaying the actual schedule with outcomes drawn from observed home/tie/away frequencies; phi ranges over (-inf, 1], phi ~ 0 means standings variance is fully explained by chance given the schedule, and the 95% null interval comes from the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles of the Monte Carlo replicates.

Cross-sport skill findings from 270,713 matches (1,503 seasons, 198 leagues, 84 countries, 2007-2016): basketball is the most skill-dominated sport (NBA phi > 0.95, all basketball seasons skill-dominated; NBA needs 17-25 of 30 teams removed before standings look random), volleyball 99.39% of seasons skill-dominated, handball 17.95% and soccer 7.13% of seasons compatible with pure luck; Algerian Division 1 2014-15 had phi = -1.93 (standings less dispersed than the random null, mechanism unexplained).

The paper's NBA Bayesian skill model: Y_k ~ Poisson(N_k * alpha_{h(k)} / (alpha_{h(k)} + alpha_{a(k)}) + epsilon_k) with log alpha_i = w^T x_i, Gaussian priors on w and epsilon, Gamma hyperpriors on precisions, Metropolis-Hastings inference (10,000 iterations, 2,000 burn-in, mean acceptance rate 0.395); the ledger flags the reported 0.7399 correlation between estimated skill and regular-season wins as circular (wins are the fitting target), not validation.

NFL port acceptance gate for the phi diagnostic: ADAPT phi only if (a) the nflverse pipeline reproduces qualitative behavior (median NFL phi in (0.3, 0.95), <10% of seasons outside (-0.5, 1.0)) and (b) season-ahead engine log-loss correlates positively with (1 - phi) across 2010-2025 seasons at Spearman rho > 0.3, p < 0.10, confirming phi measures the engine's irreducible error floor.

Promotion-readiness gate taxonomy for shadow stacks: three gate families (shadow evidence, repo boundary, owner approval) with 14 gates total; status values are blocked, owner_approval_required, or ready_for_disposable_rehearsal_review - the evaluator never sets livePromotionAllowed=true.

Entitlement law for the Stats API: FREE gets public_api only; FANTASY buys no additional API surface; PRO adds pro_api; ELITE adds elite_api; dark/blocked metrics return 403 for ALL tiers - proprietary data never leaves the internal fence at any tier.

PRISMA-2020 survey of 241 core papers (Jan 2020-Jul 2025) on LLM/MLLM applications in sports: soccer leads with 74 datasets; referee datasets are only 2% of stakeholder data; and the field-level quantitative consensus is that domain-adapted/fine-tuned models decisively beat zero-shot general models within each task.

Canonical zero-shot near-failure example: sports commentary generation scores CIDEr 42.00 on SN-Caption-test-align with a fine-tuned Llama 3 vs CIDEr 3.44 with zero-shot Video-LLaMA; action recognition peaks at Tennis7 93.80% accuracy.

Neural-rendering result (Texas A&M, arXiv:2602.15181v1): per-timestep independent implicit radiance fields (no temporal coupling, no per-frame SfM point cloud) beat 4DGS on novel-view synthesis of dynamic sports scenes - e.g., PSNR 34.28 vs 28.17 on the Dancing-Walking-Standing synthetic set at 12.7M params (~48.8 MB) per timestep vs 1-5 million Gaussians (200-300 MB) per timestep for per-timestep 3DGS; ledger verdict REJECT for GSE (graphics paper, no predictive modeling, no code link).

BERTopic over abstracts of 204 AI/analytics-in-sports journal articles (PRISMA, Web of Science SSCI, 2002-2024) extracts four latent themes ordered by prominence: (1) performance modelling, (2) physical and mental health, (3) social media sentiment analysis, (4) tactical tracking; the trust takeaway is that venue-prestige-filtered surveys systematically exclude conferences, preprints, and industry work - the venues where predictive edges are published first, making them lagging, incomplete maps of the frontier.

Honest negative result (DTU student thesis, arXiv:2506.05866v1, 709 ATP Grand Slam matches 2016-2020, 57 features): server point-win rates are 73.2% on successful first serves, 57.2% on second serves, 64.8% overall - and every ML model matches or underperforms the naive 'server wins' baseline.

ATP point-prediction bake-off numbers: first serve, all four models (logistic regression, random forest, AdaBoost, XGBoost) get accuracy = 73.2% with recall 0.0% in 10-fold CV - they degenerate to the server prior; tuned XGBoost on test manages +0.2 pp accuracy (73.4% vs 73.2%) with 1.2% recall; second serve, tuned XGBoost gets 53.1% vs baseline 57.2% (-4.1 pp) with ROC-AUC 53.5%, barely above random guess.

Engine discipline from the ATP negative result: in any domain where public summary features are thin, a strong-model baseline check against the naive prior must gate adoption; XGBoost gain-based feature importance showed only score/state features (sets won, break points, rank, surface) mattered - serve and return position accumulated features had no significant influence.

MambaMOT motion-predictor loss (UW Hwang lab, arXiv:2403.10826v2): L_pred = L_giou + L_mse (GIoU + MSE vs ground-truth next box); MambaMOT+ adds a trajectory-embedding head with contrastive loss L_cos(i,j) = 1 - cos(f_i, f_j) if i = j; max(0, cos(f_i,f_j)) if i != j, joint loss L_total = L_pred + L_cos.

MambaMOT results: DanceTrack test HOTA 55.5 (+8.2 over ByteTrack's 47.3 under identical detections); SportsMOT test 70.4 (+8.4 over ByteTrack); MambaMOT+ adds +0.6 HOTA / +1.0 IDF1 via tracklet merging; inference 28.8 FPS on a single GPU (real-time) vs <10 FPS for transformer trackers like MOTR.

Tracklet-merging design: compare per-tracklet features with cosine similarity and run hierarchical clustering to merge fragments, with temporal threshold 50 frames and spatial threshold 50 pixels to veto unreasonable merges - O(N) per-tracklet forward passes vs O(N^2) Siamese merging networks.

Bayesian predictive-density result (arXiv:1903.10889v1, NHL scoring time): the restricted estimator injecting ancillary information as the order restriction lambda_1/lambda_2 >= 1 achieves KL prediction error pe = 0.04 vs 0.45 for the unrestricted non-informative-prior estimator - roughly an 11x win under KL loss; ledger verdict REJECT for GSE (hockey scoring-time machinery, no NFL analogue in the engine).

Governed MCP (arXiv:2604.16870v2): every MCP call_tool passes a six-layer pipeline - schema validation (0.10 us), trust tier check (1.15 us), rate limit (0.02 us), adversarial regex prefilter (7.50 us), ProbeLogits semantic gate (332-556 ms), constitutional policy match (1.83 us) - with a Blake3-hashed audit chain (0.73 us per append, ~30K records in a 4 MB ring buffer) and fail-closed semantics (if the inference engine is unavailable, layer 5 returns Deny system-wide).

ProbeLogits safety primitive (reconstructed from garbled PDF - marked UNCERTAIN in the source): score s = logit(Dangerous) - logit(Safe) at the verbalizer position, calibration bias subtracted, scaled by deployment knob alpha; graduated response denies only when the model says Dangerous AND calibrated p = sigma(s) > 0.90, logs warnings in band [0.70, 0.90], and proceeds normally below 0.70.

Measured results: Custom-101 (37 dangerous / 64 benign prompts, full 6-layer) F1 = 0.789 (accuracy 84.2%, TP 30, FN 7, FP 9, TN 55); ablation without ProbeLogits drops F1 to 0.357 (TP 10, FN 27 - hand-rule firewalling without semantic understanding admits 27/37 dangerous calls); Custom-260 F1 = 0.980 with FP = 0; end-to-end latency ~358 ms (~2.8 governed calls/s).

SportSQL (arXiv:2508.17157v1, ADOPT verdict): natural-language sports queries via entity resolution, then schema-only LLM SQL generation (LLM sees schema, not data, executed read-only), just-in-time materialized in-memory views for expensive temporal aggregations, and a dataframe byte-for-byte verification gate - generated plotting code must reproduce the query dataframe byte-for-byte before any chart renders.

SportSQL benchmark (DSQABench, 1,793 questions): GPT-4o string exact-match 80.48, overall 0.75 vs Gemini 2.0 Flash 76.23 / 0.69; the bottleneck is compositional join/aggregation queries (Manipulate/join cases 15.4%, Retrieve+Filter+Calculate 22.3%, vs single-Retrieve 100%) - directly relevant to football analytics where most questions are joins.

Kelly wealth growth decomposition (Hubacek & Sir, arXiv:2010.12508v1, Eq. 32): W_G = D_KL(R||M) - D_KL(R||T) - the trader's wealth growth equals the difference in quality of her estimates T over market prices M in KL divergence; positive Kelly returns iff XENT(R,T) < XENT(R,M).

Ideal decorrelation loss (Eq. 59): MSE*_Omega(R,M,T) = (1/|Omega|) sum_{omega_i in Omega} (t_i - r_i)^2 + gamma*(t_i - r_i)(m_i - r_i), gamma > 0; the betting-adapted form is E[(T - R)^2 - gamma*(T - M)^2], where gamma trades accuracy vs decorrelation.
equation: MSE*_Ω(R,M,T) = (1/|Ω|) Σ_{ω_i ∈ Ω} (t_i − r_i)² + γ·(t_i − r_i)(m_i − r_i)

claim: Empirical result on 9,093 NBA games (2006-2014, chronological protocol, Pinnacle closing odds): Sharpe-portfolio wealth with decorrelation gamma = 0.4 was 1.74 +/- 0.14 without odds as feature (vs 0.38 at gamma = 0.0) and 1.49 +/- 0.10 with odds as feature; gamma = 1.0 destroys profit (-1.92) and collapses accuracy to ~61-62; Theorem 4.1 states for unbiased estimators Corr[T,M|R] = -1 maximizes essential profitability.

Regime caution: decorrelation can HURT if the trader's model is actually superior (paper section 4.3, Figure 5) - fractional Kelly benefits from decorrelation while full Kelly is blind to it, so before deploying gamma > 0 the model must be verified as NOT already XENT-superior to market consensus.

N-vote rule for exact Metropolis-Hastings from stochastic pairwise-preference votes (Sairien et al., arXiv:2609.00905v1): alpha_N(x,x';K) = min{1, r_0(x,x') * K/(N-K+1)}, where K = number of N judge votes favoring x' and K/(N-K+1) is the unbiased-in-ratio estimator of the ideal odds p/(1-p); exact (Theorem 2) and Peskun-Tierney optimal among exact rules (Theorem 3), PROVIDED judge votes follow the Bradley-Terry model.

Pref-MH results: image generation achieves 63.6% preference success vs 7.4% for Pointwise-MH vs 4.5% for the base sampler; molecule design QED 0.698 +/- 0.002, SA 0.781 +/- 0.001, diversity 0.899 +/- 0.001, MolSkill mean -1.432 +/- 0.398.

Exactness caveat: with a fixed sampling budget no exact oracle-based BT-MH implementation exists (Theorem 1); exactness is conditional on BT judges - real LLM/human judges routinely violate transitivity, independence, and stationarity, and under a non-BT judge the chain targets an undefined distribution and the 'exact' guarantee evaporates silently.

Step-and-turn representation (Nguyen & Yurko, CMU, arXiv:2603.17866v3): each frame's movement is step length s_t = sqrt((x_{t+1}-x_t)^2 + (y_{t+1}-y_t)^2) and turn angle phi_t = b_t - b_{t-1} with bearing b_t = atan2(y_{t+1}-y_t, x_{t+1}-x_t); turn-angle model is von Mises with concentration log kappa_{ijt} = gamma_0 + gamma_1 s_{ijt} + w_j, ball-carrier random intercept w_j ~ N(0, tau^2_w) - step length dictates turn concentration.

Ghost evaluation (Eq. 6-7): frame value vs ghost delta^(h)_{ijt} = lhat_{ijt} - lhat^(h)_{ijt}, frame-average delta-bar = (1/H) sum_h delta^(h)_{ijt}; yards success rate (Eq. 8) = (1/H) sum_h 1(delta^(h)_{ijt} > 0) averaged over frames; explosiveness (Eq. 9) = 1(lhat_{ijt} > q_0.95(lhat^(h)_{ijt})) averaged over frames, where play value lhat = sum_{l=10}^{110} l * P(L_{ijt} = l | X_{ijt}) estimated with a CatBoost multinomial classifier over 1-yard ending-yardline bins.

Yards success rate leaders (weeks 1-9 2022, min 70 attempts, fraction of frames beating the ghost): Josh Jacobs 0.542, Miles Sanders 0.539, Travis Etienne 0.527, Dameon Pierce 0.512, James Robinson 0.507; bottom: Michael Carter 0.446, A.J. Dillon 0.448; explosiveness leaders: Etienne 0.118, Aaron Jones 0.095, Kenneth Walker 0.093.

Movement-profile insight: correlation r = 0.279 between step-length and turn-angle random effects; Jonathan Taylor has the least variable turn angle (scouting 'straight-ahead runner'); Taylor = long strides/low turn variability vs McCaffrey = short steps/high turn variability; credible intervals at leaderboard top vs bottom do not overlap (discriminative-power check).

Negative result catalog (Rimbot, Jaggi & Barba, EPFL, arXiv:2503.00458v1, climbing move-sequence prediction): all three models fail - seq2seq predictions are 'not even holds'; the autoregressive Transformer suffers padding-collapse (almost always outputs the padding token); the simplified Transformer reports 35% accuracy but only 2/14 non-padding tokens correct, the rest being correctly-predicted padding tokens; evaluation metric was perplexity PPL(x_0,...,x_t) = exp(-(1/t) sum_i log(p_theta(x_i | x_{<i}))).
equation: PPL(x_0, x_1, …, x_t) = exp(−(1/t) Σ_i log(p_θ(x_i | x_{<i})))

claim: Advantage-differential feature pattern (Chiang & Denes, arXiv:2303.16776v1): RANKDIFF = RANK_a - RANK_b (set to 0 when both players ranked over 100, since rank differences are unreliable at the tails); BALANCE = (|SA| + |SRA| + |FHA|) / 3 where SA = serve minus receive win %, SRA = short-rally minus long-rally win %, FHA = forehand minus backhand win %.

Feature ablation: with derived features logistic regression reaches 0.699 validation accuracy vs 0.631 without; SVM-RBF collapses to 0.500 (random) without derived features vs 0.700 with; random-forest Gini importance ranks RANKDIFF most important.

Leakage audit lesson: the paper's headline ~70% accuracies are computed on post-match features (leaky for a 'prediction' claim); the exclude-target-match aggregate robustness check gets 61-67% test accuracy, comparable to live features - the portable pattern is a leave-one-game-out aggregate parity audit (criterion: <=5 pp accuracy loss) for every matchup-level feature.

Live-betting overreaction finding (Oetting et al., arXiv:2108.00821v2): a zero-adjusted-gamma ARX(1) state-space model on 1 Hz bookmaker stakes across 306 Bundesliga 2018/19 matches finds surprising goals (pre-goal odds >4.00) produce a latent-activity spike beta = 0.531 [0.494, 0.567] vs unsurprising goals (odds <2.00) beta = 0.034 [0.001, 0.067) - more than 15x the effect - meaning bettors overreact to surprising news even though odds have already shortened.

Model-selection evidence: the state-space formulation beats the no-state regression by Delta-AIC = 217,117 in favor of the state-space formulation - the latent activity state does nearly all the explanatory work; latent persistence phi-hat = 0.968 [0.967, 0.970].

Estimation recipe (Kitagawa 1987): discretize the continuous latent state into m = 150 bins over [-4, 4] yielding an m-state HMM, likelihood via forward algorithm O(T m^2), numerically maximized with many random starts; validated virtually exact for m >= 50 - a reusable continuous-latent-state estimation pattern.

Ridge tuning heuristic (Macdonald, arXiv:1201.0317v2, NHL adjusted plus-minus): choose lambda as the MAXIMUM of four candidates - (1) randomized generalized cross-validation (Girard 1991 trace estimator), (2) trace-curve stabilization point, (3) Hoerl-Kennard-Baldwin lambda_HKB = p*MSE/(beta-hat^T beta-hat), (4) the lambda needed to bring all ridge VIFs below 10, where ridge VIFs are diagonal elements of (X^T X + lambda I)^{-1} X^T X (X^T X + lambda I)^{-1}.

Proxy-outcome rescaling caution: Ovechkin's EV offense is G 0.46 (0.18) on goals vs C 0.63 (0.05) on Corsi rescaled by league-average shooting - a cautionary data point for ANY metric that rescales a high-frequency proxy by a league-average conversion rate, since the rescaling moves conclusions substantially.

Cautionary example (Kramov & Bauzha, arXiv:2010.13629v1, hobbyist heart-rate monitor): the device's tachycardia/bradycardia detection was validated 'by construction' and never measured against any ground truth - no accuracy figure, no Bland-Altman vs ECG, no true/false positives - an example of how NOT to claim a detector works.

Causal home-field model (Price, Cai, Shen & Hu, arXiv:2205.07193): Y_{i,j} = alpha_{i,j} + beta_i + epsilon_{i,j} with hierarchical beta_i ~ N(Delta, sigma^2); the paired home/away cancellation Y_{i,j} + Y_{j,i} = beta_i + beta_j + epsilon_{i,j} + epsilon_{j,i} cancels the neutral-field nuisance term, giving the linear system H beta + epsilon = Y with estimator beta-hat = (H^T H)^{-1} H^T Y (the paper prints (H^T H)^{-1} H Y, missing the trailing transpose - a typesetting slip).
equation: Y_{i,j} + Y_{j,i} = β_i + β_j + ε_{i,j} + ε_{j,i}

claim: EPL 2020-21 causal HFA results (380 games, 11 statistics): 7 of 11 significant at alpha = 0.05, ALL offense-side (Expected Goals Delta-hat = 0.232, sigma = 0.092, p = 0.011; Attacks w/ Shot 1.568 p = 0.005; Reaching Opponent Half 3.592 p = 0.000); defensive stats and the referee proxy (yellow cards -0.026, p = 0.834) NOT significant - home advantage lives in offensive chance creation, not goals, not defense, not officiating; weaker teams (Fulham, Brighton, Newcastle, Wolves) retain larger home advantage.

Estimator validation (simulations, 1000 replicates): bias tiny (e.g., n=20, sigma_0^2=1: bias -0.0059); coverage approaches 95% nominal as n grows (n=10: 0.882-0.913; n=20: 0.914-0.950; n=80: 0.947-0.955); sample variance and mean-of-variance-estimates match closely (e.g., n=40, sigma_0^2=1: SV 0.0030, MV 0.0030) - and the unbiased league-variance estimator via the law of total variance sigma-hat^2 = (1/(n-1)) sum_i (beta-hat_i - Delta-hat)^2 - (1/n) sum_i diag{sigma-hat^2_beta (H^T H)^{-1}}_i is reusable for any hierarchical shrinkage of team effects.

Two-stage uncertainty estimator (Mendes-Neves et al., arXiv:2501.05873v1): train a mean regressor from (ELO_home, ELO_away) to the mean of shot quantity/quality, then train a second-stage model on the first model's training-set residuals to predict sigma (uncertainty) - a cheap uncertainty estimator without Bayesian machinery; generative pipeline: draw quantity N ~ N(mu_quant, sigma_quant^2), sample shot qualities S ~ N(mu_qual, sigma_qual^2), home goals = sum_{i=1..N} I(hs_i > X_i), X_i ~ U(0,1), then Monte Carlo outcome/scoreline probabilities from simulation frequencies.

Reality check on the generative pipeline: test-set RPS 0.201 vs bookmaker 0.198 - the model does NOT beat bookmaker probabilities; betting evaluation was +1.1% absolute with one flat strategy but -0.8% absolute with the other, on an unaudited window with no stated number of test games - a pipeline that doesn't out-calibrate the market adds complexity without edge.

Classwise expected calibration error (Walsh & Joshi, arXiv:2303.06021v4, Eq. 3): (1/k) sum_i sum_j (|B_{j,i}|/n) |y_i(B_{j,i}) - p-bar_i(B_{j,i})|, with k classes and m equal-width bins over [0,1], bin-size-weighted.

Headline result: calibration-driven model selection beats accuracy-driven selection - on the 2018/19 NBA season the calibration-selected SVM earned ROI +32.45% fixed-$100 (+36.93% eighth-Kelly, $13,692.86 from $10,000) vs the accuracy-selected SVM at +5.56% fixed ($10,556.29) and -75.9% eighth-Kelly ($2,409.66); the accuracy-driven model's value-bet predictions clustered at probability extremes (variance 0.036 vs 0.034) - overconfidence on value bets that self-destructs under Kelly.

Kelly definition used (Eq. 1): k = (pb - q)/b where p = model probability, q = 1 - p, b = odds - 1; portable protocol: SFS on classwise-ECE (20 bins) with an 80%-nonempty-bins guard (violated -> ECE set to 1, preventing 'predict the base rate' degenerate calibration), BO-TPE on ECE, Spearman |rho|>0.7 correlated-pair feature filter, two-sample KS covariate-shift test at 1%, and fractional Kelly capped at 1/8.

Semi-supervised caution: the TFD paper's label-fraction sampling is random with no statement that match identity is preserved, so the unlabeled 90% may leak the same matches as the labeled 10% - group structure (match/team/season identity) must be respected in any fractional-label or cross-validation design; boundary-sharpness finding: cosine similarity of TFD features at event boundaries is 0.003 (tennis) vs DINO features >=0.999 (over-smoothed).

FENCE multi-account fraud system (arXiv:2310.05651v1, Dream11 production, 190M+ users): user graph on shared attributes (device, IP, payment instrument, referral links) with Random-Forest edge prediction and alternating connected-components clustering; automated flow precision 96.7% / recall 55.2%, manual-review flow precision 70.2% / recall 86.4%, 86% relative decrease in false-positive volume; cluster score > 0.95 triggers automatic restriction; real-time path 4-second SLA via Redis 1-hop lookup; batch on 6 x r5d.4xlarge. Ledger verdict REJECT for GSE - operator anti-abuse with no prediction transfer.

Latent neural-ODE motion forecasting (Takamido, Suzuki & Nakamoto, arXiv:2602.11492v1): transformer encoder (3 layers, 8 heads, dim 256, causal mask) maps motion x_{0:T-1} in R^{T x 45} to K=12 latent points z in R^{K x 3}, with z_0 encoding ~first 8% of motion as the ODE initial condition; neural ODE dz-hat(t)/dt = f_theta(z(t), t) with f_theta = 3-layer MLP (2 hidden x 128, tanh); MLP decoder (2 hidden x 256 ReLU) reconstructs 45-D joint positions.
VAE-style loss: L = lambda_recon L_recon + lambda_KL L_KL with lambda_recon = 1.0, lambda_KL = 1e-3 (KL toward standard normal); time-resolved R^2(t) = 1 - SS_res(t)/SS_ori(t).

Pitching results: mean RMSE 66.1 +/- 15.7 mm over the full prediction interval; mean R^2 0.46 +/- 0.20 (0.49 +/- 0.20 over the second half) - roughly 50% of variance in the latter half explained from only the initial ~8% of the sequence; training Adam lr 1e-4, batch 32, 1500 epochs on NVIDIA T4.

Causal trajectory factorization (Teoh, CausalTraj, arXiv:2511.18248v2): p(X_{P+1:T} | X_{1:P}) = product_{t=P}^{T-1} p(X_{t+1} | X_{1:t}); output is a mixture of M=8 Gaussians per timestep p(Delta X_{t+1} | X_{1:t}) = sum_{m=1}^{M} pi_{t+1,m} N(Delta X_{t+1}; mu_{t+1,m}, Sigma_{t+1,m}) with per-agent 2x2 Cholesky covariance; loss L = LNLL - lambda_ent L_ent with lambda_ent = 0.05; joint metrics minJADEk = min_j (1/NF) sum_i sum_t ||x-hat^j_{i,t} - x_{i,t}|| and minJFDEk = min_j (1/N) sum_i ||x-hat^j_{i,T} - x_{i,T}||.

CausalTraj Football-U results (yards, 20-frame NFL Big Data Bowl): joint minJADE20/minJFDE20 = 1.12/2.68 (best), vs MoFlow 1.16/2.82; NBA SportVU 4.0s joint 1.38/2.57 vs LED 1.63/2.99; NBA 1.0s per-agent 0.14/0.20 best; ball-player coupling is the known failure mode (unrealistic ball-carrier gaps) traced to the block-diagonal covariance.

Entropy-regularized NLL detail: L_NLL = -E_t log(sum_{m=1}^{M} pi-hat_{t,m} N(Y_t; mu-hat_{t,m}, Sigma-hat_{t,m})); L_ent = -(1/log M) sum_{m=1}^{M} pi-hat_{t,m} log(pi-hat_{t,m} + eps); AdamW + OneCycle, max LR 0.02, weight decay 0.01; ablation shows removing the spatial relation encoder or dropping to a single Gaussian degrades joint metrics.

Unsupervised phase segmentation (Badatya et al., arXiv:2509.24606v1, javelin): Adaptive ST-GCN denoising encoder (3 blocks, Chebyshev order 7, 64-d features -> 40-d latent, Gaussian noise sigma=0.1 injected as denoising objective) followed by structured unbalanced optimal transport over latent phase prototypes (fused Gromov-Wasserstein temporal-structure term + Kantorovich appearance-cost term + KL relaxation), closed with a pseudo-label cross-entropy loop; denoising objective L_total = L_MSE + lambda_vel L_vel.

Javelin results: Ours 71.02 mAP, 74.61 F1, 48.01 mIoU, 64.04 MoF vs ASOT 60.20/57.55/41.80/61.19; mIoU (48.01) markedly lower than F1 (74.61) - a boundary-localization weakness even where frame-level classification is strong, which is problematic for timing-sensitive uses like snap timing or release time.

Fourier frequency-band attention (Park, Yang & Jo, UIST 2024, arXiv:2507.23215v1): splitting IMU input into low 0-4 Hz (whole-body), medium 5-20 Hz (arm swing), high >20 Hz (impact vibration) bands with per-band temporal attention added +6.8% classification accuracy on the passive (non-dominant) wrist, closing the passive/dominant gap from 9.1 pp to 1.9 pp (passive 88.2 +/- 2.0% vs dominant 90.1 +/- 3.0%, 6,000 shot sequences); shot detection F1 86.0% on the passive arm.

Normalised segmental edit score (Lea et al. 2016, copied verbatim): Edit Score = (1 - (event additions, deletions or replacements needed) / (number of events in longer label)) x 100; VideoLLaMA2-7B LoRA-tuned on tennis rallies reaches only 34.4 edit score (best 39.7 at 32-frame sampling) vs the dedicated CV benchmark F3EST at 82.1.
equation: Edit Score = (1 − (event additions, deletions or replacements needed) / (number of events in longer label)) × 100

claim: CV-feature fusion finding: default pure-video 39.7 edit score -> bounding boxes drawn in the video HALVES it to 18.2 (drawn lines break the vision encoder) -> boxes in the prompt 61.3 -> boxes + court corners + ball coords in the prompt (every 2 frames) 76.0, approaching the 82.1 benchmark - the portable lesson is the 'structured-CV-features-as-text-in-the-prompt' hybrid pattern, not raw MLLM video reasoning.

Vision-encoder recipe: fine-tuning the vision encoder separately (0.55-0.56 single-event accuracy) then reloading into VideoLLaMA2 beats joint unfreezing (0.075-0.087, overfit); oracle event count in the prompt jumps edit score to 49.8 (diagnostic leakage); the model's strong textual-pattern learning (rally structure right, events wrong) warns that confident structure with wrong particulars needs grounded verification against detector outputs.

SpinePose distillation (Khan, Krauss & Stricker, arXiv:2504.08110v1): extends RTMPose with nine vertebral keypoints (C1 to sacrum) via teacher-student distillation; training objective L_total = alpha L_pos + beta L_distill + gamma_1 L_structure + gamma_2 L_spine with ablation weights alpha=5, beta=2.5, gamma_1=0.1, gamma_2=0.5, where L_pos = sum KL(student, ground truth), L_distill = sum over body joints KL(student, teacher), L_structure is a bone-angle orientation penalty, and L_spine is a differentiable smoothing loss dampening abrupt spinal bends.
equation: L_total = α L_pos + β L_distill + γ_1 L_structure + γ_2 L_spine

claim: SpineTrack results: SpinePose-l reaches 91.4 spine AP and 88.4 overall AP; the spine extension costs ~1.5-2.1 AP points vs same-size RTMPose on COCO (75.2 vs 76.9) and Halpe26 (77.0 vs 78.4); adding the spine-smoothness term paradoxically adds +3.9/+3.4 on the benchmarks, attributed to rule-based knowledge preventing interference.

Classifier-free guidance for tactic-conditioned diffusion (Qi, Yang & Ma, arXiv:2412.15673, Eq. 9): f_epsilon(y,G) = f_epsilon(y,A) + s_g * (f_epsilon(y,G) - f_epsilon(y,A)), with guidance scale s_g = 0.1 and 100 diffusion steps; tactic info randomly dropped during training and replaced with raw trajectory embedding A.

Banzhaf Interaction Learner: exact Banzhaf Interaction is NP-hard, so a learned MLP-self-attention-MLP network predicts the N x k agent-tactic similarity matrix I_pred = gamma_o(SA(gamma_ctx(A))) supervised by the masked-attention heuristic I^j_B = (S_a2t + S_t2a)/2 with L2 loss; total loss L = L_noise + L_distance + eta*L_unc + alpha*(L_tactic + beta*L_bi) with focal loss L^j_tactic = alpha^j (1 - p^{tactic}_j)^{gamma^j} log(p^{tactic}_j), gamma = 4.0, game factor 0.001.
equation: L = L_noise + L_distance + η·L_unc + α·(L_tactic + β·L_bi)

claim: Results: NBA SportVU trajectory minADE/minFDE 0.19/0.29 at 1s, 0.84/1.17 at 4s (beats LED by ~9.5% and ~5.6% ADE); TeamTrack-soccer beats LED by 15.4% ADE at 4.8s; tactic prediction Top-1 60.23% / Top-2 81.15% / Top-5 96.79% vs finetuned Llama3-8B at 22.39% Top-1; the ball has the highest Banzhaf interaction (~0.285) for both teams.

Cox-process framework (Maia et al., arXiv:2312.04338v1): each event type j follows a Cox process with intensity lambda^j(t); event-time CDF/density: Phi^j_{lambda^j}(s;t) = 1 - exp(-Lambda^j(s,t)); phi^j_{lambda^j}(s;t) = lambda^j(t) exp(-Lambda^j(s,t)); Lambda^j(s,t) := integral_s^t lambda^j(r) dr; log-linear intensity ln lambda^j(t) = sum_i xi^j_i psi^j_i(t).

Theorem 1: the parametric log-likelihood is concave on R^I and strictly concave under linear independence of regressors, so MLE is a unique convex optimization solvable with standard convex solvers (linear equality constraints like attack/defence normalization preserve convexity); fitting 78 parameters to 3,039 matches took <10 s on an Intel i7-10700F.

Quantified state effects (Brazilian Serie A 2015-2022, 3,039 matches): a red card reduces the receiving team's goal intensity by 30.48%; losing by one goal raises a team's goal rate by 1/0.9082 = +10.11%, losing by two by +21.24%; a team leading by one has its rate x0.9082; home goal intensity is +51.40% vs away; second-half goal rate +20.62%; second-half stoppage time is on average >1 minute longer when the score difference <= 1.

Calibration: G4S5R predicts 27.48% draws vs 27.42% observed - far better than Maher's original static models (24.46% / 27.32% on 27.92% observed); the forecast serving template is simulate 100,000 scenarios from each in-game state, take the earliest event, update state, repeat.

Hybrid tracker design (Castro, Andrade & Fraguela, Pattern Recognition 2020, arXiv:2003.03271v2): a slow player-specific Faster-RCNN (45 ms/frame) runs every 'jump' frames to initialize and correct drift; SSD refines on the remaining frames within the ROI; KCF runs every frame inside the ROI for fine-grain tracking; the KCF box is adjusted only when it diverges from SSD for MORE THAN 3 CONSECUTIVE FRAMES - adjusting on first disagreement was found to make the solution unstable.

Per-frame precision metric: average overlap via Intersection over Union, with per-frame overlap phi = (R_t^G intersect R_t^T) / (R_t^G union R_t^T) where R_t^G is the ground-truth box and R_t^T the tracker box; success threshold IoU > 0.5; OPE curve = percentage of frames with IoU above threshold across thresholds, AUC = its integral in [0,1].

Results: Faster-RCNN alone achieved IoU > 0.5 in only ~45% of 200 challenging frames (AUC 0.32, far from SOTA); the hybrid achieved IoU >= 0.5 in 80-90% of frames with AUC ~0.60-0.66 (e.g., Player 1: avg overlap 0.620, 91.75 fps, AUC 0.610, 2 lost frames) at 80+ fps on 1920x1080 - but the per-player network training cost (~15-47 GPU-hours per player on 1,500 semi-automatically labeled frames) makes roster-scale deployment infeasible without a generic detector + jersey-number re-ID head.

Benchmark pruning machinery (Navasardyan & Davtyan, arXiv:2608.25940v2): greedy forward selection under utility U(b|S) = g(b) * (1 - R^2(b~S)), where g(b) = Gini coefficient of the benchmark's score distribution (discrimination) and R^2(b~S) = OLS fit of the candidate on the selected set (marginal information) - the product form zeroes utility if either criterion fails; Bradley-Terry ranking P(i>j) = sigma(r_i - r_j) by MLE with L2 penalty 1e-3, Elo_i = 1500 + 400*r_i/ln10.

Empirical redundancy: across a 51-models x 12-benchmarks matrix, average pairwise Spearman rho = 0.487 (all positive); the median benchmark has roughly half its variance reconstructible from the other 11 via leave-one-model-out ridge; greedy forward selection picks 4 benchmarks (RefSpatial-Bench -> MindCube -> VSI-Bench -> BLINK) retaining 78.5% of total utility, and collapsing two substitute pairs (EmbSpatial/CV-Bench rho = 0.876, Where2Place/RefSpatial-Bench rho = 0.860) moves 22 of 51 models by >=3 ranking places.

Meta-LMS two-stage protocol (Li & Guo, arXiv:2512.00342v2): offline nonlinear-least-squares base fit, then an online meta layer running N_2 parallel models (N_2 = 500 in simulation) with exponential weighting w_{t+1,i} = w_{t,i} exp(-lambda l_t) / sum_j w_{t,j} exp(-lambda l_t), each producing y_{t+1,i}^{pred} = beta-hat_{t,i}^T phi_t(alpha-hat, x_t) aggregated as sum_i w_{t,i} y_{t+1,i}^{pred}; projected LMS per model with discount accumulator.
equation: w_{t+1,i} = w_{t,i} exp(−λ l_t)/Σ_j w_{t,j} exp(−λ l_t)

claim: Offline generalization bound (Lemma 10): (1/T) sum_{t=0}^{T-1} E|f_t(alpha*,beta_0(t),x_t) - f_t(alpha-hat,beta_0(t),x_t)|^2 <= C_1 log(N_1 T)/(N_1 T^{1-b_2}) + 8 sup_alpha M_{T,N_1}(alpha) + 8 L^2 R_M^2 b_1' D(P_T||P_T')/T^{1-b_2'}, covering temporal dependence via a dependency matrix and distribution shift via KL divergence D(P_T||P_T') - no i.i.d. requirement.

Theory limitation with practical consequence: the paper's constants are existential, not computable, and all demonstrations are simulation-only with smooth bounded drift; NFL drift is abrupt (injuries, QB changes), so the file proposes regime-conditional meta weights (separate weights for high-QB-injury vs stable weeks) and an adoption gate of >=0.005 Brier improvement over 2022-2025 weekly walk-forward, improvement concentrated in weeks 6-18.

Player similarity pipeline (Gyarmati & Hefeeda, arXiv:1603.05583v1): 660,848 sparse movement vectors (x1,y1,x2,y2,T,speed,ball-flag) from Opta 2012/13 La Liga -> mini-batch K-means K=200 -> per-player normalized 200-dim cluster-histogram profiles -> cosine-distance similarity; uniqueness U_i = sum_{j=1}^{M} d_{ij} with M=5 nearest neighbors; consistency C_i^k = (1/N) sum_t D(c_i^k, c_i^t) across periods.

Headline scouting example: Ruben Castro (Real Betis, market value 4.5M euros) sits at cosine distance 0.079 from Cristiano Ronaldo (100M euros) - a near-identical movement profile at 4.5% of the price; Messi uniqueness 0.860 (3,809 movements, consistency 0.30), Ronaldo uniqueness 0.55 (consistency 0.51); evaluation is illustrative case studies only, no holdout validation.

Per-team 2-state HMM for run/pass (Oetting, arXiv:2003.10791v1, 318,691 NFL plays 2009-2018): transition probabilities gamma_ij^(p) = exp(eta_ij^(p)) / sum_{k=1}^N exp(eta_ik^(p)) with eta_ij^(p) = beta_0^(ij) + sum_l beta_l^(ij) x_l^(p) for i != j (0 for i=j), fitted per team with AIC forward selection including interactions ydstogo x scorediff, downs x ydstogo, shotgun x ydstogo, nohuddle x scorediff, nohuddle x shotgun.

Results: weighted-average out-of-sample accuracy 0.715 on the full 2018 holdout season vs ~0.67 for earlier play-by-play-only baselines and ~0.75 for player-data models vs 58.4% naive pass-rate; per-team range 0.602 (Seattle Seahawks) to 0.779 (New England Patriots) - predictability itself is a scoutable coaching trait; but the marginal value of the HMM over a static covariate-only logistic was never tested, so the headline number does not establish that streak structure helps.

Honest validation design: strict temporal split (train 2009-2017, test 2018), clean holdout, per-team fitting, no leakage; forecast cost <1 second per match, fit cost ~7 hours per team for forward selection on a standard desktop; limitation: data ends 2018 (pre-modern pass-happy era), binary target ignores scrambles/sacks/RPOs, and the static 2009-2017 fit applied to all of 2018 has no online updating.

Xu & Moka (2024, arXiv:2409.05052v1) estimate CS:GO player ratings from team outcomes alone using a participation design matrix (rows = matches, columns = 518 players; X_ij = +1 if player j on team 1, -1 if on team 2, 0 if absent) regressed on match score differential, comparing OLS, ridge, elastic net, logistic variants, and Bayesian models whose prior mean is the player's standardized HLTV Rating2.0 box-score metric, on HLTV 'big event' matches 2018-2023 with a player-exclusion floor of 50 matches.

Pearson-test p-values for correlation between players' true plus/minus and predicted plus/minus on test data: ridge 0.57 (non-significant), Bayesian 0.03323, logistic 2.092e-05, elastic-logistic 2.2e-16; the p=0.293 correlation between initial Rating2.0 and plus/minus was also non-significant. The brief flags these claims as uninterpretable as predictive evidence because p-values are reported with no effect sizes, no MAE, no log loss, and no calibration; it also flags leakage (random 80/20 split lets same-roster matches straddle train/test; Rating2.0 prior computed from test-period matches).

Caio, Van Zandycke & De Vleeschouwer (2023, arXiv:2309.03640v1) localize a basketball in 3D from a single calibrated image by regressing the pixel displacement vector from the ball center to its vertical ground projection with an ImageNet-pretrained CNN plus 3-layer regression head (Huber loss delta=1.0, Adam lr 1e-4, 100 epochs, 8 head initializations), then lifting the projection to 3D via back-projection onto the known court plane. On the DeepSport test set the method beats the diameter-based depth baseline by ~1.7-1.8x on every metric: MAE 34+-3 px, MAPE 1.25+-0.11 m vs 2.88+-0.22, median APE 0.92+-0.15 vs 2.10+-0.38, MA3DE 1.29+-0.10 vs 2.97+-0.23, median A3DE 0.95+-0.16 vs 2.18+-0.40.

Crop-size ablation for the 3D ball-localization CNN: 64px -> MAPE 1.71+-0.17; 96px -> 1.52+-0.13; 128px -> 1.46+-0.06; 256px -> 1.04+-0.11 (best); 320px -> 1.17+-0.09; 480px -> 1.18+-0.07; 512px -> 1.25+-0.11; 640px -> 1.16+-0.07; 800px -> 1.08+-0.06. No monotonic gain beyond ~256-320 px, and image downscaling to 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 barely changes MAPE (1.33, 1.32, 1.22 vs 1.25 at full resolution). The ~1.25 m in-distribution error was judged too coarse for any NFL probability feature use.

Foulley (2021, arXiv:2106.14345v2) applies three complementary Brier-score decompositions to football WDL probability forecasts. The Murphy calibration-refinement decomposition splits expected Brier score into uncertainty minus resolution plus reliability, separating irreducible outcome variance, how well the forecast separates event classes, and miscalibration cost.
equation: E[S(P,X)] = Var(X) − E_P[(E_X(X|P) − E_X(X))²] + E_P[(E_X(X|P) − P)²] (eq. 1) = UNC − RES + REL

claim: The Brier skill score relates to Murphy components as skill equals resolution minus reliability divided by uncertainty. Empirical discrete estimators: REL = N⁻¹Σ_k n_k(x_k − p_k)², RES = N⁻¹Σ_k n_k(x_k − x̄)², UNC = x̄(1−x̄), with binning via fixed intervals, quantile intervals, or isotonic regression via PAV.

Cox (1958) logistic calibration test for probability forecasts: fit the model below and run Wald/LR tests of α=0, β=1. Pattern diagnosis: (α>0,β=1) = concave under-forecasting; (α<0,β=1) = convex over-forecasting; (α=0,β>1) = sigmoid; (α=0,β<1) = inverse-sigmoid. Applied on 384 UCL matches (2017-2020), the Poisson-ELO model showed over-forecasting of home wins (α̂=-0.259, Wald p=0.030) while away wins were very well calibrated (p=0.610/0.693).

On 384 UEFA Champions League matches (2017-2020), de-vigged bookmaker probabilities beat the Poisson-ELO scoreline model by ~4-6pp Brier skill on home and away wins (HWIN: ODD Brier 0.1732, skill 29.5% vs POI 0.1849, skill 24.8%; AWIN: 0.1569, 27.3% vs 0.1700, 21.2%), while draws were near-unforecastable for both (skill 1.4% POI, 3.0% ODD). Yates decomposition showed the within-class scattered variance (VPW) term as the dominant loss for draws (CB2 96.9% of UNC).

Osokin, Bach & Lacoste-Julien (2018, arXiv:1703.02403v4) define a calibration function as the infimum excess conditional surrogate risk when excess task risk is at least epsilon. Their Theorem 2 states: if R_Φ(f) < R*_Φ,F + Ȟ(epsilon) then R_L(f) < R*_L,F + epsilon, i.e., small excess surrogate risk implies small excess task risk whenever the calibration function is positive. It is a pure-theory paper with zero numerical results.
equation: H_{Φ,L,F}(ε) := inf_{f∈F, q∈Δ^k} δφ(f,q) s.t. δℓ(f,q) ≥ ε

claim: Osokin et al. give an ASGD optimization guarantee for consistent convex surrogates in structured prediction: explicit sample complexity so that expected excess task risk falls below epsilon after more than N* iterations, under bounded stochastic-gradient norm M, bounded optimum norm D, and a convex score set F. Level-eta consistency is the graded notion: H > 0 for all epsilon > eta. The paper concludes the classical 0-1 loss is ill-suited to structured prediction.

Osokin et al. (2018) ASGD step-size rule for the consistent convex surrogate in structured prediction, paired with the sample-complexity bound: step size gamma := 2D/(M*sqrt(N)), where M bounds the expected squared stochastic-gradient norm and D bounds the optimum norm.

Wang et al. (2026, arXiv:2601.11492v2) 'BoxMind' builds a closed-loop boxing system: atomic punch-event detection from video (anchor-free TCN detector, Pose-Region Guided two-stream attribute classifier, MoE heads), 18 hierarchical technical-tactical indicators, a BoxerGraph matchup model fusing explicit style profiles with learnable time-variant latent embeddings, and gradient-based strategy recommendation where the top-5 positive-gradient indicators are the recommended tactical adjustments. Time-variant latent embedding: E_b(t) = sum_{c=0}^{C-1} E_b^{(c)} t^c.

BoxMind's BoxerGraph-80KG matchup prediction test accuracy: Glicko 58.7%, Elo 60.3%, WHR 60.3%, indicator-only 54.0% (68.8% on Olympics), latent-only 63.5% (75.0% Olympics), unified BoxMind 69.8% (87.5% Olympics) - +9.5pp over the best baseline on the test set. The brief flags that indicator-only ablation at 54.0% suggests the system is largely a sophisticated strength-rating model, and that the Olympic 'validation' (14/16 correct on men's 80kg) is uncontrolled with expert-comparison p-values failing significance (recommendation F1 0.601 vs experts 0.467, paired t=1.623, p=0.111; advantage-label F1 0.854 vs 0.802, p=0.230).

Buhamra & Groll (2025, arXiv:2502.01613v2) augment conventional tennis covariates with statistically motivated engineered features for Grand Slam match-winner prediction: Age.30 = |age - 30| and Age.int = 0 if 28 <= age <= 32 else min(|age-28|, |age-32|), with every covariate x entering as a player difference x = x_player1 - x_player2, plus Elo ratings. Three model classes were fit on 21 feature combinations: logistic regression, GAM with P-splines, and random forest (400 trees, mtry via 10-fold CV). All validation was strictly time-ordered: expanding-window prediction on the four 2022 Grand Slams, leave-one-tournament-out over 47 tournaments, and rolling 12-tournament windows.
equation: Age.30 = |age − 30|; Age.int = 0 if 28 ≤ age ≤ 32, else min(|age − 28|, |age − 32|)

claim: On 5,013 matches from 47 men's Grand Slam tournaments (2011-2022), random forest with Points+Rank+Age.30+Elo gave classification 0.820, likelihood 0.667, Brier 0.151; the spline model with Elo+Age.30 gave the best Brier 0.149 (classification 0.792, likelihood 0.703). Enhanced features helped most model classes and metrics, but absolute likelihood/Brier gains were modest (e.g., Brier 0.153 -> 0.149), and the brief flags an inconsistency in the paper between stated subtraction direction and coefficient interpretations, making the sign of every reported effect suspect.

Yurko et al. (2019, arXiv:1906.01760v3) propose a modular continuous-time within-play valuation framework for NFL tracking data: an LSTM ball-carrier model predicts expected yards-from-current-position at every 10 Hz frame, feeding expected end-of-play yard line and, via RFCDE conditional densities, within-play expected-points/win-probability curves. Data: 1,075,720 unique frames across 14,167 plays (NFL Big Data Bowl 2017 weeks 1-6); modeling subset 154,908 frames from 4,502 ball-carrier sequences (rushes + QB scrambles), sequences mostly 2-5 seconds long.

Yurko et al. integrate a transformation g of end-of-play yard line over the estimated conditional density f-hat to get within-play expectations of arbitrary functions of final field position, e.g. expected points and win probability at any 10 Hz frame. Competing ball-carrier models: intercept-only, LASSO (glmnet, 1-SE penalty), XGBoost (100 trees, depth 3), feedforward NN (2x50 ReLU, L1, Adam), LSTM (2 layers x 50 units, 20% recurrent dropout, zero-padded sequences); validated by leave-one-week-out CV on RMSE. The LSTM had the lowest LOWO-CV RMSE overall and at every point across the sequence; XGBoost top-2 features were closest-defender distance (defense1_dist_to_ball) and ball-carrier speed (bc_s).

Kelley, Mureika & Phillips (2006, arXiv:physics/0608228v1) fit annual MLB home-run distributions as exponentials (Gutenberg-Richter analogy), frequency(N) ~ b e^{-rN} fit on the 95% of players with the lowest HR totals per year, and extrapolated the exponential parameters' evolution since 1948 to forecast record-breaking. Their headline forecast - probability of someone hitting 74 HR within 5 years >50%, after 10 years >80% - was falsified post-hoc: Bonds's 73 HR record still stood as of 2026. The brief keeps it as a negative-control case of a parametric stationarity assumption failing its own forward prediction, likely confounded by the steroid era inflating 2001-era parameters.

Kelley et al. (2006) era-relative rarity framings: Bonds's 73 HR (2001) = once-in-10-year event; Andruw Jones's 51 HR (2005) = once-in-3-year event; Ruth's 60 HR (1927) = once-in-10,000-year event, 'far more impressive than that of Bonds, even though the latter hit 73'. The brief notes no backtesting, no train/test split, no uncertainty on the probability estimates, and retains only the era-relative rarity idea as a media-framing device, not a predictive model.

Yamasaki (2026, arXiv:2608.02081v1) proposes the Isotonic Bradley-Terry (IBT) model: alternately learn BT rating parameters by (sub-)gradient and learn the rating-to-win-probability inverse link function itself by isotonic regression (PAV), guaranteeing monotone training-error improvement and exact ties (sigma=0.5) for undecidable pairs. Empirical pairwise outcomes with draws handled as half-wins: y_ij = (wins of i over j + 0.5*draws)/(matches between i,j), y_ji = 1 - y_ij.
equation: yᵢⱼ = (#{i beats j} + 0.5·#{draws})/(#matches between i,j); yⱼᵢ = 1 − yᵢⱼ

claim: IBT rating estimation minimizes average loss of sigma(r_i - r_j) against empirical win proportions y_ij, with NLL loss phi_nll(u,v) = -v log u or squared loss phi_sq(u,v) = (u-v)^2. The PAV inner problem has closed form z_k = group mean for NLL/squared loss; adjacent groups merge while monotonicity is violated; sigma-hat_ij = z_k for rating diffs in [L_k, R_k]. Ranking uses Borda count sum_j sigma(rhat_i - rhat_j), not raw rates, because a non-strictly-increasing link breaks the rate-Borda equivalence.
equation: (r̂ᵢ) ∈ argmin (1/|D_tra|)Σ φ(σ(rᵢ−rⱼ), yᵢⱼ); NLL φ_nll(u,v) = −v log u; squared φ_sq(u,v) = (u−v)²

claim: IBT evaluation uses Kendall's tau in the form tau = (n+ - n-)/sqrt((|D|-n+)(|D|-n-)), with n+ counting concordant (sigma(r_i-r_j)-0.5)*(y_ij-0.5)>0 pairs and n- the analog, and a tie-rate statistic = |{(i,j) in D : sigma(r_i-r_j)=0.5}|/|D| capturing exact ties for undecidable pairs.

On synthetic misspecified-link data (Cauchy-N), IBT improved test win-probability-prediction error vs logistic-BT in most cells - e.g. n=25, N=1, 1:9 split: .3956+-.0474 BT vs .3689+-.0489 IBT; n=50, N=25, 9:1: .0084+-.0011 vs .0080+-.0011, many cells Mann-Whitney significant p<0.05 - with gains most pronounced when n, N, |D_tra| are small (regularization prevents |rhat_i - rhat_j| blowups). Ranking improvements were driven by exact ties (sigma-hat=0.5) for undecidable pairs; more alternating updates beyond t~1 often degraded performance (overfitting), so the update count is chosen by 10-fold CV. Real-data wins: PL 2024/25, MLB 2025, and ATP 2025 (n=457, sparse: only 2522/104196 pairs observed).

Grishina et al. (KDD '26, arXiv:2606.07492v1) show a Bradley-Terry tournament over pairwise algorithm comparisons across 89 recommender datasets beats naive mean/sum NDCG aggregation on a transitive-triplets consistency metric and stays robust to ~70% missing comparisons. BT model: Pr(i beats j) = p_i/(p_i + p_j) with sum_i p_i = 1 or product_i p_i = 1; log-likelihood l(p) = sum_{i,j} W_ij (ln p_i - ln(p_i + p_j)); Zermelo iteration p'_i <- sum_j W_ij / sum_j (W_ij + W_ji)/(p_i + p_j), renormalized p_i <- p'_i/(prod_j p_j)^{1/n}.
equation: Pr(i ≻ j) = p_i/(p_i + p_j), Σ_i p_i = 1 or Π_i p_i = 1

claim: The transitive-triplet ratio = 1/((n choose 3)*D - missing) * sum_d sum_{i1!=i2!=i3} I{i1^d beats i2^d beats i3^d} measures ranking consistency across datasets, tie-aware (transitive if i1 >= i2 >= i3). Results (NDCG@10, triplet ratio w/o ties -> w/ ties): Mean 0.488->0.613; Sum 0.484->0.613; BT 0.510->0.631; PL 0.503->0.631; mean Kendall tau: Mean 0.542, Sum 0.541, BT 0.567, PL 0.558. Triplet ratio for BT/PL stays ~0.6 until >0.7 of comparisons are missing, while Sum/Mean decline 0.6 -> ~0.4.
equation: = 1/((n choose 3)·D − missing) · Σ_d Σ_{i_1≠i_2≠i_3} I{i_1^d ≻ i_2^d ≻ i_3^d}

claim: Grishina et al. covariate-adjusted BT: P(i beats j | x) = sigma(beta_{i0} - beta_{j0} + <x,beta_i> - <x,beta_j>) with fusion-regularized likelihood L(B) = lambda_0 sum_{i<j} sqrt((beta_{i0}-beta_{j0})^2+eps) + lambda_1 sum_k sum_{i<j} sqrt((beta_{ik}-beta_{jk})^2+eps), objective l(B) - L(B) maximized subject to sum_i beta_{ij} = 0 for all j, fitted by L-BFGS-B. Holdout prediction (Train 79 / Holdout 10), top-1 hits: Mean 0.02, BT 0.24, Covariate BT 0.28, BT tree 0.26; Kendall tau: Mean 0.438, BT 0.489, Covariate BT 0.572, tree 0.501. Bayesian BT variant: W_ij ~ Binomial(N_ij, e^{beta_i}/(e^{beta_i}+e^{beta_j})), beta_i ~ Normal(0, sigma-bar), sigma-bar ~ LogNormal(0, 0.5) via Metropolis-Hastings.

Maitra et al. (2026, arXiv:2512.18013v1) propose a data-driven Elo tuning protocol: enumerate candidate experience-based K-factor schedules and game-count cutoffs, compute rating histories under each, and select the configuration maximizing a rating-difference classifier's accuracy/F1. Standard Elo: expected score E_A = 1/(1 + 10^{(R_B - R_A)/400}) (D=400 deliberately not tuned) and update R' = R + K_i(S - E), S in {1,0}; piecewise K-function K_i = K_a if n_i <= n_{c1}, K_b if n_{c1} < n_i <= n_{c2}, K_c if n_i > n_{c2}, where n_i = games played.

The fitted K schedule from Maitra et al. (2026): K_i = 60 if n_i <= 5; 30 if 5 < n_i <= 10; 16 if n_i > 10. Candidate space: K triples {(60,30,16) [online-chess baseline], (30,30,30) [constant-K control], (30,16,8) [stability], (100,50,25) [responsiveness]} x cutoff pairs {(5,10), ([q10]+1,[q25]+1), ([q25]+1,[q50]+1)}. Tuner: logistic regression P(Player 1 wins) = sigma(beta_0 + beta_1*(R_1 - R_2)); real-data fit beta_0 = -0.0623 (se 0.001), beta_1 = 0.0046 (se 9.49e-06), t = 489.545, all p ~= 0. The brief flags adversarial problems: tuner fit AND evaluated in-sample (data snooping by construction), top configs tied at F1 0.554 vs 0.548 with 'random' selection among ties, no CV or walk-forward, and Ludo is high-luck.
equation: K_i = K_a if n_i ≤ n_{c1}; K_b if n_{c1} < n_i ≤ n_{c2}; K_c if n_i > n_{c2}

claim: GoalNet (arXiv:2503.09737) is a GNN-based soccer player evaluation system that builds an event-centric graph of up to 22 on-pitch players per event, predicts the change in expected threat (Delta-xT), and attributes that Delta-xT across involved players proportional to their learned final-layer embedding magnitudes - surfacing 'hidden pivotal' facilitators (defensive mids, defenders) that action-valuation systems like VAEP under-credit. Three variants: Basic GoalNet (2 GCN layers), GATGoalNet (multi-head graph attention), TransGoalNet (graph transformer with role/spatial positional encodings and relational encodings r_uv).

GoalNet GCN propagation: H^{l+1} = sigma(A H^l W^l) with sigma = ReLU; edge MLP e'_uv = ReLU(W_2 . ReLU(W_1 . e_uv)); mean pooling z = (1/|V|) sum_v h_v with prediction yhat = W_4 . ReLU(W_3 . z) trained with MSE. Delta-xT response: Delta-xT = xT_current - xT_previous for the same team; Delta-xT = xT_current + xT_previous when possession changes (erasing opponent threat + adding own).

GoalNet graph-attention weights: alpha_uv = exp(LeakyReLU(a^T [W h_u^l || W h_v^l])) / sum_{w in N(v)} exp(LeakyReLU(a^T [W h_w^l || W h_v^l])); multi-head update h_v^{l+1} = sigma(concat_m sum_{u in N(v)} alpha_uv^m W^m h_u^l). Temporal-context ablation (previous events k in {1,3,5,7,9}): TransGoalNet validation MAE stayed flat at 0.0030-0.0031 across k=1-7 (best at k=5), while Baseline GCN varied 0.0082-0.0227 and all models deteriorated at k=9 (overfitting/noise). Player rankings diverged from VAEP: VAEP top-3 Ryan Bennett, Andrew Surman, Harry Arter vs TransGoalNet top-3 Mesut Ozil, Cesc Fabregas, Junior Stanislas; Aston Villa baseline/GAT credited defensive midfielder Idrissa Gana Gueye vs VAEP's striker Rudy Gestede.

Zhong & Ling (2023, arXiv:2309.03808v2) sharpen the entry-wise (l-infinity) eigenvector perturbation bound for spectral rank aggregation under the Erdos-Renyi Outliers (ERO) model, cutting sample complexity for accurate ranking from Omega(n^{4/3} log^{3/2} n) to Omega(n log n) pairwise measurements via a leave-one-out proof technique. ERO model: H_ij = r_i - r_j with prob. eta*p; Z_ij ~ i.i.d. U[-M,M] with prob. (1-eta)*p; 0 with prob. 1-p; unified as H_ij = X_ij(Y_ij(r_i - r_j) + (1-Y_ij)Z_ij) with X~Bernoulli(p), Y~Bernoulli(eta). Algorithms: top eigenvector of iH (H anti-symmetric => iH Hermitian), and degree-normalized top eigenvector of iD^{-1}H with D = diag(|H| 1_n), both phase-resolved and ranked by entries of Re(e^{i theta-hat} phi_1).

The spectral rank-aggregation SNR condition: SNR(eta,p,n,r,M) := sqrt(eta^2 p n / log n) * ||r - alpha 1_n|| / (sqrt(n) * M) must exceed ~1 (Assumption 3.1). Theorem 3.2 gives min_{|beta|=1} ||phi_1 - beta phi-bar_1||_inf <= SNR^{-1} ||phi-bar_1||_inf and ranking error R(x, xbar) <= SNR^{-1}; for uniform scores r_k=k the maximum-displacement bound simplifies to rho_inf(pi, pi-hat) <= SNR^{-1}. Numerically: SNR=0.5 -> relative l-inf error ~0.8; SNR=0.8 -> ~0.5; SNR=1.7 -> ~0.2, confirming the SNR^{-1} decay rate; maximum displacement at SNR 0.5/0.8/1.7 was ~0.4/0.3/0.15.

Anderson et al. (2022, arXiv:2206.11258v1) extend rankability from r = f(k, |P|, tau) to r = f(k, |P|, tau, beta), where k = distance of the dominance matrix D-bar from a perfectly rankable matrix, |P| = number of optimal rankings, tau = diameter of the optimal set (Kendall-tau distance between the two farthest optimal rankings), and beta = a new measure of the LOCATION of indecision among multiple optimal rankings: a weighted function of the number and location of fractional entries of the X-bar* matrix from the linear ordering model, penalizing fractional entries further from the diagonal and lower in the ranking (lower beta is better). Four artificial matrices engineered to have identical k, |P|, tau but different beta showed beta separates them while the other three measures cannot.

RPLIB motivating findings: 98% of the 50 instances in the LOLIB IO folder have more than one optimal ranking even though LOLIB stores only one; an example model card (dataset_id 363) lists 1,095 optimal rankings with objective value 204 on a 65x65 dominance matrix; a dominance matrix with beginning/ending row indices 6 and 10 yields (10-6+1)! = 5! = 120 multiple optimal rankings. March Madness 2002 vs 2008 X-bar* matrices showed little top-of-ranking disagreement in 2002 vs visible top disagreement in 2008, consistent with prior findings that rankability correlates with tournament predictability.

Fioravanti, Delbianco & Tohme (2021, arXiv:2110.00001v2) decompose English Rugby Premiership 2020/21 score differences into latent team ability (random walk anchored on prior season), an 'effort' proxy (tries share of scoring attempts), home advantage, and heavy-tailed luck. Likelihood: y_g ~ t_nu(a_diff(g) + eff_diff(g) + ha(g), sigma_y) with nu ~ Gamma(9, 0.5); ability a_{hw,ht} = a_{hw-1,ht} + sigma*eta (random walk), season start a_{1,ht} = beta_prev*prevperf(ht) + eta; effort eff_diff(g) = beta_effort*(effH(g) - effA(g)); home advantage ha(g) = beta_home + beta_atten*atten(g) (atten = 0/1 fan attendance).
equation: y_g ~ t_ν(a_diff(g) + eff_diff(g) + ha(g), σ_y), ν ~ Gamma(9, 0.5)

claim: On 122 English Premiership Rugby 2020/21 games, the variance decomposition Var(Performance) = Var(Luck) + Var(Effort) + Var(Ability) gave Var(Luck) = p(1-p)/g = 0.01136364 (p=0.5, g=22), Var(Performance) = 0.03798835, Var(Effort) = 0.01563645, Var(Ability) = 0.01098826 - roughly equal thirds of performance variance from ability, effort, and luck. Posteriors: beta_effort = 3.114 [1.574, 4.639]; beta_home = 0.366 [0.036, 0.704] (Model I); nu = 13.011 [5.445, 25.335]; sigma_y = 1.683 [1.380, 2.012]. The brief flags a fatal leakage for direct predictive use: the effort proxy is computed from game g's own tries and kick attempts - the same game whose score difference y_g is the target.

Sandholtz, Mortensen & Bornn (2020, arXiv:1912.05129v2) measure spatial allocative efficiency in basketball: a lineup is allocatively efficient at a court location if players' FG% ranks match their FGA-rate ranks (best shooter takes the most shots). Lineup Points Lost: redistribute the shot vector A_i to A*_i via a permutation g(.) matching FGA ranks to FG% ranks (total attempts per cell preserved), LPL_i = sum_j v_i * xi_ij * (A*_ij - A_ij), per-shot version LPL^Shot_i = LPL_i/sum_j A_ij; player contribution PLC_ij = LPL_i * (A*_ij - A_ij)/sum_j |A*_ij - A_ij| (positive = undershooting, negative = overshooting).

The Bayesian game-level regression linking misallocation to outcomes: Score_abg = mu + alpha_a + beta_b + gamma*I(Home_ag) + theta*TGLPL_ag + epsilon_abg, epsilon ~ N(0, sigma^2), where TGLPL aggregates game-level Lineup Points Lost. Posterior mean theta = -0.62 with 95% HPD (-1.08, -0.17): each additional lineup point lost costs 0.62 actual points; Houston lost only ~1 point/game to misallocation (most efficient), Washington lost >3 points/game (least); 10% of 2016-17 games were decided by <=2 points. Permutation test on starting lineups: GSW and POR p-hat = 0.000 (best allocative efficiency), CLE 0.002, SAC 0.442 (worst).
equation: Score_abg = μ + α_a + β_b + γ·I(Home_ag) + θ·TGLPL_ag + ε_abg

claim: FG% surfaces in the allocative-efficiency framework (Bayesian hierarchical, Cervone et al. 2016 adaptation): logit(pi_j(s)) = beta'x + Z_j(s) with x = [intercept, player position, shot distance, position x distance]; Z_j(s) = w_j' Lambda Psi(s) is a Gaussian process with deterministic basis Lambda (D=16 bases) from NMF of per-player LGCP intensity fits of made-shot locations (P ~= B Lambda), and Psi(s) a linear-interpolation mesh basis; player weights regularized by a CAR prior shrinking toward the 5 nearest neighbors in NMF loading space: (w_j | w_{-(j)}, tau^2) ~ N(mean of neighbors, tau^2/n_j * I_D), tau^2 ~ InvGam(1,1); fit by INLA on a 1ft x 1ft court grid (M=2350 cells). Simpson's-paradox finding: aggregate FGA-rate vs PPS looks flat/slightly negative, but conditioning on court region flips it positive everywhere - motivating the spatial treatment.

Chen, Chen & Li (2017, arXiv:1710.06056v1) study asymptotically optimal sequential design for rank aggregation: adaptively choosing which pair to compare next, when to stop, and how to rank, to minimize expected Kendall's tau distance plus comparison cost c*T as c->0. Loss: sum_{i<j} I(theta_i>theta_j)I(R_i>R_j) + I(theta_i<theta_j)I(R_i<R_j) + cT (Kendall's tau distance + sampling cost). The brief verdict: REJECT for the prediction stack (a fixed 272-game schedule has no control over data collection), ADAPT only Lemma 5's exponential MLE deviation bound as a ratings-convergence diagnostic.

Chen et al. Lemma 5 (exponential MLE deviation bound for sequential rank aggregation): P_theta(sup_{n<=t<=m} ||theta-hat^{(t)} - theta|| >= eps_1) <= e^{-Omega(n eps_lambda^2 eps_1^4)} x O(m^K), for n eps_lambda^2 eps_1^4 -> infinity. The pair-selection rule is epsilon-greedy: with prob. 1-p solve the saddle-point D(theta) = max_{lambda in Delta} min_{theta-tilde: r(theta-tilde) != r(theta)} sum_{(i,j)} lambda^{i,j} D^{i,j}(theta || theta-tilde), with prob. p explore uniformly. The brief ports this as an early-season 'ratings have converged' gate replacing the 'ratings converge by Week 6' heuristic, though it flags the O(m^K) term as vacuous at K=32 NFL teams.
equation: P_θ(sup_{n≤t≤m} ‖θ̂^{(t)}−θ‖ ≥ ε_1) ≤ e^{−Ω(n ε_λ² ε_1⁴)} × O(m^K)

claim: Catterall, Lynch et al. (arXiv:2601.19479v1) forecast time-to-injury - not binary injury/no-injury - in elite women's football using a DeepHit neural survival network (MLP backbone, deliberately not RNN because irregular spacing/heavy missingness made recurrence infeasible) outputting a PMF over discrete time bins for first-hitting-time of injury, trained with combined log-likelihood + ranking loss, over 21-day input windows with a 7-day prediction horizon. Data: SoccerMon Team B subset - 37 players from two elite Norwegian women's first-division teams, 322 recorded days (2020-2021), 4,449 player-date observations, 39 features (self-reports, STATSports APEX GNSS), 43 injuries.

DeepHit chronological 80/20 C-index went from 0.660 (linear interpolation imputation) to 0.762 (bespoke teammate-relative imputation) - a +0.102 C-index lift from imputation choice alone. Baselines on next-day binary injury prediction: RF F1 0.533, AUC 0.779, precision 1.000, recall 0.364 (zero false positives, caught 36.4% of injuries); XGBoost F1 0.429, AUC 0.876, precision 1.000, recall 0.271; logistic F1 0.071, AUC 0.758, precision 0.037, recall 0.833. LOPO validation: C-index IQR = 0.192, best held-out player 0.974, worst near-useless - high within-player load variance hurts generalization. Global feature importance: average running speed, soreness, monotony, prior injury count most influential; session time surprisingly important; ACWR, sprint metrics, subjective stress contributed little. Sports-injury models average AUC 0.69 / F1 0.73 (Leckey et al. 2024).

Michels, Otting & Langrock (2022, arXiv:2202.10085v2) fit a beta-inflated state-space model of in-play betting stakes on all 306 matches of the 2017/18 Bundesliga season (1 Hz aggregated to 1-minute intervals; 306 series x up to 85 minutes = 26,010 observations), testing whether bettors trade on pre-game strength (fundamental analysis) or in-game momentum (technical analysis). Observation: y_t ~ BEINF(mu_t, sigma, p, q) (beta-inflated to allow y_t exactly 0 or 1); density f(y_t) = p if y_t=0, (1-p-q)h(y_t) if 0<y_t<1, q if y_t=1, with a = mu_t(1-sigma^2)/sigma^2, b = (1-mu_t)(1-sigma^2)/sigma^2. Baseline mean mu_t = logit^{-1}(alpha_0 + alpha*prewindiff + g_t); latent market-sentiment state g_t = phi g_{t-1} + beta*vaepdiff_{t-1} + omega eta_t, eta_t iid N(0,1), phi in (-1,1).

Extended in-play stake model with P-spline time-varying coefficients: mu_t = logit^{-1}(alpha_0 + sum_k nu_k^alpha B_k(t)*prewindiff + zeta_1*scorediff_t + zeta_2*winprobteam_t + g_t), K=10 cubic B-splines with roughness penalty on second differences, lambda_alpha and lambda_beta chosen by AIC over a 7x7 grid. Penalized log-likelihood: l_p = log(L_approx) - lambda_alpha/2 sum_{k=3}^K (Delta^2 nu_k^alpha)^2 - lambda_beta/2 sum_{k=3}^K (Delta^2 nu_k^beta)^2; AIC = -2l + 2*df-hat via Gray (1992); likelihood via Kitagawa (1987) fine state discretization to an m-state HMM, forward algorithm O(m^2 T).
equation: μ_t = logit⁻¹(α_0 + Σ_k ν_k^α B_k(t)·prewindiff + ζ_1·scorediff_t + ζ_2·winprobteam_t + g_t)

claim: Baseline SSM estimates: phi-hat = 0.968 [0.964; 0.971] (market sentiment highly persistent); omega-hat = 0.249 [0.238; 0.261]; sigma-hat = 0.300 [0.296; 0.303]; alpha-hat_0 = -0.195 [-0.278; -0.113] - away-team stake bias at equal odds (bettors underestimate home advantage, cf. Levitt 2004); alpha-hat (prewindiff) = 2.395 [2.151; 2.640]; beta-hat (vaepdiff) = 0.600 [0.550; 0.651]. Model comparison: no-prewindiff Delta-AIC = 339.17, no-vaepdiff Delta-AIC = 522.04, time-varying coefficients favored by Delta-AIC = 270.62. Varying-coefficient model: pre-game strength effect positive throughout but decreasing approximately linearly over time (strongest at kickoff); VAEP/in-game momentum effect slightly positive in the first half then rapidly increasing in the second half - bettors overweight late in-game momentum. A case study (HSV vs Werder) found bookmaker live win probabilities derived from odds barely respond to VAEP swings: 'changes in the win probability are almost exclusively resulting from the time remaining' - bookmakers do not price in-play momentum the way bettors bet it.

Maystre, Kristof, Gonzalez Ferrer & Grossglauser (2016, arXiv:1609.01176v1) predict national-team soccer matches by relating matches through shared PLAYERS via a 'player kernel' in a Gaussian-process classification framework - team strength = sum of player skills, sharing knowledge from abundant club matches into sparse national-team fixtures. Zermelo/Bradley-Terry/Elo as GP classification: P(u beats v) = 1/(1+exp[-(s_u - s_v)]) = 1/(1+exp(-s^T x)), s ~ N(0, sigma^2 I) so f(x) = s^T x is a GP with k(x,x') = sigma^2 x^T x'. Draws via Rao-Kupper: P(u beats v) = 1/(1+exp[f(x)-alpha]), P(draw) = (e^{2alpha}-1) P(u beats v) P(v beats u).

Player kernel: lineup vector z in R^P with z_p = +1 (winner's lineup), -1 (loser's), 0 else; k(z,z') = sigma^2 z^T z'. Positive when the same players win both matches; negative when players win one and lose the other; zero for disjoint lineups. The dual/match-space view avoids estimating per-player skills in the P > N regime. Metric: average log loss = -(1/T) sum_i [1{y_i=W} log p_i^W + 1{y_i=D} log p_i^D + 1{y_i=L} log p_i^L].

Player-kernel GP results (average log loss, lower better): Euro 2008 (N=4,390 matches, P=7,875 players, T=31 test): PlayerKern 0.969 vs Elo 0.910 vs Odds 0.979 vs Random 1.099; Euro 2012 (N=15,594, P=21,735, T=31): 0.939 vs 1.003 vs 0.953 vs 1.099; Euro 2016 (N=24,887, P=33,157, T=51): 1.067 vs 1.102 vs 1.020 vs 1.099. PlayerKern was competitive with bookmaker odds in 2008/2012 and worse in 2016 (a less predictable tournament overall), but more CONSISTENT than Elo across tournaments (Elo swung 0.910 -> 1.003 -> 1.102) - the uncertainty quantification pays off. The kernel heatmap showed national-team matches have non-zero covariance with club matches of all competitions - the transfer channel is real.

Teich, Lutz & Kassarnig (2016, arXiv:1601.00574) predict the outcome of individual NFL plays from game situation + parsed play-description strings across classification and regression framings. Their 'progress' measure - a down-aware continuous play-outcome target needing only down/distance (no win-probability model like EPA): progress(down, togo, gained) = 0 if down in {3,4} and gained<togo; (gained/togo)^down if down in {1,2} and gained<togo; 1 if gained>=togo (linear on 1st down, quadratic on 2nd; ad hoc - quadratic penalty asserted, not fitted). Data: 177,245 plays from all NFL games 2009-2014 via nflgame API (penalties, field goals, punts, sacks, fumbles filtered out).
equation: progress(down, togo, gained) = 0 if down∈{3,4} and gained<togo; (gained/togo)^down if down∈{1,2} and gained<togo; 1 if gained≥togo

claim: Teich et al. NFL play prediction results: success classification (70% failure / 30% success): RBF SVM best - accuracy 66.65%, precision 67.62%, recall 63.75%, F1 65.63% (C=2^1, gamma=2^-17); SVD LDA 66.91%/67.20%/65.05%/66.11%; decision tree (1 rule: togo <= 7.5) 69.2% accuracy but precision 47.9%, recall 50.0%; neural nets collapsed to majority class (~70.5% accuracy, recall ~0). Yards regression: RBF SVR best - MAE 5.207 yds, RMSE 8.977 yds. Progress regression: RBF SVR best - MAE 0.1351, RMSE 0.2332. ANOVA F-test: togo 16146.92 (highest), down 6690.42, pass 2927.44; team=NE 48.01 vs team=MIA 0.00005 - million-fold spread suggesting memorization of team identity (one-hot features let the model memorize team names) rather than generalization.

Singh, Reddy & Chopra (2026, arXiv:2607.00164v1) train an LLM forecaster (Qwen2.5-7B) via RLVR on NFL in-game win probability using a reward of 1 minus squared error against a state-conditioned EMPIRICAL-RATE TEACHER p-hat(x) instead of the realized binary outcome: reward r = 1 - (p - p-hat(x))^2 (rate target), vs naive r = 1 - (p - y)^2 (realized outcome).
