Murphy RES and Brier min explainer (ops/MURPHY_RES_AND_BRIER_MIN.md): Brier score (verbatim): `Brier = average of (p − y)²`, where p = forecast probability and y = outcome (1 = win, 0 = loss). Range 0–1; lower is better. Perfect always-right certainty → near 0. Coin-flip 50/50 → about 0.25. Murphy decomposition (verbatim identity): `Brier ≈ REL − RES + UNC`, computed by sorting forecasts into bins (e.g., 10 equal-width buckets of p). Table (verbatim): UNC uncertainty = baseRate × (1 − baseRate), want: context only, live ~0.25; REL reliability = how wrong each bin's average p is vs actual win rate, want: low, live ~0.026; RES resolution = how much each bin's actual win rate differs from overall average, want: high, live ~0.002. Murphy RES in one sentence (verbatim): 'When we group picks by confidence, do those groups actually win at different rates?' If every group wins ~50%, RES ≈ 0 — the model is not ranking.

Murphy Brier minimization plan: back-of-envelope derivation (verbatim logic) - if UNC ≈ 0.25 and some residual REL ≈ 0.02 remain, then to hit Brier ≤ 0.22 you need roughly RES ≳ 0.03 (order of magnitude) — ~15× live 0.002. Minimization plan (honest, prioritized): 1) Raise RES (main job): fewer, better picks; better ranking score; independent model probabilities; sport models; pause dead markets. 2) Lower REL (secondary): Platt / temperature / isotonic — only after RES moves; 'maps alone cannot unlock PROVEN at RES≈0.' Recalibration maps (Platt/temperature/isotonic) are explicitly secondary: they lower REL but cannot fix RES≈0 — so calibration alone can never unlock PROVEN from this state. GSE floor: Brier ≤ 0.22 before PROVEN is even considered. Autonomy rules: selective + pause + proven-path plan automatic; metrics cron automatic; PROVEN publish only when floors + GREEN×K + AUTO_PUBLISH policy — never faked; founder needs no clicks for measurement or filtering. The Murphy file's live values (REL ~0.026, RES ~0.002, UNC ~0.25) are consistent with Brier ≈ 0.026 − 0.002 + 0.25 = 0.274 ≈ 0.275, so they describe the same underlying state as the 2026-08-09 snapshot.

Rules (verbatim): 1) `asOf` must be ISO-8601 with time (date-only refused — ambiguous for decisions). 2) Query `asOf` must not be beyond wall-clock + 120s skew (`asof_future` → HTTP 422). 3) Stored rows only readable when `record.asOf <= query.asOf` (equality allowed) — the core anti-look-ahead rule. API codes: `asof_missing` (empty), `asof_invalid` (unparseable / date-only), `asof_future` (beyond skew), `future_leak` (record after query), `pit_flag_false` (write without pitCorrect). Writes require the `pitCorrect: true` flag; a write without it is rejected. Records under `rights_hold` cannot be public. Functions: `parseAsOfMs`, `validateQueryAsOf`, `validateFeatureWrite`, `validatePitQuery`, `selectLatestAsOf`, `detectFutureLeak`, `assertNoLeak`. Any historical backtest that replays features must honor `record.asOf <= query.asOf` or its results are contaminated by look-ahead.

PROVEN path hard definition (ops/PROVEN_PATH_HONEST_2026-08-09.md): PROVEN gate conditions (all must hold) - canonical settled ≥ floor (observed: 1017 ≥ 100); live eligibility GREEN for streak K=3 (3 consecutive GREEN runs); publish policy effective (AUTO_PUBLISH or PUBLISHED); `canExposePerformanceStats` = publishedEffective && GREEN. Absolute floors (live): Brier ≤ 0.22 · ECE ≤ 0.05 · Murphy REL ≤ 0.05 · n ≥ 100. Honest live p resolver priority (in `live-calibration-p.ts`): `marketFairProb` → independent `trueProb` → MONEYLINE confidence only; SPREAD/TOTAL picks without a fair p are excluded from absolute floors (never feed rank scores into p). Hard rules: never conf-echo rankingP as independent; never edge-as-p; PERFORMANCE_STATS stays dark while RED. Progression ladder steps: A) deploy honest p + re-run calibration-metrics → recompute Brier/ECE without rank-as-p pollution; B) `generate-signal-slate` every 2h → new picks with independent rankingP; C) settle + accumulate → RES rises when independents price; D) 3 consecutive GREEN runs. Regression guard: maps (temperature / Platt / PAVA isotonic calibrations) stay OFF until an offline bakeoff shows holdout improvement AND the founder enables them.

PROVEN path post-mortem (2026-08-09 calibration failure): live class was stuck RED with Brier ≈ 0.275 (vs ≤ 0.22 floor), ECE ≈ 0.112 (vs ≤ 0.05), RES ≈ 0.002 (essentially zero discrimination). Three measured root causes: (1) p = confidence/100 applied to SPREAD/TOTAL rank scores → artificial overconfidence; (2) independentCoverage 0% on the historical sample → ranking could not raise RES; (3) calibration maps correctly OFF (using isotonic to rewrite p to invent GREEN would be fabrication). Shipped: honest live p resolver; wiring into calibration-metrics cron; signal slate generation so future independents carry rankingP coverage; reliability chart component (`components/calibration/reliability-chart.tsx`) for ops/methodology; RPCP residual attribution showing `missing_independent` as the primary bottleneck - any picks without an independent fair probability cannot move RES, so engine coverage must carry independent pricing to be credible. Sample n vs map n integrity memo (ops/SAMPLE_N_VS_MAP_N.md): reconciles two different settled-pick populations so nobody 'fixes' the gap by dropping the eligibility filter. `sample.canonicalSettled` population: published · !bootstrap · not seed · result ∈ {WIN, LOSS, PUSH}. Calibration map n population: published · !bootstrap · not seed · result ∈ {WIN, LOSS} · `signalSnapshot.eligibleForLearning=true` · finite confidence · used for Brier/ECE. Integrity rule: map n is stricter (no PUSH, learning flag); PROVEN uses map metrics (Brier/ECE/Murphy on learning-eligible WIN/LOSS), never raw win rate on the 1017 canonical settled. Findings: canonicalSettled = 1017 ≈ wins 515 + losses 499 + pushes 3; calibration map n = 760 = learning-eligible WIN/LOSS rows with usable confidence; gap ≈ 254–257 rows ≈ W/L rows excluded by `eligibleForLearning=false` and/or missing confidence (NOT hidden seed rows - both populations exclude seed/bootstrap). The ~25% gap (257/1017 ≈ 25.3%) between canonical settled and calibration-usable picks is the eligibility-confidence attrition rate; the memo treats this as intentional and unfixable-by-convention. Explicit anti-gaming rule: do not 'fix' 760→1017 by dropping `eligibleForLearning`.

Pick-proof trust-layer design (2026-07-10): SHA-256 Merkle receipts are live per output pre-kickoff; Pedersen commitments are additively homomorphic, perfectly hiding and computationally binding at ~128-bit DLOG security (not ZK in the proof-system sense, not post-quantum); Halo2/IPA recursion yields constant ~3-5 KB proofs with under 60 ms mobile verification and no trusted setup, and is explicitly not post-quantum; STARK proofs are hash-based (FRI), transparent, post-quantum under standard hash assumptions, with larger proofs and slower provers.

Rotation deskew (reconstructed): let v_axis be the unit direction vector of the detected field-axis line in image coordinates and e_x = (1, 0) the canonical field long axis; the camera roll angle is phi = arccos(v_axis · e_x) with sign from the cross product (v_axis × e_x)_z, and the image is deskewed by rotating by -phi about its center; the exact operands of arccos are reconstructed (paper only names the function and the two lines), confidence MEDIUM.

Per-frame yard calibration: yard lines are painted every 5 yards; detecting adjacent full-field lines and measuring pixel separation d_5yd gives px_per_yard = d_5yd / 5 (worked example ~82 distance-units per yard), recomputed per frame; the homography cross-check asserts the fitted H's local scale agrees with measured px_per_yard within 10% tolerance (derived), and disagreement means H is rejected.

Euclidean speed is computed as d(p, q) = sqrt((q1 - p1)^2 + (q2 - p2)^2); worked example (DeSean Jackson top speed): 215.5 distance-units over 0.2 s (5 fps) × (1 yard / ~82 d) = 12.8 yd/s = 38.4 ft/s = 26.2 mph; the paper notes this reads HIGH vs Next Gen Stats and recommends relative comparison across players, not absolute values.

arXiv:1808.07501v2 (Greenberg, ADAPT) introduces a 'Practical' transform of proper scoring rules that stays proper while making scores human-legible: 0 points = random guess, positive points iff correct, bounded losses, capped confidence; the transform is S*(p,c) = S_max·(S(p,c)−S(p_rand,c))/(S(p_max,1)−S(p_rand,1)), proved proper on [p_rand,p_max], and is base-independent in the binary case (reduces to a linear transform of the log score).

The practical log rule is parameterized s_max=10, p_max=0.99, s_min = -((10·log(99/50))/log(50)) = -57.26893683880667, δ=0.4 interval expansion, c=100 (Distance rule) / c=ln(100)=4.60517 (Order-of-Magnitude rule): a correct 99% forecast earns max 10 points, worst loss floored at -57.27, random guess scores 0; proposed gate is Spearman rank correlation ≥ 0.95 vs raw log score.

Hunter, Vielma, Zaman 2016 (ADAPT) formulate DFS tournament lineup construction as maximizing U(S) = P(∪_{i∈S} E_i), the probability at least one of k entries wins; U is nonnegative, monotone, submodular, so greedy gives U(Sg)/U(S*) ≥ 1 − e^{ -1}; the pairwise approximation is U₂(S) = Σ_i P(E_i) − (1/2)Σ_{i≠j} P(E_i ∩ E_j) with error bound 0 ≤ U(S) − U₂(S) ≤ 20c(kp)³.

The DFS portfolio paper operationalizes construction as a sequential integer program: maximize projected score subject to variance ≥ floor, pairwise covariance/overlap ≤ caps with prior lineups, salary/position constraints; Type 4 stacking (correlated teammates) performed best; recommended max overlap 7 (very small slates) to 4 (slates with >9 games); in MLB (10 contests, 200 lineups each) it produced outright wins and best ranks 1/47,916, 3/38,333, 7/38,333, 2/38,333 in large-field GPPs.

arXiv:2609.08249v1 (Tsuboi 2026) on projectile projection angles in track-and-field (drag/lift perturbations) carries a REJECT verdict: no data, no ML, no mechanism connecting to fantasy or game prediction; rejected in favor of ledger 1309's replacement paper 2603.21163 (ADAPT).

Baughman et al. 2021 (ADAPT with heavy caveats) describe a production-scale NLP pipeline for fantasy football: 50,000 sources → NER (13 entity types) → doc2vec embeddings (94 GB training text) → deep classifiers for boom/bust/hidden-injury/meaningful-touches → projection adjustment fitting 24 PDFs per player with 1,000 Monte-Carlo draws, displaying 15th/85th percentiles; label equations, loss functions, and the 24-PDF fitting procedure are not given (trade-secret omissions).

Classifier results reported in the Baughman et al. ledger: entity detector precision 79%, recall 73%, F1 76%; bust accuracy 55%, boom 67%, hidden injury 77% (PPV 68.1%), meaningful touches 91.4%; bust NPV 85.5% against a real-world bust base rate of 12%; projection RMSE ESPN 6.81, Watson-adjusted 6.92 (worse standalone), combined 6.78; red flags include the 98-layer depth claim being implausible and 2018 deployment claims being unverifiable.

Zigler & Cefalu 2017 (ADAPT) propose Posterior Predictive Treatment Assignment (PPTA) for causal-effect estimation under poor propensity-score overlap: marginal structural model E(Y_a) = θ + Δa; units stochastically included via S_i ~ Bernoulli(p_i) with p_i = P(A_i^rep ≠ A_i^obs | X, data) under the posterior-predictive treatment model; two-stage design with no outcome feedback into the design stage (modularization / 'cutting feedback'); the estimand is an overlap-population effect (ATO spirit), explicitly NOT guaranteed to be the full-population ATE.

PPTA simulation (500 replications, n=500, true outcome effect 0.2): PPTA and overlap weights had the least variability as overlap worsened while IPTW became unstable and biased; in the US power plants 2002-2014 application (n=1,505-2,028 yearly, treatment prevalence 15%-47%) PPTA achieved near-zero standardized differences (best balance) but wider intervals — the price of honest uncertainty.

Rodrigues et al. 2025 (ADAPT for method, REJECT for accuracy claims) built a synthetic triathlete cohort (1,000 athletes × 365 days = 365,000 daily records) with 7-14-day warning patterns injected retrospectively before each scheduled injury; the best XGBoost AUC 0.858 / AP 0.726 is explicitly treated as CIRCULAR (the model recovers the simulator's own assumptions) and must never be cited as evidence of real injury predictability.

The injury-paper ledger recommends a synthetic-sandbox-as-negative-control protocol for availability models: a synthetic cohort with known ground-truth injury mechanisms and 100+ features (3/7/14-day rolling load summaries) as a standing regression test — the GSE adoption gate is that the availability model must rank true injected-mechanism features in its top 5 by attribution on ≥80% of sandbox replications, else its real-data injury outputs are downgraded to 'experimental.'

Rosenof 2025 (ADAPT) derives a closed-form differentiable win-probability objective V = Φ(µD/σD) for Rotisserie fantasy basketball, with µD = ((|O|+1)/|O|)µT − |C|(|O|+1)/2 − µL and σD² = ((|O|+1)/|O|)²σT² + σL²; the portable insight is the tournament objective form 'maximize Φ((expected edge)/uncertainty)' and its corollary that variance is upside, mapping to NFL DFS GPPs and best-ball construction.

Core insight from the Rotisserie paper (§7.2.1): because µD is generally negative, increasing σD raises V; per-matchup variance Φ(1−Φ) is maximized at Φ=1/2, so the objective rewards balanced 50-50 exposures and penalizes punting — punting only pays when it raises EV enough to offset the variance loss; simulation showed win rates of 37.5% (χ=0.25), 17.2% (χ=0.5), 12.1% (χ=0.75) vs the 1/12 ≈ 8.3% random baseline.

Tayebati et al. 2025 (ADAPT minus the RL gimmick) propose Conformalized Abstention Policy (CAP): nonconformity s(x,y) = 1 − p_y(x); q̂_predict = quantile({s_1..s_n}, ⌈(n+1)(1−α)⌉/n); q̂_abstain = quantile({s_1..s_n}, ⌈(n+1)(1−β)⌉/n); regimes are s(x) < q̂_predict → single prediction, q̂_predict ≤ s(x) < q̂_abstain → prediction set, s(x) ≥ q̂_abstain → abstain; coverage guarantee P(Y_t ∈ C(X_t)) ≥ 1 − α.

CAP benchmark results: hallucination AUROC / selective-gen AUARC LLaVA-34B CAP 0.8000/0.9735 vs LAC 0.7388/0.9111 vs APS 0.7070/0.9287; coverage 91.94-93.92% across models (all ≥ 90% target); ECE LLaVA-34B CAP 0.0285 vs LAC 0.1109 vs APS 0.1666 (claimed 70-85% ECE reduction); the ledger recommends dropping the REINFORCE-on-(α,β) RL tuning layer and tuning (α,β) on validation instead.

Babichenko & Garber 2018 (ADAPT): the optimal aggregation of expert forecasts in a repeated setting where the aggregator never sees the experts' evidence is linear in log-odds space — r̃*(s) = Σ_j(x̃_j − μ̃) + μ̃; F̃ = Aỹ + μ̃1_n; optimal weights h* = 1_m(AᵀA)^{-1}Aᵀ; learn h by online gradient descent on the log-loss-convexified objective with an unbiased gradient estimator; regret Õ(nσ_min(A)^{-1}√T) in learnable regimes.

Impossibility result: a non-injective evidence matrix A yields strictly positive per-period regret forever (worked example: per-period regret ≈ 0.024 when optimal is 1/4 or 3/4 but both experts forecast 1/2); forecasts outside [τ, 1−τ] with τ = T^{-1/2} are handled by a 'follow the extreme expert' rule; design rule for GSE: never include redundant sub-models that see identical evidence.

Arevalo et al. 2022 (ADAPT): ensemble classification fused with Dempster–Shafer/Yager evidence theory — evidence mass per classifier m = [p_1·w_1, …, p_n·w_n, U] with U = 1 − p·w (weights from F1 + class specialization + diversity); anomaly rule: anomaly ⟺ (UQ_DS > τ_DS^max) AND (UQ_Y > τ_Y^max), i.e. fusion conflict itself is the unknown/anomaly trigger; on Tennessee Eastman hard faults the ensemble M3 reached 91.88/90.75/91.25/94.13% FDR vs best literature (AAE ~34%, MOD-PLS 72.66%).

Cost finding: EC M5 vs H5-2 had comparable avg F1 (0.62 vs 0.63) at 1.9% vs 92.9% relative inference time (~1/50th cost); poor-classifier ensembles (F1 0.20-0.30) had poor anomaly detection (0.03-0.24 F1) — poor classifiers add fusion noise; hard-multiclass ECs ~0.22-0.23 F1 underperformed individuals 0.50-0.58, showing ensembles hurt when base classifiers are poor.

Baran & Mihalina 2026 (ADAPT): sharpening neural-network parametric post-processing by adding a direct interval-width penalty to the CRPS training loss — CRPSmod(F,y) = CRPS(F,y) + α·w(F,p), headline α = 0.006, p = 50/52, where w(F,p) is the width of the central p prediction interval; on EUPPBench (ECMWF 51-member ensemble, 122 European stations, 1,870,260 samples) interval width decreased 8.2%-12.46% while empirical coverage decreased only 1.8%-2.35% in relative terms, and mean CRPS/RMSE did not deteriorate.

HIGFormer (Wang et al., KDD '25, ADAPT): per-match heterogeneous directed soccer graph (46 player nodes, 10 key-event-count features, 2 edge types {pass-related, defense-related}) + Heter. Transformer (TokenGT extension) + Heter. GCN fused by MoE gating [p^i_glo, p^i_loc] = Softmax(Gating(X_V^i)), plus a team-interaction GAT over head-to-head win-rate edges; prediction ŷ^i = σ(f_MLP(r^i − b^i)) with MSE on ordinal targets (win=1, draw=0.5, lose=0); on WyScout data (1,941 matches) total accuracy 52.19 vs DraftRec 48.33, RNN 47.30.

HIGFormer ablations: removing the Player Interaction Network drops accuracy to 48.59 avg; cross-entropy instead of ordinal MSE → 51.16; one-stage training → 47.95; player-evaluation what-if: swapping L. Messi into Real Betis raises predicted win% by +7.14, into low-ranked Celta Vigo only +1.49; attention concentrates on midfielders and defenders, least on goalkeepers; draw prediction poor (24.53%).

Weinberger 2009 (REJECT — withdrawn by the author v5, 2026-02-28, self-described as expository of well-known results): pragmatic information I(A;M) = Σ_m Σ_A Pr(A,m) log[Pr(A,m)/(Pr(m)Pr(A))]; horse-race Kelly E[log₂Σb_iX_i(n)] = D(p∥q) − D(p∥b) − log₂T optimal at b = p(n); market efficiency ⟺ i(P;μ⁻) = h(P) − h(P|μ⁻) = 0 ('tradable past'); no empirical content, nothing implementable for GSE.

Hsieh, Barmish & Gubner 2018 (ADAPT): optimal bet-update frequency for a Kelly bettor — per-period objective g_n(K) = (1/n)·E[log(1 + K·X_n)] with n-step return X_n = ∏_{k=0}^{n-1}(1 + X(k)) − 1; even-money Bernoulli closed form K_n* = (2^n·p^n − 1)/(2^n − 1), classical n=1 gives K_1* = 2p − 1; sufficient attractiveness theorem (proved): if E[1/(1 + X(0))] ≤ 1 then g_n* = g_1* for all n, i.e. re-staking frequency gives no benefit.

With transaction cost ε = 0.1 and p ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9}, the plotted optimal waiting period is n* = 2 — with costs, staking less often beats every-period staking; limitations: let-it-ride compounding doesn't match sports betting (settled stakes return to cash), ε = 0.1 is illustrative not calibrated to vig, i.i.d. returns violated by nonstationary edges.

Dinis, Unterberger & Lacoste 2020 (ADAPT): risk-sensitive betting objective J̃ = α⟨W⟩ − (1−α)σ_W with α ∈ [0,1] on the growth-rate/volatility Pareto frontier; capital C_{N+1} = o_x·b_x·C_N w.p. p_x; ⟨W⟩ = Σ_x p_x·ln(o_x·b_x); Kelly b*_x = p_x; near Kelly's point the Pareto slope is always vertical — 'if one is willing to sacrifice a small amount of the average growth rate, one can lower the fluctuations significantly'; two-horse case b± = p ± γ·σ with σ = p(1−p).

TUR-like bound: σ_W ≥ ⟨W⟩/σ_q where q_x = r_x/p_x, r_x = 1/o_x (fair odds), saturated at b_x = r_x (null strategy); the lower front between null and Kelly strategies is convex (proved) — no other phase transitions; limitations: fair-odds assumption fails under sportsbook vig and probabilities are assumed known (no estimation error).

Tepelyan & Lam (Bloomberg, Apr 2026, ADAPT): the Frullani/Laplace factorization makes multivariate Kelly tractable — Frullani identity log x = ∫₀^∞ (e^{−t} − e^{−tx})/t dt reduces the Kelly objective over N simultaneous independent binary bets from O(2^N) to O(TN), with factorized MGF Q(t) = e^{−tw₀}·Π_i[(1−p_i) + p_i·e^{−tc_i}] optimized by Newton-CG; max relative objective error 3.92×10^{-7} vs solvers; binding limitation is the independence assumption (collapses with correlated outcomes like same-game parlays).

Fitted shortfall scaling law: y ≈ (1 + Q·e^{−B·Logit(x)})^{-1/v}; misspecification study mean MSE 4.53×10^{-4}, median MAE 3.95×10^{-3}; the sigmoid law is fitted not derived, data are synthetic prediction-market prices only, and binary payoffs only.

Ricou & Mahony 2026 (ADAPT): the 'denominator gradient' gamma = slope of log(recorded minutes) on recent exposure, with denominator identity b_off = b_app - gamma; negligence threshold gamma < 0.05 (at gamma=0.05 the measured attenuation ratio is 1.20, ~4.1% of the rate ratio); changing only the offset moved the seven-day injury rate ratio from 1.27 (95% CI 1.11-1.44, fixed-90) to 1.09 (0.95-1.25, recorded minutes) — two-thirds of the excess association above the null was lost; pooled gamma = 0.303 across 88,573 appearances by 1,208 EPL players and replication cohorts of 628,487 men's + 29,799 women's appearances across 15 European leagues (all leagues above 0.05).

MacKay 2026 (ADAPT): Murphy Brier decomposition S_B = -f(1-f) + N^{-1}Σ N_μ (f - f_μ)^2 - N^{-1}Σ N_μ (q_μ - f_μ)^2 = -uncertainty + resolution - reliability; luck/skill split S_B(q) = -p(1-p) + (2q-1)(X-p) - (p-q)^2 = uncertainty + luck + skill; forecaster comparison Delta = N^{-1}Σ (q'_i - q_i)(q'_i + q_i - 2X) is approx normal with sigma^2 <= N^{-2}Σ (q'_i - q_i)^2, so sd(Delta) < delta/sqrt(N) where delta is the RMS forecast difference.

Rule of thumb: over 100 questions with typical RMS forecast difference delta ~ 0.1, a mean Brier-score gap > 0.02 is ~2 sigma (≥95% confidence of a real skill difference) against typical scores ~ -0.25; a 10%-off forecaster at p=0.5 has penalty -0.01 vs exposure sigma 0.1 (10x larger) — 100 questions needed for luck to shrink to 1 sigma, 400 for 2 sigma; 2010 World Cup winner's margin was 0.002 ('probably got lucky') and rankings are confident only within ±3-5 places.

Gabrio 2019 (ADAPT): joint three-module Bayesian hierarchical factorization — y_hi ~ Poisson(theta_hi) with log theta_hi = mu + lambda + att_{h(i)} + def_{a(i)}; log theta_ai = mu + att_{a(i)} + def_{h(i)}; d^s_i (5 sets) ~ Bernoulli(pi^s_i) with logit pi^s_i = gamma_0 + gamma_1 y_hi + gamma_2 y_ai; d^m_i (home win) ~ Bernoulli(pi^m_i) with logit pi^m_i = eta_0 + eta_1 y_hi + eta_2 y_ai + eta_3 d^s_i; joint p(y) * p(d^s|y) * p(d^m|y, d^s) — a template for NFL margin + win-probability + totals from one coherent posterior instead of separate heads.
equation: log theta_hi = mu + lambda + att_{h(i)} + def_{a(i)}

claim: The Gabrio paper's own ablation shows the scaled inverse-Wishart multilevel prior gains are negligible (rank probabilities vary 1-7% between specs), and its efficiency covariates are in-game (post-treatment), so the model cannot generate pre-match predictions as written — the ledger explicitly rejects the scaled-IW extension and any in-game covariates for pre-game prediction.

Vercellino 2026 WIRED (ADAPT): CRPS-weighted marginal expert mixture with weights w_k = exp(-ŝ_k/tau) / Σ_l exp(-ŝ_l/tau), tau = empirical SD of predicted scores (entropy-regularized reading w = argmin Σ v_k ŝ_k + tau Σ v_k log v_k), separately estimated adaptive copula dependence; sample CRPS formula CRPS(X, z) = (1/m)Σ|Xi - z| - (1/2m^2)ΣΣ|Xi - Xk|.

WIRED's honest negative result (paper's words): 'WIRED-full is not the overall winner in this benchmark. The Gaussian-copula bootstrap baseline has the best average CRPS, energy score, and variogram score' — synthetic Table 3: WIRED-full CRPS 0.00650 vs Gaussian-copula bootstrap 0.00599; equal weights beat WIRED-full on CRPS (-0.00039) and Energy (-0.00093); adaptive CRPS weighting needs regularization toward equal weights or it loses to uniform.

Dhanuka et al. 2026 AdaWeather (ADAPT): offline U-Net trained by CRPS ERM fed as expert N+1 into the online VT-MOS aggregator, with measure update d mu_{t+1}/d mu_t(p) = exp(-eta * CRPS(F_t^{(p)}, y_t)); Theorem 3 regret bound Reg_T <= ((b-a)(N-1)/2) * ln T + C vs the best static mixture in hindsight — logarithmic in T, linear in (N-1) and support length.

AdaWeather benchmark: VT-MOS+U-Net overall CRPS 0.503 < VT-MOS+MoWE 0.515 = VT-MOS 0.515 < Vovk-AA 0.537 < U-Net offline 0.541 < MoWE 0.557 < Equal Weight 0.699; gains ~28% vs equal weight, ~14% vs best individual expert, ~7% online-stage gain over offline alone; NFL caveat from the ledger: 17 discrete weekly events give far lower online-stage statistical power than weather, so GSE's offline stage must carry more weight.

Terner & Franks 2020 (REJECT — replaced by 2501.17711): a basketball-methods survey with no original experiments, reproducing textbook equations only (APM, RAPM ridge betâ = argmin (D-Xbeta)'(D-Xbeta) + lambda beta'beta, EPV, hierarchical logistic shot models, production curves) — nothing implementable beyond the cited primary sources.

Mlakar, Merse & Faganeli Pucer 2023 (ADAPT): ANET2 neural-network ensemble weather post-processing with normalizing spline flows — flow density p_temp(x;theta) = p_norm(T̃_theta(x)) * dT̃_theta(x)/dx with NLL loss L = T̃_theta(x_i)^2/2 - ln(dT̃_theta(x_i)/dx); on EUPPBench (ECMWF, 229 stations, 167,170 forecasts) ANET2 CRPS 0.923 vs ANET1 0.988 (~6.6% gain), best CRPS at 204 of 229 stations; inference cost for 167,170 forecasts: NORM 2.87 s / BERN 7.14 s / ANET2 36.08 s.

Mendes-Neves et al. 2024 (ADAPT): soccer matches modeled as language modeling — events as tokens in a 140-token ordinal vocabulary (0-100 numeric slots, 37 event-type categories, PERIOD_OVER/GAME_OVER/NaN tokens), a single MLP (3×512, ReLU) predicting the next event's full variable chain with a masked sampler restricting sampling to valid tokens (hallucination guard); K=3 variant: Type ACC 62.2% (+6.5pp over prior LEM), Type F1 0.57, X MAE 6.5 (R^2 0.81), Y MAE 11.4; admitted weakness: the model cannot capture probability shifts from events absent from context (red-card demo), the direct NFL analogue being injuries/ejections.

Bajons & Hornik (arXiv 2407.17832, ADAPT): regularized adjusted plus-minus for soccer — matches segmented into possession sequences, binomial logistic regression with four penalty structures: ridge min_β −ℓ(β) + λ‖β‖²₂, group lasso −ℓ(β) + λΣ_g w_g‖β_g‖₂ (8 groups = 4 positions × direct/indirect), exclusive lasso λΣ_g‖β_g‖₁², generalized lasso λ‖Dβ‖₁ with block-structured D; each player's rating splits into direct (on-ball) and indirect (on-field) contributions.

RAPM soccer results (Spanish La Liga 2017/18, train first 280 matches, test last 100; goal-indicator response with 1.3% positive rate): group lasso best under both validation frameworks × both criteria (Brier score, informational loss); all four penalty structures beat baseline, ELO, and PCV; ELO and PCV only slightly beat intercept-only; ridge/group/exclusive beat baseline and ELO at 5% (ordered logit) and 10% (bivariate Poisson) in paired t-tests; ridge vs group-lasso rating correlations ≥0.7 for all position groups.

LLM-SR (Shojaee et al., arXiv 2404.18400, ADAPT): LLM proposes equation PROGRAM skeletons (Python functions with placeholder params), an off-the-shelf optimizer (numpy+BFGS / torch+Adam) fits params, and an islands-model experience buffer evolves the population; fitness s = Score_T(f,D) = −MSE(ŷ, y); cluster sampling P_i = exp(s_i/τ_c)/Σ exp(s_i'/τ_c); program sampling P(f_i) ∝ exp(−l̃_i/τ_p) favoring high score + short programs.

LLM-SR results: on four custom anti-memorization benchmarks, LLM-SR (GPT-3.5 and Mixtral-8x7B) consistently outperformed all symbolic-regression baselines (gplearn, PySR, DSR, uDSR, LMX, FunSearch) ID and OOD at 2.5K vs 2M+ iterations; E. coli OOD NMSE ~0.0037 vs all baselines >1 (worse than predicting the mean); memorization control: on Feynman-120 the method solves problems in <20 iterations (recitation evidence — hence the custom benchmarks).

Brugger et al. (arXiv 2503.16953, ADAPT): MGMT ablation of neural-guided symbolic regression yields transferable design rules — supervised learning outperforms RL in nearly all module combinations (headline negative result for RL-SR); grammar-rules-as-MCTS-actions beats tokens; NPT best on the contrastive auxiliary task but simpler LSTMs win end-to-end (12M-param NPT loses to 82K-param LSTM in the real loop — auxiliary-task wins don't transfer); risk-seeking backprop (Q(s,a) ← max over children instead of mean) and AmEx-MCTS both improve over classic MCTS.

ELATE (Murray, Dervovic, Cashmore, arXiv 2508.14667, ADAPT): an LLM evolves a population of pandas-code time-series features over generations — feature sampling P(Xj) = exp(E(Xj,Y)/T)/Σ exp(E(Xk,Y)/T) with T = T0·e^{−K·nfeat/Nmax} + ε (T0=10, K=5, ε=0.1); evaluator E(Xj,Y) = (E_GC + E_MI)/2 where E_GC = |b1| from a statsmodels VAR F-test (p<0.05); TreeSHAP-interventional pruning with |corr|>0.9 dedup, recursive worst-10% removal until N=50 from Nmax=100; RMSE must improve vs the previous generation or the set reverts.

ELATE results: 4o+SHAP best in 6/7 forecasting domains on MAE and RMSE; average vs hand-built features −9.6% MAE, −8.4% RMSE (Energy RMSE 0.1145→0.0933, −18.5%); trading tied with Base (no gain — stock returns too noisy); Zero-Shot GPT-4o often worse than hand-built (ILI RMSE 0.0621 vs 0.0427) — the evolutionary loop, not the LLM alone, does the work; tsfresh blew past 128GB RAM in 6/7 domains; a cited consumer-goods survey: 10% forecast-accuracy gain ≈ 5% inventory-cost reduction + 2% revenue increase.

Rakuten Institute of Technology (arXiv 2312.00076, ADAPT for the tokenizer design): a 'large trajectory model' with a 3-stage spatial tokenizer — (1) lat/lon → Uber H3 resolution 8, (2) spatiotemporal clustering (10 minutes, one H3 hexagon) to control point density, (3) hierarchical hashes split into sub-hashes with WordPiece to a 30k vocab (example: 49 unique hashes → 15 sub-hashes); BERT pretrained with whole-hexagon pre-masking at 20% masking ratio for 40 epochs (~240h on 2× Tesla V100); validation perplexity 2327 (random init) → 5.27 (epoch 1) → 3.79 (epoch 40); pretrained beats random-init fine-tune by 33.6% average F1 across three downstream tasks.

CDSeer (Pham et al., arXiv 2410.09190, ADAPT the inspector protocol, reject the labeling machinery since NFL labels are free): a lightweight random-forest 'inspector model' runs beside the deployed model emitting pseudo-labels while a standard supervised drift detector (Page–Hinkley/DDM) monitors the disagreement-rate stream error_i = 0 if ŷ = ŷ_{insp,i} else 1; achieves supervised-grade drift detection with 0.6-0.8% labels (ROUTER: 96.76 MAcc, 71.4% precision, 100% recall at 0.6% labels vs ECHO's 48.1% labels; industrial deployment: 57.1% precision improvement with 99% fewer labels).

PETSA (Borealis AI, arXiv 2506.23424, ADAPT): parameter-efficient test-time adaptation for time-series forecasting — freeze the big forecaster, update only tiny gated low-rank input/output calibration modules (X̂^cali = X + (tanh(α⊙X)·W + b), α ∈ ℝ^V per-variable gating, W = A·B low-rank, A Xavier-init, B zero-init); PETSA loss ℒ_PETSA = ℒ_T + ℒ_pt where each = ℒ_Hub + ℒ_pw + β·ℒ_freq; Huber δ=0.5; ℒ_freq = ‖ℱ(ŷ^cali) − ℱ(Y)‖_1; 127 best-MSE wins vs TAFAS's 88 with up to 33.6× fewer parameters (window 720: 0.21MB vs 3.70MB).

Ding et al. (arXiv 2208.08135, ADAPT): three orthogonal MAML upgrades — (1) per-task init selection θ₀ = argmin loss over a stored checkpoint pool, (2) weight generator m_i = (lossk^t_i − lossk_i)/Σ_j(lossk^t_j − lossk_j) upweighting tasks with big support-vs-query loss gaps, (3) homoscedastic meta-loss ℒ(w,σ_1..n) = Σ_i (ℒ_i(w)/σ_i² + log σ_i); sine regression adapts with only 10 data points where MAML cannot; miniImageNet 5-way 1-shot 53.97±1.80% vs MAML 48.70±1.84%, 5-shot 71.62±0.43% vs 63.11±0.92%; learned per-task σ_i auto-downweights noisy outlier seasons (e.g. 2020 COVID) rather than by hand.

arXiv:2508.06312 Chain-of-Alpha (ADAPT): an LLM-driven dual-chain framework for formulaic alpha mining — a Factor Generation Chain proposes diverse seed formulas and a Factor Optimization Chain refines each seed using backtest feedback and optimization history; every factor is scored on a four-dimensional scorecard Score = Evaluate(f) = [S, C, E, D] where S (Strength) = cross-sectional RankIC vs future returns, C (Consistency) = RankICIR = mean(RankIC)/std(RankIC), E (Efficiency) = turnover rate of implied positions, D (Diversity) = min_{f_k ∈ F^e} (1 − Corr(f, f_k)); binary gate E = Check(f, S) ∈ {0,1} routes factors to a candidate pool F^e or a deprecated pool F^d.

Chain-of-Alpha results (China A-share CSI 500/CSI 1000, 2010-2025): best in 10 of 12 metrics — CSI 500 IC/RankIC/ICIR/RankICIR/AR/IR 0.0485/0.0771/0.3047/0.5013/0.1324/1.4178 vs AlphaGen 0.0460/0.0769/0.2786/0.4711/0.1150/1.2751; the AR/IR edge (the metrics that matter for real trading, per the reader) is the largest margin; reader-flagged limitations: top-100-by-RankIC from 1,000 candidates is an uncorrected multiple-testing machine (no deflated-Sharpe/White correction) and no transaction-cost modeling beyond turnover.

arXiv:2401.02710 (ADAPT): a PPO-based RL generator for formulaic alphas whose reward is combination-level pool performance (pool of 20) rather than individual alpha quality ('synergistic' = generated alphas must complement rather than duplicate, and the combination model may remove seeds during training), plus self-bootstrapping — seeding the RL pool with its own previously generated alpha set instead of the hand-curated Alpha101.

Synergistic-alpha results (CSI300 IC/RankIC, mean over 5 PPO seeds): baseline 0.045/0.058 → expanded operator space 0.069/0.073 → + Alpha101 init 0.071/0.071 → + self-generated init 0.085/0.087 (std 0.003) — near-doubling of IC; self-generated seeds beat Alpha101 seeds (the model bootstraps better priors than the human-curated set); pool-size study: gains plateau at pool size 20 with no benefit at 50/100.

TTS-GAN (arXiv:2202.02691, ADAPT): a pure-transformer GAN (no RNN anywhere) for fixed-length multivariate time-series synthesis — generator and discriminator each 3 transformer encoder blocks; losses d_loss = MSE(D(real),1) + MSE(D(G(z)),0), g_loss = MSE(D(G(z)),1), LSGAN-style with soft labels and label flipping; noise z ∈ R^100 with z_i∼U(0,1); Adam lr_G=1e−4, lr_D=3e−4, batch 32.

TTS-GAN fidelity protocol (Appendix 0.B): 7 signal features per channel (median, mean, std, variance, RMS, max, min) → feature vector f; avg_cos_sim = (1/n)Σ cos_sim(f_real, f_synth) (higher better); avg_jen_dis = Σ_i √[(D(f_i,real‖m) + D(f_i,syn‖m))/2] with m = pointwise mean (lower better); results beat Time-GAN in 7/10 comparisons (5 classes × 2 metrics) with small margins; the biggest gap is NO TSTR (train-synthetic-test-real) utility test — fidelity scores alone don't prove synthetic data helps a downstream model.

SELA (arXiv:2410.17238, ADAPT): an LLM-agent AutoML framework using Monte Carlo Tree Search over ML pipeline configurations — an insight-proposer LLM generates candidate pipeline insights, MCTS (selection → expansion → simulation → backpropagation) decides which configuration to try next, an LLM executor codes and runs it; per node x: v(x) = cumulative simulation score of node + descendants, n_visits(x) = total simulations of node + descendants.

SELA results: 65-80% win rate against each baseline across 20 tabular datasets (13 classification + 7 regression); nuance — AutoGluon has marginally higher average rank, but SELA's higher average Normalized Score means 'it performs strongly in the datasets where it excels, while its losses in other datasets are relatively minor'; limitations: AMLB datasets likely in LLM pretraining (insight proposer may recall rather than reason — unmeasured) and random 6:2:2 splits ignore temporal structure (wrong for sports).

PassAI (arXiv:2503.08945, ADAPT — 'the most directly transferable paper in this lane', mapping ~1:1 onto NFL pass-completion modeling): two-stream soccer pass success/failure classifier fusing a rendered 224×224×3 tracking image (player + ball positions, velocity vectors, ball departure→arrival dotted line, offense/defense by color, open space white, field scaled to x,y ∈ [−1,1]) with a 15-d standardized passer seasonal-stats vector; ConvNeXt-Tiny (fine-tuned) → 768-d, MLP (one 64-unit hidden layer) on stats → 64-d, concatenated → FC → softmax over {success, failure}.

PassAI results: accuracy 77.6% on 6,349 final-third passes (3,663 successful, 2,686 failed; 95 games J1 League 2023-2024, tracking at 25 Hz); confusion: successful 83.0% correct, failed 70.8%; multimodal gain +2-4% over image-only Pure-ConvNeXt; two-stage explainability — Stage 1 C_B = Σ_{i,j,k} |∂y/∂x_{ijk}| (image) vs C_S = Σ_i |∂y/∂v_i| (stats), each standardized to [0,1] across passes; Stage 2 Grad-CAM α_k^c = (1/Z)Σ_{i,j} ∂y^c/∂A^k_{ij}, L^c = ReLU(Σ_k α_k^c A^k); reader-flagged limitations: random 10-fold CV over games NOT time-ordered (player/team memorization inflates accuracy) and single-frame input discards pre-pass dynamics.

MOMENT (arXiv:2402.03885v2, ADAPT): open encoder-only time-series foundation models (40M/125M/385M params) — T5-style transformer with patching (fixed input 512, patch length 8, stride 8 → 64 tokens), reversible instance normalization (RevIN) before patching, channel-independent multivariate handling; pretraining objective L = (1/|M|)Σ_{j∈M} ‖ŷ_j − y_j‖² (MSE over masked patches only) on the public 'Time Series Pile' (long-horizon subset: 25,959,994 observations over 1,247 series; classification subset: 634,084,943 observations over 290,226 series).

MOMENT results: encoder-only masked pretraining matches supervised SOTA (TimesNet/PatchTST) on long-horizon forecasting without per-dataset architecture tuning; ablation shows removing RevIN or random masking degrades transfer and 385M beats 40M on forecasting; limitations: fixed 512-length input (17-game NFL seasons need upsampling), channel-independent — cannot learn cross-series structure (QB EPA ↔ WR usage ↔ team margin) without new attention — and point-forecast MSE/MAE evaluation with no calibrated uncertainty.

Chronos-2 (arXiv:2510.15821v1, AWS lineage, ADOPT — 'the strongest verdict in this chunk', 'the closest thing in this lane to a deployable GSE probabilistic forecaster'): pretrained foundation model with group attention across related series (a game = margin + total + player stat targets + weather/rest covariates as one group) and a direct 21-quantile multi-step head Ḹ ∈ ℝ^{H×D×|Q|} over Q = {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, …, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99}; quantile regression loss L = Σ_{q∈Q} [q·max(z−Ḹ^q,0) + (1−q)·max(Ḹ^q−z,0)]; 120M params, two-stage training (pretrain at context 2048, extend to 8192).

Chronos-2 results: fev-bench win rate 90.7% / skill 47.3 / 3.6s / 0% leakage / 0 failures — top on win rate and skill; TiRex 80.8/42.6, TimesFM-2.5 75.9/42.3 (8% leakage), Toto-1.0 66.6/40.7 (8% leakage), Moirai-2.0 61.1/39.3 (28% leakage — disqualifies its score); SOTA on all three benchmarks with covariate tasks won 'by a wide margin'; limitations: 3.6s/task heavy for real-time per-game refresh across hundreds of props, O(G²) group cost needs group-size discipline, 21 quantiles ≠ full distribution, key-number discreteness unmodeled.

arXiv:2012.04626 (ADAPT): robust planning under model uncertainty — instead of optimizing worst-case expected value (provably over-conservative), optimize worst-case regret reg(s_0,π) = V(s_0,π) − V(s_0,π*) over a finite sample set of MDP instantiations, via a regret Bellman recursion comparing each action against the optimal value function in each sample (Prop. 1; core innovation vs CEMR's myopic local-action comparison); the authors retracted the 'exact for independent uncertainties' claim post-publication (corrigendum) — the DP is a strong heuristic with empirical support, NOT an exact solver.

Minimax-regret results: medical decision-making (250 UMDPs, normalized max regret, lower better) 0.391±0.03 vs next best 0.557±0.20, CEMR-style baselines 0.84-0.91; generalization 0.574±0.12 vs 0.625-0.87; speed 3.75-4.64s typical vs MILP 66.9-103s (where MILP finished at all); limitations: quality depends on the sample set covering the true uncertainty and no learning — the uncertainty set must come from elsewhere.

arXiv:2510.09187v1 (REJECT — cricket broadcast-video classification, no NFL transfer): prior reported 93-99.2% cricket-shot-classification accuracies re-implemented at 10.6-57.7% under a unified protocol (CricShot10, 1,894 clips, single stratified 70/15/15 split, seed 27) — reported-vs-reimplemented gaps 96%→46.0% (LRCN), 99.2%→55.6% (Bhat et al.), 93%→57.7% (Sen et al.); best re-implementation (EfficientNet-B0 + bidirectional GRU + temporal attention) reached 92.25% accuracy / 92.13% F1; the ViT+GRU hybrid hit 10.56% accuracy (flagged as likely implementation failure, not architectural verdict); residue is a research-hygiene caution — re-implement published sports-ML methods under GSE's own backtest before trusting reported accuracy.

arXiv:2505.05120v1 (REJECT — unvalidated single-author MLB season-simulator hobby project, superseded by Yang & Swartz 2004): two-stage Beta-Bernoulli game-outcome model λ_s = α_s^{r_1} · β_s^{r_2} · γ_s^{r_3} with p_s ~ Beta(m·λ_s, m), X_s ~ Bernoulli(p_s) via MCMC (values not numerically reported — model not reconstructable), batting-average innovations Normal(0, 0.0015), ERA state-space x_{t+1} = x_t + w_t, y_t = x_t + v_t; 1,000 simulated seasons per team after a 20-game burn-in, with zero out-of-sample validation (no backtest, calibration, or market comparison) — a negative exemplar: the author concedes playoff probabilities were 'disproportionately extreme' (some >90%, others near 0%).

arXiv:2402.12149v2 (REJECT — tennis momentum, headline result is label leakage, never tested as an out-of-sample predictor): the fusion formula is given verbatim as F(x,y) = 0.926·SVM(x,y) + 0.964·RF(x,y) + 0.975·XGBoost(x,y), but the file flags an internal inconsistency — weighted-average coefficients stated as 0.323/0.336/0.340 just above, both used without reconciliation; XGBoost test R² = 0.999851105 (train MAPE 0.191 / test MAPE 0.168) while RF R² = −0.089, AdaBoost −0.032, NN −5.367 — a textbook label-leakage signature (label point_victor effectively in the point-outcome-derived features), not a modeling achievement.

Momentum-lane standing negative result referenced in the tennis-momentum ledger: Garrett's momentum lane already holds the harder negative result (Koopman/DMD momentum REJECTED at p=0.89, AR(1) wins) — in-sample non-randomness does not equal a predictive signal; the correct momentum test is out-of-sample, time-ordered, vs an AR(1)/Elo null.

Divos, del Bano Rollin, Bihari, Aste 2018 (ADAPT): Fundamental Theorems of Asset Pricing applied to in-play soccer betting — closed-form arbitrage-free prices from independent Poisson goal processes with underlyings S¹_t = N¹_t + λ₁(T−t), S²_t = N²_t + λ₂(T−t); pricing X_t = E^Q[X_T | F_t]; European closed form X_t = Σ_{n₁≥N¹_t} Σ_{n₂≥N²_t} Π(n₁,n₂) P(n₁−N¹_t, λ₁(T−t)) P(n₂−N²_t, λ₂(T−t)); Greeks δ₁X_t = X_t(t, N¹_t+1, N²_t) − X_t(t, N¹_t, N²_t); Kolmogorov ∂_tX_t = −λ₁δ₁X_t − λ₂δ₂X_t; ∂X_t/∂λ_i = (T−t)·δ_iX_t; hedge weights φ¹_t = δ₁X_t, φ²_t = δ₂X_t.

In-play pricing empirical results (Betfair, UEFA Euro 2012, 10 games): calibration error mean 1.57 ± 0.27 bid-ask spreads ('outside the bid-ask spread, but not significantly' for a 2-parameter model on 31 quotes/minute); implied intensities are NOT constant — clear increasing trend (drift μ = 0.55/90min, σ = 0.51/√90min), consistent with Dixon & Robinson 1998 on 4,012 matches; replication jump correlation mean 80% (std 19%; Portugal–Netherlands 89%, Germany–Italy 99%, Spain–Rep. of Ireland 98%, Italy–Croatia 47%, Sweden–England 50%); hedging errors significant when implied intensities shift abruptly (unmodeled state changes like red cards); replication uses 'Next Goal' bets as the natural hedge (delta matrix nonsingular even at large score gaps; Match Odds deltas collapse).

arXiv:2603.18071v4 (REJECT for prediction — flagged for replacement; 3.5-year production experience report on authorized YouTube→Joystream bulk content replication, zero prediction value): three production incidents — 28 duplicate on-chain objects (DynamoDB throttling → duplicate Creation batches), 10,000+ channels mass-expired in one polling cycle (OAuth mass expiration), 719 daily errors (queue pollution); central operational claims: 'Perfectly regular request intervals are a stronger bot signal than high volume with natural variance' and download concurrency 50 → 2 (25× survivability-over-throughput tradeoff); the OAuth token-lifecycle lesson (refresh tokens expire after 6 months inactivity; 'testing'-status tokens after 7 days) is a checklist item for GSE's Google/YouTube connected accounts.

On labeled attack corpora, CNN detectors for GraphQL payload attacks achieved: SQLi accuracy 0.9678, precision 0.9940, recall 0.9403, F1 0.9664; OS command injection 0.9767 / 0.9950 / 0.9659 / 0.9802; XSS random forest 0.9938 / 0.9988 / 0.9879 / 0.9933; XSS MLP 0.9948 / 0.9961 / 0.9926 / 0.9943.

Attack corpora used: SQLi ~77K malicious / 75K benign; OS command injection 7.5K / 7.5K; XSS 38K / 44K. Split sizes, collection dates, and dedup protocol are not stated in the paper; no code or dataset URLs were provided.

A symbolic-regression-discovered NFL scoring-drive formula simplified exactly to a sine of a square root with linear components for field position (b) and distance (c), with the boundary where c binds validated at goal line (1.000) and own territory (0.000).
equation: score_drive ~= sin(sqrt(max(c - b, 0))); b = 0.0446 x yardline_100 - 2.3621; c = 0.2007 x ydstogo - 1.0574; c binds iff yl > 4.5 x ytg + 29.25

claim: The pre-registered ablation verdict was DIE for the novel min-kink form: smooth c - b (AUC 0.6039) beat the discovered sin(sqrt(max(c-b,0))) (0.5818), b alone (0.5700), min(b,c) (0.5602), |c-b| (0.5473), (b+c)/2 (0.5402), c alone (0.5077), and max(b,c) (0.4726) on logistic refit (train <=2023 n=22,810, test >=2024 n=11,271, HGB reference 0.6268). The pre-registered prediction that min(b,c) beats all by >=0.02 AUC FAILED, losing to c-b by 0.0437 (~4 sigma). The linear distance-minus-field-position differential is real, cross-era-stable signal (AUC ~0.59-0.60 vs 0.5 baseline, ~95% of HGB's lift).

The NFL hash gap is 18 feet 6 inches (3.0833-yard half-width) vs NCAA 40 feet (6.6667-yard half-width); using the wrong competition template shifts every hash keypoint by 3.58 yards, a silent systematic bias, so competition must be an explicit validated input.

A conditioning trap was verified in practice: hash-band-only correspondences gave 1.31 px in-band residual while the projected grid visibly drifted off painted lines away from the hashes, so calibration requires vertically-spread landmarks (sidelines, endzone corners). No public American-football keypoint dataset exists; building 200-500 labeled broadcast frames was called the highest-leverage data investment.

Football broadcast homography QC gates (720p): >=6-8 non-collinear vertically-spread correspondences, RANSAC <=10 px, held-out reprojection <5 px, inlier ratio >=0.6, completeness target CR >90% on live-play shots; fit on >=6, withhold >=2-3 for QC. Benchmark reference (soccer, no public football benchmark): SOTA MRE 4.47 px, JaC10 92.84 (Broadcast2Pitch). The only football-specific pretrained keypoint option is Roboflow's keypoint model with verified 16/20 identity accuracy.

Hedge/exponential-gradient adaptive-delta shadow logic: on sample (p,y), if |p - 0.5| >= delta_j the pick publishes with loss = Brier (p-y)^2, else it sits out with loss = 0.25 (~UNC, coin-flip). The live selective publish filter is delta = 0.08 (default ON). The integrity condition is BS_paused ~= UNC (segmented Murphy): sit-out Brier far below UNC means the middle has skill, so do NOT raise delta.
equation: publish iff |p - 0.5| >= delta_j; loss = (p - y)^2 when published, 0.25 when sat out

claim: The adaptive-delta decision matrix: integrity warn_sitout_skill -> don't raise selective delta, fix mid-p ranking instead; recommended delta > live delta + integrity ok -> optional founder trial of a higher delta after RES re-measure; recommended delta < live delta -> live may be too aggressive, re-check published Brier; n < 40 -> keep current delta. Analysis fields include recommendedDelta (argmax of final Hedge weight), bestFixedDelta, regretVsBestFixed (<=0 good), weightOnRecommended, publishedBrier/sitOutBrier, and integrityStatus in {ok, warn_sitout_skill, insufficient_n}.

The Phase 1 OOF calibration recipe: beta tails plus isotonic middle, cross-fit selection by held-out Brier reliability-resolution decomposition (NOT ECE), the logit-pool falsifiable edge test Y ~ logit(q) + beta x logit(p) with Newton MLE where CI containing 0 means FIRE_NOTHING, and inductive Venn-Abers where the model fires only if LCB(e) > tau.
equation: Y ~ logit(q) + beta * logit(p); CI(beta) contains 0 => FIRE_NOTHING; fire iff LCB(e) > tau

Hawk-Eye accuracy arithmetic from the Geeklocker deep-dive: 6 8K cameras per stadium, 75 yards (2,700 inches) per camera / 7,680 px = ~0.35 inches per pixel theoretical floor, consistent with the NFL telling ESPN it expects 'half an inch'. The per-frame accuracy floor transfers to GSE as meters_per_pixel = field_width_covered / frame_width_px computed from the estimated homography, with a sanity anchor of 1920px -> 53.3 yards wide giving ~1.0 inch/px (0.02539 m/px).
equation: floor = 2,700 in / 7,680 px ~= 0.35 in/px; never state precision better than max(pixel floor, reprojection error)

claim: The accuracy ladder across tracking systems: MLB ball/strike calling (2020) +/-0.25 inches; Wimbledon Hawk-Eye (2020) +/-0.10 inches; FIFA semi-automated offside (2024) est. +/-1.6 inches; NFL Zebra RFID (2024, per NFL) +/-6 inches; CV in general ~0.1 inch at 300+ fps. Tech classes: GNSS ~12 inches max at 10-18 Hz; LPS (UWB/Zebra) ~4 inches max at 10-20 Hz; CV ~0.1 inch, camera-dependent, 300+ fps. Occlusion was identified as THE hard visual-tracking problem (prioritize detector recall on piles over association tuning).

Zac Yauney's Madden NFL Computer Vision Classifier is a two-stage pipeline: a fine-tuned Inception v3 (custom final layer) classifying 4 shotgun-formation variants (Gun Bunch, Gun Empty Base Flex, Gun Normal Y Off Close, Gun Trey Y-Flex) from manually labeled screenshots, reported qualitatively as 'high accuracy'; then a ResNet18 per-frame classifier aggregated by a 'voting mechanism' over the full play sequence into 4 play classes (Inside Zone, Y-Sail, Mesh Spot, Escape). Corpus anchors: Sloan 2018 CART formation classification 72.3% (coordinates, no pixels); THI thesis 74.13% run/pass with YOLOv8+OCR+XGBoost; Chung thesis found images + play-by-play text beats either alone. Consensus: formation/play classification from visual features is a solved-shape problem at ~70-85% accuracy.

The transferable vote-margin confidence signal: confidence = (winner - runnerUp) / total votes. Test fixture: 10 frames, 7 Inside Zone vs 3 Y-Sail -> voteMargin = 0.4 exactly; a phase-weighted variant flips to Y-Sail (9 vs 7); a 5/5 tie -> deterministic first-seen tie-break; empty frames -> throws /no frames/. Improvement path: phase-weighted voting (weight the development phase over pre-snap milling), then fuse with play-by-play text per Chung's finding.

Deep read of arXiv:2608.07168: a Bayesian bivariate conditional Poisson (BCP) regression modeling signed home-away goal dependence in the English Premier League, with log-linear intensities and empirical-Bayes priors fit by Stan/HMC (4 chains x 2,000, 1,000 warmup). Verdict ADAPT for the joint-modeling technique, not the soccer model.
equation: log lambda_{j,i} = beta_{0,j} + beta_{j,Att} log(Att_i + 1) + beta_{j,F} FS_{i,j}; theta ~ N(0, se-hat(theta-hat_MLE)^2)

claim: Joint ELPD-LOO: BCP away-given-home -3552.0, home-given-away -3552.1, vs independent Poisson -3565.0 (~13 points gained from modeling dependence). Conditional ELPD2 favors away-given-home (-1721.8 vs -1817.2). The dependence parameter phi (H->A) has posterior mean -0.107, 95% CI [-0.147, -0.066]: one home goal multiplies the away conditional mean by exp(-0.107) ~= 0.899. Attendance elasticity beta_{1,Att} = 0.024, CI [0.013, 0.034]; foul effects' 95% CIs both include zero. Independent Poisson fails on observed goal correlation and home-loss proportion; BCP posterior predictive checks replicate both (R-hat ~= 1.0).

Deep read of arXiv:2601.07980: a Hawkes/self-exciting process extension with latent random finite memory (hot/regular regime switching) fit to 2019 Chinese Super League corner-kick clustering. Hot-state mean duration ~= 2 minutes (e.g., home Gamma(8.76, 4.43), mean 1.98, sd 0.67; away mean 2.00, sd 0.69), stable across specs and teams; hot-state intensity ~= 2x the regular state (multiplier nu-hat); only ~10% of corner kicks form 'quick' clusters. Verdict ADAPT as a building block for NFL in-game scoring-burst modeling.

Covariate effects from the corner-kick Hawkes model: home teams have a lower corner rate when leading (X2: -0.122, SE 0.057) and after a goal (X3: -0.090, SE 0.022); away teams are higher in the 2nd half (X1: 0.090, SE 0.061), lower when leading, with a negative X4 x X2 interaction (-0.006, SE 0.002); no covariates were significant in the hot state. A simulation check of 200 replicated seasons matched observed home corners/match (5.21 observed vs 4.95-5.56 simulated), away (4.72 vs 4.36-4.94), and first-10-min home (0.98 vs 0.86-1.15).

Deep read of arXiv:2605.05487: a baseball pitch-velocity study where ML models collapse under leave-one-subject-out evaluation - cross-individual R^2 = 0.38 (best: Transformer (4,64,128)) vs within-individual R^2 = 0.91; GNN-GRU configs ranged 0.14-0.28. A pooled train/test split inflates reported accuracy massively when athletes leak across folds (50 pitchers, top 5 fastballs each, 250 pitches, 16 motion-capture cameras 200-500 Hz). Signed error revealed systematic bias: intermediate players were systematically overestimated (t(48)=2.13, p=.03, d=0.67). Verdict ADAPT for the validation discipline (LOPO/LOSOCV) and the signed-residual-as-ability method.

Transfer to GSE: bolt leave-one-player-out CV onto the prop/DFS pipeline (pooled vs LOPO MAE/R^2 on 2023-2024 nflverse; adopt as mandatory gate if degradation >= 10% relative), and adopt per-player mean signed residuals as a weekly efficiency prior if residuals are week-to-week stable (Spearman >= 0.5 across consecutive 4-week windows). Pivot leg/trunk were the most generalizable body regions (pivot-leg R^2 > 0.25 even in weight-shift initiation).

Deep read of arXiv:2502.08565: a 48-team FIFA World Cup format study whose methodological innovation (weighting stakeless matches by win expectancy) is ADAPTed to NFL dead-rubber games. Win expectancy uses the Elo formula; expected goals are modeled as a quartic polynomial of win expectancy fit by least squares on ~40,000 national-team matches.
equation: W_ij = 1 / (1 + 10^(-(E_i - E_j)/400)); S_i^W = S_i x W_ij; P_ij(k) = (lambda_ij^(f))^k exp(-lambda_ij^(f)) / k!

claim: Simulation outputs: stakeless probability for already-qualified teams is <=2.5% for any team in the imbalanced format (except 8 Tier-2 Pot 3-4 teams) vs 39-66% (16th-strongest) and 64-92% (Argentina) in the official format; average weighted stakeless S_i^W is 0.042 imbalanced vs >0.053 official; the best last-round schedule (1-4, 2-3) minimizes stakeless ratios in both formats. All results are simulation outputs under author assumptions with no empirical calibration check.

Deep read of arXiv:2303.16648: analysis of the German TOTO 13er Wette soccer lottery deriving exact coverage-sizing formulas for multi-entry contest portfolios. The key derived formula (Eq 15, valid under sum x Mx << (N - n)) gives the number of entries n needed for safety level Q of at least one ticket with >=x strikes; the 13-strike case has the closed form n = N x Q. Verdict ADAPT for the safety-level coverage math (new capability: no pick'em/parlay portfolio-sizing math exists in the corpus), not the lottery venue.
equation: Q(kx >= 1 in n) = 1 - (1 - sum x Mx / N)^n; n = N[1 - (1 - Q)^(1 / sum x Mx)]

claim: The hit-rate ladder from the paper: random 33.33% -> tipster ~43% -> better-team 50.98% -> home-win ~50.4% -> prediction markets/odds 52-57%. Portfolio sizing examples: at p=1/3 (N=1,594,323), >=10 strikes needs n=1,397 at Q=90% -> 5,580 at Q=99.99%; at p=1/2 (N=8,192), >=10 strikes needs 50 -> 198, >=12 needs 1,243 -> 3,949. Full coverage costs EUR 863,592 vs EUR 107,813 expected return - a negative edge. A sequential strategy (four 90%-safety bets) gives P(>=1 success) 99.99% with worst-case spend 4 x EUR 674 = EUR 2,696 for EUR 6,449 expected return.

Read-note on arXiv:2108.05796 (Le & Pham 2021) modeling Premier League home goals with Poisson GLM over 2000/01-2020/21. Verdict REJECT: a pooled chi-square test of FTHG vs Poisson(mean 1.52) gives p < 0.05 rejecting Poisson, but the authors subset teams until the test passes (cherry-picked compatibility); best model (HTAG + logHST + logHC + HR + AR + HomeTeam) was chosen by in-sample AIC (deviance 5622.496, AIC 17006.4877) with no out-of-sample validation. Key coefficients: logHST 0.6947 (z=31.04, strongest driver), logHC -0.2298 (z=-12.27, NEGATIVE - a multicollinearity artifact per the note), HR -0.1733 (z=-3.63), AR 0.140 (z=4.45), HTAG 0.0246 (p=0.11, n.s.).
equation: log(E[FTHG]) = beta_0 + beta_1 x HTAG + beta_2 x logHST + beta_3 x logHC + beta_4 x HR + beta_5 x AR + sum_team beta_team x 1{HomeTeam=team}

claim: 171,797 MLB games 1901-2008; 222 games with a team scoring >=20 runs; mean inter-arrival time 760.8 games, lambda-hat = 0.001314444. A single exponential was rejected: K-S = 0.1581 (exact p = 0.000026), A-D = 8.207 (critical 2.534 at 0.25%), chi-square = 44.616 vs critical 18.31 (df=10). Era rates (lambda-hat / mean IAT): Dead Ball 0.001632613 / 612.5; Lively Ball 0.002495138 / 400.8; Integration 0.001538142 / 650.1; Expansion 0.000433401 / 2,307.3; Free Agency 0.000640466 / 1,561.4; Long Ball 0.001408975 / 709.75. ANOVA by era: p < 0.0001; the era boundaries were defined ex post from baseball history, so the 'era differences' finding is partly circular.
equation: f(t; lambda) = lambda e^(-lambda t), t >= 0; E[T] = 1/lambda; Var(T) = 1/lambda^2

claim: Pawlik, Figiela & Malawski (2019) benchmarked 5,120 concurrent identical Linpack invocations on AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, and IBM Cloud Functions (2019 numbers are stale but the methodology is ADAPTed to GSE's batch pipelines). Mean GFlops (SD): AWS 256MB 2.95 (1.38), 512MB 4.62 (1.40), 1024MB 10.10 (4.27), 1536MB 14.04 (7.18), 2048MB 27.26 (8.37), 3008MB 27.05 (8.40); GCF 256MB 6.92 (6.23), 512MB 9.54 (3.03), 1024MB 16.11 (1.60), 2048MB 20.23 (2.03); IBM 256MB 7.35 (3.47), 512MB 7.15 (3.50).
