Authors conclude FaaS is viable for bursty workflow stages but hidden throttles and variance must be measured, not assumed.

Deep read of a League of Legends patch-effects study (Sapienza et al. 2017 data: 1.2M unique players, 437k matches, 62 patches versions 4.6-6.22, Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/B0GRWX). Method: causal trees greedily partition features to minimize expected HTE variance (not CART loss), min leaf 5% of samples, max depth 10, per-node treated-minus-control mean difference with t-test, Tran-Zheleva validation set. Patch 4.20 (pre-season): mean kills +0.5 per match; patch 6.9 (mid-season mage update): +0.4; remaining 60 patches far smaller. Lucian on team -> win rate +5% (patch 4.12); Jhin + Fiora -> +23% (patch 6.4). Lucian-Vayne win rates negatively correlated: r = -0.46, p = 0.0002.
equation: tau(x_i) = E[Y_i(w_{t+1}) - Y_i(w_t) | X_i = x_i] (patch = treatment, consecutive versions w_t -> w_{t+1})

claim: The counterintuitive headline: high-skill players benefit MORE from patches than weak players - patches widened the skill gap, contrary to balancing intent (skill effect-gap p-values slightly above 0.05). The first tree-based HTE/causal-forest-family method in this sweep transfers to NFL rule-change analysis (e.g., the 2024 dynamic kickoff rule): implement Tran-Zheleva causal trees on nflverse pbp 2022-2025 (treated 2024-25 vs control 2022-23, team-game kickoff-drive EPA) with DiD pre-processing (season + team fixed effects) to fix the paper's before/after confounding.

Causal 'hangover effect' study: NBA (n=9,517 back-to-back observations) - party discrete -0.557*** (SE 0.149), party continuous -0.158* (SE 0.095); all other controls insignificant (spreads already price rest/jetlag/travel/home). Log-likelihood -6586.3, AIC 13200.6. MLB (n=26,473): continuous nightlife x weekend -0.120* (SE 0.071); no-weekend 0.137 (SE 0.134, n.s.); bookmaker odds 2.682*** (0.158).
equation: logit P(cover spread) = beta_party x Party + controls (rest, jetlag via logged travel distance + east-west bearing interaction, home, lagged possession-change fatigue, time of day) [NBA]; logit P(win | moneyline-implied probability) with party continuous x weekend [MLB]

claim: The hangover mechanism is defense, not offense: points models (n=6,234) show party discrete -> +2.970*** points allowed (SE 0.835), continuous -> +1.661*** allowed (SE 0.644), while points scored -0.139 is not significant (R^2 ~= 0.09). A placebo on NBA teams with >24h rest gives 0.053 (SE 0.084) - the null is not rejected, so the effect dissipates with rest. A betting backtest (MLB, $100 flat on positive-EV spots) was positive all 7 seasons 2011-2017 (2016 ended +$11.5k) with no CIs or Sharpe reported. Weaknesses flagged: party proxies unvalidated (San Antonio misranks in appendix), NBA travel schedule unobserved, MLB continuous measure only p<0.1 at n=26k.

Extreme-wind probabilistic forecasting: twCRPS-trained EMOS vs CRPS-trained gives ~0.8% twCRPS skill gain at the 80th-percentile threshold and ~1.3% at the 90th, with maxima ~1.4% and ~2.5% across stations/models. The linear pool at lambda=0.6 retains most tail gain while controlling most body loss - the recommended operating point. The file proposes a GSE spec: twCRPS objective with thresholds at 80th/90th percentile of totals/margins, twin models pooled at lambda=0.6, acceptance gate >=1% 90th-percentile twCRPS gain with <=0.5% body degradation on 2024-2025 test.
equation: F_lambda = lambda x F_tail + (1 - lambda) x F_body, lambda = 0.6

claim: Deep-read ledger of arXiv:1904.08916v1 (Piergiovanni & Ryoo, 2019): I3D on optical flow from cropped MLB broadcast video for binary per-pitch injury classification, with unseen-pitcher/injury/handedness generalization studies and explicit dataset-bias audits. Model: I3D optical-flow stream initialized from Kinetics pre-training, fine-tuned 100 epochs, lr 0.1 decayed x10 every 25 epochs, dropout 0.5. Verdict ADAPT - directly portable to GSE mechanics-based injury-risk flags from broadcast video (QB throwing motion, WR cutting, OL stances).
equation: BCE loss L = sum_i (y_i log p_i + (1 - y_i) log(1 - p_i)); F1 = 1 / (0.5 x (1/recall + 1/precision))

claim: The injury-video paper's dataset-bias audits are the reusable trust method: a game-identity classifier on cropped optical flow scores ~chance (0.45-0.55) vs 0.86-0.98 on RGB, and a temporal-order classifier scores ~chance (0.49-0.54), as negative controls ruling out identity and ordering leakage. The file proposes a GSE spec: crop+flow pipeline for NFL QB dropbacks aligned to official injury reports, horizon sweep k in {1,2,4} weeks, ship gate unseen-QB F1 >= 0.55 with audits ~= chance.

Black-Litterman-style view fusion for correlated sources: view models were ARIMA (1-yr rolling; epistemic from 6-mo OOS error-variance minus aleatoric, floor 1e-8), CatBoost (2-yr window; aleatoric from loss, epistemic from ensemble variance), and GP (RBF+white-noise kernel; aleatoric = kernel noise, epistemic = total - aleatoric). Validation: 29-yr OOS bi-monthly rebalancing (1993-2021); Sharpe, IR, Sortino, max drawdown net of transaction costs, volatility-normalized to S&P 500 TR; paired 1-sided t-tests with Ljung-Box independence check (1 of 28 rejected at 10%), BCa bootstrap 90% CIs, Wilcoxon signed-rank.

Over 29 years, median Sharpe: PW 0.11, CU 0.16, CI 0.38, ICI 0.48 (single-view medians 0.01-0.53); global 29-yr Sharpe PW 0.10 -> ICI 0.34. PW (precision weighting) was the weakest fusion - assuming independence yields inconsistent estimates and hurts (authors' note), a direct warning that naive precision-weighting overconfidences correlated sources. The S&P 500 TR beat all view/fusion models; fusion improved relative standing but did not beat the index. Significant performance decay of view models over the 30-year period.

Synthetic-financial-data fidelity comparison (S&P 500 daily closes Jan 2000-Jun 2024, ~6,150 days; real stats mean 0.00041, std 0.0127, skew -0.45, kurtosis 7.88): fidelity (KS / Wasserstein / mean DTW) - ARIMA-GARCH 0.128/0.0047/0.243, VAE 0.095/0.0031/0.187, TimeGAN 0.062/0.0018/0.132 (best). Risk: real vol 1.27% / VaR_0.95 -2.11% / ES_0.95 -2.88% vs TimeGAN 1.30% / -2.05% / -2.79% (within ~4%), VAE 1.19% / -1.92% / -2.63% (VAE is tail-blind). Backtest train-on-synthetic -> test-on-real: real-trained Sharpe 0.89 / Sortino 1.31 / MaxDD 23.4% vs TimeGAN-trained 0.84 / 1.26 / 25.1% vs VAE-trained 0.78 / 1.14 / 27.6%.

Discrete-time portfolio optimization under a drawdown constraint with partial information: unknown drift B with prior mu_0, Bayesian filtering plus change of measure reduces the dynamic programming equation to finite-dimensional form in the Gaussian case (Kalman filter); numerics use Hybrid-Now (Bachouch et al.) deep NNs approximating the value function/control backward in time. Simulation: d=3 risky + riskless, 1-yr horizon, N=24 biweekly rebalances, 1000 trajectories; drift prior mean b_0=[0.05, 0.025, 0.12]; prior covariance diag(0.2^2, 0.15^2, 0.1^2); noise vol [0.08, 0.04, 0.22]; noise correlation [[1,-0.1,0.2],[-0.1,1,-0.25],[0.2,-0.25,1]].
equation: S_{k+1}^i = S_k^i exp(R_{k+1}^i); R_{k+1} = B + epsilon_{k+1}; X_{k+1}^alpha = X_k^alpha (1 + alpha_k' (e^{R_{k+1}} - 1_d)); X_k^alpha >= q x Z_k^alpha a.s., Z_k^alpha = max_{l<=k} X_l^alpha, q = 0.7; V_0 = sup_{alpha in A_0^q} E[U(X_N^alpha)], U = CRRA with p = 0.8

claim: Learning (Bayesian updating) vs Non-Learning (x_0=1): total performance 9.34% vs 6.40% (+2.94% value of learning); terminal-wealth sigma 11.88% vs 16.67%; average max drawdown -1.53% vs -6.54%; worst MD -11.74% vs -27.18%. Learning vs constrained equally-weighted: +5.49% return, -1.92% sigma, +182.08% Sharpe, worst MD +10.09%, Calmar +647.56%. Learning starts nearly flat for the first period (waits one step to update the prior before allocating - 'safer approach'); Learning's advantage grows with prior uncertainty scale; as q->0 Non-Learning converges to constrained Merton (both pile into Asset 3, highest drift).

Construction injury-precursor NLP extraction methods: (1) predictive regions - select receptive-field embeddings with highest norms per report, aggregate over the training set -> top n-grams per outcome level; (2) word saliency = |dCNN/da| at a - one backward pass on the prediction, NOT the loss; (3) HAN attention weights at word and sentence level. Results: incident_type mean F1 - HAN 68.98, CNN 63.33, TF-IDF+SVM 71.55, random 15.74; HAN beats CNN almost everywhere but trains ~3x slower (216.99 vs 71.47 s/epoch on incident_type) with slightly fewer params (1.63M vs 1.71M). TF-IDF+SVM beats deep learning except on bodypart - attributed to dataset size and keyword-sufficiency of the task. Leakage warning: narratives often contain the outcome ('his eye', 'access'), so headline F1s are inflated.
equation: saliency(a) = |partial CNN / partial a| at a

claim: Era renormalization of performance metrics (MLB 1871-2009 ~17,000 careers; NBA 1946-2008 ~4,000 careers; ~104,000 career-years): season-metric kernel-density PDFs across eras collapse; career PDFs fit by MLE to Gamma and Log-Series distributions (eq. 4 and 5; Gamma alpha in [0.4, 0.7]); HR Log-Series fit p = 0.996975 -> X_c ~= 331. Dickey-Fuller: HR raw stat -3.7 (p = 0.57, non-stationary) -> renormalized -31.5 (p = 0.0004, stationary); NBA points -6.4 (p = 0.3) -> -22.2 (p = 0.003). HR per-AB rose 5x from 1919 to 2001; NBA assist prowess peaked 1984, -25% by 2008. Transfers: prowess-deflator era adjustment for NFL player features, and backtest deflation so cross-era backtests aren't rewarded for era trends.
equation: P_Gamma(X|alpha,X_c) proportional to X^(-alpha) exp(-X/X_c), alpha in [0.4, 0.7]; P_LS(X|p) proportional to p^X / X

claim: Japan Racing Association study (n = 894,127): the late-movement coefficient beta_2 = -0.3386 (SE 0.0392), ~= 8.6 sigma significant - the final-odds-only 'sufficiency' null is rejected, so the price path adds information beyond final odds. Economic translation: a 10% late move implies ~14x the return association of an equivalent cross-sectional final-odds difference (at median odds 25.5). Descriptively, nearly half (~50%) of all JRA wagering volume arrives during the final five minutes before post time.

Transfer to GSE: build late-odds-path steam features (velocity/convexity) on the Pinnacle odds archive with a gate that late-move features add significant CLV explanatory power beyond final odds (p < 0.01 on the move coefficient in at least one league); otherwise the finding is parimutuel-specific. Improvement direction: steam-vs-noise decomposition separating 'informed' (persistent moves consistent with syndicate action) vs 'public steam' (correlated with media/betting splits), following informed and fading public.

PlayeRank soccer player ranking: team-outcome SVM AUC 0.89, F1 0.81, accuracy 0.82 vs majority baseline (0.50/0.48/0.62). Top weights: assists, key passes, shot accuracy; strong negative weights for red/yellow cards, especially hand/violent fouls. Role detection: k-means (k=8, Hartigan-Wong) on each player-match's center of performance, best at k=8 with silhouette 0.43, roles scout-validated; a player belongs to a role's ranking if >=40% of matches carry that role (soft/hybrid assignment via k-silhouette, delta_s=0.1 -> ~5% hybrids).

PlayeRank rating properties: mu=0.39, ~94% within mu +/- 2 sigma; excellent (r > mu+2 sigma) = 5%; only 11% of players achieve excellence at least once; excellence in <=21% (Neymar) / 9% average of performances - top players are excellent more often, not always excellent. Scout concordance: c_maj = 68%, c_una = 74% (random = 50%); rank gap >=20: c_maj=86%, c_una=91%. PlayeRank beats PSV by +16% relative / +13% absolute and Flow Centrality by +30% relative / +21% absolute. Weight stability: mean NRMSE ~6% across competitions (Euro 2016 17%, World Cup 2018 20%). The 'exclude the outcome from the features' leakage discipline is the reusable trust lesson.

Competitive-balance definition: match M between teams T1, T2 is balanced iff |r| < theta, where r = predicted final score difference and theta is a threshold hyperparameter; f(r) is the indicator of |r| < theta. The Delalleau win-prob baseline says balanced iff |Pr(A beats B) - 1/2| <= omega, with omega tuned to 0.3. Test-set F1 (mean +/- SD, 20 days): 3v3 - Linear 0.53, RndFrst 0.56, NN 0.59, Linear+ 0.60, NN+ 0.62; 6v6 - Linear 0.68, RndFrst 0.61, NN 0.68, NN+ 0.71. The industry-standard mean-skill (AvgSkill) approach scored F1 0.00 on 3v3 and no better than Dummy on 6v6; score-difference models beat win-prob models in 3 of 4 matched pairs.
equation: f(r) = 1_{|r|<theta}(r); balanced iff |Pr(A beats B) - 1/2| <= omega, omega = 0.3

claim: Caveats and economics: the dataset contains only matches between already-close-skill teams, so skill rating's apparent irrelevance is selection bias (acknowledged). Timing: Linear+ trains in 5.6 s (3v3)/3.7 s (6v6), infers in 5.0e-05 s/8.0e-05 s; NN+ trains in 470 s/160 s, infers in 2.4e-02 s/2.8e-02 s - linear inference is ~100x faster for ~3-4% relative F1 sacrifice. Significant features (all p < 0.001): avg_freq_dropout +1.128/+1.164; avg_assists_abs_diff +0.889/+0.741; avg_freq_defense +0.850/+0.918; avg_freq_wins -0.334/-0.178 (negative - more past wins predicts less balance); cnt_players +0.117/+0.142.

Tennis intransitivity study: the dominance score weights games won by surface similarity alpha, prestige beta, and time decay, with lambda=0.38 tuned; MagNet is a magnetic-Laplacian spectral GCN (q=0.25, Chebyshev K=2, L=2 layers, 64 hidden, lr 0.003, wd 1e-4, dropout 0.3, label smoothing 0.19), retrained 30 epochs every 38 snapshots.
equation: D_n^s(u,v) = sum alpha beta phi g / sum alpha beta phi; phi_k = exp(-lambda (tau_n - tau_k)), lambda = 0.38; A_uv[i,j] = log(w_ij / (1 - w_ij)); I = (1 + ||cyclic||_F) / (1 + ||transitive||_F); I* = I x sqrt(sum alpha beta phi)

claim: Test (2023-01-01 to 2025-06-08, 8,375 matches): model 65.7% accuracy / 0.215 Brier; Weighted Elo 66.4% / 0.212; Pinnacle 69.0% / 0.196 - the bookmaker is superior overall. Women's tennis is +11.5% more intransitive than men's (3.02 vs 2.71). The Brier gap vs Pinnacle narrows 68.3% from Bin 0 (+0.023) to Bin 3 (+0.007); the model beats WElo in moderate/high-intransitivity bins (Spearman rho = +0.049, p < 0.001). Tuned weights: alpha_hg=0.37 (hard-grass transfer high), clay isolated (alpha_hc=0.01); beta^1000=0.85, beta^Finals=0.94, beta^500=0.69.

In the tennis study's betting simulation (bankroll reset, threshold gamma=2.55 tuned on validation, Wunderlich-Memmert bootstrap p-value): filtered Kelly ROI +3.26% over 1,903 bets, Sharpe 0.61, p=0.005; unit +1.14% over 2,063 bets, p=0.022 (both survive Bonferroni alpha=0.025); unfiltered: -5.49% Kelly. At extreme intransitivity the strategy turns negative - bookmakers are efficient where evidence is thickest.
equation: Kelly f* = (p-hat x o - 1) / (o - 1); annualised Sharpe S = (P-bar / sigma_P) x sqrt(365.25)

claim: Soccer player pressure map (POP): possessions >5 s -> sequences of 50 PPMs (every 2 s); 3 graph-conv layers + ReLU + global mean pooling, dropout 0.5, FC head; the team-pressure output pop(t) is the GNN's probability of losing possession in [t, t+4 s].
equation: pop(t) = P_GNN(lose possession in [t, t+4 s])

claim: Possession-outcome accuracy: tracking-only 55.8% vs 2D PPM 75.2% vs 3D PPM 78.7% - the 2D representation alone adds ~20 pp, 3D body features add ~3 pp more. Two 300+-pass players, both ~80% raw passing accuracy, are separated by the metric: player 184341 (top PL attacking midfielder) handles pressure consistently while player 225796 (average CDM) collapses at pressure level 3, where raw accuracy cannot distinguish them. Midfielders face the highest, most consistent pressure; attackers have the lowest passing accuracy at all pressure levels (compact blocks).

Fully synthetic handball tournament-design study (no real match data; simulator validated at p_ij=0.5 and deterministic extremes, convergence verified at 10^6 runs): format D(8+6)/S vs D(4x7)/S - average rank of Final Four #1: 3.138 vs 3.332; #2: 4.163 vs 4.540; #3: 4.202 vs 4.602; #4: 5.710 vs 6.401. Expected quality 48.43 vs 55.17; expected competitive balance 10.59 vs 20.11 (mismatch severity nearly halved); 200 matches vs 212. Under homogeneity, D(8+6) looks unfair ex post: QF reach probability 7/16 (top group) vs 1/12 (bottom group), a 5.25x advantage.

BALAF framework for active learning with abstention feedbacks: joint Bayesian posterior over label functions h and abstention functions r; when a label is received both are updated, on abstention only r is updated. Model: Bayesian logistic regression with N(0, sigma^2) priors on H and R, MAP estimation. The posterior-mean abstention probability is the Eq. 2 expression; the average-case greedy (ALa) acquisition is the Eq. 3 Gibbs-error-like expression with abstention terms, within (1-1/e) of optimal expected utility (adaptive submodularity).
equation: r-tilde(x) = E_{r ~ p_{i-1}}[r(x)]; x* = argmax_x {1 - r-tilde(x)^2 - (1 - r-tilde(x))^2 sum_y p_{i-1}[Y=y;x]^2}

claim: Active-learning-with-abstention results: scenario 1 (unrelated abstention) - ALa/ALw consistently beat passive learning and standard active learning at abstention >=40%, and with a good r* estimate above 30%; scenario 2 (abstain on easy) - clearly better above 50% abstention, advantage fading at low abstention (learning r costs more than ignoring it); scenario 3 (abstain on hard) - better only at 20-40%, and without a good r* estimate little advantage elsewhere. Limitations noted: results were chart-read, with no numeric tables or confidence bands on 10 seeds, and the abstention model doubles modeling cost.

Video pose distillation for few-shot action recognition (Eq. 1): the student F on RGB crop x_t (128x128) plus RAFT flow phi_t (5 channels) regresses the teacher pose p_t and velocity Delta p_t = p_t - p_{t-1} through a 2-layer FC decoder D, which is discarded after training. Two variants: 2D-VPD (d=26, HRNet joints) and VI-VPD (d=64 view-invariant VIPE* embedding; d=128 on Diving48). Confidence gate: mean joint score < 0.5 (0.7 tennis) excluded; horizontal flips; 20% frames withheld for validation.
equation: min_{Student, PoseDecoder} sum_t || D(F(x_t, phi_t)) - [p_t; Delta p_t] ||_2^2

claim: Few-shot top-1: Diving48 VI-VPD beats next-best by 6.8-22.8 pp (k=8-64); FX35 by 5.0-10.5 pp; FSJump6/Tennis7 slight over teacher. Full-data top-1: FSJump6 97.4% (SOTA, +0.6 over VIPE*); Tennis7 93.3% (+1.5); FX35 94.6% (SOTA, +1.0 over GSM); Diving48 88.6% (trails GSM-no-crop 90.2 by 1.6 pp, +8.4 over MS-G3D ensemble 80.2). Ablations (16-shot): distillation alone +7.9/+19.9% (full/16-shot) Diving48, +2.7/+7.7% FX35 over teacher; motion decoder adds +1.5-3.9 pp; distilling on uncut video beats action-only segments. Cost: student training ~8 h on one Titan V; inference = ResNet-34 on 128x128 crops.

SoccerDB (270 matches from SoccerNet 2014-2017, 76 from Chinese Super League 2017-2018, FIFA World Cups 18/19/20; ResNeXt-101-FPN via COCO, SlowFast/I3D via Kinetics): MRTS mAP 72.11 vs SlowFast-32 62.70 - the object-mask stream adds +9.41 absolute points (+15% relative) on action recognition. Video detection: player 73.9-74.3, goal 70.5-71.2, ball 41.0-41.6 mAP - small fast blurry objects are the hard case. Highlight detection AP: branched multi-task 78.50 vs full fine-tune 76.99 vs naive multi-task 74.65 vs fc-only 68.72; SoccerDB-trained extractor mAP 54.30% vs Kinetics-pretrained 52.35% on temporal detection.

NBA schedule-fatigue study (OLS of game net rating on fatigue proxies): rest differential +0.35 game net rating per additional rest day; three-hour westward travel -1.740; third game in four days -1.290. But the structural model explains under 0.1% of residual variance (R^2 < 0.001) - schedule fatigue is real but tiny at game level, and most fatigue proxies showed negligible or ambiguous relationships (the paper's headline null/discipline result). The '<0.1% variance' baseline is the null prior every fatigue claim must beat.

Bayesian weighted discrete-time dynamic team ratings (footBayes R package >=2.1.0): commensurate prior theta | theta_0, phi ~ N(theta_0, 1/phi); weighted dynamic prior beta_{i,att,tau} | beta_{i,att,tau-1} ~ N(beta_{i,att,tau-1}, 1/phi_{att,tau}) separately for attack/defense; spike-and-slab hyperpriors on phi with spike N+(100, 0.1), slab N+(0, 5), p_l = 0.99; scoring rates log lambda_1 = beta_0 + home + beta_att(h) + beta_def(a). Fit: Stan MCMC 4 chains x 2000 iters, 1000 burn-in; zero-sum identifiability constraints per period; fixed evolution precision sigma ~ Cauchy+(0,5) for baselines.
equation: theta | theta_0, phi ~ N(theta_0, 1/phi); beta_{i,att,tau} | beta_{i,att,tau-1} ~ N(beta_{i,att,tau-1}, 1/phi_{att,tau}); phi_{k,tau} ~ N+(mu_s, psi_s)(1-p_l) + N+(mu_l, psi_l)p_l, p_l = 0.99; log lambda_1 = beta_0 + home + beta_att(h) + beta_def(a)

claim: The weighted dynamic was consistently best across three leagues x three scenarios. Final round: Bundesliga BP Brier 0.593, ACP 0.409; EPL Skellam Brier 0.545, DIBP ACP 0.449; La Liga DIBP Brier 0.462, ACP 0.485 (gains small but consistent, e.g., La Liga DIBP 0.499 vs 0.518/0.521 baselines). Computation 32-55% faster than baselines (EPL ZISM 32% faster than Owen, 55% faster than Egidi et al.); R-hat ~= 1.00, ESS in the thousands. Metrics: Brier = (1/M) sum sum (p_{r,m} - delta_{r,m})^2, plus ACP, RPS, pseudo-R^2.

Full-season 2018/19 FPL simulation: the multi-stream recommender scored 2,314 points, avg ~63-64 pts/gameweek, rank ~30,000 of 6.5M (top 0.5%), vs the stats-only baseline 1,994 points, ~52-54 pts/gameweek, rank ~800,000 (top 13%) - an improvement of +320 points (~+11 pts/week). Per-position precision: forwards 92% (multi) vs 88% (baseline); goalkeepers 79% vs 82% (baseline better - text adds noise for keepers). Accuracy paradox: overall accuracy 89% (multi) vs 91% (baseline) - accuracy slightly down while points strongly up. Blog-sentiment ablation: odds alone and blogs alone each significantly beat baseline; combined, 'considerably more powerful than their individual counterparts'. Limitations: single season, no cross-season validation, no probability calibration.

The k-periodic universal portfolio (k-PUP) decomposes the sequence into k subsequences and runs an independent Universal Portfolio per cycle position (Eq. 2.5), with mu = uniform or Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2); the generalized Kelly k-log-optimal portfolios maximize E sum_{i=1}^k log<b_i, X^i> with the stated Kuhn-Tucker condition (Lemma 2); Theorem 2 says the k-log-optimal k-cyclic strategy attains the highest asymptotic growth rate among all dynamic strategies in block-wise i.i.d. markets, and Corollary 2 says the k-PUP rule attains it without knowing the distribution.
equation: b_{kt+i} = integral b prod_{j=0}^{t-1} <b, x_{kj+i}> mu(b) db / integral prod_{j=0}^{t-1} <b, x_{kj+i}> mu(b) db; regret <= k(m-1)(log n + 1) (uniform mu) or <= k(m-1)/2 log n + 1 + k log 2 (Dirichlet); E prod_{i=1}^k (<b^i,X^i>/<b^{i*},X^i>)^(1/k) <= 1; S_n(b_n) = prod <b_i, x_i>; W_n = (1/n) log S_n

claim: Empirics (CRSP daily adjusted closes 1992-12-31 to 2019-12-31, 6,798 trading days, 4 NYSE/NASDAQ blue chips HON/BA/AMD/JPM, 11,437-point Riemann discretization of the simplex step 0.025): final wealth at n=6798 - best 1-CC hindsight 38.46; 1-PUP 28.05; 2-PUP 44.98 (beats best constant); 6-PUP 38.86 (marginally beats); others 31.3-37.7. Growth rates: 2-PUP 0.000560 vs best 1-CC 0.000537 vs 1-PUP 0.000490. Sharpe: 1-PUP 55.92 vs 2-PUP 54.46 (higher growth does not mean higher Sharpe). Best k-CC in hindsight explodes with k: 446.7 (k=2), 1773.7 (k=6), 3054.2 (k=10) vs 38.46 (k=1) - up to ~80x headroom. Limitations: k swept ex post (no walk-forward selection); no transaction costs; block-wise i.i.d. is a strong idealization.

Accuracy on 2,048 test matches: Bet365 odds 54.13% [51.96%, 56.28%]; Elo two-stage 52.40% [50.23%, 54.56%]; Elo with covariates two-stage 52.78% [50.61%, 54.95%] (best model); score-difference two-stage 52.59%; naive home-win 46.07%; trace-norm batch 45.89% (below naive baseline). Two-factor/rank-four two-stage ~= 51.30-51.34% (no better than Elo). Hypothesis tests: H1 two-stage > online - Elo p=7.8e-05, two-factor p=4.4e-14, rank-four p=9.8e-09, score-diff p=2.2e-16 (all highly significant); H2 new model > Elo - two-factor p~=1, rank-four p~=1 (FAILED), score-diff p=0.235 (not significant), Elo with covariates p=0.002 (significant). Mean out-of-sample log-likelihood: Bet365 -0.9669 [-0.9877, -0.9460] (best); Elo two-stage -0.9854; Elo with covariates -0.9807; Elo online -1.0003.

The paper's durable contributions: the two-stage training recipe (batch MLE init + online updates) and the gradient-residual unification (same (Y-p) term across all variants). Authors' conclusion: everything lost to Bet365; only three observable influential factors confirmed - a general 'good vs bad' skill quantifier, home advantage, and newly-promoted status. Fairness analysis (10,000 Monte Carlo season replays): only Manchester United ended with the same rank >50% of cases; the middle 50% of teams spread over 5+ ranks. Rejected variants for GSE's NFL Elo: two-factor, rank-four, trace-norm - per the paper's own evidence.

Verification log dated 2026-07-04 for the API v1 shadow-stack hardening slice on branch codex/api-v1-autonomous-polish-hardening: 34 eval contracts validated; model freeze verified at v5.1.0; secret scan across 3268 tracked files passed.

The API v1 durable adapter conformance suite runApiV1DurableAdapterConformanceSuite() verifies seeded registry/audit validation, quota incremented exactly once on allowed requests, one allow audit event per allowed request, one deny audit event per rejected request, no usage increment on rejects, quota exhaustion recorded as a denial with consumer context, and a valid hash-chained audit ledger preserved.

The mock transactional store exposes injectNextCommitFailure(reason); on an injected commit failure the staged audit is not committed, quota is not incremented, the transaction log records rolled_back, and the snapshot is unchanged. The mock is explicitly not a database transaction and does not imply production readiness.

The api-v1-durable-local-synthetic-v1 fixture run passed with operation count 5 and the mock_transactional_store conformance adapter passed with case count 5; all boundary attestations (route exposed, database touched, provider called, executable) are false and the 8-check checklist passes non-blocking, while the live-promotion-blocked check passes as a live blocker, so livePromotionAllowed=false.

The promotion-readiness matrix evaluator always keeps livePromotionAllowed=false, including in the best-case ready_for_disposable_rehearsal_review state; promotion gates require disposable-DB rehearsal with owner approval of the named disposable target, rehearsal scope, destroy-by timestamp, rollback evidence, and raw-key absence proof.

Yip et al. (arXiv:2112.13001v3) model soccer corner-kick counts with a Bayesian discrete compound Poisson (geometric-Poisson) regression: Y = sum_{i=1}^N X_i with N ~ Poisson(lambda); the negative-binomial parameterization has E[Y]=lambda and Var[Y]=lambda+lambda^2/kappa, while the geometric-Poisson has E[Y]=lambda/theta and Var[Y]=lambda(2-theta)/theta^2.

The corner-kick rate regression is log lambda_i = beta_0 + beta_1 log(TG_i) + beta_2 log(|SUP|_i+0.01) + beta_3 TCTarget_i + beta_4 log(HomeAvg3_i+0.01) + beta_5 log(AwayAvg3_i+0.01) + beta_6 log(HomeShotOnGoalAvg3_i+0.01) + beta_7 log(AwayShotOnGoalAvg3_i+0.01), where TG is market-implied expected total goals and SUP is market-implied supremacy.
Shape is regressed on market-implied supremacy: log(kappa_i)=alpha_0+alpha_1 log(|SUP_i|+0.01) for the NB model and logit(theta_i)=alpha_0+alpha_1 log(|SUP_i|+0.01) for the geometric-Poisson model.

Market-implied expected total goals (TG) and supremacy (SUP) are extracted by fitting a Maher-1982 double-Poisson model to de-vigged home-draw-away plus over/under odds using L-BFGS-B, giving a cross-market information-extraction recipe with no published NFL equivalent in the corpus.

Shin's margin-removal formula is p_i=[sqrt(z^2+4(1-z)pi_i^2/pi)-z]/[2(1-z)]; the paper's bake-off found multiplicative margin removal best for corner O/U (log score 14,187.07) and goals O/U (14,465.44), while Shin was best for home-draw-away (19,612.15), supporting per-market de-vigging instead of one default method.
Corner counts are overdispersed with variance-to-mean 1.1856 versus 1.0396 for goals (20,190 HKJC matches, 1 Aug 2016 - 10 Jun 2021, 90 leagues/cups).
By elpd_loo, geometric-Poisson (-30,856.4, best) > GP+shape (-30,856.8, se_diff 1.4) > NB+shape (-30,858.4) > NB (-30,871.4) > Poisson (-30,877.2).

Estimated coefficients: beta_1 (log TG)=0.1545 (95% CI 0.1046, 0.2069), so each expected goal raises expected corners 16.70%; beta_4 (HomeAvg3)=0.5957 (0.53, 0.6625); beta_5 (AwayAvg3)=0.6052 (0.5405, 0.6652); SUP and shot-on-goal terms were non-significant (CIs cover zero).
The geometric-Poisson theta posterior median is 0.9577 (0.9441, 0.9705): each corner induces 0.0423 additional corners, with implied variance-to-mean 1.0883.

Betting simulation ($100 per positive-EV selection, 1 Jan - 10 Jun 2021, 2,057 HKJC matches): NB+shape best with 1,137 bets, +$6,578, +5.785%, Sharpe 3.065; GP+shape +$6,256, +5.561%, Sharpe 2.922; blind bet-under 2,056 bets, -$3,530, -1.717%, Sharpe -1.267. The elpd_loo winner (GP) loses the betting sim to NB+shape: scoring-rule-optimal is not the most profitable model.
HKJC average margin is 7.61% (payout 92.38%); over-selection payout 85.71% versus under 98.24%, a structural under-bias the authors flag as uncaptured by their model.

Eghbalian & Desai (arXiv:2607.08725) train BioModule, a 4-layer transformer (hidden d=256, 8 heads, FFN 4x, dropout 0.1, window W=81 frames) that infers 17 biomechanical attribute heads from a root-centered 17-joint 3D skeleton, with multitask loss L = 1.0*L_kinematic + 0.5*L_kinetic + 0.3*L_neuromuscular; the ledger verdict is REJECT (lab motion, simulated labels, no NFL validation).

Feeding the frozen BioModule estimated poses instead of ground truth degrades coordinates MAE 0.228 to 0.583-0.658, active torque MAE 9.529 to 15.4-16.9, GRF MAE 28.900 to 37.5-39.1, and touch accuracy 67.500% to 41.8-43.7%; fine-tuning recovers coordinate MAE to 0.260-0.278 and touch to 67.5-68.6%, but the checkpoint was selected by minimum training loss with no validation set, so some recovery is likely overfit.

All BioModule biomechanical labels are OpenSim simulation outputs, not measured forces; data are 520,509 frames from 7 indoor lab subjects (Human3.6M) with no contact, cutting, sprinting, or equipment, and the bidirectional 1.62 s window makes it offline inference only.

Bhattacharjee et al. (arXiv:2309.14390v1) predict Dream11 fantasy-sports user churn from a 30-day window of 11 daily user-product interaction features with 4 binary weekly targets (churn = full week of inactivity); weekly-horizon AUCs: Transformer 0.858/0.756/0.732/0.716 vs GBT 0.646/0.773/0.703/0.694 (mean 0.7655 vs 0.704). Adapt only to GSE product/retention analytics, never the sports-prediction engine.

The churn paper's random (non-time-ordered) 0.75/0.05/0.20 train/val/test split over three years of seasonal user data causes temporal leakage that inflates all AUCs, so reported numbers are optimistic; a GSE port must use walk-forward splits and add a randomized retention experiment (heterogeneous treatment effects), since the paper optimizes prediction AUC but never tests whether acting on predictions reduces churn.

Petridis & Pelechrinis (arXiv:2601.15000v1) define Lineup-RAPM as ridge regression of per-possession scoring on lineup dummies shrunk toward informed priors: min_beta sum_i(y_i-(beta_0+sum_j beta_{j,off}x_{i,j,off}+sum_j beta_{j,def}x_{i,j,def}))^2 + lambda sum_j(beta_{j,off}-pi_{j,off})^2 + lambda sum_j(beta_{j,def}-pi_{j,def})^2, where the prior pi_{la,off} = league ppp + sum_{k=1..5} gamma_{k,off} (prior-season member RAPMs) and rookies/unseen players are imputed at RAPM=-1.
equation: min_β Σ_i(y_i−(β_0+Σ_j β_{j,off}x_{i,j,off}+Σ_j β_{j,def}x_{i,j,def}))² + λΣ_j(β_{j,off}−π_{j,off})² + λΣ_j(β_{j,def}−π_{j,def})²; π_{λa,off} = league ppp + Σ_{k=1..5} γ_{k,off}

claim: Player RAPM (Sill 2010) is the same ridge structure shrunk toward zero with tuned penalties lambda_off=4000 and lambda_def=6000 on 2022-23 NBA data.
equation: min_γ Σ_i(y_i−(γ_0+Σ_j γ_{j,off}x_{i,j,off}+Σ_j γ_{j,def}x_{i,j,def}))² + λ_offΣ_j γ²_{j,off} + λ_defΣ_j γ²_{j,def}

claim: L-RAPM beats raw lineup ratings in every week of the 2023-24 evaluation (expanding-window out-of-sample, weekly RMSE of points per possession), with the largest gains for lineups with <50 training possessions and ~5% improvement (delta_{L-RAPM}) on unseen lineups; the authors frame 1.5% improvement as ~3.4 points per game, larger than the ~2-point home edge markets price.

NBA sparsity motivates the method: teams use 600+ lineups per season with average lineup ~17 offensive + ~17 defensive possessions (std 56); the paper flags its own single-lambda-for-offense-and-defense choice as a limitation since offense stabilizes faster, which maps to using separate lambdas for early vs late down in an NFL port.

RacketVision (Dong et al., arXiv:2511.17045v3; 1,672 clips, 435,179 frames from 942 professional broadcasts) finds naive concat fusion of racket-pose embeddings with ball trajectory consistently underperforms the ball-only baseline across both backbones (LSTM, Transformer) and all three sports, while cross-attention fusion (ball trajectory as Query, racket pose as Key/Value) is best overall: the portable design note is to use cross-attention selective fusion, never naive concatenation, for event-conditioned modality fusion.

Long-horizon trajectory ADE/FDE (pixels): tennis ball-only 62.5/108.7, concat 76.8/125.0, cross-attention 55.5/94.7; multi-sport training gains mAP +19.2% on tennis (81.9 vs 68.7) and +14.6% on badminton (83.1 vs 72.5); background modeling cuts MDE by 54.0% (table tennis), 61.4% (tennis), 54.8% (badminton). The paper's own honesty: fusion gains concentrate at rare hit/turning-point frames with modest average gains.

3DPCNet (Ekanayake et al., arXiv:2509.23455v1) predicts a per-frame global rotation from a continuous 6D representation converted to SO(3) via Gram-Schmidt, producing X_hat_c = R_hat^T X + Delta, trained with pose MSE (wp=1) + geodesic rotation error arccos((tr(R_hat R_GT^T)-1)/2) (wr=1) + cycle consistency (wc=0.25) + bone/joint perceptual terms (wperc=0.15).
equation: X̂_c = R̂ᵀX + Δ; geodesic error = arccos((tr(R̂R_GTᵀ)−1)/2)

claim: On MM-Fi, 3DPCNet cuts MPJPE ~24-28% versus the geometric baseline (S2: 62.85 to 47.57/46.24; S3: 64.58 to 48.83/47.71) and rotation error from ~21 degrees to ~3.5-4.3 degrees, with cross-environment transfer holding. The non-rigid residual Delta breaks strict rigidity and can silently edit joint positions, so a GSE port must remove or penalize ||Delta|| (e.g. >3% limb-length alteration = reject).

Kim et al. (arXiv:2507.22438v1) adapt a DEKR pose estimator from sharp to motion-blurred images with supervised loss L_g = L_H + lambda_g*L_O (lambda_g=0.03) and mutual-uncertainty-masked pseudo-labeling with cross-score C(P_i)=H_c^T(p_c^i)*sum_k H_k^T(p_k^i)/K kept only if min(C,C')>=0.1; rejected for GSE because the method requires co-located event-camera hardware. Blur mAP improves from 37.5 (source-only) to 51.6, with the Stage-2 pseudo-labeling jump (+8.7 mAP) far larger than motion augmentation alone (+0.2 mAP), and the oracle still leads by 7.2 mAP.
equation: L_g = L_H + λ_g·L_O, λ_g=0.03; B̃^src(x,y)=Σ_t W_tδ_t/(Σδ_t+ε); C(P_i)=H_c^T(p_c^i)·Σ_kH_k^T(p_k^i)/K

claim: Alberico et al. (arXiv:2506.07860) build real-time ping-pong ball trajectory prediction from an egocentric event camera: IMU-gyro motion compensation x_i^mc=K[I-[omega-bar]_x(t_i-t_0)]K^{-1} x_i, binary map B(x)=1 iff rho(x)>theta_0+theta_1||omega-bar||, circularity gamma_j=P(conv(S_j))^2/(4pi*A(conv(S_j))), depth Z_hat_{m,ball}=f*W_metric/r_hat_{m,ball} (W_metric=0.02 m).
equation: x_i^mc=K[I−[ω̄]_×(t_i−t_0)]K^−1 x_i; B(x)=1 iff ρ(x)>θ_0+θ_1‖ω̄‖; γ_j=P(conv(S_j))²/(4π·A(conv(S_j))); Ẑ_m,ball=f·W_metric/r̂_m,ball

claim: The paper's ball-flight physics are p(t_i)=p(t_{i-1})+v*Delta_t, v(t_i)=v(t_{i-1})-k_d|v|v*Delta_t+g*Delta_t, derived from sum F = m g - 1/2 C_d rho A |v| v (C_d=0.4, rho=1.225, r=0.02 m, m=0.0027 kg), with Magnus extension F_m=C_m rho A r (omega x v) and inelastic bounce v_z^+=e*v_z^-; portable to football by replacing circle fitting with ellipse fitting (a football projects as an ellipse) and adding a spin/Magnus term.

Ping-pong pipeline latency is mean 2.35 ms (worst 4.5 ms) versus 66 ms perception-only for a 30 FPS camera; gaze-ROI cropping gives 10.81x event reduction (1.5 ms, 735 events vs 16.18 ms, 7,157 events) and detection rises to 92.59% (theta_1=0.8) versus 81.48% without ROI.

Impact-point RMSE at 0.2 s horizon: DCGN 0.1072+/-0.1085 m (best), Diff Eq at 200 Hz 0.1472+/-0.0938, Diff Eq at 30 Hz 0.1915+/-0.1705, oracle 0.0121+/-0.0075; 200 Hz event updates cut error by 4.8 cm (physics) / 8.4 cm (DCGN) versus frame-based; DCGN horizon analysis shows short lookaheads underperform (0.01 s: 0.2616 vs 0.30 s: 0.1177), so flight-model horizon choice must be validated, not assumed.

Szczecinski (arXiv:2608.23859) defines the adjacent-categories ordinal model P_y^h(z) = exp(alpha_y^h + delta_y z)/sum_l exp(alpha_l^h + delta_l z) with home boost P_y^h(z) = P_y(z+eta); Lemma 1: a points score s_i = sum_y xi_y k_{y;i} is sufficient for skill iff (i) the score rule is constant-sum xi_y + xi_{L-1-y} = 1 and (ii) the AC model has slopes delta_y = xi_y.
equation: P_y^h(z) = exp(α_y^h + δ_y z)/Σ_l exp(α_l^h + δ_l z); P_y^h(z) = P_y(z+η)

claim: MAP skill estimation under the AC model uses Gaussian prior precision gamma with EM marginal likelihood (Gauss-Hermite quadrature), estimating equation: sum_{j!=i}[k_{i,j} G-tilde(theta_hat_i-theta_hat_j) + d_{i,j} G-bar(theta_hat_i-theta_hat_j)] + gamma theta_hat_i = s_i.
equation: Σ_{j≠i}[k_{i,j} G̃(θ̂_i−θ̂_j) + d_{i,j} Ğ(θ̂_i−θ̂_j)] + γ θ̂_i = s_i

claim: Proposition 1: for schedule-equivalent + venue-balanced team pairs, s_i >= s_j iff theta_hat_i >= theta_hat_j; on a venue-balanced round-robin, point counting = MAP skill ranking = Elo ordering (Corollary 2: order-invariant to intercepts, eta, prior). NFL's unbalanced 17-game schedule violates the conditions, which is a principled argument for model-based NFL team ratings over standings.

Constant-sum test results: football (0-1-3) FAILS, NHL (0-1-2-2) FAILS, SHL (0-1-2-3) passes; for L=3, sufficiency forces draw = half a win (0-1-2). The uniform rule (xi_y = y) beats each league's own rule everywhere they differ: NHL own 0.907 to uniform 0.965 (fitted 0.968), SuperLega own 0.963 to uniform 0.993, EPL/Championship own 0.952-0.965 to uniform 1; fitted slopes add at most 0.01 beyond uniform.

Fitted home advantages eta_hat: Division 1 2pt-era 0.80+/-0.02, EPL 0.58+/-0.02, Championship 0.51+/-0.02, Bundesliga 1.13+/-0.03 (2pt) / 0.56+/-0.03 (3pt), NHL 0.23+/-0.02, SHL 0.42+/-0.03, SuperLega 0.64+/-0.08; free slopes NHL delta_hat_1 = 0.38+/-0.02 (~1/3), SuperLega delta_hat_1 = 0.20+/-0.02, delta_hat_2 = 0.40+/-0.02. Where schedule equivalence fails, at most 3.2% of pairs are reordered, clustering at similar scores (median 0.4 pts apart vs 7.0 overall).

Duplicate-intake entry: Martonosi et al. (2023), arXiv:2303.04963v1, on predicting elite NBA lineups with order statistics, was already deep-read as ledger 1300 with an ADAPT verdict; this entry exists only as a REJECT-duplicate marker (replaced in queue by ledger 1499, arXiv:2409.09884v1).

Lee, Merrill & Karger (arXiv:2606.18686) build ForecastBench-Sim: Freeciv simulation rollouts (4,655 binary + 2,310 continuous questions, 562 H0 binary / 165 H0 continuous report-reading checks) resolving unconditional, observational, and interventional forecasts (do-operator via savegame mutation) without waiting for real outcomes; binary scored with Brier, continuous with normalized CRPS from p10/p25/p50/p75/p90 quantile elicitation.

ForecastBench-Sim results: curated-model Brier 0.220-0.313, normalized CRPS 0.283-0.590; sim-to-real skill Spearman rho = +0.43 (p=0.018, N=30); horizon degradation Brier 0.205 at H1 to 0.264 at H7 (peak 0.287 at H5), CRPS 0.134 to 0.639 (4.8x); limitations: fixed rules/rule-based agents, question wording measurably affects elicited forecasts, only two interventions powered.

Bin Chen & Maung (arXiv:2010.10435): time-varying forecast combination y_{t+1} = omega_0(t/T) + f_t'omega_1(t/T) + epsilon_{t+1} with smooth weights in rescaled time; low-dim local-linear estimator with Epanechnikov kernel plus data reflection at the forecast boundary (reflection cuts asymptotic variance by >70%); high-dim two-stage: Lasso-penalized local linear first stage, then group SCAD (Fan-Li, a=3.7) solved by group coordinate descent.
equation: y_{t+1} = omega_0(t/T) + f_t'omega_1(t/T) + epsilon_{t+1}; h = C[log(p_T+1)/T]^{1/5}

claim: Low-dim simulation mean ASCFE at T=200/300/500: NPRf 1.06/1.06/1.03 (lowest mean and variance at every T) vs Bates-Granger 1.19/1.22/1.20 vs equal weights 1.29/1.34/1.34 (worst); high-dim (J=100): ASCFE 1.62/1.34/1.24 for T=50/100/150, exact-selection share 0.70 to 0.81; equity premium: plain NPRf 3.183 loses to equal weights 2.888, gSCAD 2.650 best overall (DM vs historical avg p=0.065), always selecting E/P, SVAR, NTIS, TBL, I/K - the honest failure showing plain local-linear combination fails when p is large vs T.

Bondi et al. (2022, arXiv:2112.06751v2) selective prediction: sp(x;theta) = h(x) if defer(x;theta) else m-hat(x), deferral rule defer(x;theta) = 1[m(x) in [theta1,theta2]], objective max Accuracy(D;theta) subject to DeferralRate(D;theta) <= r with r as the human-effort budget.
equation: sp(x;theta) = h(x) if defer(x;theta) else m-hat(x); defer(x;theta) = 1[m(x) in [theta1,theta2]]

claim: Human-subject results (198 Prolific participants, 80 deferred images each, Snapshot Serengeti): chosen deferral model r=1% (1,297 of ~150k images deferred; model accuracy 0.978 on non-deferred, 0.577 on deferred - genuine complementarity); showing deferral status only (DO) 61.9% vs neither (NM) 58.4% (p<0.001), but showing the uncertain prediction HURTS (57.8% vs 60.2%, p=0.003); on model-wrong images, prediction-shown human accuracy 41.9% (below chance) vs 50.6% in other conditions (p<0.001) - 8.7pp worse; human-model errors correlated (agreement 69.6% where model correct vs 44.9% where incorrect).

SoccerNet-Echoes (arXiv:2405.07354): multilingual ASR commentary layer over 550 SoccerNet games (1,030 halves with commentary) via Whisper large-v1/v2/v3 with 30-s language detection and per-video best-model selection by unique-word-ratio heuristic (unique/total words, highest wins as anti-hallucination measure), evaluated WER/CER/BLEU vs GOAL human-verified transcripts (40 halves/20 games).

Model selection result: Whisper v3 chosen 46.9% (483/1,030 videos), v1 30.7%, v2 22.4%; WER v1 0.443 / v2 0.458 / v3 0.551, CER 0.261/0.269/0.341, BLEU 54.50/52.59/47.97, best unique-word ratio v3 0.370 - v1 is best on clean English but v3 hallucinates least on noisy audio; WER ~0.44-0.55 is usable for event/context mining, not verbatim quoting; batch Google Translate introduces context errors (example: 'shtrafnoi' rendered 'penalty kick' vs correct 'free kick'); 70 of 1,100 halves lack commentary.

Feil & Nendel (arXiv:2607.17991) stochastic-control market making in binary prediction markets: price = conditional probability p_t = f(L_t) with logistic f, latent belief dL_t = mu dt + sigma dW_t (mu = -a*g, a = sigma^2/2 martingale cancellation); price SDE dp_t = p_t(1-p_t)*sigma-tilde(t,p_t)dW_t; volatility spec sigma(t,x) = sigma_0 + sigma_1(t/T)^eta + sigma_2/(1+x^2) (baseline + time-acceleration near settlement + uncertainty peak at p=1/2).
equation: dp_t = p_t(1-p_t)*sigma-tilde(t,p_t)dW_t; sigma(t,x) = sigma_0 + sigma_1(t/T)^eta + sigma_2/(1+x^2)

claim: Objective E[X_T + q_T*Y + Phi(p_T,q_T) - gamma*integral q_s^2 varsigma(s,p_s)^2 ds] with terminal settlement-risk penalty Phi(p,q) = -gamma_T q^2 p(1-p); optimal quotes pi^{b,*}(z) = (u^b)^{-1}(z), skew = (pi^a+pi^b)/2 - p; solver: implicit-Euler finite-difference backward HJB on (t,p,q) grid with fixed-point contraction kappa = 4*Lambda-bar/beta.

Monte Carlo (10,000 paths, p_0=1/2): optimal vs myopic baseline - mean PnL 12.39 vs 12.47 (99.4% of profit kept), std(PnL) 10.34 vs 28.11 (-63%), mean |q_T| 15.23 vs 49.37 (-69%), VaR_5% 4.20 vs 32.41 (-87%), ES_5% 9.68 vs 40.50; spreads decrease over time but widen near settlement for p near 1/2; skew at zero inventory positive for p<1/2, negative for p>1/2; no adverse selection modeled (takers are Poisson noise) - the paper's own biggest gap.

'You Are in a Drawdown' (arXiv:1707.01457): for Brownian motion with Sharpe ratio SR, exact joint distribution of ongoing-drawdown depth and duration reduces to 5%-tail scaling rules - Duration ~= 2.14 x SR^{-2} (years, 257 trading days/year) and Normalized depth ~= 1.50 x SR^{-1}; at SR=0.5 there is a 5% chance a ten-year process is still in drawdown after 7+ years; at SR=1.6 the normalized 5% depth is ~=0.95 and is very unlikely to end in under ~2 months.
equation: Duration ~= 2.14 x SR^{-2}; Normalized depth ~= 1.50 x SR^{-1}

claim: Companion-literature caveat (via ledger 1627): Gaussian tails understate real drawdowns by ~33% at the 90th percentile, so a non-Gaussian inflation factor is needed when applying these thresholds to discrete, heteroskedastic, regime-shifting betting returns; the method is a monitoring statistic (worry/no-worry), not a predictor.

Romano, Patterson & Candes (2019) conformalized quantile regression: (1) fit q-hat_{alpha/2}, q-hat_{1-alpha/2} on proper-train; (2) calibration scores E_i = max{q-hat_lo(X_i)-Y_i, Y_i-q-hat_hi(X_i)}; (3) C-hat(x) = [q-hat_lo(x) - Q_{1-alpha}(E;I_2), q-hat_hi(x) + Q_{1-alpha}(E;I_2)] with Q the (1-alpha)(1+1/|I_2|)-th empirical quantile; Theorem 1: P{Y_{n+1} in C-hat(X_{n+1})} >= 1-alpha under exchangeability (<= 1-alpha+1/(|I_2|+1) if scores distinct).
equation: E_i = max{q-hat_lo(X_i)-Y_i, Y_i-q-hat_hi(X_i)}; C-hat(x) = [q-hat_lo(x) - Q_{1-alpha}(E;I_2), q-hat_hi(x) + Q_{1-alpha}(E;I_2)]

claim: 2,200 experiments (11 datasets x 20 splits x 10 methods, alpha=0.1): CQR-RF mean length/coverage 1.41/90.33 and CQR-NN 1.40/90.05 vs Ridge 3.06/90.03 - CQR ~30-40% shorter than absolute-residual split conformal at equal coverage, while unconformalized QNN undercovers (88.51 vs nominal 90); the flagged live bug: GSE's cqr.ts clamps rank to n-1, falsely certifying 90% coverage at 83.33% - the true recipe is the unclamped (1-alpha)(n+1) rank.

Waghmare & Ziegel (2025) proper scoring rules survey: propriety S(Q,Q) <= S(P,Q) for all P,Q (strict iff equality iff P=Q); Savage representation - every regular proper score is the Bregman divergence of its entropy function; Brier S_Brier(P,y) = (p-y)^2, log S_log(P,y) = -log p(y), CRPS(P,y) = integral(F_P(x) - 1{y<=x})^2 dx; kernel scores S(P,y) = E_P[k(X,X')] - 2E_P[k(X,y)] (+const).
equation: S_Brier(P,y) = (p-y)^2; S_log(P,y) = -log p(y); CRPS(P,y) = integral(F_P(x) - 1{y<=x})^2 dx

claim: Comparative claims: the log score is sensitive to tail misspecification (one bad density evaluation dominates), CRPS is more robust and rewards the whole distribution, minimum-score estimators can beat MLE under misspecification; adopted doctrine: CRPS primary objective for margin/total distributions, Brier/log for cover probabilities, with a rejection gate rejecting min-CRPS training if it degrades log-score tail diagnostics by >10%.

Varin, Cattelan & Firth (arXiv:1210.1016) paired-comparison review: Thurstone P(i beats j) = Phi(mu_i - mu_j), Bradley-Terry P(i beats j) = exp(lambda_i)/(exp(lambda_i)+exp(lambda_j)) with identification mu_4 = 0; for dependent repeated judgments the novel pairwise (composite) likelihood sums bivariate log-likelihoods over pairs with Godambe sandwich SEs, benchmarked against full ML (Miwa-Hayter-Kuriki 6-D integration).
equation: P(i beats j) = Phi(mu_i - mu_j); P(i beats j) = exp(lambda_i)/(exp(lambda_i)+exp(lambda_j))

claim: Simulation results: pairwise-likelihood empirical coverage near-nominal vs limited-information at 95/97.5/99% (e.g. mu_1: 0.947/0.958, 0.982/0.978, 0.992/0.992); study 2 PL means (-0.22/1.03/-1.54) vs truth (-0.2/1/-1.5) with model SEs (0.19/0.33/0.36) matching simulation SDs, while LI SEs are inflated - paper verdict: pairwise likelihood a 'valid alternative' to full ML, far cheaper than 6-D integration.

Lee & Seregina (arXiv:2209.01697) RD-FGL forecast combination: Bates-Granger optimal weights w = Theta*iota_p/(iota_p'Theta*iota_p); factor structure e_t = B f_t + epsilon_t with Graphical LASSO only on idiosyncratic precision, precision recovered via Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury; regime breaks via discrete kernel K_{gamma,t} = gamma*1[t<=T_1] + 1[t>T_1] with kernel-weighted PCA and time-varying GL (alpha sparsity + beta temporal-consistency, ADMM at O(p^3)/iter).
equation: w = Theta*iota_p/(iota_p'Theta*iota_p); e_t = B f_t + epsilon_t; K_{gamma,t} = gamma*1[t<=T_1] + 1[t>T_1]

claim: ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters (1999-2023, p=45-59 forecasters): RD-FGL in the 90% Model Confidence Set for GDP and inflation (both GFC/COVID-broken) with MSFE ratios to equal weights as low as ~0.31-0.44 (60-70% MSFE reduction), ranked 1-3; for unemployment (no strong breaks) plain FGL beats RD-FGL; the 'Not Sparse' (tau=0) variant is among the worst - idiosyncratic sparsity is necessary; the equal-weights puzzle is explained: equal weights emerge under one-factor/homogeneous-idiosyncratic structure, exactly when FGL adds value by detecting deviations.

Pudaite (arXiv:1801.07104): hot hand reframed as causal dynamics - repetition heats, interruption cools, fatigue/stress damp - estimated in NBA free throws with Bayesian hierarchical models: 2nd FT +5.3pp over 1st on first trips (73.0% to 78.3%, z=24.6, N=79,771); exactly-2 trips +4.6pp (73.2% to 77.8%, z=46.56, N=382,031); 3+ trips 78.1% to 83.2% to 85.0%; 46% more 1st than 3rd misses (1,016 vs 695).

Interruption: 1st shot of 2nd trip 74.2% vs last of 1st trip 78.3% (cools), but above 1st-trip 1st shot 73.0% (+1.2pp retention, z=5.395); trip-to-trip displacement SD ~= 3.5pp for a typical 75.4% shooter with improvement continuing to ~6th-7th trip; fatigue decline over game (Mahalanobis 3.5/2.9), steeper from minute 45 through OT ('suggestive' only, confounded by substitution); the key identification move is conditioning on the act of shooting, not the outcome, distinguishing real heat from selection artifacts.

Konaka (arXiv:2109.09287) estimates pure MLB park effects with a pairwise logistic model p_{i,j,k} = 1/(1+exp(-(b_i - d_j - r_k))) (batter-team strength, pitcher-team strength, park effect), fit by steepest descent on squared error J = sum(p-x_l)^2 and evaluated by base-2 log-loss L = E(-x_l log_2 p_l - (1-x_l) log_2(1-p_l)) vs a constant-probability baseline, on 1,550,000 plate appearances 2010-2017.

Results: 2017 HR conventional Coors PF = 1.195 gives P(HR) = 1.195 x 0.03193 = 0.03816; proposed-conventional HR PF correlation 0.81; conventional PF improves log-loss for long hits (2B/3B/HR) but degrades it for singles and walks (home/road ratio misspecified there); proposed beats conventional for HR, 3B, H, ties on 2B, park effect on singles/walks negligible; context: a 400-ft sea-level HR travels ~408 ft in Atlanta and ~440 ft in Denver (1,609 m).

Li, Liu & Zhao (arXiv:2608.28598) OhmicFlow: Ohm's-law-inspired demand/impedance/flow decomposition for transit flow under extreme weather, with an ammeter (future-aware TFT-GAT spatiotemporal backbone predicting disrupted flow, quantiles 0.1/0.5/0.9) and a counterfactual 'voltmeter' - a weight-shared replica with disrupted travel time replaced by normal reference (10th percentile of historical same-hour travel time) to infer latent demand U.

OhmicFlow beats all 9 baselines on all 3 settings: MAE gains 38.6%/18.0%/17.1%, RMSE 38.2%/13.1%/16.3%, sMAPE 31.8%/22.9%/19.0% over best baseline; narrowest intervals (MPIW 13.40/12.12/12.82) with highest/near-highest coverage (PICP 93.6%/93.4%/94.8%); ablation shows the Ohmic constraint is the main driver, gains scale with disruption severity; Typhoons Nida (2016) and Saola (2023) case studies capture anticipatory demand shifts before landfall warnings; limitation: only 17 events.

FTR-18 dataset-construction paper: multilingual (EN/ES/PT) corpus of 2018 summer-window football transfer news + Twitter reactions with veracity labels resolved via official UEFA registration (veracity rule: rumour True iff the transfer to that destination is confirmed in the 2018 summer window, or the player stays for 'staying' rumours); scale: 3,045 news articles (1,517 EN/747 ES/781 PT) from 96 news organizations, 2,064K tweets, 304 transfer moves involving 175 players across 12 UCL group-stage clubs.

Qualitative observations: pervasive attribution hedging ('according to reports/sources', 'linked to', 'reports suggest'), echo effect of outlets re-reporting third-party rumours as news, question-headlines concentrated in Spanish media, cascading conditional-move narratives ('club will sell X to fund Y'); the contribution is the rumour-pipeline taxonomy (detection -> tracking -> stance -> veracity -> evidence retrieval) and the hedging-language lexicon usable as features for a rumor-confidence scorer.

Della Penna & Reid (2012): profit-driven market maker as a bandit problem - explore overround (margin) levels as bandit arms, price within each round via overround-LMSR cost functions, rewarded by worst-case-profit improvement: r_q(C; s) = min_p V_{q+s}(C,p) - min_p V_q(C,p) with V_q(C,p) = C(q) - <q,p>; regret bound O(T^{(alpha+1)/(2alpha+1)} log^{alpha/(2alpha+1)} T) against adaptive adversaries; reward axioms R0 zero-calibrated, R1 path-independent, R2 overround-compatible.
