The paper's learned sub-event temporal attention filters are parameterized by a learned center, width, and stride per filter: filter centers are placed on a strided grid across time T.
Each sub-event filter is a Gaussian in time with learned mean and width, normalized by Z_m, evaluated over N positions i in {0..N-1} and time steps t in {0..T-1}.
The paper trains with two binary-cross-entropy losses: a segmented multi-label loss summed over classes c, and a continuous per-frame loss summed over time steps t and classes c.
equation: Segmented: L(v) = Σ_c [z_c·log p(c|G(v)) + (1−z_c)·log(1−p(c|G(v)))]; Continuous: L(v) = Σ_{t,c} [z_{t,c}·log p(c|H(v_t)) + (1−z_{t,c})·log(1−p(c|H(v_t)))]

claim: Super-event filters use a Cauchy kernel with learned center x̂_n and width γ̂_n (reparameterized via tanh and exp), and per-class scores aggregate frame features v_t through learned attention weights A_{c,m}.
equation: x̂_n = (T−1)(tanh(x_n)+1)/2; γ̂_n = exp(1−2|tanh(γ_n)|); F[t,n] = 1/[Z_n·π·γ̂_n·((t−x̂_n)/γ̂_n)²]; S_c = Σ_m A_{c,m}·Σ_t F_m[t]·v_t

claim: On multi-label baseball activity recognition (Table 4, two-stream), sub-event filters achieve the best mean average precision: InceptionV3 62.6 vs LSTM 57.7, temporal convolution 56.1, temporal pyramid 55.3, max-pool 54.4, mean-pool 45.3; the same ranking holds for I3D backbones (sub-events 61.3 best).
Sub-event filters add only 36K parameters (Table 3) versus 10.5M for the LSTM and 31.5M for temporal convolution; the paper attributes the LSTM/conv deficit to overfitting and non-parallelizability.

Best pitch-speed RMSE is 3.6 mph (InceptionV3 + sub-events at 60 fps re-extraction; 8/3 fps features only captured 1-2 pitch frames and were insufficient), and best pitch-type accuracy is 36.4% (pose features + sub-events) vs 17.0% random, while an LSTM scores 18.5% versus a 25.8% baseline (overfitting).

CoArena (Kovuru & Jannu, 2026, arXiv:2609.14239v1) is a design whitepaper for blind-judged arena evaluation of computer-use/multi-agent systems whose worked numbers are all explicitly labeled illustrative or simulated (279 battles from a seed-11 Poisson-arrival simulation); the GSE ledger verdict is REJECT.

The paper's rating machinery uses a Bradley-Terry pairwise model p_ij = σ(θ_i − θ_j) with Elo conversion R_a = R_0 + (400/ln 10)θ_a ≈ R_0 + 173.72θ_a, ridge-penalized batch MLE plus a streaming per-vote SGD update that reduces to the Elo update with adaptive K(n_a) = K_min + (K_max − K_min)n_0/(n_0 + n_a) (K_max=48, K_min=12, n_0=30).
equation: R_ib ← R_ib + K_ib w_b(y_b − μ_b); K(n_a) = K_min + (K_max − K_min)n_0/(n_0 + n_a)

claim: On 99 World Cup 2026 matches (198 hydration-break events, 3,139 control anchors), mandated ~3-minute in-match hydration breaks have a main effect on sign-adjusted attack momentum whose 95% intervals all cross zero: within-match +0.26 [−2.50, +3.02] clock-aligned, −0.63 [−3.63, +2.37] play-aligned; net xG effect ≈ zero (−0.001 [−0.051,+0.049]).

The only statistically significant interaction in the hydration-break study is Break×Elo/100: +1.59 (SE 0.80) — breaks amplify the dominant side for favorites (implied +5 momentum points at a 400-Elo favorite, −4 points at a 200-Elo underdog dominant) — while Break×lead averages −0.90/goal and −2.19 to −2.23/goal holding strength fixed.

The paper's self-matched within-match case-crossover design (each break event's own match supplies control minutes, differencing out match-level characteristics mechanically, with clock-aligned and play-aligned counterfactuals plus placebo-break falsification) is a transferable quasi-experimental template for in-game causal questions such as injury timeouts, weather stops, and booth-review delays.
equation: Y_ic = α_i + g(c) + φ·half + λ·L^lev + ψ·L^slp + δ·S + β·D + γ(D×S) + ηᵀ(D×Z) + ε

claim: Pseudo-game regularization for Bradley-Terry models adds δ fractional wins AND δ fractional losses to every unordered pair (fractional balanced pseudo-games), shrinking ability differences, and is locally ridge with λ ≈ δJ/4.

Phantom-player regularization anchors each ability against a fixed zero-strength phantom player (resolving location nonidentifiability); it is locally ridge with λ ≈ ρ/4 but has LINEAR rather than quadratic tails (L1-like robustness to extreme abilities).
equation: ℓ_ρ(θ) = ℓ(θ) + ρ Σ_j [log F(θ_j) + log(1−F(θ_j))]

claim: The paper derives an expert-calibration formula for the shrinkage dial: if a single observed win (no other information) should imply future-win probability q > 1/2, then δ = (1−q)/(2q−1), e.g. q = 0.99 implies δ = 1/98 ≈ 0.0102; this disagrees sharply with the CV-selected δ = 1.2589 on 2025 MLB data (tuning philosophy must be chosen explicitly).

On 2025 MLB (30 teams, 2,430 games), 10-fold CV selected ridge λ = 0.01, pseudo-game δ = 1.2589, phantom-player ρ = 40 (≈80 effective phantom games vs a zero-strength team); the Milwaukee–Colorado log-ability spread shrinks 1.365 → 0.820 (ridge) / 0.907 (pseudo-game) / 0.887 (phantom), with implied neutral-field Milwaukee win probability 0.797 → 0.708 (phantom).

Wang, Chen & Hu (2026, arXiv:2512.04407v1) model heterogeneous populations with a Mixture of Finite Mixtures prior that simultaneously discovers the number of latent subgroups K (with posterior consistency, unlike Dirichlet-process CRP) and fits a separate sparse probit graphical model (precision matrix Ω_k = Σ_k^{−1} over latent Gaussians) per subgroup.

In simulations (K=3, n=100/cluster, p=10, 100 replicates), MFM-PGM recovers the true K in 100% of replicates with ARI 0.7383, versus PLE (Prob 0.00, ARI 0.0779), CRP ablation (Prob 0.32, ARI 0.6830), and BOSClust (Prob 0.38, ARI 0.4002) — matching the oracle that sees latent continuous data.

Applied to 536 NBA players (2017-18 season, 20 performance covariates discretized to tertiles), the model finds 3 archetypes: 411 'Established Stars' (Durant, Curry, Leonard; total graph degree 98), 112 'Role Players' (Beverley, Finney-Smith, Haslem; degree 38), and 13 'Adaptive Tactical Hubs' (LeBron, Giannis, Kyle Anderson; highest avg betweenness 17.60, degree 46).

The Elo process (fixed N and K) is a Markov chain with a unique stationary distribution π that it converges to almost surely and in Wasserstein metrics, with full unbounded support on the zero-sum subspace.
equation: X^i ← X^i + K{S^{ij} − b(X^i−X^j)}, X^j ← X^j − K{S^{ij} − b(X^i−X^j)}

claim: Steady-state Elo rating error scales as √K: E[(1/N)|X−ρ|_1] ≤ ((N−1)/N)·√(8K/ℓ_η) for X∼π and K ≤ ℓ_η/2, so halving steady-state rating error requires cutting the K-factor 4×; the √K law holds only for small K and error grows linearly away from 0.

Elo raw ratings are systematically biased (overestimate positive skill, underestimate negative skill) yet the transformed prediction is unbiased: E[b(2X)] = b(2ρ) — so when rating levels and win-probability diagnostics disagree, trust the probabilities, which is theoretically expected, not a bug.

Kernel Rank Centrality (KRC) kernel-smooths binary pairwise outcomes over time into a Markov transition matrix P̂(t) whose rows sum to 1, then reads time-varying item strengths π(t) as its stationary distribution — a spectral (optimization-free) dynamic rating estimator.

KRC has relative ℓ2 error ≤ C1√(1/(nMh))+C2h² and relative ℓ∞ error ≤ C3√(log(nM)/(nMh))+C4h² with optimal bandwidth h≍(nM)^{−1/5}, and entrywise asymptotic normality with asymptotically independent components; a new game changes only rows i and j of P̂, so ratings update exactly via two Sherman-Morrison rank-one updates (no re-optimization).

On NBA 2016-17–2018-19 forecasting, KRC(h=1) achieves 0.6382 total accuracy vs FiveThirtyEight Elo 0.6355 (feature-rich Elo wins 2 of 3 seasons; the +0.27pp edge is one bandwidth's margin with no CI), static Rank Centrality is worst every season, and bandwidth h=1.5 collapses to 0.6173 — season-length effective memory for team quality.

The nested ZIGP tournament model forecasts the stronger team's goals from both attack and defense perspectives and averages them, then models the weaker team's goals CONDITIONAL on the stronger team's realized score, factorizing the joint likelihood as P(G_A=i, G_B=j) = P(G_A=i)·P(G_B=j|G_A=i).
equation: log μ̄_{B|A} = α₀⁽³⁾+α₁⁽³⁾Elo_A+α₂⁽³⁾loc+α₃⁽³⁾G_A; P(G_A=i, G_B=j) = P(G_A=i)·P(G_B=j|G_A=i)

claim: The zero-inflated generalized Poisson pmf is P(X=0) = ω+(1−ω)e^{−μ/φ} and P(X=k) = (1−ω)·μ(μ+(φ−1)k)^{k−1}/k!·φ^{−k}·e^{−(μ+(φ−1)k)/φ} for k≥1 (reduces to Poisson at ω=0, φ=1), with E(X) = (1−ω)μ and Var(X) = (1−ω)μ(φ²+ωμ).

History weighting uses date weight w_date(m) = (1/2)^{D(m)/H} with half-life H = 3 years times FIFA importance weights (4 WC, 3 continental, 2.5 qualifier/Nations League, 1 other); Elo updates use Elo_after = Elo_before + K·G·(W−W_e) with W_e = 1/(10^{−D/400}+1) and goal-margin multiplier G = 1 (draw/1-goal win), 1.5 (2-goal win), (11+N)/8 otherwise.

Tournament backtests (Brier/RPS, ZIGP vs bivariate Poisson vs independent Poisson): EURO 2016 ZIGP clearly best (17.52/5.28 vs 23.27/5.97 vs 23.25/5.98); WC 2018 ZIGP worse (18.51/5.54 vs 18.00/5.51 vs 18.39/5.51 — blamed on Germany's stale-form lock-in after 10/10 qualifying wins); WC 2022 100k-sim forecast: Brazil 17.3%, Argentina 13.1%, Belgium 10.8% (actual winner Argentina was top-2).

A hierarchical Bayesian model of 41,033 elite shot-put competitions (653 athletes, 1996-2016) uses y_ij = f_i(t_ij) + μ_is + x_i(t)β + ε_ij with seasonal random intercepts μ_is = m + ζ_is carrying GARCH(1,1) errors to capture volatility clustering in performance across seasons.
equation: h_is = α_0 + α_1·ζ_{is−1}² + ϖ·h_{is−1}, stationarity α_1 + ϖ < 1

claim: LPML model comparison favors the fixed-age model M2 (−45,472) over the GARCH model M1 (−45,943); GARCH M1 posterior estimates: sex β1 = −0.120 [−0.175,−0.0675], age β2 = 6.22e-3 [4.20e-3,8.20e-3] (performance improves through career), environment β3 = 0.0453 [0.0269,0.0643] (outdoor better); the functional component collapses to a seasonal step function in practice, adding little beyond the GARCH seasonal intercepts.

A Bayesian Gaussian-process model of Test-cricket batting careers (40,273 innings, 1,018 players) estimates per-innings ability as a powered-exponential GP over career-innings time: log{μ_{2t}} ~ GP(λ, K) with K(tⱼ,t_k) = σ²·exp(−|j−k|^α/ℓ^α), α ∈ [1,2], layered on a hazard/eye-in scoring likelihood with multiplicative home/away (ψ^{v_t}) and innings-order (φ^{i_t}) context effects.

LOOCV MSE: GP 544.0 vs SMA(10%) 633.1, SMA(25%) 588.4, SMA(50%) 608.2, SMA(100%) 589.1 — the GP wins at all minimum-innings thresholds, and the shortest-window average SMA(10%) is worst of all ('predicting a player's ability purely on recent scores is unwise'); average log Bayes factor GP vs constant-ability is 1.4.

Cricket career regularities: batting averages ~17% higher at home than away, ~20% higher in the team's first innings than second; most players' ability is lowest early and peaks after many innings (Williamson's peak estimated after his 60th innings) — 'finding your feet' is supported; posterior length-scale ℓ and exponent α barely move from priors, so the data cannot distinguish smooth vs ragged short-term trajectories.

The HR-LR conformal portfolio-selection rule builds conformal prediction intervals [r̲(w), r̄(w)] per candidate, filters to the m candidates M_m with the smallest lower bound r̲, then selects S = argmax_{w ∈ M_m} r̄(w); the file flags a likely sign error — a lower r̲ means a WORSE worst case, so the rule as written picks the m worst worst-cases then maximizes upside among them (the corrected rule filters on the HIGHEST lower bound).

Results on 3 US + 3 Japanese assets (2009-2018) are FIGURES ONLY (cumulative-return plots; conformal AR/NN curves above Mean[1], Mean[3], AR(1-3), Uniform) with no exact values, no Sharpe ratios, no stated coverage level α, no transaction costs, and a false exchangeability assumption on financial returns.

Causal forests (grf) and model-based forests (model4you) are unified under the additive model E[Y|x,w] = m̂(x) + τ(x)(w−π̂(x)) (cf / mobcf), and with simultaneous prognostic+predictive splits as E[Y|x,w] = m̂(x) + μ̃(x) + τ(x)(w−π̂(x)) (mob(Ŵ,Ŷ)); the bivariate score is s_mob(Ŵ,Ŷ)(μ̃,τ̂) = (Y−m̂(x)−μ̃−τ̂(w−π̂(x)))·(1, w−π̂(x))ᵀ.

Across 16 simulated scenarios (Nie & Wager setups A-D), local centering of the treatment indicator with propensity scores is the dominant driver of causal-forest success: mob(Ŵ) vs uncentered mob gives MSE ratios 0.392 (0.334,0.461) in Setup A and 0.197 (0.190,0.205) in strongly-confounded Setup C (~5× reduction); outcome centering is secondary (0.988-1.061 in A, 2.258-2.615 in C); cf beats mob everywhere (e.g. Setup C ratio 0.148).
CRPS is approximated from quantiles as CRPS(F,x) = −∫(F(y) − 1{y≥x})² dy ≈ (2/M)Σᵢ QL_{pᵢ}(F⁻¹(pᵢ), x) with pinball loss QL_p(q,x) = (1{x<q} − p)(q − x).
equation: CRPS(F,x) = −∫(F(y) − 1{y≥x})² dy ≈ (2/M)Σᵢ QL_{pᵢ}(F⁻¹(pᵢ), x); QL_p(q,x) = (1{x<q} − p)(q − x)

claim: In the battery-arbitrage experiment (German day-ahead electricity, 554-day OOS test covering the COVID crash), the statistically best CRPS-learning ensemble earns LOWER trading profits than its naive equal-weight quantile-average counterpart (especially at low risk appetite), CRPS learning is ~500× slower than equal weighting, and all ensembles earn 80-96% of crystal-ball profits (13,587 EUR max; naive ex-post fixed-hours strategy 8,048 EUR).

For a single binary ±1 game, the Kelly fraction is f_K(p) = 2p−1 with growth G_K(p) = ln 2 − S(p), S(p) = −[p ln p + (1−p) ln(1−p)]; p=0.6 gives f_K = 0.2 and compounded R_K = 2.0% vs 20% naive expected return.

For M simultaneous binary games the unsaturated optimal fraction is f*(p) = (2p−1)/[M(2p−1)² + 4p(1−p)] (Eq. 10), the saturated f* = (1/M)[1 − 2p(1−p)^M/(2p−1)] (Eq. 11), and for M=2 exact f*_2 = (2p−1)/(4p²−4p+2); the outsider beats the insider when Δ < (p−1/2)(√(2M)−1), so diversification beats information over a wide range.

When win probability must be estimated from the last L outcomes, the Kelly growth penalty is G(p,L) ≈ G_K(p) − 1/(2L) (Eq. 19) with minimum memory L_min ≈ 1/[2·G_K(p)]: p=0.51 needs L ≥ 1,761 outcomes and p=0.52 needs L ≥ 438; below p ≈ 0.63 Kelly with estimated p can have NEGATIVE growth at finite memory — most small-edge wager types cannot be safely Kelly-sized without shrinkage.

The maximin-drawdown LP (maximize t subject to portfolio daily return ≥ t for every training day, weights summing to 1) needs no covariance estimation; the constrained MILP variant adds w_i ≥ 0.05·z_i and w_i ≤ 0.50·z_i via binary selection variables.

On ~400 S&P 500 stocks trained through the 2020 COVID crash with a 3-month OOS test: constrained MD returned 8.5% with max drawdown −3.3% (plain MD 9.4% / −3.3%) vs Markowitz 5.7% / −6.1% and reverse Markowitz 5.3% / −7.2%; the MILP solved 200× faster than the QPs (0.0001s vs 0.02s), and a 2.8% covariance perturbation moved constrained-MD allocations only 3.7% versus 38.1%-47.1% for the other models.

On ~10,000 MLB.com/FanGraphs scouting-report texts predicting MLB debut by age 24 (~7,000 usable, ~80% negative class), TextCNN has the best accuracy/F1 balance (69.02%/56.42%), followed by LSTM+Self-Attention (68.64%/54.65%), Bag of Embeddings (64.65%/53.78%); BCN overfit the majority class (73.52% accuracy, collapsed 43.33% F1).

The scouting-report study's critical leakage finding: without NLTK named-entity masking, prospect surnames were the top discriminative terms (e.g. 'alford' 0/47 neg/pos) and the classifier hit 100% recall from prospect names alone — names, teams, and numeric quantities must be masked before training any text model on prospect prose.

On two PredictIt political markets (4,452 unique traders), consensus was REJECTED on all four diagnostics: volume SPIKES near resolution rather than settling, no one-sided open-order accumulation, portfolio transition matrices concentrated on the diagonal, and entry-time profit distributions not statistically different at 95% (KS test).

PredictIt outcomes: <1% of traders make profits >$400 while ~5% lose >$400; day-trader mean trading profit is −$214.71 and a trivial algorithm beats day traders; belief-bound intervals (Cruz [0.41,0.50], Trump [0.26,0.38], Rubio [0.06,0.10]) mostly straddle 0.5 — 'the market did not provide any more information than what was public at the time.'

PLRank puts the Plackett-Luce (ListMLE) listwise loss inside gradient boosting: the log-likelihood over a ranked list is L = Σ_i [s_{π(i)} − log Σ_{j≥i} exp(s_{π(j)})] with the paper's exact functional gradient (Eq. 9) and a Newton leaf-value step for regression trees.

Yahoo 2010 learning-to-rank NDCG@10: PLRank 0.7902–0.7903 vs LambdaMART 0.7809 (~1-1.2 pts); industry-tuned PLRank 0.802 vs LambdaMART 0.796; on Microsoft 30K PLRank matches LambdaMART/McRank at far lower training cost (126h vs 250+h single-core); linear ListMLE is unstable unless features are numerous (~200 features needed for NDCG@1, ~100 for NDCG@10 on Yahoo).

A validated few-shot pipeline (BERTopic topic discovery + Mistral-7B stance labeling with 3-shot + translation + chain-of-thought, no training data) on 132,150 German tweets about the 2022 World Cup armband controversy: Mistral+all-three reaches 76.1 accuracy / 64.2 F1 vs zero-shot 64.9/47.3; GPT-3.5 (full stack) 59.9/39.9; GPT-4 (full stack) 80.2/70.3 (per-class AUC 0.697 against, 0.769 in favor, 0.747 neutral); gold-set IAA κ=0.68.

A three-step dominance-pruning algorithm for salary-cap lineup optimization — (1) per cost value and position keep only top-n_e scorers, (2) per points value and position keep only cheapest n_e, (3) sweep budgets upward discarding any player never in the affordable top-n_e — reduces ~10^23 theoretical XIs (684 choose 11) to ~7×10^7, verified by integer programming (PuLP) on 5 seasons of Fantasy Premier League (2016/17–2020/21).
equation: maximize Σ points_i·x_i s.t. Σ GK = 1, 3 ≤ Σ DEF ≤ 5, 3 ≤ Σ MID ≤ 5, 1 ≤ Σ FWD ≤ 3, Σ x_i = 11, Σ cost_i·x_i ≤ budget, x_i ∈ {0,1}

claim: 72% of 385 optimal FPL teams (5 seasons × 7 formations × 11 budgets) have diverse salary distributions (bin method: 11 equal bins, ≤3 empty = diverse); 11 of 12 other variables are also diverse (only red cards non-diverse); optimal-team points scale logarithmically with budget (2020/21: budget 500 → 1,182 pts, 1000 → 2,178 pts); dominant formations 3-5-2, 4-5-1, 5-4-1.

In Smart et al. (2026) agent-based model of prediction markets, steady-state price distortion is δ_S = ρΔ_S — the whale's share of market capital (ρ) times the whale's valuation bias (Δ_S = W − η_S) — and a biased whale needs ≈40% of total market capital (ρ_w ≈ 0.4) to induce meaningful price error under the baseline (100 agents, expertise 0.95).

Market error follows AR(2) dynamics δ_{t+1} = (1−α)δ_t + α(V̄_t − η_t) with stability/oscillation conditions from the AR(2) characteristic roots; with zero herding the market 'quickly adjusts to counteract the price pressure of whale bettors', while high herding temporarily sustains biased-whale deviations because herding agents propagate rather than correct the pressure.

The least-squares rating system solves each game as one linear equation r_A − r_B = b (score differential); the schedule matrix A (m×n, +1 winner/−1 loser rows) and differential vector b give r̂ = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀb, the minimizer of ‖Ar − b‖₂², plus a sum-to-zero equation fixing the constant shift; LS ratings are interpretable as expected point differentials vs an average team.

On USA Ultimate Frisbee 2014–2019 (e.g. 2019 Mixed: 339 teams, 2,209 games), plain least squares has strictly better retrodictive MSE and MAD than USAU's custom sine-based iterative system in every season and division (MAD consistently ~0.25 points closer to the true differential per game), though ranking-violation rates are comparable and the evaluation is retrodictive (fit and scored on the same games), not walk-forward.

Probabilistic forecast combination via a linear CDF opinion pool F(x) = Σᵢ wᵢ Fᵢ(x), wᵢ ≥ 0, Σᵢ wᵢ = 1, with weights optimized jointly on a proper probabilistic score (DRPS) and a downstream operational (newsvendor inventory) cost using NSGA-III; the Pareto-knee solution strictly dominates single-objective weights on the opposing objective while staying near-optimal on the fitted one (M5: 28,903 daily series, 60.1% zeros; RAF: 5,000 monthly series).
equation: F(x) = Σᵢ wᵢ Fᵢ(x), wᵢ ≥ 0, Σᵢ wᵢ = 1

claim: Gupta (2017) forecasts weekly FPL points per player with ARIMA and LSTM models blended 40% ARIMA / 60% LSTM, then assembles a roster via a budget-constrained binary LP (£100m budget, 2 GK / 5 DEF / 5 MID / 3 FWD); per-player blend RMSEs: Vardy 2.539 (60/40 blend), Sagna 2.013 (30/70) — the table contradicts the single 'common' 40/60 blend — and the claimed 3,718-point dream-team season overforecast by 87 points, implying overfit/leakage.

The 'Generation of Threat' model attributes football threat-creation to players via 12-dimensional Hawkes processes on ball-touch event streams: λᵢ(t) = μᵢ + ΣⱼΣ_{tₖʲ<t} αᵢⱼ exp(−β(t−tₖʲ)), with branching matrix Γᵢⱼ = αᵢⱼ/β and stability requiring spectral radius ρ(Γ) < 1; four GoT indices: GoTᵈⁱʳᵢ = Γ_{threat,i}, GoTⁱⁿᵈᵢ = [(I−Γ)⁻¹]_{threat,i}, and two per-90 variants including an ablation index E[threats] − E[threats | row/col i of (K, μ) zeroed].
equation: λᵢ(t) = μᵢ + ΣⱼΣ_{tₖʲ<t} αᵢⱼ exp(−β(t−tₖʲ)); Γᵢⱼ = αᵢⱼ/β

claim: Simulations show ~600 min suffices for Hawkes structure learning (0.4% false-positive link rate, 0.0063 FN error, 18.6% relative Γ error; 1,200 min → 0.0% FP); Chelsea 2016-17 GoT₉₀: Hazard 14.2 (2.02), Kanté 6.2 indirect (1.40) ranked 4th (box-to-box danger role recovered), Moses 5.7, Pedro 5.5; Ligue 1 2021-22 surprises include right-back Frédéric Guilbert 8.42 (18th).

Pangu-Weather (3D Earth-Specific Transformer, ~256M params) attention is Attention(Q,K,V) = SoftMax(QKᵀ/√D + B_ESP)V with Earth-specific positional bias B_ESP keyed on absolute (height, latitude); it beat operational IFS on all variables at 1h–7d (Z500 5-day RMSE 296.7 vs IFS 333.7 vs FourCastNet 462.5 m²/s²; T2M 5-day 1.53 vs 1.75 K), with >10,000× faster inference (1,400ms on one Tesla-V100 for a 24h forecast).

Two transferable ideas from Pangu-Weather: (1) hierarchical temporal aggregation — train direct multi-lead-time models (1h/3h/6h/24h) and greedily compose them to minimize iteration count (7× chaining of 24h models recovered >30% RMSE vs FourCastNet's 28× chaining of 6h); (2) the RQE tail metric RQE = Σ_d (Q̂_d − Q_d)/Q_d over D=50 log-spaced percentiles 90%→99.99% (RQE<0 = underestimates extremes) — all methods increasingly underestimate extremes with lead time.

LightGBM fed with surrounding-grid context (11×11 surface + 7×7 pressure grids → 5,702 features) plus FS0 correlation pruning (pairwise |Pearson| > 0.9 drop) beats raw JMA MSM and operational MSMG guidance on test: precipitation RMSE 2.344 vs 2.759 (MSM) / 2.726 (MSMG); temperature 1.335 vs 1.811/1.394; wind 1.052 vs 1.999/1.237; fancier feature selection (FS1 target correlation, FS2 mutual info, FS3 LightGBM importance) adds nothing beyond FS0.

A weighted-Tweedie precipitation head (Var(Y)=φμ^p, monotone piecewise-linear weights on observed precip with knots 0/5/10/15/20 mm, clipped ≤10) raises the Threat Score at 10 mm 0.1966 → 0.2520 and at 15 mm 0.1251 → 0.1883, with Bias at 10 mm improving 0.4340 → 0.9771; event metrics are TS(τ)=H/(H+M+F), POD=H/(H+M), FAR=F/(H+F).

On ~941,000 sports text-commentary sentences (9,074 football games since 2011) classified into 12 event categories: tf-idf SVM reaches 97.30% accuracy / 88.64% precision / 83.60% recall / F1 0.85 vs Minard et al. (2016) baseline F1 0.71; fine-tuned BERT reaches 99.8% on held-out commentaries (92% on structurally different sources); but the shuffled 80/20 split leaks same-game sentences across train/test and formulaic templates inflate scores.

Sentiment per event (non-neutral predominant %): Yellow card Negative 74.01%, Red card Negative 70%, Foul Negative 18.77%, Penalty conceded Negative 100% — but most sentences are Neutral, so the author concludes sentiment adds very limited information beyond event labels.
The Hallucination–Omission Index HOI = Over-Count% − Under-Count% is a directional diagnostic (positive = systematic over-counting) for narrative→stat-table extraction.

Decomposition strategies for converting long game narratives into full stat tables (SporTabSet) beat zero-shot CoT by: Divide & Generate (n=8) +14.9 pp accuracy / −37.8% RMSE; EntityCoT +15.1 pp / −49.5% RMSE; Text–Tuple–Table (LLM emits atomic (Entity, Attribute, Value) tuples, rule-based compiler aggregates) +20.6 pp / −62.8% RMSE (best); Gemini 2.5 Flash T3: cricket batsman 94% / 0.96 RMSE, bowler 89% / 0.59, basketball 75% / 0.97.

Two stress tests show much apparent 'reasoning' is extractive cue-matching: masking dismissal summaries collapses scores (GPT-4.1 89% → 61%, Gemini 86% → 49%), and entity anonymization devastates basketball tables (Gemini 62% → 35%, −27 pp; GPT-4.1 47% → 29%); T3 has the worst tail behavior without safeguards (degenerate repetition, cumulative hallucination).

Prediction markets formulated as Bayesian inverse problems yield: the KL-projection gap K_T(y*→y) = inf_θ (1/T) D_KL(P_{y*,θ*}^{(T)} || P_{y,θ}^{(T)}) with outcome identifiable iff δ_T(y*,θ*) > 0; realized information gain IG(H_t) = KL(posterior || prior) saturating at the log 2 ≈ 0.693 nats ceiling for symmetric priors; and posterior consistency with exponential concentration in T·δ_T.
equation: K_T(y*→y) = inf_θ (1/T) D_KL(P_{y*,θ*}^{(T)} || P_{y,θ}^{(T)}); IG(H_t) = KL(posterior || prior)

claim: Synthetic experiments: estimated gap δ̂_T ≈ 1.5×10⁻² nats/period (weak per-step signal); identification accuracy deteriorates markedly as informed-trader weight ω₁ falls below ≈ 0.15 (type-composition-confounding regime); posterior-odds stability scales linearly in perturbation σ — a principled 'is this odds move actually informative?' diagnostic.

Under probability-estimation error (δ_perc = δ + ξ, ξ~N(0,σ²), staking a = max(0, 2δ_perc) at even odds), realized Kelly growth is 2(δ_true² − ξ²) if ξ > −δ_true else 0, and expected growth is E[growth] = 2(δ²−σ²)Φ(δ/σ) + 2σδφ(δ/σ); the (δ²−σ²) term dominates — expected growth is positive only when the true edge exceeds the estimation-error std (|δ| ≳ σ), and error enters quadratically and negatively.

Aldous & Bruss's actionable rule: even-odds small-edge Kelly growth is growth = 2aδ − a²/2 (optimum a = 2δ, optimal growth 2δ²); staking full perceived-edge Kelly when σ ≥ δ destroys growth via the quadratic error penalty, and Φ(δ_perc/σ) is the probability the perceived edge has the right sign — the δ/σ gate is the actionable edge (must be re-derived for general sports odds).

Strategic-Continuation Optimization (SCO) prices tournament decisions by backward-induction continuation values V(s,a) = Σ_{s'} P(s'|s,a)·C(s') (C(s') = expected prize equity from state s' under optimal subsequent play) instead of ICM equity E_i = Σ_k P_i(finish k)·prize_k; SCO earns $214.33 more prize equity per hand in a three-player jam/fold tournament ($1M pool), is favored in 2,433 of 2,838 matched decision units (85.7%), and ICM's mean absolute value error vs SCO is $9,036 per state–seat.

ICM's diagnosed flaws: it reads only stack sizes and omits action order, blind obligations, seat rotation, and the elimination pressure of the big stack on short stacks; SCO shifts jam frequency by 14.08% on average (32.42% at the button) versus ICM-priced ranges, robust across solver, LLM, and threshold-player opponents.

SCoRE (Selective Conformal Risk control with E-values, Bai et al., 2026) controls general bounded continuous risk (not just 0/1 error) with finite-sample distribution-free guarantees; the core condition is that the screening statistic must be a nonnegative e-value with E[L·E] ≤ 1 (L = bounded loss), plus a weighted extension for covariate shift via the deployment/calibration density ratio.

SCoRE controls selective risk tightly at nominal risk levels 0.05–0.5 across simulations (n=1000 calibration, m=100 test, 100 runs) and messy real data (four drug-discovery tasks, MIMIC-IV ICU length-of-stay, MIMIC-CXR report selection); Hoeffding and Rademacher baselines are valid but dramatically less powerful (select far fewer points at strict levels); code at github.com/Tian-Bai/SCoRE.

Underdispersed handball scores are best modeled on the score DIFFERENCE with the Skellam pmf P(Z=z|θ1,θ2) = e^{−(θ1+θ2)}(θ1/θ2)^{z/2} I_{|z|}(2√(θ1θ2)), z ∈ ℤ, with E(Z)=θ1−θ2, Var(Z)=θ1+θ2; theory result: the difference of two underdispersed variables is still Skellam, justifying its use for underdispersed counts.

The Skellam2 reparameterization uses μ=θ1−θ2, σ²=θ1+θ2 with covariates entering the mean linearly μ_jk = α + β_j + γ_k (home/away team abilities; team-specific home advantage = β_j − γ_j); the zero-inflated Skellam is P_Z(z) = p + (1−p)P(z) if z=0, (1−p)P(z) if z≠0; discrete normal P_N(z|μ,σ²) = Φ(z+0.5)−Φ(z−0.5) and discrete Laplace P_L(z|μ,σ²) = F(z+0.5)−F(z−0.5) are the alternatives.
equation: P_Z(z) = p + (1−p)P(z) if z=0; (1−p)P(z) if z≠0

claim: On German Handball Bundesliga 2017-18–2022-23 (1,844 matches; home goals 28.07±var 19.67, away 26.92±18.32 — underdispersed): Skellam or ZI Skellam wins the AIC bake-off every season (2021-22: Skellam 1854.39, ZI 1850.77, discrete normal 1855.83, discrete Laplace 1854.42); ZI Skellam's predicted outcome counts nail draws (152.02 home / 30.39 draw / 123.59 away vs observed 153/29/124), beating bookmaker-implied (160.63/28.22/117.14) on home/away; the Frank-copula bivariate model (38 params, AIC 3279.47) is preferred over Gumbel (3282.47) and independence (3324.09).

Brill, Yee, Deshpande & Wyner (2024) repair four statistical flaws in ML-based expected points on 491,993 NFL plays / 73,514 drives (2010-2022, nflFastR): EP(x) = Σ_k pts(k)·P(y=k|x), multinomial over 5 drive outcomes (TD=7, FG=3, no score=0, opp. safety=−2, opp. TD=−7) with log(P(y_ij=k|x_ij)/P(y_ij=No Score|x_ij)) = f_k(x_ij); the four fixes are (1) team-quality selection bias (include pre-game spread as covariate, evaluate at spread 0), (2) within-drive dependence (weighted log-loss w_ij = 1/N_i approximating M=100 averaged one-play-per-drive subsamples), (3) overfitting artifacts (catalytic prior: M=500,000 synthetic game-states from a multinomial logistic model, φ=1 smallest φ eliminating artifacts), (4) uncertainty (cluster bootstrap resampling drives, B=100).
equation: EP(x) = Σ_k pts(k)·P(y=k|x); log(P(y_ij=k|x_ij)/P(y_ij=No Score|x_ij)) = f_k(x_ij)

claim: EP study findings: good teams (spread < −3) run 32% of plays vs 26% for bad teams (spread > +3) and average 0.7 more points per drive — unadjusted EP overestimates average-team EP; weighted XGBoost rmse 2.593±0.0017, logloss 0.7506±0.0006, 95%-prediction-set coverage 0.834±0.0004 (all point-estimate prediction sets undercover ~83–86% vs 95% nominal); cluster-bootstrap coverage is correct (weighted+cluster 0.956±0.016) — sampling uncertainty, not mis-specification, was the coverage culprit; 2022 player evals: KC offense > Buffalo > rest (significant), Mahomes > Allen, Tua > rest.

The 'Generation of Threat' model attributes football threat-creation to players via 12-dimensional Hawkes processes on ball-touch event streams: λᵢ(t) = μᵢ + ΣⱼΣ_{tₖʲ<t} αᵢⱼ exp(−β(t−tₖʲ)), with branching matrix Γᵢⱼ = αᵢⱼ/β and stability requiring spectral radius ρ(Γ) < 1; four GoT indices: GoTᵈⁱʳᵢ = Γ_{threat,i}, GoTⁱⁿᵈᵢ = [(I−Γ)⁻¹]_{threat,i}, plus per-90 variants including an ablation index E[threats] − E[threats | row/col i of (K, μ) zeroed].
equation: λᵢ(t) = μᵢ + ΣⱼΣ_{tₖʲ<t} αᵢⱼ exp(−β(t−tₖʲ)); Γᵢⱼ = αᵢⱼ/β

claim: Simulations show ~600 min suffices for Hawkes structure learning (0.4% false-positive link rate, 0.0063 FN error, 18.6% relative Γ error; 1,200 min → 0.0% FP); Chelsea 2016-17 GoT₉₀: Hazard 14.2 (2.02), Kanté 6.2 indirect (1.40) ranked 4th (box-to-box danger role recovered), Moses 5.7, Pedro 5.5; Ligue 1 2021-22 surprise: right-back Frédéric Guilbert 8.42 (18th).

For Bayesian symbolic regression with a universal grammar-prior over equations, the posterior over equation forms is P(fᵢ|D) = P(fᵢ)/P(D)·Z(D|fᵢ) with the marginal likelihood approximated by the Laplace/Hutchinson form log Z(D|fᵢ) ≃ log L̂ + (p/2)log 2π − (1/2)log det Îᴴ (p = parameter count, Îᴴ = normalized observed Fisher information); model selection by log-evidence rather than likelihood-only is the core corrective.
equation: P(fᵢ|D) = P(fᵢ)/P(D)·Z(D|fᵢ); log Z(D|fᵢ) ≃ log L̂ + (p/2)log 2π − (1/2)log det Îᴴ

claim: Key findings from the symbolic-regression priors paper: likelihood-only selection NEVER puts the truth in the top two on noisy benchmarks (complexity must be penalized — physics-language prior helps on some, hurts on others, and likelihood-ratio tests are insufficient); the true equation xˣ was recovered for cosmology from noisy data; the prior's predictive power transfers out-of-domain.

RSRM (Reinforcement Symbolic Regression Machine) achieves 100% recovery on Nguyen-1..10 including the hard sin(x₁²)cos(x₁)−1 (where DSR gets 72% and GP 12%) and Livermore-21 hard cases via modulated sub-tree discovery (A±f(x), A×f(x), A^f(x)); but Livermore ablation on the hardest cases collapses (L3: 55 vs 20/0/0), and falling-ball compact forms (e.g. −4.43t²+0.36sin(t²+1.51)²+47.35) may hide numerical constants rather than physics.

CRAFTER (2026, 27 pages, real results on standard TSF benchmarks) is a residual-correction adapter for black-box forecasters: features are proposed by an LLM from training-text artifacts, evaluated by |ρ_Spearman(candidate, unexplained validation residual)| > 0.05 with pairwise redundancy caps (|ρ| ≤ 0.75, ≤2 features/family, ≤10/round), then a corrector from {NONE, additive GBDT, multiplicative GBDT} learns the residual mapping on frozen backbone forecasts; the corrector receives only engineered/contextual features — backbone forecasts enter only as the raw signal plus their moving averages.

CRAFTER mean test-wMAPE lift over RAW (relative reduction): Timer +25.7/+25.8 (with/without LLM features), Moirai +27.2/+26.8, TimesFM +3.2/+3.4, PatchTST +3.1/+3.2; ~74% of selected features are LLM-sourced (no-GPT ablations lose a few points); NONE (passthrough, i.e. pure feature discovery with no corrector) is an asymmetric floor; window size K=20 validated with ablations.

The GTN causal graph (nodes = 3D-joint streams at 25 fps) + Discrete Distribution Learning (DDL) pipeline encodes each node's motion by classifying it into one of K discrete motion codes: L = L_motion + α·L_code with KD-tree-codebook-balanced classes, and per node p_u = softmax(proj(MLP_code(h_u^(L)))/τ) with τ=1 (no temperature tuning); results: action recognition 96.21±0.29% (WorldPoseAR) and shot spotting Average-AP 0.9274±0.0030 (SuperLeague) with K∈[16,512] improving, plateauing beyond 512.

The ECDD drift detector tracks binary error streams with Z_t = (1−λ)Z_{t−1} + λX_t (λ=0.2) and alarms when Z_t > p̂_{0,t} + L_t·σ_{Z_t} where σ_{Z_t} = √[p̂_{0,t}(1−p̂_{0,t})·λ/(2−λ)·(1−(1−λ)^{2t})]; L_t comes from degree-7 polynomial lookup tables mapping (p̂_{0,t}, ARL_0) → L_t, e.g. for ARL_0=1000: L = 1.17 + 7.56p̂_0 − 21.24p̂_0³ + 112.12p̂_0⁵ − 987.23p̂_0⁷.

ECDD concept-drift findings: LED accuracy LDA 0.51→0.59–0.71 (better than the non-adaptive 0.51 baseline) with reset+decay consistently best; Electricity dataset LDA 0.70→0.86 (all variants), DWM/LVGBDT 0.73–0.75 with ECDD; λ∈{0.1,0.2,0.3} changes accuracy by ≤0.02 on tested streams (mild insensitivity).

Variational Continual Learning (VCL) minimizes ℒ_VCL = E_{q_t}[log p(D_t|θ)] − KL(q_t‖q_{t−1}) (yesterday's posterior is today's prior); Gaussian natural gradients simplify to ĝ_{μ_i} = σ_i²·g_{μ_i} (with F_{μ_i} = 1/σ_i², F_{v_i} = 2 for mean-field Gaussians); Stein coresets via SVGD φ*(x) = (1/M)Σ_j [k(x^{(j)},x^{(l)})∇log p(x^{(j)}|θ) + ∇k] augment the KL term with a coreset likelihood ℒ_t = E[log p(D_t|θ)] + E[log p(C_{t−1}|θ)] − KL(q_t‖q_{t−1}); the VCL+Stein-coreset combo hits 98.5%/90.5% on permuted/ordered MNIST with coresets of size 200/1000.
equation: ℒ_VCL = E_{q_t}[log p(D_t|θ)] − KL(q_t‖q_{t−1}); ĝ_{μ_i} = σ_i²·g_{μ_i}

claim: SRSD user study (n≈30 domain scientists, ~1,500 ratings): R²-based rankings are nearly uncorrelated with expert preference (PCC=0.00466, p=0.913), while normalized edit distance d̄(f_pred,f_true) = min(1, d(f_pred,f_true)/|f_true|) correlates strongly (PCC=−0.416, p=1.85×10⁻²⁴); domain-range difficulty is quantified by f_range(S) = |log₁₀|max S − min S||.
equation: d̄(f_pred,f_true) = min(1, d(f_pred,f_true)/|f_true|); f_range(S) = |log₁₀|max S − min S||

claim: SRSD benchmark results: PySR best on NED (Easy 0.269, Medium 0.537, Hard 0.785) with DSR 2nd (0.302/0.552/0.796); 50–100% of predictions across ALL methods use at least one dummy variable (even 'correct' predictions — DSR's 45.1% correct includes dummy-contaminated ones, E2E 100% contaminated) — a severe spurious-correlation diagnostic.

FRANS: treat each time series as its own classification class, train a 1D-CNN to discriminate series, take 16 static CNN features to replace 42 tsfeatures in the FFORMA meta-learner; forecasting accuracy is sMAPE = (200/n)Σ_t|y_t−ŷ_t|/(|y_t|+|ŷ_t|); FRANS wins 8/10 datasets (e.g. M4_Daily 3.020 vs 3.060) but the classifier was trained on windows including the test block — leakage caveat.

DIMA decomposes the multi-agent transition via the chain rule of probability (no agent ordering assumption): P(s_{t+1}, s_{t+1}^{(1):(n)}|s_t, a_t^{1:n}) = p(s_{t+1}^{(n)})∏_{k=1}^n p(s_{t+1}^{(k−1)}|s_{t+1}^{(k)}, a_t^k, s_t), trains a conditional diffusion model L(θ) = E_τ E_{k∼Uniform{1..n}}‖D_θ(s_{t+1}^τ; σ(τ), s_t, a_t^k) − s_{t+1}‖² with EDM preconditioners D_θ = c_skip·s + c_out·F_θ(c_in·s; c_noise, s_t, a_t^k), and matches or beats MARIE/MAMBA best returns on all tasks (Ant-2x4 4881±756 vs MARIE 4471±553; 2s-8x1 124±5 vs 129±6) with computation linear in the number of agents.

DIMA's scaling limits: only tested to ~6 agents (Ant-6x1), so scaling to dozens or hundreds of agents is untested; the theory is proved for discrete state/action spaces while experiments are continuous, and there is no mechanism to correct mis-modeling when the conditional factorization does not hold.

SMGDiff (REJECT): two-stage diffusion for soccer avatar motion - Stage 1 single-step diffusion trajectory generator (transformer encoder, diffusion timestep=1); Stage 2 transformer autoregressive diffusion (CAMDM-style) predicting x_hat_0^F with only 8 denoising steps; loss L = L_simple + lambda_pos L_pos + lambda_vel L_vel + lambda_foot L_foot; contact guidance at inference (last 2 of 8 steps): ball-contact detection via acceleration threshold tau_a = 2 m/s^2; contact loss L = sum_i d^i*I(d^i>tau_d)*c_hat_b^i/(I(d^i>tau_d)+delta), tau_d = 0.1 m; ball control weight w_b = 1 - ||b_p^{xy} - h_p^{xy}||/r, r = 2 m.
equation: L = L_simple + λ_pos L_pos + λ_vel L_vel + λ_foot L_foot; w_b = 1 − ‖b_p^{xy} − h_p^{xy}‖/r

claim: SMGDiff results: FID 0.1813 (vs 0.3541/0.3593/0.2494 baselines), foot sliding 0.8543, skill accuracy 93.3% (vs 73.3%/69.1%/52.9%); 8 denoising steps -> 12 ms; 32 steps -> 52 ms; Soccer-X mocap dataset: 16 OptiTrack Prime x13 cameras, 240 fps, 30 players, 1.08M frames, 2,398 sequences, 6 categories, SMPL 24-joint format (announced, not released at write time); reader verdict REJECT - character-animation product with no transfer path; the motion-synthesis family was already absorbed via papers 0380 and 2503.18589.

ArXiv 2307.02139v1 (Michels/Otting/Karlis, extending Dixon-Coles via Sarmanov, ADAPT): Dixon-Coles P(X_1,X_2) = tau_{lambda_1,lambda_2}(x_1,x_2)*Poisson(lambda_1)*Poisson(lambda_2), with tau shifting probability only among (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1); Sarmanov (Eq. 2): P(X_1=x_1,X_2=x_2) = P_1(x_1)P_2(x_2)[1 + omega q_1(x_1)q_2(x_2)]; zero-mean constraint sum q_i P_i = 0; rho = omega u_1 u_2/(sigma_1 sigma_2); key theorem: Dixon-Coles is a Sarmanov member (q_dc(x_i) = -lambda_i if x_i=0, 1 if x_i=1, 0 if x_i>=2).

Women's football empirics from 0392: home-away goal correlations England -0.269, Germany -0.352, France -0.395, Spain -0.263; the classical Dixon-Coles correlation floor is only -0.08 (at lambda=1.3/1.2) - DC cannot represent the observed negative dependence; NB marginals beat Poisson on AIC for every league (e.g. Spain: double NB 14,953.09 vs double Poisson 15,432.49); ANS was AIC-preferred among 11 formulations for all four leagues in baseline fits; predictive demo: German Frauen-Bundesliga 2021/22 fit on first 15 matchdays, 1,000 Monte Carlo completions of last 7 matchdays -> 95% prediction intervals contained all teams' observed final points; limitations: only one league-season out-of-sample (thin); NFL transfer needs re-derivation (NFL points are not low-count Poisson - apply to TD counts or binned totals).

Fitting method from 0392: numerical MLE in R via nlm(); team models log(theta_1j) = home + att_{h_j} + def_{g_j} with sum-to-zero defence constraint; comparison by AIC and sum|model - empirical| over scores 0-0 through 11-11 x100; new models: q_hat (quadratic-exponent on 4 pairs), q_tilde (shifting over x_i in {0,1,2}, 9 pairs), q^(s) (general shifting over (s+1)^2 pairs), NB marginals with q_nb/q_hat_nb/q_tilde_nb, full-support Laplace-based q_Sar, and novel ANS q_ANS(x) = [phi_i/(phi_i+mu_i)]^{x_i} - c_i.
